products.name: 1872 Men Type Formula
products.description:
This is our exclusive deluxe formula for the surprisingly complex Clive Christian fragrance from master perfumer Geza Schoen (of Escentric Molecules fame). It was released in 2001.

Clive Christian has a great reputation for quality and unlike some brands (Amouage and Tom Ford for example) the high price the brand commands really is often justified by the complexity and richesse of their scents.

Top Notes: Petitgrain, Lime, Bergamot, Rosemary, Lavender, Galbanum, Pepper, Peach, Pineapple, Mandarin and Nutmeg
Heart Notes: Clary Sage, Cyclamen, Marigold, Jasmine and Freesia
Base Notes: Virginia Cedar, Musk, Patchouli, Amber, Olibanum and Labdanum

Total Lines: 58
Naturals: 19
Bases: 4

products.name: 2-Acetyl Pyridine
products.description:
2-Acetyl pyridine is the single most convincing popcorn molecule available to perfumers. At full strength it is heavy, oily, and tobacco-like, but dilute it below one per cent and you get warm, freshly popped corn, toasted bread crust, and roasted grain. A secondary hazelnut sweetness rounds it out.

Use this molecule in traces to add gourmand warmth and roasted depth to your tobacco, coffee, and chocolate accords. It transforms oriental bases with a comforting, baked quality that nothing else delivers. Dose with extreme caution — its potency is staggering and overdose ruins compositions instantly.

Blend with vanillin and ethyl maltol for rich gourmand effects. Try it alongside tobacco absolute and coffee CO2 for naturalistic depth. Pair with other pyrazines and roasted materials to build complex, layered accords that smell authentically toasted.

products.name: 2-Acetyl Thiazole
products.description:
2-Acetyl thiazole smells convincingly of toasted hazelnuts and freshly baked bread crust. Where 2-acetyl pyridine gives you pure popcorn, this molecule leans nuttier and more complex, with cocoa, roasted cereal, and savoury facets adding depth. Work from a one per cent solution — it is extraordinarily potent.

Use this molecule in your gourmand and tobacco compositions where you need authentic roasted-nut character. It bridges the gap between edible gourmand sweetness and smoky-woody depth. A trace in chocolate or coffee accords adds the toasted dimension that makes them smell genuinely realistic.

Pair with vanillin and cocoa absolute for rich praline effects. Try it alongside tobacco absolute for convincing pipe-tobacco warmth. Combine with 2-acetyl pyridine for a layered roasted accord that covers both the popcorn and nutty sides of the spectrum.

products.name: 2-Ethylhexyl Salicylate
products.description:
2-Ethylhexyl Salicylate barely announces itself on the strip — a faint, sweet orchid quality with soft balsamic warmth, almost too quiet to notice. That discretion is exactly the point. At typical use levels, it slips into a formula virtually undetected.

Use 2-Ethylhexyl Salicylate as your UV shield. It absorbs ultraviolet light that would otherwise yellow your juice and degrade sensitive top notes over time. Citrus, aldehydic, and pale floral compositions benefit most — anything where colour clarity and scent stability matter.

Pair it with Avobenzone, Octinoxate, Oxynex, Hexyl Salicylate and Benzyl Salicylate for a layered UV-protective base that also brings floral depth to your dry-down. In clear glass bottles or sun-exposed retail displays, a salicylate backbone keeps your creation looking and smelling as intended.

products.name: 2-Isobutyl Quinoline
products.description:
2-Isobutyl Quinoline (not to be confused with Pyralone AKA Isobutyl Quinoline) is a soft but very persistent weedy and leathery chemical. It is the key to the dry down of Aventus (formula below) and works very well in combination with the classic and closely related Pyralone (CAS 65442-31-1) and Isopropyl Quinoline (CAS 135-79-5).

Use traces to support moss, roots, patchouli or leather notes, or use a larger amount for a novel character. 2-Isobutyl Quinoline is extremely powerful and very popular in classic chypre and fougère type fragrances.

products.name: 2-Isopropyl Phenol
products.description:
2-Isopropyl Phenol opens with a sharp, medicinal-creosote bite. The phenolic backbone carries toasted wood warmth and something reminiscent of charred oak barrels. On dilution you find smoky depth with subtle burnt rubber and tar undertones that recall cade oil.

This phenol belongs in leather accords, smoky bases, and dark woody compositions. Combine it with birch tar and castoreum for Russian leather, or add traces to oud blends for raw medicinal edge. The creosote character anchors these accords with convincing naturalism.

Use 2-Isopropyl Phenol at trace levels — it dominates in overdose. Blend with cade oil and labdanum for bonfire accords, or alongside isobutyl quinoline for vintage leather character. It occurs naturally in whiskey and dried bonito, which gives you a sense of its fierce, savoury nature.

products.name: 4-Ethyl Guaiacol
products.description:
4-Ethyl Guaiacol is the smell of oak barrels, smoked meat, and aged whisky. It occurs naturally in all of those things — formed when heat breaks down the lignin in wood — and it brings that same warm, smoky, cured quality to perfume compositions. The clove note is prominent but not sharp; it sits underneath a layer of soft vanilla warmth and dry woodsmoke.

Use it in leather accords where you want genuine smokiness without the heaviness of birch tar. A trace alongside castoreum or Suederal and you have a smoked leather that smells like it has been sitting in a tannery, not a laboratory. In tobacco compositions it provides the cured, pipe-smoke facet that dried tobacco leaf alone cannot deliver. It works in gourmand fragrances too — paired with coffee or dark chocolate, it adds a roasted, almost savoury complexity.

Dose it carefully. Like most phenolic materials it can overwhelm a composition at anything above trace levels. At the right concentration it is invisible as itself and simply makes everything around it smell richer, warmer, and more real.

products.name: 6-Methyl Quinoline
products.description:
6-Methyl quinoline smells of dark leather, castoreum, and tobacco, with a sweet tonka-vanilla warmth underneath — and then something unexpected: a mineral quality like wet concrete or pebbles on a rain-soaked beach. In concentration it can read fecal; in dilution it reveals its extraordinary complexity. Work from a heavy dilution and it rewards you.

This is not the green, rooty leather of isobutyl quinoline. It is browner, warmer, more animalic, with that unique mineral facet that no other material gives. Use it in traces to build castoreum reconstructions, tobacco accords, and dark leather bases. A single drop transforms an oriental or chypre, adding depth and fixation that lasts over 400 hours.

Two quinolines, two leathers

We also stocks Civettal (tetrahydro para methyl quinoline), which is more purely civet-like — honeyed, ambergris-tinged, animalic without the mineral edge. 6-Methyl quinoline is broader: leather, castoreum, tobacco, mineral, tonka. Use Civettal for civet reconstructions; use 6-methyl quinoline for castoreum depth and that wet-stone quality nothing else provides.

products.name: Absolute Ambergris™
products.description:
Absolute Ambergris™ is a painstaking reconstruction of 25 year aged Ambergris resin. Use it one for one in vintage formulas to replace 3% ambergris tincture, or as a magnificent and rich animalic ambergris note. 

This is an essential item for all perfumers as there is nothing on the market that comes close to the elegance and blending power of Absolute Ambergris. Not only do you get the full scent of rich aged ambergris, but also all of the qualities of fixation, blending, and exaltation that natural ambergris gives.

This has an indistinguishable scent from natural aged white ambergris tincture but we do not use alcohol in its manufacture.

Unlimited use allowed for IFRA 49 and up to 8.3% for IFRA 51 and IFRA 52.

products.name: Acalea
products.description:
Acalea (mimosa heptanal) is a soft, powdery mimosa in bloom. Its heliotrope-and-mimosa floralcy stays fresh and dewy rather than sweet and heavy, brightened by a green lift and a light berry-fruity nuance. Creamy and rounded, it is gentle and natural, like newly opened petals.

Use it in the mid-notes to build mimosa and heliotrope accords, or to add a soft, powdery roundness to white florals and fruity-floral bouquets. It rounds jasmine, smooths mixed-flower hearts, and lends a dewy, natural freshness that keeps a floral from turning cloying. Its green side also freshens sweeter compositions.

products.name: Acetal CD
products.description:
Also known as Hyacinth Acetals or Phenylacetaldehyde Glyceryl Acetal, Acetal CD is a light floralising material that finds use in floral compounds needing a soft but very long lasting heart.

With delicate nuances of dried rose, honey, black tea and, of course, hyacinth, this is a great material to overdose in an age of heavily restricted florals.

products.name: Acetanisole Crystals
products.description:
Acetanisole stands as a cornerstone ingredient for powdery-sweet compositions. This crystalline material delivers an exceptional sweet-anisic profile with remarkable longevity. Leverage its hawthorn-like character to bridge the gap between vanilla accords and floral bouquets with unparalleled effectiveness. This makes a great alternative or booster to anisaldehyde when you hit IFRA limits of that material.

These crystals work wonders in vanilla bases to add depth and realism. Acetanisole pairs brilliantly with heliotropin, coumarin, and hay absolute. Use in floral-powdery compositions at 0.03-0.15% to extend pollen notes and smooth aldehyde harshness.

If you are not used to working with crystals and powders, check out our handy Guide To Powders.

products.name: Acetate C-9
products.description:
Acetate C-9 (nonyl acetate) opens with a sweet, waxy fruitiness—clean and green with a distinctive tropical quality that immediately suggests ripe fruit. Beneath the fruit sits an earthy, mushroom-like facet that gives the material its unusual character: part gardenia petal, part forest floor after rain. The overall impression is mild, diffusive, and surprisingly natural.

This ester is most useful where you want green-fruity freshness with floral dimension. It brings a convincing naturalism to gardenia and white floral accords, where that earthy-mushroom undertone adds the damp, living quality that separates realistic flowers from synthetic ones. Use it in tropical fruit compositions for waxy depth, or in citrus blends where it adds a ripe, peel-like richness beneath the sparkling top notes.

products.name: Acetoin
products.description:
Acetoin opens with unmistakable buttery-creamy character—sweet, rich, and instantly evocative of fresh dairy. The caramel undertone adds warmth without becoming confectionery, while mild fatty nuances provide the authentic quality that separates this from simpler sweet materials. The overall effect is comforting, milky, and surprisingly versatile.

This material transforms abstract florals into flesh and substance - add traces to tuberose and watch it become waxy and carnal. In gourmand compositions, acetoin bridges the gap between flat sweetness and three-dimensional richness, turning sugar into toffee and fruit into jam. Pair it with lactones for condensed milk effects or layer it under sandalwood to recreate that coveted buttermilk top note.

Use acetoin when you need to soften synthetic edges without adding heaviness. It excels at creating fermented nuances in fruit accords and adding the fatty richness missing from reconstituted white florals.

products.name: Acetophenone
products.description:
Acetophenone has been a reliable ingredient in perfumery for more than a century. Its soft, almond-like odour, enriched with warm floral nuances, adds sophistication to both classic and modern compositions. While its sweetness is delicate, its effect is considerable, enhancing the richness of florals and the creaminess of gourmand notes.

Acetophenone blends perfectly into compositions featuring jasmine, heliotrope, and tonka bean (which, in traces. it reinforces and boosts). Its warmth also lends a smooth, powdery effect to mimosa and hawthorn accords. Known for its fixative properties, it subtly anchors volatile top notes, allowing them to linger.

Acetophenone does have a harsh side so a slap-happy dosing is not recommend. Exercise care.

products.name: Acetyl Methyl Anthranilate
products.description:
Acetyl Methyl Anthranilate presents as a white powder with an unexpectedly gentle aroma - soft powdery strawberry, a trace of grape, and delicate orange blossom sweetness. Nothing like its parent Methyl Anthranilate's aggressive narcotic punch. This is anthranilate character reduced to something quiet and refined.

The real story here is stability. Where Methyl Anthranilate reacts with aldehydes to form Schiff bases - causing discolouration and unpredictable odour shifts - this acetylated version sits perfectly stable alongside hydroxycitronellal, lilial, and other aldehyde partners. That compatibility opens formulation possibilities methyl anthranilate simply cannot.

Use Acetyl Methyl Anthranilate as a fixative - its tenacity on blotter rivals the most persistent base notes. It occurs naturally in champaca concrete and jasmine absolute. Blend with strawberry furanone, linalool, and alpha-methyl ionone for powdery floral effects that last.

products.name: Acetyl Propionyl
products.description:
Acetyl propionyl hits you with unmistakable buttery richness—this is the real thing, not a polite suggestion of cream. The caramel-toffee facet follows immediately, warm and inviting. Underneath sits a toasted, almost roasted almond quality that adds unexpected complexity to the dairy character.

This material occurs naturally across an impressive range of foods: butter, bread, milk, yogurt, coffee, cocoa, roasted nuts, beer, wine, and whisky. In perfumery, it belongs to the essential custard note family alongside acetoin and butyric acid. When you need that authentic dairy-caramel warmth in gourmand compositions, nothing else quite matches its impact.

Use acetyl propionyl sparingly—the odour strength is high, so dilute to one percent or less before evaluating. It transforms vanilla accords from sweet to genuinely custardy. The 12-hour substantivity provides solid mid-note performance. Blend with lactones and vanillin for irresistible dessert effects.

products.name: Adoxal
products.description:
Adoxal opens with unmistakable marine freshness—ozonic, aldehydic, and immediately evocative of sea breezes and crisp clean linens. The waxy floral undertone emerges quickly, bringing lily-of-the-valley brightness without sweetness. A subtle ambergris-like warmth anchors the composition, making this far more sophisticated than simple aquatic materials.

This Givaudan aldehyde has become essential for aquatic and fresh fragrance categories. Its profile sits close to Calone territory—watermelon-marine-ozonic—but with added aldehydic complexity and better performance in functional products. The 168-hour substantivity on blotter translates to exceptional longevity in finished compositions. Use it in detergent and fabric care fragrances where that fresh linen character defines the category.

Deploy this material strategically at different concentrations for varied effects. Use traces (0.01-0.1%) as a floralizer that adds air and radiance to rose or jasmine. Push it to 1-5% for avant-garde metallic effects that evoke ink or cold metal. Partner it with Ambroxan for modern marine dry-downs or with Dihydromyrcenol to create that distinctive "blue" freshness.

products.name: Aerolide®
products.description:
This is the only white musk accord you will ever need. Aerolide® combines the essential high volume musks with the most modern radiant ones in a perfectly blended base. In complete equilibrium and dosed to get the optimum power and nuance that each included musk has to offer, Aerolide® can be used in traces to megadose (over 20%).

Aerolide® gives your fragrance vitality, diffusion, radiance and longevity.

Aerolide® blends exceptionally well with other musks, particularly Helvetolide®.

products.name: Aetoxylon “White Oud” Oil
products.description:
A large fruiting tree endemic to West Borneo Aetoxylon (also known as Gaharu Buaya or Black Eaglewood) that is becoming extremely desirable as a new wood note in perfume that is particularly synergistic with agarwood and consequently being used in high amounts in Middle Eastern luxury fragrances where it is easier to obtain.

Imagine Oud without the intense animalic quality and you have Aetoxylon. More versatile and appealing even to those who don't normally like Oud. Dress it up for a full Agarwood impression, or use it as it for a lovely complex and little-known wood note.

To ensure the highest possible quality on the market, we supply the finest quality from MANE in Grasse.

Origin: West Borneo
Part: Wood

products.name: Agarwood Boya Oil
products.description:
Agarwood Boya Oil is the waxy extract of the aquilaria tree taken from uninfected wood (oud oil is distilled exclusively from disease-infected wood). The oil (which presents as a solid wax like orris butter), is gentler and creamier than oud oil but still retains all the characteriistic animal power, with fruity facets. This material is absolutely convincing as the much higher cost oud oil in fragrances and if we are honest, it is probably what makes up the bulk of the oud note in premium oud fragrances these days. It is also known to be used to adulterate real oud to attract higher profits. If you are not an expert, it is wise to stick with the oud extracts from prestige houses like Firmenich which supplies our marvellous Bangladeshi Oud Assam oil, and LMR (maker of this Boya oil) which has an intense but fruitier Vietnamese Oud oil. In fact, this boya oil comes from the same source wood as the LMR Vietnamese oud. 

Note: This is a creamy, semi-solid wax at room temperature, not a free-flowing liquid, so it needs gentle warming to work with. We offer this perfumery marvel at 10% in a Superessence. To achieve this, we dilute the pure oil in a blend of Benzyl Benzoate (approximately 20%) and IPM (approximately 70%) resulting in a clear and easy to use liquid.

products.name: Akigala Extreme
products.description:
Akigalawood is all the rage at Givaudan right now. It is a captive molecule derived from the upcycling of waste from patchouli manufacturing and it has a profile which is peppery and woody and, as is to be expected given the starting material, distinctly patchouli like. It stars in such fragrances as Dark Rebel (2015) by Rodrigo Flores-Roux for Varvatos where it contributes both patchouli and pepper notes. It is also used in Tom Ford's Fougère d'Argent (2018) where it blends with lavender and tonka and features in Quentin Bisch's Purpose (2023) and Guidance (2023) both for Amouage. 

Akigala Extreme is our interpretation of the Akigalawood captive in the form of a base built around an extraordinary quality (and amount) of molecular distilled patchouli with accents of pepper and dank woods. Use Akigala Extreme in place of patchouli or as an entirely novel new earthy wood note.

products.name: Alcohol C-10
products.description:
Alcohol C-10 greets the nose with a sweet, waxy warmth wrapped around a distinctly floral core - something between fresh orange peel and soft rose. A clean, fatty-oily smoothness gives it body without heaviness. On a strip, the floral-orange character holds for over four days.

This material sits right between the lighter Alcohol C-8 and the heavier Alcohol C-12 Lauric in the fatty alcohol series. Its floral-orange quality makes it essential for rose accords and neroli reconstructions. It rounds aldehydic florals with the waxy bloom that makes classic perfumes feel opulent.

Pair it with Aldehyde C-10 (Decanal) for a complete orange-waxy spectrum from sparkling top to warm base. In citrus colognes, a trace adds floral body beneath the volatile head. It occurs naturally in orange oil, coriander, and rose - a familiar companion to materials you already use.

products.name: Alcohol C-11 Undecylenic
products.description:
Alcohol C-11 undecylenic greets you with a bright, clean freshness—waxy rose petals with a citrus zing and a hint of cool ozone. This is one of the defining materials for that dewy, just-washed, sparkling quality you recognise from classic floral perfumes. The fatty undertone is milder than the aldehyde and rounds the freshness rather than dragging it down.

This material gives florals an instant lift. It brightens rose compositions with waxy petal realism, adds citrus-fresh sparkle to jasmine and magnolia bases, and brings clean ozone to modern aquatic accords. In lilac and tuberose reconstructions, it provides that elusive dewy-morning freshness that separates good from great.

products.name: Alcohol C-12 Lauric
products.description:
Alcohol C-12 Lauric is a waxy solid at room temperature with a soft, clean, soapy aroma and an unmistakable fatty quality. Warm honey and coconut nuances sit underneath, giving it more character than you might expect. On the strip it's quiet but remarkably persistent, lasting over 80 hours.

Use Alcohol C-12 Lauric to build convincing mimosa and cassie accords — its waxy-honey character is essential to both. It anchors aldehydic florals with warm soapy depth while acting as a fixative. In tuberose compositions, the coconut facet reinforces that naturally creamy undertone.

Pair it with its aldehyde counterpart, Aldehyde C-12 Lauric, for a complete waxy spectrum from sparkling top to warm base. Orange blossom absolute and ylang ylang are natural partners. Everything you build around Alcohol C-12 lasts longer — it's a quiet fixative that should be in every perfumer's arsenal.

products.name: Alcohol C-6
products.description:
This simple alcohol captures the essence of freshly mown grass with remarkable accuracy. However, unlike harsh green notes, Alcohol C-6 provides a softer, more diffuse greenness that evokes lush foliage and garden freshness. Its under-ripe fruit character is crucial—this isn't sweet jamminess, but the crisp tartness of green apple skin or firm pear.

The material's fatty and waxy undertones provide essential texture, mimicking the feel of fruit skin or flower petals. A subtle winey quality emerges at higher concentrations, adding fermented complexity that prevents compositions from smelling flat. This fusel oil character becomes an asset when creating realistic wine or cognac accords.

Use this when you need to add life and naturalness without overwhelming other notes. Its extremely short substantivity means it works as a top note modifier, creating a "tender atmosphere" that enhances floral realism. At higher concentrations, it becomes structural for crisp fruit accords.

products.name: Alcohol C-7
products.description:
Straight from the bottle, Alcohol C-7 is assertive and not particularly pleasant — sharp, green, musty, like crushed stems left in a vase too long. That is precisely the point. Perfumery is full of materials that smell crude in isolation and become indispensable in context.

Use it at trace levels to add a raw, crushed-stem leafiness to green florals. It gives violet leaf accords a wild, just-picked naturalism that cleaner materials like cis-3-hexenol can't quite achieve. In hyacinth and lily-of-the-valley compositions, a whisper of C-7 provides the slightly musty, vegetative undertone that separates a convincing flower from a flat one.

Think of it as the imperfection that makes green accords believable. Too much and it turns harsh; the right trace and your florals gain depth. It blends well with galbanum, violet leaf, and the leafy green aldehydes. Handle it with respect — this is a seasoning, not a main ingredient.

products.name: Alcohol C-8
products.description:
Alcohol C-8 has a distinctive green, waxy character with fresh orange and citrus brightness up front. A subtle rose-violet florality weaves through the middle alongside sweet, fatty coconut undertones. There is an earthy, almost mushroom-like facet that adds unexpected naturalistic depth.

This works as a blending agent that smooths and naturalises compositions rather than adding a standalone note. Use it in citrus accords to round sharp edges, or in florals to add green body and depth. It contributes convincing naturalistic quality to rose and violet reconstructions.

Try small additions in orange blossom and neroli-based fragrances where its waxy-green character reinforces the natural material. The coconut-like sweetness also makes it useful in tropical and gourmand compositions. Moderate additions contribute a soft, skin-like quality that helps fix volatile top notes.

products.name: Alcohol C-9
products.description:
Alcohol C-9 sits at the point where the green, vegetative character of the lower alcohols gives way to something distinctly floral. The rose and orange blossom facets are immediately apparent, though filtered through a waxy lens. It smells like roses seen through frosted glass — the floral is there, but it's not clean or pretty.

That waxy-fatty quality is what makes it useful. Rose accords built entirely from clean materials can feel thin and synthetic. A small addition of C-9 gives them the oily, petal-skin quality of a real rose — the slightly fatty note you get when you crush a fresh petal between your fingers. It serves the same function in orange blossom accords, adding body and naturalism.

It blends particularly well with phenylethyl alcohol, citronellol, and geraniol — the classic rose materials — where it fills the lower register. Use it also beneath neroli reconstructions to add waxy substance. Like all fatty alcohols, restraint is essential.

products.name: Aldalia
products.description:
Aldalia is a beautiful woody aldehydic lily of the valley base used in large quantities in such fragrances as 1000 by Jean Patou and La Rose Jacqueminot by Coty—his first commercial success. It was copied by Roure in the form of Aldehone which was used by Jean Carles in Ma Griffe.

At its core is a beautiful rich lily of the valley with accents of rose and cistus. The whole is topped with a big dose of sparkling aldehydes. There is no better way to floralise and enhance a fragrance. Use it in place of a single lily chemical or as part of a more complex heart.

Fraterworks Aldalia is a restoration of the original formula, being modified only to comply with EU regulations banning the use of musk ambrette. It is otherwise completely IFRA compliant up to 18.78% of the finished product.

products.name: Aldambre
products.description:
Aldambre opens with dry woody-amber character that feels remarkably clean—no dustiness, no heaviness. The distinctive hot iron facet emerges quickly, adding an intriguing metallic edge that sets this material apart from conventional ambers. Soft musky undertones provide a skin-like finish, while the overall effect remains warm without becoming cloying or animalic.

You'll find Aldambre invaluable for abstracting woody bases and creating contemporary mineral effects. Add it at 0.5-2% to strip earthiness from vetiver and patchouli, leaving elegant driftwood bones. Combine with salicylates for authentic hot stone accords or pair with Ambroxan to amplify mineral facets. At higher doses, it becomes a statement material for conceptual fragrances.

This heart-note musk bridges top and base beautifully, radiating outward during the crucial 1-4 hour window. Use it to modernise aldehydic florals or create that coveted "anti-perfume" aesthetic. For something truly electrifying, combine Aldambre with Metal Oxazole and Habanolide—together they create a hot metal accord that crackles with industrial heat, like a forge at midnight.

products.name: Aldehone Extra
products.description:
Aldehone Extra is Jean Carles' (when working at Roure) artistic replica of Aldalia from Chuit Naef & Cie which we also stock. Aldehone Extra combines aldehydes with a fond of delightful floral and wood materials. Beautifully decorated with citrus and luxurious oriental resins, this is a marvel to behold and despite its historic age, is an astonishingly modern base with great potential for a revival today.

Use our demonstration formula of Nuit de Paris (based loosely on the ideas contained in Soir de Paris) to understand the power of Aldehone Extra or use it as a one for replacer in our formula for 1,000 by Patou for a variation on that same theme.

products.name: Aldehyde C-10
products.description:
Aldehyde C-10 hits you with unmistakable waxy-citrus power—think freshly zested orange peel with a soapy, almost metallic brightness. This is the aldehydic sparkle that defines an entire genre of perfumery. Harsh in concentration, it transforms into pure elegance when properly diluted and balanced.

First synthesised in 1883, Aldehyde C-10 waited nearly four decades for its moment of glory. In 1921, Ernest Beaux overdosed it alongside three other aldehydes—C-11 Undecylenic, C-12 Lauric, and C-12 MNA—to create Chanel No. 5. This legendary quartet became perfumery's shot heard around the world, establishing the aldehydic floral as a defining genre. Where earlier perfumes like Houbigant's Quelques Fleurs (1912) used aldehydes subtly to brighten florals, Beaux pushed concentration until the aldehyde complex became a recognisable note in its own right.

Use Aldehyde C-10 at trace levels—typically 0.02% to 1% maximum in your concentrate. It occurs naturally in orange peel and coriander leaf, lending authentic citrus lift. The 224-hour substantivity surprises for such a volatile-seeming material. Always dilute before evaluating; neat assessment tells you nothing useful about its magnificent behaviour in finished compositions.

products.name: Aldehyde C-11 Intreleven
products.description:
Aldehyde C-11 Intreleven opens with powerful clean aldehydic character—green, rosy, and immediately evocative of fresh linen and quality soap. The ozonic-marine facets add modern brightness, while citrus-orange undertones provide lift without heaviness. This is aldehydic perfumery at its most refined: sparkling, diffusive, and remarkably versatile across fine fragrance and functional applications.

This material delivers a fresher, more complex profile than simple Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic. The 400-hour substantivity on blotter translates to exceptional longevity in finished products, and the excellent stability in body lotions, shampoos, and all-purpose cleaners makes it valuable across categories. The fresh linen aspect has made it particularly popular in fabric care applications where clean, aldehydic character defines the category.

Use it as a top note booster in white floral concepts, or to add aldehydic sparkle to citrus, marine, and green compositions. It blends beautifully with other aldehydes, rose materials, and fatty-floral notes. Excellent soap stability makes it a workhorse for functional fragrances.

Aldehyde C-11 Intreleven vs Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic

These two C-11 aldehydes share the same carbon chain length but differ significantly in character. Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic  is waxy, fatty, and distinctly rosy-citrus with a soapy quality; one of the three aldehydes Beaux used in Chanel No. 5. Intreleven is several times stronger than Undecylenic, with a fres

products.name: Aldehyde C-11 MOA
products.description:
Aldehyde C-11 MOA — Methyl Octyl Acetaldehyde — hits you with explosive citrus-peel zestiness, radiant and immediately diffusive. Underneath is a waxy tangerine warmth that gives it body beyond a simple top note. The drydown settles into something clean and watery, almost marine.

This is your go-to fresh aldehyde for contemporary citrus and marine accords, where its zesty radiance adds instant sparkle. Orange compositions gain authentic peel character from even small additions. Blend with dihydromyrcenol and calone for aquatic work, or with other C-series aldehydes for classic aldehydic lift.

Use Aldehyde C-11 MOA sparingly — its diffusive power is remarkable. Pair with bergamot and vetiver for a modern masculine citrus, or with hedione and linalool for luminous white florals. It also brings that sparkling just-washed character to laundry and fabric care accords.

MOA vs Undecylenic vs Intreleven

Both carry the C-11 label — eleven carbon atoms — but they smell and behave quite differently. MOA is zesty, citrus-peel bright, and watery-marine. It's entirely synthetic and leans modern and fresh. Undecylenic is waxier, fattier, and more traditionally aldehydic: rosy-citrus with a soapy-green character. It occurs naturally in coriander leaf and is one of the three aldehydes Ernest Beaux selected for Chanel No. 5.

The practical divide: MOA excels in contemporary citrus, marine, and fabric care compositions. Undecylenic is the classic aldehydic floral ingredient, delivering rich

products.name: Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic
products.description:
Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic is one of the two fatty (or aliphatic) aldehydes which are not found in nature (the other is Aldehyde C-12 MNA). 

C-11 Undecylenic is particularly useful for adding inimitable accents to florals and, owing to its green fatty quality, it blends well with mossy and woody notes. This is one of the three aldehydes used by Ernest Beaux in his masterpiece of perfumery No 5 for Chanel.

As with all true aldehydes, we recommend dilution in an alcohol upon receipt of this product. Ethyl alcohol is the most commonly used for this purpose, but others such as phenyl ethyl alcohol or benzyl alcohol are also suitable.

products.name: Aldehyde C-11 Undecylic
products.description:
This is not the classic Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic as seen in Chanel No 5.

Aldehyde C-11 Undecylic opens with a clean, waxy-soapy burst that immediately evokes fresh laundry and citrus peel. An effervescent orange brightness runs through the middle, accompanied by subtle green and faintly floral undertones. The overall character is brighter and more citrus-focused than the heavier lower aldehydes.

Use this as the aldehydic backbone of citrus colognes and soapy-fresh compositions. It adds instant radiance and diffusion to floral hearts without the green-rose character of its Undecylenic cousin. In classic aldehydic florals it provides the waxy sparkle that lifts an entire composition.

Pair with Aldehyde C-10 and C-12 for a classic aldehydic ladder, or combine with bergamot and neroli for luminous citrus compositions. Always dilute before use, as the neat material is intensely powerful. It blends surprisingly well with musks and woods for clean, modern masculine structures.

Undecylenic vs Undecylic

We also sell the classic Aldehyde C-11 Undecylenic, which is greener and more floral-rose in character. This Undecylic version is waxier, soapier, and more citrus-forward with a clean orange-peel facet. Choose Undecylenic for rose-tinged green lift in florals and chypres; choose Undecylic for soapy brightness in aldehydic accords and citrus colognes. Blend both for a fuller aldehydic effect.

products.name: Aldehyde C-12 Lauric
products.description:
Aldehyde C-12 Lauric opens with sharp citrus zest on warm waxy paper. Green stem nuances rise alongside leafy herbs, balanced by creamy fattiness that prevents thinness. Within seconds, violet-rose breath emerges whilst the fatty facet turns pleasantly soapy-clean.

You'll find this aldehyde essential for creating classic aldehydic florals where its sparkle makes heavy hearts feel lighter and modern. It excels at brightening citrus openings, making bergamot and lemon more diffusive. Use it at 0.01-0.1% dilution—its power means traces create lasting clean halos without dominating compositions.

Blend C-12 Lauric with rose and jasmine for classic aldehydic bouquets or combine with violet and iris for powdery sophistication. Pair with other aldehydes (C-10, C-11) for the full Chanel effect. This material bridges citrus tops with floral hearts beautifully whilst adding pine-fresh complexity.

Alongside the classic trio of C-10, C-11 Undecylenic and C-12 MNA, this aldehyde was used in the original Chanel No 5.

NOTE: we also supply this aldehyde diluted to 10% in 96% pure perfumer's alcohol. Alcohol is the best diluent for aldehydes as it slows down the degradation process.

C-12 Lauric vs C-12 MNA

C-12 Lauric's straight-chain structure creates bright, zesty citrus-soapy character, whilst C-12 MNA's branched methyl group produces warmer amber sweetness with herbaceous depth. Where Lauric sparkles with sharp citrus-violet freshness ideal for bright florals, MNA offers complex ambe

products.name: Aldehyde C-12 MNA
products.description:
What marvellous wonders of perfumery are created by the judicious use of Aldehyde C-12 MNA. It singlehandedly adds character to Raphael's 1944 Replique (one of the forgotten masterpieces of classical perfumery), it adds a je ne sais quoi to Monsieur Roucel's novel Eau de Cologne (2000) for Helmut Lang and it was perfumery's metaphorical shot heard around the world when Ernest Beaux overdosed it with three other aldehydes (C-10, C-11 Undecylenic, and C-12 Lauric) in No 5 for Coco Chanel's first foray into scent. And, if I may be so bold as to name myself amongst these luminaries of our art, at an overdose of 0.3% I use it to add an amber sweetness to the French lavender top note of my perfume Porthos (2022).

Fun Fact: Madame Chanel offered No 5 as a free gift to her clients and customers but soon her shop was filled with Parisienne ladies clamouring (elegantly of course) to obtain just the scent. And so she popped on a price tag — $30 to be exact (equal to a jaw dropping $650 today) and the rest is history as the cliché goes.

This aliphatic aldehyde (one of only two not found in nature) transforms a scent in ways no other material can. The merest whisper in a blend creates olfactory pleasures beyond words. One drop and you have instant perfume. Alchemists dreamed of the transmutation of lead into gold. Aldehyde C-12 MNA performs just that powerful magic on aroma chemicals.

As with all true aldehydes, we recommend dilution in an alcohol upon receipt of this product. Ethyl al

products.name: Aldehyde C-7
products.description:
This material demonstrates the fundamental principle of aldehydic perfumery: power through dilution. Neat, it appears harsh and fatty with fermented fruit and wine-lees character. But diluted to 1% or less, it transforms into the quintessential aldehydic sparkle that revolutionised 20th-century perfumery.

The aldehydic lift effect is irreplaceable—it cuts through dense florals, resins, and animalic notes, making them feel lighter and more effervescent. This is the "rocket fuel" that launches fragrances from the bottle with that characteristic "whoosh." Its green, herbaceous, and ozonic facets provide freshness whilst the aldehydic power creates radiance.

Use this when you need to transform heavy compositions into something brilliant and sparkling. Essential for white florals like hyacinth and ylang-ylang, and perfect for creating that classic aldehydic bouquet when blended with other C8-C12 aldehydes. The key is extreme precision—overdosing creates harsh plastic effects.

products.name: Aldehyde C-8
products.description:
Aldehyde C-8 (Octanal) is intensely orange zest in scent and provides lift and natural citrus notes to fragrances. It is particularly helpful in functional fragrances when natural citrus oils may be too delicate for the base material.

Use tiny amounts to add a waxy and fresh quality to your top notes, or dose it slightly higher for a very distinctly orange character. 

As with all true aldehydes, we recommend dilution in an alcohol upon receipt of this product. Ethyl alcohol is the most commonly used for this purpose, but others such as phenyl ethyl alcohol or benzyl alcohol are also suitable.

products.name: Aldehyde C-9
products.description:
Aldehyde C-9 hits with immediate waxy brightness—fresh orange peel zest wrapped in a clean, fatty-floral haze. There is a distinctive rosy quality hiding beneath the citrus punch, almost like smelling a rose through a veil of orange blossom. It evaporates quickly but leaves a long lasting, lovely, petal-like impression on the skin.

This is your go-to material for aldehydic sparkle in top notes. A trace in rose compositions gives that unmistakable dewy, just-picked petal effect. In citrus accords it amplifies orange peel realism, and in jasmine, lily, or peony bases it adds the luminous bloom that makes the whole composition feel alive and lifted.

Handle aldehyde C-9 with care—it is powerful far beyond what a sniff from the bottle suggests. Work at well under one percent; even a fraction too much turns waxy and soapy.

products.name: Aldron®
products.description:
Aldron is a strange material. Some people can't smell it at all and some people (especially women) are repulsed by it when smelled pure. Why? No one really knows.

But in the right amounts in a blend, it has a power to naturalise and add musky elegance that is appreciated by all and really impossible to obtain with any other materials. It's particularly valuable in enhancing sandalwood and musk accords, as well as in woody, tobacco, musk, and incense blends.

It's definitely a quirky one but well worth the buy. For those who can smell it, the odour profile is animalic, woody, amber and musk (in the direction of sweaty human skin).

products.name: Allyl Anthranilate
products.description:
This is not your sweet fruit methyl anthranilate — it is the scary big brother! Allyl Anthranilate greets you with sharp, penetrating green-leaf intensity — far removed from the soft grape of its cousin Methyl Anthranilate. A bitter, almost almond-like bite cuts through immediately, metallic and arresting. Beneath that aggression hides unexpected floral warmth and heliotropin-like creaminess.

This is a modifier, not a standalone note. Trace additions bring realistic grape-skin astringency to fruity accords that would otherwise read as candy. It sharpens galbanum and violet leaf with metallic green bite, adding modern edge to compositions that feel too soft or botanical.

Dilute Allyl Anthranilate before evaluating — the neat material is overwhelmingly chemical. The creamy grape drydown only reveals itself at working concentrations. Blend with methyl anthranilate, heliotropin, and indole for narcissus accords, or with galbanum for sharp green-floral metalwork.

Like Methyl Anthranilate, Allyl Anthranilate is a primary amine and will form Schiff bases with aldehydes, resulting in increased substantivity and characteristic deepening of color. Out of interest, Allyl-Aurantiol (Hydroxycitronellal and Allyl Anthranilate) is more radiant than classic Aurantiol (Hydroxycitronellal and Methyl Anthranilate).

products.name: Allyl Cyclohexyl Propionate
products.description:
Allyl cyclohexyl propionate is the most convincing and long-lasting pineapple ester available. Sweet, tropical, and candy-like, it delivers ripe pineapple with green apple freshness and a surprising chamomile-like floral warmth underneath. Most fruity esters vanish in hours — this one persists for over a week on a blotter.

Use it to build tropical and exotic fruit accords that actually last in your compositions. It adds pineapple sweetness to fruity-floral hearts without disappearing before the drydown. A trace in chamomile recreations contributes authentic floral-fruity warmth you cannot get elsewhere.

Pair with other fruity esters for complex tropical blends. Try it alongside hedione and linalyl acetate for a fruity-fresh floral effect. Blend with Iso E Super and musk materials for a modern fruity-woody accord where the pineapple note carries all the way to the base.

products.name: Allyl Ionone
products.description:
Allyl Ionone is a unique and versatile ionone derivative with a floral-woody character and a fruity nuance. Its profile combines the powdery, violet-like facets typical of ionones with a subtly fresh and juicy note, making it indispensable for adding complexity to modern floral, fruity, and woody compositions. This material provides a dynamic lift and smooth diffusion, especially in the heart and base notes of a fragrance.

Allyl Ionone pairs beautifully with woody and powdery materials such as Iso E Super, cedarwood, and musk, creating a soft and diffusive effect. It also complements floral components like jasmine and rose, amplifying their luxurious qualities. For fruity blends, combining Allyl Ionone with notes like peach, raspberry, or apricot creates a playful yet refined result.

products.name: Almond Pyrazine
products.description:
Almond Pyrazine opens with explosive roasted intensity—imagine almonds crackling in a hot pan. This isn't the sweet marzipan of benzaldehyde but pure Maillard magic. Hazelnut and peanut facets emerge alongside smoky undertones, creating the authentic aroma of nuts transformed by heat.

This pyrazine requires extreme respect—we sell it as low as 0.1% in DPG but up to pure for those who need it. At parts-per-million levels, it transforms compositions with authentic roasted character. Deploy it in coffee reconstructions where its smoky-nutty profile completes the espresso illusion, or use it to add depth to chocolate accords beyond simple sweetness.

Master this material by starting at 0.0001% of your finished fragrance and building carefully. It excels when paired with coffee Arabica CO2 for ultra-realistic café effects, or combine with vanillin and ethyl maltol for sophisticated praline gourmands. The pyrazine's potency means a single drop can dominate—approach with caution and precision.

products.name: Alpha Angelica Lactone
products.description:
Alpha Angelica Lactone opens with sweet caramel warmth — immediately gourmand, with a creamy coconut undercurrent. Hay-like and nutty facets add complexity beyond simple sweetness. A distinctive tobacco-like quality emerges in the drydown, earthy and quietly addictive.

This is a remarkable fixative — tenacity on blotter exceeds two weeks at full strength. It occurs naturally in coffee, honey, and liquorice, and that natural pedigree shows in the rounded, believable sweetness. Use it to bring authentic caramel depth to tobacco, gourmand, and oriental compositions.

An interesting pro-tip from the flavor industry that translates perfectly to fine fragrance: it is used to "de-edge" mint. If you have a fragrance with a sharp Peppermint or Spearmint top note that feels too medicinal or "toothpaste-like," a trace of alpha-Angelica Lactone (even at 0.1%) will pull the mint into a "mint-chocolate" or "creamy herbal" direction without making it smell like a dessert.

Blend with coumarin and tonka bean absolute for rich, convincingly natural hay-sweet warmth. Try it alongside vanillin and ethyl maltol for caramel depth. The coconut facet makes it a surprisingly effective companion to tropical and solar floral compositions too.

products.name: Alpha Pinene
products.description:
Alpha-Pinene is the sharp blast of pine needles you get when you snap a fresh conifer branch — piercing, camphoraceous, and immediately resinous. It delivers extraordinary top-note diffusion, filling a room the moment you open the bottle. A warm turpentine undertone sits beneath the bracing, almost medicinal freshness.

Use Alpha-Pinene when you want the bracing, terpenic side of a fragrance front and centre — forest floor, mountain air, snapped pine branches. It gives coniferous accords their immediate blast of reality. Even a trace sharpens rosemary, sage, and juniper with an authenticity synthetic pine bases lack.

Blend Alpha-Pinene with camphene and limonene for a full turpentine reconstruction, or pair it with juniper berry and cedarwood for deep forest compositions. It sharpens aromatic fougères alongside lavender and rosemary. Use sparingly — its piercing top note dominates aggressively while present but fades fast.

Alpha-Pinene vs Beta-Pinene

Alpha and Beta-Pinene are closely related but smell and behave quite differently in a formula. Alpha is the sharper, more aggressive of the two — piercing pine-needle character with a camphoraceous edge, extremely volatile, and immediately impactful. Beta is softer, greener, and more woody-citrus, with a dry spicy-balsamic quality and none of Alpha's camphoraceous bite.

Alpha dominates in turpentine, rosemary, and sage; Beta is more prominent in lemon, lime, and nutmeg oils. In practice, Alpha provides the bracing blast that

products.name: Amarante
products.description:
Amarante is a beautifully balanced floral base that melds muguet, lilac, jasmin and rose notes with a soft woody dry down. Originally created by Marius Reboul for Givaudan in 1924, Amarante was popularised in the 1920s by Henri Almeras who loved it so much he used it in doses well beyond 30% in multiple fragrances for Jean Patou. Its presence can be felt profoundly in Amour Amour (1925).

This base is perfect as a core blender around which a distinctive character can be built with nuancers and high impact materials. Usable at up to 10% when seeking IFRA 51 compliance, this is a very versatile base.

Amarante is the epitome of classic French elegance.

products.name: Amaretto Saronno
products.description:
Amaretto is an Italian liqueur flavoured with the almond-scented kernels of apricots. The drink dates back to the town of Saronno in the 16th century and its true origin is unknown. In addition to apricot kernels, some recipes also add bitter almonds and peach kernels. Most importantly the drink is rounded off with a burnt sugar giving rise to its name ("amara" means bitter in Italian).

Our Amaretto Saronno base is a wonderfully boozy top note interpretation of the esteemed drink containing all its nuances and character. It can be used as an alternative almond / benzaldehyde note in a scent and we highly recommend blending it with Coconut Dream and Raspberry Ripple for a “wow” gourmand accord. It also blends incredibly well with Wild Cherry.

products.name: Amazonia™
products.description:
Amazonia™ is unspoiled nature distilled. It is the scent of rushing water, wild jungles, untrodden earth and fresh air. It is a boat ride down the Amazon river. If Werner Herzog's masterpiece Fitzcarraldo had a scent, this would be it.

Constructed around a combination of radiant and ultra-modern molecules (including Firmenich's Cascalone®), there is nothing old school about Amazonia™; this is pure modernism.

Use it as a completed scent with just a touch of musk added, or embellish it with woody molecules and a touch of floralisation as seen in our demonstration formula, Waterfall, below.

Amazonia™ blends extraordinarily well with Jasmolactone® Delta, Jasmin Fleurs, Aetoxylon Oil, Orcanox™ and Gardenia J. Ellis.

Demonstration Formula Details

Waterfall, a short demonstration formula, combines a simplified Grojsman accord with Cedramber® for a sheer wood effect, while Helional® extends and enhances the freshness of an overdose of Amazonia™. A light touch of Gardenia and Champaca Red Absolute adds an exotic floral nuance while MANE's Orcanox adds radiance and longevity and an incredibly modern ambergris note.

products.name: Amber Core
products.description:
Amber Core is a member of the amber family but unlike the most common ones (Ambrocenide, AmberXTreme, Hydroxyambran and Operanide) it is far softer and easier to work with. Try it as an alternative to the more common wood chemicals like Cedramber which it is similar to in terms of strength. Previously able to be overdosed massively, it is now under a 1.3% restriction in IFRA 51 which is still rather generous.

Amber Core blends beautifully with Operanide, Ambrocenide, florals (particularly light ones like Muguet and Lilac), and wood chemicals like Orbitone® T and Iso E Super. It is an excellent blender and is especially good at linking woods, amber and citrus materials.

Amber Core features in Amouage Interlude Black Iris (0.8%), Amouage Memoir Women (0.9%), Creed Royal Oud (0.08%), YSL La Nuit de L'Homme Bleu Électrique (11%), and Gucci Pour Homme (10%).

products.name: Amber Crave
products.description:
AMBER CRAVE® is a profoundly evocative neo-gourmand fragrance base masterfully created by esteemed perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the relentless allure of indulgence, AMBER CRAVE® transforms the amber accord into an intensely desirable scent experience—an olfactory narrative of insatiable hunger, comfort, and sweet obsession.

Top notes: Honey, Liquorice, Davana
Heart Notes: Beeswax, Lily of the Valley, Rose, Peach
Base notes: Myrrh, Patchouli, Tonka Bean, Benzoin, Vanilla, Ambergris

Scent Profile

AMBER CRAVE® unfurls with a luscious, irresistible blend of golden honey and sensuous liquorice, enriched by davana’s uniquely fruity, aromatic touch. At its sumptuous heart, beeswax imparts a warm, enveloping texture, harmoniously paired with delicate lily of the valley, romantic rose, and the ripe sweetness of peach. Anchored in a decadent base, AMBER CRAVE® rests on a bed of resinous myrrh, smoky patchouli, rich benzoin, creamy vanilla, luxurious tonka bean, and the subtle allure of ambergris, crafting a scent that embodies the moment when urgency turns into necessity.

Perfumery Usage

AMBER CRAVE® is expertly crafted to deliver remarkable intensity, warmth, and complexity, making it perfect as an enticing standalone fragrance base or as a sophisticated note within diverse fragrance compositions. Its rich, yet universally appealing gourmand character is designed to blend seamlessly with oriental ambers, luscious fruit accords, and luxuri

products.name: Amber Flux
products.description:
AMBER FLUX® is a daringly innovative neo-gourmand fragrance base expertly envisioned by esteemed perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Infused with contemporary dynamism and a luxurious oriental amber foundation, AMBER FLUX® reinvents the amber genre with electrifying intensity and a distinctly futuristic edge—where indulgent excess becomes sublime perfection.

Top Notes: Cedrat, Toffee, Star Anise
Heart Notes: Hibiscus, Magnolia, Metallic Notes
Base Notes: Super Amber, Patchouli, Tolu Balsam, Vanilla Bean

Scent Profile

AMBER FLUX® bursts forth with an exhilarating opening of sparkling cedrat infused with molten toffee, enlivened by star anise's captivating warmth. At its vibrant heart, lush hibiscus and radiant magnolia blend masterfully with innovative metallic notes, imparting a luminous, forward-thinking allure. A luxurious base of super amber harmonises seamlessly with velvety patchouli, rich tolu balsam, and creamy vanilla bean, crafting an opulent, futuristic gourmand fragrance that pulses with vibrant energy and sophisticated indulgence.

Perfumery Usage

Formulated to deliver outstanding projection, longevity, and complexity, AMBER FLUX® excels as a luxurious standalone neo-gourmand fragrance base or as a dynamic enhancer in contemporary compositions. Its uniquely modern profile blends flawlessly with vibrant citrus accords, sophisticated floral materials, experimental metallic nuances, and avant-garde synthetic ambers—allowing perfumers to inn

products.name: Amber Genesis
products.description:
AMBER GENESIS® is a luxurious neo-gourmand fragrance base masterfully composed by renowned perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the timeless allure of classical amber bases reimagined through a contemporary lens, this fragrance invites you into a decadent world where temptation becomes tangible. Rich labdanum, velvety vanilla, and opulent rum intertwine elegantly, offering a modern interpretation of the globally coveted amber profile—an olfactory overture to refined indulgence.

Top notes: Rum, Caramel, Red Fruit
Heart notes: Lily of the Valley, Egyptian Geranium
Base notes: Vanilla Bean, Vetiver, Patchouli, Tonka Bean, Labdanum

Scent Profile

AMBER GENESIS® opens with a provocative introduction of lush dark rum, splashed upon ripe red fruits draped in silken caramel. At its heart, the soft purity of lily of the valley elegantly complements Egyptian geranium, delivering refined floral clarity. Gradually, the fragrance transitions into a sumptuous base, harmonising sweet vanilla bean, deep vetiver, earthy patchouli, comforting tonka bean, and resinous labdanum. The result is a fragrance of captivating warmth, embodying an irresistible, sophisticated temptation.

Perfumery Usage

AMBER GENESIS® is meticulously formulated to deliver exceptional longevity, depth, and complexity, ideal both as a foundational base and as a sophisticated enhancer within modern fragrance compositions. Its versatile neo-gourmand character blends effortlessly with com

products.name: Ambergris Intense™
products.description:
The heart of our Absolute Ambergris™, we are now making available the pure resin for those who need to go a step further into intensely animalic territory.

This product is strong. Incredibly so. It is the most intense ambergris product we sell and the one most like classic aged pure ambergris resin - you would treat this as you would a resinoid made from pure ambergris.

Dilute it as you would civet absolute in terms of power for making tinctures, or dose it as is in a fragrance that is bold enough to handle it.

Animalic this may be, but it is also one of the most strangely beautiful odours you will ever smell.

products.name: Ambergris Tincture 2%
products.description:
It seems almost too good to be true but it isn't! This is a deluxe natural grey ambergris tincture that goes against the norm by being a mainstay of our specialist supplier's catalogue. Through a very long relationship with local ambergris gatherers in New Caledonia, this is a readily available material.

Ambergris tincture is marine and animalic with fecal qualities. It's ability to fix (to make something last longer) a perfume is historically renowned and despite its origins as a pathological metabolite of sperm whales which are considered endangered, this is not restricted in perfumery (though some countries do have restrictions on importing the product).

While no hard and fast rule ever existed to determine the right amount of tincture to use in a perfume, we recommend around 1% – 3% of the total weight in alcohol. so 100 grams (or mls or drops) of alcohol will have 1–3 grams (or ml or drops) of Ambergris Tincture 2% added. Bear in mind that you can add significantly more tincture if you wish, particularly if you wish to have the ambergris easily perceptible in odour rather than simply as a fixative.

If you are seeking a vegan alternative to Ambergris tincture we recommend our acclaimed Ambergris Intense or Absolute Ambergris™ products.

products.name: Ambermax® 50
products.description:
Givaudan positions Ambermax as "the most powerful and efficient dry ambery note ever". It opens with an arresting dry woodiness that shoots straight through any composition like a cedar arrow. The material presents that coveted pencil-shaving character but stripped of natural cedar's rough edges. This transparent amber effect creates remarkable vertical lift in your formulas. It also excels with citrus materials, adding depth without dulling brightness.

The extreme potency means a little goes very far; overdosing creates the "spiky wood" effect common to super ambers. Blend with Karanal, Okoumal, Z11, and woody-amber materials for sophisticated bases. Layer it with Ambrox to balance its trigeminal sharpness with creamy warmth. Remember this material causes rapid nose fatigue, so take breaks when evaluating your trials.

products.name: AmberXtreme
products.description:
AmberXtreme opens with an explosive woody-amber blast that fills space instantly. Its musky-animalic character creates warmth whilst grape-anthranilate facets add subtle fruitiness. This molecule radiates with unprecedented power, perceivable below 0.1% concentration.

You'll find this material essential for modern masculine fragrances where projection and longevity define success. It excels as a volume booster in woody and fougère bases, transforming linear compositions into radiant statements. Use it sparingly—even 0.01% creates noticeable aura whilst higher doses risk overwhelming entire accords.

Blend AmberXtreme with Iso E Super and Cashmeran for the legendary Cashmeran Velvet effect. Combine with Ambrettolide for enhanced musk complexity or pair with Ambroxan for marine-amber depth. This powerhouse performs brilliantly in detergents where its stability ensures lasting freshness.

Comparison with Operanide and Ambrocenide

AmberXtreme sits between Operanide's creamy softness and Ambrocenide's sharp aggression in the radiant amber family. Where Operanide offers controllable mossy-cedar elegance and Ambrocenide delivers piercing agarwood dryness, AmberXtreme provides balanced woody-amber power with animalic warmth. Choose AmberXtreme for maximum diffusion, Operanide for sophisticated heart notes, or Ambrocenide for cutting-edge sharpness.

products.name: Amboryl Acetate
products.description:
Amboryl Acetate opens with a fleeting acetate sparkle that quickly settles into its true character—a remarkably soft woody-amber that sidesteps the harsh dryness plaguing many synthetic ambers. This sesquiterpenoid acetate brings together the smooth, refined woodiness of vetiveryl acetate with sandalwood's creamy richness. You'll detect subtle hints of clary sage's aromatic sweetness woven through it also.

This material excels where others fail in functional perfumery, maintaining its sophisticated character through aggressive product bases that destroy lesser ingredients. Its 280-hour tenacity on blotter translates to genuine lasting power in detergents, fabric softeners, and personal care products. Deploy it at 5-15% in functional bases where you need amber sophistication without the luxury price tag—it transforms mundane household products into olfactory experiences worth remembering.

Fine fragrance perfumers overlook this gem at their peril, dismissing it as merely functional when it offers unique bridging qualities between top and heart accords. Use it at up to 50% in your base to create woody-amber foundations with unusual softness and powdery nuance. Combine with Iso E Super for enhanced diffusion or layer with natural sandalwood to amplify creamy facets without breaking the budget. Its acetate functionality provides superior adhesion to skin and fabric, ensuring your creation maintains its character from first spray to final dry-down.

products.name: Ambra Velvet
products.description:
Ambra Velvet captures that precious velvety quality of fine aged ambergris—smooth, warm, and unmistakably luxurious. The amber character sits at the heart, rich without being cloying. Subtle animalic undertones provide the complexity that separates true ambergris effects from simple synthetic alternatives.

This classic base has anchors fine fragrances, filling the void left by increasingly scarce and prohibitively expensive natural ambergris. The composition brings together natural animal musks with key ambergris molecules including ambrox, providing radiance and woody warmth—together creating a complete ambergris impression that rounds out fragrances in a way that purely synthetic ambergris replacers can't.

Use Ambra Velvet as the foundation for oriental compositions or as a sophisticated fixative in florals and woody blends. It works beautifully from the smallest traces, adding depth and tenacity without overwhelming. The velvety smoothness makes it particularly valuable when you need ambergris warmth without harsh edges.

products.name: Ambranum
products.description:
A rich, complex amber compound offering exquisite depth and radiance in perfumery applications. This sophisticated specialty base combines vanillin's sweet warmth with Peru balsam's resinous character, creating a full-bodied amber that enhances compositions with its remarkable persistence and dimension.

Ambranum provides the perfect foundation for oriental, woody and amber fragrances, adding both complexity and longevity. Its balanced profile works beautifully with labdanum, vanilla, and woody notes, making it an exceptional building block for distinctive signature scents while ensuring excellent performance in fine fragrance applications.

If you like this product you'll love our own Ambre Royal which is extremely similar in profile but enriched with luxurious natural oils and absolutes.

Ambranum makes a great foundation material and works very well with the following: Ginger Oil, Vetikolacetat, Rose Oxide Laevo, Ylang Ylang Extra, Veticoeur and many more.

products.name: Ambrarome®
products.description:
Ambrarome (also known as Ambrarome Absolute) is one of the oldest bases still made and sold by the same company that created it (Synarome). It was created in 1926 by Hubert Fraysse (co-founder of the company with his brother George) and was key to Arpège, created his brother André Fraysse who was the chief perfumer of Lanvin.

Ambrarome is an intensely animalic base with a strong character of ambergris, noble labdanum fractions and aspects of leather. In fact, it was the first speciality product designed to replicate the then-already expensive ambergris. It was followed later by specialities from competing companies such as Grisambrol and Grisambrene by Firmenich.

François Coty loved Ambrarome so much that upon smelling it for the first time that he reformulated his great Chypre to include it (and at the same time removed Musk Ambrette and increased the Musk Ketone).

Due to the thickness and odour strength of this material we are offering it at 50% diluted in TEC as well as pure.

products.name: Ambre Aegyptus
products.description:
Ambre Aegyptus is the scent of Ancient Egypt. Weave a magical tale of Ancient Egypt into the fabric of your fragrances with this beautiful modern amber base. Constructed around a heart of intensely sweet vanilla tempered with exotic mandarin and crowned with rare herbs and precious oriental resins, this amber is a fragrant treasure. Dazzling white musks meld with the latest radiant wood molecules in perfect balance with luscious Mysore sandalwood, sweet patchouli and aged cedarwood. Jasmine absolute from the grand Nile Delta recalls the anointing of the king-gods as they were laid to rest in the gilded tombs of the ancient city of the dead: Abydos.

Use Ambre Aegyptus alone in overdose as a more beautiful and interesting version of Ambre Sultan by Serge Lutens, or use it as the foundation of a magnificent modern oriental fragrance needing little more than a tweak in a novel direction. Usable at a whopping 25.37% of your finished product.

“The only lamp of this lone hour
Is glimmering in Zuleika's tower.
Yes! there is light in that lone chamber,
And o'er her silken Ottoman
Are thrown the fragrant beads of amber,
O'er which her fairy fingers ran; 
Near these, with emerald rays beset,
(How could she thus that gem forget?)
Her mother's sainted amulet, 
Whereon engraved the Koorsee text,
Could smooth this life, and win the next;” 
— The Bride of Abydos, by Lord Byron, 1813.

products.name: Ambre Doux
products.description:
A delicate liquid amber base first created by Roure in the 1930s and used in Tabu. This is a light and airy amber based on labdanum and vanilla notes without the characteristic dominance of citrus making it a wonderful fixative and enricher of those more common ambers such as Ambreine Samuelson and Opoponax Doux.

The sheer nature of this amber makes it decidedly modern and it can most certainly be used easily in that context. Pair with Ambre Royale in overdose with sweet notes of ethyl hydrocinnamate, phenyl propyl alcohol and ethyl safranate.

products.name: Ambre Royal
products.description:
Supremely beautiful, Ambre Royal is a modern amber base built around vanilla, citrus, resins and woods. It can be used in small amounts to impart a wonderfully sweet dry down or in overdose for a novel new take on an oriental scent.

Ambre Royal contains radiant modern musks and luxurious aged naturals woods and floral absolutes. This base is essential for all perfumers — it is a fragrance unto itself. Safe at up to 100% of the finished product!

products.name: Ambre Solide (Ambre 83)
products.description:
Ambre Solide is a classical amber fixative base built around resins and vanilla with an intensely floral note dominated by floral absolutes, including jasmine and rose, and civet. Depending on environmental conditions, Ambre Solide is a solid paste or highly viscous liquid. It can be added directly to your formulas or diluted — we recommend 50% in DEP.

This is the original Ambre 83 Solide of De Laire which was used in Chanel No 5 in combination with Ambreol, a balsamic vanilla base. It was also used by Ernest Beaux in Bois des Îles and by Jean Carles in Miss Dior.

Due to the high content of the permitted purified musk ketone, this product can be used at up to 7% of your finished product in Europe and 40% in other countries for compliance with IFRA.

NOTE: This product contains no musk xylene or other prohibited materials.

products.name: Ambreine Biolandes
products.description:
A thick, honeyed amber opens with warm balsamic sweetness before revealing a smoky leather undertone and faint olibanum dryness. The overall impression is of something ancient and precious — amber that glows rather than shouts. Viscous and deeply comforting on the blotter.

Where labdanum absolute can overwhelm a formula, this extract channels the same raw material into a more refined, focused amber impression. Oriental accords take on a darker, more sensual foundation. Your leather and incense compositions gain a complexity from this extract that sets it apart from standard labdanum absolute.

Low doses in a chypre or fougere furnish amber warmth without tipping the balance. Go full oriental by stacking it with benzoin resinoid, vanilla absolute, frankincense and myrrh for a sacred resin effect. The smoky-sweet facet also grounds oud compositions that need a softer anchor.

Owing to its thickness we sell this pure and diluted to 50% in natural TEC, making it easier to use when working in natural perfumery.

NOTE: This is a specialty extract of labdanum by Biolandes and should not be confused with Ambreine Samuelson (and the natural variant of the same) which is a historic base of citrus, resins and vanilla.

products.name: Ambreine Natural
products.description:
100% Natural and ISO 9235 compliant. The famed Ambreine Samuelson base back from the golden age to add beauty and opulence to your perfumes — but now all natural! Fraterworks Ambreine is loaded with Mysore sandalwood, resins and pure oils and absolutes.

Ambreine type bases are rich base notes built on a harmony of citrus oils, vanilla, resins and woods.

Ambreine Natural by Fraterworks in traces, adds a balsamic warmth to a scent's dry down and in overdose it imparts a wonderful ambery quality felt through the whole life of the fragrance.

This is a perfume unto itself. Beloved by Messrs Coty and Guerlain, it can now be part of your creative toolkit.

This version is 100% natural, being composed entirely of luxurious essential oils, absolutes and certified natural isolates. Just floralise and add unadulterated ethanol to have a complete 100% natural fragrance!

For the standard version, go here.

NOTE: This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris.

products.name: Ambreine Rustica
products.description:
This is the marvelous agrestical ambreine base used at over 40% of the total formula of Coty's last perfume La Fougeraie au Crépuscule (formula below named Twilight Fern). Whilst most ambers focus solely on the resinous and vanilla qualities, this base places a stronger emphasis on the herbal notes. This is the closest thing you will get to a top note ambreine base.

This base is loaded with Mysore sandalwood, natural tonka bean and many other absolutes and oils.

If you're not sure which amber base or bases you need, take a look at our handy guide to understanding ambers.

NOTE: This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris.

products.name: Ambreine Samuelson
products.description:
The famed Ambreine Samuelson base back from the past to add beauty and opulence to your perfumes! Fraterworks Ambreine Sameulson (formerly known simply as "Ambreine") is loaded with Mysore sandalwood and pure oils and absolutes.

Ambreine type bases are rich base notes built on a harmony of citrus oils, vanilla, resins and woods.

In traces Ambreine adds a balsamic warmth to a scent's dry down and in overdose it imparts a wonderful ambery quality felt through the whole life of the fragrance.

Ambreine by Fraterworks is a perfume unto itself. Beloved by Messrs Coty and Guerlain, it can now be part of your creative toolkit. This base is also similar to the other great ambreine type base Coralys. This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris.

We also have a 100% natural and vegan version of this base which is available here.

NOTE: This product may partially crystallise at low temperatures. Gently heat prior to use.

products.name: Ambreol
products.description:
Ambreol was a classical vanilla base, similar to Ambreine Samuelson (our Ambreine) and Opoponax Doux but with a pronounced vanilla note. In overdose and balanced with Sephora (our Sophira base), it was the key of Tabac Blond and was a vital component of both Bois des Iles and Chanel No 5.

Fraterworks' restored Ambreol is rich with mysore sandalwood, natural vanilla, tonka bean absolute and many resins and essential oils. IFRA safe at up to 17.7% of the finished product.

products.name: Ambretone®
products.description:
Ambretone® is more famously known as Velvione® by Givaudan but what most perfumers don't know is that Ambretone came first and is the superior quality of Velvione®. While Velvione® is pure Cyclohexadecen-5-one, Velvione also contains some Cyclohexadecen-6-one which, in my opinion, reduces its power and beauty.

Ambretone® is a macrocyclic musk that behaves similarly to dextro-Muscenone (the captive pure form of Muscenone) and finds applications in very much the same areas. Ambretone®, however, is less animalic and has nuances of ambrette seed. A particular radiance occurs when blending Ambretone with genuine Hedione®.

Ambretone® makes up fully 8.5% of Carnal Flower by Frederic Malle.

Ambretone® is also closely related to the cheaper Globanone (Cyclohexadec-8-en-1-one), which is slightly less animal and, in my opinion, less elegant.

This product is often solid at room temperature and requires a slight amount of warming to liquify.

products.name: Ambrette Seed Oil
products.description:
The seeds of this hibiscus-like flowering plant contain one of the treasures of the perfumery world: ambrettolide — one of the few natural non-animal musks. With a delicate raspberry nuance, this rich oil adds softness, muskiness, and radiance to every blend. A trace can completely remove the chemical sharpness from alcohol making it a wonderful alternative to Ambergris.

Our Ambrette Seed Oil is manufactured in France by LMR, one of the finest makers and suppliers of precious essential oils and absolutes.

There is no denying that you'll need a swooning couch when you see the price tag on this beauty! Therefore, we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, keeping it ISO 9235 compliant and making it more cost effective.

Origin: France
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Ambrette Seed Tincture 20%
products.description:
Being one of the few natural plant musks, ambrette seed is absolutely essential for perfumers and those seeking all natural or vegan musks. But it comes at a very hefty price tag.

In classical perfumery another option existed, one very often overlooked today: tincture of ambrette seed. For a significantly lower cost you get all the smoothing and fixing power of ambrette seeds.

Ambrette Seed Tincture 20% is pale yellow in colour and very light in scent, but don't be fooled, its magic is not in its smell, but in the fact it contains natural ambrettolide, one of the most diffusive and powerful musks in modern perfumery.

As with all our tinctures, this is made with 100% pure and natural alcohol produced with glacial waters from the Southern Alps. The absence of denaturants allow this to be used in natural perfumery, both EU and US standards.

products.name: Ambrettolide
products.description:
Ambrettolide (more accurately Iso Ambrettolide) is incredibly popular owing, in large part, to its astonishing ability to soften the edges of alcohol. In traces it has powerful fixative properties and in overdose it contributes a lovely soft red fruit nuance (though some people may have difficulty smelling it due to the size of the molecules). If you could only ever possess two musks, they would be Exaltolide® (from Firmenich) and Ambrettolide (from IFF).

This IFF quality possesses a sweeter and more pronounced musk note to the Givaudan type making it our preferred version.

According to Arctander: “[Ambrettolide] is one of the finest fixatives among the distinguished group of those showing a synergistic and amplifying effect upon perfumes and flavors. At the same time it increases the diffusiveness of fragrances in which it is incorporated. Its fixative effect is easily recognized by the fact that solutions of 0.01% Ambrettolide (or even less) in slightly diluted alcohol show practically no odor of alcohol, only a faint, floral-musky, sweet and pleasant odor of the lactone. Ambrettolide is particularly useful in fragrance types of delicately floral, mildly animal or Ambre-like type.”

products.name: Ambrexol™
products.description:
Ambrexol features the addictive and subtly animalic sweetness of long aged wild ambergris. Once you smell this amazing product, you'll want to add it to everything.

 Ambrexol™ is an alternative to the old Fixateur® 404 product of Firmenich® which was temporarily replaced by a dilution of racemic Cetalox® under the new code name of Fixateur 505. Ambrexol is softer and less animalic (though it does still maintain a soft animal warmth).

Fraterworks Ambrexol™ pairs the nearest equivalent of ambrox classique with traces of supporting materials to honour the power and magical effect of Fixateur with a more rounded scent of ambergris.

Just a touch is all that's needed to turn any blend into a perfume.

products.name: Ambrinol 95
products.description:
Ambrinol is one of perfumery's most formidable amber ingredients. It delivers extraordinary projection alongside remarkable tenacity in finished compositions. It has the ability to transform ordinary accords into compelling, memorable statements and its provocative animalic undertones evoke primal responses in wearers.

This Ambrinol is the finest we have tested owing to its particularly high purity (greater than 96% Alpha Ambrinol).

Ambrinol must be deployed with surgical precision in minute quantities as even trace amounts produce dramatic effects. Its multifaceted character bridges traditional amber accords with contemporary minimalist structures.

Apply ambrinol at 0.2-1% concentration in final formulations. This material strengthens woody accords and adds realistic amber depth. Combine with vanillin, labdanum, and cedarwood for amplified warmth and richness in oriental compositions.

products.name: Ambrocenide Crystals
products.description:
