Ambrocenide is a woody amber chemical with a radiance almost impossible to believe. It can be used in the merest traces to add elegance and power but it also works surprisingly well in overdose (as evidenced by the Amrita demonstration formula below - Millennium Mysore Sandal Soap).

We sell Ambrocenide as pure crystals or in a 10% solution with DPG making it easier to handle.

According to Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine): “Ambrocenide is the best discovery in the amber-woody family […] since Ambrox was commercialised. The top note of Ambrocenide is radiant, diffusive, elegant, ambery, woody—indeed both precious, and unique.”

Blends with Absolute Ambergris, Sandexol, Miraclewood, Iso E Super, Norlimbanol Dextro, Z11 MIP, Cetonal, the ionones and, in truth, almost everything.
tags: locale:use gentle heat to dissolve crystals in diluted version only

products.name: Ambrofix™ (Ambroxan)
products.description:
Givaudan's Ambrofix™ crystals are currently the finest form of classic Ambrox / Ambroxan on the market — very nearly identical to the superior captive Firmenich's ”Ambrox Classique“ used in Aventus and numerous other high class fragrances. Ambrofix is the most beautiful smelling version of this woody ambergris chemical, far surpassing in radiance and beauty all others, including Ambroxan® (Kao) and Ambrox Super (Firmenich).

Ambrofix has the scent of luxury wood, clean laundry, ambergris and old paper. Furthermore, this product is biodegradable and 100% naturally derived, however synthetics are used during the manufacturing process so this is not considered a natural product. The search for the perfect ambroxan ends here.

If you want to replicate Creed's Aventus or Escentric Molecules' Molecule 02 this is the chemical that will get you closest.

Ambrofix 10% Fluide

Due to popular demand we are now selling a 10% solution of Ambrofix. Ambrofix 10% Fluide uses a very special blend of diluents to ensure complete solubility of the Ambrofix crystals and stability at all temperatures. That means it remains mobile even when stored in the refrigerator!

Other Varieties

We also stock Orcanox™, the V. MANE Fils version of Ambroxan taking the world by storm.

NOTE: Ambrofix, ambroxan, Ambrox®, Ambrox Super, and ambroxide are synonyms. They are simply different trade names for the same chemical though produced through different processes.

products.name: Ambroxan® Crystals
products.description:
Ambroxan is probably the most popular chemical in perfumes today. It has progressed from being dosed at 10% via the classic Fixateur base of Firmenich to being the central wood / amber material in many fragrances.

Admired by many perfumers for its warm, musky-amber scent and lasting depth, it was originally developed to mimic the fragrance of natural ambergris, but has since become valued for its stable and powerful diffusion. Ambroxan adds richness, helps with projection, and acts as a strong anchor that lingers on the skin. Its dry amber quality can also enhance or extend other notes in a composition, giving a perfume both lift and persistence without overpowering more delicate ingredients.

This version is our specially selected non-branded type, chosen for its wonderful sweetness and clarity but also its amazing price. This comes in flakes and is much nicer than any generic ambrox we've smelled.

We also stock Orcanox™, the V. MANE Fils version of Ambroxan taking the world by storm, Firmenich's Ambrox® Super and Givaudan's wonderful Ambrofix.

NOTE: Ambrofix, ambroxan, Ambrox®, Ambrox Super, and ambroxide are synonyms. They are simply different trade names for the same chemical though produced through different processes.

products.name: Ambrox® DL
products.description:
When is Ambrox® not Ambrox? When it's Ambrox DL! Ambrox DL is a Firmenich product which blends around 30% captive Cachalox® with 70% Cetalox (9-epi Ambrox). 

While most Ambrox on the market (Ambrox Super, Ambrofix, Orcanox, Ambroxan) is Laevo-ambrox, Cetalox is the racemic version and has a more linear, clean dry wood character. It is subtler and less diffusive than Ambrox and it has less tendency to overwhelm other light materials. Laevo-Ambrox will give a richer, warmer and more intense result than Cetalox but Cetalox, on the other hand, can sometimes be perceived as more elegant.

The other part of Ambrox DL is Cachalox, which is related to but has a weaker odour than Laevo-Ambrox. It does, however, have heightened fixative and diffusive properties. Ambrox DL is often a solid or pasty thick liquid at room temperature and some heat (typically hotter than tap or faucet hot) may be needed to loosen it up for pipetting.

Notable as an example of oriental style perfumery, Areej Al Shouk by Ajmal uses just over 1% Ambrox® DL to boost the rich woody notes whilst giving lift to the tonkin deer fond (a blend of Muscenone® Delta and Muscone Laevo) and sparkle to the florals.

Some other perfumes that incorporate Ambrox® DL are Not A Perfume (2010) by Juliette Has A Gun in which it is the only ingredient, Interlude Black Iris (2020) by Pierre Negrin for Amouage, Patchouli Absolu (2014) by Richard Herpin, Neroli Portofino (2011) by Rodrigo Flores-Roux and Tobacco Vanille (2007) by Ol

products.name: Ambrox® Super
products.description:
Ambroxan (all types) have the scent of luxury wood, clean laundry, ambergris and old paper. While we prefer Ambrofix from Givaudan, the Ambrox Super variant from Firmenich is probably the most popular globally due to its close relationship with the captive “Ambrox Classique” used in Aventus by Creed. Ambrox Classique is also by Firmenich but remains a captive to this day. Ambrox Super and Givaudan's Ambrofix are the nearest in quality on the public market.

We also stock Orcanox™, the V. MANE Fils version of Ambroxan taking the world by storm and the marvellous Ambrofix™ from Givaudan which is our personal favourite.

NOTE: Ambrofix, ambroxan, Ambrox®, Ambrox Super, and ambroxide are synonyms. They are simply different trade names for the same chemical though produced through different processes.

products.name: Amyl Acetate
products.description:
Amyl acetate smells of fresh, ripe pear and green apple — clean, ethereal, and bright. It is lighter and more pear-forward than its better-known cousin isoamyl acetate, which leans more toward banana. At high concentrations there is a solvent-like quality, but in traces it delivers pure, sparkling fruit.

Use amyl acetate at very low levels to add fruity lift and sparkle to your top notes. A trace in oriental and floral compositions creates an airy brightness without any obvious fruitiness. It pairs naturally with white florals and aquatic notes, boosting freshness and diffusion.

Other fruity esters, hedione, and linalool are its natural companions. Less is always more here — this is a top note modifier, not a core building block. A fraction of a per cent is often enough to introduce that airy, pear-like sparkle without anyone being able to identify what you have done.

products.name: Amyl Benzoate
products.description:
Amyl Benzoate is a lovely soft fruity floral material with balsamic nuances that works extremely well as a general floraliser and blender.

It isn't exploited much in modern fragrances but it really should be as it is quite distinctive and there is great potential to create novel accords with it. Its fruity aspects make it ideal for honeysuckle and sweet pea fantasy blends and it can be used at a very high dose in a fragrance as it is IFRA safe to 100%.

products.name: Amyl Cinnamic Aldehyde
products.description:
Amyl cinnamal aldehyde delivers a gentle, oily-sweet jasmine character that fills a room without ever shouting. The first impression is soft and floral with a slight fruity warmth—think ripe apricot wrapped in jasmine petals. A faint powdery spiciness sits underneath, giving the material a rounded, natural quality.

This is one of perfumery's true workhorses. It anchors jasmine accords and white floral bases from gardenia to tuberose, and its alkali stability makes it equally at home in fine fragrance and soap. Use it to soften rough edges in compositions heavy with synthetic florals—it rounds off sharpness from benzyl acetate and methyl anthranilate beautifully.

Push amyl cinnamal aldehyde to higher doses for a lush, enveloping floral blanket, or use it at trace levels as a quiet fixative that extends the life of lighter notes. It performs brilliantly across alcoholic perfumes, shampoos, body care, and household products. One of those materials you should always have on your bench.

Amyl vs Hexyl Cinnamal Aldehyde

These two are close relatives—hexyl cinnamal simply has one extra carbon in its chain. In practice, the hexyl version leans sweeter, more overtly floral, and slightly waxy, making it the preferred choice for jasmine bases.

Amyl cinnamal aldehyde is fresher, oilier, and feels more natural, but does not last quite as long. Many perfumers use both together, finding that neither alone gives the full picture. Think of amyl as the brighter, more natural sibling and he

products.name: Amyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
Amyl phenyl acetate opens with a distinctive green-honeyed sweetness that feels immediately natural and inviting. A soft rosy character develops underneath, joined by fruity hints of ripe apple and a balsamic warmth. The overall effect is gentler and greener than you might expect from the phenylacetate family.

This material earns its keep in hyacinth accords, where it bridges the gap between sharp green top notes and rosy floral hearts with remarkable smoothness. It brings a honeyed, almost gourmand quality that sets it apart from other green-rosy materials like Phenoxanol or Rosacetol. Use it in rose compositions where you want naturalness and warmth rather than clinical precision.

Add amyl phenyl acetate to floral-balsamic and oriental bases for sweet, honeyed depth. It pairs well with phenyl ethyl alcohol for rounded rose effects and with galbanum or violet leaf for green-floral contrasts. Unrestricted and stable across applications, it works in fine fragrance, soap, and cosmetics alike.

Amyl vs Isoamyl

Do not confuse this with its positional isomer, isoamyl phenyl acetate (CAS 102-19-2), which is a very different material—darker, more chocolatey, and more animalic. This straight-chain amyl version is greener, lighter, and more honeyed. They are not interchangeable.

products.name: Amyl Salicylate
products.description:
When Fougère Royale launched as the first perfume with synthetics in 1889, it wasn't just coumarin that made it popular: it also contained amyl salicylate and a number of other synthetics.

Amyl Salicylate is the classic orchid and clover synthetic. Orchids are mostly (but not always) odourless and in the golden age of perfumery the master noses decided that if orchids had a smell, it would be this. Accented with rose alcohols, anisic aldehyde and acetophenone, most classic bases relied on rather large doses. Poucher has one such base in his formulary with a whopping 50% amyl salicylate though he preferred Isobutyl Salicylate if it were available.

Here is his complete Orchid No 1085:

500 Amyl Salicylate
200 Anisic Aldehyde
100 Geraniol Extra
50 Acetophenone (perhaps too much for modern tastes)
50 Rosewood oil (substitute Rosewood Cayenne base)
2 Benzaldehyde
50 Peru Balsam
3 Aldehyde C-9
10 Dimethyl Hydroquinone (found naturally in violet flowers)
35 Heliotropin

He accents the above with orange blossom, cassie and jasmine absolute.

Aside from Houbigant's Fougère Royale (1882), Amyl Salicylate was featured in a huge overdose in the great Pompeia (1907) by Piver. Both demo formulas can be found below.

products.name: Amyris Alcohol
products.description:
Amyris Alcohol (also known as Amyrol) is the pure heart of Amyris oil. It has a softer and sweeter quality than the essential oil (from Amyris balsamifera) and can be used one for one wherever Amyris is used. 

Amyrol is particularly good for sandalwood accords or fragrances needing a high dose of natural wood materials that don't impart too strong a character of their own. It is well suited to modern fragrances that like to represent naturals in a more abstract or minimal way, just as Patchoulol and Olibanol do the same for Patchouli notes and Olibanum respectively.

Amyris Alcohol blends beautifully with Sandexol®, Sandalwood Imperial, Rose products and woods.

products.name: Amyris “Signature” Oil, Haiti
products.description:
Amyris wood oil (often colloquially referred to as West Indian Sandalwood and historically as santal citron) is a soft creamy wood oil which frequently finds itself at the heart of Sandalwood recreations alongside Guaiacwood oil and cedarwood oil.

But it should not be seen as a replacer oil because in its own right it has a beautiful rich complexity which blends with all the usual modern wood chemicals like Orbitone, Iso E Super and the ambers and super ambers.

Our Amyris is particularly elegant and smooth, coming from a single origin harvest in Haiti by Payan Bertrand a company we hold in the highest esteem when it comes to naturals.

Note: Owing to scarcity of supply, the cost of Amyris oil has recently increased significantly.

products.name: Andrane
products.description:
Andrane opens with a structured cedarwood character that quickly reveals an earthy, patchouli-like depth and a distinctive dry ambergris quality. There is subtle tobacco warmth in the background. The overall impression is of a precious, aged wood — complex, noble, and extremely tenacious, lasting for days on a blotter.

Use andrane to add woody-amber depth and earthiness to your orientals, chypres, and masculine compositions. It modifies and extends patchouli accords beautifully, adding a cleaner, more structured framework. In cedarwood blends it contributes an ambergris-like dryness that elevates the entire accord.

Pair with patchouli and vetiver for a rich, earthy woody base. Try it alongside ambroxan and sandalwood for modern amber-wood accords. Blend with Iso E Super and cashmeran for a contemporary, transparent woody heart with lasting power.

products.name: Anethole ex Star Anise
products.description:
Anethole greets you with unmistakable licorice warmth—sweet, herbaceous, and deeply comforting. Unlike harsh synthetic alternatives, this natural isolate from star anise delivers a mellow, almost root beer-like quality. The balsamic undertone adds richness, while subtle woody facets provide grounding depth that lingers beautifully.

Use anethole to build authentic licorice and anise accords in oriental compositions. It adds unexpected warmth to mimosa and certain white florals. The famous ouzo effect—where anise spirits turn cloudy when diluted with water—occurs because anethole dissolves in alcohol but not water. Blend with fennel, basil, tarragon, and warm spices for complex herbaceous effects.

products.name: Angel
products.description:
Compound Angel is our internal formula for the original 1992 Angel by Thierry Mugler – not the later reformulations. Created by Olivier Cresp and Yves de Chiris at Quest International, this is the fragrance that invented the modern gourmand: an amber vanilla built on an unprecedented overdose of patchouli against caramel, praline and chocolate.

This compound reproduces the original composition as it was launched, before successive reformulations thinned the patchouli and flattened the sweetness. The base is dense and earthy, wrapped in vanilla, tonka bean, caramel and chocolate, with the maltol lift that made the original so instantly recognisable. The top notes of bergamot, mandarin, cassis and cotton candy open with an almost edible sugar rush, while a heart of honey, red berries, blackberry, plum, peach and apricot sits over jasmine, rose and lily-of-the-valley. The result is a monumental, unapologetically divisive fragrance with enormous projection and legendary longevity – exactly as it smelled in 1992.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Because it contains Lilial, it is not EU compliant.

Top Notes: Bergamot, Mandarin Orange, Cassis, Melon, Coconut, Cotton Candy, Jasmine
Heart Notes: Honey, Red Berries, Blackberry, Plum, Apricot, Peach, Nutmeg, Caraway, Rose, Lily-of-the-Valley, Orchid
Base Notes: Patchouli, Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Caramel, Chocolate, Praline, Amber, Musk

products.name: Angelica Glauca Oil
products.description:
Angelica glauca oil takes the familiar angelica character and pushes it somewhere darker and wilder. The earthy, rooty depth is far more pronounced, with an ancient, almost subterranean quality. Subtle celery-lovage sweetness emerges alongside warm spice, but the dominant impression is brooding, untouched earth.

This oil brings a dark, almost archaeological earthiness to orientals and chypres. Pair it with oakmoss and patchouli for a damp, forested accord, or blend it into your amber bases where its ancient rootiness adds extraordinary dimension. Its fixative power is remarkable.

Use angelica glauca to ground floral compositions with earthy darkness. A trace transforms rose accords into something enigmatic and deep. It fills a similar role to lovage and costus root but with a quality all its own — brooding, ancient, and endlessly tenacious on the blotter.

If you know Angelica archangelica root oil — musky, peppery, amber-like — you will recognise glauca as family, but a wilder branch. The earthy depth is far more pronounced, the musk gives way to something darker and more ancient, and the tenacity is even greater. Fraterworks carries both, and they complement each other beautifully.

Visual Differences

Angelica glauca and Angelica archangelica are easily distinguished in the field. The European species, A. archangelica, is the larger and bolder of the two — a tall, robust biennial reaching up to 2.5 metres, with bright yellow-green leaves, thick fleshy stems, and large gl

products.name: Angelica Root Oil
products.description:
Angelica root oil opens with a distinctive peppery-green freshness that quickly reveals a rich, musky-amber heart unlike anything else in perfumery. The scent carries an unmistakable earthy quality — damp forest floor mingled with warm spice. Naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed give this oil its remarkable tenacity.

This is one of perfumery's great fixatives, capable of anchoring compositions while adding mysterious depth. It excels in chypres alongside oakmoss and patchouli, where it contributes an earthy-musky foundation. Fougères gain complexity from its herbal-amber character, and oriental bases benefit from its warm, almost animalic undertones.

Use angelica root oil sparingly — its power sneaks up on you and can dominate a blend over time. Pair with vetiver for earthy richness or with clary sage for herbaceous sophistication. In citrus colognes, a trace adds unexpected depth and lasting power without announcing itself.

Angelica Root Oil vs Angelica Seed Oil

Both oils come from Angelica archangelica but deliver very different results. The root oil is dark, earthy, and distinctly musky thanks to naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed — it is one of perfumery's great natural fixatives. The seed oil is lighter, fresher, and more peppery with a sweet anisic undertone — a top-to-heart note that adds herbal spark rather than musky depth. Where the root oil anchors, the seed oil lifts. Blending the two gives you the complete ang

products.name: Angelica Seed Oil
products.description:
Angelica seed oil opens with a strong, fresh, peppery-green burst that feels almost bracing at full strength. Beneath that initial rush sits a sweet, almost anisic undertone — the signature that makes it immediately recognisable. The impression is bright, herbal, and surprisingly clean.

Use it to add peppery-green spark to chypres, fougères, and citrus colognes — accords where you need herbal lift without heaviness. It sits in the top-to-heart transition, providing aromatic freshness that complements oakmoss, clary sage, and bergamot. Pair it with the root oil for a complete angelica signature.

Both angelica oils are among the rarest essential oils in commerce — world production of each has historically been under a ton annually. Evaluate at 10% dilution; the peppery top overwhelms at full strength. The seed and root come from the same plant but deliver entirely different effects.

Angelica Seed Oil vs Angelica Root Oil

Both oils come from Angelica archangelica but deliver very different results. The seed oil is light, fresh, and peppery with a sweet anisic undertone — a top-to-heart note that adds herbal spark. The root oil is darker, earthier, and distinctly musky thanks to naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed. Where the seed oil lifts, the root oil anchors — it is one of perfumery's great natural fixatives. Blending the two gives you the complete angelica spectrum from bright peppery top to musky earthy base.

products.name: Animalia™ CMP
products.description:
Animalia CMP is the Fraterworks restoration of the magnificent original Animalis base of the 20th century. Featured in such fragrances as Cabochard, Men's Club, Obsession, Opium and Bourjois's Mais Oui.

Use it as a one for one replacer for Animalis to get a more luxurious and elegant result. Loaded with natural woods and precious spices, Animalia can enhance any fragrance. See the demo formula for an Aramis-like gentleman's scent. Once you've smelled this base you will never reach for the Animalis Hypo 27 or Animalis 1745-3 again.

Use up to 1.65% of your finished product for IFRA 51.

Animalia CMP contains no animal products.

products.name: Animusk™ Extra
products.description:
Animusk Extra is our restoration of Chevral, the incredible base by Bernard Chant which he used in numerous fragrances. Animusk contains natural animal musks and is IFRA and EU compliant.

This base is, in our opinion, the finest animalic musk ever created, far surpassing Animalis (our Animalia™ CMP). 

In small amounts this base imparts a wonderfully elegant and smooth animalic note, far gentler and kinder than pure animal musk but decidedly more interesting than synthetic musk.

It was used in the great Aramis, Van Cleef and Arpels for Men, Drakaar Noir, Kouros and many others.

products.name: Anisaldehyde, Natural
products.description:
Anisaldehyde is an indispensable aroma chemical for contributing Hawthorne, mimosa, lilac and powdery notes to a scent. This EU natural version is beautifully soft and rounded and while the synthetic is a nice material, you can achieve a more refined and elegant result even in a non-natural scent using this version.

And best of all, unlike virtually every material restricted by the EU or IFRA, Anisaldehyde has seen a lifting of restrictions from a maddeningly low 0.2% under IFRA 43 to a whopping (comparatively) 1.4% under IFRA 51.

products.name: Anisic Aldehyde
products.description:
Anisic aldehyde (anisaldehyde) is an indispensable aroma chemical for contributing Hawthorne, mimosa, lilac and powdery notes to a scent. It delivers exceptional performance as a bridge note in complex compositions. This powerful aldehyde creates seamless transitions between floral and gourmand elements. Exploit its multifaceted character to achieve sophisticated sweetness without cloying heaviness.

This material blends exceptionally with heliotropin for powdery effects and benzyl acetate for jasmine modifications. Apply sparingly in floral compositions where it amplifies sweetness without overwhelming delicate notes.

And best of all, unlike virtually every material restricted by the EU or IFRA, Anisaldehyde has seen a lifting of restrictions from a maddeningly low 0.2% under IFRA 43 to a whopping (comparatively) 1.4% under IFRA 51.

We also stock a beautiful 100% natural version of this chemical. It is our Anisaldehyde, Natural.

products.name: Anisyl Acetate
products.description:
Anisyl acetate opens with inviting powdery sweetness—soft, creamy, and reminiscent of fine vanilla extract. Fruity plum and cherry facets add juiciness without becoming jammy, while a coumarin-like warmth provides the tonka-bean quality that makes this chemical so versatile. The balsamic undertone grounds everything beautifully.

Use it as a modifier in floral compositions where it imparts sweetness without cloying heaviness. It excels in oriental and chypre fragrances, adding depth and a soft fruity-balsamic signature. The material works particularly well in mimosa accords and anywhere you want cherry or almond nuances without reaching for obvious gourmand notes.

Work with anisyl acetate in the heart and base of your formula where its low volatility becomes an asset. The 100-hour substantivity ensures your sweet powdery effect persists beautifully into the drydown. Blend with balsams for rich oriental effects, or pair with narcotic florals like tuberose and jasmine. It combines well with cyclamen aldehyde and heliotropin for complex powdery-floral signatures.

products.name: Anisyl Acetone
products.description:
Anisyl Acetone opens with an immediate burst of intense sweetness—ripe raspberries crushed with cherries, but this isn't simple fruitiness. The material quickly reveals sophisticated floral facets reminiscent of mimosa and cassie absolute, creating a powdery-sweet effect that bridges fruit and flower. This remarkable complexity extends to subtle anise and licorice notes that link to its "Anisyl" heritage, while woody-balsamic undertones add unexpected depth to what might otherwise be a purely sweet material.

Utilise Anisyl Acetone strategically in accords where you need fruity sweetness with floral sophistication. In Oriental bases, it provides essential berry-sweet facets that prevent heavy ambers from becoming cloying—use at 0.5-2% to add lift without overwhelming warmth. For sweet floral accords, it excels as a Heliotropin modifier, offering similar powdery sweetness without the discolouration issues that plague many formulations. In Fougère structures, small amounts (0.1-0.5%) sweeten harsh aromatic notes while maintaining masculine sophistication. Its true genius emerges in raspberry and cherry accords where it provides authentic fruit character with unusual persistence.

Anisyl Acetone finds its most sophisticated applications in complex bases where its multifaceted nature truly shines. In vanilla accords, it contributes essential fruity complexity that prevents flat sweetness—combine with Vanillin and Ethyl Vanillin at 2-3% for three-dimensional warmth. For licorice c

products.name: Anisyl Alcohol
products.description:
Anisyl Alcohol opens with an immediate powdery sweetness that distinguishes it as the softest member of the anise family. Where its relatives can be sharp or intensely fruity, this alcohol whispers rather than shouts—a gentle hawthorn blossom accord with lilac's purple sweetness woven throughout. The material brings that coveted heliotrope character perfumers seek: almond-like creaminess married to powdery florals, but without the stability headaches that plague heliotropin in alkaline bases.

This alcohol excels in creating naturalness within synthetic floral bouquets, particularly in mimosa and cassie reconstructions where its powdery-balsamic profile adds authentic depth. Deploy it at 1-10% in fragrance compounds to round sharp edges and add volume to flat florals. Its moderate tenacity (30 hours on blotter) provides excellent support through the heart phase without overwhelming delicate top notes. The material's superior stability in soap, creams, and antiperspirants makes it invaluable for functional perfumery where aldehydic alternatives would discolour.

Beyond its primary floral applications, Anisyl Alcohol serves as an exceptional modifier in gourmand and oriental compositions, where its vanilla-honey facets enhance edible qualities without adding excessive sweetness. Combine with benzyl salicylate and coumarin for classic powder accords, or pair with methyl eugenol to create stunning lilac soliflores. Its chemical stability and IFRA restrictions (varying from 0.21%

products.name: Antillone™
products.description:
Antillone™ is typically pineapple but with nuances of other fruit. It is a natural molecule and a speciality of V. MANE Fils. Beyond any doubt this chemical is a must-have for anyone wanting to add naturalness for a fruit blend or to create more characterful and rich natural pineapple notes.

John Wright wrote an article about this molecule in Perfumer & Flavorist and said: “The character of this chemical is somewhat similar to allyl hexanoate. It is sharp and fruity in a similar way to allyl hexanoate and instantly recognisable as pineapple. It fits equally well into pineapple flavors, adding brightness and freshness. In some ways it is preferable because it has a higher level of the dry, almost dusty, note that is reminiscent of the fresh fruit.”

products.name: Aphermate
products.description:
You can never have too many fruity and fresh materials and the marine quality of this formate from IFF makes it an extra interesting product. Aphermate is, first and foremost, fruit (apple to be precise) followed by hints of pine tree and the seashore. It is a lovely material to add interest to the more classic freshies such as Calone and Cascalone. It also has an unusual opening note that hints at burnt plastic.

Aphermate blends well with the Rose Ketones, Ethyl Safranate, Theaspirane, Amazonia, and Verdantol.

products.name: Apo Patchone Coeur
products.description:
Upon smelling Apo Patchone Coeur it is easy to imagine hand-cobbled leather shoes, dusty Parisian lofts and antique suitcases waiting in dark corners for the outing that will never come.

Apo Patchone Coeur is a refined patchouli-derived material which softens the loamy and musty top that can overshadow patchouli compositions, instead, delivering a smooth, woody-amber signature with a subtle but notable leather nuance. This makes it versatile in both masculine and unisex fragrances.

Its leather-like quality often emerges as a sleek, suede-like dryness rather than the raw, animalic leather we tend to associate with birch tar or castoreum (which, it must be said, blends extremely well with this chemical). Its nuanced, tactile impression of soft leather supports other richer materials without dominating.

Apo Patchone Coeur works beautifully with our Royal Leather base and needless to say it blends exceedingly well with other leather aroma chemicals such as Iso Butyl Quinoline. However, don't neglect its floral side — pairings with rose materials are fascinating and worth experimenting with for novel modern accords.

Typical Usage

At lower concentrations (0.5–1%), it provides a subtle, smooth enhancement to woody, leathery, or amber accords, adding depth without dominating.

At higher concentrations (2–3%), it becomes more prominent, contributing a sleek suede-like leather quality and a modern patchouli twist that can define a composition

products.name: Apple Supreme
products.description:
Every bit of crunchy apple that you need. This base is an instant "apple shampoo" note for me, taking me right back to stingy eyes in the bath as a child. This can be used in overdose — up to 100% in perfumes in fact, or as a nice top note modifier when something more interesting than Verdox is wanted.

This is one you will find yourself opening just to take a guilty-pleasure sniff from time to time.

products.name: Aprifloren®
products.description:
A lovely fruity lactone which is more powerful that similar materials such as Gamma Undecalactone. It can be used with those materials to create a velvety and complex stone fruit accord, or on its own for a different impression of peach or apricot. We highly recommend it.

Aprifloren blends beautifully with Persicol, Paradise Molecule, extreme dilutions of grapefruit odourant Thiocineole, Edenolide, Ambrofix™, Floralozone, AmberXTreme, Kephalis and all the lactones.

products.name: Apritone
products.description:
Apritone is ripe, fleshy apricot — warm, sweet, and disarmingly realistic. But it's far more than simple fruit: peach and jasmine undertones layer underneath, with a subtle rose ketone-like facet and ambrette creaminess adding unexpected complexity. Exceptionally tenacious on the strip.

Use Apritone wherever you need apricot that persists deep into the dry-down — most fruit esters vanish quickly, but this terpenoid ketone stays. It anchors peach and jasmine accords with real tenacity. Try it in woody compositions where its fruity warmth adds a supple, rounded quality you wouldn't expect.

Combine Apritone with gamma-undecalactone and damascones to build full-bodied stone fruit accords. Prunolide strengthens the apricot realism. Layer it with sweet musks for a skin-scent effect where the fruit feels intimate and worn-in rather than bright and projecting — this is not a top note material.

products.name: Aquaflora
products.description:
Aquaflora smells of fresh lily of the valley, clean and gently green. The muguet floralcy stays light and watery, almost see-through, with none of the usual heaviness. A touch of cyclamen and soft fruit rounds off the edges.

Use Aquaflora to build airy muguet and cyclamen accords, or to open a floral with a fresh, just-watered lift. It adds body and a clean aquatic feel without turning soapy or sharp. Even at low levels it threads a transparent green floralcy through the top and heart.

products.name: Armenian Wood Base
products.description:
Armenian Wood Base opens with a wave of sweet, resinous warmth — vanilla-rich benzoin interwoven with a soft cinnamic spice and a faint trail of woodsmoke. It calls to mind the experience of burning Papier d'Armenie, that traditional French incense paper soaked in Siam benzoin resin. The effect is at once cosy and quietly exotic.

This is a ready-made accord built around Siam benzoin as its central axis, but it goes much further than a simple benzoin reconstitution. Soft sandalwood and powdery woody notes provide structure, while a subtle animalic funk — likely from styrax-type components and a trace of civet character — gives the base surprising depth and longevity. Reach for it whenever you need instant balsamic richness in oriental, amber, or incense accords, or use it to add smoky sweetness beneath a floral heart.

Treat Armenian Wood as a shortcut to complex resinous warmth. It pairs beautifully with oud, patchouli, and frankincense for dark oriental work, and it will soften and sweeten woody-amber frameworks when used at low levels. A few percent can transform a flat vanilla into something layered and smouldering.

products.name: Armoise Heart
products.description:
Armoise Heart is cool, sharp and camphoraceous, with a minty bite and the bitter, green freshness of wormwood. Underneath runs a dry, resinous pine note. It hits the nose with real force, clean and bracing rather than dusty or muddy.

A little brings instant freshness and green lift to aromatic structures. Use it to sharpen fougères and chypres, to give colognes a herbal snap, and to add a cool, wild edge to lavender and rosemary. It works best in traces, where its diffusive power reads as energy rather than bitterness.

products.name: Artemal™
products.description:
Artemal™ is our reconstruction of an original IFF internal masterpiece named Amaro, a base of fresh forest notes with herbs, spices and masculine florals. It is one of the finest green type bases we know and provides the key olfactory character to Polo Green.

On its own this base is practically an entire fragrance and would be especially suited to forest fresh fragrances. Add a percent or two to a body wash, shampoo or conditioner base and you have a luxurious fresh product ready to go.

products.name: Asparagus Twigs Absolute
products.description:
Asparagus Twigs Absolute (produced from the foliage and twigs of the plant, not the green spears we eat) opens with astonishing complexity—dry tobacco leaves mingle with bitter cocoa dust. This isn't the sulfurous vegetable you'd expect. Instead, woody stems yield cigar-box richness with earthy undertones reminiscent of aged oakmoss, creating immediate intrigue and sophistication.

This absolute bridges disparate olfactory families with remarkable finesse. Deploy it to connect tobacco accords with gourmand bases, adding mysterious depth without sweetness. The subtle animalic-valerian facet makes it invaluable for modern oud compositions where its sour tang enhances natural wood complexities without dominating.

Work with this material at 0.1-1% to exploit its fixative properties and unique character. It excels when paired with tobacco absolute for ultra-realistic cigar accords, or combine with cocoa and labdanum for avant-garde leather-gourmands. The absolute's unexpected profile rewards experimental perfumers seeking distinctive signatures.

This absolute transforms traditional tobacco compositions by eliminating fruity damascone characters, instead delivering dry, masculine cigar-box woodiness. You achieve remarkable oud synergies by exploiting its unique sour valerian aspect, which harmonises beautifully with acidic Assam oud oils. Layer it with vetiver and patchouli to amplify its oakmoss-like structural properties in IFRA-compliant chypre bases.

products.name: Attar Base N.18
products.description:
Attar Base N.18 is a one-for-one drop-in replacement for Dioctyl Phthalate — a now-prohibited chemical formerly used in very large quantities as an odourless direct replacer for sandalwood oil due to cost. For some time, DOP was the go-to carrier for attars and other blends, but with its prohibition, perfumers have had to look at alternatives such as DPG overdoses (note: in most cases these are being used instead of alcohol in non-alcohol perfumes — hence their use at up to 80% in some cases). However, DPG on its own is not the best carrier, as it lacks a silken hand-feel and cosmetic appeal.

Attar Base N.18 gives you that hand-feel and longevity on the skin, while also supporting your formula with a touch of natural antioxidant and an antibacterial blend to combat the negative effects of using a dipper which touches the skin and then goes back into the bottle of perfume.

Fraterworks Attar Bases

Once upon a time, an attar was a co-distillation of precious botanical matter, traditionally done using two stills. Nowadays the term has broadened considerably to include blends of plant extracts and aroma chemicals diluted in sandalwood as a carrier oil. Cost and rarity make pure sandalwood difficult to justify, so alternatives are needed.

Fraterworks Attar Bases are designed to be used as ingredients in precious mukhallats (the Arabian term for a blend of naturals and aroma chemicals — in other words, a perfume base) and other fragrance forms. Each Attar Base has different nuan

products.name: Attar Base N.27
products.description:
Attar Base N.27 is a sandalwood/oud-character carrier — not a neutral replacement like Attar Base N.18, but an active participant in your composition. Where N.18 is designed to disappear, N.27 is designed to evoke the creamy, woody warmth of traditional sandalwood oil at a fraction of the cost.

The result is a carrier that behaves like sandalwood oil on the skin: the slow, radiant diffusion, the creamy warmth, the way it lifts and supports everything blended into it. If you've ever used genuine Mysore sandalwood as a carrier and mourned the cost, N.27 is what you've been waiting for.

Use N.27 wherever your formula calls for sandalwood oil as a carrier or diluent — in attars, mukhallats, and oil-based perfumery of all kinds. It gives you the character of sandalwood without the extraordinary price tag, while also supporting your formula with a touch of natural antioxidant and an antibacterial blend to combat the negative effects of using a dipper which touches the skin and then goes back into the bottle of perfume.

To use, simply add 20% (or more!) of your favourite Mukhallat blend (or oud oil, attars, etc) to 80% of Attar Base N.27. Alternatively use it as an incredibly cost effective sandalwood alternative that will cause any oriental blend to bloom. This can also be used in an alcohol perfume in the same way Sandalwood oil is used.

Fraterworks Attar Bases

Once upon a time, an attar was a co-distillation of precious botanical matter, traditionally done using two stills.

products.name: Aurantiol®
products.description:
Aurantiol is the most common of the Schiff bases, a product resulting from the chemical reaction of methyl anthranilate with an aldehyde, in this case hydroxycitronellal. While there are many suppliers of Aurantiol (and you can even make it yourself by blending the two key materials in a ratio of roughly 56:44), not all Schiff bases are created equal. Poor quality versions are everywhere — the result of wrong proportions or incomplete (or worse still non-existent) dehydration of the final product. Because the process produces water as a side effect, you will often see inferior qualities which are cloudy and should be avoided. Our Aurantiol is perfectly dehydrated and has excellent clarity and a fine aroma.

Aurantiol has the distinct scent of orange flowers and honey and it is in those contexts that it is most often used. Our Aurantiol is intensely yellow and very viscous (though easily pourable with a little heat). We offer it pure and in dilution due to its thickness.

products.name: Aurelione
products.description:
Aurelione opens with a gentle, powdery warmth that settles into a soft balsamic musk with an intimate, skin-like quality. There is nothing sharp here - just a smooth, enveloping radiance with the faintest animalic whisper beneath. It recalls the warmth of clean skin on a summer evening.

This is a macrocyclic ketone built on a sixteen-membered carbon ring, sold as a mixture of positional isomers including Globanone. At low doses it rounds off floral accords with invisible warmth; push it higher and you get a clean, billowing fabric-softener effect. It particularly excels at enhancing floral notes - experienced perfumers note it outperforms its close relative Globanone in this regard.

Try Aurelione at 1-5% to give florals a gentle halo of warmth and persistence. In musky skin scents, push it well above 10% for full effect - it can handle overdose gracefully. Combine it with other macrocyclic musks and lactones for complex, layered musk accords that never turn harsh.

products.name: Avobenzone
products.description:
Avobenzone is the most effective UVA absorber available to perfumers. This crystalline powder shields the full UVA range (320–400 nm, peaking at 357 nm) — the long-wave light that yellows liquids and breaks down vanillin. At typical use levels, it adds no perceptible odour to your composition.

Dissolve Avobenzone in a co-solvent — benzyl benzoate, IPM, or Octinoxate — by heating to 80–85°C until completely clear. Its solubility in pure ethanol is poor (under 1%), so alcohol-based fragrances need a carrier oil in the formula. Compositions containing vanillin or citrus oils benefit most from its protection.

The catch: Avobenzone is photounstable and degrades in light unless stabilised. Always include Oxynex ST at 0.5% — it quenches the reactive excited state that causes degradation, boosting photostability dramatically. Never combine Avobenzone with Octinoxate alone — without a stabiliser, the two accelerate each other's breakdown.

Avobenzone vs Octinoxate

Avobenzone and Octinoxate protect against different portions of the UV spectrum. Avobenzone absorbs UVA (320–400 nm) — the longer-wavelength light responsible for yellowing liquids and degrading vanillin and other phenolics. Octinoxate absorbs UVB (280–320 nm) — the shorter-wavelength radiation that attacks terpenes, aldehydes, and other volatile components.

products.name: Azarbre
products.description:
Azarbre is a herbal material that can add wonderfully delicate orris and honey nuances to a fragrance. It is an infrequently seen material that is used to great effect in the Dior Private Collection fragrance Bois D'Argent (2004) by Annick Menardo which is enormously popular with French Hip Hop stars. See our demo formula below.

According to A. B. Camps: “This material […] is missing from most laboratories. Azarbre is less agrestical than Opalal and more woody-honey-rooty, with notes of dry flowers. Azarbre mixes well with rooty essential oils such as corydalis or Cyperus scarious and all kinds of agarwood oils as well. The material forms great accords with isophorone, phenylacetic acid, oxophorone, tobacco absolute, ionones, damascones, phenylacetates, nectarol, the usually great myrrhone, dihydroionol, and osmanthus[.]”

Azarbre blends well with Aetoxylon Oil, Fenchone Alpha, Geosmin, Linalool Oxide, Amazonia™ and Miraclewood™.

products.name: Bacdanol®
products.description:
Bacdanol opens with immediate sandalwood warmth enhanced by creamy, almost cosmetic milkiness. Its sweet gourmand character suggests vanilla whilst subtle rose facets add floral sophistication. This powerful material radiates with impressive diffusion, creating lasting woody depth.

You'll find Bacdanol invaluable for building cost-effective sandalwood accords where diffusion and longevity matter. It excels at supporting floral hearts, particularly rose and jasmine, whilst adding creamy depth to woody bases. Use it at 0.5-2% where its power provides excellent value compared to natural sandalwood without sacrificing quality.

Blend Bacdanol with Javanol for enhanced floral-sandalwood complexity or combine with Ebanol for deeper leather nuances. Pair with Iso E Super where transparent woody diffusion amplifies its creamy character. This material bridges floral hearts with amber bases beautifully, particularly with musks.

Bacdanol vs Dartanol

Whilst chemically similar, these materials offer distinct olfactory profiles perfumers value differently. Bacdanol presents sweeter, creamier, more gourmand character with vanilla-milky richness ideal for modern compositions. Dartanol delivers drier, more natural sandalwood with cedar-like texture and radiant elegance preferred for premium fragrances. Choose Bacdanol for cost-effective sweetness and powerful diffusion; choose Dartanol for authentic sandalwood refinement.

products.name: Basil ct Methyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Basil ex Methyl Cinnamate has an unexpected sweetness—candy-like, fruity, and distinctly different from our other basil oils. The cinnamon-balsamic warmth emerges quickly, while strawberry and cherry facets add intriguing fruitiness. Fresh green basil character remains present but softened, creating a profile that bridges herbal and gourmand territories with surprising grace, lending itself to a potentially modernised gourmand take on the classic Diorella fragrance.

This chemotype represents one of four major basil oil varieties (the others being linalool, methyl chavicol and eugenol/methyl eugenol), distinguished by its high methyl cinnamate content. Cultivated primarily in Bulgaria, Egypt, and Haiti, this basil develops its spicy-sweet character from the same molecule that gives cinnamon its warmth. The linalool content adds familiar basil freshness, while the absence of camphor keeps the profile smooth and approachable.

The fruity-spicy profile blends beautifully with berry notes like blackcurrant and osmanthus for fantasy fruit accords. Use alongside citrus oils for bright, airy herbaceous effects, or with oriental bases where its cinnamon warmth adds natural depth. The sweet-balsamic quality complements rose, geranium, and other florals seeking spicy complexity.

products.name: Basil Oil ct Linalool
products.description:
LMR is fast becoming our favourite supplier. Time and again they end up on a level above all other suppliers. This basil oil from Egypt is no exception. This is the treasured sweet basil "Grand Vert", chemotype linalool. Because it is low in methyl chavicol it is a significantly softer and more refined basil oil with a much subdued anise note.

If you are looking for something bolder in odour, our beautiful Basil oil ct Methyl Chavicol from Floral Concept is for you.

Basil was used to great effect in Eau Sauvage and At The Barber's (ct Linalool) and Brut (ct Methyl Chavicol), demonstrations formulas for which are below.

Basil oil (both types) blends extremely well with Suralette™ Extra, Canthoxal and most other herbal notes. It is particularly popular in mens fragrances.

products.name: Basil Oil ct Methyl Chavicol
products.description:
This lovely basil oil (Basil de Grasse) has a high methyl chavicol count which makes it more anisic than the linalool rich type. Basil was used to great effect in Eau Sauvage (ct Linalool) and Brut (ct Methyl Chavicol), demonstrations formulas of which are both below.

Basil oil blends extremely well with Suralette™ Extra, Canthoxal and most other herbal notes. It is particularly popular in mens fragrances.

We also stock Basil Oil ct Linalool (sweet linalool also known as Egyptian Basil or Comoros Basil) from LMR.

Origin: Vietnam
Part: Leaves
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Baume Ambré
products.description:
Baume Ambré is a co-distillation — benzoin resin distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is benzoin transformed: still sweet, still vanillic, but carrying the memory of hot stone and burning paper.

The classic benzoin sweetness is immediately recognisable, but the gurjun co-distillation pushes it somewhere strange and nostalgic. A faint plastic edge adds tension to the sweetness. As the top notes vaporise, a cinnamic warmth emerges underneath — tying Baume Ambré back to the ancient balsamic family while keeping it unpredictable. The smoke quality is not birch or cade but papier d'Arménie: delicate, sweet, devotional.

Use it as a base anchor in orientals where standard benzoin feels too simple. It bridges the gap between clean vanillic sweetness and the darker, more complex resinous territory that modern niche compositions demand. Layer it beneath florals to give them warmth without heaviness.

Note that in colder climes, Baume Ambré may have some separation. It is simply the heavier benzoic acid from the benzoin fraction. Gentle warmth will homogenise the material.

products.name: Bay Oil, Dominica
products.description:
Bay oil from Dominica hits the nose with a bold, sweet-spicy warmth built on rich eugenol. Beneath the clove-like character you find a fresh, almost lemony lift, balanced by sweet-balsamic undertones. The effect is immediately recognisable—warm, rounded, and distinctly Caribbean.

This oil defines the classic bay rum accord that has anchored masculine grooming since the 19th century. It excels in aftershaves and hair tonics, but sells itself short if confined there alone. Blend it with lavender or lavandin for a traditional Rondeletia-type accord, or pair with citrus oils, petitgrain, and ylang-ylang for sophisticated colognes with real backbone.

Push bay oil into modern territory by combining it with oakmoss and patchouli in spicy chypres. A few drops transform oriental bases, adding lived-in warmth without heaviness.

Don't confuse your bays

This West Indian bay oil (Pimenta racemosa, Myrtaceae family) is an entirely different material from bay laurel (Laurus nobilis, Lauraceae family), the culinary herb with a sharp, medicinal, cineole-heavy profile. It is also distinct from pimento berry oil (Pimenta dioica)—commonly called allspice—which shares the same botanical family but produces a rounder, warmer, more cinnamon-clove spice character from its berries rather than leaves.

products.name: Beeswax Absolute, Glacé
products.description:
Beeswax is a wonderful animalic product for perfumery. It contributes a softness and natural rounding of scents as well as being a long lasting fixative.

The biggest annoyance with Beeswax Absolute is the difficult in dissolving it and the fact that it is mostly insoluble waxes that must ultimately be chilled and filtered from your fragrance. But not so with our incredible Beeswax Absolute Glacé from LMR.

In a special process LMR processes this absolute with a technique they call glazing. That process involves freezing the beeswax absolute and removing insoluble matter so what you are left with is pure beeswax odour with guaranteed solubility. 

Discarding nearly 75% of the non-useful material does come at a price: this absolute is an incredibly expensive product. But oh what a product it is. We love it, we use it and we heartily recommend it. In fact, this is the only Beeswax absolute we use at Fraterworks and Frater Perfumes; nothing else comes close in quality and usability.

Splurge: your fragrances are worth it.

“Their musk encroaches, circle after circle,
A well of scents almost too dense to breathe in." — Sylvia Plath, The Beekeeper's Daughter

Origin: France
Part: Beeswax
Process: Solvent extraction followed by speciality freeze filtering

products.name: Benzaldehyde 50% DPG
products.description:
Benzaldehyde is the classic almond chemical and makes up 80-95% of natural almond oil. In addition to its obvious uses providing almond and cherry notes to a fragrance, in trace amounts it adds beautiful and inimitable nuances to top notes. Overdose it with Acetophenone for a cherry accord, mix it with Vanillin “Signature” and a touch of Maltol for a marzipan accord, or use a trace to bring out the hidden almond nuances in Exaltolide.

Due to DEA requirements in the USA we sell this at 50% dilution only.

products.name: Benzoin Oliffac
products.description:
Benzoin Oliffac 63 opens with a creamy, vanillic sweetness (almost milkshake-like) that sits deeper and rounder than typical vanilla materials. There's a soft powdery quality underneath, dusted with faint cinnamon and almond nuances. The effect recalls warm resin tempered into something smooth and immediately usable.

This IFF base solves the notorious handling problems of crude benzoin gum—no heating, no filtering, no wax precipitation. It dissolves completely in ethanol and pours cold from the bottle, which saves you time in production. At 1–3% of your concentrate, it adds soft vanillic sweetness without announcing itself; at 5–10%, it becomes the structural backbone of amber and oriental accords.

Use Benzoin Oliffac when you need the classic benzoin character without the laboratory drama. Pair it with labdanum and vanillin for traditional amber structures, or blend with tuberose and jasmine to round harsh indolic edges. Its 400+ hour tenacity on blotter makes it exceptional in functional products—candles, detergents, fabric care—where heat stability and lasting warmth matter most.

products.name: Benzoin Siam Resinoid 50% TEC
products.description:
This is a wonderfully sweet and fine benzoin resinoid made from only Grade A tears (the highest quality). Furthermore, to maintain its natural certifiability it is diluted to 50% in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless diluent isolated from citrus oil).

Many Benzoin products have chemical side odours (or perhaps worse, no odour at all) because they are produced in a relatively careless way owing to their use more as a fixative than a note in itself, but this Benzoin from V. MANE Fils pays homage to the raw material — being made with as much dignity and care as it would receive if it were the finest rose extract. 

Origin: Laos
Variety: Styrax Tonkinensis
Part: Exudate
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Benzoin Siam “Signature” Tincture 20%
products.description:
Fraterworks manufactures this superior tincture using completely cold alcohol and highest quality wild-harvested benzoin Siam gum. The drug (raw gum) is the highest grade and our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of benzoin extracts and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop.

In addition to being a perfumery material, Benzoin Siam Tincture was a starting material for Friar's Balsam, a medicinal compound invented in the 1760s by Dr Johua Ward who combined it with smaller amounts of styrax resin and the bitter aloe ferox (a plant related to aloe vera). Fraterworks' Benzoin Siam Tincture is not produced in a food safe or pharmaceutical environment and as such is not be taken internally. This is not a medicine and is not made according to the USP standards.

Combining this tincture in a ratio of 1:10 up to 1:50 with distilled water will give you Lac Virginis (virgin's milk), an olden days cosmetic to brighten a young lady's complexion. The tincture may louche upon blending with water.

Origin: Siam (Thailand)
Variety: Styrax tonkinensis
Part: Gum
Method: Cold ethanol tincture

products.name: Benzoin Sumatra Resinoid 50% TEC
products.description:
Benzoin Sumatra resinoid has a warm, balsamic aroma with a distinctive blend of sweet vanilla, smoky undertones, and a spicy edge, largely due to its content of cinnamic acid alongside benzoic acid. This cinnamic acid contributes a subtle cinnamon-like sharpness that sets it apart from the more common Siamese variety, giving Benzoin Sumatra a rugged, slightly resinous depth with a hint of smokiness

 In comparison to Benzoin Siam, Sumatra's thicker, darker consistency and reddish hue further reflect its robust character, appealing to perfumers seeking a bold, anchoring base note.

Benzoin Sumatra is ideal for grounding spicy, oriental, or woody perfume compositions.

Due to its thickness, we offer it at 50% in natural TEC making it ISO 2935 compliant.

products.name: Benzyl Acetate ex Ylang-Ylang
products.description:
A truly special product, this fractionated Ylang-ylang has a massive 46% Benzyl Acetate making it a wonderfully complex alternative to that often harsh chemical. Use it on its own for a rich and intense Ylang note, or in combination with other materials for sweetness, creaminess and floralcy.

This is a speciality of Payan Bertrand and we are very excited to be able to offer it in small quantities.

products.name: Benzyl Acetate “Signature”
products.description:
We currently sell natural versions of Benzyl Acetate (the treasured Ylang Ylang isolate and an extract from Apples) but sometimes you just need a cost effective workhorse. That's where our signature synthetic comes in. Benzyl Acetate “Signature” is an FCC (Food Chemicals Codex) product. While this is not to be used in food as we don't prepare our packages in a food safe environment, this special grade of is particularly pure because it is made with food use in mind. This is undeniably the cleanest and most usable synthetic version and at a price that simply cannot be beaten. This is the benzyl acetate we use everywhere unless we specifically need a natural isolate to be all-natural compliant.

Use Benzyl Acetate (which smells like banana candy and nail polish remover) to create floral heart notes of Jasmine, Tuberose and Ylang Ylang, or use it as a sweetener in a general floral melange.

products.name: Benzyl Acetate, Natural
products.description:
Benzyl acetate is vital for adding jasmine and ylang-ylang notes to a fragrance. Classic florals (muguet, lilac, and even rose) also frequently have large amounts. In small doses it can be used as a sweetener for a more general floral accord.

This natural form of Benzyl Acetate is extremely clean and has no chemical off notes that so many synthetic versions do. In fact, it is nice enough to wear on its own.

products.name: Benzyl Acetone
products.description:
Benzyl acetone is an indispensable chemical for adding a fruity nuance to oud replacers or as a modifier to the much more delicate benzyl acetate. Benzyl acetone is very powerful and very small amounts are perceptible in a fragrance. This material is also a key component of the scent of cocoa and the most bee-attracting chemical in many flowers.

Benzyl Acetone has nuances of tobacco, cinnamon, pineapple, banana and white flowers.

NOTE: this product should not be confused with Benzyl Acetate, the common chemical used to reproduce the scent of jasmine and ylang-ylang.

products.name: Benzyl Alcohol
products.description:
Benzyl alcohol is not a star note but a quiet workhorse. It polishes florals, dissolves tough ingredients, and lends gentle fixative power. Keep it fresh, dose with restraint, and it will make your formulas feel more professional. Even traces (under 0.5%) can soften and naturalise floral bases built around harsh aroma chemicals like Benzyl Acetate.

Due to its natural occurrence in many white florals and its blending properties, Benzyl Alcohol is frequently employed in the construction or support of accords such as Jasmine, Lilac, Gardenia, Tuberose, Heliotrope, Muguet (Lily of the Valley), Rose, Orange Blossom, and Ylang-Ylang. It is often found in formulations alongside materials like Benzyl Acetate, Benzyl Salicylate, Lindenol (terpineol), Hydroxycitronellal, Lilial and Lyral and Methyl Anthranilate.

The odour of benzyl alcohol ranges from extremely faint, to mildly almond-like. The almond facet comes not from the material itself but degradation into benzaldehyde which is very common. Once you receive your benzyl alcohol you should keep it well sealed and in a cool dark place to maintain its freshness.

products.name: Benzyl Benzoate
products.description:
Benzyl benzoate is a quiet achiever in perfumery having a dual role as both a fixative and a solvent. Its mild, slightly sweet balsamic scent rarely steals the spotlight but works wonders behind the scenes, boosting the performance of other materials. It can also stabilise volatile ingredients.

In floral compositions, it lends a unique smoothness and natural feel to jasmine, tuberose, and ylang-ylang accords. It's also a key component in recreating the rich, warm depth of natural balsams.

Thanks to its exceptional solubility, benzyl benzoate is vital in dissolving challenging materials like crystalline musks or stubborn absolutes (as evidenced in our Violet Leaf Superessence in which a small amount of naturally derived benzyl benzoate is combined with natural triethyl citrate for maximum solubility.)

We do have stock of this in a natural form if necessary. Contact us for pricing.

products.name: Benzyl Butyrate
products.description:
Benzyl Butyrate opens with an intense burst of ripe stone fruits—imagine biting into a perfectly ripe plum as its juice mingles with sun-warmed apricot flesh. This fruity character possesses remarkable complexity, weaving together tropical pineapple brightness with a creamy, almost vanillic sweetness. What sets this material apart is its inherent jasmine-like floral facet that emerges as the initial fruitiness settles.

This dual fruity-floral nature makes Benzyl Butyrate indispensable when you need to bridge fresh fruit top notes with deeper floral hearts. Use it to add authentic fruit ripeness to jasmine reconstructions or to inject tropical exoticism into traditional florals. Its medium strength and slow evaporation rate ensure these effects persist throughout your composition's development.

Reach for Benzyl Butyrate when crafting summer-inspired fragrances where playful fruitiness meets sophisticated florals. Combine it with other benzyl esters to build complex white floral bases, or contrast its sweetness with woody materials for unexpected depth. At 0.08-5% in your formula, it transforms simple accords into memorable signatures that capture both youthful exuberance and refined elegance.

products.name: Benzyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Benzyl cinnamate opens quietly—a soft, sweet balsamic warmth with a powdery, floral haze. There is no sharpness here; the cinnamic character reads as rounded and resinous rather than spicy. Faint cherry and apricot nuances hover in the background, giving the material a subtle fruity sweetness beneath its amber glow.

Benzyl cinnamate excels behind rose, carnation, and heliotrope. It occurs naturally in Peru balsam and Tolu balsam, and you can lean into that connection by pairing it with benzoin, styrax, and vanillin for rich resinous accords.

Benzyl vs Methyl Cinnamate

These two cinnamate esters occupy opposite ends of the volatility spectrum. Methyl cinnamate is brighter, more intense, and distinctly fruity—strong strawberry and cherry notes with a sweet balsamic punch that projects immediately.

Benzyl cinnamate is heavier, quieter, and far more tenacious—a powdery balsamic base note where methyl cinnamate is a radiant top-to-heart modifier.

Use methyl cinnamate when you want a vivid fruity-balsamic opening; reach for benzyl cinnamate when you need warm, lasting balsamic depth in the drydown. Together, they create a complete cinnamic arc from bright fruity flash to slow resinous fade.

products.name: Benzyl Formate
products.description:
Benzyl formate greets you with a surprisingly fruity take on the jasmine theme. Unlike its cousin benzyl acetate, this formate delivers sweet raspberry and blackberry facets alongside the expected white floral character. A distinctive black tea quality weaves through, adding depth and intrigue.

This ester proves remarkably versatile across floral and fruity compositions alike. It rounds and softens jasmine accords while adding fresh cherry-berry lift. You'll find it invaluable in hyacinth reconstructions—Arctander lists it among the key components for building convincing hyacinth bases. Rose, tuberose, and heliotrope compositions also benefit from its sweet fruity modifier effect.

Try benzyl formate in stone fruit accords where you need floral complexity beneath the fruit. It bridges the gap between purely fruity and purely floral materials beautifully. The 8-hour substantivity at full strength gives you reliable mid-note performance without disappearing too quickly.

products.name: Benzyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
Benzyl isobutyrate opens with a notably smooth sweetness—the familiar jasmine-like quality of benzyl esters but without the penetrating sharpness that can characterise benzyl acetate. This rounded character immediately reveals ripe berry facets, particularly strawberry and raspberry, interwoven with the floral heart. Subtle tropical notes emerge, suggesting pineapple without becoming overtly fruity. The overall impression is one of sophisticated smoothness—a powdery, slightly oily quality adds depth while fresh aromatic notes prevent heaviness. This is benzyl acetate's gentler cousin, offering similar floral-fruity effects with superior blending properties.

Use Benzyl isobutyrate at 0.5-6% when you need to smooth harsh edges in floral compositions or add natural fruity depth without overwhelming sweetness. Its primary value lies in modification—use it to transform sharp benzyl acetate into something more rounded and sophisticated. In jasmine and gardenia accords, it provides essential fruity sweetness while maintaining floral integrity. The material excels at bridging disparate notes, particularly useful when connecting bright citrus tops to heavier floral hearts. In modern fruity-florals, it adds the elusive "ripe" quality that makes synthetic fruits smell natural. Consider it your go-to when fruity lactones feel too heavy but simple esters lack complexity.

Where benzyl acetate delivers sharp, penetrating jasmine-pear sweetness, benzyl isobutyrate provides smoother, rounde

products.name: Benzyl Isoeugenol
products.description:
Benzyl isoeugenol smells of quiet, powdery carnation — warm, spicy-sweet, and balsamic, but far softer than isoeugenol or eugenol. Rose and violet facets emerge alongside the spice, with a faint vanilla warmth in the drydown. It is a white crystalline powder that melts into a blend readily.

Think of this as isoeugenol's well-behaved sibling — the same carnation character but milder, broader, and more versatile. It works as a fixative in floral compositions, adding tenacity without asserting itself. Use it in carnation accords, violet bases, and ylang-ylang reconstructions.

Pair it with ionones and benzyl salicylate for a complete violet base, or with eugenol and vanillin for a warm spicy-floral heart. It lasts 75 hours on a blotter — genuine fixative power. Dissolve in warm ethanol before adding to your formula.

products.name: Benzyl Isovalerate
products.description:
Benzyl Isovalerate is a heavy floral and fruity material which lacks the penetrating sweetness of its more famous cousin benzyl acetate. It is well suited to oriental fragrances and is a wonderful addition to rich florals, in particular jasmine.

Nuances of sour milk with a vague hint of emesis belies its true nature as an ester of butyric acid. However, despite the unpleasant associations of that acid, Benzyl Isovalerate has the positive effect of adding naturalness to fruit and gourmand accords and fragrances (especially apple and pineapple). 

Benzyl Isovalerate excels in doses below 1% and blends exceedingly well with Ylang Ylang, Dimethyl Benzyl Carbinyl Butyrate, Cis 3 Hexenol and its esters, Benzyl Acetate and most fruit materials. Try it with a touch of benzoin resinoid in an oriental scent.

products.name: Benzyl Propionate
products.description:
Benzyl propionate opens with a burst of ripe, juicy fruit—banana, pineapple, and pear tumbling over one another in a bright, sweet rush. Beneath the fruit salad, a clear jasmine-floral quality anchors the scent and stops it reading as purely edible. The overall impression is cheerful, sweet, and immediately appealing.

This ester outperforms benzyl acetate when you want a pronounced fruity-tutti-frutti effect in a composition. It works beautifully in jasmine accords where you want the flowers to feel lush and tropical rather than austere. Add it to oriental and amber bases for fruity warmth, or use it in red and yellow fruit reconstructions—strawberry, apricot, plum, and grape all benefit from its sweet juiciness.

products.name: Benzyl Salicylate
products.description:
Benzyl Salicylate is a wonderful light floraliser, fixative and solar aroma chemical that can be used at high doses to provide a soft and delicate canvas upon which to layer rich florals.

It is indispensable for transforming a blend of eugenol, patchouli and lily of the valley into the famous Mellis accord, key to such fragrances as Coco and Poison.

Some people cannot smell benzyl salicylate but will still perceive its effect in a fragrance.

As mentioned Benzyl Salicylate blends beautifully with all types of Patchouli and florals but especially Ylang-Ylang.

products.name: Bergamot Oil FCF, Côte d'Ivoire
products.description:
Forget everything you know about bergamot. Côte d'Ivoire bergamot grows under equatorial sun in West Africa, and it shows. The oil opens with recognisable bergamot brightness but quickly reveals a warmer, rounder, more honeyed character than any Italian oil you have smelled. The sharp green-terpenic edge of Calabrian bergamot is absent here.

This is an LMR captive — a material specially offered to us and unavailable to independent perfumers through normal channels. The terroir shifts the entire balance of the oil toward tropical-fruity warmth. Where Italian bergamot leads with crisp aldehydic freshness, this leads with sun-ripened sweetness and a soft floral undertone that sits comfortably in the heart, not just the top. It lasts noticeably longer on a strip than its European counterpart.

Use it when you want bergamot's signature without bergamot's sharpness. It excels in oriental-citrus fusions, amber accords that need a golden top note, and any composition where a conventional bergamot feels too cold or too brief. This is a genuine rarity — treat it as one.

products.name: Bergamot Oil FCF, Organic
products.description:
This is bergamot for people who already know what bergamot smells like and want more of it. The organic cultivation produces a fuller, more three-dimensional oil — the familiar bright citrus top is there, but underneath it you find a richer floral-sweet body and a smoother, less terpenic drydown than conventional FCF.

Compare it directly to our CAPUA 1880 Bergamot "Superior" Oil FCF — both are excellent, but the organic takes a different path. The linalyl acetate heart is broader and more expressive. The green-peppery facets soften into something almost tea-like. This is the bergamot you choose when the formula is simple enough that every ingredient has to justify its presence.

Use it wherever you would use standard bergamot FCF and want the quality to show. It earns its place in stripped-back soliflores, transparent colognes, and any composition where the citrus top note IS the story. Furocoumarin-free and skin-safe without compromise.

products.name: Bergamot Oil FCF, Terpeneless
products.description:
Despite appearing in, arguably, the most famous perfume in the world (Chanel No 5), Terpeneless Bergamot is virtually unknown today. It has the characteristic delicate Earl Grey tea quality that we all love in a quality Bergamot oil, but in a concentrated form, without the sharp fresh notes.

When would you consider using terpeneless bergamot over regular? When you have a perfume that needs an elegant and refined bergamot note more for its scent than its top note lightness. Fragrances designed for very high parfum or extrait concentrations (such as No 5's original 38% strength) tend to have a different ratio of notes, with top notes being reduced in favour of heart and base. That is where bergamot terpeneless shines and it is the logic behind Ernest Beaux's decision to use it.

This Bergamot oil is free of furocoumarins, making it safe for use in large quantities.

Origin: Calabria, Italy
Variety: Citrus sinensis
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source and molecule distilled

products.name: Bergamot Oil Melito
products.description:
In Melito di Porto Salvo (25km from Reggio) there can be found two treasures — the first is the holy image of the Madonna of Porto Salvo, and the second the locals call "Green Gold"… Bergamot Melito.

The finest bergamot in the world grows in the Calabrian region of Italy and Melito di Porto Salvo is home to the most revered crops. For that reason we present it here in its purest form. This is not bergaptene or furocoumarin free. This is 100% pure and natural green bergamot oil and you will never find better.

Hand selected by Fraterworks, this is the very same quality bergamot used by master perfumers such as Jean Carles, Ernest Beaux, Edmond Roudnitska, the heads of the House of Guerlain and many others.

Fortunately, while IFRA restricts the amount you can use of this oil, it is still perfectly permissable up to 0.4% of your finished fragrance. Max it out and then top up with our superior Bergamot Oil FCF Calabria which is, in itself, a masterpiece of modern citrus meets molecular science.

Origin: Melito, Calabria (Italy)
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source

products.name: Bergamot Oil Spugna, Calabria
products.description:
Spugnato bergamot oil is richer, rounder, and more floral than any machine-pressed bergamot you have smelled. The hand-sponging preserves delicate jasmine-like sweetness and an oily-herbaceous depth that industrial extraction destroys. The drydown is warm, tobacco-balsamic, and remarkably persistent for a citrus oil.

Spugnato means 'sponged' — the rind is pressed by hand against a natural sea sponge, with no machines, no metal, no heat. Traditionally the sfumatori worked through the night, protecting the delicate essence from the Calabrian sun. Before machines arrived in 1840, this was the only way bergamot oil existed.

Fraterworks is currently the only supplier on earth stocking spugnato bergamot oil. Ongoing supply is not guaranteed — treat this as a rare, one-off treasure. Once it is gone, there is no certainty it will return.

Dior used oil extracted with this method in a one-off limited supply of their Sauvage fragrance (not Eau Sauvage) and commissioned CAPUA 1880 to produce the oil. The process was so time consuming that even CAPUA will no longer make this oil on demand and Dior now utilised the same highest quality FCF Bergamot that we stock.

products.name: Bergamot Reggio
products.description:
Bergamot Reggio is a reconstruction of Calabrian bergamot pure and natural. As an alternative to bergaptene free oil this base is vastly superior, offering more personality and vibrance than the chemically degraded natural.

Surpassing all other bergamot bases in quality, this is a one for one replacement for the natural oil that can be used with virtually no restrictions as it is IFRA compliant up to 88% of the finished product!

products.name: Bergamot “Superior” Oil, FCF
products.description:
CAPUA 1880's Calabrian bergamot oil FCF (furocoumarin* free) is produced using a highly specialised cold extraction process that removes restricted furocoumarins (including bergapten) without any damage to the oil. Because of the process used, this bergamot oil remains 100% natural. There is no doubt this is one of the highest quality FCF bergamot oils on the market and the closest to the classic pure and natural oil. It is so good it even retains some of its true colour!

Most furocoumarin free bergamot from other suppliers is modified with a chemical process involving caustic soda; as a result the oil is often damaged to a point that while it may still smell of bergamot, it lacks much of the beauty of pure bergamot oil. Furthermore, caustic treated oil may often not be considered natural.

You will not find a finer and more true to the classic Italian green bergamot oil than Fraterworks' bergaptene free Bergamot “Superior” Oil. Our oil can't be beaten, and neither can our price!

* Furocoumarins (or furanocoumarins) are a type of molecule that react with human DNA in the skin, causing changes which makes the skin extremely sensitive to sun damage. Some common furocoumarins are bergapten, bergamottin, psoralen, and xanthotoxin.

products.name: Bergamote 000136
products.description:
Bergamote 000136 from Firmenich opens with bright, sparkling citrus — clean bergamot zest with a subtle herbaceous-tea undertone. It reads as brighter and more lifted than the natural oil, with a fizzy, almost champagne-like quality. Firmenich captive molecules give it a character you cannot build yourself.

Natural bergamot oil is phototoxic. Remove the offending compounds and you get bergamot FCF, which solves the safety problem but often loses character in the process — most FCF oils are stripped flat. This base gives you the full Calabrian bergamot impression without that compromise, and with batch-to-batch consistency natural oil cannot guarantee.

Use Bergamote 000136 as a direct substitute for bergamot oil or FCF in any fine fragrance formula. Fraterworks also carries its own bergamot reconstruction, Bergamot Reggio, built to the same purpose but with different character. Try both side by side to find your preference.

products.name: Berryflor
products.description:
Berryflor opens with a soft, fruity raspberry impression wrapped in jasmine warmth and anisic transparency. The effect reads more floral than fruity — ripe berries filtered through something clean and sweet. A gentle balsamic backdrop smooths everything into a quietly complex whole.
