This Givaudan creation works best as a modifier — quiet on its own, transformative in a blend. Even trace amounts soften floral accords and add convincing berry realism. Use too much and the composition drifts toward a muddy, damp character, so dose with care.

Pair Berryflor with beta-ionone and raspberry ketone for lush berry hearts. It harmonises naturally with Isoraldeines and ionones, bridging fruit and flower within woody or musky bases. Twenty-four hours on blotter gives your fruity accords genuine staying power.

products.name: Beta Pinene
products.description:
Beta-Pinene is the softer, greener side of pine — woody and citrus-tinged rather than sharp and camphoraceous. Where Alpha-Pinene hits with an aggressive needle-like blast, Beta is more diffusive and rounded. A dry, spicy quality, almost balsamic, ties it closer to lemon peel and nutmeg than turpentine.

Use Beta-Pinene for sophisticated citrus reconstructions, especially lemon and lime, where it adds a natural backbone without Alpha's medicinal punch. It brings a "snapped twig" greenness to floral and woody compositions that smells genuinely botanical. In spicy accords, its nutmeg-adjacent quality pairs naturally with clove and cardamom.

Blend Beta-Pinene with limonene for natural-smelling lemon and lime reconstructions — it's the backbone that makes citrus accords smell real rather than synthetic. Pair it with galbanum and green notes for a fresh, botanical greenness. In woody compositions, it adds a snapped-twig naturalness that grounds heavier base materials.

Beta-Pinene vs Alpha-Pinene

Beta and Alpha-Pinene are closely related but smell and behave quite differently in a formula. Beta is the softer, greener of the two — a dry, woody-citrus character with spicy-balsamic undertones and no camphoraceous bite. Alpha is sharper and more aggressive, with piercing pine-needle and turpentine qualities. Beta is prominent in lemon, lime, and nutmeg oils; Alpha dominates in turpentine, rosemary, and sage.

In practice, Beta blends more seamlessly into citrus and woody heart notes

products.name: Beyond Blue™
products.description:
The Fraterworks® Perfumer's Palette™ is a range of dyes that can be used alone or in combination with each other to add vibrance and colour to your perfumes or cosmetic products. Our proprietary blend of FD&C and D&C colours are sold in liquid form.

Perfumer's Palette colours contain distilled water which is perfectly safe for alcoholic perfumes in the quantities needed for colouration. Typical use is from 0.01–0.5% of finished product.

At these low levels, staining of clothing or skin is minimal to none but you should always test your finished product against white cloth or paper.

products.name: Bicyclononalactone
products.description:
Bicyclononalactone is a creamy and sweet lactone but with a distinctly tonka and hay character. Its has a subtle earthiness that makes it far more interesting than many of the other lactones that tend to be variations on a theme of coconut or peach.

Use it as an interesting alternative to Coumarin in a classic fougère and as a replacer for Dihydrocoumarin which is prohibited in many places except when naturally occurring in plant extracts.

Bicyclononalactone is used to great effect in such scents as Ambre Narguile (2004) by Hermès where it is found at an enormous 4% and Grand Soir (2016) of Maison Francis Kurkdjian at a more reasonable 1.5%.

products.name: Bigaflower™
products.description:
Bigaflower opens with the bittersweet glow of fresh orange blossom, all dewy white petals and sunlit neroli. A crisp green petitgrain note cuts across the top, sharp and leafy. Underneath, a soft creamy sweetness rounds everything into a smooth floral whole.

This is a truly beautiful complete orange blossom heart in a single bottle, built on a generous dose of MANE captive Bigarane™ for that green petitgrain freshness. Use it to brighten citrus colognes and add a natural, just-picked lift. It also smooths and fills out heavier white florals.

Push Bigaflower into fruity accords and it lends a creamy, marshmallow-like softness that tames sharp edges. Small amounts ground a cologne in believable neroli; larger ones turn a fragrance fully into orange blossom. Let its green side carry your topnote and the floral warmth linger below.

products.name: Bigaradier Heart
products.description:
This is petitgrain bigarade stripped down to its most beautiful fractions — the floral, the woody, the delicate. What you smell is orange flower water in concentrated form: cosmetic, slightly green, with a subtle violet-like quality from its ionone content. The harsh herbal top notes of whole petitgrain are gone.

Use it wherever you want a neroli-like florality without neroli's price. It furnishes a sparkling top that lifts citrus-floral-woods structures and adds unexpected contrast to amber bases. In eau de colognes, it sits between bergamot and lavender, supplying the orange blossom character that makes classic formulas glow.

The refined character means it blends without dominating — a trait the whole oil rarely achieves. Try it in chypres where the green-floral facet bridges oakmoss and citrus. In rose compositions, it introduces a clean, soapy freshness. Pair with neroli oil for a richer orange blossom effect, or with linalool and petitgrain for a modern cologne heart.

products.name: Biocyclamol
products.description:
Biocyclamol opens deceptively mild—patience rewards you here. Give it time on the blotter and a beautiful muguet-cyclamen character emerges with impressive tenacity and diffusive power. The green-floral heart feels genuinely natural, lacking the ozonic, aldehydic, or lactonic distractions common in modern muguet materials.

This sesquiterpene alcohol is chemically related to farnesol but offers a distinctly different olfactory experience. Found naturally in cyclamen flowers, it brings authentic botanical character to your compositions. The material works at remarkably low dosages while delivering substantivity exceeding 36 hours—exceptional performance for a floral note.

Use Biocyclamol to anchor muguet accords with clean, smooth naturalism. It pairs beautifully with Takasago's Biomuguet for extended linear radiance into the drydown. The material also enhances neroli compositions unexpectedly well, adding floral volume without heaviness.

products.name: Biomuguet
products.description:
Biomuguet delivers a muguet character unlike the classical aldehydes. This is abstract, luminous, faintly metallic — more ozonic radiance than sweet lily. A creamy floral body sits underneath the aldehydic lift, with subtle citrus and green facets that give it a distinctly modern feel.

Takasago produces this from sugarcane-derived farnesene, making it bio-based though not classified as natural. With Lilial and Lyral banned in Europe, Biomuguet offers an unrestricted muguet building block for compositions that need floral luminosity. It softens harsh green and citrus notes while adding shape, rhythm, and diffusive volume.

Pair Biomuguet with Biocyclamol (it's related alcohol) for the complete muguet experience — the aldehyde provides top-note radiance while the alcohol extends into the drydown. It also works beautifully with Hedione in jasmine-muguet accords. Strong at the top but moderate longevity on its own.

products.name: Birch Tar Oil, Purified
products.description:
Warm smoke and charred wood, then a sweet, oily leather note emerges underneath — unmistakably Russian leather. This purified grade has had the harsh medicinal bite stripped away. What remains is the heart of birch tar: pure, smooth cuir with extraordinary diffusion.

Fraterworks carries three grades of birch tar oil. Rectified is the standard perfumery grade — smoky and leathery but with a rough, medicinal edge. Clear is the same oil decolourised; purified goes furthest, stripping out the harshest notes to leave only the smooth leather heart.

Pair birch tar with castoreum and isobutyl quinoline for a full Russian leather accord, or with styrax and labdanum for a smoother amber-leather effect. It bridges beautifully into oud and tobacco compositions. Work from a dilution — the diffusion is extraordinary.

products.name: Birch Tar Oil, Rectified
products.description:
Just because Birch Tar is mostly used in very small amounts doesn't mean we can't find the most beautiful example of the material. Far too often perfumers seek the lowest cost birch tar but at Fraterworks we consider that every material must be truly exquisite to be used in our fragrances and bases and sold to our clients and customers. And so we present this marvellous product from Payan Bertrand.

Payan Bertrand's rectified Birch Tar from Finland is a model of good behaviour. It sits smoothly in a blend with absolutely no unwanted meaty or fishy notes that so often mar lower-quality versions of this natural.

Because of the strength and cost of this birch tar we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural triethyl citrate which means it is still compatible with natural perfumery. Even at 10% dilution this oil is still very strong, so we suggest diluting further to 1% where its effect is still noticeable (as evidenced in our Aventus demonstration formula below).

If you prefer something a little easier to dose and historically interesting, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840.

We are also offering our signature Birch Tar Clear oil which is IFRA compliant, low colour and more refined.

Origin: Finland
Part: Bark
Process: Distillation followed by rectification

products.name: Birch Tar “Signature” Oil, Clear
products.description:
Payan Bertrand is the master of Birch Tar and so we stock their wonderful rectified product — IFRA safe and not fishy. But we are now offering another of their marvels: Birch Tar Clear.

While rectified Birch is the scent of camp fires and outdoor winterly adventures, Birch Tar Clear is the scent of pipe ash, cigars and warm hearths — and it's IFRA compliant too! This clear oil is also about 50% lighter in colour than standard rectified oil. Clear Birch has a more refined and complete scent and has hints of boozy liquor and vanilla. This oil also has less top note impact making it more useful when a smoky dry down is wanted without the dirty top notes that can sometimes be apparent in other birch oils.

Because of the strength and cost of this clear birch tar we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural triethyl citrate which means it is still compatible with natural perfumery. Even at 10% dilution this oil is still very strong, so we suggest diluting further to 1% where its effect is still noticeable (as evidenced in our Aventus demonstration formula below).

If you prefer something a little more historically interesting, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840.

Origin: Finland
Part: Bark
Process: Distillation followed by rectification for IFRA compliance and decolourisation

products.name: Bisabolene
products.description:
Bisabolene opens with an immediate recognition factor—this is the warm, resinous sweetness you detect at the heart of genuine myrrh and opoponax absolutes. The material presents a remarkably complex profile that explains its pivotal role in recreating some of perfumery's most precious naturals. Beyond its primary balsamic-spicy character lies a sophisticated interplay of woody warmth, subtle citrus facets, and even delicate floral whispers that allow it to bridge multiple fragrance families with extraordinary grace.

This material's true genius lies in its ability to recreate the authentic signatures of prohibitively expensive natural materials. Deploy bisabolene at 0.5-3% when reconstructing myrrh or opoponax accords—it provides the crucial molecular backbone these resins are built upon. More remarkably, it makes an important contribution to the recreation of oud, offering perfumers a lower cost pathway to this increasingly rare material. Its presence in natural bergamot and lemon oils explains why it adds such authentic depth to citrus reconstitutions, transforming flat synthetic citrus into living, breathing recreations. Use it as a fixative for neroli at 0.1-0.5% to anchor those fleeting orange blossom notes without masking their delicacy.

products.name: Bitter Orange Oil
products.description:
Bitter orange oil is more complex and, in our opinion, more interesting than sweet orange oil. It is, however, quite restricted by IFRA with an allowance of up to 3% of your finished product. 

Bitter orange (also known as bigarade or Seville orange) is the fruit from which the original Marmalade was made. The finest qualities come from Europe where adulteration is unlikely.

According to Steffan Arctander: "The odor is very peculiar, fresh and yet "bitter" in the sense of "dry", but with a rich and lasting, sweet undertone. There are notes which remind of bergamot, grapefruit and sweet orange, but overall, the odour is distinctly different from that of other citrus oils. It is a different ype of freshness, a peculiar floral undertone which occasionally shows indolic notes, and a comparatively good tenacity."

It is interesting to note that cold pressed citrus oils are not technically essential oils as they do not undergo distillation.

Origin: Calabria, Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source

products.name: Black Agar Givco® 215/2
products.description:
Black Agar Givco is one of (if not THE) most popular replacer bases for agarwood (oud). It is a rather bright (and rather loose) interpretation of the natural oil and has very elegant nuances of olibanum and amber which makes it a particularly good blender. 

Black Agar Givco is built around a hefty dose (around 9%) of Amber Formate (Oxyoctaline Formate) accented with naturals such as patchouli oil, amyris wood, cedar, labdanum, frankincense and guaiacwood.

This is what Givaudan has to say of the material: “Odor: Woody, Ambery, Olibanum. Use: Agarwood is a classical material used in perfumery. When this wood is infected by fungi, it develops dark streaks charged with an odouriferous oleoresin. The darkest grade, black or true agar, resembles black stone because of the intense impregnation of oil. This resin is highly valuable due to its rich, complex, powerful, woody-ambery scent. It is however an extremely expensive material that is difficult to find.”

Black Agar Givco is a new base reflecting the typical odour of the black resin of agarwoood. This complex, powerful formulation with a resinous character brings together olibanum and balsamic/oriental notes.”

products.name: Black Currant Bud Abs MD 37% TEC
products.description:
This is a very special Black Currant bud absolute from LMR. It is molecular distilled absolute which amplifies the fruity quality of the material while downplaying the sulphurous and unpleasant side-notes. It is a rare material and LMR doesn't typically advertise its existence, reserving it for special uses and clients (such as Hermès).

The most notable feature of this absolute is just how clean and refined it is. The balance is almost hard to believe for a natural extract of this type. It is also decolourised making it very useful for modern perfumery.

Use it as a one for one replacer for Black Currant Bud 50% as the refined nature of this product gives it more top note presence.

Once you try this black Currant bud absolute you will be a convert for life. 

Regulatory

Please note that Black Currant Bud absolute is unrestricted by IFRA and can, as such, be used at any level in a finished perfume. However, LMR performs its own Human Repeated Insult Patch Test (HRIPT) and have an internal company limit of 1.1% of the finished fragrance. The IFRA certificate we offer below is a Fraterworks issued certificate under IFRA 51 and is the necessary legal limit. The LMR certificate based on a combination of IFRA 51 AND HRIPT can be downloaded here.

Origin: Burgundy, France
Part: Buds
Method: Solvent extraction and molecular distillation

products.name: Black Datura
products.description:
BLACK DATURA® is a powerful fragrance base developed by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour for Fraterworks. Inspired by the enigmatic Datura flower—renowned for its intoxicating beauty and hallucinogenic potency—this base explores the intersection of seduction and danger. Sweet, creamy floralcy is laced with soft spice and a narcotic depth that expands on skin like a velvet shadow.

Perfumery Usage

BLACK DATURA® offers bold character and long-lasting diffusion, ideal for adding richness and mystery to florals, orientals, and modern chypres. It blends especially well with Tuberose, Cumin, Suederal®, and dark ambers. Use sparingly to add tension, or in full bloom as a central floral theme.

Process

This complex base is composed of layered synthetic florals, trace spice notes, and select naturals, carefully balanced to reflect Datura’s rich scent and symbolic weight. The composition pushes the boundary between the hypnotic and the forbidden, staying true to the flower’s role in folklore and ritual.

Background

Datura’s infamy in medicine, mythology, and magic is matched only by the beauty of its flower. BLACK DATURA® brings this contradiction to perfumery: it is lush yet unsettling, refined yet raw. It offers perfumers a tool to express the darker side of floral storytelling.

BLACK DATURA® is the Poison Bloom of The Night Garden—beautiful, narcotic, and not to be trusted.

Creative Director: Jamie Frater
Master Perfumer: Bertrand Duchaufour
Fragrance Composition House: Frat

products.name: Black Opoponax
products.description:
Opoponax bases are a subset of amber (or ambreine) type bases; both are loaded up on citrus, animalics, resins and sweet crystallines (vanillin and coumarin in very high doses usually). While Ambreine bases are usually erogenous and very vanilla-oriented, Opoponax bases are drier, more agrestic and often featuring lower (but still significant) amounts of crystallines.

A classic base, Black Opoponax was used by Jacques Cavallier in the classic men's oriental fragrance Opium Pour Homme (1995) at around 5%. This base is extremely versatile and fits just as nicely into a post-modern fragrance as it did into the '90s YSL hit.

Absolutely IFRA compliant and built entirely without the use of any musks (nitro or otherwise), this base is an excellent fixative. With judicious amounts of luxurious oriental resins, natural Mysore sandalwood and patchouli Aceh oil, Black Opoponax is a fragrance in its own right.

products.name: Black Pepper Absolute
products.description:
Black Pepper Absolute is nothing like the essential oil. Where the distilled oil gives you bright, terpenic freshness, the absolute delivers the deep warmth of freshly crushed peppercorns — leathery, smoky, almost tar-like, with an animalic dirtiness hiding in the base.

Solvent extraction captures heavy, non-volatile fractions that steam distillation misses — the eugenol warmth, the tobacco and old-leather facets, the barnyard undertones. This makes it indispensable for leather accords and oriental bases where a lighter pepper note would vanish. Pair with oud, labdanum, or birch tar for seriously dark territory.

The absolute also works beautifully in rose compositions — the warmth rounds and deepens the floral character without overpowering it. Try it alongside castoreum and vetiver for a smoky-leather backbone. Dose carefully: this is thick, concentrated material with real potency.

This is extracted in a two step purification process using propylene glycol which is suitable for perfumery but most often seen in the flavours industry.

products.name: Black Pepper Oil
products.description:
Black pepper oil is a surprisingly versatile spice which blends very well with the salicylates, other spice oils and earthy naturals like Vetiver. 

For a novel use of black pepper try using it with a sweet rose to add texture and warmth or make a spice blend that departs from the beloved clove, cinnamon and cardamom combo.

Out Black Pepper Oil is produced by Floral Concept a company with an exceptional understanding of the subtle nuances of spice oils. It is rounded, balanced and very well behaved. This is now the only black pepper oil we use.

products.name: Black Tea Supreme
products.description:
This beautiful Fraterworks base represents fine black China tea of the variety used by Sir Joseph Banks who invented Earl Grey Tea (later named for Banks' friend the second Earl Grey, prime minister of England).

It is a full bodied robust tea base built around many rich and luxurious naturals. It will impart a top to bottom tea note and can be used in very small amounts to overdose though we recommend something in the vicinity of 0.5 – 1%.

Add Bergamot for a distinct Earl Grey note, or a touch of Fir Needle Oil and our signature rectified Birch Tar to mimic Lapsang Souchong tea.

products.name: Black Tea “Signature” Resinoid
products.description:
A very refined and distinctive black tea note that has absolutely no off notes and is considered a signature speciality of Payan Bertrand. It is really one of the finest specimens of tea that we have experienced and we are thrilled to offer it alongside our Black Tea base.

The natural resinoid is found in such fragrances as L'Ombre Des Merveilles (2020) by Hermès, Kilian's Imperial Tea (2014) and Gucci Pour Homme II (2007).

Make a lovely Earl Grey tea note by combining this product with Neobergamate Forte and our marvelous Bergamot Reggio base.

This material is very stiff when cold so heat should be used to liquify it.

products.name: Blackcurrant Bud Absolute
products.description:
Blackcurrant bud absolute has a powerful, tangy fruit note with a very characteristic ammoniac "cat pee" nuance, alongside spicy-woody and green minty-sulfurous facets. This variant from LMR is the very best classic extract of pure Burgundy blackcurrant buds. We also offer a very special molecular distilled version also from LMR.

Use this material as a powerful modifier in trace amounts (often <1% of concentrate) to add sparkling, naturalistic effects. Its exceptional ability to lift florals makes it invaluable for preventing heavy white florals from becoming too indolic. Apply minimal quantities to create seamless transitions between citrus tops and floral hearts.

This material functions as an "exalting agent," brightening compositions with effervescent quality whilst providing remarkable longevity that bridges top through base phases. Its multifaceted profile allows strategic use as a connector between different olfactory families - green facets link to herbaceous notes, fruity aspects harmonise with citrus, woody undertones connect to sandalwood bases.

Apply sparingly in citrus colognes to add sparkling freshness. Combine with galbanum or violet leaf to enhance green facets. Use traces in rose or jasmine bases for surprising naturalness.

products.name: Blackcurrant Mercaptan
products.description:
Blackcurrant Mercaptan presents an intensely sulfurous, catty blackcurrant character with tropical-fruity facets, green onion-like notes, and a distinctive minty-piney undertone from its buchu origin.

You must deploy Blackcurrant Mercaptan at extremely low concentrations (0.005-0.5% maximum, often below 0.05%) using pre-diluted solutions of 1%, 0.1%, or even 0.01% to achieve proper control. This sulfur-containing monoterpenoid transforms dramatically with dilution - overwhelming and harsh neat, but revealing vibrant blackcurrant magic at trace levels. Working with this material neat will almost always lead to a failed batch so do use caution. We sell this material pure and diluted to 10%, 1% and 0.1%.

Combine Blackcurrant Mercaptan with Tropical Thiazole for the quintessential "fuzzy peach-skin" effect, or blend with β-Damascone for rich jammy red fruit complexity. Works synergistically with ionones for realistic berry-violet accords, or pair with cis-3-Hexenol for hyper-realistic "blackcurrant bud" leaf-fruit combinations. Essential partner with Raspberry Ketone for complete berry profiles.

products.name: Blackwood Base 199939 RF17
products.description:
Blackwood Base defies its name entirely. The opening is bright and rosy with a strong rosewood-linalool character — almost sparkling and citrus-touched. It feels modern and clean, nothing like the dark, brooding wood the name suggests. That brightness is what makes this base so versatile.

As it develops, a serious woody-amber character emerges in the heart and base. The rosewood facets recede and a dry, leathery quality takes over, anchored by potent woody captives including Acetarolle, Mysoral, and Myrrhone Neo. Use it in masculine compositions where you want complexity without heaviness, or layer it to build skeletal oud-style effects.

Blackwood Base excels as a structural backbone. Pair it with real oud for added dimension, or combine with patchouli and labdanum for a contemporary chypre foundation. In feminine work, keep it below the point where the pungent topnotes dominate — let the amber drydown do the talking instead.

products.name: Blonde Amber Type Formula
products.description:
In 2022 Clive Christian really hit its stride with this fragrance which I dare say may be the best in its lineup. Formulated by Vincent Ricord who should probably be more well-known than he is, it combines my personal favourite sandalwood accord of Sandalore®, Polysantol® and Javanol® with sweet natural woods and luxurious florals.

Clive Christian has a great reputation for quality and unlike some brands (Amouage and Tom Ford for example) the high price the brand commands really is often justified by the complexity and richesse of their scents.

Top Notes: Petitgrain, Rum, Rock Rose, Bitter Orange, Cardamom, Pink Pepper, Ginger, Bergamot and Grapefruit
Heart Notes: Dried Fruits, Tobacco, Sandalwood, Tuberose, Saffron, Osmanthus, Orris and Jasmine
Base Notes: Tonka Bean, Myrrh, Vanilla, Labdanum, Patchouli, Cedar, Musk and Vetiver

Total Lines: 52
Naturals: 16

products.name: Blood Orange Oil
products.description:
Blood orange oil opens with the bright, zesty freshness you expect from orange peel, then immediately reveals something more. A distinctive tart, berry-like sweetness sits beneath the citrus, giving this oil a richness and depth that standard sweet orange completely lacks. The overall impression is of a fuller, more luxurious orange.

Use blood orange to add premium citrus character to your top notes. It lifts gourmand compositions with a sparkling tartness, bridges citrus and fruity-floral accords naturally, and brings modern complexity to colognes where plain sweet orange would feel ordinary. Slightly better tenacity than standard orange too.

Pair blood orange with black pepper and cardamom for a vibrant spicy-citrus opening. Try it alongside bergamot and neroli for a sophisticated Sicilian hesperidic accord. Blend with elemol, frankincense or sandalwood to extend its fruity warmth deeper into the heart of your composition.

Three orange oils, three distinct characters. Sweet orange is bright, simple, and cheerfully familiar — the classic citrus top note. Blood orange keeps that freshness but adds tart berry sweetness and a fuller body. Bitter orange is drier and sharper, with a sophisticated floral edge closer to bergamot. Sweet lifts, blood enriches, bitter refines.

products.name: Blue Cypress Oil
products.description:
Blue Cypress Oil delivers an extraordinary aromatic signature unlike any other woody material. The thick blue-green liquid exudes powerful woody depth with wonderfully sweet undertones. This rare Australian oil is treasured for its exceptional fixative properties and remarkable tenacity.

This extraordinary material commands attention in woody-oriental blends. Apply at 0.5-2% concentration for optimal results in base accords. Pair with sandalwood, vetiver, or citrus notes to enhance its multi-faceted character. Use sparingly to ground floral compositions without overwhelming delicate notes.

Blue Cypress blends exceptionally well in combination with Ambergris Intense™, Paradisamide®, and Madranol.

products.name: Blue Hemlock Abs, Decolourised
products.description:
Blue hemlock absolute opens with a burst of sweet, juicy forest berries and blackcurrant that immediately set it apart from other conifer materials. A rich caramelised sugar quality reminiscent of warm berry jam underpins the fruitiness. Resinous woody depth and subtle smokiness emerge gradually, grounding those unusual fruity facets. This is almost like liquid fir balsam.

Add this to pine accords for multidimensional forest depth that no synthetic can replicate. In fruity florals the natural berry sweetness reads as genuinely real, not candy-like. Even trace amounts lend unexpected juiciness to citrus compositions and woody orientals.

Build autumn-inspired gourmands by pairing blue hemlock with davana and patchouli for a berry-woods foundation. Use it to add naturalistic depth to forest fantasy accords where synthetic berries fall flat. The decolourised version (which has an orange tone) gives you all this character without staining your blends.

This is extracted onto 80% IPM making it a fully mobile liquid.

products.name: Blue Tansy Oil
products.description:
Blue Tansy Oil pours out a deep ink-blue and smells nothing like the sharp common tansy. The scent is sweet and fruity, like ripe apple and warm honey, softened by a gentle herby-floral haze. A faint camphor coolness keeps it lively.

Use Blue Tansy to bring a natural, chamomile-like sweetness to florals and to soften the green bite of aromatic and fougère accords. It rounds sharp herbs and lends a sun-warmed, fruity glow underneath top notes. A little goes a long way, since its colour and odour both take over fast.

Think of it as a sweetener for herbal and apple-fruity effects rather than a loud feature. Trace amounts lift a chamomile or clary sage heart; a touch more pushes a blend toward jammy, wine-like richness. Its blue tint also tells you instantly how much you have added.

products.name: Bois d'Encens
products.description:
Bois d'Encens is a Robertet all-natural speciality in which olibanum is co-distilled with cedarwood. Co-distillation is the process in which two or more materials are turned into a single essential-oil type material by combining them prior to or during distillation.

Bois d'Encense has the sweetness of fine Virginian cedarwood with the majesty and richesse of exotic frankincense. It is a wonderful material that can be used at quite high amounts. Replace all of some of the cedarwood in your scent for a more oriental touch, or just wrap it in some refined musks or a monolithic accord like Grojsman Plus for a finished perfume.

Bois d'Encens blends wonderfully with smoky Cade oil or Birch tar but don't neglect the Fraterworks treasure Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 which is enormously popular. This also combines marvellously with Artemal and, if you are not tied to IFRA requirements, pure Tree Moss Absolute.

products.name: Bois de Cendres
products.description:
The nostalgic scent of a campfire that radiates with cedarwood and resinous nuances and a powerful smoke note. This is a base with a split personality: it is smoky intensity with extreme radiance from power ambers and some of the longest-lasting wood chemicals in the industry.

Use Bois de Cendres (wood of ashes) at less than 1% as an alternative to birch tar or cade when wanting to represent glowing embers, cinders and floating sparks from a crackling fire. But at 2% IFRA compliance in a finished product, this can also be overdosed to give Tauer's Lonestar Memories a run for its money!

Synergies: Frankincense and resins in all forms but especially Fumencens HTC, Hydrocarboresine, and Olibanum Vulcain.

products.name: Bois de Violette
products.description:
Bois de Violette is a beautiful and very stylish violet base which gives the simplest, cleanest and most elegant form of a violet note to fragrances. While our Violette Bleue focuses on the modern green molecules found in violet leaves, Bois de Violette conveys the wild flowers in their entirety. This is the violet smell that floats on the air and surprises you on a walk through a cottage garden.

If you pick just one violet, this is the one we recommend. In small amounts it can add a purple nuance while in overdose, as is, it contributes the finest violet note possible for a modern fragrance. This violet is built with rare ionone molecules so it really does add a special quality to a fragrance impossible to get otherwise.

This base is classical in its conception but absolutely fits into a modern context perfectly. This is not an old fashioned violet, this is simply “violet”.

Blends beautifully with Iso E Super, Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha, Iraldeine Delta, Epice FW, Dianthine Extra, Cyclamen des Alpes and, of course, Violet leaf absolute.

products.name: Bois Noir Type Formula
products.description:
This is our exclusive deluxe formula for Chanel's Bois Noir (1987) the first public release of what was to become Égoïste just a few years later. When first released Bois Noir didn't sell well so Chanel removed it from the shelves. It eventually found its way back to the public with a few fairly minor tweaks for simplicity. Bottles of Bois Noir are so rare they currently sell in the $2,000 range when they come up on eBay.

When comparing this to the Égoïste Cologne Concentrée the Bois Noir has a softer and more velvet dry down most likely coming from the broader range of musks which were removed in favour of just 0.5% Musk Ambrette in the Égoïste family.

This demonstration formula was derived some inside knowledge and multiple GCMS analyses of a pristine bottle owned by Fraterworks. Comparisons were also made with Égoïste Cologne Concentrée and vintage Ëgoïste.

Top Notes: Bergamot, Rosewood, Green Mandarin, Grapefruit, Lemon, Plum, Anise, Cinnamon
Heart Notes: Lavender, Coriander, Ylang Ylang, Carnation, Geranium Bourbon, Thyme, Tagetes Minuta
Base Notes: Sandalwood Mysore, Amber, Leather, Musk, Labdanum, Myrrh, Tobacco, Castoreum

Total Lines: 50
Bases: 5

products.name: Boisambrene Forte
products.description:
Boisambrene Forte presents a distinctive woody-amber fragrance, characterised by refined cedar-like notes combined with warm ambergris nuances, creating a dry, sophisticated aroma. Its subtle, elegant scent provides depth without being overwhelming, balancing medium intensity with exceptional tenacity.

In perfumery, Boisambrene Forte excels as a powerful, long-lasting base note and effective fixative, significantly enhancing fragrance longevity and structure. Its versatility makes it ideal for woody, amber, masculine, and unisex compositions, and its notable stability in soaps, shampoos, and detergents further broadens its application in both fine and functional perfumery.

products.name: Boisiris®
products.description:
Boisiris is a rich woody heart note with iris connotations which can be used in traces to add volume to a fragrance or in overdose, as in the case of Royal Oud by Creed where it forms a full 12% of the fragrance.

Boisiris' versatility can be seen in its broad uses: in the great Fixobois base of Firmenich (which was sadly recently reformulated) it adds a blending and smoothing effect, while in their Civettte Synthetic it contributes volume and a woody nuance to the animalics.

Boisiris is also found in Duro (2007) by Nasomatto, Candy Aoud (2005) and Elysium Pour Homme (2017) by Roja Dove, Colors Man Black Intenso (2021) by Benetton and 212 Heroes Forever Young (2022) by Carolina Herrera.

products.name: Bornafix®
products.description:
Bornafix opens with a distinctive warmth that sits between dry cedarwood and dusty amber. Unlike the transparent smoothness of Iso E Super, this material has genuine texture - a green, mossy density that evokes sun-baked Mediterranean hillsides thick with rosemary and thyme. The herbal facets emerge gradually, lending an agrestic, almost landscape-like quality that sets it apart from cleaner synthetic woods.

Consider Bornafix when modernising fougère structures - its thyme and lavender-spike facets bridge traditional aromatic herbs to contemporary musky bases. Combine it with Iso E Super and vetiver for complex modern woods, or layer it beneath citrus accords to give them staying power.

products.name: Boronal
products.description:
Boronal opens with a sweet, caramel-touched floral impression that immediately recalls violets, iris and boronia absolute. Hay and soft leather emerge as it develops, alongside a bran-like warmth. The drydown is the revelation: a powdery ambergris character that lasts for days.

This Symrise aldehyde works as a genuine bridge between floral hearts and woody bases. Pair it with ionones and methyl ionones for complex violet accords, or combine with Ambroxan and sandalwood for ambery depth. It adds fruit-forward warmth to osmanthus constructions and powdery richness to orientals.

Blend Boronal with dihydro-beta-ionone for lush orris effects, or with mate absolute and myrrh for dark, resinous florals. It performs well in soap and powder formulations but avoid body lotions where stability suffers. It gives you boronia absolute character at a fraction of the cost.

products.name: Boronia Supreme TruAbs
products.description:
With Boronia absolute at an eye watering price there is a real need for an incredibly high quality completely natural replacer base. This is it. With all the complexity of the natural absolute, this base is magic. It adds floralcy, nuance and luxury to all fragrances. Boronia absolute was a key floral addition to Diorissimo by Edmond Roudnitska.

Boronia is one of those few flowers rich in ionones (along with violet, mimosa and cassie). In the Southern hemisphere it's brief appearance marks the start of summer as it stains the air with its profoundly beautiful scent.

Like our amazing Rose de Mai Supreme, this base is created scientifically for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from pure and natural Boronia absolute.

Due to the high cost of this replica, we sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Boronia Supreme TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing.

This product may contain traces of nicotine: < 3ppm.

products.name: Bouleau Pyrogene 1840
products.description:
In days past, birch tar (le bouleau pyrogéné) was used in its crude form. Modern safety requirements mean that it must now be rectified via distillation to be used in cosmetics and fragrances. This rectification process removes unwelcome molecules but it also destroys a large number of safe and decidedly beautiful ones. This results in a piercing "smoke essence" far stronger than the original and lacking much of its character. Classic birch tar was more than just smoke: it was sweet, it was woody and it was evocative.

Using a sample of a well-preserved batch of crude birch tar from 1840 as a guide, we were able to reconstruct this treasured oil in the form of a base. Centred around a heart of IFRA compliant rectified birch tar, Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 includes many natural materials and highly specialised aroma chemicals that allow us to offer a product that not only smells just like the real thing, but is also balanced when used in bold doses; indeed you may use this up to 1.81% of your finished product though we suggest far less.

The base opens with an appealing hint of herbal medicaments making it an ideal companion to intense florals such as Tuberose Absolute and Ylang-ylang, especially the Extra Superior quality. Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 is animalic, smokey and woody with accents of florals, fruit and wild honey.

This is the true birch tar profile so beloved of perfumers like Ernest Beaux who used it liberally in Bouquet De Catherine (later Rallet Le No 1 — formula below),

products.name: Bourgeonal®
products.description:
Bourgeonal opens with a burst of fresh, watery lily-of-the-valley — clean, dewy, and immediately recognisable. A bright aldehydic edge rides on top, giving it sparkle without harshness. Underneath, a quiet woody-sandalwood depth anchors the freshness and extends the drydown.

This is the muguet note you build accords around. It slots naturally into aldehydic florals, green bouquets, and fresh compositions where you need a clean floral heart. Pair it with Hedione and hydroxycitronellal for a convincing lily-of-the-valley that reads as lifelike, not soapy.

With Lilial no longer available in the EU, Bourgeonal covers similar muguet territory with its own greener, more openly aldehydic character. Evaluate from a 10% dilution; neat, the aldehydic top can mislead. Avoid pairing with Aldehyde C-11 (Undecanal) — it suppresses the muguet.

products.name: Bouvardia DL
products.description:
Bouvardia was an iconic 20th century De Laire base of citrus with orange flower and jasmine nuances. Beloved by Francois Coty and used skillfully in L'Origan (at 0.8%), it is now available to the market for the first time in decades.

It hints at the highly scented notes of both flowers and due to its somewhat ambiguous nature blends beautifully with many other floral materials. It is a wonderful nuancer for top notes based on bergamot and it is beautifully at home in oriental types. 

This early De Laire base is more of a citrus top note base than a heart base, making it a rather unique product.

products.name: Boxtree Absolute 50% TEC
products.description:
Known to most of us as trimmed and shaped hedges à la Edward Scissorhands, living Boxtree (buxus) has a characteristic grimalkin scent not dissimilar to an odour exhibited by some black currant extractions. MANE's boxtree absolute does not have that urinous note, instead being primarily woody with complex moss and iodine nuances. It also has a very unique fruity character in the opening which hints at the scent of cooked ripe bananas.

Boxtree absolute is an interesting material to use when considering one's options for replacing highly restricted oakmoss and tree moss absolutes. It is intensely green and in its normal form a solid mass similar to very high quality pure castoreum absolute. For that reason we supply it at 50% dilution in natural triethyl citrate, making it possible to use it in all natural perfumes.

Origin: France
Part: Twigs

products.name: Brahmanol
products.description:
Brahmanol smells of rich, creamy sandalwood with a warm musky glow underneath — soft, enveloping, and remarkably close to santalol, the heart of natural Mysore oil. It lacks the delicate floral top of the real thing, but that creamy, skin-like warmth is unmistakable, and a touch of hindinol can be used to fill that gap. Brahmanol lasts over 400 hours on a blotter.

Use it as the foundation of sandalwood accords, either alone at high concentrations or blended with other sandalwood materials for a more complete picture. It adds creamy depth to floral compositions — tuberose, jasmine, and ylang-ylang all benefit from its warm, musky support. It is one of the most versatile and underrated sandalwood materials available.

Where it sits in the sandalwood basic synthetics family matters. Sandalore is the most widely used replacer — sweet, creamy, powerful, with a slightly synthetic edge at high doses. Sandela is drier and more transparent, a background contributor. Ebanol is the most powerful of the group, rich and milky-sweet with a buttery maple quality. Bacdanol splits the difference between creamy and rosy, with a distinctive milky sweetness. Brahmanol is none of these. It is more musky and less floral than the natural oil, more restrained than Ebanol, warmer than Sandela, and less overtly sweet than Sandalore. Think of it as the workhorse sandalwood — reliable, tenacious, and honest. Hindinol, Polysantol, Firsantol and Javanol pack the power of the bunch and, so, are typically

products.name: Bran Absolute
products.description:
Bran absolute opens with a rich, buttery warmth — toasted wheat grain, the honeyed sweetness of a just-baked biscuit. Dried apricot and hay facets emerge quickly, giving it a sun-dried pastoral quality that sits somewhere between bakery and field. The drydown settles into soft pecan nuttiness with a whisper of chocolate.

This is a textural material. It fills the gap between sharp gourmand synthetics and the lived-in warmth of real food. Drop it into a tobacco accord and watch the harshness smooth out. Use it beneath tuberose or jasmine and the florals gain a honeyed, skin-warm quality that feels expensive. It pairs particularly well with dried fruit notes, tea accords, and anything amber-adjacent where you want golden warmth without cloying vanilla.

Bran absolute has solubility quirks — its waxy nature means it can cloud in high-alcohol solutions. Pre-dissolve in a warm carrier or blend it into your base notes first. It fixes beautifully and extends the life of lighter materials around it. Think of it as liquid cashmere: invisible structure that makes everything above it feel richer.

products.name: Buchu “Extra” Oil
products.description:
Buchu Betulina is a flowering shrub from South Africa (which should not be confused with Korean Buchu AKA garlic chives or Allium tuberosum) with a strong and distinctive odour of blackcurrant (particularly its cat-pee quality) and peppermint. It is not for no good reason that one of the most sulphurous and intense aroma chemicals in perfumery is named after it: Buchu Mercaptan (Thiomenthone).

It has still to find its place as an overdose material though it does make up a distinct part of Tom Ford's Azure Lime (2010), Calvin Klein's CK Free (2009) where it is blended with Juniper, tobacco, coffee and Armoise and Calice Becker's Killing Me Slowly (2014) for Kilian where it combines with Black Currant and Lychee.

Use Buchu Oil to add interesting and natural fruit notes to synthetics or to bring out certain aspects of other naturals.

This Extra oil from Payan Bertrand is superbly extracted, with a particularly refined and almost tamed top note making it far more versatile than those of other manufacturers.

Owing to its high strength and cost, we are also offering this in a 10% solution with natural triethyl citrate (an odourless natural extract from citrus).

products.name: Buddhawood “Mulacro” Oil
products.description:
Buddhawood oil (AKA “Mulacro” oil) is the steam distilled extraction from the Buddha Wood shrub (Eremophila mitchellii), a native Australian plant that is also known as false sandalwood or desert rosewood.

Dark brown in colour, this viscous essential oil has a wonderfully soft woody smell with subtle traces of smoke and spice. It is effective in doses under 1% (though it could potentially be used in overdose) and it is a superb naturaliser and enhancer of all members of the Iso E Super family and amber materials.

Blends of cinnamon leaf oil, muscade absolute and theaspirane are sublime and the oil works wonderfully with grapefruit and rhubarb notes.

This is a highly deceptive material, seeming to be mild or ineffective but its ability to add velvety naturalness and luxury to wood synthetics is unparalleled. Great skill is required to use this oil to its fullest potential.

products.name: Butter “Signature” CO2
products.description:
This Butter CO2 is a wonderful non-vegan natural which can be used in traces to add naturalness and richness to a scent or in larger doses to add character go a gourmand as in our demonstration formula for Sora Dora's Jany (see below).

This comes in a solid waxy form but gentle warmth will bring it to a liquid state. As natural animalics become more scarce we highly recommend this product as it is a much needed filler for a gap in the market.

The scent of Butter CO2 is characteristic of fresh butter (this is used in the flavour industry also) with a mildly butyric acidity in the top. It is very useful for adding creamy notes to florals and woods (especially sandalwood) and it blends beautifully with the likes of Acetoin and Sulfurol.

products.name: Butylated Hydroxytoluene (BHT)
products.description:
BHT arrives as white crystalline powder with the faintest whisper of phenolic character that vanishes entirely once dissolved at working strength. This near-odourless profile makes it the perfect silent protector in perfumery. You'll detect nothing at the 0.1% level typically used to stabilise volatile aldehydes and citrus oils.

Transform your most fragile materials into shelf-stable champions by adding BHT directly to pure aldehydes upon receipt. Watch as those temperamental aliphatic aldehydes maintain their sparkling character instead of degrading into rancid acids. Citrus oils retain their zesty freshness for years rather than developing stale terpene notes. Dissolve crystals directly in your fragrance concentrate before dilution for seamless incorporation and complete protection.

Combine BHT with tocopherols for synergistic antioxidant power that outperforms either alone. Add citric acid to chelate trace metals that catalyse oxidation. This multi-pronged approach delivers superior stability using lower total antioxidant levels—perfect for meeting modern formulation demands whilst maintaining exceptional performance.

products.name: Cabreuva Wood Oil
products.description:
Sweet, woody and floral with a metallic hint of tinsel, Cabreuva oil is a wonderful material for adding natural richness and complexity to orange blossom and neroli type fragrances and, owing to its very high nerolidol content, many other florals that need naturalising or lift.

Cabreuva is an excellent blender for wood materials (especially Cedarwood) and has great longevity so it can be used as an interesting fixative alongside the more common synthetics.

products.name: Cadamba Attar
products.description:
The cadamba tree produces golden globe-shaped blossoms during the Indian monsoon season — round, spiky, and intensely fragrant. These are gathered at dawn and distilled into sandalwood oil over about fifteen days, with fresh flowers added daily. The yield is vanishingly small, making cadamba one of the rarest of the classical Indian attars.

The scent opens with a surprising cool, almost minty flash, then settles into thick, honeyed, powdery sweetness unlike any other flower. It touches on champaca, neroli, and orange blossom without precisely duplicating any of them. Arctander described its staying power as "almost incredible" — flowers wrapped in a damp cloth held their fragrance for over a week. That tenacity carries through to the finished attar.

Use cadamba as a honeyed floral heart in orientals, or alongside champaca for a lush, narcotic Indian floral accord. It pairs well with ylang-ylang, neroli, and jasmine. Cadamba rewards careful blending — let it support florals rather than lead, and its deep sweetness adds extraordinary persistence to everything around it.

We have an excellent article on Cadamba by Christopher McMahon of White Lotus Aromatics fame that you can read.

products.name: Cade Oil, Rectified
products.description:
Cade oil is the most common alternative to Birch Tar oil but it shouldn't be seen as the poor cousin. In fact Cade Oil (also known as Juniper Tar Oil) has qualities that, to our mind, can make it a superior option. While Birch Tar oil can have an oily quality (and some low class versions - from other suppliers - a decidedly fishy aroma), Cade Tar Oil is drier and bears a stronger resemblance to a freshly extinguished camp fire, ash and all. It is certainly different enough from Birch oil that interesting and novel accords might be come to by blending the two.

For IFRA compliance this oil is rectified which is a distillation process that removes potential allergens and harmful chemicals from the naturally produced tar oil.

If you prefer something a little different, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 or our exquisite Birch Tar Oil, also from Payan Bertrand.

Origin: Spain
Part: Twigs and branches
Process: Burning, followed by distillation and rectification

products.name: Calamus Oil
products.description:
Calamus root essential oil, also known as "Sweet Flag",  is a pale yellow liquid displaying a smooth, warm,  woody-earthy-spicy bouquet with a milky, sweet undertone of very good tenacity. You have never smelled anything quite like this lovely rare oil.

Our calamus oil is wonderful for adding complex and interesting notes to a scent. It's gentle spice is vaguely reminiscent of the scent of cinnamon bark floating on the air while its earthy tones are well rounded and subtle.

Calamus oil can contain around 70% asarones which are highly restricted by IFRA in natural oils to 0.01% of a finished product, however this Payan Bertrand speciality still allows for a maximum use of 0.47% in your finished product. Despite the restrictions this is still a wonderful material to have in the perfumer's palette and is most certainly still useable in commercial scents.

Origin: Korea
Part: Rhizomes
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Calone® 1951
products.description:
Calone® 1951 was discovered in 1966 by chemists from Camilli, Albert & Laloue a fragrance company founded in 1830 and owned by Coty until 1963. It was an accidental discovery in the process of inventing a new tranquilliser which eventually came to be known as Valium. It was named for the first letter of the company (C, A, L + Ketone). The “1951” relates to the chemical registration number.

Calone, a crystalline substance, has the most wonderful odour of fresh air and water with hints of watermelon. It set the stage for the '90s after its patent expired and it began to enter mass production. Fragrances of especial interest were Issey Miyake's L'eau d'Issey (1992) by Jacques Cavallier, Pierre Bourdon's Cool Water for Davidoff (1988), and Aramis New West For Her (1990) by MANE's Yves Tanguy with its 1.2% overdose.

Calone® Plus is a Fraterworks® manufactured 50% dilution of Firmenich's quality of this aroma chemical fortified with traces of other materials to round it out and boost its performance. This product is easy to use because it comes in a liquid form, making it a cinch to add to your formulas.

products.name: Camphor Crystals
products.description:
Camphor Crystals hit the nose with an immediate sharp, cooling blast — clean, dry, and purely camphoraceous. A herbal-minty quality underneath connects it to rosemary and lavender. This is a trigeminal material: you feel it in your sinuses as much as you smell it.

Use camphor in traces to add sharp freshness and clarity to aromatic and fougère compositions. It cuts through heavy materials like patchouli and myrrh, bringing air and definition. In lavender accords, a touch reinforces the natural camphoraceous facet that's already present in good lavender oils.

Pair camphor with eucalyptus and rosemary for medicinal-aromatic effects, or with bright citrus for a clean, bracing opening. Small doses alongside incense and resinous materials create an unexpected cool contrast to warm, smoky bases. Dose carefully — camphor overwhelms everything if overdone.

products.name: Cananga Oil
products.description:
Cananga oil is not ylang-ylang. They share the same species but come from different varieties, different islands, and different distillation methods. Where ylang-ylang from the Comoros is bright, sparkling, and overtly floral, Javanese cananga is heavy, woody-leathery, and balsamic. The great perfume writer (and spy) Arctander was emphatic: they are not interchangeable in character or in function.

Ylang-ylang is fractionally distilled into grades — Extra, I, II, III — letting you choose brightness or depth. Cananga is a single complete distillation: the whole flower in one oil, from the lightest floral top to the heaviest balsamic base. That gives it a roundness and tenacity that no single ylang-ylang fraction matches. It also survives alkaline conditions, making it far more reliable in soap formulations where ylang-ylang's bright topnotes simply fall apart.

Use cananga oil in leather accords alongside castoreum, labdanum, and birch tar — this is one of its classic roles. It anchors fougères with balsamic warmth and lends lasting power to oriental bases. Think of it as the dark, serious side of the ylang family: less pretty, more powerful, and built to last.

products.name: Canthoxal
products.description:
Canthoxal is a light anise aroma chemical with facets of liquorice and a very delicate wateriness. 

Canthoxal blends beautifully with Armoise Oil, Basil Oil, Spanish Anise Oil, Toscanol, Anisic Aldehyde (and others members of the same family).

Canthoxal has the very rare distinction of having had its IFRA limit considerably liberalised in the latest standard, going from 0.82% to the much larger 2.5%.

products.name: Canthoxalia
products.description:
This material offers a richly layered profile built around a persistent, inviting sweetness that defines its charm. At its heart lies a distinct anise or liquorice note, evoking the nostalgic depth of root beer, with a soft hawthorn edge that feels both floral and faintly medicinal. A powdery veil lends refinement—delicate, cosmetic, and unmistakably vintage—tempering the sweetness with a soft-focus finish.

Balancing its warmth is a green-fresh brightness, adding lift and subtle complexity, at times reading as marine or dewy. It draws frequent comparison to mimosa absolute, sharing that same warm, honeyed floralcy with a plush, gently animalic undertone. Hints of orange blossom add radiance, while a whisper of spice and a dry cortex-like texture round out the base.

Due to the viscous nature of this material, we are selling it diluted to 50% in TEC or pure.

products.name: Cantryl®
products.description:
Cantryl smells wild — damp undergrowth, crushed herbs, pine needles, and hay all at once. It has a raw, almost untamed quality that instantly reads as "outdoors." There is real woody depth underneath the herbal freshness, with hints of juniper berry and rosemary. Despite being a top-note material, it lasts remarkably well — over 40 hours on a blotter.

The practical value here is twofold. First, Cantryl strengthens and lifts herbal notes — lavender, rosemary, clary sage — without adding sweetness or distortion. A small amount makes these familiar materials smell more vivid and natural. Second, it is exceptionally stable in difficult bases including shampoos and acidic cleansers, where many green-herbal materials fall apart.

Use Cantryl in fougère compositions alongside lavender, coumarin, and oakmoss for a green-herbal lift. It adds a natural, peely freshness to citrus accords and brings realism to violet leaf notes. Work from a dilution — it is potent and can dominate unexpectedly at higher concentrations. A little goes a long way.

products.name: Caprylic Acid
products.description:
Caprylic acid natural takes its name from the Latin word for goat (caper), and the connection is immediately obvious. It smells fatty, waxy, and unmistakably animal — warm goat milk with a cheesy, rancid edge. At trace levels it reads as creamy warmth; push it higher and the barnyard appears.

Use it in micro-doses to add animalic body and creamy depth to leather accords, boozy rum notes, and gourmand compositions. A tiny amount dirties up overly clean white florals or adds realistic goat-milk character to lactonic blends. It also functions as a linking agent in chypres, bridging mossy bases to citrus tops. Always work from heavy dilution.

Pair it with castoreum and labdanum for full leather, with delta decalactone and gamma nonalactone for creamy milk effects, or with indole to push white florals into animalic territory. It lasts over 336 hours on a blotter — a true fixative. Coconut oil is its richest natural source.

products.name: Caramel Acetate
products.description:
Caramel acetate has a fascinating dual personality. At full strength you get warm toffee, brown sugar, and molasses with a baked-bread quality. Dilute it to traces and it shifts to a soft, sweet strawberry. This concentration-dependent behaviour makes it versatile — a single material serving two very different roles.

Use caramel acetate in your gourmand and oriental compositions where you need authentic caramel warmth and toffee sweetness. At higher levels it builds convincing brown-sugar accords. At lower levels it contributes a fruity strawberry facet that blends beautifully into floral and fruity hearts.

Pair with vanillin and ethyl maltol for rich caramel-gourmand effects. Try it alongside lactones for creamy toffee depth. Blend with fruity esters to exploit its strawberry side — even a trace adds a soft, sweet, berry-like warmth that lifts an entire composition.

products.name: Caraway Seed “Superior” Oil
products.description:
Caraway seed (actually a fruit not a seed) is often confused with cumin seed due to the similarity in appearance (both are from the Apiaceae family). The main visible difference is that Caraway seeds are crescent shaped with raised ridges while cumin seeds have smoother ridges and are not curved.

The main odiferous component of caraway is carvone giving it a herbal minty quality while cumin has a more animal or skin like scent owing to the cuminaldehyde dominance.

Caraway seed features in Le Male by Francis Kurkdjian for Gaultier (1995), Declaration by Cartier, Tom Ford's Santal Blush (2011), and the beautiful Hypnotic Poison (1998) by Dior.

Our oil hails from the Netherlands, long the preferred source of Caraway seed oil to the top luxury fragrance houses. 

Origin: Netherlands
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Carbinol Muguet
products.description:
Carbinol Muguet opens with soft, clean floral freshness—delicate yet substantial. The lily and hyacinth character feels natural and unforced, while sweet rose undertones add warmth. A gentle violet nuance and mild herbaceous quality round the profile beautifully, creating something that feels lifted yet grounded.

Arctander considered this material "probably the most valuable and versatile of all the so-called carbinols"—high praise indeed. It combines the best qualities of linalool and terpineol without their drawbacks: none of linalool's volatility and none of terpineol's woody-piney character. Use it as a structural floraliser at levels from 2% up to 25% of your concentrate. It builds floral body in muguet, rose, jasmine, and magnolia compositions while working equally well as an undertone in chypres and non-florals.

The 244-hour substantivity makes Carbinol Muguet exceptional value for floral work—your lily character persists beautifully into the drydown. Blend with linalool and linalyl acetate for lifted muguet effects, or pair with lindenol, orris, and cinnamyl alcohol for complex floral hearts. It serves a similar structural role to benzyl salicylate but with a distinctly different character.

products.name: Carbitol™
products.description:
Carbitol is a low gravity low odour diluent with the faintest hint of an alcoholic scent. It is the best solvent for cardboard and car diffusers and it finds use in many historic animalic bases in rather high amounts where its delicate odour contributes more than just solubility.

Carbitol may primarily be a solvent but it is not a stranger to fine fragrances, being found in fairly decent amounts in 212 For Men (1999) by Alberto Morillas for Carolina Herrera, Moon Dance (2014) by Juliette Has A Gun, YSL's Opium Pour Homme (1995, Jacques Cavallier), and Pour Lui (1980) by Oscar de la Renta.

products.name: Cardamom Absolute
products.description:
Cardamom Absolute is a rich and long lasting extraction from green cardamom pods harvested in Guatemala. It has a similar profile to the essential oil but is much more intense. Despite being an absolute, it has a rather interesting and vibrant top note presence with a clear ginger nuance making it very useful from top to bottom as a replacer or booster for the oil.

Owing to the high cost we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural triethyl citrate, an odourless extract from citrus.

Interpreting Arctander: “Cardamom Oil has been used in perfumery for centuries, first written about in 1540 by Valerius Cordus. The oil is pale yellow to light brown and darkens in sunlight. Its scent starts strong and fresh, like eucalyptus, but softens into a warm, spicy, and woody aroma with a sweet floral touch. It is long-lasting and adds depth to any fragrance.

In perfumes, cardamom oil brings a warm sweetness and spicy richness. It works well in floral bases like rose and lily of the valley. It also adds warmth to Oriental fragrances, chypres, and powdery scents. Cardamom blends beautifully with oils like bergamot, ylang-ylang, and labdanum. Coriander oil is its perfect partner, making the scent more complex and refined. For perfumers, it is a versatile and essential ingredient.”

We also offer the finest steam distilled essential oil of cardamom and Cardamom CO2.

products.name: Cardamom CO2
products.description:
Cardamom CO₂ is a luxurious extraction that captures the true soul of cardamom with unmatched depth and purity. Unlike traditional methods, this gentle technique preserves the full aromatic spectrum, unveiling a vibrant, spicy warmth interwoven with hints of sweet resin and fresh citrus undertones. Its exceptional clarity and aromatic potency make it indispensable for perfumers crafting refined fragrances where authenticity and complexity are paramount.

Used at just 0.2–0.5%, Cardamom CO₂ adds a captivating spicy elegance without overshadowing delicate accords. Its versatile nature makes it a harmonious partner for bright citrus oils, sophisticated woods, and rich balsamic notes, enhancing depth and dimensionality in compositions. A subtle touch in the top notes brings an alluring, spicy sparkle that instantly elevates any fragrance, making Cardamom CO₂ an essential ingredient in the palette of the discerning perfumer.

products.name: Cardamom “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Green cardamom (the queen of spices) is a radiant gem in perfumery. While most suppliers sell oil from Ceylon and India, the supreme variety comes from the lush volcanic nation of beautiful Guatemala. In its native land of India, the spice is held in such high esteem that it forms a vital part of the festival dish payasam, a sweet and highly fragrant rice pudding.

Our cardamom oil comes from the highest grade of green cardamom pods and is the ultimate extraction of the spice. So much so that we call it our signature oil.

Interpreting Arctander: “Cardamom Oil has been used in perfumery for centuries, first written about in 1540 by Valerius Cordus. The oil is pale yellow to light brown and darkens in sunlight. Its scent starts strong and fresh, like eucalyptus, but softens into a warm, spicy, and woody aroma with a sweet floral touch. It is long-lasting and adds depth to any fragrance.

In perfumes, cardamom oil brings a warm sweetness and spicy richness. It works well in floral bases like rose and lily of the valley. It also adds warmth to Oriental fragrances, chypres, and powdery scents. Cardamom blends beautifully with oils like bergamot, ylang-ylang, and labdanum. Coriander oil is its perfect partner, making the scent more complex and refined. For perfumers, it is a versatile and essential ingredient.”

products.name: Caress Musk
products.description:
Caress Musk is a soft but powerful white musk blend blend that contributes elegance, richness and depth to a scent without dominating. Its blends with vanilla odourants are supreme but it also works wonders in floral compositions.

Use it in an overdose like you would the Grojsman accord or in small amounts to add complexity and interest to your fragrance while benefiting from its extraordinary fixative power.

Caress Musk is beautiful in its own right and can be worn as a complete fragrance.

Blends with Cashmeran, Grojsman Accord, Ambreine Samuelson, Vanillin “Signature”, Ethyl Vanillin, Vanilla Supreme, Solafleur™ and Celestafleur™.

products.name: Carnation “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Carnation absolute is as rare as hen's teeth and getting rarer by the day. We have searched high and low to bring you the very finest carnation extract. We found that perfect extract in LMR one of the few large scale companies that produce this absolute. With LMR comes the guarantee of compliance with set standards meaning you don't have to worry that the next batch will vary wildly as is the case with the small batch makers.

In the words of LMR: “A warm powdery floral note that has a spicy clove-like body, gives a green olive impression, and has a herbaceous fruity background with honey undertones.”

products.name: Carrot Heart MD
products.description:
Carrot heart from LMR is a revelation! Starting with a luxurious extraction of seeds from finest French carrots, a molecular distillation process gives us the purest heart. This unique product from one of France's most esteemed luxury oil producer is rich with notes of apricot skins in the opening and fresh earth and classic powder in the dry down.

In the words of LMR: “We source our carrot seeds from France in July, mainly from the South of France, but also from Anjou and Normandy.⁣ To create this extract, our sourcing experts have carefully selected the highest quality of carrot seeds that were destined to be discarded. [This is] a classic perfumery ingredient with a sustainable twist.⁣”

Origin: France
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation at source followed by molecular distillation

products.name: Carrot Seed Oil, Vaucluse
products.description:
While cheap and cheerful carrot seed oil from India is widely available, the very precious Vaucluse carrot seed oil is not so. The French take their carrots very seriously and unlike we étrangers who like our vegetables crisp and cold, French gastronomes know that carrots are best after aging; limp and warm is the name of the game en France.

Vaucluse is renowned for its carrots and, indeed, the seeds of the same. Vaucluse carrot seed oil is a wonderful blender for iris materials, adding naturalisation to synthetics and nuance to naturals. It has a slightly tangy quality with accents of earth after gentle rains, musky cumin seeds and sweet apricots.

Comparing this oil to the Indian, we find the French to be vibrant and transparent with a very discreet carrot nuance, while the Indian oil has a decidedly muddy aspect which can stifle the delicate odour. The Vaucluse oil practically dances.

Origin: Vaucluse, France
Variety: daucus carota
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Carvacrol
products.description:
Carvacrol opens with an immediate assault of dry, penetrating phenolic intensity that announces its presence unmistakably. This is not the gentle herbaceous note of lavender or the sweet spiciness of basil—this is the concentrated essence of sun-baked oregano and wild thyme stripped of all sweetness and comfort. The material presents a stark, medicinal quality that bridges the gap between kitchen herb and apothecary cabinet, with camphoraceous undertones that create a cooling sensation despite the inherent warmth of its spicy character.

In perfumery applications, Carvacrol serves as a powerful modifier for creating authentic Mediterranean herb accords, particularly valuable when you need the characteristic pungency of oregano without resorting to the variable and often oxidation-prone essential oil. Deploy it at trace amounts to 1% maximum in fine fragrance, or up to 4% in functional products where its remarkable stability in alkaline conditions truly shines. This phenolic powerhouse maintains its character in harsh soap bases where other spicy notes decompose, making it invaluable for masculine grooming products and heavy-duty cleaners requiring a "clean" medicinal signature. Its complete lack of sweetness differentiates it crucially from thymol—where thymol offers warmth with a gentle sweetness, Carvacrol provides uncompromising dryness and intensity.

The material excels in building complex aromatic accords when combined with rosemary, sage, and lavender for dry herbal co

products.name: Carvacryl Methyl Ether
products.description:
Carvacryl Methyl Ether opens with the sun-baked essence of Mediterranean herbs, capturing oregano's warmth without its medicinal edge. This methylated derivative strips away carvacrol's harsh phenolic character, revealing cleaner herbal facets. Its dry spiciness mingles with subtle citrus peel notes, creating natural complexity.

This middle-note material bridges fleeting citrus tops with heavier bases beautifully. You'll find it invaluable for extending aromatic themes deep into your composition's heart, preventing abrupt transitions between volatility levels. It modernises classic fougères by adding garrigue warmth to lavender hearts, while in contemporary chypres it creates intriguing herbal contrasts against bergamot and patchouli bases.

Use it at 0.5-3% to naturalise synthetic accords or boost authenticity in herb-forward compositions. Pair it with black pepper for vibrant spicy diffusion, or combine with vetiver to accentuate dry earthiness. In trace amounts, it adds unexpected spicy depth to carnation reconstructions and green texture to white florals.

products.name: Caryophyllene Acetate
products.description:
Caryophyllene acetate delivers a smooth, dry, woody-amber character with a distinctive vetiver-like earthiness. It is far more refined than raw caryophyllene, which can feel harsh and dusty. Subtle fruity and spicy facets warm the drydown, and the overall impression is of a polished, amber-tinged wood — versatile and easy to blend.

Use this material to add dry woody depth and vetiver-like character to your orientals, chypres, and woody compositions. It extends and refines vetiver accords beautifully, contributing a cleaner amber warmth. As a fixative it is outstanding, anchoring volatile top notes while adding its own woody signature to the base.

Blend with vetiver and patchouli for a rich, earthy woody foundation. Try it alongside sandalwood and ambroxan for modern amber-wood accords. Pair with oakmoss and clove for classic chypre constructions where its smooth woodiness adds lasting depth.

products.name: Caryophyllene Beta
products.description:
Caryophyllene Beta greets you with a dry, dusty woodiness wrapped in warm clove spice. There is something of lacquered church pews about it—sweet, polished, and quietly persistent. The peppery edge fades into a clean, oily-woody drydown that lingers for hours.

This material does serious heavy lifting without demanding attention. Use it to build spicy foundations in orientals and fougères, or to anchor volatile top notes like cinnamic aldehyde that need a fixative partner. It provides an unrestricted clove-like spiciness, making it a practical alternative where eugenol limits become a concern.

Blend Caryophyllene Beta with gum resins and balsams for warm, incense-like depth. Try it alongside black pepper oil and nutmeg for layered spice accords. At low doses it adds woody complexity to florals; pushed higher, it brings a confident, dry spiciness that reads unmistakably masculine.

products.name: Caryophyllene Oxide
products.description:
Caryophyllene Oxide opens with a crystalline woody sweetness that immediately distinguishes itself from its precursor β-caryophyllene. You'll detect a refined dryness reminiscent of aged cedar and antique furniture with none of the dusty harshness. Its spicy warmth suggests clove and black pepper but smoothed and mellowed through oxidation.

It seamlessly connects spicy top notes to woody bases while adding depth to oriental structures. You'll find it indispensable for creating realistic spice reconstructions where it provides the warm woody body beneath sharper phenolic notes. Its unique dry-sweet character prevents fruity accords from becoming cloying while lifting heavier base materials.

products.name: Cascalone®
products.description:
Cascalone® is the latest member of the Calone® (discovered 1966) family and when compared has a fruitier and more watery quality. Like Calone, Cascalone is crystalline, and so we offer it pure and in 50% dilution with DPG.

Traces of cascalone add freshness, lift and modernisation to a fragrance, while overdoses can be used to introduce interesting and unusual effects.

Cascalone and Calone® Plus blend perfectly. It also works beautifully with related chemicals Helional, Floralozone, and Cyclamen Aldehyde and bases such as Amazonia™, Celestafleur™ and Verdantol.

products.name: Cascarilla Bark Oil
products.description:
Cascarilla bark oil is a wonderful spicy oil extracted from the bark of the croton eluteria tree. Most production of the oil takes place in the Bahamas. Our cascarilla is a delight to the senses with an odour profile that walks the line between nutmeg, black pepper and ginger.

The bark, dried and processed to remove sapwood and heartwood, yields a pale yellow to amber liquid with a spicy-aromatic, warm-woody, and slightly peppery scent reminiscent of nutmeg, myrtle, and hyssop. Its top note may not appeal initially, but its diffusiveness and strength make it a valued "trace" component in perfumes.

Renowned for its complex spiciness and warm, woody undertone, Cascarilla Oil has intrigued perfumers, finding use in chypre bases, Oriental fragrances, men’s colognes, and fantasy scents. It pairs harmoniously with materials like nutmeg, pimento berry oil, oakmoss, and coumarin, offering depth and intrigue to high-class perfumes. Though often underestimated, its versatility and power make it a key asset in sophisticated fragrance design.

Deceptively powerful, cascarilla is perceptible at less than 1% of a fragrance. Cascarilla is part of the secret formula for Campari, the wonderful Italian liquor, and featured in the classic Coty fragrance, L'Origan.

products.name: Cashmeran®
products.description:
Cashmeran® has it all — fruit, florals, musk, wood and spice. It is one of the most interesting materials in the perfumer's palette and really quite indispensable these days. Fragrance marketers often refer to it as “Cashmere Wood” or “White Wood” but there is so much more to it.

Cashmeran® works from traces to overdose, as evidenced by the nearly 7% used in By The Fireplace (2015) by Maison Martin Margiela where it blends with Boisambrene Forte, Z11 and a massive 4% of Trimofix. A mere whisper exploits Cashmeran's fruity side in Tom Ford's Lost Cherry (2018), and we would be remiss not to mention the astonishing overdose of 25% found in Duro (2007) by Alessandro Gualtieri for Nasomatto where Spirambrene and an additional overdose of Javanol at 3.5% focus its woody energy.

products.name: Cassie Absolute, Egypt
products.description:
Cassie and mimosa are both members of the Acacia family. Mimosa is sweeter and more refined, while cassie is fuller bodied and complex. Both are essential naturals for perfumers, with mimosa often appearing as a rich floral note in fine fragrances and cassie being used to create masterful floral bases or add a je ne sais quoi. Cassie is a wonderful naturalizer and can round out and enrich fragrances at mere traces in much the same way as violet leaves do.

For clarification, we offer the following:

Mimosa (Acacia dealbata or decurrens): Natural Absolute, or Mimosa de Provence [base]
Cassie (Acacia farnesiana): Natural Absolute [this product], or Fleur de Cassie [base]
Pink Acacia: Unrelated to the acacia plant family this is faux acacia or Black Locust.
