Cassie absolute blends exceptionally well with the aforementioned bases as well as Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute, Violette Bleue and the classic synthetics of this family Isoraldeine™ Cetone Alpha (Givaudan), Iralia® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF).

Because of the high cost of this material, we are also offering it at 10% in natural odourless triethyl citrate.

products.name: Cassiffix®
products.description:
Cassiffix is a very special material in the world of black currant odourants. It fills rooms with its diffusion, it lasts a day on the smelling strip (unlike most similar materials which are fleeting), and it is devoid of the sulphurous note that black currant extracts and chemicals exhibit.

Boost its fruity qualities with damascones (delta and beta in particular) or add it to a grapefruit or rhubarb accord for an effect similar to that of Un Jardin sur le Nil by Jean Claude Ellena. Given the huge dose of beta damascone in Firmenich's Dorinia SAE base, Cassiffix has great potential to combine with it to make a whole new style of fruity rose.

Its sweeter and cleaner profile also means it can tolerate overdosing so it is very versatile and certainly deserves a place in every perfumer's organ.

Cassiffix has a synergy with Feuille de Cassis, Cassis Base 345 B, and Blackcurrant Mercaptan.

products.name: Cassis Base 345B
products.description:
This classic blackcurrant base from Firmenich is so ubiquitous you'll recognise it immediately upon smelling even if you've never purchased it before. It features in an overdose in Un Jardin Sur Le Nil by Jean-Claude Ellena for Hermès where it forms part of his green mango accord, and is found in traces in virtually every modern department store fragrance.

When you need blackcurrant, this is the base you should turn to. Use it in amounts up to 0.1% to add nuance, radiance and a light fruity connotation to the opening of your fragrance, or in higher amounts for a distinctly blackcurrant note. 

And don't be fooled by the name, Cassis Base 345B is also floral (particularly in the rose direction), green and minty. The versatility of this base cannot be overstated.

We stock 345B because it is the favoured version of this base. Firmenich also makes a cheaper 345F.  Cassis Base 345B delivers warm, fruity notes with ripe blackcurrant sparkle, consistently producing professional results. It offers reliability and sophisticated depth that perfumer wearers appreciate. 345B's exceptional warmth provides that perfect finish most projects demand. 345F exists as a cooler, greener option, but lacks the refinement and balance of 345B.

products.name: Castoreum Firbest®
products.description:
Castoreum Firbest opens with a warm, leathery-animalic character—smoky, phenolic (somewhat akin to calamine lotion), and unmistakably reminiscent of traditional castoreum. There are birch-tar facets and a sweet, resinous undertone that softens the smoke. As it develops, a musky sensuality emerges with hints of fruitiness in the drydown.

This is Firmenich's Firbest reconstruction of castoreum, created without any animal-derived ingredients. The Firbest technology combines natural and synthetic materials to replicate the olfactory profile of traditional castoreum absolute—the warm, animalic, leather-like sweetness that made natural castoreum essential in classic chypres, fougères, and leather perfumes. Use it wherever you need that distinctive smoky-phenolic warmth and animalic depth.

Castoreum Firbest is clearer in colour than traditional natural extracts, making it suitable for a wider range of applications.

products.name: Castoreum Hyperessence 50% TEC
products.description:
Robertet's Castoreum Hyperessence 50% TEC is a particularly clean castoreum absolute. Formerly under the Charabot brand (now owned by Robertet), Castoreum Hyperessence tones down the rough edges of the material and enhances the sweet raspberry facets, making for a castoreum absolute of the finest quality and a product much easier to use than most.

Castoreum Hyperessence is solid when pure so we offer it here at a 50% dilution in completely natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus. Use Castoreum Hyperessence anywhere you would normally use Castoreum absolute.

We also offer an intense Castoreum “Signature” Absolute from Floral Concept which has more of a wild character and the elegant and 3% Siberian Castoreum Tincture, the softest of the group.

products.name: Castoreum Synth 184004D
products.description:
Castoreum Synth hits with immediate smoky-phenolic intensity — warm leather, birch-tar depth, and a dark animalic presence that commands attention. Beneath the smoke sits a surprising dried-fruit sweetness, almost plum-like. The overall effect is richer and darker than most castoreum reconstructions.

This Firmenich creation functions as both a standalone castoreum note and a powerful fixative — it smooths transitions between top, heart, and base while adding depth. Use it in leather accords, chypres, tobacco bases, and oud compositions. Even trace amounts transform a blend's character.

Pair with isobutyl quinoline for a green-leather chypre, or bridge into balsamic amber with labdanum and benzoin. At eighty hours on a smelling strip, Castoreum Synth anchors your base notes with extraordinary persistence. Dose carefully — its odour impact is immense.

Castoreum Synth and Castoreum Firbest are both Firmenich castoreum bases, but they differ in construction and character. Firbest achieves its animalic note through natural sources (non-animal) and reads clearer and more phenolic. Synth uses captive synthetic molecules to deliver a darker, richer profile with distinctive dried-fruit depth that Firbest lacks.

products.name: Castoreum Tincture 10%
products.description:
This replaces our previous Canadian castoreum tincture (9 years aged) which is now sold out. This new product is one of great refinement owing to the extremely high quality wild castors we have used to produce this special tincture. In comparison to our Siberian tincture, this is less smoky and more typical of the scent most people associate with classic castoreum.

‘Castoreum [tincture's] warm, animal, leather-like sweet odour makes it an interesting item in “men's perfumes”, fougeres, chypres, Oriental bases, leather notes, Tabac bases, etc. [It blends] particularly well with ambra notes, calamus, cananga, cedarwood Atlas, chamomile moroccan, creosol, labdanum products, isoeugenol, oakmoss products, sandalwood oil, […] etc.’ — S. Arctander. Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin, Carol Stream: Allured Publishing Corporation, 2008, pp. 136–137.

French Name: Infusion de Castoréum

products.name: Castoreum “Signature” Absolute 50%
products.description:
Floral Concept is an expert when it comes to animalics and this Castoreum Absolute is proof indeed. Intensely leathery, this black solid material lacks all of the off-notes characteristic of most other products on the market.

At room temperature Castoreum Absolute is a solid mass requiring heat to make mobile, therefore we are making it available in a 50% dilution in natural benzyl benzoate.

NOTE: our most recent batch was made with 50% castoreum and 50% Triethyl Citrate. We are now using natural Benzyl Benzoate as it gives a much better and more easily controlled solution.

Origin: Canada
Variety: Castor canadensis
Part: Castor Sacs
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Cedarome
products.description:
Cedarome is a rich and mysterious woody base loaded with vetiver, Mysore sandalwood, rose, cedar and more. It has a very long heritage, being first used in L'Origan in 1905. 

This magnificent piece of perfume history can be used as a complete fragrance, or in small amounts as you would use sandalwood or cedarwood in a luscious dry down accord. Absolutely IFRA compatible up to an enorrmous 16.7% of the finished product.

NOTE: Cedarome may crystallise at low temperatures. Warm gentley if necessary.

* Cedarome by Firmenich (formerly CNC) and Sophira (AKA Sophora by Roure) were very similar bases, with Sophira being an artistic copy made by the great Marius Reboul.

products.name: Cedarwood Oil Rect, Texas
products.description:
Cedarwood Oil Rectified Texas opens with clean, sweet woody character—that unmistakable pencil-shavings aroma everyone recognises. Balsamic-smoky depth adds complexity, while dry powdery facets prevent heaviness. The rectification process removes the darker, tarry notes of crude oil, leaving a refined woody profile that works across fine fragrance and functional applications alike.

The cedrol-rich composition provides excellent fixative properties, anchoring more volatile materials. Blend with vetiver, patchouli, sandalwood, and leather notes for classic masculine accords. It works beautifully in fougères alongside lavender and coumarin, and adds dry woody depth to amber and oriental compositions.

Cedarwood Texas vs Virginia vs Atlas vs Alaska

The three major perfumery cedarwoods each offer distinct character. Texas (Juniperus mexicana) is the sweetest and most pencil-like, with pronounced balsamic-smoky depth and excellent tenacity.

Virginia (Juniperus virginiana) is drier and more austere, with a sharper, less sweet profile.

Atlas (Cedrus atlantica)—a true cedar—is the most refined, with cleaner, brighter woody character and subtle camphoraceous lift.

Alaska (Chamaecyparis nootkatensis) is the most complex and unusual, with fresh sparkling grapefruit-citrus top notes, spicy cumin-like facets, and leathery-herbal undertones alongside its woody base.

Use Texas for warm, sweet woody effects; Virginia for dry, austere woodiness; Atlas when you want elegant cedar brightne

products.name: Cedarwood Oil, Alaska
products.description:
Owing to a very high natural content of nootkatene and nootkatone, this treasure from Firmenich has a definite grapefruit character. A fascinating and unique wood oil, Alaskan Cedar is produced entirely from the sustainable offcuts of the forestry industry.

This is also a replacer for the now discontinued Wood 49 of Robertet and is sometimes referred to as Nootka Tree Oil. 

In Firmenich's words: “Not as camphoraceous and smoky as a cedarwood but stronger, longer-lasting and very linear.”

products.name: Cedarwood “Superior” Oil, Virginia
products.description:
Virginian Cedarwood oil (from the cypress family) is the most versatile and important of the various so-called cedarwood oils (the others being Texas, Himalayan and Atlas, the latter two being members of the pine family and not the cypress family).

It is an excellent extender to Sandalwood oil, Guaiacwood and Oud and owing to its refined and low-key odour it can be used as a wonderful canvas material upon which to build an entire fragrance.

This Payan Bertrand quality is of a particularly fine character, with only the nicest aspects of the oil presenting.

products.name: Cedramber
products.description:
Cedramber delivers a powerful woody and velvety amber note with remarkable strength and diffusiveness. Its deep cedar-like character is complemented by a warm amber quality, making it indispensable for perfumers. It gives structure and sophistication to a scent while enhancing spicy-woody accords.

Cedramber pairs beautifully with Iso E Super, Vertofix Coeur, and Cashmeran to create luminous and modern woody blends. In florals, it adds dryness and balance, while in orientals, it melds with labdanum, patchouli and vanillin to deliver a luxurious depth and richness.

Cedramber lends its characteristic elegance to fragrances like Yves Saint Laurent’s Opium for Men (1995), enhancing its spicy oriental depth, and Bleu de Chanel (2010), where it provides a radiant structure to fresh-woody accords. It also demonstrates its wonderful ability to lift rich wood scents in Ajmal's masterpiece Dahn Oudh Al Shams (0.4%).

products.name: Cedrat Heart
products.description:
Cedrat Heart captures the most compelling fractions of citron peel oil — the bright, mouthwatering zest and the elegant bitterness — while discarding the unstable monoterpenes that make whole citrus oils so fleeting. What remains is sparkling, sweet-bitter, and surprisingly tenacious. A candied quality sets it apart from lemon or bergamot.

This concentrated citrus is equivalent to a terpeneless oil, so you use it at roughly one-tenth the rate of whole cedrat. That concentration means citrus character reaches deep into the heart of a composition rather than flashing and vanishing in the first minutes. Classic Guerlain-style colognes depend on exactly this kind of persistent citrus backbone.

The sweet-bitter balance invites creative use beyond pure cologne work. It sharpens vetiver and woody compositions with a zesty edge. In gourmand accords, the candied facet bridges citrus and vanilla. Try it alongside bergamot and neroli for a full hesperidic heart, or with lavender and coumarin for a citrus fougere with real sparkle.

products.name: Cedrat Oil, Italy
products.description:
Cedrat, AKA Citron, is one of the oldest citrus fruit — indeed it is one of the varieties from which most other citrus has developed from. Cedrat has a wonderfully gourmand quality which makes it a wonderful oil to use in modern food-related formulas.

Reminder: this is an essential oil for manufacturing and it is not a food. Do not consume this product.

Origin: Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source

products.name: Cedrene Alpha
products.description:
Alpha-cedrene is the sharp, dry topnote of cedarwood — the pencil-shavings character that hits you first when you snap a cedar branch. It lacks the sweet, balsamic warmth of cedrol or cedryl acetate. This is cedar stripped back to its lightest, driest essence.

Use it to add crisp woody dryness to leather accords, chypres, and masculine fougères. It anchors compositions without adding sweetness, giving you the top fraction of cedarwood oil in isolated, controllable form. It also makes an excellent starting point for building custom cedar accords by blending with richer cedarwood materials.

Pair it with cedryl acetate and cedrol for a full-spectrum cedar effect, or with vetiver and patchouli for dark woody depth. It works beautifully with Iso E Super and its derivatives, adding definition to their transparent warmth. A true workhorse of the woody palette.

products.name: Cedrenyl Acetate
products.description:
Cedrenyl acetate opens with dry, polished woodiness — cedar made quiet and wearable. Vetiver-like depth and subtle amber-balsamic warmth sit beneath the surface. Distinctive peanut and waxy facets give it a rounder, greener character than cedryl acetate crystals.

This is a fixative above all else — four hundred hours of substantivity makes it one of the most tenacious base notes you can buy. Use it to anchor fougères, chypres, and woody orientals with dry cedar depth that never overpowers. It extends top-note life from below without colouring the composition.

Combine with vetiver and patchouli for rich woody bases, or add to sandalwood accords for dry cedar structure. It rounds out amber and oriental compositions with quiet woody warmth. Dose generously at medium strength — cedrenyl acetate rewards bold use.

Cedrenyl vs Cedryl Acetates

Three products share the cedar acetate family, each with its own character.

Cedryl acetate crystals (CAS 77-54-3) are pure cedryl acetate — bone-dry, precise, and solid at room temperature with a melting point around 44°C. 

Cedryl acetate liquid (CAS 77-54-3 / 1405-92-1) is a blend of both materials — mixing the two prevents crystallisation, keeps it liquid at room temperature, and produces the broadest, most natural cedar impression of the three. Choose the crystals for bone-dry precision in delicate florals and citrus. 

Cedrenyl acetate (this material, CAS 1405-92-1) comes from a different cedarwood fraction and gives a softer, greener

products.name: Cedrol Crystals
products.description:
Cedrol crystals open with an almost imperceptible whisper—pure, high-grade material can seem nearly odourless at first encounter. This isn't a deficiency but rather the material's unique character: a soft, dry cedarwood note so refined it lacks the rough edges of cedar oil. What begins as faintness transforms into extraordinary persistence—400 hours on a blotter isn't unusual. The initial impression reveals clean, dry wood with none of the turpentine sharpness found in crude cedar oils. Subtle sweet undertones emerge only in less pure grades, where trace compounds add faint balsamic nuances. The crystalline form ensures maximum purity and consistent performance.

Use Cedrol at 1-10% as your primary fixative when building fragrances that must last. This alcohol excels where other fixatives fail: in alkaline soap bases, it remains stable while musks degrade; in functional fragrances, it provides tenacity without interfering with fresh top notes. Use it as the invisible foundation beneath woody accords, where it amplifies cedar and sandalwood effects without adding its own prominent character. In floral compositions, it provides structural support that prevents ethereal notes from disappearing. Consider it your "tutor note"—present throughout the fragrance evolution, lifting and supporting rather than dominating.

products.name: Cedroxyde®
products.description:
Cedroxyde is a refined woody molecule which, unlike traditional cedarwood notes, has a subtle ozonic quality, imparting a slightly aquatic, invigorating facet.  It gives lift to heavy woody accords and pairs beautifully with other synthetic ingredients like Iso E Super, Cashmeran, or Ambroxan. It works exceptionally well in marine-inspired creations, fresh woods, and contemporary fougères, often serving as a heart or base note enhancer. Its nuanced drydown reveals a touch of creamy smoothness that tempers its otherwise vibrant edge.

Cedroxyde excels when used alongside Sandalwood oils and lactonic elements to create creamy, smooth wood accords. Pair it with bright citrus notes like bergamot or grapefruit for a zesty, refreshing top, or mix it with synthetic amber molecules like Ambrofix or Orcanox for a more profound, resinous base. For green compositions, the ozonic cedar aspect integrates seamlessly with galbanum oil and vetiver aromachemicals like vetiveryl and vetiver acetate.

Notable appearances of this material include Henry Jacques Galileo (2019) by perfumer Christophe Tollemer, Elysium (2017) Roja Dove, Dior Homme Sport (2021) by François Demachy, and Bleu de Chanel Parfum (2018) by Olivier Polge. Cedroxyde also features in the luxurious Bakhoor Al Arais (2012) by Swiss Arabian.

products.name: Cedryl Acetate, Crystals
products.description:
Crystals are the purest form of this aroma chemical and far less common (and much harder to find) than the liquid form. Also sometimes known as Cedrenyl Acetate, this material is a wonderfully soft woody note and has no IFRA restriction unlike the closely related (olfactorily) Cedrene and Cedrol. 

This very long-lasting material is wonderful as a soft wood in floral bases, but also works extremely well as an alternative to Sandalwood, Vetiver and Cedarwood.

Simply add it to your formula in its solid form as the crystals melt very easily.

products.name: Cedryl Acetate, Liquid
products.description:
Cedryl acetate liquid greets you with a clean, dry woodiness—think cedar pencil shavings made velvety. The leather and vetiver-like undertones give it a masculine warmth, while a faint balsamic sweetness stops it reading as austere. It smells like cedarwood distilled to its most wearable essence.

This is the workhorse woody fixative that quietly sits in countless fragrances. Use it to give any composition a smooth, long-lasting woody base without the terpenic top notes of cedar essential oils. It excels in fougères, chypres, and leather accords, but works equally well behind florals, where it adds silent structure and tenacity.

Cedryl acetate is one of the most tenacious materials you can buy—over four hundred hours on the blotter. It anchors ambers and orientals with dry woody depth, extends citrus and herbal compositions from below, and rounds out vetiver and sandalwood accords. Dose generously; its medium strength rewards bold use.

Liquid vs Crystals

The liquid form contains both cedryl acetate (CAS 77-54-3) and cedrenyl acetate (CAS 1405-92-1)—the result of acetylating a broader cedarwood fraction rather than isolating pure cedrol first. This mixture stays liquid because the two differently shaped molecules cannot pack into a crystal lattice.

The cedrenyl acetate component is softer and slightly greener than its saturated counterpart, rounding out the sharpness and giving the liquid a more complete, living-cedar character. Choose the crystals when you want a bone-dry

products.name: Celeriax
products.description:
We use celery seed in perfume to give tuberose brightness and uplift. It works in a similar way to cis-jasmone in fact. Celeriax is a molecule that does a similar thing at a slightly lower cost and with more power. Furthermore, behind its salted-skin façade lies a maple syrup note and a distinct umami quality.

This is a base note material for sure which gives it some interesting potential uses as a booster for restricted oakmoss, and an extender for expensive naturals like opoponax essential oil.

Synergies with celeriax can be found in Immortelle, fig leaf, and nutty notes where it can be effective in bridging nuts and wood. This is an aroma chemical you don't know you need, until you try it, at which point you'll be trying to find excuses to pop it into every blend!

products.name: Celery Seed Oil
products.description:
Celery seed bears little resemblance to the scent of its more well-known celery plant, having really just a faint nuance of green celery. Mostly this material has a warm quality that is not entirely dissimilar to the scent of Cis Jasmone. Unsurprisingly, then, celery seed oil is a wonderworker when it comes to adding naturalness to heady florals; in particularly it adds space and lightness to intense tuberose accords.

Despite its light aroma, celery seed is deceptively powerful and can overtake a blend quite easily, so careful dosing is required.

Origin: India
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Celestafleur™
products.description:
Forget Lyral® and Lilial replacers; now is the time for the ascent of true alternatives that offer beauty and elegance and the benefit of what modern lily and green chemicals have to offer us as perfumers.

Celestafleur™ is radiant and long lasting but it has a quality that really sets it apart from the classic muguet chemicals: it is effervescent. Celestafleur™ sparkles like stars in the firmament and it is from that characteristic that it derives its name.

Usable at a massive 9%, this can be a one for one replacer for Lyral® and Lilial but it can also be overdosed as the foundation of a highly modern monolithic lily scent. Celestafleur™ makes for a perfect general floraliser upon which to layer other luscious flowers, as in the case of Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) for which we present a demonstration formula further down this page.

Celestafleur™ blends incredibly well with citrus oils and has a synergy with green, ozonic and watery chemicals such as Calone® Plus, Cis 3 Hexenol (and its esters), Florhydral, Floralozone, and Helional. Bases such as Amazonia™ are elevated when combined with Celestafleur™, and herbal bases such as Suralette™ Extra and Artemal™ are wonderful with it.

products.name: Celestolide
products.description:
Celestolide is a bright and diffusive musk that can be used at very high doses (though it is also effective in low amounts). Arctander has this to say of it: "Mild, sweet-musky odour with a faint, animal undertone and good tenacity. Relatively stable under normal conditions in perfume creations. May develop a slightly sour note during storage, a note which is appreciated by some perfumers, disliked by others."

Celesolide features in the luxurious Bakhoor Al Arais by Swiss Arabian along with Cedroxyde (for its cedar note) and luxurious saffron in the form of Safranal.

products.name: Centifolether
products.description:
Centifolether opens with fresh, dewy rose petal character reminiscent of Rosa centifolia, the hundred-petalled rose of Grasse. A metallic oxide-like facet adds a modern, lifted sparkle. Subtle anisic and exotic fruit nuances round out an aroma that reads completely natural.

Use Centifolether as a rose oxide enhancer or substitute — it delivers the same rosy-metallic sparkle with far superior stability. In fine fragrance it lifts rose accords at trace levels without ever dominating. Its exceptional chemical stability makes it equally valuable in demanding functional products like laundry detergents and bleach-based cleaners.

Blend Centifolether into green accords where its rosy freshness adds floral complexity. Pair it with linalool and geraniol for classic rose construction, or with citrus oils for sparkling floral-fruity top notes. Its three-hour tenacity on blotter makes it a true top note — layer over longer-lasting rose materials for naturalistic evolution.

products.name: Cervolide®
products.description:
CERVOLIDE® is a rare macrocyclic musk known for its radiant softness and deeply soothing character. A molecule of exceptional pedigree, it blends the airy, fruity grace of Ambrettolide with the sleek, metallic warmth of Habanolide—delivering a musky signature that is both elegantly skin-like and subtly enveloping. CERVOLIDE® reveals itself not as a brute force base note, but as a gentle anchor: quiet, complex, and tenacious.

Its musky presence doesn’t just linger—it soothes, offering you a rare chance to design not just for olfactory impact, but also emotional atmosphere.

Perfumery Usage

CERVOLIDE® excels in fine fragrance, personal care, and functional formulations, where it imparts a natural, second-skin effect. It has remarkable synergy with ambers, florals, and woods, and enhances blooming materials such as orange flower, jasmine, or rose by extending their drydown without altering their core identity. Use it to round sharpness, amplify warmth, or infuse a composition with creamy diffusion and elegant longevity. In white musk accords, it provides a quiet sophistication that cheaper musks often lack.

Performance

CERVOLIDE® is highly stable in soaps, shampoos, and emulsions, with excellent retention on skin and fabric. Despite its fixative strength, it maintains a clean, biodegradable profile—a modern musk aligned with green chemistry values. Its ultra-low vapor pressure allows it to act as a fragrance extender with minimal environmental footprint.

Background

CERVOLI

products.name: Cetalox®
products.description:
Cetalox (racemic ambrox) excels at providing the warm, skin-like quality that makes ambergris notes so addictive in modern perfumery. Use at 0.1-2% for subtle warmth or up to 5% for pronounced amber character. Its creamy facets make it particularly valuable in oriental compositions where it bridges spicy tops with balsamic bases. Its softer profile compared to single-enantiomer versions (Orcanox, Ambroxan, Ambrofix and Ambrox Super) creates a more enveloping, intimate aura.

Combine Cetalox with labdanum and benzoin for classic amber accords, or layer with modern musks for contemporary skin scents. Its versatility extends from supporting rose and jasmine absolutes to amplifying woody materials like cedar and sandalwood. This material provides the foundation for countless modern masterpieces, delivering that distinctive "second skin" warmth consumers associate with luxury fragrances.

Chirality and Material Differences

The distinction between ambrox materials lies in their molecular handedness. Ambroxan (CAS 6790-58-5) consists of a single enantiomer—specifically the laevo form—creating its characteristic dry, crystalline, mineral-like radiance with exceptional sparkle. Cetalox (and generic alternatives), however, are racemic mixtures containing equal parts of both left- and right-handed molecules, resulting in their warmer, creamier, more musky character. This 50:50 blend of enantiomers produces a softer, more linear evolution on skin compared to Ambroxan's sharp brilliance.

products.name: Cetonal®
products.description:
Cetonal is a fascinating material with nuances of tobacco, leather, iris, animals and wood. It has a low odour profile but is surprisingly long lasting and quite profound in its effects at even very low doses (below one percent).

According to Givaudan, “Orris, Woody, Powerful. Cetonal is an elegant ingredient used in woody, orris accords as well as with leather, tobacco and animal notes where it acts as an excellent blending agent and adds to the harmony of a fragrance.”

Its softness shines in accords with Cashmeran, dihydro-ionones, and amber notes, pairing brilliantly with Norlimbanol, Ambrocenide, Boisambrene, Operanide, and Somalian frankincense oil

products.name: Cetylic Alcohol
products.description:
Cetylic alcohol is not an aroma chemical — it is a white waxy solid that melts at around 50°C and resolidifies into a smooth, silky mass. You buy it for what it does, not what it smells like. Its near-total lack of odour makes it an ideal carrier that lets your fragrance speak without interference.

It melts gently with warmth and sets to a smooth, waxy solid at room temperature. Blending it with beeswax and a carrier oil gives you the classic base for solid perfume — a format that is experiencing a genuine revival among niche perfume buyers. It also helps oil and water stay mixed in creams and lotions, giving them that rich, velvety slip.

If you are purely a fine fragrance compounder working in alcohol, you will never need this material. But if you are building scented products beyond the spray bottle — solid perfumes, body balms, scented candles, cream perfumes — cetylic alcohol is foundational.
