products.name: Chamomile Isobutyrate
products.description:
Chamomile Isobutyrate (also known as Isopentyrate) captures the smell of fresh chamomile flowers: fruity, clean and naturally herbaceous, with a soft floral warmth. It reads as bright and true rather than medicinal or sharp. A single material that does the work of a whole chamomile accord.

This is one of the rare materials that genuinely makes things smell more natural. Add it at low levels to synthetic compositions and you'll notice an immediate lift in diffusion and a convincing botanical quality that's hard to achieve any other way.

products.name: Chloroxylenol
products.description:
Chloroxylenol opens with an unmistakable antiseptic sharpness that immediately evokes clean, clinical spaces. This powerful phenolic material carries the signature Dettol aroma. Its penetrating medicinal quality cuts through compositions with surgical precision.

You'll find this material invaluable for creating authentic hospital or medical environments in conceptual fragrances. At extreme dilution, it adds a subtle phenolic dryness to leather accords. Blend it with vanillin to create intriguing, sweet-medicinal contrasts that evoke vintage apothecary preparations.

Use Chloroxylenol sparingly—its potency demands respect. A mere trace transforms woody bases into something darker and more complex. Combine with creosol and guaiacol for intense tar-leather effects that push boundaries in avant-garde perfumery.

Of note, the reason for its dettol like smell is because this is actually a component of Dettol; it has amazing anti-microbial and preservative properties, and while we sell it mainly as an interesting odour chemical, those other facets are a bonus.

products.name: Chocovan
products.description:
With the very high cost of cocoa related materials, Chocovan from Givaudan is a God-send. It has a powerful powdered chocolate profile which, despite its clearly gourmand characteristics, is surprisingly versatile. Traces add a natural powderiness to orris accords, and it blends beautifully with resins for a modern take on the classic oriental form. It pairs beautifully with coffee notes, hazelnut materials like Filbertone, and lactones for creamy dessert accords. 

While we sell it pure, it is highly recommended that you keep a 10% dilution handy as it really is much stronger than it appears to be upon first sniff, and it has a tendency to overwhelm.

The base saves you significant formulation time when chocolate is your target.

products.name: Choya Loban
products.description:
Think about the difference between holding a lump of frankincense resin to your nose and placing it on a glowing coal. Conventional frankincense oil preserves the bright, citrusy, piney top of the raw resin. Choya loban preserves the smoke — it captures what frankincense actually smells like when it burns. The result is sweet, balsamic, deeply warm, and comforting.

Indian frankincense resin is roasted in a sealed clay pot at high temperature, and the aromatic smoke is captured by distillation. The natural balsamic sweetness of the resin survives the charring process, softening the smokiness into something rounded and approachable. Of the three traditional choya materials — raal, nakh, and loban — this is the most immediately familiar to Western noses.

Use choya loban wherever you want the smell of frankincense incense rather than frankincense oil. It excels in dark amber accords, ecclesiastical compositions, and resinous bases where conventional olibanum feels too clean or too bright. Pair it with labdanum, benzoin, and opoponax for a complete temple-incense foundation, or with styrax for added depth.

products.name: Choya Nakh
products.description:
This is one of the strangest materials in all of perfumery. Choya nakh is made by dry-roasting the hard, nail-like trapdoor discs from certain sea snails in a sealed clay pot, then distilling the smoke into sandalwood oil. These same shell pieces appear in the Book of Exodus as an ingredient in sacred temple incense, and they have been used across India, Japan, and the Middle East for centuries.

There is smoke here, certainly, but beneath it lies something oceanic and mineral — a briny, mossy depth with faint animalic warmth that no synthetic marine note can touch. In aged choya nakh, the harsher smoke recedes and the amber-marine character deepens beautifully. It is a natural route to smoky-marine effects that feel organic and alive rather than clean and manufactured.

Use choya nakh with extreme restraint — a single extra drop changes everything. In heavy dilution it reveals extraordinary nuance: salt, dry moss, warm mineral amber. Pair it with oud and labdanum for dark orientals, or use traces in marine accords for a living, salty depth. Best appreciated well diluted before blending.

products.name: Choya Raal
products.description:
Choya raal is made by roasting the resin of the sal tree (Shorea robusta) inside a sealed clay pot until it chars, then capturing the smoke. The sal is one of India's great native hardwoods — sacred in both Hinduism and Buddhism, with tradition holding that Buddha was born and died beneath one.  The result of the distillation smells of dry, mineral smoke with a sweet resinous undertow — imagine standing downwind of a controlled resin fire on a warm night.

This is one of the few genuinely natural leather notes available. The dry, mineral smokiness creates a leather effect that synthetic approaches struggle to replicate. In traditional Indian perfumery, choya raal provides the smoky backbone of complex attars like shamama and hina — the dark foundation that everything else is built upon.

If you know cade oil or birch tar, choya raal occupies similar smoky-leathery territory — but it is noticeably warmer and sweeter because it starts from a balsamic resin rather than wood or bark. Cade and birch tar hit harder, more phenolic, more purely tarry. Choya raal keeps an amber sweetness underneath the smoke that they lack, making it softer and more versatile. Use it wherever you want natural smokiness and leather without harshness, or try it as a warmer alternative to birch tar in leather accords. Pair it with labdanum and cypriol for a complete smoky foundation, or with patchouli for earthy darkness.

Caution: do not confuse the sal tree with the cannonball tree (Couroupita guianens

products.name: Cinnamaldehyde
products.description:
Cinnamaldehyde delivers the unmistakable warmth of freshly ground cinnamon bark—sweet, spicy, and deeply comforting. The balsamic undertone adds richness without heaviness. Honeyed facets emerge as it develops, contributing to that characteristic "red hots" candy quality that makes this material so immediately recognisable.

This aromatic aldehyde comprises roughly 90% of cinnamon bark essential oil and defines the entire cinnamon-cassia olfactory family. The trans isomer predominates and delivers warmer, more authentically cinnamon character than its cis counterpart. Iconic oriental fragrances from Tabu (1932) to Opium (1977) relied on cinnamaldehyde to create their signature spice accords, working alongside eugenol, clove, and nutmeg for multi-dimensional warmth.

Use cinnamaldehyde at 0.5–2% in oriental compositions, 0.1–0.8% in florals, and 0.2–1.5% in masculine woody-spicy accords. Above 2%, the spice character overwhelms. It introduces fascinating warmth when used discretely in rose and hyacinth bases. The material blends beautifully with benzoin (especially Sumatra with its more cinnamic qualities than Siam), labdanum, and other balsamic fixatives that extend its natural tenacity.

products.name: Cinnamic Alcohol ex Styrax
products.description:
In crafting his fragrances, Edmond Roudnitska, the greatest perfumer of his generation, would put as much thought and care into the aroma chemicals as he would the naturals. He would use benzyl acetate ex Ylang-ylang or Jasmine, Geraniol ex Palma Rosa, Linalool ex Bois de Rose, Cinnamic Alcohol ex Styrax and on and on.

This 100% natural Cinnamic Alcohol ex Styrax (a speciality of Payan Bertrand) has to be smelled to be believed. It is so good you simply want to melt into it and fade away in to a world of odour perfection.

Use it in small amounts for a richesse impossible to obtain otherwise, or go wild and overdose in a floral base! It is useable to a very respectable 2.18% of your finished product.

NOTE: because this is a natural isolate, it contains approximately 55% cinnamic alcohol with the remainder being made up of natural phenyl propyl alcohol and natural cinnamic aldehyde from the same extraction source (see associated SDS for more details). This also means the product is in a liquid state making it far easier to use than pure cinnamic alcohol which is a solid at room temperature.

products.name: Cinnamon Bark Ceylon “Supreme” Oil
products.description:
In the golden age of perfumery one type of cinnamon was king: cinnamon bark oil Ceylon with 60% cinnamaldehyde. Our “Supreme” oil is exactly that. No competing product comes close to the exquisite complexity imparted by our precious cinnamon bark oil. Any cinnamon with less than 60% cinnamaldehyde content is an inferior product.

Featured in such masterpieces as YSL Opium (1977), Dior's Poison (1985), and the treasure of the golden age, Jicky (1889) by Guerlain (along with many other Guerlain classics). This is the smoothest and most complete cinnamon bark. It's fullness and subtle nuances even surpass that of modern CO2 extractions! One whiff will transport you to the wild jungles of faraway Ceylon. This is the gold standard of cinnamon extracts.

Blends beautifully with sticky fruit notes (particularly plum), resins and balsams.

Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka)
Part: Bark only
Method of production: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Cinnamon Ceylon Tincture 25%
products.description:
In days past, even though cinnamon bark and leaves had long given up their precious oils to the steam distillers of the 19th century, tincture of cinnamon bark was still a thing and was prized for its softer and more rounded scent profile. Fragrances such as the original Jicky (formula below) capitalised on this by using the tincture to modify essential oil of cinnamon.

This Fraterworks Tincture is made according to the oldest traditions of French infusion manufacture with purest glacial food grade alcohol. It makes for a wonderful alternative to cinnamon oil and SFE products.

Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka)
Variety: Cinnamomum verum
Part: Dried bark
Method: Cold ethanol tincture

products.name: Cinnamon Leaf Oil, Low BAP
products.description:
Cinnamon leaf oil is the unsung hero of the cinnamon family. While the bark oil sits at the head of the table as patriarch, cinnamon leaf is usually relegated to the role of little brother. But ourcinnamon leaf oil is not just a cheap soap oil; it brings a brighter top note spice to fragrances and accents the richer deeper bark oil as well as standing on its own.

Our cinnamon leaf oil from Ceylon has been hand picked from the offerings of numerous suppliers. We are very proud of this Ceylon origin oil which presents with all usual characteristics of leaf oil but with a more intensely rich body and dry down.

Like cinnamon bark, the leaf oil blends beautifully with sticky fruit notes (particularly plum). It is also a wonderful companion to rose in fragrances and works extremely well alongside the classic oriental resins.

Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka)
Variety: Cinnamomum zeylanicum
Part:  Foliage
Method of production: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Cinnamon “Gold” Absolute
products.description:
We stock several cinnamon materials — Ceylon bark oil, leaf oil, the tincture — and each has its place. But nothing we have ever carried smells like this.

Cinnamon "Gold" Absolute is an extraction of the whole bark that captures everything steam distillation leaves behind: the sweet, baked, buttery facets that make cinnamon one of the most universally beloved spices on earth. Where cinnamon bark oil hits you with a sharp, aldehydic top note that can overwhelm a formula at even modest levels, this absolute is smooth from the first moment. It smells the way cinnamon tastes — warm, rounded, confectionery, with a Red Hots candy sweetness that is immediately recognisable and immediately appealing.

The colour is a deep olive green, slightly viscous but readily pourable at room temperature. We also offer it at 20% in TEC for easy weighing and incorporation.

In perfumery, this changes what cinnamon can do. An amber base of labdanum, benzoin, and vanillin — materials that already lean warm and sweet — becomes something extraordinary with the addition of this absolute. The cinnamon warmth integrates seamlessly instead of sitting on top as an aggressive spike. Gourmand compositions that would normally require careful balancing to tame a bark oil can use this absolute more freely, because there is nothing to tame.

It also works brilliantly in contexts where you want cinnamon warmth without the spice-rack cliché: woody-amber accords, soft orientals, tobacco bases, even certain floral

products.name: Cinnamoxal™
products.description:
Cinnamoxal™ opens with sweet cinnamic warmth characteristic of authentic cassia bark from which it naturally crystallises as stearoptene. This material delivers the oily-woody texture found in genuine Cinnamomum cassia oil. The paper-like dryness and medicinal-phenolic undertones create sophisticated depth beyond simple cinnamon sweetness.

You'll find Cinnamoxal essential for building authentic cassia and cinnamon bark accords. Use at 0.5-5% for sweet spicy warmth with woody-resinous character. The material's natural occurrence in cinnamon bark and leaf oils makes it crucial for reconstructing these naturals. Its medicinal nuances add complexity that distinguishes fine oriental compositions from simple spice blends.

The compound excels in creating authentic bark effects with its characteristic oily texture and woody depth. Combine with eugenol for complete cinnamon bark reconstruction, coumarin for sweet hay-like warmth, or benzoin for enhanced balsamic character. Found naturally in cassia oil alongside cinnamaldehyde, it provides unique facets the simpler molecule cannot achieve.

Difference from Cinnamaldehyde

While cinnamaldehyde delivers the sharp, bright, almost aggressive cinnamon heat familiar from red-hot candies and cinnamon toothpicks, Cinnamoxal offers a completely different interpretation. The ortho-methoxy group transforms the molecule's character entirely - where cinnamaldehyde is hot and piercing, Cinnamoxal is sweet and rounded. Cinnamaldehyde can read as s

products.name: Cinnamyl Acetate
products.description:
Cinnamyl acetate is cinnamon's softer, more floral side. Where cinnamaldehyde burns and cinnamyl alcohol warms, cinnamyl acetate sweetens and lifts, with a gentle spicy-balsamic character and unexpected fruity-green facets. It occurs naturally in ylang ylang, cinnamon leaf, and narcissus absolute.

Use cinnamyl acetate to add sweet, warm spice to your floral compositions without the harshness of cinnamic aldehyde. It excels in hyacinth, narcissus, and honeysuckle accords, where its mild balsamic warmth blends seamlessly. In rose compositions it contributes a subtle oriental spiciness.

Hydroxycitronellal and phenylethyl alcohol bring out its warm floral side. Styrax and benzoin take it in a balsamic direction. In ylang ylang and jasmine accords it contributes the note you didn't know was missing — because it occurs naturally in both flowers.

products.name: Cinnamyl Alcohol
products.description:
Cinnamyl (or cinnamic) Alcohol is a vital material for hyacinth, lilac and muguet accords but also for generally sweetening a formula. It has a delicate cinnamic nuance and blends beautifully with Hydroxycitronellal, Terpineol and balsamic naturals like Styrax (oil and resinoid) and Benzoin especially.

We also stock the luxurious natural isolate Cinnamic Alcohol ex Styrax which is a rare treasure from the golden age of perfumery. We highly recommend both.

products.name: Cinnamyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Cinnamyl cinnamate is one of perfumery's great silent fixatives. Its own scent is barely perceptible — a very mild, sweet balsamic warmth with soft hints of jasmine, rose, and honey. But its tenacity is extraordinary, persisting on a blotter long after louder materials have vanished. It occurs naturally in styrax, Peru balsam, and hyacinth.

Use cinnamyl cinnamate to anchor and extend your heavy floral, oriental, and balsamic compositions. It fixes volatile top and heart notes without adding any obvious character of its own. In styrax reconstructions it is an essential building block alongside cinnamyl alcohol and other cinnamate materials.

Its natural companions are the other balsamic materials — styrax, benzoin, Peru balsam, tolu — where it acts as invisible glue, binding volatile notes to the base. In heavy floral compositions it reinforces jasmine, rose, and carnation from underneath, adding hours of persistence to your drydown without altering the character above.

products.name: Cinnamyl Propionate
products.description:
Cinnamyl Propionate is the scent of stewed summer fruit, bubble gum, grape soda and balsams. It is used to great effect in Firmenich's famous Dorinia rose base (demo formula below) where it adds a soft spice to the intensely fruity rose ketones.

With no limitation on use this could also be used to boost styrax notes or as a general fixer and blender for resins and balsams.

products.name: Cis Jasmone
products.description:
Perhaps Edmond Routnitka's favourite aromachemical, Cis Jasmone has an inimitable ability to naturalise almost any blend. For that reason it features in traces to overdose in numerous essential oil reconstructions. However it finds most value in jasmine and tuberose bases and accords.

At less than 1% of your formula, Cis Jasmone will add radiance and natural beauty. In much bigger amounts, it can lend an unusual mushroom like quality, an effect exploited most dramatically in Dior Dior by the aforementioned Roudnitska. The demo formula for that incredibly rare fragrance is below.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenol
products.description:
Cis-3-hexenol and its ester Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate are the two most important green chemicals in the perfumery palette. Both chemicals are naturally exuded by grass as a a type of defence against cuts and so in combination they produce that characteristic odour of newly trimmed lawns.

Cis-3-Hexenol can be dosed higher than its acetate and it is a wonderful way to add natural greenness to floral notes or to simply add a lovely green nuance to a scent.

Owing to the high strength of this material we also offer it pre-diluted to 10% in DPG.

Fragrances featuring Cis 3 Hexenol include Chanel No 19 and Cristalle and Eau de Champagne (1976) by Sisley.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate
products.description:
Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate (an ester of CIs-3-hexenol) is the sharper and more powerful member of the leaf alcohol family. It is found naturally in numerous essential oils and absolutes and is indispensable when making muguet or fresh air notes in fragrances. 

While often used in combination with Cis-3-hexenol, this material works wonderfully alone and we highly recommend having both in your perfumery organ.

Blends beautifully with Verdantol™, Muguet bases, Jasmine Sambac, and Rose Absolute where a trace of Cis-3-hexenyl can take it in the direction of the lovely green Rose Bourbon.

Owing to the high strength of this material we also offer it pre-diluted to 10% in DPG.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Benzoate
products.description:
Cis-3-Hexenyl Benzoate is a light floralising material with nuances of orchid and green leaves. It is a wonderful blender, especially with the classic members of the same family: Cis-3-Hexenol and Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate. 

It's balsamic facet is particularly nice when blended with fruit materials which can have a tendency to be overly chemical. 

Great for modern fougeres and chypres this also blends nicely with herbaceous oils like Clary Sage Oil and Lavender Oil and Absolute.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Butyrate
products.description:
This material captures something remarkable—the scent of ripe fruit that's still growing on the tree. Unlike harsh green notes that smell purely vegetal, this butyrate ester brings creamy richness that bridges fresh and ripe. You immediately recognise the buttery, waxy quality that makes fruit accords feel real rather than synthetic.

The winey, cognac-like character sets this material apart from simpler green esters. This facet adds sophistication and maturity, transforming basic fruitiness into something more complex and adult. You can leverage this quality to create modern gourmand effects where green meets creamy, or to add unexpected depth to floral compositions.

Use this when you need to move beyond one-dimensional fruit notes. Its exceptional 216-hour substantivity means it bridges from top notes deep into the heart, whilst its creamy texture prevents fruit accords from becoming candy-like. Perfect for creating the impression of biting into fresh, waxy-skinned fruit.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Cis-3-Hexenoate
products.description:
Cis-3-Hexenyl Cis-3-Hexenoate (Williams Ester) opens with a burst of pure pear juice—not sweet or candied, but the fresh, watery essence of biting into ripe fruit. This double-unsaturated ester captures something most materials miss: the textural sensation of pulpiness. You smell the saccharine flesh of the pear, complete with its characteristic ethereal quality.

This material transforms beyond simple pear into complex territory. Its green tomato leaf facets add sharp, vegetal sophistication whilst metallic undertones prevent any cloying sweetness. You can leverage these complex secondary notes to build modern green compositions or use its exceptional 13-hour longevity to anchor fruity top notes deep into the heart.

Use Williams Ester when you need to transcend ordinary fruit notes. Its natural occurrence in gardenia makes it perfect for floral modifications, whilst its melon and tropical facets open doors to aquatic compositions. The key lies in understanding its dual nature—intensely fruity yet surprisingly green.

If you need help understanding the very complex myriad of leaf alcohol esters, check out our comprehensive blog article The Scent of Broken Leaves.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
Cis-3-hexenyl isobutyrate hits you with an immediate burst of freshly cut grass laced with ripe apple and pear. The green and fruity facets arrive simultaneously—neither dominates, creating an impression of biting into a crisp apple in a just-mown garden. It is potent and diffusive, filling space quickly.

This material brings convincing naturalism to fruity-green accords. Use it to boost the green freshness in floral compositions—it lifts jasmine, muguet, and violet bases with an outdoorsy vitality. In citrus blends it adds a leafy depth that stops the top note feeling purely chemical. Try it in plum and tropical fruit accords where its sweet ripeness reads as authentically juicy.

Work at low doses—under one percent is usually plenty, as it is a powerful diffuser that easily overwhelms subtler notes. 

Isobutyrate vs Butyrate

Cis-3-hexenyl butyrate (CAS 16491-36-4) shares the same green-fruity family but leans in a different direction. The butyrate has a noticeable buttery, winey-brandy character beneath its green notes, almost like green Sweets with a boozy twist. This isobutyrate is cleaner, sweeter, and more purely fruity—apple-pear rather than apple-brandy. The butyrate is also somewhat milder and less diffusive. Choose the isobutyrate when you want crisp, clean fruit; choose the butyrate when you want richer, butterier depth.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Isovalerate
products.description:
This material captures the exact sensation of biting into a crisp Granny Smith apple—complete with the mouth-watering juice and complex ripeness. The isovalerate portion provides the secret weapon: a subtle funky, cheese-like undertone that mimics the natural fermentation processes in real fruit ripening.

This sophisticated funkiness prevents fruit accords from smelling flat or synthetic. The slight valerian-like character grounds the bright apple notes, creating three-dimensional realism that tricks the nose into perceiving genuine fruit flesh. You can leverage this complexity to transform basic fruity compositions into convincing, textured experiences.

Use this when you need to move beyond generic fruit notes into photorealistic territory. Its exceptional tenacity carries the juicy character from top notes into the heart, whilst its natural occurrence in black tea and herbs opens doors to sophisticated aromatic compositions. The key is understanding that the slight "off" note isn't a flaw—it's the source of its naturalism.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Propionate
products.description:
This green ester (a material made when an acid is reacted with an alcohol - in this case Cis-3 Hexenol and Propionic acid) captures something extraordinary—not just the smell of fruit, but its tactile quality. When you encounter this material, you immediately recognise the waxy skin of a fresh apple or unripe pear. This textural element separates it from basic fruity esters that smell flat and confectionary.

This material transforms ordinary fruit accords into photorealistic experiences. Its waxy character prevents compositions from becoming overly sweet or artificial, whilst the green-leafy backbone connects seamlessly to floral hearts. You can use it to create the impression of biting into crisp fruit or walking through a dewy orchard at dawn.

Apply this when you need precision over power. Its strength lies in refinement—a few drops can shift an entire accord from synthetic to natural. Build your pear and apple notes around this foundation or use traces to add sophisticated texture to tropical fruit compositions.

If you want to make a hyper-realistic pear, this is a must have in combination with Pear Ester and a sneaky trace of Safraleine to boost that gritty pear flesh texture. Try it - you won't believe how real it is!

If you need help understanding the very complex myriad of leaf alcohol esters, check out our comprehensive blog article The Scent of Broken Leaves.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Salicylate
products.description:
Cis-3-Hexenyl Salicylate is probably the most versatile of the green family, owing to its lightness and blending capabilities. Often replacing the hugely popular Benzyl Salicylate of the past, Cis-3-Hexenyl Salicylate offers virtually all of the same benefits with the added fresh connotations. 

Cis-3-Hexenyl Salicylate is balsamic, floral, green and orchid-like. It adds freshness and a sense of space to perfumes and could be considered beneficial to virtually every scent type.

This material blends beautifully with its relatives, particularly Cis-3-Hexenyl Benzoate, Cis-3-Hexenol and Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate.

Like the benzoate, this also blends nicely with herbaceous oils like Clary Sage Oil and Lavender Oil and Absolute.

products.name: Cis-3-Hexenyl Tiglate
products.description:
Cis-3-Hexenyl Tiglate opens with distinctive warm green character that immediately sets it apart from typical leaf alcohol esters. This unique material captures fresh-cut mushroom earthiness - not mouldy but clean and vegetal - combined with unexpected banana-melon fruitiness. The subtle gardenia-chamomile floralcy adds sophisticated depth that transforms simple green accords into complex botanical stories.

You'll find Cis-3-Hexenyl Tiglate invaluable for adding naturalistic warmth to green compositions that feel too sharp or synthetic. Use at 0.5-5% where its earthy-herbaceous character provides the missing link between bright green top notes and heavier base materials. Found naturally in honeysuckle flowers and comprising 1.34% of gardenia headspace, it's essential for authentic white floral reconstructions requiring green warmth.

The material excels in fougère compositions where its mushroom-earth facets enhance lavender's herbal character while adding modern complexity. Combine with lavender for enhanced naturalness, gardenia bases for authentic headspace effects, or violet leaf for sophisticated green depth. Its unusual banana-melon fruitiness bridges green and tropical territories brilliantly.

The Tiglate Signature

Tiglates possess a distinctive warm, slightly spicy-sweet character inherited from tiglic acid that sets them apart from common acetates or propionates. While simple esters like cis-3-hexenyl acetate deliver straightforward fresh-cut grass, tiglates add u

products.name: Cis-Jasmone Lactone
products.description:
This is the smell you get at the top of a fresh milk bottle that has come to room temperature. It has a very addictive scent with a classic coconut bent and an almost imperceptible cinnamic nuance.

This is an extremely precious lactone — a very sophisticated and natural smelling material that is far too underused in today's labs. Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) opined that it was one of the finest chemicals known (alongside Norlimbanol Dextro, Laevo Muscone, Ambrocenide and Helvetolide).

An elegant lactonic accord is made by combining Jasmolactone, Cis-Jasmone Lactone and Lactojasmone (a slightly less green isomer of Cis-Laevo Aerangis Lactone).

Cis-Jasmone Lactone blends with Operanide, Benzyl Acetate, Jasmine bases, Persicol, and rich florals like Gardenia J. Ellis and Tuberose Supreme.

products.name: Cistulate
products.description:
Cistulate (fix carboxylate) smells like a walk through a sun-warmed pine forest. Crisp fir needles and fresh green pine lead, clean and natural, while a soft cistus-resin warmth glows underneath. A light woody, faintly fruity edge rounds it off, fresh and lifted, never heavy or dark.

Use it to freshen and lift pine, fir and juniper accords, giving them a natural, outdoorsy sparkle at the top. It brings a green, resinous diffusion to fougères and aromatic colognes, and its cistus warmth lets it bridge fresh coniferous notes into softer woody and amber bases.

products.name: Cistus Creticus Resin Absolute, 50% ETH
products.description:
This is a speciality Fraterworks product. Starting from wild cistus gum gathered by hand in Crete using the ancient ladanisterion tool, we cold extract the pure labdanum heart and then remove 50% of the alcohol leaving us with a classic “Resin Absolute of Cistus Creticus, 50% ETH”.

Cretan cistus (also known as Cretan Rock Rose or Rockrose) is very similar to the more well-known cistus ladanifer, the source of cistus essential oil, labdanum resinoid and labdanum absolute but it differs in having a richer complex of accent notes. A more radiant resin, cistus creticus has distinct nuances of fine styrax resin, frankincense and herbs.

We use pure food grade ethanol produced with water from glacial lakes and the lowest temperature possible to extract the resin absolute from the raw gum. This maintains the integrity of the product and respects the heritage and labour of the men of Crete who collect this material in the same way as their ancient forebears.

Crude Exudate → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil
Crude Exudate → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resinoid
Crude Exudate → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute of Exudate, 𝓷% [evaporated to 𝓃%]
Crude Exudate → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [vacuum distilled to 100%]

While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent).

products.name: Cistus Green Absolute
products.description:
Cistus green is all about terroir and artisanship. It is extracted from the young foliage of cistus plants growing wild in the Moroccan Atlas Mountains. It has more of the green leaf volatiles of the plant and less of the dark animalic growl of labdanum absolute (which is why it was used in perfumes like Ralph Lauren's Polo Green and Coco by Chanel). And because of the special conditions of the area in which it grows, it even has some trace elements that are unique to its type.

Use it for a more modern approach to cistus. Accords with Cistus essential oil and Labdanum Light absolute are extremely special and new, and this finds itself perfectly suited to aquatics and ozonics in a way that the richer labdanum products normally don't.

It loves to be with herbal notes (not surprisingly) so you must try it with Artemal, and the very nature of its colour cries out for blending with green mandarin (à la Coco).

Because cistus absolute is highly viscous, we offer it pure and diluted to 50% in triethyl citrate, a completely natural, odorless plant extract. Perfect for perfumers who maintain an all-natural ingredient philosophy.

products.name: Cistus Oil “Rock Rose”
products.description:
As featured in the luxurious fragrance Rock Rose (2016) by Clive Christian, cistus oil is the essential oil of the plant more commonly known for labdanum resinoids and absolutes. Cistus is supremely elegant, offering a wonderfully bright top note. It blends extremely well with other resinoids (particularly those of its own family) and is synergistic with aldehydes. 

The extraction we sell has been selected from the offerings of all the top global suppliers. It is particularly vibrant and has the clearest and most warming scent of luxurious labdanum.

Due to it's high cost and power, we are offering this pure and at 10% dilution in natural odourless triethyl citrate.

products.name: Citral
products.description:
Citral provides unmatched authentic lemon character with exceptional diffusion. This powerful aldehyde consists of two geometric isomers (Geranial and Neral) that impart slightly different nuances. Perfumers value its bright, zesty profile for creating realistic citrus impressions and adding fresh lift to compositions.

Use Citral at 0.05-2% concentration with careful attention to formula stability. Combine with limonene for enhanced citrus effect or pair with florals for refreshing top notes. This material requires stabilization against oxidation and alkaline conditions, particularly in soap and detergent applications.

products.name: Citroasis
products.description:
Citroasis revolutionises citrus perfumery by solving volatility issues inherent to natural citrus oils. This pre-engineered specialty base delivers authentic citrus character with unprecedented 3-4 day longevity on smelling strips. Contains stabilised citral acetals that slowly release freshness over extended periods.

Use at 1-2% to boost natural citruses or up to 10% as foundational core structure. The aldehydic sparkle combined with neroli heart creates an instantly recognisable cologne signature that performs exceptionally in modern fresh fragrances.

Blend this material with Paradise Molecule® for enhanced diffusion, Dihydromyrcenol for masculine freshness, or Ambroxan for contemporary amber-citrus contrasts. The built-in grapefruit sulphur notes pair beautifully with Elemi or Frankincense for naturalistic bridges. Always work from 10% dilution due to extreme potency and consider IFRA limits of 4.3% maximum in fine fragrance applications.

products.name: Citronella Oil
products.description:
Citronella oil is fresh, sweet, and lemony-rosy — a clean, bright, green-grass character with a surprisingly warm woody drydown. It bridges citrus and floral families in a single natural oil. The sweetness is genuine and complex, not the harsh chemical note you might expect from the name.

Citronella oil appeared in two of the twentieth century's greatest perfumes — Tabu and Ma Griffe — where it contributed fresh, rosy-green sparkle to compositions that redefined their categories. It fell from favour because cheap citronella became synonymous with insect-repelling candles. That association is deeply unfair to the real oil.

Citronella deserves a comeback. Use it in green chypres, citrus colognes, and rosy-fresh compositions — it adds a naturalistic sparkle that isolated materials cannot replicate. Pair it with geranium, bergamot, cedarwood, and oakmoss for the kind of bright, green freshness that defined mid-century perfumery.

products.name: Citronellal
products.description:
Citronellal opens with intense lemon-citronella freshness that's both harsh and powerful, immediately evoking sunlit citrus groves and crushed lemongrass. This monoterpenoid aldehyde carries distinctive rosy undertones that bridge citrus and floral families. The green citrus-leaf character with subtle woody-musky depth prevents it from reading as simple lemon, adding sophisticated complexity.

You'll find Citronellal invaluable as both primary citrus note and crucial modifier. Use at 0.5-10% for authentic lemongrass character or bright citrus lift in colognes. Its rosy facets make it essential for building realistic rose accords when combined with geraniol and citronellol. Surprisingly, trace amounts (0.01-0.1%) work brilliantly in muguet compositions, adding naturalistic green stem freshness - a secret employed in the famed Coroliane de Laire base by Roudnitska.

The compound serves as the essential precursor to hydroxycitronellal through hydration, making it the chemical parent of classic muguet aldehydes. Combine with linalool for enhanced floralcy, vetiver for woody depth, or aldehydes for sparkling top notes. Found naturally at 35% in Java citronella oil and up to 80% in Eucalyptus citriodora, it provides the authentic citronella character impossible to replicate synthetically.

products.name: Citronellol 98
products.description:
BASF, founded in 1865 as a dye maker, has come to produce some of the best aroma chemicals. Boasting high purities and a quality much appreciated by perfumers, they are the top of the class in many instances. 

Citronellol, a key component of rose and geranium, is often viewed as a fairly uninteresting and standard material which seldom receives the scrutiny it should when selecting raw materials. That shouldn't be the case so we did the comparative testing so you don't have to.

Amongst the numerous qualities of Citronellol we evaluated, BASF's Citronellol 98 came out on top, a clear winner. 

Citronellol is rich and rose-like, deeper than Geraniol (which it complements greatly) and waxy. It has more of a rose's leafy character than the other rose alcohols.

Citronellol blends beautifully with Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Geraniol Extra, Rose Oxide Laevo, and Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon.

products.name: Citronellyl Acetate
products.description:
Citronellyl Acetate opens with remarkable freshness - neither the heavy sweetness of phenylethyl alcohol nor the sharp citrus of citronellol, but something uniquely textured. Think waxy rose petals dried in sunlight, mixed with ripe apricot skin. The fruity facet reads as pear and apricot compote without excessive sweetness.

You'll find this indispensable for modernising rose accords where traditional materials feel dated. Replace 10-15% of your heavy alcohols with citronellyl acetate to achieve that contemporary "living flower" quality. It excels at bridging top note citrus freshness into floral hearts, maintaining transparency while adding substantial body to thin compositions.

Work with citronellyl acetate in top and heart positions where its 8-hour substantivity provides lasting freshness. Unlike geranyl acetate which can feel green-apple sharp, citronellyl acetate offers a softer, rounder rosy-fruity effect. Its excellent alkali stability makes it valuable for soap perfumery. Blend with citronellol, geraniol, rose materials, and citrus oils for natural-smelling floral compositions.

products.name: Citronellyl Formate
products.description:
Citronellyl formate opens with an immediate punch of fresh rose petals—not the sweet, jammy rose of bases but the sharp, almost pungent quality of roses still wet with morning dew. This powerful rose character is inseparable from its leafy-green geranium facets, creating an effect like crushing rose petals and geranium leaves together. Fresh cucumber and subtle lemon notes add crisp coolness, while an unexpected honey-like undertone provides natural sweetness without becoming cloying. The overall impression is remarkably fresh and vegetable-like, with the kind of natural complexity rarely achieved with synthetic materials alone.

Deploy Citronellyl formate at 0.5-10% when you need authentic natural rose effects with fresh green lift. Its powerful character means it dominates at higher concentrations—use carefully in delicate compositions. Found naturally in geranium oil (up to 12% in Chinese varieties), it's essential for authentic geranium reconstructions. In rose compositions, it provides the elusive "fresh rose petal" quality that bridges the gap between citrus top notes and heavier rose heart notes. The material excels in soap perfumes where its fresh-vegetable character survives alkaline conditions beautifully. In lily of the valley and other white florals, it adds natural green freshness without synthetic harshness.

The structural difference between Citronellyl formate and Citronellyl acetate creates distinct olfactory profiles despite their shared citronellol base. Ci

products.name: Civet “Supreme” Absolute
products.description:
Ethiopia (historically Abyssinia) is the classic source of civet materials for perfumery. Our highest quality "supreme" absolute (obtained within the CITES guidelines from Ranched animals) is intensely fecal and, to most people, extremely obnoxious in scent.  However, in dilution (typically from 1–10%) the material becomes far more appealing and begins to show the qualities for which is has earned its long-standing position as the peak of perfection in legally traded perfume animalics.

Civet absolute is easier to use than raw paste as you simply dilute it to your needs and use it immediately; on the other hand the unprocessed secretion must be tinctured and rested for many months (or even years) to be fully usable.

Civet is a CITES appendix II product. In most countries this can be lawfully traded without extra paperwork if purchased for personal use. We recommend checking in advance with your own regulatory bodies.

If you are purchasing for commercial reasons you may need a CITES re-export or origin certificate to accompany your purchase. You should check with your national authorities. We charge $60 USD for this certificate and it takes approximately ten days for us to apply and provide it. Simply contact us for help. We will endeavour to make the process as seamless and speedy as possible.

NOTE: We ship civet and other very high-odour products in sealed foil bags to prevent cross-contamination in the event of leaks or parcel damage.

We are also now selling this at 10%

products.name: Civettal
products.description:
Civettal (Animal Quinoline), or tetrahydro para methyl quinoline, is a powerful animalic material that is indispensable when creating non-natural civet blends or where a civet note is needed without the full complexity of the real product. It also works well in honey and tobacco blends.

Civettal has a leather nuance but far less than the more common isobutyl quinoline. The two cannot substitute for one another. An excellent fixative when dosed right.

Because of its strength, we sell this pure and diluted to 10% and 1% with Dipropylene Glycol. As with all high odour materials, we ship this in a sealed foil bag.

products.name: Civette Synth 039648
products.description:
Civet whether natural or synthetic is a marvelous naturaliser. In florals it is indispensible as evidenced by the masterwork of François Coty, 1917 Chypre. 

Use it one for one anywhere natural civet is used for a vegan alternative to one of the famous, and perhaps most controversial animal musks.

For those needing the natural article, we also sell Civet “Supreme” Absolute.

products.name: Civettone
products.description:
Found naturally in civet extracts, Civettone delivers extraordinary tenacity as a key structural element in luxurious fragrances. This powerful musk forms the foundation of sophisticated oriental and floral compositions. Perfumers leverage its warm, animalic character to create memorable signature traits in prestigious formulations.

Use Civettone at 0.1-0.5% concentration for optimal effect in fine fragrances. This material blends exceptionally with jasmine, rose, and amber accords while intensifying longevity. Apply sparingly to benefit from its distinctive radiant muskiness.

This is a material found in almost all modern Chanel perfumes, often in combination with Muscone Laevo. See below for some demo formulas that illustrate its use.

products.name: Civettone Base 184332
products.description:
Civettone Base 184332 is a brand new Firmenich specialty designed to replicate the smell of civettone, the prized macrocyclic musk. You get the same smooth, warm, powdery musk character — radiant, skin-like, and softly animalic — in a ready-to-use base without sourcing the pure molecule which is, for all intents and purposes, no longer available.

Use this base anywhere you would use civettone itself. Even a trace adds radiance and musky warmth to florals, giving jasmine, rose, and tuberose a glowing depth they cannot achieve alone. It anchors orientals and chypres while adding the diffusive power that makes a fragrance project.

Dose with care — this base is potent and a little goes far, however it is sultry and soft so an overdose would be perfectly fine. Blend with sandalwood, labdanum, and amber materials for classic musky warmth. Try it alongside castoreum, ambrette, and other animalic materials to build rich, multifaceted musk accords.

Curiously those who can smell muscone often can't smell civettone, and vice versa. Civettone base is perceptible to all.

products.name: Claritone
products.description:
Claritone is a multi-layered beast. It is herbal (in the direction of clary sage), peony floral, vaguely fruity and, to top it off, it sparkles like a coupe of champagne!

While its most obvious use will be fougères, it can add diffusion and interest to all types of fragrances and it shouldn't be relegated to masculines only.

It is a nice top note modifier in small amounts, but you can also push it to the extreme in overdose. Claritone was used at 1.5% in Clive Christian 1872.

products.name: Clary Sage Absolute
products.description:
Clary Sage Absolute is a solvent extraction from Russian clary sage with the most wonderful herbal pipe tobacco quality. This is a solid and requires heating to liquify. It can be added pure to your formula as it will dissolve in the other materials.

Average Constituents

Linalyl Acetate 66.5% (cf. French Oil: 49–73.6%)
Linalool 8.9% (cf. French Oil: 9–16.0%)
Geramacrene D 9.4% (cf. French Oil: 1.6–2%)
Sclareol 2.4%
β-Caryophyllene 1.9% (cf. French Oil: 1.4–1.6%)
α-Copaene 1.1%
Bicyclogermacrene 1.1%

* R. Tisserand * R. Young. Essential Oil Safety. Churchill Livingstone Elsevier, 2014. pp 1084–1085.

Synergies and Blending

Clary sage absolute is an excellent fixative and extender for Clary Sage Oil, France.

Blends well with Bergamot Oil, FCF and other citrus oils, Cardamom, Cinnamon, Cedarwood Virginia, Olibanum and Frankincense, Geranium Bourbon, Genet, Hay (Flouve), Jasmine Absolute, Juniper Oil Rectified, Lavender (oil and absolute), Lavandin, Patchouli, Rose Absolute, Sandalwood Mysore Oil, and Ylang-ylang.

Complimentary Base pairings: Fleur de Tabac, Suralette™ Extra, Verdantol, Artemal™, Jasmin Russe, Foin Coupé de Laire.

Origin: Russia
Part: Leaves and flowering tops
Method: Solvent extracted absolute

products.name: Clary Sage Oil
products.description:
Our clary sage oil from Provence opens with complex notes of herbs and flowers. It is by far the most floral and luxurious clary sage we have experienced which is what led us to select it for our exclusive offering. Traditionally manufactured and steam distilled onsite, this oil is the finest example of a truly versatile and loved top note oil.

Clary sage blends perfectly with bergamot, lavender and other fresh notes, adding complexity and interest. Touches were used to great effect in Moment Supreme where it modifies the beautiful aldehydic lavender opening and helps unite the central floral notes of the fragrance with the sweet labdanum in the dry down.

Origin: France
Part: Leaves and flowering tops
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Clearwood®
products.description:
Clearwood® is an all-natural product made by Firmenich to mimic the sweetest and cleanest properties of patchouli oil whilst removing anything even hinting at dirt. This is effectively a natural blend of a selection of the preferred molecules found in natural patchouli.

Rich in patchouli alcohol (patchoulol), Clearwood is closest to our wonderful Patchoulol Crystals PA99 but about half the strength owing to the inclusion of other molecules. It blends wonderfully with Iso E Super and other light wood materials and can be used as a one for one replacer of natural patchouli oil. Use it in traces up to overdose.

According to Firmenich: “Created from white biotechnology, Clearwood delivers all the rewards of modern ingredient design. Beaming with light, it offers the creamy warmth of amber and a dark woody character reminiscent of patchouli.”

We also now offer the extraordinary Clearwood PRISMA range, launched by Firmenich in 2024.

Contains 0.05% of Tocopherol as a preservative.

products.name: Clearwood® PRISMA
products.description:
Clearwood® PRISMA is an exciting 2024 release from Firmenich. It is previously a captive 100% natural (ISO 9235) and sustainable biotech product and marks the ten year anniversary of Clearwood, one of the company's most iconic products. We are excited to be the first retailer to offer this marvel.

Clearwood® PRISMA boasts an astounding 90–99% patchoulol content and so, in pure form, it is solid (similar to candle wax) but at certain warmer temperatures it may be liquid.

Firmenich also makes this product at 50% blended in Hedione® (product code 970961) due to the performance boost found in the their laboratory tests and as a prevention against solidification; we certainly concur with their master-perfumers and scientists — the Hedione Clearwood blend is a revelation. However, for those customers who prefer it, we also offer Clearwood PRISMA at 50% in odourless IPM.

In Firmenich's own words: “Clearwood® Prisma, at low dosage, adds a sheer touch, harmonizing with a nuanced patchouli background. Compared to Clearwood® and Patchouli Indonesia, it reigns with sheer brilliance, keeping the citrusy sparkling notes and the spicy ones, while its counterparts, though voluminous, seem to veil the citrus and spice in their embrace. Clearwood® Prisma gives a new chypre-like vibe.”

Clearwood® PRISMA blends with classic Clearwood®, Iso E Super and other light wood materials and can be used as a one for one replacer for natural patchouli oil. Use it in traces up to overdose. Undiluted Cle

products.name: Clematis
products.description:
Clematis flowers have no odour and so historically (like classic orchid bases,) they are fantasy creations. This Fraterworks base is a restoration of the wonderous Roure Clematis base of the 1930s which was used by Jean Carles in combination with his Fleur de Tabac base to construct Shocking for Schiaparelli in 1937, a wild perfume built around a heat of pink florals. It is from this fashion house and fragrance that the colour “shocking pink” was born.

Wonderfully floral, rich and aldehydic, this clematis base would find a home in a modern fragrance as easily as it did the classics of yesteryear.

products.name: Clonal™
products.description:
Clonal (Dodecane Nitrile) is a powerful citrus top note with intensely metallic nuances. It is perfect for boosting the sparkle on a cologne or fougere or for creating a modern and exciting fragrance with sci-fi characteristics.

Be careful of this one! It's definitely strong and a little goes a long way. We recommend diluting it to 1% or 0.1% in DPG before using it.

products.name: Clove Bud “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Clove bud oil is perhaps the most versatile of all the spices. It adds naturalness and warmth to rose bases, delightful spiced notes to gourmands and interesting medicinal notes to more exotic blends.

This clove bud oil is a speciality of Payan Bertrand and is superior to all others. We hand selected it from the myriad options on the market today. Having a sweeter and more vanilla nuance, this Madagascan clove is extremely close to the near-mythical Zanzibar clove bud oil of the past.

products.name: Clovebud Zanzibar Tincture 25%
products.description:
In the golden age of perfumery the most sought after clovebuds were those of Zanzibar, hand plucked in the beating African sun on plantations owned by the Sultan. The sultan is now exiled and the global demand is mostly met by Madagascar. But many Zanzibar families still make a living harvesting the buds of wild trees by hand.

Fraterworks imports these superior cloves from Zanzibar and tinctures them with care using the classical cold alcohol method. Our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of clove extracts and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop.

Tincture of cloves has a smoother and sweeter fragrance than the essential oil now commonly found. It also has the power to soften the oil when used in combination with it.

Origin: Zanzibar
Variety: Syzygium aromaticum (L.) Merr. & L.M. Perry
Part: Unopened flower buds
Method: Cold ethanol tincture

products.name: Cocoa Absolute 5% IPM
products.description:
Cocoa absolute opens with immediate dark chocolate richness reminiscent of melted couverture. Its roasted character evokes freshly ground cacao beans whilst creamy liqueur facets add indulgence. The subtle bitter edge provides sophisticated balance preventing cloying sweetness.

You'll find this absolute essential for authentic chocolate notes in gourmand compositions where synthetic alternatives disappoint. It excels at adding sensuality to amber bases and unexpected depth to white florals. Use it sparingly—its intense concentration means tiny amounts create lasting chocolate impressions without dominating delicate accords.

Blend cocoa absolute with vanilla and tonka for complete gourmand indulgence or combine with benzoin for balsamic chocolate warmth. Pair with coffee absolute to enhance roasted facets. This material bridges fruity top notes with amber bases beautifully, particularly with cherry and citrus accords.

This comes pre-diluted to 5% in IPM by LMR so it is not suitable for all natural perfumers.

Resinoid vs Absolute

Cocoa Resinoid from V. MANE Fils presents a slightly bitter dark chocolate profile ideal for fine and functional applications. LMR's Cocoa Absolute offers superior aromatic refinement with an even truer-to-life chocolate character. Where MANE's resinoid provides robust chocolate with practical advantages, LMR's absolute delivers concentrated luxury with deeper complexity and smoother integration into sophisticated compositions.
tags: locale:new! do not confuse with 20% resinoid from MANE

products.name: Cocoa Hexenal
products.description:
Cocoa Hexenal captures dark chocolate's bitter edge rather than its sweetness—think roasted cocoa nibs and nutshells, not milk chocolate bars. The aldehydic opening brings sharpness that transitions into warm, brown, nutty tones. Green vegetative hints recall cocoa pods on the tree while subtle honey and mocha facets round out the profile.

This material forms the backbone of authentic chocolate accords where pyrazines alone fall short. Work it into gourmand compositions at 2-8% of your concentrate for recognisable cocoa impact, or use traces below 1% to add subtle brown richness to orientals and ambers. It brings unexpected depth to tobacco reconstructions and enhances hazelnut and praline effects without obvious chocolate character.

Handle Cocoa Hexenal with precision—its power demands restraint but rewards careful dosing. Combine it with vanillin and tonka for classic chocolate effects, or pair with patchouli and labdanum for dark, resinous warmth. Layer it with coffee materials in masculine fragrances or work it alongside Honey Supreme where its aldehydic bite prevents cloying sweetness.

products.name: Cocoa Resinoid 20% TEC
products.description:
Imagine the smell of smashed chunks of chocolate slowly warming in your hands and releasing their enticing aroma; white chocolate, dark chocolate, milk chocolate and every variety in between. From V. MANE Fils comes a truly wonderful cocoa resinoid extracted with ethanol rather than harsh chemicals and made practical with the addition of natural odourless triethyl citrate — our own personal favourite when it comes to natural diluents and dilutants.

Cocoa resinoids and absolutes are famously difficult to work with and all suppliers tend to offer the virtually impossible pure product which all need diluting not just to render them usable but also because cocoa is a very strong material (deceptively so).

This beautiful resinoid is clean, powder, richly chocolate and wonderfully clean. There are no off notes and no surprises. It's just good chocolate.

Some of our favourite combos are Wild Cherry and Cocoa Absolute with a touch of Rum P. Jungle Essence for a crazily good Cherry Chocolate Liqueur accord or blend it with all the rich orris materials to enhance and enrich their powdery side, just as master perfumer Olivier Polge did in the now near-mythical 2005 original Dior Homme Intense.

This Cocoa Resinoid has < 0.6% Caffeine and is IFRA 51 compliant to 100% of your finished product.

products.name: Coconut CO2, P. Jungle Essence
products.description:
This extract smells exactly like cracking open a fresh coconut. Warm, creamy richness fills the air alongside waxy-nutty facets and gentle toasted sweetness. MANE's low-temperature CO2 process captures the full aromatic picture from bright fruity top through rich, buttery base.

You can add this to white floral hearts without creating an overtly tropical effect. Instead it plumps up petal notes and renders the fleshy quality of flowers through textural creaminess. It also forms the backbone of convincing beach-inspired accords where synthetic coconut reads hollow.

Try it with vanilla and tonka for rich gourmand indulgence. Blend with jasmine and ylang-ylang for an unexpected tropical floral that avoids cliche. Massoia bark CO2 makes an excellent partner, layering complementary coconut facets for deep, convincing richness.

To power it up for a bold coconut note we recommend Coconut Delight, our complex coconut base, or Gamma Octalactone, the single best coconut lactone. And for a beautifully tropical perfume, try it with Gardenia J. Ellis, Rum CO2, and Dark Ginger CO2 P. Jungle Essence.

Pure, this is solid. So we offer it in a 10% solution with IPM. Natural perfumers should purchase the undiluted material as IPM (Isopropyl Myristate / MIP) is a synthetic diluent.

products.name: Coconut Delight
products.description:
In perfume history coconut is often supplied as a simple touch of Nonalactone Gamma (Aldehyde C-18 so-called) with occasional accents added by other lactones that vary in intensity and nuance.

Coconut Delight, on the other hand, gives you the full coconut experience. A delicious oily opening leads to a sweeter and more interesting dry down. This can be used as a replacer for nonalactone and is far easier to dose. We recommend starting at around 0.5% and working up to doses of 5% though you can certainly use more if you wish.

Coconut Delight blends beautifully with our boozy Amaretto Saronno base and Raspberry Ripple.

products.name: Coffee Arabica CO2
products.description:
Foggy headed you rise from your slumber and drift to the kitchen to imbibe your first coffee for the day. The rich scent of freshly roasted beans awakens your senses as warm sunlight streams through the windows; all is good with the world and your day now begins.

Coffee Arabic Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils manages to encapsulate that very moment when the colour rushes back to the world and the fuzz of sleep departs. It is the scent of hot coffee, freshly poured. It is the scent of optimism and the scent of anticipation. This is such a rich and luxurious coffee extract that nothing at all compares to it; no other supplier comes close to capturing this most beloved material.

This is practically begging to be part of a gourmand fragrance. Pair it with the caramel notes of Opoponax Resinoid, the chocolate nuance of Orris Resinoid, or the fresh pasty delight of Tonka Bean resinoid; and don't forget luscious Bourbon Vanilla Absolute.

MANE states that this product is soluble in 10% Oil, TEC, DPG and IPM. For full solubility in alcohol it should be diluted with 50/50 ethanol and IPM.

products.name: Coffee Espresso SFE
products.description:
Our Coffee Arabica CO2 from MANE is the gentle morning cup — warm sunlight, the colour rushing back to the world. It is refined, rounded, optimistic.

This is not that coffee.

This is 11pm in Naples. A tiny cup, almost too hot to hold, from a machine that has been running all day. The barista doesn't smile. He doesn't need to. The espresso speaks for itself: dark, intense, slightly burnt, impossibly concentrated. You bury your face in the grounds and breathe in. That is what this smells like.

Firmenich's Coffee Espresso SFE captures a roast level and an intensity that the MANE extract deliberately avoids. Where the Arabica CO2 paints a nuanced portrait — chocolatey, nutty, sophisticated — this one fills the room with a single, uncompromising statement: coffee, at full volume. The slightly charred edge lifts woody-smoky undertones that make it feel less gourmand and more animalic. Less pastry shop, more leather armchair.

Both are supercritical CO2 extracts. Both are extraordinary. But they are as different as a light-roast Ethiopian pour-over and a ristretto from a Neapolitan bar — the word "coffee" and precious little else in common. You definitely want both.

The Espresso SFE cuts through sweetness rather than adding to it. Pair it with tobacco, leather, labdanum, or dark woods for compositions where a softer coffee note would simply vanish. With birch tar and castoreum, it produces a coffee-leather accord that is devastatingly good.

products.name: Coffee Pentenolone
products.description:
Coffee pentenolone (ethyl cyclopentenolone) delivers a dark, complex sweetness that goes well beyond simple caramel. Coffee, rum, whiskey, and brown sugar notes intertwine with a subtle smokiness that gives it depth. Where cyclotene (methyl cyclopentenolone) gives you clean maple-syrup sweetness, this material is darker, more brooding, and more layered — think burnt toffee rather than fresh syrup.

The potency is extreme. Work from a pre-diluted stock (the material is supplied at 50% in propylene glycol for this reason). At proper dosage — parts per million — it contributes a warm, gourmand sweetness that smells expensive and authentic. Overdose quickly turns compositions cloying and unrecognisable.

Vanillin and tonka bean absolute bring out the caramel side. Coffee CO2 and tobacco absolute amplify the roasted facets. In leather accords a trace contributes a subtle sweet-smoky dimension. Labdanum and benzoin provide a balsamic foundation for its dark warmth to rest upon.

products.name: Cognac Oil, Green
products.description:
Green Cognac Oil opens with a distinctly panary note with a recognisable dry-winey character—tart, herbaceous, and immediately evocative of crisp white wine. Green apple facets dominate the top, while fatty-oily undertones add naturalistic depth. The herbaceous-grassy dryness recalls late summer hayfields, and the overall effect is of sparkling, boozy freshness that transforms any composition it touches. The initial baked-bread note makes this very an excellent oil to temper the saccharine intensity of sweeter gourmands.

This essential oil comes from wine lees—the yeasty sediment left at the bottom of oak barrels after Cognac fermentation. Copper still distillation creates the distinctive emerald-green colour through oxidation, a traditional French method now increasingly rare. The result is an intensely diffusive oil with remarkable 200-hour substantivity. Work with it heavily diluted (5–10%) to tame its raw power before blending.

Use Cognac Oil Green in trace amounts—one or two drops can lift an entire composition. It excels in colognes, fougères, and aftershave fragrances where its sparkling freshness adds sophistication. Blend with bergamot, lavender, clary sage, and ylang-ylang for classic effects. Pair with methyl anthranilate for authentic grape-wine accords or the rarer allyl anthranilate if you seek more power. The tart green apple character makes it valuable in fruit compositions seeking naturalistic depth rather than synthetic sweetness.

Cognac Oil Green vs Cogn

products.name: Cognac Oil, White
products.description:
White Cognac Oil greets you with rounded, fruity-winey warmth — muscatel grape tartness and a champagne-like sparkle that immediately distinguishes it from its harsher green sibling. Delicate floral nuances thread through the dry-wine character. The overall impression is of polished, boozy elegance without any fatty heaviness.

Use White Cognac Oil where you need boozy sparkle without overwhelming power. It lifts floral accords — jasmine, rose, and neroli all respond beautifully — and adds sophisticated winey warmth to orientals. Work in dilution; even at five percent this oil transforms a composition's top notes.

Blend with methyl anthranilate for an authentic grape-wine accord, or pair with vanilla and Benzoin Oiffac for brandy-amber warmth. Stainless steel distillation gives White Cognac its cleaner, more refined character versus the copper-distilled green type. Use this version for feminine florals and orientals.

Cognac Oil Green vs Cognac Oil White

These two Cognac oils share the same botanical source (Vitis vinifera lees) but differ meaningfully in character. Green Cognac, distilled in traditional copper stills, is bolder, more boozy, with pronounced herbaceous-grassy notes, green apple tartness, and an almost harsh bready intensity that demands careful dosing.

White Cognac, distilled in stainless steel, is smoother and more refined—less boozy, with rounder fruity-floral qualities and a champagne-like elegance that's easier to blend.

Use Green Cognac when you want

products.name: Cologne Imperiale 1853
products.description:
Use it just like perfumer's alcohol. This is the original 1853 eau de cologne that launched the Guerlain brand. It is a ready-to-wear 5% strength cologne as was the norm for distilled fragrances such as these. 

According to the house: “[c]reated in 1853 by Pierre-François-Pascal Guerlain, Eau de Cologne Imperiale is the first cologne Guerlain specially composed for the Empress Eugenie, wife of Napoleon III, earning its creator the title of ‘Her Majesty's patented Perfumer’.”

This cologne was used as the base for the first version of Jicky which was decidedly different from the construction style of later versions. Below is a formula for a Jicky-style fragrance that illustrates how this was done as well as a formula for an Eau Sauvage type to demonstrate a modern use of the style. This is a wonderful technique never seen today but is certainly due a renaissance. And now with Fraterworks Cologne Imperiale 1853, it is possible to experience this treasured perfumery style.

Fraterworks distills this cologne in a classic copper still (as pictured) just as the original was. A truly unique product.

Top notes: Bergamot, Lemon, Orange, Rosemary
Heart Notes: Neroli, Lavender, Verbena
Base Notes: Cedarwood, Tonka bean, Benzoin, Ambergris

products.name: Compound 33
products.description:
Compound 33 is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Santal 33 from Le Labo. Launched in 2011, this is a modern woody fragrance built around Australian sandalwood and cedarwood with a distinctive violet-iris accord that gives it its characteristic dry, slightly pickle-like opening.

This compound features sandalwood lactones and cedarwood derivatives creating a dry, pencil-shaving effect, enhanced with Iso E Super for diffusion and Ambrox for depth. The addition of cardamom, papyrus, and leather accord creates a minimalist yet complex composition that has become one of the most recognisable fragrances of the 2010s.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Violet Leaf, Australian Sandalwood, Cardamom
Heart Notes: Iris, Papyrus, Ambrox
Base Notes: Cedarwood, Leather Accord, Musk

products.name: Compound Afternoon
products.description:
Compound Afternoon is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Afternoon Swim from Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2019, this is a bright citrus-aquatic fragrance built around mandarin and orange with a distinctive ginger note and clean ambroxan base.

This compound features high levels of mandarin and orange oils combined with fresh ginger and a transparent aquatic accord. The base of ambroxan provides the characteristic clean, skin-like drydown while maintaining the citrus brightness throughout wear.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Mandarin, Orange, Bergamot
Heart Notes: Ginger, Aquatic Accord
Base Notes: Ambergris

products.name: Compound Aramis
products.description:
Aramis, launched in 1966 and created by the great Bernard Chant, was an icon of classic masculinity, is to be discontinued. It was a derivative of Gris' Cabochard (by the same perfumer) but replacing the floral notes with green aromatic ones.

This compound is for a scent in the style of the original with authentic oakmoss levels, musk ambrette, and animalic notes that modern reformulations have stripped away. The opening is sharp and challenging: sparkling aldehydes cut through herbal artemisia and bergamot, lifted by thyme and clover. The heart reveals a complex spiced floral accord of patchouli, sage, jasmine and cardamom, grounded by powdery orris root.

The base is where Aramis earns its reputation – rich leather, dense oakmoss, warm sandalwood, vetiver and amber create a foundation of unmistakable masculinity. The result is a fragrance of commanding presence with exceptional longevity and projection – not for the faint-hearted.

To evaluate properly, dilute to 14% and use a smelling strip. Do not put on the skin.

Note: This compound is based on the original 1966 formula and is not IFRA compliant. It is intended for educational use only and not for commercial resale or cosmetic use.

Top Notes: Aldehydes, Bergamot, Artemisia, Thyme, Clover, Myrtle
Heart Notes: Patchouli, Sage, Jasmine, Cardamom, Orris Root
Base Notes: Leather, Oakmoss, Musk, Vetiver, Sandalwood, Amber

products.name: Compound Armenie
products.description:
Compound Armenie is our faithful reconstruction of a scent in the style of Bois d'Arménie by Guerlain, based off meticulous GCMS analyses and research. Launched in 2006 as part of the L'Art & La Matière collection, this is a smoky oriental woody fragrance inspired by the tradition of burning benzoin-infused Armenian paper as incense. Tragically discontinued in 2024, this compound is as close as you can possibly get to the original formula which we have painstakingly restored. his fragrance costs upwards of $1,000 per bottle on the secondary market today.

This compound features a rich resinous heart of benzoin and guaiac wood that evokes smouldering incense. The top notes of frankincense, iris and pink pepper provide a powdery, spiced opening with immediate smoky depth, while coriander adds an aromatic lift to the heart. The base delivers copaiba balsam alongside earthy patchouli and soft white musk for a warm, lingering finish. The result is a contemplative, incense-laden fragrance with excellent longevity and close-to-skin projection – refined, meditative and quietly distinctive.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Incense, Iris, Pink Pepper 
Heart Notes: Benzoin, Guaiac Wood, Coriander 
Base Notes: Copaiba Balsam, Patchouli, White Musk

products.name: Compound Balade™
products.description:
In French, Balade means "ride" and it is a term used in the popular French film "La Balade Sauvage" (The Wild Ride). It is also the name of a marvellous Dior fragrance created by François Demachy and launched in 2018 in their Collection Privée. Alas it has been discontinued from 2024.

Balade Sauvage is a light cologne that has perhaps the most wearable representation of a fig note. The scent is hugely popular, garnering 4.3 stars out of 5 on Fragrantica and it contains no EU or IFRA prohibited materials so the discontinuation seems rather odd.

Fraterworks now presents this intricate and luxurious scent in the style of the original in compound form for perfumers to understand and appreciate the odour of a masterpiece prior to dilution and mass distribution. The price is very good — in fact it is commercially viable at the 1kg point.

Top Notes: Ozone, Bergamot, Petitgrain
Heart Notes: Fig Tree, Fig, Sunlight, Seaside, Peach, Orange Blossom, Hedione, Rose
Base Notes: Pebbles, Amberwood, Labdanum, Vanilla

Allergens: Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Eugenol, Limonene, Linalool, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Farnesol, Coumarin, BHT.

products.name: Compound Black®
products.description:
Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of our private label formula for a scent in the style of Aventus, a popular Creed men's fragrance launched in 2010.

Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials we stock two versions of Compound Black®. The original version is the unaltered original fragrance and the (EC) No 1223/2009 version is as close as we can get while complying with EU requirements. Both compounds are IFRA compliant because the original Aventus was.

If you prefer a smokier version of this fragrance add a trace of our Birch Tar Rectified (dilute it to 1% first). And to boost the fruit, try a little of our highly popular Pineapple Supreme.

Did you know?: just 50g of Compound Black® and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

products.name: Compound Blue®
products.description:
Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of a scent in the style of Bleu by Chanel as launched in 2010 and created by Jacques Polge. This remains, to this day, the definitive blue scent.

Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation and is IFRA compliant. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram.

Allergens: Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Eugenol, Limonene, Linalool, Coumarin, Butylphenyl Methylpropional.

products.name: Compound Brut™
products.description:
“There's something about Brut, that's nice to be close to.” So said the commercials way back in 1964 when perfumer Karl Mann created what could arguably be considered the most iconic men's scent in history.

With a massive overdose of Musk Ambrette (an astonishing 13%) it is not surprising this fragrance was practically destroyed by legislative banning of raw materials and what is on the shelf in drug stores and department stores today is a mere shadow of what once was. Until now.

Compound Brut is our internal version of a scent in the style of the unchanged original fragrance. There is no EU compliant or IFRA compliant version of this compound - it just isn't possible. Instead what you get is a compound that will allow you to study the profile and qualities of one of the most popular perfumes for gents without having to imagine what it was like.

Freshly made with the finest materials (as with all Fraterworks products) you will be astonished by how good this product is. This is not a "perfume for grandpa" or an old man's scent. This is class to the extreme. With high quality Mysore sandalwood (a lot!), patchouli, green oakmoss and vetiver you realise just how much care went in to scents in the past - even those that are now deemed to be nasty cheapies.

Originally diluted to 10% it was Brut. Diluted to 5% (with some distilled water in the alcohol blend) it was Brut 33. 

WARNING: This is not compliant with any fragrance laws in any countries and should not be worn on the sk

products.name: Compound Celsius™
products.description:
Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of a scent in the style of the original Dior masterpiece from 1988: Fahrenheit. The fragrance was created by Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Michel Almairac, and Maurice Roger and was the first to exploit a high dose of Methyl Heptine Carbonate.

Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation and is IFRA compliant to 5%. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram and IFRA/EU Compliant to 20%.

Allergens: Citral, Citronellol, Geraniol, Linalool, Benzyl Benzoate, Coumarin, Eugenol, Benzyl Alcohol, Benzyl Cinnamate, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Cinnamal, Limonene, Isoeugenol, Hydroxyisohexyl 3-Cyclohexene Carboxaldehyde, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Methyl 2-Octynoate, Butylphenyl Methylpropional.

products.name: Compound Cool
products.description:
Compound Cool is our internal formula for a perfume in the style of Cool Water from Davidoff. Launched in 1988, this is the fragrance that defined the aquatic genre — a bold marine fougère built on dihydromyrcenol's cool transparency, layered with aromatic herbs and a warm musky base.

This compound balances crisp mint and lavender against a powerful calone-driven sea breeze accord, with rosemary and neroli adding aromatic complexity in the heart. The drydown settles into a clean sandalwood and musk foundation with subtle tobacco warmth, giving the fragrance its distinctive masculine signature.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. However, it is not EU compliant as it contains Lyral. We can produce special order versions that are EU compliant on request with a minimum order quantity of 1kg.

Top Notes: Mint, Green Notes, Lavender
Heart Notes: Sea Air, Rosemary, Neroli, Geranium
Base Notes: Sandalwood, Musk, Tobacco, Cedarwood

products.name: Compound Correspondence
products.description:
Compound Correspondence is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Correspondence by Henry Jacques. Launched in 2016 as part of the Les Classiques de HJ collection, this is a floral oriental fragrance built around two varieties of rose and precious oud, with powdery and fruity facets.

This compound features an exceptional rose accord combining bright damask rose with the honeyed richness of rose de mai.
