The top notes of damask rose, iris and hyacinth provide a powdery, almost soapy elegance, while the heart adds soft apricot – reading more as the bitter kernel than the flesh – alongside earthy patchouli. The base delivers a refined natural oud deepened with ambergris and smoothed by vanilla. The result is a dark, mesmerising rose oud with outstanding longevity and moderate sillage – opulent without shouting.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Recommended concentration: 40% extrait.

Top Notes: Damask Rose, Iris, Hyacinth
Heart Notes: Rose de Mai, Apricot, Patchouli
Base Notes: Ambergris, Oud, Vanilla

products.name: Compound Drakkar
products.description:
That famous metallic freshness hits first — dihydromyrcenol at full 1982 strength, backed by lavender, bergamot, and a cooling herbal rush of rosemary, basil, and mint. Nothing in the modern version comes close to this opening. It reads as clean, sharp, and almost industrially powerful.

The heart thickens with spicy carnation, coriander, and cinnamon, lifted by juniper. The spice sits on a dark animalic foundation the reformulated versions stripped away entirely. Our compound preserves all the great historic bases that gave the original its depth.

Underneath everything lies the real Drakkar Noir — patchouli, oakmoss, leather, and vetiver at full strength. The 1989 reformulation gutted the patchouli; subsequent versions removed the animalic and mossy fixatives too. This compound is for a scent in the style of the original.

This formula contains IFRA compliant oakmoss and Lyral so while it is IFRA compliant (to 1.75%) it is not EU compliant. We are able to craft an IFRA and EU compliant variant that is safe to a higher level. Contact us for details. An MOQ of 1kg applies on custom modifications.

products.name: Compound Elixir
products.description:
Compound Elixir is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Le Male Elixir by Jean Paul Gaultier. Launched in 2023 and created by Givaudan's Quentin Bisch, this is an amber fougère fragrance that amplifies the DNA of the iconic 1995 original into something richer, sweeter and more intense.

This compound features a bold lavender accord lifted by cool mint in the opening, transitioning quickly into a creamy, resinous heart of vanilla and benzoin. The base delivers warm honey, nutty tonka bean and a subtle tobacco note that adds depth without heaviness. The result is a sweet, gourmand-leaning masculine with outstanding projection and longevity of eight to ten hours – confident and unapologetically warm.

As with most of Bisch's fragrances, the original contains a number of Givaudan captives. Our captive replacer bases are arguably equal to the products they substitute, and paired with our exceptionally high-quality raw materials library, the result is a compound we believe surpasses the original.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Lavender, Mint
Heart Notes: Vanilla, Benzoin
Base Notes: Honey, Tonka Bean, Tobacco

products.name: Compound Feminité
products.description:
When Feminité du Bois was unveiled by Shiseido in 1992, it marked a watershed moment in perfumery that would reshape how we think about gendered fragrance. Created by the masterful duo of Christopher Sheldrake and Pierre Bourdon under the artistic direction of Serge Lutens, this scent dared to centre massive doses of cedarwood—traditionally masculine territory—in a composition explicitly celebrating femininity.

The timing was audacious. The early '90s fragrance market was dominated by aquatic freshness (L'Eau d'Issey had just launched) and clean, ozonic scents. Into this landscape came Feminité du Bois with its unapologetic 60% woods concentration, wrapped in dried fruits and spices like something from a Moroccan souk. Sheldrake's genius was in softening the cedar's astringency with an innovative plum accord—not fresh plum, but rather dried, honeyed, almost wine-like—creating a push-pull between austere wood and sensual fruit that had never been attempted at this scale.

This wasn't just a pretty wood scent; it was architectural, almost brutalist in its commitment to cedar, yet somehow intimate and skin-like. The composition became the template for Lutens' entire wood series (Cèdre, Santal Blanc, Chêne) and influenced everything from Hermès Terre d'Hermès to contemporary niche brands. It proved that women would embrace—even crave—compositions beyond the floral-oriental safety zone.

This compound is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the original.

Top Notes: G

products.name: Compound Five™
products.description:
Compound Five is a raw compound of our scent in the style of Chanel No 5 by Ernest Beaux! 

Because the original perfume contained Musk Ambrette which is prohibited from perfume use, we are offering this as an archival compound only. It must not be used or sold as a perfume and must not be applied to skin.

We recommend pairing this with our Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol which contains Solgard® (to minimise the destructive properties of the sun), a 15ml Luxury Glass Bottle and a set of 100 mouillettes so you can display this piece of history in your own home and allow friends and family to enjoy its scent safely through the use of smelling strips. 

Compound Five contains more than 25% pure jasmine absolute, rare Iris absolute, Ylang-ylang, finest Bourbon vanilla absolute, and many many more naturals and isolates which were cutting edge in 1921 when Mr Beaux crafted this masterpiece.

The original perfume was sold as a 38% dilution. All you need to fill a 15ml bottle is 5 grams of Compound five blended with with 10 grams of alcohol.

products.name: Compound Green™
products.description:
Polo Green was a masterpiece in refined perfuming from IFF perfumer Carlos Benaim in 1978. Benaim (born in Tangiers) is behind some of the most popular scents of the modern era, scents such as Flowerbomb, Armani's My Way, Calvin Klein Eternity for Men, Quorum, and Elizabeth Taylor White Diamonds.

The prohibition on large quantities of tree moss and the restriction of chemically modified IFRA "safe" tree moss all but destroyed the scent and so Polo Green faded from popularity and in some cases can be virtually impossible to find on a department store shelf (even in its now thin reformulation).

Compound Green fixes that. All perfumers should have a chance to smell and experience the original Polo — to understand what Benaim intended and why it was such a smash hit. Compound Green is our internal formula reconstructing the smell of the original. 

WARNING: This product contains non-IFRA compliant oakmoss and tree moss as well as other materials prohibited under IFRA 51 (including but not necessarily limited to Musk Ambrette). Compound Green is sold in an undiluted form for educational and industrial purposes only. To evaluate, apply a small amount to a smelling strip. Not for application to skin.

products.name: Compound Gris™
products.description:
Iris Gris (1946) from Jacques Fath is perhaps the most famous of all perfumes (amongst aficionados) and certainly the greatest Iris scent. It is now so rare to find a bottle that the cost currently runs over $10,000 US for one ounce of parfum! It was created by master perfumer Vincent Roubert who worked for Coty and produced Knize Ten in collaboration with him as well as number of other great scents like L'Aimant (1927) and A Suma (1934).

Fraterworks now presents this intricate and luxurious scent in the style of the original for perfumers to understand and appreciate the odour of a masterpiece prior to dilution and mass distribution. This is loaded with Jasmin absolute and Rose de Mai from Grasse and, of course, an overdose of natural iris.

Because the compound contains IFRA prohibited Musk Xylene, this compound must not be sold as a commercial fragrance and is for educational purposes only. Sampling should be done by smelling strip and this should not be applied to the skin.

Notes: Iris, Peach, Musk, Violet, Cedar, Vetiver, Lilac, Heliotrope, Carnation, Rose de Mai, Sandalwood, Lily of the Valley, Tuberose, Jasmin de Grasse.

Allergens: Citral, Farnesol, Geraniol, Linalool, Citronellol, Limonene, Eugenol, Benzyl Benzoate, Hydroxycitronellal, Benzyl Alcohol, Amyl Cinnamal, Benzyl Salicylate, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Isoeugenol, Coumarin, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Methyl 2-Octynoate, Cinnamal.

products.name: Compound Homme™
products.description:
Homme 2005 was a masterpiece of perfumery precision and is, at least in our opinion, one of the finest men's fragrances ever crafted. The classic Dior scent had the distinction of being one of the few modern fragrances to use a hefty dose of genuine Orris Absolute which it combined masterfully with other treasured naturals of cocoa, myrrh, incense, and much more.

Our compound is an internal formula in the style of the original, based on GCMS. We have not skimped and we have not made substitutions.

Top Notes: Lavender, Bergamot, Sage, Incense
Heart Notes: Iris, Cocoa, Cardamom, Amber
Base Notes: Leather, Myrrh, Vetiver, Patchouli

Allergens: Linalool, Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Coumarin, Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Eugenol.

products.name: Compound Imagination
products.description:
Compound Imagination is our internal formulation for a scent in the style of Imagination by Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2021, Imagination is a modern synthetic fragrance built around a massive dose of Ambroxan with black tea and citrus notes, creating a clean, radiant, and futuristic scent.

This compound features an exceptionally high concentration of Ambroxan (approaching 20%), paired with synthetic citrus molecules and a unique black tea accord. The result is a polarising but distinctive fragrance that embraces its synthetic nature rather than mimicking natural materials.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Sicilian Lemon, Calabrian Bergamot, Orange
Heart Notes: Black Tea Accord, Nigerian Ginger, Cinnamon Bark
Base Notes: Ambroxan, Guaiac Wood, White Musks

products.name: Compound Insensé
products.description:
This is probably the most demanded perfume compound from Fraterworks customers. Considered by many to be the greatest men's scent, it is a work of art. Alternating with the original Drakkar Noir, this is the fragrance I wear the most. I recommend 18% dilution for personal wear but IFRA compliance requires a lesser amount for sale.

Compound Insense opens with shimmering aldehydes, deep green fir, and bright citrus — luminous, almost crystalline. An extraordinary lily of the valley blooms at the heart, cool and radiant, threaded with sharp green basil. Powdery iris and creamy magnolia support the florals as conifer notes rise from the base.

This is a scent in the style of Givenchy's legendary 1993 masculine — awarded five stars by Luca Turin. The original was discontinued twice, leaving one of the finest men's fragrances ever created nearly impossible to find. Our compound preserves the original's character with the key materials that made it great. 

This compound is IFRA (but not EU) compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Aldehydes, Blackcurrant Bud, Lavender, Basil, Bergamot, Mandarin, Lemon
Heart Notes: Lily of the Valley, Magnolia, Iris
Base Notes: Fir Balsam, Vetiver, Cedar, Amber

products.name: Compound Male
products.description:
Compound Le Male is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the original Le Male from Jean Paul Gaultier. Launched in 1995, this is a classic fougère with an unconventional twist—featuring prominent vanilla and sweet notes alongside traditional barbershop lavender and mint.

This compound features a distinctive sweet-spicy profile with high levels of vanilla and coumarin, balanced with lavender, mint, artemisia, cardamom and cinnamon. The result is a powerful masculine fragrance that helped redefine men's perfumery by proving that sweetness and strength could coexist.

This compound is IFRA compliant (at a huge 25%) and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Please note that as this is the original formula it contains Lilial and is therefore not EU compliant. We may produce an EU compliant edition if there is sufficient demand.

Top Notes: Mint, Lavender, Bergamot, Artemisia
Heart Notes: Cinnamon, Cumin, Orange Blossom, Cardamom
Base Notes: Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Sandalwood, Cedar, Amber

products.name: Compound Nile
products.description:
Compound Nile is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Un Jardin sur le Nil by Hermès. Launched in 2005 as part of the Jardins collection, this is a fresh green floral fragrance built around tart green mango and aquatic lotus with vegetal and woody facets.

This compound features a distinctive green mango accord brightened with grapefruit and unusual vegetable notes of tomato leaf and carrot. The top notes of sparkling grapefruit and unripe mango provide a crisp, tangy opening, while the heart reveals delicate lotus and earthy bulrush evoking the riverbank. The base delivers soft musk, subtle incense and woody sycamore for a clean, airy finish. The result is a refreshing, transparent fragrance with moderate longevity and gentle sillage – natural and unforced.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Grapefruit, Green Mango, Tomato Leaf, Carrot
Heart Notes: Lotus, Bulrush, Peony, Hyacinth
Base Notes: Musk, Incense, Sycamore Wood, Labdanum

products.name: Compound Nomade
products.description:
Compound Nomade is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Ombre Nomade from Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2018, this is an intense oud-centric fragrance featuring a dark, smoky oud accord balanced with rose and raspberry.

This compound features a high concentration of oud accord combined with incense, benzoin, and amberwood. The addition of raspberry gives a subtle fruity facet to the composition while Damascus rose adds depth. The result is a powerful, long-lasting Middle Eastern-inspired fragrance with exceptional projection.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Incense
Heart Notes: Rose, Raspberry
Base Notes: Oud, Benzoin, Amberwood

products.name: Compound Oscar
products.description:
When Oscar de la Renta launched his first fragrance, simply called Oscar, in 1977, it was a significant moment in the perfume world for several reasons. At the time, the fragrance industry was buzzing with bold, statement-making scents, and Oscar stood out by blending elegance with a fresh, modern twist that reflected the designer's fashion ethos.

Created by perfumer Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Oscar wasn’t just a pretty floral—it had depth, with aromatic herbs like basil and rosemary cutting through the sweetness, and a powdery, musky base that gave it staying power. This made it a bridge between the floral classics of earlier decades (think Guerlain’s L’Heure Bleue) and the bolder scents that would dominate the '80s. People noticed its versatility—it could be worn by a socialite at a gala or a professional woman in the office, which broadened its appeal.

This is our internal compound of a scent in the style of the original.

Top Notes: Basil, Coriander, Orange Blossom, Peach
Heart Notes: Tuberose, Ylang-Ylang, Jasmine, Rose, Orchid, Lavender
Base Notes: Sandalwood, Patchouli, Musk, Amber, Vetiver, Cloves, Opoponax

products.name: Compound Oud Wood
products.description:
Compound Oud Wood is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Oud Wood by Tom Ford. Launched in 2007 as part of the original Private Blend collection, this is a refined woody amber fragrance built around smoky oud and creamy sandalwood with warm spices and resinous depth.

This compound features a smooth, accessible oud accord softened by rich sandalwood and earthy vetiver. The top notes of Brazilian rosewood, cardamom and Sichuan pepper provide an exotic yet approachable spiced opening, while the heart reveals precious oud notes balanced by creamy woods. The base delivers tonka bean, vanilla and amber for lasting warmth. The result is an elegant, quietly confident fragrance with moderate longevity and intimate sillage – sophisticated rather than challenging.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Notes: Brazilian Rosewood, Cardamom, Sichuan Pepper, Oud, Sandalwood, Vetiver, Tonka Bean, Vanilla, Amber

products.name: Compound Outlands
products.description:
Compound Outlands is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Outlands by Amouage. Launched in 2024 as part of the prestigious Essences collection, this is a sophisticated oriental woody fragrance built around frankincense and patchouli with a striking contrast between bright citrus opening and deep resinous base.

This compound features a complex incense-forward heart enhanced with earthy patchouli and warm spices including saffron and cumin. The top notes of lemon, bergamot, and cardamom provide an unexpectedly bright and invigorating opening, while elemi and Sichuan pepper add aromatic lift. The base delivers a rich amber accord layered with vanilla, benzoin, and labdanum, grounded by subtle oud and birch. The result is a dry, resinous fragrance with excellent projection and exceptional longevity – sophisticated and uncompromising.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Lemon, Bergamot, Cardamom, Elemi, Frankincense, Sichuan Pepper 
Heart Notes: Patchouli, Saffron, Orange Blossom, Anise, Geranium, Rose, Coriander, Cumin 
Base Notes: Vanilla, Benzoin, Amber, Labdanum, Oud, Opoponax, Frankincense, Birch, Musk

products.name: Compound Pink
products.description:
Launched in 2018 and originally crafted by Givaudan's Quentin Bisch, this is an oriental fragrance built around fruit, flowers and luxurious woods. 

This is enormously popular in the lab, amongst both male and female staff. It is one of our most universally requested compounds in fact. The original formula contains a number of Givaudan captives which we have carefully replaced to great effect in this, our compound in the style of the original.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Lychee, Pear, Bergamot, Pink Pepper, Grapefruit
Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Oud, Incense
Base Notes: Vanilla, Amber, Woody Notes, Musk, Vetiver, Evernyl

products.name: Compound Portrait
products.description:
Compound Portrait is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Portrait of a Lady from Frederic Malle. Launched in 2010, this is an opulent rose-patchouli fragrance with a distinctive dark, wine-like rose accord supported by frankincense and spices.

This compound features an extremely high concentration of Turkish rose absolute combined with patchouli, frankincense, and sandalwood. The addition of cinnamon, clove and blackcurrant creates a rich, baroque composition with exceptional depth and longevity.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Cinnamon, Clove, Blackcurrant
Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Frankincense, Raspberry
Base Notes: Patchouli, Sandalwood, White Musk

products.name: Compound Privé
products.description:
Compound Privé is our internal formula for a perfume in the style of Patou Pour Homme Privé by Jean Patou. It was perhaps the greatest men's fragrance ever made and most certainly the finest lavender fougère in existence. Launched in 1994 and crafted by Jean Kerléo (who served as chief perfumer of Jean Patou from 1967 to 1998), it represents the perfecting of his celebrated Patou Pour Homme from 1980.

Where the original was a bold oriental fougère built for the boardroom – dense with civet, castoreum and animalic leather – Privé took a different path. Kerléo softened the structure into something more intimate and bohemian whilst retaining the uncompromising quality of materials that defined the house. The result was a fragrance of extraordinary refinement: still unmistakably masculine, but approachable in a way the 1980 original never attempted to be. It rates a remarkable 4.6 on Fragrantica and commands four-figure prices on the secondary market for original bottles, on the rare occasion they come up for sale.

This compound features an exquisite lavender opening tempered by bitter galbanum and bright citrus of bergamot and mandarin. The heart transitions through subtle florals lifted by black pepper, before arriving at what many consider the finest base accord in masculine perfumery: bone-dry hay intertwined with green patchouli, authentic oakmoss, powdery orris root and creamy vanilla, all grounded by vetiver and Virginia cedar. The hay note in particular – crinkly, tobac

products.name: Compound Red™
products.description:
Due to high demand, we are now selling "private label" compounds of some popular demonstration formulas. Compound Red™ is our internal version for a scent in the style of a very popular unisex perfume which was launched in 2015.

The fragrance we are replicating here is built around a core of three accords, a mineral accord, a "fire and heat" accord, and a savoire-faire accord. Naturals such as Fir Balsam, Marigold, Jasmine and Saffron are found within those accords and add a surprising complexity.

This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Did you know?: just 50g of Compound Red™ and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

products.name: Compound Sauvage
products.description:
Compound Sauvage is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the best selling Sauvage crafted by François Demachy. This is neck and neck tied for best-selling men's fragrance with Aventus by Creed. Our private label compound contains all the luxurious naturals and premium aroma chemicals of the real thing.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Calabrian bergamot and Pepper
Heart Notes: Sichuan Pepper, Lavender, Pink Pepper, Vetiver, Patchouli, Geranium and elemi
Base Notes: Ambroxan, Cedar and Labdanum

products.name: Compound Seven™
products.description:
In 2002 the world of perfumery was changed forever when Yves Saint Laurent launched the first western styled Oud fragrance M7 (by Jacques Cavallier and Alberto Morillas under the creative direction of Tom Ford). As shocking as the scent was, the company went further by using a full frontal male nude in its marketing.

The perfume was a masterpiece of perfumery but as so often is the case with fragrances released before their time (think Chanel Bois Noir), it was soon removed from general sale. An attempt in recent years has been made to re-release the scent in a new formulation but that new formula is as bad as the original was great.

Fortunately we are able to offer our internal compound in the style of the original. It is Compound Seven and, despite containing all the original materials we can determine by GCMS (including the luxurious woods), it is IFRA compliant to a whopping 48% today. The original contained the merest trace of Lyral which we have sympathetically replaced for full EU compliance also.

This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Did you know?: just 50g of Compound Seven™ and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

products.name: Compound Tobacco Vanille
products.description:
Compound Tobacco Vanille is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Tobacco Vanille by Tom Ford. Launched in 2007 as part of the original Private Blend collection, this is a rich oriental spicy fragrance built around opulent tobacco leaf and creamy vanilla with warm gourmand facets.

This compound features a sumptuous tobacco accord enhanced with tonka bean and cacao for depth and indulgence. The top notes of tobacco leaf and warm spices including ginger provide a bold, aromatic opening, while the heart reveals tobacco blossom alongside rich vanilla. The base delivers dried fruit nuances and woody undertones that extend the fragrance's considerable longevity. The result is a warm, enveloping scent with exceptional projection and outstanding lasting power – confident and unapologetically luxurious.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Tobacco Leaf, Ginger, Spicy Notes 
Heart Notes: Vanilla, Cacao, Tonka Bean, Tobacco Blossom 
Base Notes: Dried Fruits, Woody Notes

products.name: Compound Tweed™
products.description:
Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of the our private label formula for a perfume in the style of Green Irish Tweed, a popular Creed men's fragrance launched in 1985.

Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram.

This is an incredible fragrance you will want to wear a lot so be sure to buy more than you think you need.

It is particularly expensive because it has a high amount of natural Mysore Sandalwood.

products.name: Compound XJ 1861™
products.description:
Due to high demand we are now selling "private label" compounds of some popular fragrances. Compound XJ 1861 is our internal formula for a scent in the style of XJ 1861 Naxos from Xerjoff. This is a celebration of Sicily and one of the top sellers for the brand.

The notes are:

Top: Lavender, Bergamot and Lemon
Heart: Honey, Cinnamon, Cashmeran and Jasmine Sambac
Base: Tobacco Leaf, Vanilla and Tonka Bean

This is a very gourmand scent with the sweet vanilla/honey taking pride of place in the opening. 

This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

products.name: Copaiba Oil Coeur
products.description:
Copaiba Balsam Coeur is one of those wonderful naturals which blends with virtually everything and is a great fixative. 

This Copaiba is especially luxurious as it the pure fractionated heart of the balsam made by one of the finest suppliers of natural oil in the world: LMR. The key components of the product are alpha-copaene, beta-caryopyllene, and alpha-humulene.

Copaiba Coeur has great value as a blender for more powerful materials used in making oud reconstructions. It is found in such fragrances as Tom Ford's Black Orchid, Tabu by Jean Carles and classic M7 of YSL.

Origin: Brazil
Method: Hydro distillation followed by fractionation
Part: Plant exudate

products.name: Coranol
products.description:
Walking a tightrope between the scent of linalool and coriander, Coranol is a wonderful floral fresh heart note that is practically indispensable in modern perfumes. Traces added freshness, overdoses add a much-loved modern character. Coranol is the warm blow of tropical holiday air. On first sniff it is obvious why this is such a beloved aroma chemical.

In the words of Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine): “[Coranol is o]ne of the most important chemicals used today. Coranol has an extremely fresh, floral, somewhat vibrant rosy-metallic note that is really almost impossible to replace. It combines exceptionally well with Dihydromyrcenol … imparting to every fragrance its freshness, its strength and its diffusion. It blends exceptionally well with citrus, florals, woody, spicy and musky notes and harmonises with green-metalic products such as Stemone, Paradisamide, Labienoxime or Buccoxime.”

Coranol is found in Aventus at around 2%, 3.5% in 1 Million Elixir, 3.5% in 212 Men Aqua by Carolina Herrera, 2% in Aqua di Gio Profondo, 2.7% in Aqua Pour Homme by Bulgari, and a whopping 6.5% in Light Blue by Dolce and Gabbana.

products.name: Coriander Seed Oil
products.description:
A high quality coriander seed oil is essential for perfumers. It adds freshness, links richer spice notes to the top of a scent and adds discreet warmth when dosed correctly.

Our Coriander seed oil is from Biolandes, a company that really excels in a number of areas such as Ylang-ylang and spices. You will definitely not be disappointed by this excellent quality and great priced product.

Origin: France, Russia, Moldova
Part: Roots
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Corinal® 184008B
products.description:
Corinal® 184008 B is an intense leather base featured prominently in such fragrances as Sublime by Jean Kerleo for Patou, a huge 5% in Habit Rouge (1965) by Jean-Paul Guerlain for Guerlain, and in a lesser amount in Vetiver (2000) by the same. It was also used in the more recent 2015 Pierre Guillaume scent Metal Hurlant.

Corinal blends exceptionally well with Lavender and Lavandin, Vertofix Coeur, Aerolide®, Styrax Resinoid, and all patchouli oils.

products.name: Cornmint Oil
products.description:
Cornmint Oil hits you with bold, clean mentholic freshness — brighter and more assertive than true peppermint. A harsh-woody undertone gives it raw, unpolished character. The dryout turns bitter-herbaceous, with a cooling sensation that lingers on skin.

This is the workhorse of the mint world — produced in vast quantities and far cheaper than true peppermint oil. It drives fresh colognes, fougères, and aftershave accords where raw minty power matters more than peppermint's balsamic refinement. The harsh-woody character adds masculine edge to cooling compositions.

Blend with lavender and rosemary for classic fougère freshness, or pair with eucalyptus and camphor for bracing aromatic intensity.

products.name: Coroliane
products.description:
Coroliane was an elegant De Laire lily of the valley base that, in combination with Mayciane and Mousse de Saxe provided the key character to No 19 by Chanel and many other fragrances of the 20th century. It was originally created by Edmond Roudnitska.

Coroliane is here restored to its original glory and IFRA compliant up to 6.3% of the finished product. It is a wonder of perfume art and is a very modern muguet that will suit any fragrance of today.

products.name: Corps Racine
products.description:
The most intense and longest lasting green chemical in the perfumer's arsenal, Corps Racine has a powerful note of crisp freshly shelled peas, green peppers and the bitter green of snapped twigs. 

Corps Racine is a powerful, green pyridine with unparalleled strength and persistence, lasting months longer than alpha-santalol. Like citronitrile, it extends the impact of volatile notes without diminishing them. Essential for any perfumer's toolkit, it blends beautifully with Verdantol™ and all of our luxurious muguet bases.

Due to its unbelievable power, we are offering this at 1% diluted in dipropylene glycol (DPG) or pure for those with the need for it. Note, however, that even at 1% this is incredibly strong and we recommend further dilution to at least 0.1% in the carrier of your choice.

products.name: Cosmonex 1485B
products.description:
Cosmonex 1485B rebuilds the scent of the Givaudan musk Cosmone (CAS 259854-70-1). With supplies collapsing, prices increasing dramatically and rumours of a complete discontinuation, a replacer base was needed.

Cosmonex opens warm and powdery, a rounded musk threaded with sweet ambergris and the softest clean-skin animalic hum. The impression is elegant, cosmetic, and quietly glowing. It is, in fact, an elegant musk blend in its own right.

Rebuilt one-for-one from rare musks and accessory notes, a trace lends outstanding cosmetic volume and a soft, second-skin warmth to florals, woods and amber accords. Use it to round rough edges, add lift, and make a composition feel finished and expensive.

Cosmone always shone in chypres and fougères, and Cosmonex slots straight into those accords with no reformulating. Slip it beneath white florals for a warm, powdery skin effect, or thread it through citrus and green tops to add body and glow. Even a single drop reads as pure luxury.

Analyses of finished perfumes show how widely the Cosmone character travelled: the musk this base reproduces appears in Chanel Pour Monsieur at around 0.09% and in Serge Lutens Tubéreuse Criminelle at roughly 0.36%. Cosmonex 1485B lets you build that same effect into your own work.

products.name: Costus Oil
products.description:
Costus oil opens with a startling animalic warmth — the smell of fur, wet hair, and human scalp. Beneath that surprising start, you find a soft woody-rooty core threaded with violet and orris facets. The fatty quality lingers and slowly turns powdery.

This is your secret weapon for vintage chypres, orientals, and any composition that needs a pulse of human warmth. A trace dose lifts a floral heart into something animal and alive. Pair it with rose absolute and orris butter for a richly warm natural accord. Jean Carles famously used a whopping 0.6% pure in Miss Dior.

Our oil comes from costus farmed in its native Himalayan habitat — same soil, same altitude, same climatic stress that shapes the wild plant. The result preserves every facet of the wild character. Use it in trace amounts; even a tiny addition reshapes the composition entirely.

Costus features in several of our demo formulas (see below), such as YSL Homme, Dana Tabu, Femme by Rochas, and Patou Pour Homme. Costus Root Tincture, a related preparation made from the same root, also threads through our Mitsouko, and L'Origan reconstitutions.

NOTE: Costus oil has an IFRA prohibited specification so this should not be used in fragrances that are required to comply with IFRA standards.

Costus Oil is on CITES Appendix I. That means, for now, we can't sell it from New Zealand. We are working on a solution.

products.name: Costus Oliffac
products.description:
Costus root oil is now prohibited by IFRA and its trade is highly restricted due to CITES. Fortunately IFF produce this wonderful base which, as far as natural replacers go, is an extremely good facsimile of the wild variety.

Costus oil is a rather unusual oil, having a distinctly animal odour (in the direction of wet dog or goat). It is particularly good blended with orris materials and it probably had its greatest outing as a key player in the original Miss Dior (1947) by Jean Carles for Dior.

Use this base one for one as a replacer whenever Costus Oil is called for in an old formula.

products.name: Coumarin
products.description:
Switching between hay and tonka beans depending on the context of the material in a fragrance, coumarin is one of the most widely used and popular synthetic aroma chemicals. It was the first synthetic used in a fragrance — 10% of Fougère Royale by Paul Parquet for Houbigant in 1882 (see the formula for this fine fragrance below).

A touch of coumarin can naturalise vanillin giving a truer note of vanilla beans, while an overdose contributes a wonderful cut hay scent.

products.name: Coumarin ex Cassia, Natural
products.description:
Switching between hay and tonka beans depending on the context of the material in a fragrance, coumarin is one of the most widely used and popular aroma chemicals. It was the first synthetic used in a fragrance — 10% of Fougère Royale by Paul Parquet for Houbigant in 1882 (see the formula for this fine fragrance below).

A touch of coumarin can naturalise vanillin giving a truer note of vanilla beans, while an overdose contributes a wonderful cut hay scent. 

This natural coumarin is isolated from cassia bark and may be said to hint at its originating source as it has a slightly warmer, spicier and more pungent odour profile than synthetic coumarin. It lacks that cherry-like note that is part of a synthetic material.

products.name: Coumarone
products.description:
Incredibly powerful, coumarone is a distinctly tonka / coumarin like synthetic with a very powerful nuance of orange blossoms. With the very high restrictions on methyl naphthyl ketone (oranger crystals) and coumarin itself, coumarone really comes into its own as a booster for both those materials.

Coumarone can also be used to create interesting fragrances that present tonka beans and orange blossoms in whole new light. A wonderful material that all perfumers should have in their organ.

products.name: Creosol
products.description:
Creosol opens with an intriguing smoky-spicy character that immediately sets it apart from simple vanilla materials. This phenolic warmth creates the illusion of vanilla pods charred over open flames, delivering both sweetness and edge in perfect balance. Its distinctive campfire-like quality brings depth without overwhelming the composition.

This complexity makes creosol indispensable when you need vanilla with gravitas. Rather than the flat sweetness of vanillin alone, creosol introduces woody depth and leather-like sophistication that transforms gourmand accords. Reach for it when building masculine vanillas, smoky orientals, or any composition requiring vanilla's warmth without its juvenile sweetness.

Perfumers use creosol's dual nature to bridge seemingly incompatible elements. In castoreum bases, it provides essential vanillic warmth that softens harsh phenolic notes. Use it at 0.1-0.5% to add smoke to gourmands, or push to 1% in leather accords where its phenolic bite enhances the animalic illusion. It excels at making white florals more narcotic and mysterious.

products.name: Cresylex™
products.description:
A powerful base to be used in place of a 10% dilution of para cresol. The IFRA 51 guidelines allow for a maximum use of 0.005% para cresol in your finished fragrance. Para cresol is incredibly strong but with the right balance of other materials, it can be an invaluable note at quite high doses. For that reason, Fraterworks is making this para cresol alternative available.

This is a slightly more floral alternative to Para Cresol and can be used at up to 100 percent of your finished product.

products.name: Cuir de Russie
products.description:
Cuir de Russie (Russian leather) is a classic base originating in the late 1800s. First appearing as a fragrance by Amie Guerlain in 1875, Cuir de Russie is a rich and intensely smoky animalic leather with rose and jasmine nuances. It has been used in countless fragrances and upon smelling its influence is clear in Knize Ten by Coty, Cuir de Russie by Ernest Beaux for Chanel, and numerous others. 

Cuir de Russie is in the DNA of many Chanel fragrances and may even offer a key to the authorship of Mademoiselle Chanel No 1, the illicit fragrance Coco Chanel had made during the second world war. This enriched leather scent is not far removed from the original Russian Bouquet de Catherine, the fragrance chosen by Chanel to become No 5.

Cuir de Russie can be used in place of birch tar for a sweeter and more refined smoke note.

Fraterworks® Cuir de Russie is a classical leather base. If you are looking for a more modern leather, see our Royal Leather 674276.

products.name: Cumin Seed Oil
products.description:
Cumin is an extremely powerful spice that can contribute unusual and interesting human skin like notes to the dry down of a fragrance. Cumin blends extremely well with rich florals, particularly Jasmine and Rose, and other spices and spiced bases like Jasmin Épicé.

Origin: Egypt
Part: Seeds
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Cuminaldehyde
products.description:
Cuminaldehyde opens with the unmistakable intensity of cumin spice - pungent, green, and immediately recognisable. This powerful material represents approximately 40% of natural cumin seed oil, delivering its characteristic warmth with additional herbaceous complexity. The animalic-sweaty undertones create intriguing depth that bridges spicy and leathery territories.

You'll find Cuminaldehyde invaluable for building authentic leather accords where its animalic warmth adds realistic skin-like facets. Use at 0.01-1% in oriental compositions for genuine spice market atmosphere. The material excels in carnation bases where its spicy-green character enhances the flower's natural clove-like aspects. Surprisingly, small amounts (below 0.2%) work brilliantly in muguet bases, adding naturalistic green stem effects.

The compound requires careful handling due to air sensitivity - minimise exposure to prevent oxidation. Its hydrogenation yields Mayol, explaining its connection to lily-of-the-valley notes. Combine with labdanum for enhanced leather effects, eugenol for spiced carnation depth, or sage oil for herbaceous complexity. Works particularly well in chypre and fougère modifications at low dosages.

Synergistic with historic bases Muguet des Bois, Cedarome and Jasmin Blanc.

This is such a potent material we are selling it at 10% and 1% dilutions in addition to the usual pure version.
tags: locale:Super strong. Discard gloves after use.

products.name: Cyclamen Aldehyde
products.description:
Cyclamen aldehyde is a beautiful and diffusive aroma chemical that brings to mind cucumber, melon and linden blossom. It is mainly used as an elegant nuancer for muguet, cyclamen and lilac notes though it also finds good use when carefully dosed in peony, violet and orange blossom accords.

Cyclamen aldehyde is a watery chemical that contributes beautiful fresh green top notes to a fragrance. It really is an essential material in the lily of the valley family.

Cyclamen aldehyde blends beautifully with Gardenia J. Ellis, Cyclamen des Alpes, Sandexol, all our Muguet bases, Dreamwood™, Florol, and Hivernal® Neo.

products.name: Cyclamen des Alpes
products.description:
Cyclamen des Alpes was one of two great De Laire bases created around the scent of two varieties of cyclamen flowers. “The wild Cyclamen which grows in Switzerland is called Alpine Violet, and possesses a very delicate and sweet odour. That botanically known as Persian Cyclamen has a somewhat harsher odour.” Cyclamen des Alpes reproduces the odour of the former.

The scent of cyclamen flowers is something of a blend of white lilac, lily and violet flowers (hence its sobriquet) with a suspicion of hyacinth.

This base is enriched with many luxurious floral absolutes and thanks to its delicate nature makes a perfect overdose material for the heart of a novel modern fragrance.

products.name: Cyclemax™
products.description:
Cyclemax opens with an unmistakable transparency—a clean, dewy floralcy that sits somewhere between lily of the valley and cyclamen. What sets it apart is a crisp, juicy melon-rind facet that feels modern and aquatic rather than powdery or old-fashioned. A subtle metallic-green edge, inherited from its cuminyl heritage, gives it the naturalistic snap of freshly snipped flower stems.

This material has become essential in the post-Lilial era, offering similar diffusive power without the regulatory concerns that ended its predecessor's reign. Use it to build the transparent backbone of muguet soliflores, or add it at trace levels to citrus accords where it amplifies juiciness and extends perceived freshness deep into the heart. It bridges heavier florals like Florol with sparkling top notes, acting as the engine that propels a composition outward.

products.name: Cyclohexyl Ethyl Alcohol
products.description:
Cyclohexyl Ethyl Alcohol greets you with clean, waxy floral freshness — cool and dewy, like morning moisture on peony petals. Lily and rose facets emerge alongside a green, faintly minty undertone. The overall impression is soft, transparent, and unmistakably floral.

This is Phenylethyl Alcohol's cooler, waxier cousin — translucent where PEA is warm and rosy. That icy quality makes it ideal for dewy peony and lily-of-the-valley accords that need crisp, clean radiance. Blend with hydroxycitronellal, linalool, and hedione for sheer white florals.

Use Cyclohexyl Ethyl Alcohol freely — it tolerates concentrations from traces to high doses without distortion. Soap, shampoo, and detergent bases that destroy other florals leave this one intact. Add it to rose or gardenia for a cool, waxy transparency that lifts the entire heart.

products.name: Cyclomethylene Citronellol
products.description:
Cyclomethylene Citronellol presents a soft, dewy floral — fresh rose petal and muguet entwined with a gentle pear-like fruitiness. Sweet citrus brightness adds lift without competing. The overall impression is quieter and more transparent than geraniol, elegant rather than assertive.

This dsm-firmenich creation is a universal harmoniser — it smooths and develops the notes of almost any composition. Jean-Paul Guerlain made it central to Héritage (1992), where its petal character bridges the lavender-spice top with the sandalwood-amber base. Use it wherever you need floral body without a dominant signature.

Build linden blossom accords by pairing it with muguet aldehydes and undecavertol, balanced against rosy materials. It gives remarkable body to citrus-floral compositions built from powerful materials at trace levels. Over one week's tenacity on blotter means your heart note anchors well into the drydown.

products.name: Cyclopidene
products.description:
Cyclopidene masterfully delivers a "salicylate/cresyl harmony" within a single molecule. This provides radiant, solar warmth whilst contributing naturalistic animalic depth. Perfumers utilise this powerful aroma chemical primarily as a modifier at 0.1-0.5% to create vibrant, multifaceted floral accords.

Use Cyclopidene at trace levels for authentic white floral impact. Combine with hedione to amplify diffusion and salicylates to enhance solar facets. Apply sparingly—its potency easily dominates compositions when overdosed. This material works effectively as a strategic replacer for restricted cresyl derivatives in modern formulations.

Beyond traditional floral applications, Cyclopidene finds remarkable utility in masculine fougères where its cresylic facet adds unexpected depth at 0.05%. In functional fragrances, it survives harsh detergent environments whilst maintaining radiance on wet fabrics.

When combined with ylang-ylang oil, Cyclopidene acts as a powerful booster, enhancing the natural characteristics of the oil, increasing its diffusion, and adding its unique solar and lactonic complexity. This synergy compensates for IFRA restrictions on ylang by amplifying its presence at lower concentrations—use 0.2% Cyclopidene to double the perceived ylang impact without exceeding regulatory limits.

Synergies: Ylang-ylang oil, Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Hedione®, Cis-3-Hexenyl Salicylate, Benzyl Salicylate, para-Cresyl Acetate, Indole, Citronellol.

products.name: Cyclosia®
products.description:
Hydroxycitronellal was first synthesised in 1905 by Knoll and Co. At the same time, Chuit Naef & Cie (founded in 1895 and now known as DSM-Firmenich) produced the finest quality of the chemical, called it Cyclosia® and used it to branch out into the aroma chemicals industry (it had previously dealt only in naturals). Cyclosia® is so vastly superior to all other versions of hydroxycitronellal that nearly 120 years later it remains a staple product of the company and the most sought-after white floral / lily of the valley chemical for the finest fragrances in the industry.

Cyclosia® has a radiance and diffusion that sets is apart from generic hydroxycitronellal. This makes it a desperately needed material today as it remains one of the few refined lily of the valley aldehydes that can be used in fairly generous amounts (up to 2.1% of the finished perfume) whilst retaining IFRA 51 compliance.

Discovered around the same time as the other famed floral chemical Iralia®, Cyclosia® formed a substantial part of the midcentury masterpiece Muguet des Bois, the lily of the valley perfume and then base created by Henri Robert for Coty and later used as the foundation of Diorissimo by Edmond Roudnitska for Dior.

Cyclosia is hydroxycitronellal… in 3D!

products.name: Cycloverdyl Propionate
products.description:
Cycloverdyl propionate opens with a soft, sweet floral-herbal character that sits somewhere between jasmine and fresh basil. A gentle anise undertone weaves through the heart, giving it unexpected depth. Green-woody facets round out the base, fruity and oily rather than sharp.

This is the softer, longer-lasting cousin of Verdyl Acetate (Jasmacyclene) — where the acetate is bright and forcefully green, the propionate trades sharpness for refined herbal-floral warmth. It adds depth to jasmine and green-floral accords without dominating. Fougères and fresh compositions benefit from its sweet herbal backbone.

Blend it with Hedione and benzyl acetate for a herbal-jasmine heart, or with dihydromyrcenol and coumarin for a green fougère. At 144 hours on a strip, tenacity is exceptional for such a gentle material. It works from traces up to 8% without turning aggressive.

It is important to note that this material is also often referred to simply as Verdyl Propionate. They are the same thing.

products.name: Cyclozonal
products.description:
Cyclozonal opens with a sharp, metallic freshness that captures the scent of air after rain - clean, cool, and almost silvery. This aldehyde combines ozonic transparency with subtle floral nuances, creating an impression of dewy lily-of-the-valley blooming in crisp mountain air. Its unique character bridges the gap between high-impact marine notes and sophisticated modern florals.

This material is a powerful booster for citrus accords — even small additions amplify bergamot, lemon, and grapefruit with crystalline lift. It excels in fougères and colognes where you need that clean, just-showered effect. Its stability across all classical applications makes it equally valuable in functional products.

Use Cyclozonal when you need to cut through heavy base odours in functional products or when building contemporary fougères that demand crisp, clean openings. It pairs brilliantly with citrus oils, aldehydes, and woody materials like vetiver. Its metallic-ozonic facets bring remarkable diffusion and a sense of spaciousness to dense compositions.

products.name: Cypress Oil
Cypriol Heart “Superior” Rect.
products.description:
This natural Cypriol Heart from Floral Concept (the finest quality as of 2026) opens with a polished woody-earthy character, cleaner and more refined than standard nagarmotha oil. You get the same smoky-leathery depth but stripped of harsh edges, revealing subtle saffron-like warmth beneath. The dry spiciness sits beautifully between patchouli and vetiver territory.

This rectified heart fraction excels in building convincing oud accords without the price tag of genuine agarwood. Pair it with sandalwood to soften its intensity and reveal sweeter undertones. It transforms leather compositions with authentic smokiness and adds mysterious depth to chypres and oriental bases.

Try Cypriol Heart as a modifier in florals where a touch of darkness elevates the composition. Combine with benzoin, labdanum, and frankincense for incense-style warmth. Start at low dosages—its tenacity and richness can dominate if overdosed.

products.name: Cypriol “Signature” Oil
products.description:
The smoky nuance of a winterly campfire smoulders beneath the surface of this marvelous oil from LMR. Cypriol (or Nagarmotha) is frequently used (often in large doses) to recreate the scent of Oud in a fragrance because Cypriol is something of a chameleon oil. A good example of this is Ajmal Dahn Oudh Al Shams in which Cypriol is blended with Guaiac Wood Oil and Gurjun Balsam Oil.

At first Cypriol is spicy with aspects of Cinnamon and Cascarilla, and the next minute it is earthy green and vetiver like. But then, from out the blue, it reveals the mystical scent of frankincense before retreating back to its woody default.

LMR, one of the finest makers and suppliers of natural oils in the world, has created a genuine masterpiece in their handling of this treasured oil. There are more facets in this Cypriol than any we sampled from other suppliers and so it is our Signature oil.

products.name: D-Limonene
products.description:
D-Limonene opens with unmistakable fresh orange character—zesty, sweet, and instantly recognisable as citrus peel. The light terpenic quality adds naturalistic freshness without harshness, while subtle fruity nuances hint at tangerine and berry. This is the defining molecule of orange: clean, bright, and universally appealing.

This terpene constitutes roughly 98% of sweet orange essential oil, making it nature's most abundant citrus compound. The 4-hour substantivity limits its use as a standalone top note, but its value lies in providing immediate citrus impact and fresh lift and it can be blended with terpeneless or folded orange oil to extend its llife.

D-Limonene vs L-Limonene vs Dipentene

These two molecules smell distinctly different despite identical structure. D-Limonene (the dextro form) delivers the familiar fresh, zesty orange-peel character found in citrus fruits.

L-Limonene (the laevo form) smells piney, terpenic, and turpentine-like—closer to coniferous oils than citrus.

You may also see Dipentene which is the racemic variant (a 50:50 blend of Laevo and Dextro). As you'd expect it smells like a piney-citrus blend.

products.name: Dahna
products.description:
Compound Dahna is our internal formula in the style of Les Sables Roses by Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2019 and created by Jacques Cavallier Belletrud, the original is an oriental floral built on a deliberately simple contrast: two qualities of rose set against oud wood, with nothing crowding them out.

This compound features a bright, faintly watery rose accord — more red and spicy than powdery — carried over a clean oud that stays smooth rather than barnyard. Saffron and black pepper sharpen the opening and give the composition its characteristic edge, while ambergris lifts and warms the drydown without adding sweetness. The result is a refined Arabian-style rose oud with above-average projection and excellent longevity – opulent but uncluttered.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Saffron, Black Pepper
Heart Notes: Rose, Bulgarian Rose
Base Notes: Oud, Ambergris

products.name: Damascenone
products.description:
Damascenone is the most important rose ketone in reconstructions of rose absolute and oil. It is frequently blended with Damascone Beta and Damascone Alpha which we also stock. In small amounts (diluted to 1%) Damascenone gives lift and radiance and in larger amounts it adds a distinctly sweet rose. It is indispensable.

Because of its incredible strength and the high IFRA restriction we sell this in 10% dilution or pure.

We only stock the original Firmenich quality which far surpasses all other manufacturers in beauty.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Damascenone Total
products.description:
Damascenone Total is the same molecule and same CAS family as Damascenone; the only difference that they differ in purity and cost. Damascenone pure is minimum ninety-nine percent beta-damascenone: cleaner, marginally more honeyed, and more efficient drop for drop. Damascenone total is minimum ninety-three percent, with the remainder being less powerful or non-odorous isomers of the same compound.

In practice, the two smell very close and can be used interchangeably. The pure version gives you slightly more impact per unit weight, which matters when you are working near your rose ketone ceiling. The total version is less expensive, making it the practical choice for most formulation work. If you are building a fine fragrance where every fraction of a percent counts, reach for the pure. For everything else, the total delivers the same magnificent rose-plum radiance at a friendlier price.

products.name: Damascol 4
products.description:
Damascol opens with a distinct peppery bite before revealing a deep, dark rose absolute character underneath. The overall effect is rounded and warm rather than bright, with woody undertones and subtle fruity facets. A faint iris-like powderiness lingers in the drydown.

Use this to extend and darken rose accords where you want depth rather than brightness. It stretches rose absolute beautifully, adding spicy warmth without shifting the floral identity. In geranium compositions it works as a rich modifier that adds sophistication.

Start at low doses and build up, as the pepper note can dominate unexpectedly at higher levels. Combine with alpha-damascone and damascenone for a complete dark rose palette. It pairs particularly well with black pepper, vetiver, and cedar for spicy-woody floral structures.

products.name: Damascone Alpha
products.description:
Damascone Alpha is a member of the Rose Ketones, a group of chemicals with incredible radiance and sublime beauty. They have a special IFRA standard in which any one or combination of all must be counted towards a maximum total load of 0.043% in a finished fine fragrance. Fortunately traces have impact so these are still some of the most valuable perfumery materials today.

Damascone Alpha is more fruit (apple and plum) than rose, with a metallic and slightly spicy edge. It was first sold at 3% of the Firmenich base Cetylia®, a lovely rose base which partnered with Dorinia® the launch-pad for Damascone Beta.

Because of its incredible strength and the high IFRA restriction we sell this in 10% dilution or pure.

We only stock the original Firmenich quality which far surpasses all other manufacturers in beauty.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Damascone Beta
products.description:
Damascone Beta is the sweetest of the rose ketones and is often found alongside Damascone Alpha or Damascenone Beta (and less often Damascone Delta). It has nuances of tobacco (along with Damascenone).  It was first sold at 3% of the Firmenich base Dorinia® (formula below) alongside Cetylia® which showcased Damascone Alpha the sharper and more metallic of the two.

Because of its incredible strength and the high IFRA restriction we sell this in 10% dilution or pure.

We only stock the original Firmenich quality which far surpasses all other manufacturers in beauty.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Damascone Delta
products.description:
Damascone Delta is probably the least used (except the somewhat less-interesting and extremely expensive gamma) of the rose ketones but it shouldn't be. Damascone Delta has a wonderful black doris plum note backed by sweet black currant, rose, tobacco and a hint of vibrant mint. It is sweeter than Damascone Alpha and livelier than Damascone Beta.

Because of its incredible strength and the high IFRA restriction we sell this in 10% dilution or pure.

We only stock the original Firmenich quality which far surpasses all other manufacturers in beauty.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Damascone Gamma
products.description:
Damascone gamma smells of rose and cooked apple with ripe plum depth and — distinctively — a herbal, almost wormwood-like edge that sets it apart from its alpha and beta siblings. The effect is fruity, floral, and green at once. Subtle tobacco undertones emerge in the drydown.

Use damascone gamma at trace levels — it is potent and will dominate if overdosed. A tiny amount adds fruity-floral complexity to rose accords, green compositions, and herbal blends. The herbal dimension makes it irreplaceable where you want damascone character with a green, sage-like twist.

Alpha-damascone is sharper and more metallic; beta is the sweetest and most wine-like; gamma brings a herbal-green quality the others lack. Pair it with other rose materials, ionones, and aldehydes. Always evaluate well diluted — its complexity unfolds at low levels.

We carry Damascone Alpha, Damascone Beta, Damascone Delta, Damascenone, and Damascenone Total. Try them side by side — they are four distinct materials with a family resemblance, not interchangeable versions of the same thing.

products.name: Daphne Supreme
products.description:
As the gloomy days of winter near their end, the burgeoning flowers of Daphne Odora begin to appear. Daphne has one of the most beautiful scents in the entire world of flowers and yet it is relatively unknown in its true form in Western perfumery. Historically many Daphne bases existed, but they were of a fantasy type and not reflective of the true Daphne shrub.

Adding to its scarcity in fine fragrances is the fact that Daphne plants are highly toxic to man and brute and so extracts do not exist.

Fraterworks Daphne Supreme is not a fantasy base but rather a wonderful representation of the flowers in full bloom. As is often the case with winter flowering plants, Daphne is extremely powerful and its odour is one of penetrating citrus, green leaves and white flowers.

This is perhaps the most beautiful of all our modern floral bases and one that we are certain will form part of a world class fragrance in the near future.

Daphne Supreme blends extraordinarily well with Jasmolactone® Delta, Jasmin Fleurs, Verdantol™, Suralette Extra and Gardenia J. Ellis.

products.name: Dark Ginger CO2, P. Jungle Essence
products.description:
Upon first smelling this dark Ginger Oil CO2 (Pure Jungle Essence), my heart skipped a beat. In a moment not only did I experience an incredibly true to life and beautiful scent of ginger, but a million nuances hit me invoking a flood of memories. Wood notes reminding me of childhood years spent wandering through the building sites of homes crafted from fine timbers in a relative's luxury construction business, the scents of dank earth from rugby fields at school and walks in the forested hills surrounding my childhood home, and rich gingerbread fresh from the oven on winterly days.

Unlike the lighter "Top Note" variant (M51690), this standard version (M51689) delivers full-spectrum richness with deeper base notes. Use it to energise woody bases with vetiver and sandalwood, cut through heavy white florals, or build authentic gingerbread accords with vanilla and tonka. Its unmatched realism makes it indispensable for contemporary compositions demanding genuine naturalness.

Like all MANE products you are not just buying beautiful scents, you are buying art. In this CO2 extracted oil, MANE has managed to encapsulate a lifetime of wonderful odours and memories.

For an inimitable fragrance of exquisite elegance we recommend a pairing of Ginger Oil Pure Jungle Essence with Payan Bertrand's dazzlingly citrus-fresh Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire, the rare top note CO2 extraction, also from MANE, or LMR's marvellous Madagascan Fresh Ginger essential oil. For something a little dif
