products.name: Dartanol®
products.description:
Dartanol is the highest quality Laevo form of Bacdanol. It is the same chemical but the purest and finest version. It can be used one for one in place of Bacdanol for a richer and more cosmetic result.

Blends of Dartanol with Polysantol and Firsantol are supreme but significantly more Dartanol can be used in a fragrance because a) it is not restricted by IFRA, and b) it is less powerful than the others. But despite that, you should not be fooled into thinking Dartanol is not a powerful and rich sandalwood chemical. It is, in fact, one of the finest substitutes for natural sandalwood in chemical form and a simple combination of Dartanol with Ebanol is a truly classic combo.

Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) sings the praises of this material thus: “[Dartanol] is better than Bacdanol. It is similar but more beautiful, more radiant, possessing a more natural sandalwood character. It is also more diffusive. I believe [Dartanol] will slowly replace Bacdanol because, although similar, it is both comparably priced and livelier. The material’s uses are similar to those of Bacdanol.”

For more information on Sandalwood aromatics, see our Sandalwood Synthetics Primer.

products.name: Datilat
products.description:
Datilat smells like a bowl of dried fruit: figs, dates, raisins and prunes, waxy and dense, with a brandy-like warmth rising off them. Behind the sweetness sits a greener fig-leaf facet that stops it turning sticky. Neat it can seem slightly plasticky; once diluted, the fruit comes sharply into focus.

Use it for any dried-fruit or boozy effect. It gives fig accords their fruit, deepens oriental bases with date and raisin, and supplies the raisin character that makes a cognac accord read true. In florals a trace adds a fruity twist and underlines the plummy side of the damascones.

For a fig theme, balance it with green leaf notes and creamy peach materials. For dates or plums, pair it with davana and beta-damascone; for cognac, add rum ether and a touch of ethyl crotonate. In an oud composition it builds the boozy, raisiny sweetness of a good aged spirit.

products.name: Davana Oil
products.description:
Smelling Davana oil for the first time you would be forgiven for thinking you are smelling a fine aged bourbon or rum. Beloved for its fruity and liquor top notes, this luscious oil comes from many of the same areas as Indian Sandalwood Oil and it is prized, especially amongst natural perfumers, for contributing a fruit note that is otherwise difficult to obtain.

It is a member of the Artemisia family and not surprisingly it modifies and blends well with its relatives (particularly Armoise).

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

Part: Foliage and stems
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Delphol HC
products.description:
Delphol HC opens with green jasmine freshness — clean, airy, and immediately reminiscent of magnolia blossom. A tea-like quality adds translucent brightness. Beneath that, delicate peach fruitiness and an earthy warmth recall the celery-seed facet of its cousin cis-jasmone.

This dsm-firmenich creation belongs to the Hedione family — a by-product of methyl jasmonate synthesis. At trace levels in fine fragrance, it adds volume and body to white floral accords. Push it higher in functional bases for convincing celery-seed and exotic fruity effects.

Pair Delphol HC with hedione and benzyl acetate for luminous jasmine hearts. Its 48-hour tenacity on blotter gives your magnolia and tea accords lasting presence in the drydown. Exceptional chemical stability across all bases — including laundry and cleaning products — makes it a true workhorse.

products.name: Delphone
products.description:
Delphone hits the nose with immediate jasmine power — diffusive, complex, and unmistakably floral. A celery-seed spiciness adds unexpected bite. Coconut-lactonic warmth and an oily green-herbal quality round out the profile, making this far more interesting than a simple jasmine substitute.

Born as a by-product of Hedione synthesis, Delphone shares the jasmonate family's gift for radiance. It functions primarily as a white floral booster — even at trace levels it adds volume, body, and diffusion to floral accords. The lactonic facet gives it surprising versatility in fruity compositions built around peach and mango.

Use Delphone sparingly in fine fragrance — it is powerful enough to dominate at anything above trace levels. Blend with hedione and methyl dihydrojasmonate for layered jasmine complexity. Its 16-hour tenacity anchors floral hearts effectively, though it works best paired with longer-lasting base materials.

products.name: Delta Decalactone
products.description:
Delta decalactone is without doubt the most coconut-like of the common lactones. It opens with a rich, creamy sweetness—fresh coconut flesh, condensed milk, and a buttery smoothness that reads as immediately tropical and edible. Subtle peach and nutty undertones add complexity, but the overwhelming impression is pure, lush coconut cream.

Use this lactone to build convincing coconut accords or to add creamy, milky body to white florals like gardenia, tuberose, and frangipani. It softens and naturalises synthetic sandalwood, rounds out peach and tropical fruit bases, and gives gourmand compositions that irresistible dessert-like richness—think coconut cream pie and vanilla ice cream. In musky skin-scent accords, it adds a warm, lactonic intimacy.

Delta Decalactone vs Delta Dodecalactone

Both are delta lactones with a creamy, coconut-milky character, but the two extra carbon atoms in delta dodecalactone shift its profile noticeably. Delta decalactone is the brighter, more overtly coconut of the pair—fresh coconut cream with a sweet, almost fruity lift.

Delta dodecalactone is heavier, more buttery, and leans further into peach and dairy territory; think warm coconut butter rather than fresh coconut milk. The dodecalactone also has a more pronounced oily-fatty quality and a slightly metallic top note that the decalactone lacks.

In practice, the two work beautifully together: the decalactone provides the recognisable coconut sparkle while the dodecalactone adds buttery depth a

products.name: Delta Dodecalactone
products.description:
Delta Dodecalactone opens with an opulent wave of creamy richness—imagine coconut cream folded into melted butter with ripe peaches suspended throughout. This material doesn't whisper; it envelops with its distinctive combination of dairy-like creaminess and tropical fruit depth. The initial impression reveals a complex interplay between buttery lactonic notes and fruity facets that lean toward peach and apricot, all wrapped in a characteristic oily richness. A subtle metallic edge at concentration adds intrigue, while exceptional tenacity ensures this creamy signature persists for hours, creating a luxurious base that anchors compositions.

Deploy Delta Dodecalactone at 0.5-5% when you need pronounced creamy effects with superior fixation. Its six-membered lactone ring (versus five in gamma lactones) creates a softer, more dairy-like character ideal for gourmand accords where buttery richness is paramount. Use it as a modifier in white florals—particularly tuberose and gardenia—where it softens harsh edges while adding creamy depth. In fruity compositions, it transforms simple peach notes into "peaches and cream" complexity. The material excels at bridging disparate elements: linking citrus tops to woody bases, smoothing transitions between florals and musks, or adding edible appeal to abstract compositions.

The structural difference between Delta Dodecalactone (C12) and Delta Decalactone (C10) profoundly impacts their olfactory character. Delta Decalactone delivers sweet,

products.name: Delta Nonalactone
products.description:
Delta nonalactone presents coconut in its most naturalistic form—creamy, fatty, and milky rather than synthetic or overtly sweet. This six-membered ring lactone captures the essence of fresh coconut milk with remarkable authenticity. The material's coumarin-like facet makes it invaluable for modern fougères where traditional coumarin faces restrictions, providing that distinctive hay-sweet warmth without regulatory concerns.

You'll find delta nonalactone particularly effective at dosages from trace amounts up to 5% in concentrate, where it creates authentic tropical bases superior to gamma nonalactone's more artificial sweetness. The material excels in lavender and floral-aldehydic compounds where its coumarin character bridges fresh aromatics with warm bases. Its fatty-milky quality transforms simple vanilla accords into sophisticated crème brûlée effects, while in tropical compositions it provides the exact coconut milk character that eludes other lactones.

Layer delta nonalactone with sandalwood for creamy tropical woods, combine with jasmine sambac for exotic white florals, or blend with real vanilla absolute for indulgent gourmand bases. The material's stability and naturalness make it perfect for compositions requiring authentic coconut without the piercing sweetness that betrays synthetic origins. This lactone represents your best choice when coconut must read as genuine rather than confectionery.

Delta vs Gamma vs Bicyclononalactone

The nonalactone family showcase

products.name: Delta Octalactone
products.description:
Delta octalactone captures the smell of real coconut flesh more faithfully than its gamma counterpart. The character is soft, creamy, and milky, with peach-apricot facets and a faint tonka-like sweetness. Where gamma octalactone can veer toward spicy and herbaceous, this stays purely tropical and gentle.

That 400-hour blotter life is remarkable for a material that smells this soft. It anchors compositions invisibly, contributing creaminess long after brighter materials have faded. In gourmand fragrances it provides the milky-coconut base that vanillin and ethyl maltol need to lean against. In white florals it supplies the creamy tropical undertone found naturally in gardenia and tiare.

Delta-decalactone and delta-dodecalactone build a layered coconut effect alongside it. Vanillin and coumarin push it toward gourmand territory. Sandalwood highlights its creamy-woody facets. In peach accords, gamma-undecalactone handles the fruity side while delta octalactone provides the creamy body.

products.name: Delta Undecalactone
products.description:
Delta undecalactone delivers soft, creamy coconut wrapped in milky warmth and a gentle peach undertone. Where gamma undecalactone is bold and attention-grabbing, the delta form is rounder, smoother, and more naturalistic — it blends rather than dominates. The waxy quality gives it a comforting, almost edible character.

Use delta undecalactone to add coconut-cream depth to your gourmand and oriental compositions. It softens sharp florals, rounds woody bases, and adds milky smoothness to vanilla accords. Its extraordinary tenacity — persisting for hundreds of hours on blotter — makes it an invisible but powerful fixative.

Blend with gamma undecalactone and gamma nonalactone for layered lactonic effects. Try it alongside vanillin and coumarin for creamy gourmand depth. Pair with tuberose and gardenia bases to add the natural coconut-milk warmth found in tropical white florals.

products.name: Deluxe Sample Spray Bottles, 2ml
products.description:
These deluxe sample vials are the industry standard for high end and artisanal perfumery. Each vial can hold 2ml (around 1.7 grams) of perfume. 

No tools are needed — simply fill and push the closure mechanism into the bottle until it snaps in place. These are highly resistant to leaking and the spray pump offers consistent and uniform dispersion.

Bottles (including pump) are 60 mm high and 10 mm wide.

These luxury sample bottles are made in France.

products.name: Dewfruit
products.description:
Dewfruit opens with an exotic burst of lychee and raspberry, both fresh and sophisticated. The cassis heart emerges powerfully—this is the base's signature, built around Givaudan's molecule Neocaspirene. Subtle herbal-green undertones keep the fruit from becoming candied, lending an elegant naturalism.

This iconic base originated at Quest International before Givaudan's acquisition and has become essential in modern perfumery. The sparkling fruity top note in Thierry Mugler's Angel came from Dewfruit, demonstrating its power to define legendary compositions. Use this base specifically to access the Neocaspirene molecule, which delivers cassis character that was difficult to achieve before its development.

Use Dewfruit between 0.1% and 5% in your compositions. It transforms rose, violet, and cassie accords with fruity radiance. The base works beautifully in chypres needing modern fruit, gourmand compositions, and abstract contemporary designs. Expect bright, happy complexity without excessive sweetness.

products.name: Dianthine Extra
products.description:
Dianthine Extra is a classic early 20th carnation base built around luxurious and rich essential oils and absolutes. Overloaded with iris roots, Bulgarian rose oil from LMR and finest ylang-ylang Comoros, this is our first choice carnation. Fully present in the top notes of a fragrance but also very long lasting despite no reliance at all on highly restricted chemicals such as Isoeugenol.

Overdose it in our L'Origan replica formula instead of Dianthus for a richer and perhaps even better balanced fragrance than the original!

products.name: Dianthus
products.description:
From traces for warmth to overdose (3.7% of the finished product according to IFRA 50), Dianthus can be used in virtually every fragrance type. Fraterworks Dianthus is a famed carnation base from the early 20th century.

Anywhere eugenol finds a place, Fraterworks® Dianthus can be used. The spicy clove heat of the opening is balanced with a balsamic vanilla and heliotrope accord that is perceptible through the whole product.

Dianthus is a masterpiece in classical perfume arts which adds richness to even the most modern scents. For a synergistic longer lasting and equally great historic carnation base, we also stock Oeillet.

products.name: Diethyl Hexyl Adipate
products.description:
Diethyl hexyl adipate is not a fragrance material — it is a tool. This colourless, odourless liquid serves as a neutral carrier and diluent for concentrated aroma chemicals and fragrance oils. Its complete lack of smell means it dilutes without distorting, letting your materials express themselves cleanly.

The main application is in candle and wax fragrance work. Diethyl hexyl adipate is compatible with waxes, does not block wicks, and is non-flammable — solving three common problems at once. It allows you to achieve higher fragrance loads in candle formulations without the flash-point issues that alcohol-based solvents create. It also works as a co-solvent for rich, heavy fragrance oils that need thinning.

Beyond candles, use it to dilute potent aroma chemicals for easier handling, or as an emollient carrier in skin-safe fragrance balms and lotions. It is universally compatible with fragrance materials and leaves no residual odour. Think of it as the perfumer's equivalent of a clean glass — it holds whatever you pour into it without adding anything of its own.

products.name: Diethyl Malonate
products.description:
Diethyl malonate opens with unmistakable crisp green apple freshness—clean, sweet, and instantly appealing. A soft pineapple undertone adds tropical warmth, while the subtle winey-estery character provides sophisticated depth. The gentle balsamic quality rounds the profile beautifully, preventing the sharpness that mars lesser fruity materials.

This chemical occurs naturally in grapes, strawberries, guava, melon, pineapple, blackberries, and even whiskey—which explains its remarkable naturalism despite the low cost. Use it as the lead note in apple or pear accords, or to brighten berry, melon, and tropical mixes. Drop it alongside light florals like lily of the valley or freesia for playful fruit sparkle without turning your composition into candy.

Work between 0.1% and 2% for subtle lift that enhances other fruits without announcing itself. Push toward 3–5% and the green apple becomes obvious with a boozy, cocktail-style wine nuance.

products.name: Diethyl Phthalate (DEP)
products.description:
DEP is one of the longest used fragrance diluents due to the fact that it is able to dissolve more perfumery materials than any other single solvent. It is also colourless, odourless and does not develop off notes — problems which can plague other diluents.

Despite its long-standing use and safety (attested to by having no IFRA restriction and no EU restriction in cosmetic and fragrance use), many industries are shifting toward non-phthalate alternatives due to regulatory and consumer preferences. Always check regional compliance and consider testing alternatives like triethyl citrate (TEC) or dipropylene glycol (DPG) for specific applications.

DEP is Miscible with alcohol and oils but insoluble in water.

products.name: Diethyl Succinate
products.description:
Diethyl succinate is a material of quiet utility. Its own scent is barely there — a mild, wine-like fruitiness with stewed apple and grape nuances and a faint ylang-like quality. You would never build a composition around it, but you might wonder why your fruit accords lack naturalness without it.

Its real value is dual: it adds a subtle vinous character while simultaneously extending the life of the brighter, more volatile fruity materials around it. Most materials this mild would be dismissed, but diethyl succinate's ability to add persistence and naturalness to fruit and white floral accords is genuinely useful.

White flower compositions gain an unctuous richness from a small addition. Wine and cognac accords become more convincing. In fruity top notes, it acts as invisible support — the customer smells better fruit without knowing why.

products.name: Diethyl Tartrate (DET)
products.description:
Diethyl Tartrate opens with barely-there character—vinous, faintly fruity, and pleasantly neutral. Unlike commodity solvents that contribute nothing to your composition, DET adds subtle wine-like body and a caramellic warmth that supports rather than suppresses. This is living space, not dead space.

Derived from tartaric acid—the compound that gives wine its structure—DET shares chemical lineage with grapes and cognac. This makes it the solvent of choice for vintner-style accords where authenticity matters. Use it to add mouthfeel and viscosity to brandy, cognac, and wine notes; pair it with Brandy CO2 for boozy compositions that feel genuinely alcoholic rather than synthetically fruity. The subtle polarity helps sustain volatile top notes that standard solvents would flatten.

Use Diethyl Tartrate as a carrier for precious floral absolutes—rose, osmanthus, boronia—where DPG might mute the sparkling top notes you paid premium prices for. It excels at dissolving difficult crystalline materials like vanillins and synthetic musks, providing a warm, non-chemical solvent profile that vintage perfumers appreciated. Note: DET is polar, making it excellent for absolutes and polar crystals but less suitable for waxy citrus oils.

products.name: Dihydro Alpha Ionone
products.description:
Dihydro Alpha Ionone is the shy (and costly) member of the family, rarely making an appearance. But this underrated aroma chemical forms a natural part of some of the most wonderful natural materials: Osmanthus, Champaca and violets. While the gamma variant (a constituent of ambergris) is warm and woody, this alpha type is ambery, floral and woody making it ideal for adding a violet note in a way that differs from most commercial fragrances which tend to rely on the much cheaper ionones. 

Our Dihydro Alpha Ionone is very high purity and has a wonderfully addictive and enticing odour which is far more delicate and natural than Dihydro Beta Ionone which is also fruitier and greener. Blends of all three can be used for interesting and novel effects.

Dihydro Alpha Ionone blends very well with Petitgrain and other oils of the citrus family, as well as violet odorants and naturals. Accords with Iso E Super and ambers like Norlimbanol, Operanide, Ambrocenide and especially Spirambrene are interesting and extremely modern smelling.

products.name: Dihydro Beta Ionone
products.description:
Dihydro Beta Ionone is a major component of the natural scent of osmanthus flowers. It adds floral volume and feminine sophistication. It blends beautifully with Iralia and Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha, enhancing their violet character. This material really is indispensable and should be included in all perfumer's toolkits.

According to Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine), Dihydro Beta Ionone “has an odor somewhat mild, woody, floral and slightly fruity, possessing great beauty. It is a relatively old product that has only recently found a wider audience when introduced in the creative accord of Issey Miyaki for ladies. Afterwards it was used in many fragrances, among them Dolce Vita and Bulgari for ladies. However it is found in traces in many fragrances because it is an important part of the reconstruction of osmanthus absolute, along with dihydro-beta-ionol, gamma-decalactone and theaspirane. I believe it will be used increasingly in perfumery, with many accords being created with its complex and ambiguous, floral, woody and fruity notes.”

products.name: Dihydro Gamma Ionone
products.description:
Both the finest and most noble member of the family, Dihydro Gamma Ionone is found naturally in tincture of ambergris to which it contributes a refined tobacco quality. This elegant aromachemical is complex, rich and extremely nuanced. Less fruity and earthy than Dihydro Ionone Beta, and more intense and warm than Dihydro Ionone Alpha, this is a first choice material that all perfumers should have in their organ.

Dihydro Ionone Gamma blends exceedingly well with Irisone® Alpha, Isoraldeine® Cetone Alpha, Iralia®, Iraldeine Delta and Dihydroactinidiolide in which it accentuates the delicate tea and tobacco qualities.

We also stock Dihydro Alpha Ionone and Dihydro Beta Ionone.

products.name: Dihydroactinidiolide
products.description: Dihydroactinidiolide (also known as musk coumarin) is a wonderful long-lasting lactone found naturally in black tea, tobacco, fenugreek, and in the scent glands of the red fox. It also functions as a pheremone in red fire ants and certain fruit flies. A very uncommon musk, dihydroactinidiolide is a unique material that enhances and blends with tea chemicals and accords and harmonises wonderfully with tobacco, coumarin and tonka materials. It also has delicate nuances of spices, peach and medjool dates.

products.name: Dihydroambrate
products.description:
Dihydroambrate opens with a warm, rounded woody-amber impression — not sharp, not sweet, just quietly rich. There is a subtle ambrette-like quality in the heart, a gentle seed-musk warmth that makes the material feel organic and skin-close. Dry cedar facets give it structure without making it smell specifically like cedarwood.

Givaudan designed this to do one thing extremely well: add richness and balance. Drop it into a composition and everything gets warmer, fuller, more three-dimensional. It does not impose its own character on your blend — instead it amplifies what is already there, smoothing rough transitions between notes and giving thin compositions genuine body. It works at concentrations up to several percent without becoming intrusive.

Its stability is remarkable. Dihydroambrate survives virtually every functional base — fabric softeners, detergents, soap, shampoo — which made it a staple in consumer products. But its real beauty shows in fine fragrance, where its quiet woody-amber warmth provides the kind of invisible foundation that makes everything above it smell more expensive. Pair it with Ambroxan for a modern amber, or use it under sandalwood materials for added depth and projection.

products.name: Dihydroanethol
products.description:
Dihydroanethole is anethole's softer sibling. The sharp crystalline bite that makes pure anethole so assertive has been smoothed away. What remains is a rounder anise character: warm black liquorice, sweet fennel, a hint of sassafras root. It smells like the memory of anise rather than anise itself.

That softness is the reason to stock it alongside anethole. Where anethole dominates and announces itself, dihydroanethole blends. It slides into oriental bases and fougères without elbowing other materials aside. Use it beneath lavender and coumarin in a fougère for herbaceous sweetness that reads as vintage and complex. In orientals, it provides the same sweet-spicy warmth that absinthe brings to a classic Guerlain structure.

It is also more stable than anethole in certain formulation conditions — less prone to oxidation. If you need anise character in a product with a long shelf life, dihydroanethole is the safer choice. It works well with star anise oil, tarragon, basil, and coumarin.

products.name: Dihydrocarveol
products.description:
Dihydrocarveol opens with intense spearmint coolness that immediately distinguishes itself from menthol's sharp chill. This complex mixture of eight stereoisomers delivers camphoreous depth alongside minty freshness. Sweet-woody warmth emerges as it develops, revealing unexpected spicy facets that whisper of its carvone ancestry.

This material transforms compositions through sophisticated modulation rather than domination. Deploy it in trace amounts to lift heavy florals like tuberose and gardenia without disturbing their narcotic character. In woody complexes, it adds mysterious cooling without the medicinal edge of camphor or the aggressive chill of menthol.

Use it at 0.1-1% to enhance rose and geranium accords with natural spiciness, or pair with ionones for contemporary floral-woody structures. The material's 20-hour substantivity ensures your cooling effects persist through the drydown.

products.name: Dihydrocarvyl Acetate
products.description:
Dihydrocarvyl acetate smells of soft spearmint sweetness with an unexpected rosy, floral twist. It is gentler and more rounded than carvone or raw spearmint oil — the minty edge is there, but it is cushioned by a sweet, almost candy-like softness. Fresh and clean, with a green herbal quality.

Use it to add sweet, herbal freshness to aromatic and fougère compositions without the sharpness of pure mint materials. It bridges mint and floral notes beautifully, softening one and lifting the other. It occurs naturally in spearmint and celery, which gives you a clue to its character — herbal, fresh, and surprisingly versatile.

Pair it with lavender and coumarin for modern fougères, with geranium for a rosy-herbal heart, or with bergamot and linalool for a sweet, fresh opening. It also works well alongside carvone and menthol when you want a complete mint accord with added depth and sweetness.

products.name: Dihydroeugenol
products.description:
While eugenol is reminiscent of clovebud, dihydroeugenol smells more of bay leaves and pimento. Dihydroeugenol is brighter and more radiant than regular eugenol and it works wonderfully in combination with the same.

For a lighter and slightly sweeter but dry spice note than Eugenol, Dihydroeugenol is an excellent choice. This product has a quite restrictive IFRA standard of 0.73%.

products.name: Dihydrolinalool
products.description:
Dihydrolinalool opens with an airy, clean floral sweetness that immediately signals freshness. You'll detect subtle blueberry and green-weedy undertones alongside its primary lily-of-the-valley character. This remarkably stable material bridges citrus top notes to floral hearts with exceptional grace.

In compositions, dihydrolinalool serves as both harmoniser and problem-solver. Its chemical resilience allows fresh floral character to survive harsh detergent bases where natural linalool would degrade. Combine it with dihydromyrcenol and white musks to create the iconic "clean laundry" accord that defines modern fabric care fragrances.

Use dihydrolinalool at 20-30% in white floral hearts for diffusive freshness. Partner it with hedione for transparent jasmine effects or layer with lilial substitutes for amplified muguet. In functional fragrances, deploy it generously—its stability masks base malodours whilst contributing pleasant floralcy that persists through product use.

products.name: Dihydromyrcenol
products.description:
A perfumery critic one said this chemical was "lavender on steroids" and while there is much merit to such an idea, Dihydromyrcenol is so much more. It is such an easy material to blend that it can't simply be pigeonholed into the lavender family.

Dihydromyrcenol in overdose is the classic material for masculine top notes but in small amounts it adds a modern and very inimitable twist to feminine top notes as evidenced in Gabrielle by Chanel and myriad other scents. Dihydromyrcenol is almost as indispensable as a high quality Bergamot FCF and Linalool these days.

A 1:1 ratio with the best Lavender oil you can buy is beautiful and a supremely addictive synergy is created when the same is modified with a touch of Allyl Amyl Glycolate.

Ours is a fine quality from Ventos.

products.name: Dihydromyrcenyl Acetate
products.description:
Dihydromyrcenyl Acetate opens with a juicy bergamot character softened by lavender undertones. Where its parent alcohol Dihydromyrcenol can feel sharp and metallic, the acetate ester reads sweeter, rounder, and more elegant. You get that same citrus-cologne sparkle but wrapped in a velvety fruitiness that feels more refined and versatile.

This material bridges the gap between aggressive top notes and the floral heart of your composition. Its tertiary ester structure gives it remarkable stability in alkaline environments where natural citrus oils and standard esters like Linalyl Acetate rapidly degrade. Reach for it when you need lasting citrus freshness in soaps, detergents, and household products where other citruses fail miserably.

Blend it alongside Dihydromyrcenol to temper the alcohol's harshness while extending its citrus-lavender signature. It pairs beautifully with Linalyl Acetate for synthetic bergamot accords and with Allyl Amyl Glycolate for modern aromatic-fruity effects. Use it in lime fragrances to support and extend fleeting citrus top notes into the heart.

products.name: Dihydrorose Oxide
products.description:
Dihydrorose oxide captures the whole rose experience—not just petals but the green calyx, thorny stems and morning dew. This piercing, vibrating quality cuts through heavy florals with its characteristic metallic sharpness. You'll find it creates that elusive "living rose" quality missing from traditional rose absolutes.

In fine fragrance, combine it with phenylethyl alcohol and citronellol at 0.1-0.5% for photorealistic roses. For exotic fruits, it's your secret weapon—essential for authentic lychee accords and adding the bitter green skin note to mango compositions.

Use dihydrorose oxide to bridge citrus tops with floral hearts, exploiting its grapefruit nuance. Its exceptional diffusion ensures immediate impact whilst the metallic facet provides modern edge. Apply it sparingly in masculine fougères with dihydromyrcenol for that steely urban freshness.

Dihydrorose Oxide vs Rose Oxide

Think of rose oxide as the loud, confident sibling—sharp, penetrating, and impossible to ignore even at trace levels. It announces itself with brilliant green-metallic freshness that can dominate a composition.

Dihydrorose oxide is the gentler version: same family character but softer, rounder, and far more forgiving. Where rose oxide demands careful handling lest it overwhelm everything around it, dihydrorose oxide blends in politely while still contributing that distinctive green-geranium-rose signature.

Use rose oxide when you want a material that punches above its weight; reach for di

products.name: Dihydroterpinyl Acetate
products.description:
Dihydroterpinyl acetate opens with a dry bergamot zest that's less juicy than natural citrus but more persistent. You'll recognise its distinctive camphoraceous-lavender facet that bridges citrus tops to woody hearts. This saturated ester brings the clean, soapy quality that defines modern freshness.

In fragrance construction, this material excels at extending expensive naturals without diluting their character. Blend it with bergamot oil to stretch your citrus budget while maintaining authenticity. It's indispensable in masculine accords where it reinforces both the lavender and bergamot notes characteristic of classic Fougères, creating seamless transitions between volatile tops and heavier bases.

Dihydroterpinyl Acetate vs Terpinyl Acetate

Both materials occupy similar bergamot-lavender-pine territory, but their personalities differ noticeably. Terpinyl acetate is the brighter, more complex sibling—sweeter, more spicy-herbaceous, with prominent bergamot sparkle and lilac-floral facets that make it a convincing bergamot substitute. Dihydroterpinyl acetate is warmer, woodier, and more subdued—the pine and cologne aspects dominate while the floral brightness recedes.

Think of terpinyl acetate as the extrovert that lifts compositions with sparkling freshness, and dihydroterpinyl acetate as the steady workhorse that provides reliable woody-aromatic support without demanding attention. Choose terpinyl acetate for bergamot reconstructions and bright fougères; reach for dihydr

products.name: Dimethyl Anthranilate Natural 50% TEC
products.description:
Also known as Methyl N Methylanthranilate, Dimethyl Anthranilate is a key component of mandarin oil (from which this product is isolated). It has a wonderfully grape-like and dusty quality which makes it very useful for the recreation of fruit and floral notes.

Unlike its counterpart Methyl Anthranilate, this product won't form Schiff bases with aldehydes and is far less likely to cause discolouration. The caveat, however, is that it has a very low maximum IFRA use of 0.1%.

Due to DEA restrictions, we sell this product at 50% diluted in natural Triethyl Citrate, maintaining its 100% natural status.

Odour profile: neroli, grape, powdery, musty, wine, phenolic.

products.name: Dimethyl Benzyl Carbinol
products.description:
Dimethyl benzyl carbinol (DMBC) is a key material in fine fragrance, valued for its rosy character and exceptional diffusion. It bridges accords seamlessly, ensuring structural integrity and enhancing floral compositions throughout the dry-down phase.

DMBC’s versatility makes it essential in modern perfumery. Its warm, inviting profile refines mainstream fragrances, elevating them to luxury status. At optimal dilutions, it blends effortlessly, enhancing compositions with a signature depth and technical precision.

products.name: Dimethyl Benzyl Carbinyl Acetate
products.description:
Dimethyl benzyl carbinyl acetate is known for a floral-fruity profile, often described as rosy with a crisp, green apple or pear-like freshness. It’s brighter and more sparkling than DMBC, with a clean, uplifting quality.

This ester’s versatility makes it essential in high-end fragrance design. Its subtle fruity undertones add signature depth, transforming traditional florals into dynamic compositions. Perfumers use it to bridge olfactory contrasts, creating complexity and unexpected dimensionality in floral accords.

products.name: Dimethyl Benzyl Carbinyl Butyrate
products.description:
Dimethyl benzyl carbinyl butyrate offers a floral-fruity note with a richer, juicier fruitiness—often likened to plum or peach—combined with a creamy, velvety warmth. It’s deeper and softer than DMBCA, with a lush, rounded edge.

This butyrate ester is vital in high-end perfumery, providing a substantive character that bridges fruity top notes and floral hearts. Its exceptional diffusion ensures smooth transitions, allowing perfumers to craft sophisticated, multidimensional fragrance structures.

products.name: Dimethyl Cyclormol
products.description:
Dimethyl Cyclormol opens with a cool diffusive freshness that has immediate impact. Beneath this sits an unmistakable fungal-mushroom character—damp cellar floors, freshly picked button mushrooms, the underside of forest logs after rain. The woody backbone is dry and rather neutral — neither creamy nor pencil-like.

Pair this interesting material with Veramoss to build convincing modern moss accords that boost (or sidestepentirely) IFRA-restricted oakmoss or treemoss. In florals like hyacinth, muguet, or mimosa, a trace adds a realistic "growing in soil" texture. Oriental and leather bases benefit from its camphoraceous cut because of its ability to aerate heavy labdanum and amber resins, preventing cloying sweetness.

products.name: Dimethyl Hydroquinone
products.description:
This material opens with intensely sweet, sharp-green notes reminiscent of crushed hyacinth stems and fresh fennel. Use it in traces to create the classic "foin coupé" (mown hay) accord when combined with coumarin. Its remarkable tenacity despite low molecular weight makes it invaluable for bridging top to base notes.

The powerful herbaceous character transforms floral compositions, particularly white florals where naturalness proves elusive. In hyacinth reconstructions, this material provides the essential sweet-green foundation that defines the flower's character. Tobacco and oriental bases benefit from its warm, nutty facets that add sophisticated aromatic dimension without overwhelming sweetness.

Surprisingly this material is naturally found in violet flowers. Traces can be useful in constructing a complex and true-to-life violet accord.

products.name: Dimethyl Sulfide 1% DPG
products.description:
Dimethyl Sulfide (also known as Dimethyl Sulphide in British English) is an incredibly intense and volatile chemical smelling mainly of creamed corn. Despite the food connotations it is not deemed pleasant to most people owing to the nuances of sulphur it also bears (it should be noted, however, that it should not smell of rotting cabbage — that indicates a low quality or degraded material).

Dimethyl Sulfide is absolutely amazing at adding naturalness to fruit and floral notes, particularly rose, where the merest trace is perceptible. Consequently great care should be taken in the use of this product and we highly recommend diluting it further to 0.1% or even 0.01%.

But the area in which this material truly excels is in recreations of the scent of the seaside. This is because Dimethyl Sulfide is the main chemical involved in the actual scent of the sea as it is released naturally in large amounts by phytoplankton.

Due to the volatility of Dimethyl Sulphide, we recommend storing it in the refrigerator as it has a tendency to evaporate right out of the bottle when left at room temperature.

products.name: Dimetol®
products.description:
Dimetol AKA Freesia Heptanol is used in the same way as dihydromyrcenol but for some reason it has never attracted quite the same superstar level of appeal despite being universally liked. Nevertheless it has still found fairly wide use in gentlemen's scents such as the original Polo Green, Pour Lui by Oscar de la Renta, Van Cleef and Arpels for Men and Paco Rabanne.

This material has a natural brightness reminiscent of lime and lemon zest, making it suitable for modern, fresh, and clean compositions. Its unique character contributes a green sparkle and lively diffusivity to the top and heart notes of a fragrance.

products.name: Dimyrcetol
products.description:
Dimyrcetol is IFF's proprietary blend of dihydromyrcenyl formate and dihydromyrcenol. The formate is the key component, and it gives Dimyrcetol a fresh, citrus-lime character with herbal and marine facets that broaden the profile beyond straightforward citrus. This is a rare material that most perfumers will not have encountered.

Strip life is modest — under three hours — but that number tells only part of the story. On skin and in the air, Dimyrcetol projects powerfully, with a cool, clean diffusion that carries well beyond what the blotter suggests. That projection is its most distinctive quality.

Bergamot and linalool complement the citrus side naturally. Lavender brings out the cologne character. Hedione, Iso E Super, and white musks all support it in modern accords, while ambroxan in the base adds amber warmth.

Dimyrcetol and dihydromyrcenol are distinct materials that are easily confused. Dihydromyrcenol is the well-known metallic-lime freshness found in Davidoff Cool Water and countless masculine fragrances.

Dimyrcetol is this IFF blend — primarily dihydromyrcenyl formate with some dihydromyrcenol — offering a rounder, more herbal-marine profile with greater projection but shorter blotter life.

We also stock Dihydromyrcenyl Acetate.

products.name: Diphenyl Oxide
products.description:
Diphenyl oxide has a geranium-like odour with green, leafy and metallic facets, and nuances of rose and powder. This material provides exceptional diffusion and can dramatically extend the persistence of volatile citrus components. Its geranium-like character transforms conventional rose accords into strikingly modern blends.

Incorporate diphenyl oxide at low concentrations, around 1%, to avoid harshness. Combine with classic florals like lindenol™ (terpineol) and geranyl acetate, or green notes like citral, for balanced blends. Its metallic character brings a modern edge, but requires careful handling in fragrance creation.

products.name: Dipropylene Glycol (DPG)
products.description:
Dipropylene Glycol (DPG) is the most common diluent and solubiliser in perfumery today. It is sometimes used to pad out a formula (bringing its total to 1,000 for uniformity) and it can offer some minor benefits as a fixative, but an intelligent combination of musks is usually a better option for that purpose.

DPG is almost odourless — in general it has a very faint almost alcohol-like odour that some only some people can perceive. Unlike alcohol, however, it is non-flammable having a closed cup flash point of 138°C (280°F). It has a higher viscosity than water.

Some fragrances contain very large amounts of DPG to lower their cost or even their strength as we see in Baccarat Rouge 540 which uses nearly 50% in the finished formula for Eau de Parfum (compared to almost none in the Extrait).

DPG is not readily soluble in fixed oils such as Fractionated Coconut Oil and can cause turbidity. If you are working with fixed oils a better option is ethanol or IPM (MIP).

When DPG passes its expiry (usually after three or four years) it can develop an unpleasant bready-sour note. This can make it unsuitable for some long-term dilution needs. TEC, DEP and IPM are potential alternative options for those cases.

NOTE: This must not be used in food or vape juices. Dipropylene Glycol is not a safe alternative to Propylene Glycol. Do not consume.

products.name: Doremox
products.description:
Doremox opens with bright, potent rose character laced with the lemony sparkle of fresh geranium leaf. A crisp green edge keeps the floral alive and modern. The overall impression sits close to rose oxide but rounder, more polished, and free of metallic hardness.

This Firmenich creation delivers fresh diffusive rose effects even at low concentrations. Use it anywhere you would normally use rose oxide but want a cleaner, more refined result. It combines beautifully with citrus, herbal, and fruity notes for lifted modern florals.

Pair Doremox with linalool and citronellol for naturalistic rose constructions. Try it with blackcurrant bud absolute and lavender for contemporary chypre accords. Its 48-hour tenacity on blotter gives your rose heart real staying power.

products.name: Dorinia SA E
products.description:
Dorinia revolutionised rose bases when Firmenich launched it alongside Damascone Beta in 1975. The prominent apple note from damascones defines this material's character. Deploy this powerhouse at 0.1-2% maximum—its diffusive strength overwhelms inexperienced noses.

This polycyclic musk-free reformulation offers superior skin affinity compared to its predecessor Dorinia SA, making it ideal for premium fine fragrance applications. The material functions as complete rose accord, eliminating need to build complex rose hearts from individual components.

Combine Dorinia SA E with natural rose absolutes where it lifts and brightens extraction-dulled facets. Blends seamlessly with white florals (jasmine, peony, violet) for sophisticated bouquets, or pair with fruity notes (lychee, raspberry, cassis) for modern fruity-florals. Works beautifully in woody-oriental structures as elegant floral counterpoint to sandalwood, amber, and gourmand notes.

Add dimethyl sulfide at 0.001% for authentic rose absolute depth. Incorporate phenyl ethyl phenyl acetate for rosy-honey sweetness that bridges the damascone intensity.

products.name: Douglas Fir Needle Oil
products.description:
If you wanted to distill the scent of Christmas, this precious New Zealand Douglas fir oil (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is just that. Despite being unrelated, It melds together aspects of the very best of the two more well-known perfumery products of Siberian fir needle oil (Abies siberica) and fir balsam absolute (Abies balsamea) but adds a wonderful (and unexpected) sparkling citrus note. Every drop exudes the fresh wild scent of nature. This is a superior oil in every way.

This fir oil is grown and harvested in the pure unspoilt regions of the South Island of New Zealand and uses only young branch tips and needles. It is steam distilled. 

According to Steffan Arctander, Douglas fir needle oil exhibits “a softness and a sweetness, a very rich bodynote and a great odour tenacity which exceptional for a ‘pine needle oil’.”

Blends well with: other conifer oils, oakmoss, citrus oils (particularly grapefruit), labdanum.

Origin: Otago, South Island, New Zealand
Part: Young needles and branches
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Dreamwood™ 184270B
products.description:
From Firmenich: “Dreamwood Base takes its inspiration from the iconic Mysore Sandalwood, also known as the “royal tree” in the Mysore district of Karnataka, India.

Created around Dreamwood, our latest breakthrough captive ingredient from white biotechnology, Dreamwood Base is designed for pure performance. It brings naturality and natural effect, impressive tenacity, warmth and creaminess to any fragrance.

The traditional woody creamy warms of sandalwood is also brought to light by our best sandalwood molecules, some of which captive.”

Boost the otherwise mild Dreamwood with our rich and powerful Sandexol® base. Dreamwood also blends well anywhere Sandalwood is used.

products.name: Driftwood
products.description:
Driftwood is a speciality amber base by V. MANE Fils built around their captive molecule Ambramone®. It has a lovely soft cedar quality with the faintest hint of suede and ambergris. It can be used in overdose (and indeed I would recommend its use that way) when you want an elegant wood note to use in place of the more common Vertofix, Vertenex or Iso E Super. But in small amounts it is a great nuancer with captive character.

There is nothing unpleasant in Driftwood and as a foundational wood it is a great addition to the perfumer's organ.

Blend this with green or fruit notes to emphasise those facets in the base. For richness and beauty, boost it with Miraclewood.

products.name: Dulcinyl
products.description:
You'll recognise this as raspberry preserves spread on warm brioche. The heliotrope character adds powdery depth, while cassie and mimosa undertones bring sophisticated floral complexity. This is sweetness done elegantly, never cloying despite its intensity.

This IFF molecule (also known as heliotropyl acetone) bridges the gap between fruity and floral families with remarkable grace. The 400-hour substantivity on blotter makes it one of the longest-lasting berry materials available, ensuring your raspberry effect persists well into the drydown. Use it in jasmine compositions where its fruity juiciness adds the realistic touch that separates fine florals from generic sweetness.

Work with Dulcinyl at up to 15% of your concentrate, though lower doses often suffice given its medium strength. The recrystallised form handles easily despite being a solid at room temperature. Blend with raspberry ketone, ionones, vanillin, and jasmine absolutes for complex fruity-floral effects.

products.name: Dupical
products.description:
Dupical is an incredibly powerful and transparent muguet aldehyde. It carries the fresh, green, slightly watery character of lily-of-the-valley petals without the heavy indolic side. Underneath the floral top sits a light marine-aldehydic quality that keeps the whole thing airy. But be warned: a trace is very perceptible. This is one of the most overpowering lily chemicals you'll experience.

Use it to reinforce muguet accords where Lilial, Lyral or Florol feel too heavy or too sweet. A small amount gives lift and watery freshness to fresh floral compositions, cologne structures and marine-floral accords. It also pulls back the waxy thickness of hydroxycitronellal.

Pair with Lyral, Florol and hydroxycitronellal to build a lily-of-the-valley heart, or use against citrus and green notes in cologne tops. A trace in aquatic accords reinforces the watery character. Dose it low — overdose flattens subtler materials around it.

Something important to note with Dupical is that it can be perceived as a very dense note — so while it does have a watery odour quality, it benefits from opening up with an ozonic or freshie like floralozone. This is a material that, in traces, can represent your entire muguet note, preventing the need for bulk additions of the classics like florol and hydroxycitronellal.

products.name: Dynamone
products.description:
Dynamone is a natural Biolandes speciality in which labdanum (cistus) resin is transformed by a proprietary process into a refined and unique extract.

In the words of the manufacturer: “In fine perfumery, this mythical extract from the cistus offers mineral and metallic notes allowing the contribution of dark and deep notes. Perfect for the creation of leather bases, in association with amber notes, ideal to bring a very original oriental touch.”

This is a really excellent material to add a kinder and gentler animalic tinge to a perfume when straight up labdanum can be a tad dominating.

Origin: Spain
Part: Resin from leaves and stems
Method: Proprietary extraction

products.name: Dynascone
products.description:
Dynascone hits with astonishing power—this is one of perfumery's most diffusive materials. The green-galbanum character dominates, but a juicy pineapple fruitiness weaves through alongside delicate hyacinth floral notes. It is pungent but, when properly controlled, reminiscent of ripe pineapple with green pepper heat.

Use Dynascone in traces only—even at 10% dilution, it demands respect. Fine fragrance concentrations run 0.04% to 0.1%, while functional products tolerate slightly more. It pairs beautifully with cis-3-hexenol, and galbanum oil. The 348-hour substantivity ensures your green note persists through to drydown.

Dynascone vs Neobutenone Alpha

While sharing the same CAS number, these materials differ meaningfully in character. Dynascone delivers pronounced pineapple fruitiness alongside its galbanum character—juicy, pungent, and somewhat tropical. Neobutenone Alpha represents the purer alpha isomer, which is greener, less fruity, and closer to natural galbanum in character.

Neobutenone Alpha is the "the Paradisone of green materials" and it is vastly superior for achieving authentic green effects. It features in fragrances like Creed Aventus, where traces create that inimitable green-fruity top note. If you want prominent pineapple-galbanum punch, choose Dynascone; if you want cleaner, more naturalistic greenness, Neobutenone Alpha is the better choice.

products.name: Eau de Brouts Absolute
products.description:
"Brouts" is old Provençal for the young shoots and leafy twigs pruned from bitter orange trees. When those cuttings are steam-distilled to make petitgrain oil, the leftover water holds a faint, beautiful fragrance of its own. Extract that water with solvent and you get this — eau de brouts absolute — deep green, smoky, watery, and unlike anything else in the palette.

It smells of freshly torn bitter orange leaves, but airy and subtle in a way that petitgrain oil itself is not. Not to be confused with Orange Flower Water Absolute, which comes from neroli distillation and is floral, indolic, and honeyed. Eau de brouts is purely green and herbaceous. Arctander described it as "musty, dry, faintly floral, more herbaceous" — though his definition blurred the line by including mixed flower and leaf waters, which modern producers keep separate.

Use it to build convincing neroli and bitter orange accords — it fills the gap between bright neroli on top and petitgrain in the heart. It brings naturalness to jasmine, ylang-ylang, and gardenia compositions too. Pair it with bergamot, sandalwood, and olibanum for a green-woody cologne effect. Use sparingly — it is potent and easily dominates.

products.name: Ebanol
products.description:
Ebanol opens with an intense sandalwood-musk fusion that's immediately recognisable for its creamy, almost edible quality. This isn't just woody—it's rich and buttery with a distinctive maple syrup sweetness. The material delivers exceptional depth and volume to woody accords while maintaining remarkable stability across pH ranges.

You'll find Ebanol transforms simple woody structures into complex, multidimensional bases. Its musky character amplifies when combined with macrocyclic musks, creating exponential warmth and diffusion. In floral compositions, particularly jasmine and lily-of-the-valley, it provides the tenacious backbone these delicate notes need. The material excels at rounding sharp edges in fruity accords while contributing its signature creamy texture.

Combine with Javanol for radiant sparkle or layer with Sandalore for fuller dimensionality. Its 400-hour tenacity on blotter makes it indispensable for extending top note longevity—perfect for functional fragrances requiring exceptional substantivity.

products.name: Edenolide
products.description:
Edenolide presents a remarkable top-note musk character, an uncommon and highly prized attribute.  Its excellent diffusion projects powerfully from the outset.  This allows you to weave a complete musk signature throughout the entire fragrance experience.

Edenolide is an enriched form (chiral isomer to be precise) of the discontinued Applelide®. This refinement yields a softer, richer, and more diffusive character. It represents a significant advancement over Applelide's baseline performance.

This material imparts unique effects, beautifying compositions with unparalleled volume and dimension.  Its inherent fruity-apple facet and sensuous warmth create exceptionally comforting, sophisticated scents.

Utilise Edenolide up to 30% for sheer musk qualities from the top.  It effectively supports citrus and floral top notes.  Combine with Iso E Super® or Bergamot FCF for enhanced diffusion and vibrant openings.

Blend Edenolide with other modern musks like Helvetolide® for a diffusion "storm".  Its fruity facet excels in fruity and floral accords needing musky depth.

products.name: Elderflower TruAbs
products.description:
This 100% natural Elderflower base has to be smelled to be believed. While the natural absolute is available, it is somewhat disappointing (even from great vendors like Firmenich). Fraterworks' Elderflower TruAbs® on the other hand is simply sublime.

In the words of our founder Jamie Frater: "Elderflower TruAbs carries me back to my carefree youth in New Zealand and the scent of warm Southern Hemisphere Christmas mornings with all the pleasure and optimism that implied. No singular base moves me quite so emotionally as this one. Elderflower TruAbs is pure bliss."

Elderflower TruAbs® has nuances of honey, new mown hay, fresh country air and orchard fruits. It is so beautifully constructed that you cannot tell it is a crafted blend.

Use this product one for one in place of Elderflower Absolute. From traces this product has impact and will add richesse and elegance to your fragrances.

Like our amazing Hyacinth,  Rose de Mai and Boronia TruAbs' this base is created especially for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from a single plant extract.

Due to the high cost of this replica, we also sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Elderflower TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing.

products.name: Elemi Oil
products.description:
Elemi is a perfumer's secret weapon, possessing a dynamic dual character. It provides an initial peppery-citrus lift while anchoring compositions with resinous depth. This versatility makes it an unparalleled bridge ingredient, connecting disparate olfactory families.

Pair Elemi Extra strategically with bergamot and pink pepper for contemporary masculine openings, or blend with frankincense and cedarwood for sophisticated woody accords. The elemol content provides exceptional tenacity—lasting over 400 hours on blotters—making this material invaluable for anchoring volatile compositions. Deploy lower concentrations as a radiance enhancer, higher percentages to feature its unique lemony-peppery signature.

products.name: Elemi SFE
products.description:
Supercritical CO2 extraction captures what steam distillation cannot — the full aromatic spectrum of fresh elemi resin, including volatile compounds that heat would destroy. The result is cleaner, greener, and more vertical than the conventional oil. You smell the resin as it actually is: bright, peppery, lemony, with a green facet the distilled version lacks.

Where the steam-distilled oil can feel broad and slightly blurred, this SFE reads as focused and precise. The peppery-citrus top is sharper, the balsamic background is smoother, and the whole profile hangs together more naturally. In fine fragrance, that clarity translates to better integration — the elemi character supports without muddying surrounding notes.

Use it wherever you would use elemi oil but want a more refined result. In spicy compositions, the green facet adds a botanical freshness. In citrus-woody accords, the peppery brightness provides lift without the instability problems of the conventional oil. Pair with pink pepper, cardamom, and olibanum for a resinous spice accord with genuine aromatic depth.

products.name: Elemol ex Elemi
products.description:
Elemi is a lovely fresh citrusy resin, and at its heart is pure Elemol. Elemol is to Elemi oil as Olibanol is to Frankincense and Amyrol is to Amyris Oil. Because Elemol is an isolate, it is a more refined form of the oil.

Elemol has lovely nuances of antique wood, roses and citrus. For something akin to the wonderful Versailles candle of Cire Trudon (mimicking the scent of the polished wood floors of the Versailles Palace), Elemol would be a perfect starting point with Virginia Cedar Wood and enhancements from Honey Supreme and Birch Tar Oil.

Elemol is a light fluid making it easy to use and is 100% natural so compliant with the various natural perfumery standards.

products.name: Epice FW
products.description:
In 1926 Hubert and George Fraysse founded Synarome and produced the greatest bases of their time: Animalis and Ambrarome. The following year their brother, André, became in-house perfumer for Lanvin and created the masterpiece Arpège in collaboration with Paul Vacher.

Fraysse and Vacher crafted Arpège around one of Synarome's lesser-known (but in many ways equally influential) bases called Epicea, which remained in production right up to the twenty-first century. Fraterworks Epice FW revives that forgotten masterpiece, rich in nutmeg, pepper and allspice.

While Epice FW has a somewhat ancient pedigree it is beautifully suited to modern fragrances and would make a wonderful starting point for a sophisticated and rich spicy gourmand fragrance.

products.name: Espicene Gamma
products.description:
Gone (until now) but not forgotten, Epicene Gamma from IFF was a classic masterpiece — a veritable panoply of herbs, woods and spices blended perfectly and used in such classics as Guerlain's Vetiver (2000), Opium Pour Homme (1995, formula below) and Equipage by Hermès (1970).

It was an IFF captive and recently discontinued which is regretful as some great fragrances will now be reformulated to accommodate the loss.

In a modern context this base is usable up to 1.2% and lends a wonderful spice vibe to a fragrance without the need to balance individual spice materials. 

This product has been slightly reformulated to remove an EU prohibited aroma chemical. Espicene Gamma contains 8% musk ketone which is unrestricted by IFRA but has a use limit in the EU of 1.4%.

Afterword: this base should not be confused with Epice FW which was a classic Synarome base Epicea used in Arpege.

products.name: Ethyl 2-Methyl Butyrate
products.description:
This material opens with immediate green tartness that perfectly captures biting into a crisp apple. Its sharp, ethereal quality provides tremendous volatility and lift. You'll find it transforms flat fruit accords into vibrant, mouth-watering compositions.

Use it strategically as a brightness catalyst in your fruity-florals, where its apple-pineapple character bridges fresh openings into heart compositions. Combine it with gamma-undecalactone to add juicy bite to creamy peach notes, creating realistic fruit skin effects. Blend with cis-3-hexenol for photorealistic green apple accords that sparkle.

products.name: Ethyl Acetate
products.description:
Ethyl Acetate is a highly volatile top note with distinct ethereal liquor nuances (particularly brandy and rum). It is used to round out the rough edges of sharp top notes but also to give dazzle to the opening of a scent. Arctander says it is used to give an aged quality to perfumes which might be useful in this modern age of little to no aging of fragrance compounds.

Do not inhale. Caution should be exercised when working with this material. See the attached safety data sheet for more information.

Due to the very volatile nature of this product we also sell it at 10% dilution in DPG.

products.name: Ethyl Acetoacetate
products.description:
Ethyl acetoacetate greets you with a gentle wave of crisp green apple and soft ethereal sweetness. Unlike harsher fruity esters, this material possesses an approachable, almost creamy quality. The rum-like winey undertones emerge as you work with it, adding unexpected complexity.

This ester excels at creating convincing green apple top notes without the aggressive punch of similar materials. You can push the dosage higher than most fruity esters before it becomes artificial. Pair it with florals to add volatility and lift, or layer into kiwi and strawberry accords for naturalistic depth.

Try blending with citrus oils to enhance fresh, sparkling effects. The aged brandy facet works beautifully in masculine fougères and chypres needing sophisticated fruit. Watch for potential reactions with aldehydes over time—fresh batches perform best.

products.name: Ethyl Benzoate
products.description:
In contrast to its close relative methyl benzoate, ethyl benzoate is softer, sweeter, and slightly fruity-floral, with nuances of jasmine and gardenia, lending itself to fixative roles in floral and fruity perfumes. Due to its higher volatility, methyl benzoate (with its sharp, fruity-solvent-like scent with strong floral facets reminiscent of tuberose and ylang-ylang) is more commonly used in top notes, whereas ethyl benzoate, with its longer-lasting presence, supports mid-to-base note stability.

Ethyl benzoate delivers intense fruity sweetness at remarkably low thresholds. This material anchors berry accords while giving lift to floral compositions.

Use strategically to prevent overwhelming sweetness while contributing a fruit character.

products.name: Ethyl Benzoyl Acetate
products.description:
Ethyl benzoyl acetate is unusual because we are used to seeing the benzyl substituents in perfumery aroma chemicals and not the benzoys. Ethyl benzoyl acetate is a fascinating material with distinct nuances of fruit (especially maraschino cherry), hawthorn, cumin, and almond.

The complex scent of Ethyl Benzoyl Acetate is excellent for adding a cherry pit note and it blends wonderfully with our Wild Cherry base, dimethyl anthranilate. Interesting effects result when combining with the very powerful Yara Yara and Filbertone.

This material somehow manages to conjure up an achingly beautiful montage of summer flowers, wild honey and countryside air.

Also known as benzoyl acetic acid ethyl ester.

products.name: Ethyl Butyrate
products.description:
Ethyl butyrate is the intensely sweet scent of overripe bananas and pineapple. Absolutely essential for any fruit accords, this material is also an excellent top note when you are looking for something a little more interesting that the standard allyl amyl glycolate sparkle.

The butyrate differs from the acetate in having a slightly sour butter quality which is particularly naturalising and indispensable in a complex gourmand.

products.name: Ethyl Caproate
products.description:
Ethyl Caproate is an immediate burst of juicy pineapple — bright, sweet, and unmistakably tropical. Ripe banana and soft strawberry fill out the picture. A clean waxy quality stops it from tipping into cloying territory, keeping the fruit transparent and natural.

Use Ethyl Caproate to bring tropical sparkle to your top notes. It lifts exotic florals — think frangipani or ylang — with a fruity brightness that feels effortless. Compared to allyl caproate or isoamyl butyrate, it reads cleaner and less syrupy, making it ideal for fine fragrance work.

Balance Ethyl Caproate against green notes like cis-3-hexenol to keep the sweetness grounded. A trace amount adds a pineapple-strawberry glow to gourmand accords without dominating. Push it harder in tropical compositions where you want that sun-drenched fruit cocktail effect right from the opening.

A note on naming

Ethyl Caproate is the traditional perfumery name; modern chemistry calls it ethyl hexanoate. "Caproate" derives from caproic acid (now hexanoic acid), itself named from the Latin *caper* (goat) for the free acid's distinctly goaty smell. You may see either name on supplier catalogues — they are the same material.
