products.name: Ethyl Decanoate
products.description:
Ethyl decanoate brings a waxy, oily dimension to fruit notes that cleaner materials cannot provide. The cognac and grape-skin character is prominent — mature, vinous, and warm rather than bright or candy-sweet. Think ripe grapes and aged brandy rather than fresh fruit salad.

That waxy quality is what sets it apart. Most fruity materials deliver clean, transparent fruit; ethyl decanoate contributes body, texture, and a grown-up richness. Its 44-hour blotter life places it in the heart-to-base transition zone — longer-lasting than fleeting fruity top notes, useful for anchoring fruit accords that would otherwise fade too quickly.

Other wine-like materials (ethyl octanoate, ethyl hexanoate) reinforce the boozy direction. Damascenone and gamma-decalactone add fruity complexity. In floral compositions, a trace contributes an unctuous warmth reminiscent of the waxy notes found in natural absolutes.

In GCMS analyses of classical French fragrances, traces of this material may indicate the use of brandy spirits as the carrier, rather than standard alcohol.

products.name: Ethyl Formate
products.description:
Ethyl formate hits you with an immediate ethereal flash—rum, ripe raspberry, and fermented fruit all at once. A winey, cognac-like warmth sits behind the sparkle, with faint green and rosy undertones emerging on close inspection. It smells like opening a bottle of aged rum in a fruit market.

This is the smallest and most volatile of the ethyl esters, and that extreme lightness is its superpower. Use it at trace levels to give gourmand compositions a convincing boozy-fruity effervescence—rum accords, brandy notes, and fermented fruit reconstructions all come alive with a tiny addition. It lifts baked-fruit and dried-fruit bases with an ethereal top that reads as genuinely alcoholic.

Pair it with heavier fruit esters and lactones that carry the fruity-boozy impression into the heart once this fleeting top note has done its work.

products.name: Ethyl Furaneol
products.description:
At full strength, Ethyl Furaneol presents a dense, almost overwhelming caramel-butterscotch character with distinct savoury-roasted facets. Dilute it to one percent and discover its true nature: an exquisite jammy berry sweetness with wine-like elegance and burnt sugar depth. The odour detection threshold sits at an astonishing 20 parts per billion.

This material outperforms its relative Furaneol (Strawberry Furanone) on two critical fronts: potency and stability. Where standard Furaneol can degrade into unpleasant fenugreek-curry off-notes, Ethyl Furaneol maintains its clean caramel-berry profile throughout your product's shelf life. Pair it with vanillin for creamy richness, ethyl maltol for cotton-candy lift, or gamma-undecalactone for peaches-and-cream indulgence.

Use trace amounts below 0.05% to round florals with honeyed warmth or add ripeness to citrus without overt sweetness. Increase to 0.25% for dedicated gourmand compositions where you need that sticky, cooked-fruit syrupiness. Combine with pyrazines for biscuit-toasted effects or lactones for fruit-tart opulence.

products.name: Ethyl Heptanoate
products.description:
Ethyl heptanoate smells unmistakably of cognac. The aroma is richly fruity, vinous, and warmly boozy — fermented rather than fresh — with pineapple, apple, and berry notes. This is the molecule you want when a composition needs to smell like it has been aged in oak.

Use it to build convincing cognac, wine, and brandy accords in your fruity and gourmand compositions. It bridges fresh citrus top notes and richer heart materials with its fermented-fruit character. A trace in oriental compositions adds an unexpected warmth that reads as luxurious and aged.

Pair with other fruity esters for complex fruit effects. Try it alongside vanillin and lactones for boozy gourmand depth. Blend with oakmoss and labdanum for a sophisticated cognac-chypre accord that smells genuinely expensive.

Poucher recommends adding a touch to ethanol to mimic the olden days ethanol used in French perfumer's alcohol.

products.name: Ethyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
This material opens with immediate ethereal sweetness that floods your senses with bright, diffusive fruitiness. Its extraordinary power means even trace amounts create significant olfactory impact—the odour threshold reaches as low as 0.01 parts per billion. The rum-like alcoholic facets add sophisticated complexity beyond simple fruit candy sweetness.

You deploy this workhorse for creating vibrant fruit accords where it serves as a cornerstone for pineapple and strawberry compositions. Blend with ethyl maltol for the famous pineapple synergy through configural perception—your brain processes their combination as fresh pineapple rather than separate strawberry-plus-caramel notes. Use dilutions of 10% or less to maintain precise control over its overwhelming strength.

Remember its four-hour tenacity positions it perfectly as a fleeting top note that creates brilliant openings before gracefully fading. The low flash point demands careful storage away from ignition sources. This material enjoys complete freedom from IFRA restrictions, giving you maximum creative latitude across all product categories from fine fragrance to functional applications.

products.name: Ethyl Laurate
products.description:
Ethyl laurate is a quiet, understated material — a gentle waxy sweetness with a creamy floral quality and soft, soapy undertones. This is the kind of background waxiness you find in the depth of natural rose and jasmine absolutes. On its own it barely whispers, but in a blend it adds body and naturalness.

Use ethyl laurate to bring waxy, petal-like authenticity to your floral reconstructions. It fills the gap between clean synthetic florals and the rich fatty depth of natural absolutes. Its extraordinary tenacity means it quietly anchors your floral heart long after lighter materials have faded.

Blend with rose materials, hedione, and hydroxycitronellal for realistic white floral accords. Try it alongside benzyl acetate and linalyl acetate to add naturalistic body. It works as an invisible fixative, extending your florals without drawing attention to itself.

products.name: Ethyl Levulinate
products.description:
Ethyl Levulinate is a versatile and richly faceted material with a fresh, sweet odour marked by fruity and green nuances. It contributes juiciness and depth across a wide range of fragrance types—especially in fruity, floral, and gourmand compositions. The olfactory profile includes recognisable notes of apple, pineapple, rhubarb, and mixed berries, supported by ethereal and lightly floral aspects.

It’s particularly effective at rounding out top and mid notes, lending a naturalistic, mouth-watering character without overpowering the blend. It also adds subtle lift to floral accords, notably rose, and brings body to sweet or rum-like structures in gourmand creations.

products.name: Ethyl Linalool
products.description:
Linalool is found in thousands of naturals, including most citrus oils, so it is ubiquitous in scents where it adds fresh top notes. But when you want that lovely scent to dry into the heart of a perfume or need something a little less agrestic, Ethyl Linalool comes to the fore.  And better still, ethyl linalool is not an EU allergen and so doesn't need to be declared on the outer packaging of a perfume.

Our supplier, Firmenich, is the premium supplier of ethyl linalool, with its process resulting in a smoother, softer and more floral product than others.

According to Arctander, “This alcohol has been suggested for use in perfume compositions as a modifier for LinaIool with certain advantages over that material. Ethyl Iinalool has a somewhat slower rate of evaporation and is easier to work with, needs only normal fixation, and blends with more materials. It introduces softer, more floral-woody, less citrusy notes, according to the composition in which it is used. Along with Ethyl Iinalyl acetate, it forms a pleasant Bergamot-type background note even in soap perfumes, a combination which is more stable than Bergamot oil itself. The alcohol is also an interesting item in Muguet, Lilac, Lily, Appleblossom, etc. as well as in fantasy creations.”

products.name: Ethyl Linalyl Acetate
products.description:
Ethyl Linalyl Acetate opens with brilliant bergamot brightness softened by fresh pear and tropical fruit nuances. Its floral character emerges smoother and rounder than linalyl acetate, with less herbaceous lavender and more refined petitgrain elegance. The material displays impressive substantivity, maintaining its character for over sixteen hours on a blotter.

You'll find this ester transforms compositions where linalyl acetate previously served. Use it at concentrations up to 40% to enhance the bergamot effect in citrus colognes or to add refreshing elegance to floral bouquets. Its greater stability and richer odour make it particularly valuable in formulations requiring longevity. Pair it with ambroxan, iso-amyl salicylate, cardamom, cypress, geraniol, and patchouli to build sophisticated accords. It also complements cistus, frankincense, juniper berry, galbanum, and black pepper beautifully.

Consider this material when you need the fresh bergamot-floral character of linalyl acetate but require better tenacity and a softer, more refined profile. It blends with virtually unlimited application across conventional perfume and soap perfumery materials. Work with it as you would linalyl acetate, but expect enhanced performance and a more sophisticated character that elevates both citrus and floral compositions.

products.name: Ethyl Maltol
products.description:
Ethyl Maltol was thrust in to the public consciousness with the launch of Thierry Mugler's Angel (1992) by Olivier Cresp and Yves de Chirin with what would now be considered a rather tame dose of 0.5%.

Now more commonly found in quantities up to and beyond that of Baccarat Rouge 540's generous 2%, this is absolutely a must-have material for modern perfumers.

Pair's beautifully with our Signature Vanillin and Sotolone.

products.name: Ethyl Myristate
products.description:
This is a material you smell through rather than at. A faint waxy sweetness, violet-tinged and gently soapy, with just enough fruity warmth to distinguish it from plain wax. The odour sits right at the threshold of perception — quiet, smooth, and lipid-rich.

That near-silence is the point. Add ethyl myristate to violet and iris accords and the ionones suddenly smell rounder, more expensive, more like actual flower petals. It provides the fatty backbone that separates a flat violet note from one with three-dimensional depth. Think of it as the waxy residue left on your fingers after handling real orris butter.

Try it at trace levels alongside alpha-isomethyl ionone and methylionones for convincing violet-iris constructions. It brings soapy body to tuberose and mimosa bases without introducing any unwanted heaviness. Found naturally in osmanthus, grape, tea, and hawthorn, ethyl myristate earns its place as a quiet workhorse — the material nobody notices until you take it out.

Ethyl vs Methyl Myristate

Don't confuse these — they smell different. Methyl myristate (CAS 124-10-7) leans into orris butter territory: faintly honeyed, waxy-floral, the backbone of iris accords. Ethyl myristate is soapier, more violet, with a creamy-fruity edge the methyl ester lacks. Choose methyl for orris. Choose ethyl for violet and powdery-floral work.

products.name: Ethyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
Ethyl phenyl acetate opens with gorgeous honey sweetness—rich, floral, and unmistakably natural in character. Rose facets emerge immediately, soft and rounded rather than sharp. The cocoa-balsamic undertone adds unexpected depth, while a gentle waxy quality provides the animalic warmth that makes this material so valuable in fine perfumery.

Ethyl phenyl acetate occurs naturally in honey, wine, and various fruits, which explains its remarkably authentic character. It serves as a vital ingredient across all styles of honey accords, blending beautifully with bright floral notes while working equally well with heavier clover effects. The 312-hour substantivity ensures your honey note persists through to drydown—exceptional performance for such a sweet, approachable material.

Use ethyl phenyl acetate in rose compositions where honey facets add naturalism—it tames high levels of citronellol and geraniol while contributing warmth. It excels in muguet, orange blossom, and oriental bases. Blend with phenethyl alcohol, benzyl acetate, ionones, and vanillin for complex floral-gourmand effects.

Ethyl vs Methyl Phenyl Acetate

Both chemicals share the sweet honey-floral character, but their personalities differ meaningfully. Ethyl phenyl acetate is softer, rounder, and more versatile—the gentler choice with the widest range of applications. Methyl phenyl acetate is more powerful and penetrating with a distinctly harsher edge, though it offers stronger diffusion at lower cost.

For deli

products.name: Ethyl Safranate
products.description:
Ethyl Safranate is a powerful and diffusive fruity rose aroma chemical this is not exploited anywhere near as much as it should be. Where the rose ketones end, Ethyl Safranate begins. With no restriction at all from IFRA and a scent profile like a more characterful damascone delta meets damascone alpha, this material deserves to be front and centre in more contemporary fragrances.

Blends with Persicol are sublime and exploit its fruity side. Its bashful minty side can be extended and enhanced with touches of Peppermint Oil “Black Mitcham”, or use it to add a sultry Saffron note to a damascone rich rose base. In vanillin base amber accords it can lend a wonderful gloss when dosed correctly.

Ethyl Safranate is indispensable and shockingly addictive.

products.name: Ethyl Salicylate
products.description:
Less well known that its cousin Methyl Salicylate, Ethyl Salicylate is clearly related but softer and more rounded and most definitely easier to dose. Both chemicals have an obviously wintergreen connotation but it is definitely sweeter in this ethyl ester.

Ethyl Salicylate is heavy, floral and fruity and is a wonderful blender and booster of Ylang-ylang (whether it be synthetic or natural) and great with Cassie and Mimosa as we see in the lovely original Zen (1964) fragrance from Shiseido (Demo formula below).

products.name: Ethyl Tiglate
products.description:
This remarkable ester opens with an immediately recognisable tutti frutti burst that captivates from the first encounter. The sweet, juicy character mirrors the authentic complexity found in ripe strawberries and fresh apples. Its unique dual personality sets it apart from conventional fruity esters that often smell synthetic.

The magic unfolds in its heart where warm caramel notes emerge, creating a cooked-fruit effect that transforms simple compositions into sophisticated gourmand accords. This facet makes it invaluable for baked apple creations, strawberry tart effects, and tropical fruit blends where depth matters. Your formulations gain the naturalistic complexity that distinguishes professional work from amateur attempts.

Its most distinctive feature appears in the drydown—an earthy, green olive note that prevents the sweetness from becoming cloying. This unusual characteristic allows you to build fruit accords with remarkable realism. Use it to bridge the gap between bright top notes and substantial heart materials in both functional and fine fragrance applications.

products.name: Ethyl Undecylenate
products.description:
Ethyl Undecylenate opens with waxy fruitiness — clean, soapy, and unexpectedly smooth. A creamy sweetness fills out the body. Warm cognac-like undertones sit beneath, lending unexpected depth and boozy richness to what first reads as a straightforward fruity ester.

This is your secret weapon for gourmand accords — the cognac-wine character brings authenticity to rum, brandy, and dried fruit compositions. It also lifts creamy-soapy florals with its clean waxy facet. Blend with ethyl maltol and vanillin for rich boozy warmth, or with aldehydes for sophisticated soapiness.

Use Ethyl Undecylenate at moderate levels — its fatty character dominates if overdosed. The waxy warmth is remarkable in amber and oriental bases. Its 20-hour tenacity on blotter gives lasting body to fruity and boozy accords that would otherwise fade too quickly.

products.name: Ethyl Vanillin
products.description:
Ethyl vanillin is the Superman of the classic vanilla aroma chemicals. It has been in use in fragrances for many decades and forms part of the wonderfully sweet core of Tabu by Jean Carles and Coco from Chanel.

Traces add sweetness while overdose adds a rich vanilla note. Ethyl vanillin is about four times stronger than regular vanillin but it has a slightly more transparent effect, being less inclined to bulk up or thicken a scent. For that reason a truly creamy vanilla is better achieved by combing both vanillin and ethyl vanillin in a proportion that suits you.

Enticing and novel blends can be had by combining Ethyl Vanillin with Heliotropin, Sandalore®, Florex®, Filbertone or Sotolone, and of course Vanillin: natural or signature synthetic. For that little touch of something magical, top it off with our rich Vanellia™ base and Vanilla Pod Tincture.

products.name: Ethylene Brassylate
products.description:
Ethylene Brassylate (a macrocyclic lactone) is one of the oldest white musks, being created by Dupont in 1934 when its potential was immediately noticed by Andre Fraysse who gave it its debut in fine fragrance by incorporating it into the musk fond of his masterpiece Arpège for Lanvin (launched seven years earlier) at just the time the company was exploding to industrial proportions.

Ethylene Brassylate became extremely popular due to its ease of use (being a liquid) and the fact that it was considerably cheaper than the other non-nitro musks of the early 20th century, for example Muscone and Civetone (Ruzicka, 1926) and Exaltolide® (1930).

This musk is very versatile and can be used in almost any fragrance, but it lends itself particularly well to scents needing a soft vanillic note in the dry down. It also has nuances of ambrette seed, fruit and a light powderiness. This is definitely a must-have musk.

products.name: Eucalyptol
products.description:
This bright, camphoraceous opening hits you with immediate clarity - like breathing mountain air after rain. The initial medicinal sharpness quickly reveals a sweet, almost woody depth that creates remarkable spatial dimension in compositions. Its crystalline transparency makes it invaluable for adding vertical lift without masking delicate heart notes.

Transform your citrus accords with eucalyptol's extraordinary diffusive power - it propels hesperidic notes skyward while maintaining their natural character. In white florals, particularly tuberose reconstructions, trace amounts create that crucial medicinal contrast against creamy lactones. Modern masculine fragrances exploit its ability to bridge fresh top notes with aromatic fougère hearts, creating that coveted "just-showered" effect.

Eucalyptol excels at creating temperature contrasts - pair it with warm spices like cardamom to achieve "cold spice" effects. Use it to ventilate heavy oriental bases or add breathing room to dense woody accords. Its extreme stability in alkaline and oxidative conditions makes it indispensable for functional fragrances where other materials fail.

products.name: Eucalyptus By-Absolute
products.description:
This material opens with a warm, softly green character that completely reframes what eucalyptus can smell like. The sharp medicinal brightness of the essential oil is gone, replaced by something richer, more textured, and far more complex. What you smell is balsamic, slightly waxy, and herbaceous, with a woody-spiced undercurrent that builds rather than fades.

That depth makes it a natural architect's material: use it to introduce a naturalistic eucalyptus signature without the clinical edge that the oil brings. In fougères and aromatic compositions, it sits beautifully in the heart without overwhelming the structure. Try it alongside lavender, clary sage, or labdanum to amplify its balsamic green facets - it strengthens the accord without demanding the spotlight.

Where it surprises is in fine fragrance. Pair it with patchouli or cedarwood and the by-absolute's resinous, almost leathery warmth comes forward. It also works as a sophisticated counterpoint to bright citrus or ozonic top notes, grounding the freshness with something altogether more earthy and substantial. This is a material that rewards experimentation.

products.name: Eucalyptus Oil, Citriodora
products.description:
Eucalyptus citriodora delivers a striking opening punch that smells like fresh-crushed citronella leaves dipped in rose petals. The citronellal-dominant profile gives way rapidly to citronellol's soft floralcy, revealing a dewy rose heart. The drydown settles into a sweet, almost balsamic finish without the camphoraceous medicinal notes typical of other eucalyptus species.

This oil serves two distinct purposes in your perfumer's organ. First, it provides unparalleled naturalistic lift to synthetic rose accords. Second, it anchors fleeting citrus top notes, extending lemon perception well into the heart.

Blend citriodora with terpinyl acetate to soften its aldehydic bite into sophisticated cologne territory. Pair it with rhodinol ex geranium or geraniol ex palmarosa to reinforce the rosy facets, or use cedarwood and vetiver to exploit its balsamic undertones.

products.name: Eucalyptus Oil, Globulus
products.description:
Classic Eucalyptus globulus oil opens with a blast of icy, camphoraceous freshness that physically cools the nasal passages. The medicinal sharpness quickly reveals herbal-green facets reminiscent of crushed leaves and pine forest after rain. As it develops, subtle woody-sweet undertones emerge before the characteristic clean dryout.

This oil excels at adding verticality to heavy compositions—a trace amount lifts dense orientals, ambers, and white florals without announcing its presence. In fougère accords, it reinforces the camphoraceous aspect of lavandin and sharpens the overall freshness. Pair it with cardamom for a sophisticated spicy-cool vibration, or blend with cedarwood to create freshly-cut forest effects.

Use eucalyptus judiciously—its power lies in small doses where it acts as an invisible structural element. Combine with calone for enhanced marine accords, or with incense for that steamy hammam contrast. Rectified grades offer linear cleanliness for functional work, while crude oils provide textural complexity and better fixation for fine fragrance applications.

products.name: Eugenol
products.description:
Eugenol has the most entrancing and familiar scent of clovebuds, bringing to mind delicious roasted meats, spiced cakes and puddings at Christmas and, perhaps less pleasingly, dental visits!

The earliest production of Eugenol for the fragrance industry was exclusively as an extract from cloves. In those earliest times, different fragrance houses had different qualities of eugenol and great care went in to selecting the finest. Today with limits on the oil in finished fragrances, the material tends to be neglected and most perfumers purchase on price alone.

At Fraterworks we have a passion for beauty, especially as it was seen in the history of our art. And so we have carefully analysed the natural clove extracted Eugenol offerings from numerous companies to offer this beautiful product, as precious as the essential oils from which it is taken.

Historically Eugenol was kept in iron drums which would turn the oil deep red. Today we use stainless steel and our oil is a pale straw colour.

products.name: Exaltenone
Exaltolide®
products.description:
Exaltolide is such a wonderful and versatile musk it has been in steady use since its discovery in 1930 first as a secret component of many great bases, but then directly in fragrances such as Jean Carles' masterpieces Tabu (1932) and Miss Dior (1947) — at around 0.35% with 3.5% each of Musk Ketone and Musk Ambrette. 

Exaltolide is most often found in doses below 1% but it can be effective at up to 8% and beyond as seen in Jasmin Noir (2008) by Carlos Benaim for Bulgari and Champs Elysées (1996) by Jean-Paul Guerlain and Olivier Cresp for Guerlain.

Our Exaltolide is produced by its inventor Firmenich and is the finest quality on the market. They say that Exaltolide “adds depth and roundness to a wide variety of creations. It offers synergy on the bouquet of a fragrance. It has an especially sensual effect on skin.”

Odour: powdery, soft, animal (deer), tobacco, natural.

products.name: Exaltolide® Total
products.description:
Exaltolide Total is the lower cost (due to lower purity) form of this great musk from the early 20th century. Exaltolide Total can be used one for one in place of the more expensive version with virtually the same effect. The remaining text below describes both the total and high-purity versions.

Exaltolide (and Exaltolide Total) is such a wonderful and versatile musk it has been in steady use since its discovery in 1930 first as a secret component of many great bases, but then directly in fragrances such as Jean Carles' masterpieces Tabu (1932) and Miss Dior (1947) — at around 0.35% with 3.5% each of Musk Ketone and Musk Ambrette. 

Exaltolide and Exaltolide Total are most often found in doses below 1% but can be effective at up to 8% and beyond as seen in Jasmin Noir (2008) by Carlos Benaim for Bulgari and Champs Elysées (1996) by Jean-Paul Guerlain and Olivier Cresp for Guerlain.

Our Exaltolide Total is produced by its inventor Firmenich. They say that Exaltolide “adds depth and roundness to a wide variety of creations. It offers synergy on the bouquet of a fragrance. It has an especially sensual effect on skin. This [TOTAL] quality of EXALTOLIDE® is an extremely fine and elegant musk but more cost effective.”

Odour: powdery, soft, animal (deer), tobacco, natural.

products.name: Exaltone® Crystals
Farnesene Alpha
products.description:
Farnesene is indispensable in the reconstruction of essential oils. It has yet to be exploited in a big way in a fine fragrance but with soft celery note and a fresh almost myrrh-like quality that blends very well with clary sage, lavender and citrus, it should not be ignored.

Farnesene blends extremely well with Myrrh and Opoponax Resinoids, Farnesol, Ocimene, Cis Jasmone and other lactonic materials like Jasmolactone and Cis Jasmone Lactone.

products.name: Farnesol
products.description:
Farnesol greets you with a whisper rather than a shout—this is one of perfumery's most delicate materials. The fresh green-floral character evokes linden trees in bloom and dewy lily of the valley. Interestingly, the scent actually intensifies as it evaporates, revealing hidden depths over time.

This material occurs naturally in over thirty essential oils, from ylang-ylang to tuberose, palmarosa to neroli. Its exceptional 400-hour substantivity makes it invaluable as a fixative, extending the life of fleeting floral notes. You'll find farnesol indispensable in muguet reconstructions, where it adds fruity nuances while anchoring the accord.

Use farnesol as a blender across virtually any floral composition—lilac, peony, rose, jasmine all benefit from its gentle touch. The material also possesses genuine deodorising properties, making it functional as well as beautiful. Start at lower concentrations and build; its subtlety rewards patience.

products.name: Fauxmoss®
products.description:
Oakmoss is now restricted to 0.1% of a finished product and only if the natural material is stripped of certain chemicals. This has resulted in the destruction of more fragrances than any other single product restriction or ban. That's where Fauxmoss® comes in.

Fauxmoss® is a rich blend of naturals and synthetics that mimic the properties of genuine oakmoss, right down to its intensely green colour (the finest quality of Oakmoss is dark green rather than the more common brown seen today). Use it as a one for one replacer for a 50% dilution of Oakmoss absolute.

And best of all, Fauxmoss® can be used with absolutely no restrictions! It is IFRA compliant to 100% of your finished fragrance.

products.name: Fenchol
products.description:
Fenchol (chemically related to terpineol but closer in scent to borneol) opens dry and woody, with a cool camphor edge that stays soft rather than sharp. Think aged wood and forest floor more than fresh pine, with a faint minty coolness and quiet sweet-herbal and lemon nuances underneath.

A small amount lends dry, woody-earthy depth and a clean camphor lift to woody, herbal and pine compositions, sharpening them without shouting. It also props up citrus and lime bases, giving them backbone and a touch of power.

Use it in traces. It is a seasoning, not a star. A touch dries out a sweet floral and stops it cloying, or lends a rosemary-and-pine freshness to a fougère. In a lime cologne it adds a rooty, woody anchor.

products.name: Fenchone Alpha
products.description:
Alpha Fenchone is found in many essential oils, particularly fennel, cedarleaf, and some lavenders. To understand its wonderfully fresh scent we can imagine a blend of Cashmeran and Geosmin with their earthy notes, blended with herbs, lavender and camphor. Fenchone is a wonderful chemical that can contribute wonderfully to freshen and naturalise a blend. It should certainly enjoy a far greater popularity than it currently has.

We can predict a future fragrance of great beauty that will capitalise on its complex top notes in combination with Dihydromyrcenol or Coranol.

Blends well with Geosmin, Dihydro Ionone Beta, Cashmeran, Suralette™ Extra, Ethyl Safranate and Pettigrain Oils.

products.name: Fennel Seed Oil
products.description:
Use Sweet Fennel at 0.06-4.4% for gentle anisic warmth in floral accords and gourmand compositions. The powdery, vintage effect works particularly well with rose and white florals. Bitter Fennel functions as a sharp aromatic top note that cuts through overly sweet compositions whilst providing the signature lift in classic fougère structures.

Sweet Fennel integrates smoothly into oriental and floral bases where you need herbaceous sweetness without harshness. Fennel oil delivers the essential masculine edge in aromatic compositions, bridging lavender top notes with coumarin bases through its unique anisic-camphoraceous character. This oil functions primarily as top to middle notes with excellent tenacity.

Fennel seeds have a similar appearance to caraway and cumin seeds; the main differentiator is that fennel seeds are distinctly green in colour.

Synergies: Lavender, Geranium, Rose, Sandalwood, Bergamot, Basil, Clary Sage, Coumarin, Oakmoss.

products.name: Fenugreek “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
This absolute opens with an almost overwhelming savoury intensity that can shock the uninitiated—pure celery seed, lovage, and curry spice. When you first smell this material neat, you encounter what seems like concentrated vegetable stock. This raw potency contains the secret to its brilliance.

Diluted properly, fenugreek reveals its true character as nature's maple syrup concentrate. The savoury notes recede to unveil deep caramel, burnt sugar, and toasted nuts—gourmand notes that vanilla simply cannot replicate. You'll find this transformation creates sophisticated sweetness in tobacco accords, adds unexpected warmth to woody bases, and introduces authentic nutty facets to amber compositions.

Use fenugreek when you need to transcend ordinary gourmand territories. Its coumarinic hay-like facets bridge perfectly into fougère structures, whilst its tenacious maple character anchors gourmand florals. This material demands respect—work from extreme dilutions and build slowly.

This comes pre-diluted to 90% in IPM by LMR so it is not suitable for all natural perfumers.

products.name: Feuille de Cassis
products.description:
Feuille de Cassis is our blackcurrant leaf base, built around an overdose of green naturals to give a vivid leafy effect rather than a bud note. In perfumery it reads as crushed blackcurrant leaves, tart green sap, stems, and sharp botanical freshness. The effect is bright, penetrating, and naturalistic, with more of the living plant than the fruit. It is useful wherever a perfume needs real greenness, lift, and that unmistakable cassis-leaf snap without moving into the darker, more animalic territory of the buds.

This base completely transforms run-of-the-mill top notes, adding verdant grace, naturalness and radiance. I guarantee it will become part of your regular use green materials.

Pairs perfectly with Cassis Base 345 B to which it adds volume and bloom, and blackcurrant bud absolute, both 37% Molecular Distilled and fine Burgundian absolute.

products.name: Fig Signature
products.description:
Fig Signature is a masterful interpretation of the lush, sun-drenched aroma of fresh figs, capturing both their creamy sweetness and green, slightly woody undertones.

Unlike many fig bases that lean too milky or artificial, this one strikes the perfect balance—ripe, pulpy fruit wrapped in crisp fig leaf and a touch of coconut lactone for that unmistakable Mediterranean warmth.

Whether used to lend natural richness to a fragrance or to add a novel green facet to florals and woods, Fig Signature is an indispensable tool for the perfumer seeking authenticity with effortless blending.

products.name: Filbertone
products.description:
Wonderful for gourmand or woody scents, Filbertone (AKA filbert heptenone) naturally contributes to the odour of hazelnuts and is also a minor component of the scent of chocolate. Due to its astonishing power, we are offering this at 1% diluted in dipropylene glycol (DPG) but we also offer it pure for those who have need of it.

Often mistaken as a flavouring, this chemical is a hidden gem in perfumery, creating remarkable accords when properly diluted. At just 0.1%, it delivers fresh, fruity, green, and nutty nuances, effortlessly boosting citrus and floral blends. Pair it with Tropathiane, Oxane,  or Passifloran, and you’ll discover vibrant, near-addictive shades that defy easy description. Even the smallest amounts can work magic.

Filbertone blends beautifully with Sandexol®, Ambrexol™, Wild Cherry and Fleur de Cassie.

products.name: Fir Balsam Absolute 50% TEC
products.description:
Fir Balsam is the scent of winterly days, the great outdoors and Christmas festivities; perhaps no other material is so deeply entrenched in our shared scent-memory. It is also incredibly versatile, with fruit notes that can subtly enrich a gourmand to woody notes that blend well with all the classics such as vetiver, cedarwood and sandalwood.

This V. MANE Fils extract is rich, green, woody and sweet. It is a truly wonderful specimen of Fir Balsam and a must-have for all perfumers.

Fir Balsam is found in Polo Green (1978, our Compound Green), Drakkar Noir (1982), Rubenstein's Men's Club (1966), Patou Pour Homme (1980) and Patou Pour Homme Prive (1994), and Oscar de la Renta's Pour Lui (1980), amongst many others.

Because Fir Balsam is extremely thick we offer it at 50% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus). It may still require gentle heating to make it fully mobile depending upon your room temperature.

products.name: Fir Balsam Oliffac
products.description:
Fir Balsam Oliffac opens with a rush of fresh pine-needle greenness that quickly unfolds into something far more complex. The resinous heart carries an unexpected jammy sweetness—think raspberry preserves meets forest sap - anchored by smoky, mossy undertones that evoke the damp forest floor. This isn't the sharp terpenic bite of raw needle oils; it's a noble, rounded woody character with exceptional tenacity. If you want to capture the scent of Christmas without messing around with thick balsams and astringent wood oils, this is the tool for you.

You'll find this material indispensable for building authentic coniferous accords that need more than just green freshness. The jammy-fruity facet adds warmth and approachability to masculine fougères whilst the powerful balsamic backbone provides serious fixative strength in orientals and chypres. Pair it with lavender and oakmoss for classic barbershop structures, or push it into gourmand territory by emphasising its berry-sweet qualities with vanilla and tonka.

Pair with geosmin for damp-forest earthiness, or layer with Douglas fir and Canadian fir needle oils for a complete coniferous accord. Evernyl and cedrol in the formula contribute mossy-woody persistence. This is incredibly synergistic with Artemal.

What is an Oliffac?

IFF Oliffacs are a range of proprietary bases. They are IFF’s own standardised reconstructions of recognisable natural notes and genre materials (e.g., balsams, fruits, woods, animalic themes), often bui

products.name: Fir Oil, Canada
products.description:
Canadian Fir Oil opens with an immediately recognisable burst of fresh pine needles—that clean, slightly tart terpenic quality that transports you directly to a snow-covered forest. This initial brightness quickly reveals the oil's distinctive character: a remarkably sweet, soft balsamic richness that sets it apart from harsher coniferous oils. The sweetness isn't cloying but rather reminiscent of fresh sap weeping from bark, providing a well-rounded, mild character that makes this oil exceptionally versatile in perfumery applications.

Use Canadian Fir Oil when you need authentic evergreen freshness with sophistication. Its balanced profile makes it ideal for creating Christmas-themed compositions that avoid the harsh, medicinal notes of cheaper pine oils. Use it to add energising lift to masculine fougères, where its clean terpenic facets complement lavender beautifully. In functional perfumery, it excels in premium air fresheners and household cleaners, providing that coveted "fresh forest" effect while its natural sweetness prevents the sharp, synthetic character common in coniferous compositions.

The distinctions between Canadian, Siberian, and Douglas Fir oils fundamentally shape your formulation choices. Canadian Fir (Abies balsamea) delivers sweeter, richer, more immediately appealing evergreen notes with its characteristic balsamic warmth and grassy roundness. Siberian Fir (Abies sibirica) presents a more complex, woody profile with distinctive aldehydic top notes a

products.name: Firascone
products.description:
Firascone captures the dark, concentrated floralcy of red rose petals intertwined with berry-like fruitiness. This isn't fresh tea rose - it's rich, jammy, and voluptuous with an integrated saffron note that adds dry, spicy leather texture. Secondary apple and mint facets provide roundness and lift, preventing cloying sweetness whilst maintaining sophisticated depth.

This material solves the damascone restriction problem elegantly. You can work with Firascone from traces to 1% in fine fragrance without regulatory anxiety, unlike its ketone cousins that require extreme dilution. Use it to boost small doses of restricted rose ketones, extending fruity-floral volume whilst staying compliant.

Build jammy rose accords by combining Firascone with phenylethyl alcohol and geranium oil. Create sophisticated saffron profiles by pairing it with safraleine - Firascone provides the softer, floral-integrated saffron facet that commercial compositions demand. Its three-hour tenacity positions it perfectly as a heart note, bridging fruity top notes into woody-floral bases.

Because of its price and strength, we are offering this pure or diluted to 10% in DPG.

products.name: Fireside
products.description:
Compound Fireside is our internal formula for a scent in the style of By the Fireplace by Maison Margiela. Launched in 2015 and created by Marie Salamagne for the Replica collection, this is a woody gourmand fragrance built around smoky guaiac wood and roasted chestnut with warm spice and vanilla.

This compound features a creamy chestnut accord wrapped in smoky guaiac wood and musky cashmeran. The top notes of clove and pink pepper provide a warming spiced opening, while orange blossom and juniper lift the heart before the woods take hold. The base delivers rich vanilla and Peru balsam for a sweet, resinous finish. The result is a photorealistic woodsmoke effect – cosy rather than harsh – with good longevity and moderate to strong projection in the first hours before settling close to the skin.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Cloves, Pink Pepper, Orange Blossom
Heart Notes: Chestnut, Guaiac Wood, Juniper
Base Notes: Vanilla, Peru Balsam, Cashmeran

products.name: Firsantol®
products.description:
Firsantol is a superstar of the synthetic sandalwood family and yet it still tends to go unused when Javanol and Polysantol are available. Why this is I do not know as Firsantol really is one of the most diffusive and luminous wood chemicals; a trace goes a long way.

Blends with Polysantol and Dartanol (Laevo Bacdanol) are outstanding. A good comparison of the various chemicals is that Javanol is the most powerful and truest to the scent of sandalwood oil, Polysantol (nearly as strong as Javanol) has more sweetness and is an excellent all-round blender, and Firsantol is slightly weaker in odour intensity but the most diffusive in power.

The following blend creates a nice mixture in which Dartanol adds the creamy milkiness of natural sandalwood, polysantol adds fruity brightness and boosts radiance and firsantol adds diffusion and a drier woody note to prevent the accord from being overly lactonic or sweet.

45 Dartanol
35 Polysantol
20 Firsantol

For use in a floral scent you might consider the following tweak where Javanol adds the link to the florals (especially good with rose) and further increases the power.

40 Dartanol
35 Polysantol
20 Firsantol
5 Javanol

Non sandalwood materials that work well with Firsantol are Norlimbanol (normal and Dextro), Amyris Wood Oil, Cedramber, Ambrocenide, Myrrh Resinoid, Helvetolide and Habanolide.

products.name: Fixomusk™
products.description:
Fixomusk™ is an elegant restoration of the original Fixomusc of Chuit Naef & Cie popularised by fragrances such as Styx by Coty, Après L'Ondée and L'Heure Bleue by Guerlain and great later 20th century scents such as Poison by Dior, Oscar de la Renta, Parfum Sacré by Caron and Gianfranco Ferré for men.

Fixomusk is a soft and sweet animalic fixative base loaded with luxurious natural oils and absolutes. It is synergistic with Ambreine, Opoponax Doux and Irrozol. Use traces to add incredible longevity to your perfumes and cosmetics, or overdose it for its unique scent profile.

Due to the presence of musk ketone at a whopping 17%, Fixomusk should be restricted to 8.2% of a finished fragrance for customers requiring compliance with EU 1223/2009. Musk ketone is legal and unrestricted by IFRA but limited in quantity in European cosmetic products (including fine fragrance).

This crystallises slightly in cold environments. Apply gentle heat to dissolve.

Note: in preparation for IFRA 51 this product has been slightly reformulated and Benzyl Benzoate has been entirely eliminated.

products.name: Fleur D'Heliotrope
products.description:
Heliotrope is an elegant flower with a sweet almond and vanilla character. While heliotropin has been the classic way of adding this note to a fragrance, restrictions on the material have made it impossible for many to obtain.

Fraterworks® Fleur D'Heliotrope is a full flower De Laire base incorporating all of the classic elements of the heliotrope flower in combination with rich absolutes and essential oils to give you a sultry drydown but extending the floralcy into the heart of the scent. 

This is a must-have base for those wanting to add an elegant heliotrope notes to their fragrances without the complications that go with the use of pure heliotropin.

products.name: Fleur D'Oranger
products.description:
Fleur D'Oranger is an orange flower absolute type base. It can be used as a direct one for one replacer or in combination with other similar bases such as Floronol which imparts the note of neroli oil. 

Fleur D'Oranger is a long lasting rich and extremely natural base. This is a must have given the incredibly high prices of raw materials. Fraterworks Fleur D'Oranger is enriched with natural orange blossom absolute.

This base was used in L'Origan by Coty and Tabu by Jean Carles for Dana.

products.name: Fleur De Cassie
products.description:
Cassie is a complex sweet floral note of the Acacia family (specifically Acacia Farnesiana). It can be used to enhance and add complexity to violet and iris notes as well as blending well with gourmand and fruit notes due to its creamy anisic dry down.

Fraterworks Fleur De Cassie (a classic De Laire base) is rich with natural oils, madagascan vanilla, French mimosa, orris butter and more. At levels below 1% in your juice it adds volume and in higher amounts is a wonderful nuancer. Can be used safely up to a whopping 22% of your finished product according to IFRA 51.

Fleur de Cassie is a wonderful blender with mimosa and cherry notes.

products.name: Fleur de Cuir
products.description:
Sublime is the only word that can be used to describe this incredible natural product of Payan Betrand. Fleur de Cuir is a co-distillation of fruity osmanthus flowers into a molecular distillation of finest cedarwood oil. The end result is the most perfect balance of floral and woody notes in a purely natural extraction. Even more extraorardinary is the wonderfully complex almost oud-like leather top note which is utterly addictive. This is truly one of the masterpieces of modern perfume science.

Fleur de Cuir is best used boldly — up to 5.035% of your finished product for both IFRA 50 and IFRA 51. Fleur de Cuir is so good you can simply add florals and musk and sign off on a completed fragrance.

The cost of this blend is extremely good, making liberal use possible. And while our 4g price is affordable for most, we are also offering 1g sample pricing because everyone needs to try this. Even if you think you don't need or want it, add a 1g sample to your cart.

products.name: Fleur De Reseda
products.description:
Reseda is an unusual floral note that was far more popular in the past than it is today. And for that reason it deserves a renaissance! Fleur De Reseda (also known as Mignonette) is fruity and floral whilst having a striking green heart. Its sweet strawberry nuances make it perfect to add character to a contemporary gourmand fragrance.

First cultivated in England during the mid-18th century, mignonette quickly became a popular scent amongst the well-to-do. If you are looking for the "next big thing" or just want a striking and unusual note to make your fragrance stand out, look no further than Fraterworks Fleur de Reseda.

products.name: Fleur De Tabac
products.description:
Fleur de Tabac is an incredible tobacco flower type base created by the master perfumer Jean Carles at the end of the 1920s when he worked for Roure. It encapsulates not just tobacco flowers, but the distinct scent of the entire plant as it would have existed in the early 20th century before genetic modification and cross breeding altered it forever.

Fleur de Tabac was most likely the foundation of the now all-but-disappeared perfume of the similar name by Cherigan in 1929 but its most famous outing was as a key note in Schiaparelli's groundbreaking 1937 fragrance Shocking (also by Jean Carles) as part of its central pink flower accord. 

The base is presented here in an essentially unmodified form. Miraculously the formula of Mr Carles has survived the onslaught of regulations and the only necessary tweak was the replacement of a trace amount of a prohibed musk.

Fleur de Tabac is like nothing you have experienced before. It is a truly unique and astonishing piece of fragrance history. This base is proof that perfumery has been, and can again be, an art form.

products.name: Fleuramone™
products.description:
Fleuramone opens with the unmistakable character of jasmine blossoms, delivering concentrated floral power reminiscent of cis-jasmone. Its lactonic quality creates creamy depth whilst green facets keep it fresh. The peach-like undertone emerges as it develops, maintaining freshness for hours.

You'll find this ketone essential for building jasmine, honeysuckle and reseda accords where natural extracts prove prohibitive. It excels when combined with macrocyclic musks and undecanolide, creating sophisticated white floral compositions. Use it to add unexpected freshness to lavender and herbal fragrances where its rue note provides intrigue.

Blend Fleuramone with hedione for radiant jasmine diffusion or combine with benzyl acetate and linalool to construct complete jasmine reconstructions. Pair with indole for authentic indolic jasmine character. This material bridges floral hearts with fruity top notes seamlessly.

products.name: Fleurs Deluxe № 1
products.description:
Fleurs Deluxe № 1 is a sublime modern floral base that perfectly balances Jasmine, Rose, tuberose and Hyacinth, with accents of other luxury flowers. It is a classic French blend that is modernised with the most radiant and current molecules thus combining the peak of historic perfumery with the best of aroma science.

The purpose of this base is to allow perfumers to incorporate a rich natural floral fond into their fragrances without having to outlay enormous amounts to buy the various precious absolutes and essential oils that are needed for this high level of fine fragrance making.

The base includes aroma molecules that are rarely used by artisans due to the high cost (in some cases many times higher than natural floral oils).

Dilute it “as-is” for a fragrance that matches the elegance and quality of Patou's famous Joy, or use it as a floralising element in a more complex fine fragrance.

products.name: Fleurs Deluxe № 3
products.description:
Fleurs Deluxe № 3 is the floral core of the great Iris Gris (1946) by Vincent Roubert for Jacques Fath. Containing every orris product available in combination with the great Persicol base and luxurious absolutes of French rose de Mai, jasmine, tuberose and more. It is easy to understand why this fragrance is considered by many to be the greatest perfume ever made.

Iris Gris is comprised of 65% of Fleurs Deluxe № 3 — unchanged and unadapted; this is the pure heart of the fragrance. Compound the demonstration formula below for an exact replica of the original Iris Gris or use Fleurs Deluxe № 3 as the starting point for your own modern luxurious orris based fragrance. 

The original Iris Gris was a multifloral perfume of carnation, iris, violet, rose, jasmine, tuberose, woods and musks (including a hefty dose of civet absolute!). This was all wrapped in a delightful sweet peach note from Firmenich's famous Persicol base.

We also have Fleurs Deluxe № 1 if you are looking for a rich French rose and jasmine fragrance in the style of Patou's Joy.

products.name: Floralate
products.description:
Despite its name, this is not a floral chemical. It's synonym, in fact, gives a better idea of what it is used for: Citrolate. Floralate is a dry bitter-fresh grapefruit material with (as is so often the case with aromatics of this type,) rhubarb nuances. It lacks the juiciness of citrus which makes it an interesting material to take a cologne in a very novel direction.

It is long lasting so it is useful for extending citrus oil (not just grapefruit) into the heart of a perfume. A touch of Nootkatone and a judicious use of vetiver Haiti can further extend it into the dry down.

For stewed fruit accords which may be on the sickly side, floralate can offer a much needed dryness.

products.name: Floralozone®
products.description:
With an effusion of ozonic freshness and salt-rich sea air, Floralozone is every bit the scent of the beach, and summer and nostalgic pleasures.

Floralozone adds diffusion and lift to most fragrance types without adding too strong a character of its own. This makes it a great nuancer for green florals, fresh air and water type materials such as Helional®, Hydroxycitronellal, and Calone.

Floralzone has a wonderful synergy with Celestafleur™, and floral bases, particularly Muguet.

products.name: Floramat
products.description:
Floramat opens with intriguing spicy-woody warmth that immediately recalls damascone territory. The floral tendency adds softness without becoming overtly rosy, while green-herbal facets provide freshness. It delivers a complex, multifaceted character that bridges spicy, woody, and floral worlds beautifully.

Floramat offers perfumers damascone-like effects at a fraction of the cost and significantly higher safe usage amount. Use it in floral compositions where you want rosy body with spicy warmth, or in fougères and lavender accords where its woody-herbal character supports aromatic notes. The material adds fruity accent to citrus blends and enhances rose-fruity compositions. At 92-hour substantivity, your spicy-floral effect persists well into the heart and drydown.

Work with Floramat at up to 5% in your concentrate. It excels alongside actual damascones where it extends and supports their effect, or as a cost-effective alternative in functional applications. The material shows excellent stability across fragrance types including flower shop accords, spicy orientals, and woody compositions. Blend with rose materials, lavender, and woody notes for sophisticated modern florals.

products.name: Floranol
products.description:
Floranol is a fantasy replacer for Neroli bigarade oil which is now beyond the budget of most perfumers. Keeping its roots in the classical bases of De Laire, our Floronol is updated for modern tastes and can be effectively used from < 1% to 6.6% of your finished product (IFRA 50). 

Fraterworks Floranol has a wonderful ability to add freshness to heavy floral rich fragrances and orientals, whilst also sitting beautifully in a classic cologne fond. Floranol is a must-have base for all perfumers and is rich with naturals oils and absolutes.

If you are looking for a more true to life Neroli oil replacer, you may prefer our Neroli Supreme TruEss™.

products.name: Florapeel
products.description:
Florapeel from V. MANE Fils is a highly diffusive floral grapefruit base built around their captive molecule Bigarane. It shares a clear familial connection to Bigaflower and Green Catcher and can be combined with either or both of those bases to great effect.

In a world where grapefruit notes are extremely popular and natural grapefruit, while readily available, often needs some help from synthetics — invariably methyl pamplemousse — this is a welcome addition to the perfumer's palette.

This joins our two other great bases: Firmenich's Grapefruit Base 184062D and our own highly popular Pomelo Grandis (“This captures the essence of the entire fruit, without the risk of degradation.” — J. Y. S.).

products.name: Florex®
products.description:
Florex (also known as Tonka Undecanone) is a powerful and long lasting lactone with a clearly coumarin note but nuances of wood and amber.

In Firmenich's own words: “A very powerful and tenacious balsamic, Tonka-like note with a unique tangy quality. It has a sweet yet tart character that suggests tobacco and coconut with a green nuance. It can be used in all types of perfumes but has especially interesting effects in white florals, citrus and fruity accords.”

products.name: Florhydral
products.description:
Florhydral smells fresh, green, and convincingly natural — a lily of the valley character with hyacinth-like brightness and a clean, dewy quality. There is no harsh synthetic edge. On dilution the green facets soften and a rounder, more delicate floral emerges, closer to a real flower than most muguet materials manage.

Hydroxycitronellal, cyclamen aldehyde, and linalool are its most effective companions for building a complete muguet bouquet. Start at low levels and build up — a little changes a composition significantly. In white floral blends it contributes a green, dewy freshness that heavier materials like jasmine and tuberose benefit from.

Ozonic materials alongside florhydral produce a fresh, aquatic white-floral effect worth exploring. Rose and geranium both gain a spring-like quality when florhydral introduces its green muguet character into the heart. Citrus top notes also benefit — the hyacinth brightness extends naturally into bergamot and lemon accords.

products.name: Florol®
products.description:
From Firmenich we offer this lovely quality of Florol which we have found to be more floral and elegant than other offerings.

Florol is a general floraliser and is vital as a replacement (alone or in an accord) for Lilial which is now banned in the EU. Florol is a soft and diffusive floral which, despite leaning in the direction of muguet, does not alter the character of a scent, making it ideal as a building block.

Florol is effective in traces to overdose.

products.name: Floropal
products.description:
Floropal is tart and fresh: rhubarb stalk and grapefruit peel first, then a green floralcy that leans toward gardenia, with chrysanthemum and cypress in the background. It smells convincingly like snapped stems and pith rather than sugared fruit, and that slight bitterness is exactly what makes it so useful.

Add it to a fruity accord for tartness and bite, or to a grapefruit theme to underline the peel-and-pith character. In gardenia and tuberose it contributes a fresh green floral element that keeps heavy white flowers airy. It is equally at home in blackcurrant, raspberry, tomato-leaf and general green notes.

Vertacetal Coeur (also from Symrise) is the same material in a purer, more grapefruit-forward form; Floropal reads more floral and fresh, and in most formulas the two are close enough to swap. Try it with methyl pamplemousse and rhubarb notes for a bright, bitter top, or with vetiver for a green, rooty grapefruit.

products.name: Flouve “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Flouve is the luxury member of the hay family, and while our Hay Absolute from V MANE Fils is incredibly beautiful, Payan Bertrand's Flouve “Signature” Absolute is sublime. It carries the IG Absolue Pays de Grasse marque, the highest form of certification for fragrance materials grown and processed in Grasse. 

Steffan Arctander describes it thus: "[Flouve absolute has] a very sweet, herbaceous, tobacco-like and coumarinic odor. The odor is so rich and so complex that one can keep on finding notes in it. However, the overall fragrance is a sweet, licorice-like, root-like, somewhat mossy-herbaceous like wet underforest and meadows, of exceptional tenacity and high penetrating power. [… U]seful in chypre, fougere, pine, oriental bases, and in traces as a sweetener for dry-woody notes which can be modified in a very pleasant way.”

Flouve blends excellently with bases Artemal™, Suralette™ Extra, Verdantol and Amazonia, as well as with French Lavender Oil, Douglas Fir Needle Oil, Oakmoss Absolutes, Roman Chamomile, Labdanum and petitgrain oils (especially LMR's marvellous Petitgrain Oil Terpeneless). Lovely accords can be made with aroma chemicals Fenchone Alpha, Linalool Oxide, Vetimoss, Azarbre, and Geosmin.

Because flouve absolute is so thick, we now optionally supply it at 10% dilution in Triethyl Citrate Natural making it ISO 9235 compliant.

Origin: Grasse, France
Part: Dried flowering tops of grass
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Foin Coupé
products.description:
Foin Coupé is the scent of freshly mown hay. It is an incredibly diffusive sweet coumarinic base with orange blossom nuances loaded with natural oils, including pure and natural French hay absolute. Use it as a modifier for coumarin or herbal notes, or as a radiant and earthy nuancer for a gentlemen's fragrance.

Featured in Patou Pour Homme Privé, one of the most highly regarded scents for men gaining a near-mythical status, this fresh cut hay base is sublime.

We also offer the original crystalline Foin Rigaud — an intensely powerful and penetrating base note product.

products.name: Foin Rigaud
products.description:
Foin bases encapsulate the dreamy scent of the wild French countryside where ribbons of orange blossom, geranium and wild flowers float on the warm hay-soaked air.
Foin Rigaud was one of the earliest types of foin (new mown hay) base. It was, in reality, an embellished form of coumarin - born from the practice by which powerful new molecules were made available to perfumers as the lead character in accords and bases.

Despite being used in a relatively small amount, Foin Rigaud played a vital role in Coty's L'Origan. An update to our earlier formula can found below.

Foin Rigaud is presented here in its original powder form. This product is very intense and powerful. If you prefer a more classic top to bottom fantasy hay base we recommend Foin Coupé which comes in liquid form.

products.name: Forest Pepper, P. Jungle Essence
products.description:
Forest Pepper CO2 (Pure Jungle Essence) opens with a tingling spicy-citrus burst — pink pepper warmth shot through with bright aldehydic orange and lemon. Underneath sit soft tropical-fruit and floral facets that round the spice. The metallic-citrus character is closer to Sichuan pepper than to black pepper, despite the name.

Use Forest Pepper CO2 to bring authentic peppery sparkle and citrus lift to colognes, modern fougères and spicy-woody accords. It works as a top-note enhancer that carries spicy presence into the heart of a composition. It also lifts dull citrus accords with a tingling, modern edge.

Pair with bergamot, pink peppercorn oil and aldehyde C-10 for a sparkling modern citrus top, or use alongside cardamom, ginger CO2 and incense for a tingling oriental opening. A trace under rose lifts the floral with peppery warmth. Dose carefully — overdose pushes the metallic sparkle into harshness.

Forest Pepper CO2 is extracted via supercritical CO2 from the dried fruits of Zanthoxylum rhetsa, known locally as Ma Khaen, a tree that grows wild in mountainous regions of northern Thailand and across Southeast Asia. The Pure Jungle Essence process uses CO2 alone — no co-solvents — at low temperature, preserving the volatile top notes that conventional steam distillation destroys. Despite its name, the species is unrelated to true black pepper (Piper nigrum) and belongs to the citrus family.

products.name: Four Corners Resinoid
products.description:
Four Corners Resinoid opens with a dark, fruity sweetness evoking dried tamarind and rum-soaked raisins. Nutty caramel, gentle balsamic warmth, and a faint costus-like earthiness follow. Extracted from the four-ridged pods of the Cameroonian aidan tree (Tetrapleura tetraptera), this is an uncommon and distinctive material for your palette.

That rich fruity-balsamic character fits naturally into gourmand and oriental bases, where it furnishes a dried fruit facet sitting somewhere between rum and benzoin. You can also use it to warm woody accords or steer amber compositions toward something more exotic and unexpected.

Think of this as the link between the balsam shelf and the rum cabinet in your collection. It grounds gourmand accords when paired with vanillin, coumarin, and tonka, and enriches labdanum-heavy amber bases with a distinctive dried-fruit twist.

This material is sold only at 10% in TEC which is how V. MANE Fils manufactures it.

Image Copyright Marina Khaytarova.

products.name: Fraistone
products.description:
Fraistone delivers a tart, bright fruitiness that sits between strawberry, green apple, and plum. There is a subtle anisic quality underneath — a faint liquorice hint that adds complexity without dominating. The overall character is clean, fresh, and inviting, with none of the heaviness that many fruity materials carry.

Use fraistone to add fruity sparkle to your floral compositions. It lifts rose, tuberose, jasmine, and orange blossom accords with a tart freshness that keeps them feeling modern. It also builds convincing strawberry and apple effects when combined with other fruity esters and lactones.

Blend with rose absolute and damascone for a fruit-forward rose accord. Try it alongside neroli and hedione for a sparkling fruity-floral opening. Pair with lilac and peony bases where its tartness creates a convincing spring-fruit character. You can dose generously — it works well up to high levels in your concentrate.

products.name: Framboise Base 184039 D
products.description:
Framboise smells exactly like a handful of ripe raspberries — the balance between sweet and tart is spot on. There is a juicy, jammy quality that feels convincingly natural, plus a subtle seedy greenness that stops it from tipping into candy territory. The overall effect is fresh and appetising.

Firmenich originally recommended this base for modifying chypre compositions, and that remains one of its best applications. The fruity tartness lifts mossy-woody accords beautifully. It also works as a standalone berry note in fruity-floral compositions, where its finesse and stability give it an edge over cruder raspberry reconstructions.

Pair Framboise with blackcurrant bud absolute for a rich dark-berry accord, or layer it with rose for a classic raspberry-rose combination. Beta-ionone adds realistic depth, while ethyl maltol can push the sweetness for gourmand work. This base rewards subtlety — a little goes a long way.

products.name: Frangipani Absolute
products.description:
Frangipani Absolute opens with intoxicating exotic florality—heady, creamy, and immediately evocative of warm tropical nights. Soft peachy facets mingle with sweet orange blossom character, while gardenia-like richness adds opulent depth. Balsamic undertones of almond and vanilla emerge in the drydown, creating a complete floral portrait that feels both delicate and seductive.

This precious absolute comes from Plumeria alba flowers, harvested between March and April from shrubs native to the West Indies. The name itself tells a fascinating story: when a French colonist encountered plumeria in the Caribbean, its scent reminded him of a famous Renaissance perfume created by the Roman Frangipani family—making this the only plant named after a fragrance rather than the reverse.

Blend with tropical fruits, coconut, tuberose, gardenia, and orange blossom for authentic compositions. The high benzyl salicylate and benzyl benzoate content provides natural fixative properties.

Frangipani absolute has a wax-like consistency when pure, and so we also sell it diluted to 20% for ease of use. Both forms may still need a small amount of gentle heat for full solubility.

products.name: Frankincense Oil, Somalia
products.description:
Also known as olibanum essential oil, this oil is a bright and fresh top note resin with long lasting effects. It works wonders with citrus oils to give longevity and interesting effects and is vital in the creation of Church incense notes.

This fine oil is sourced from Somalia and is intoxicating. There are no bad notes here, just pure incense goodness.

Origin: Somalia
Part: Exudate from bark
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Frankincense Sacra Oil, Oman
products.description:
Frankincense can be a little confusing because it has multiple names. The classical name is Olibanum (from an Arabic word meaning milk) while more recently the term Frankincense has become the norm. 

To further complicate things we have two common types used in perfumery:Boswellia carterii and Boswellia sacra. The differences between these two varieties is minuscule and basically the region of growth determines the term used (inconsistently from supplier to supplier) with the sacra type coming from Oman and Yemen and the carterii coming from Somalia and East Africa.

The Frankincense Sacra oil we offer here is from Oman and it is a spectacular version, being sweet and perfumistic with a less camphoraceous opening than the Somalian frankincense oil we also stock.

Origin: Oman
Part: Pathological exudate from bark
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Freskomenthe
products.description:
Mint has a habit of seeming medicinal (think toothpaste or cleaners) and almost entirely masculine, hence its common appearance in fougéres. But Freskomenthe bucks the trend with its woody and slightly fruity undertone (in the direction of black currant and berries).

Its agrestic and woody facets make it more of a dried mint leaf material. It is longer lasting that peppermint oil and able to stand up to some fairly harsh aroma chemicals making it ideal for functional perfumery.

Use it with lavender and dihydromyrcenol in place of peppermint oil. It combines exceedingly well with floralozone when you're seeking a cold effect.

products.name: Fructone
products.description:
Fructone opens with intense apple-pineapple sweetness that's far more complex than typical fruity esters. This ketal structure delivers exceptional tenacity with its distinctive winey character and cooked strawberry nuances. The unexpected woody-pine undertones add sophisticated depth, preventing the sweetness from becoming juvenile or candy-like.

You'll find Fructone invaluable for building sophisticated fruit accords that last. Use at 1-30% where its ketal stability provides longevity that simple esters cannot achieve. Jean-Claude Ellena reveals its secret: combine with ethyl maltol for authentic strawberry effects, or blend with frambinone and beta-ionone for realistic raspberry. Its deep fruity character enhances jasmine, tuberose, and gardenia bases without overwhelming their floralcy.

The material excels in creating exotic tropical effects beyond standard fruit notes. Combine with damascenone for jammy richness, hedione for airy lift, or iso E super for woody radiance. Its remarkable stability and 30% usage potential make it perfect for functional fragrances requiring lasting fruit impact. The woody finish bridges beautifully between fruit top notes and floral hearts.

products.name: Fruit Sec
products.description:
Fruit Sec 184078D opens with an intoxicating burst of concentrated dried fruits—imagine sun-ripened plums and apricots transformed through desiccation into something far richer. This isn't simple fruit juice sweetness but rather the complex depth of preserved fruits with their concentrated sugars, subtle fermentation notes, and that characteristic skin astringency. The damascone-rich heart radiates powerful jammy facets while ionones add sophisticated powdery nuances.

This material transforms compositions at every level—use it at trace amounts to add mysterious depth to roses or woody accords. At 1-5%, it becomes a recognisable dried fruit signature that elevates fruity-florals and adds gourmand warmth to orientals. The creamy lactonic base notes ensure smooth blending without harsh edges, solving the technical challenge of incorporating powerful materials like damascones into balanced accords.

Reach for Fruit Sec when you need instant sophistication in gourmand creations or unexpected richness in florals. It pairs brilliantly with cassis bases for dynamic tropical effects, adds unctuousness to rose accords, and creates enveloping warmth with vanilla, benzoin and spices. At higher doses (5-8%), it becomes your composition's star—perfect for modern oriental gourmands where dried fruit opulence defines the fragrance.

products.name: Fruitate
products.description:
Fruitate opens with a burst of sweet, ripe fruitiness that carries a distinct rum-candy warmth. A citrus nuance adds brightness while subtle floral facets give it dimension beyond a simple fruit note. The woody undertone in the drydown keeps it grounded and blendable.

This material's real strength is its exceptional diffusion and staying power, lasting six days on blotter. Use it to give fruity top notes persistence they normally lack, or to add ripe sweetness to jasmine and tuberose accords. It blends particularly well with bergamot and lavender.

Try Fruitate at low levels as a fruity enhancer wherever you need more bloom and radiance. At higher doses the rum-candy warmth becomes prominent, opening up gourmand and tropical directions. Combine with citrus oils for sparkle or white florals for lush fruitiness.

products.name: Fumencens HTC
products.description:
Upon the first sniff of Fumencens HTC one immediately recognises the scent of fragrant ribbons of incense swirling heavenwards in an old stone Church.

Fumencens HTC is a masterpiece of modern perfume technology in which frankincense resin is blended with natural triethyl citrate and heated to extremely high temperatures in a technique known as hydrothermal carbonization. This produces a near-burnt effect in the frankincense resin that replicates masterfully the scent of incense on red hot coals in a censer and hundreds of burning memorial candles.

This technique is very similar to the pyrogenation process used by Firmenich in making their Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain, however unlike that material Fumencens HTC has an additional (and very long lasting) aspect of cade or birch tar. It is the smokiness and mahogany-like woodiness that sets Fumencens HTC apart.

I won't say it twice: you need this.

products.name: Furfural 5% DPG
products.description:
Furfural 5% DPG opens with sweet woody-almond character—warm, inviting, and immediately evocative of fresh-baked bread. The caramellic undertone adds depth, while a bitter coffee nuance provides sophistication. This furan aldehyde smells remarkably natural and food-like, bridging almond, bread crust, and roasted coffee in a single molecule.

In compositions, furfural acts as the bridge between sweet vanillic notes and dry woody bases. You'll find it indispensable for creating authentic bakery accords where it provides the toasted crust against creamy vanilla interiors. Pair it with pyrazines to amplify nutty roasted facets, or use it to "brown" overly sweet gourmand blends that need grounding.

When you need that unmistakable scent of Maillard browning—whether for coffee, whiskey, or pastry effects—this family of materials delivers the heat-treated authenticity other materials can't match. Use it sparingly; its potency easily dominates when overdosed.

Important: the pure material has an extremely restrictive IFRA allowance of 0.001% of your finished perfume. We sell it at 5% which has an IFRA 51 and 52 level of 0.02%.

products.name: Furfuryl Acetate
products.description:
Furfuryl Acetate opens with an astringent green banana peel character that feels more sophisticated than typical banana notes. You detect the waxy, slightly woody essence of unripe banana skin alongside pear-like ethereal lift. This distinctive sharpness cuts through heavy base notes brilliantly.

This material transforms simple fruit accords into complex compositions with depth. Use it at 0.5-2% to add realistic skin and fermentation notes to banana bases, or blend with pyrazines for authentic coffee reconstruction. It bridges the gap between fresh tropical notes and caramelised gourmand elements, making your rum accords funkier and your bakery notes more golden-crusted. The acetate provides essential lift to coffee accords whilst contributing the acidic fruitiness of fresh espresso.

Combine Furfuryl Acetate with oakwood CO2 for barrel-aged whiskey effects. Add traces to white florals for narcotic jammy decay notes. Mix with maltol to transform cotton candy sweetness into crème brûlée depth—the burnt sugar edge that makes gourmands irresistible.

products.name: Galaxolide®
products.description:
Galaxolide is a clean and powerful polycyclic musk which, even in extreme overdoses of 40% or more, allows the other materials in a fragrance to shine through. It is a highly appreciated musk by consumers. It adds fixation and exaltation to all fragrances and is frequently blended with other musks which often take the role of modifiers.

“A clean, powerful and versatile iso-chroman musk having exceptional persistence and a superb fragrance quality approaching the tone of macrocyclic musks.” — IFF

Galaxolide is often the single largest aromachemical in luxury fragrance brands such as Tom Ford, Amouage and Creed. It's low cost and popular appeal make it a must-have for all perfumers.

NOTE: pure Galaxolide is extremely viscous so it needs heat to make it fluid. For that reason we are selling it here in the standard 50% dilution from IFF as well as pure. Be sure to check your dilution prior to buying.

products.name: Galbanum Resinoid
products.description:
Galbanum Resinoid opens with the same characteristic burst of intense greenness familiar from the essential oil—crushed bell peppers, torn leaves, and fresh-cut grass—but quickly reveals its distinctive personality. Where the oil remains sharp and volatile, the resinoid settles into a rich, dark green depth with pronounced balsamic warmth. This thick, viscous material carries the forest within it: coniferous resins, damp earth, and woody undertones that ground its vegetal sharpness in something more profound and lasting.

Galbanum Resinoid is best used at 0.5-3% when you need green notes with genuine staying power and complexity. Unlike the essential oil's fleeting pine-like top notes, the resinoid provides sustained green depth throughout a fragrance's evolution. Its superior fixative properties anchor volatile materials while contributing its own sophisticated woody-balsamic character. Use it as the foundation for chypre green compositions where longevity matters, or to create authentic forest atmospheres that persist from first spray to final drydown.

The differences between Galbanum essential oil and resinoid transform your formulation approach entirely. The oil delivers sharp, penetrating greenness with distinctive pine-like top notes—perfect for immediate impact but lacking persistence. The resinoid trades some of that initial sharpness for profound depth: less volatile, less harsh, more balsamic and woody. Where the oil acts as a fleeting green modifier, the resinoid

products.name: Galbanum “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Galbanum oil is powerful green oil which gives the well known distinctive odour to Chanel No 19 and the original Miss Dior by Jean Carles. Galbanum in small amounts adds a wonderful green floralcy and its blends with muguet materials are unsurpassed.

Payan Bertrand's Galbanum oil (one of their signature products) is a truly luxurious quality which surpasses all others we tested.

Origin: Persia
Part: Resin
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Galbex®
products.description:
Galbex is a speciality base created by Firmenich to showcase Dynascone when it was first created. Later it was improved upon with the use of Neobutenone Alpha and it remains in that form today.

As well as the overdose of Neobutenone, the base contains accessory notes to soften and round out the edges of the base. We highly recommend it for people looking for an easy to use green pineapple note. 

Galbex blends beautifully with Hedione, Florol, Hivernal Neo, and green materials.

products.name: Gamma Decalactone
products.description:
Gamma Decalactone is a key material used for recreating gardenia and osmanthus flowers in which it naturally appears.
