This lactone is creamy and coconut with nuances of peach like its better known counterpart Gamma Undecalactone; gamma decalactone can be used in its place (or in addition) for a slightly different take on the classic lactonic peach note. This material has a more complex and even vaguely leafy quality.

This is a wonderful lactone for creamy modern gourmand fragrances and, as you would expect, it blends extremely well with Vanellia™, Vanillin “Signature”, Vanillin Natural ex Clove, and of course the famous Persicol base.

products.name: Gamma Dodecalactone
products.description:
Gamma Dodecalactone opens with the unmistakable richness of C12 lactones—imagine ripe peaches drowning in heavy cream and melted butter. This isn't the light, ethereal fruitiness of smaller lactones; it's fruit with gravitas, substance, and an almost edible quality. The initial burst reveals overripe stone fruits—peach and apricot—but with a pronounced fatty character that suggests the richness of coconut cream or cultured butter. Metallic undertones add complexity, while an oily quality creates mouth-coating persistence that smaller lactones can't achieve.

Use Gamma Dodecalactone at 0.5-3% when you need fruity notes with exceptional depth and tenacity. Its heavier molecular weight (C12 versus C10 in Gamma Decalactone) transforms the character from creamy-fresh to fatty-rich. Where Gamma Decalactone provides bright apricot-peach with lactonic creaminess, Gamma Dodecalactone delivers a more opulent, buttery interpretation with superior fixative properties. Use it in gourmand accords where you want fruit notes that won't disappear—think peach cobbler rather than fresh peach. In tropical compositions, it bridges fruit and coconut beautifully. Combine with lighter lactones to create dimensional fruit effects spanning from fresh to preserved.

The Difference A Do- Makes

The progression from Gamma Decalactone (C10) to Gamma Dodecalactone (C12) illustrates how two additional carbons dramatically alter olfactory character. Gamma Decalactone offers creamy peach-apricot with fresh, s

products.name: Gamma Heptalactone
products.description:
Gamma heptalactone delivers exceptional performance in tropical and gourmand compositions. This versatile lactone contributes a natural coconut character without the suntan lotion effect of other coconut materials. Perfumers prize its creamy richness and ability to add authentic milky notes to fruity accords with balanced sweetness.

Use at moderate concentrations to create realistic coconut notes in tropical fragrances. Enhances peach, apricot and other stone fruit accords with creamy richness. Combines beautifully with vanilla and tonka bean for gourmand applications. Provides buttery, dairy-like undertones in dessert-inspired compositions without becoming overly sweet.

products.name: Gamma Hexalactone
products.description:
Gamma Hexalactone is one of the more unique amongst the lactones, owing to a floral fruity layer on top of a tonka and tobacco base. 

It has a very delicate cresylic nuance (vaguely similar to Cyclopidene) in combination with a low key hint of benzyl acetate giving it a ribbon of ylang floralcy through the heart. This makes it a wonderful nuancer for our Signature vanillin. It also has a hint of booziness which is great for a tipsy accord.

This is definitely one of the more interesting lactones and a firm favourite at Fraterworks.

Blend it with Rum Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils, Tonka Bean Absolute, Coumarin (Synthetic or Natural)

products.name: Gamma Nonalactone
products.description:
Like Aldehydes C-16 (Strawberry) and C-14 (Peach), Gamma Nonalactone has a common name which is incorrect: Aldehyde C-18. Gamma Nonalactone is the scent of coconut and is the most popular basic material used to impart that scent in fragrances.

With no restrictions on use and a very popular odour profile, Gamma Nonalactone is an essential chemical for perfumers. Very small amounts add a lovely creamy quality while overdose can used for fun effects as evidenced by our Beach Bum scent (free formula further down the page).

Gamma Nonalactone blends with all fruit materials but also with rich florals like Tuberose and Jasmine.

products.name: Gamma Octalactone
products.description:
Gamma Octalactone is best known for its sweet, creamy, coconut-like aroma, with a subtle herbaceous undertone. Its warm and rich character makes it an essential addition to gourmand, tropical, and creamy accords. Though sometimes compared to coumarin for its lactonic sweetness, gamma octalactone leans more toward a tropical creaminess reminiscent of coconut and tonka.

Gamma Octalactone adds lactonic warmth to fig accords, complementing Stemone’s green, woody fig leaf notes. Together, they balance ripe fig sweetness with crisp, leafy freshness for a natural profile.

products.name: Gamma Undecalactone
products.description:
Gamma Undecalactone (also incorrectly referred to as Aldehyde C-14 as it is really a lactone and not an aldehyde) is the classic peach note for perfumes. It was discovered in 1908 and was first used as part of the key of the sweet Persicol base in Nuit de Chine (1913) by Maurice Schaller for Paul Poiret's Les Parfums de Rosine, but most famously a few years later as the key peach note (in the same Persicol base) in Mitsouko (1919) by Jacques Guerlain.

Undecalactone Gamma can be used at 1% dilution to add a luscious and softening effect to a fragrance, and in higher doses (at 10% or pure) for a clearly peach-like quality. Amounts under 1% are most common but there is no limit on this material and doses far higher are perfectly fine.

Below we present a number of demonstration formulas using Persicol or Undecalactone Gamma. You can simply replace the Persicol with around 80% of the same quantity in Undecalactone Gamma for a perfectly good result.

products.name: Gardenia J. Ellis
products.description:
Named after the great 18th century naturalist who discovered the flower, Gardenia J. Ellis is a profoundly beautiful representation of the full flowering majesty of one of the most beloved flowers.

Lactonic, sweet, green and strikingly true to life, this is the finest gardenia base on the market today. Traces add creamy elegance to any multiflor while an overdose gives you a hyper-realistic floral heart. Sublime.

Gardenia In Perfume History

Gardenia has long captivated perfumers as one of the most elusive and challenging white florals to capture in a bottle. Unlike jasmine or tuberose, which yield essential oils or absolutes, gardenia's delicate petals refuse to surrender their scent through traditional extraction methods, making the true gardenia absolute extraordinarily rare and prohibitively expensive. This scarcity sparked decades of creative reconstruction, with perfumers building gardenia accords from jasmine, tuberose, and ylang-ylang, enhanced by mushroom-like methyl anthranilate and creamy benzyl acetate. The breakthrough came with synthetic molecules like styrallyl acetate (gardenia acetate), which captured gardenia's distinctive fresh-green floralcy.

Classic fragrances like Chanel's Gardénia (1925), created by Ernest Beaux, established the archetypal gardenia: creamy, narcotic, slightly mushroomy, with green freshness balancing the heavy white floral heart. The note reached new heights of naturalism in Estée Lauder's Private Collection Tuberose Gardenia (2007),

products.name: Genet “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Of the myriad absolutes of genet (aka broom), this is the finest French product. It is the highest quality genet on the market today, being produced by one of the top suppliers of high end naturals from Grasse.

Genet absolute is one of the most treasured of all the naturals, imparting a warmth and sweetness that naturalises and enriches a wide range of fragrances. Traces add interest and complexity, while larger doses add an incredibly luxurious and rich nuance of verdant fields and rolling green hills stretching far into the horizon. Blends of genet with tuberose and other floral absolutes are out of this world.

Because genet absolute is so thick and costly, we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate making it ISO 9235 compliant. This replaces our previous offering of 50% dilution only.

Origin: France
Part: Flowers
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Gentian “Signature” Resinoid
products.description:
Gentian resinoid smells of damp earth, bitter roots, and cool Alpine air. The bitterness is striking — green, vegetal, almost medicinal — but underneath sits a quiet honeyed warmth and dry woody depth. It is one of perfumery's rarest and most unusual natural materials.

Jean-Claude Ellena chose gentian for Hermès Eau de Gentiane Blanche — proof that this obscure root material can anchor a major luxury fragrance. Use it sparingly to add bitter-earthy originality to green compositions, chypres, and iris accords. It shares the powdery, rooty quality of orris but with a cold, bitter twist.

Gentiana lutea — the great yellow gentian — grows wild in Alpine meadows and takes a decade to reach maturity. Its roots give Suze, Salers, and Avèze their famous bitterness. Pair it with vetiver, oakmoss, angelica root, and bergamot for compositions that smell like nowhere else.

This extract is a signature speciality of Payan Bertrand.

products.name: Geosmin
products.description:
Geosmin is the chemical responsible for the smell of freshly turned soil and spring rain. It is one of the most powerful chemicals in nature and it is familiar to everyone, often eliciting shouts of glee from non-perfumers who thrill at the ability of a perfumer to bottle such a beloved smell.

In addition to pure, it is offered here diluted to 10% and 1% in DPG but is still very powerful; it is often used at 0.1% or even 0.01% in fragrances and blends. Traces add a natural earthiness and inimitable quality to patchouli or vetiver scents, while a very careful overdose gives interesting effects.

Geosmin is a radiant and adds power and diffusion to any fragrance.

products.name: Geraldehyde
products.description:
When you're looking for an aldehyde which isn't the usual C-10, C-11 and C-12, give Geraldehyde a try. Also know as geranyl acetaldehyde, this is a floral meets marine super-powered aldehyde. On its own it is a great way to add sparkle and flash to a citrus fragrance while contributing volume, but it also works as a booster to other aldehydic notes. It's marine quality also makes it a good partner to ozonics like Calone and the surprising sea-moss material Oceanol, also from IFF.

When dosed carefully (under 0.1% typically) you can add radiance and lift to a scent. With ylang-ylang you get a wonderful synergy which makes this a great modern material to use in a Chanel No 5 type scent.

From our own range this is great with Amazonia and Solafleur. It is also adds an inimitable twist to our highly popular Magnificent Mandarin.

products.name: Geraniol ex Palmarosa
products.description:
Geraniol is one of the four most common rose alcohols (along with phenyl ethyl alcohol, nerol and citronellol), present in all rose varieties. Geraniol naturally isolated from palmarosa (a grass native to India) is the finest quality available. It has a richness and complexity absent in synthetic products and it is the geraniol we use in all of our classical bases.

As well as forming a key part of a rose complex, geraniol adds freshness and lift to fragrances. It blends beautifully with Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon.

products.name: Geraniol Extra
products.description:
Geraniol is one of the four most common rose alcohols (along with phenyl ethyl alcohol, nerol and citronellol), present in all rose varieties. Geraniol Extra BASF, with > 98% purity, is the premium non-natural form of this material and makes an excellent cost-effective alternative to the more expensive natural isolate. For anything but the most luxurious fragrances and natural blends, we recommend this product over the natural.

As well as forming a key part of a rose complex, geraniol adds freshness and lift to fragrances. It blends beautifully with Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Citronellol 98, Rose Oxide Laevo, and Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon.

products.name: Geranium Bourbon “Supreme” Oil
products.description:
Geranium Bourbon or rose geranium is native to South Africa but it was transplanted to Réunion island (known as Île de Bourbon from 1665–1793) by the French colonists in the 1840s after natural disasters destroyed the coffee industry in 1806 and 1807. In time the importance of the Island in international trade fell and most geranium Bourbon is now produced on the neighbouring island of Madagascar, from whence this essential oil comes.

Our geranium Bourbon essential oil is, for all intents and purposes, the closest in scent you can find to the odour quality loved by the great perfumers of the 20th century who particularly enjoyed the balanced and easily managed green and floral scent. It is a key note in most of the earliest fougère fragrances.

products.name: Geranium Heart
products.description:
Everything harsh about geranium oil has been removed. No mint, no metallic edge, no green-leafy heaviness — just the soft rosy-floral heart and a clean fruity brightness reminiscent of pear and lychee. The result smells closer to rose water than to the geranium oil you know from the bottle.

This is the most subtle of the Heart range, designed to blend rather than dominate. It slips into floral accords without stamping its identity on the composition, adding warmth and rosiness in the background. In rose reconstructions, it bolsters the natural rose character more convincingly than citronellol or geraniol alone, with a complexity that single molecules cannot replicate.

The fruity facet opens territory that whole geranium oil cannot reach. Use it in fruit-floral accords where the pear-lychee quality bridges citrus and white flowers. It softens sharp green notes and warms aldehydic compositions. In masculine fougeres, it provides the rosy-geranium character at lower doses without the camphoraceous side effects of the whole oil.

products.name: Geranium Heart N.3
products.description:
Geranium Heart N.3 from LMR is the most sublime expression of geranium oil we have sampled. As with all LMR products we stock, the level of care and attention to detail that French grande dame of raw materials is apparent upon first sniff.

We stock Robertet's well-known and loved Geranium Heart also, but this LMR product is different. The Robertet product is bright, fresh and light, while the LMR oil is luscious, deep, and rich. You could most certainly utilise both in the same scent for your own special in-house geranium accord.

When I smell the Robertet product, I imagine a lovely English country garden after a summer shower; when I sniff the LMR, I see Turkish delight in a village candy-store. Geranium Heart N.3 is as much edible as Robertet Geranium Heart Egypt is fresh.

Our recommendation: buy both. But if you must pick only one, pick this one.

The N.3 in the product name refers to the stage of molecular distillation that the essential oil reaches before being done. This is a common method of naming for LMR.

products.name: Geranium Oil, China
products.description:
Geranium Oil, from Pelargonium graveolens, adds fresh green notes and a touch of rose-like sweetness. This makes it a key ingredient in numerous perfumes — particularly fougères. Its blend of floral and herbal tones gives balance and brightness.

Chinese geranium oil differs from Geranium Bourbon which is typically known for its rich, sweet rose smell with a minty hint. On the other hand, the Chinese variety has a sharper, greener scent with herbal undertones, so it works well in fresh blends. It is also a more budget-friendly option.

This oil works well with citrus, floral, and woody scents. It brightens top note blends based on lemon or bergamot, melds smoothly in the heart with rose or jasmine, and pairs beautifully with sandalwood or patchouli for a deep, rich base. Its versatility makes it a must-have for every perfumer. And of course our supplier, LMR, is world class so you know you're getting the absolute finest quality on the market.

products.name: Geranium Oil, Egypt
products.description:
Geranium Oil, from Pelargonium graveolens, adds fresh green notes and a touch of rose-like sweetness. This makes it a key ingredient in numerous perfumes — particularly fougères. Its blend of floral and herbal tones gives balance and brightness.

This marvellous Egyptian extract is sharper and fresher than the classic Bourbon type and has a more obviously citrus aspect. It's low cost should not be deemed to imply low quality, as this LMR version is really the finest on the market; so good, in fact, it is better than many Bourbon offerings from other manufacturers.

We also stock Chinese Geranium oil (fresh and herbal) and Geranium Bourbon (floral and rose-like).

products.name: Geranyl Acetate
products.description:
Geranyl Acetate is an ester of Geraniol, the classic rose alcohol. It has a lovely waxy fruity quality that makes it an excellent modifier of rose and jasmine materials. It also has hints of lavender, metal and mushrooms which explains why it suits so many different contexts.

The great Steffen Arctander (most famous for his commentary on naturals) describes it thus: “Widely used in perfume compositions as a sweetener and modifier in floral, fruity, herbaceous and citrusy fragrance types, usually at a modest level of one to five percent in the concentrated perfume oil but with great variations according to the purpose of its use. It blends well with Bergamot, Lavender, Rose, Muguet, Wallflower, Ylang-ylang, Neroli and even Leather, Oriental and other very complex fragrance types.”

products.name: Geranyl Acetone
products.description:
Geranyl Acetone (an unsaturated aliphatic ketone) opens with a penetrating freshness that immediately distinguishes it from its close relative, Geranyl Acetate. Where the acetate offers sweet, waxy rose with lavender hints, the acetone brings aldehydic brightness and a unique magnolia cream character. This material captures the elusive scent of magnolia petals—that perfect balance of citrusy freshness, creamy richness, and subtle green that makes the flower so prized yet difficult to recreate authentically.

This ketone excels where Geranyl Acetate might feel too sweet or heavy, particularly in modern compositions demanding transparency and lift. Its aldehydic facet provides natural diffusion without the soapy harshness of straight aldehydes, while the green-leafy notes prevent the cloying sweetness that plagues many floral reconstructions. Deploy it at 0.5-3% to transform flat rose accords into living bouquets, or use it as the cornerstone of magnolia compositions where authenticity matters more than intensity.

The synergy between Geranyl Acetone and Geranyl Acetate creates magic—combine them in a 1:2 ratio for unprecedented depth in rose accords. The acetate provides body and traditional rosy sweetness while the acetone adds sparkle, freshness, and that crucial magnolia cream note. Together they bridge the gap between vintage floral richness and contemporary transparency. Use this combination to create "rose complexes" that work equally well in fine fragrance and functiona

products.name: Geranyl Butyrate
products.description:
Geranyl butyrate opens with a sweet, fruity-floral burst—ripe apples wrapped in rose petals, with a tropical raspberry undertone that gives it immediate warmth. Beneath the fruit sits a soft, milky-waxy quality that rounds the edges. The overall effect is heavy but pleasant, with a richness that smaller geranyl esters lack.

This ester brings fruity sweetness with genuine floral dimension to compositions. Use it in apple accords where you want naturalness and depth, in tropical fruit blends for mango-pineapple-passion fruit effects, or in rose and muguet bases where the fruity facet adds a lush, living quality. It works particularly well in lavender compositions, where it contributes soft fruity undertones without competing with the herbal character.

Pair it with geraniol and rose materials for lush floral accords, or with tropical fruit esters and gamma-undecalactone for creamy, exotic fruit compositions.

products.name: Geranyl Formate
products.description:
Geranyl formate opens with an immediate impression of rose petals steeped in fresh tea—not the heavy, jammy rose of damascones but rather the crisp, almost transparent quality of wild roses after rain. This fresh rose character is interwoven with distinct neroli facets, creating an effect reminiscent of orange blossoms floating in rose water. The material's signature tea note isn't black tea's tannins but rather the fresh, green quality of white tea leaves. Dry, slightly choking green notes prevent any sweetness from developing, while subtle citrus-pear nuances add sparkling lift. The overall effect is remarkably diffusive—it seems to expand and fill space with its fresh complexity.

Utilise Geranyl formate at 1-20% when you need fresh, diffusive rose effects without heaviness or sweetness. Its moderate tenacity and middle note classification make it ideal for creating sophisticated fresh florals that maintain presence without becoming cloying. In rose compositions, it provides the elusive "fresh rose" quality that's difficult to achieve with traditional rose materials alone. For neroli reconstructions, it bridges the gap between citrus top notes and indolic heart notes beautifully. The material excels in cologne-type fragrances where its diffusive freshness and tea-like dryness create modern sophistication. In muguet and other white florals, it adds green freshness without the harshness of typical green materials.

The structural difference between Geranyl formate and Gerany

products.name: Geranyl Propionate
products.description:
Geranyl Propionate opens with an immediate burst of sweet, fruity rosiness that feels lighter and more diffusive than typical rose esters. This ethereal quality—what Arctander called "more etheric" than geranyl acetate—creates a floating sensation where rose petals seem suspended in grape juice. The distinctive grape facet isn't heavy or jammy but rather fresh and translucent, like crushed white grapes. Waxy undertones add smoothness and sophistication, while subtle balsamic warmth prevents the sweetness from becoming cloying. Fresh green-leafy notes provide natural lift, connecting the material to its geranium heritage.

Deploy Geranyl Propionate at 0.5-5% when you need fruity lift in floral compositions without heaviness. Its moderate tenacity and heart note classification make it ideal for bridging sparkling top notes with deeper base materials. Use it to add ethereal sweetness to rose accords where geranyl acetate might feel too soft or predictable. In lilac and lily of the valley reconstructions, it provides essential fruity-floral brightness. The distinctive grape nuance makes it invaluable for creating sophisticated fruity-florals—think rose-grape, gardenia-fruit, or passionflower effects. In functional fragrances, it performs exceptionally well in fabric softeners and detergents where its diffusive quality ensures immediate impact despite potential heat exposure during use.

While closely related to Geranyl Acetate, Geranyl Propionate offers distinct advantages for sp

products.name: German Chamomile “Signature” Oil
products.description:
German chamomile bears an intense ink-blue colour (hence its nickname of blue chamomile or chamomile blue oil). It has wonderfully sweet notes making it a hidden gourmand treasure.

Our German chamomile is from a single estate in England, a nation that is regarded as the finest source of this oil. Unlike most commercial blue chamomiles which can be quite heavy, ours practically dances. It is delicate and refined - a real treasure. We love this quality of oil so much that it is the only German chamomile we use in our products. The care that has gone in to the manufacture of this essential oil is obvious from first sniff. 

Once you have tried our German Chamomile “Signature” Oil, you will be a convert for life.

If you are wondering, the difference between the German and Roman chamomile plants is that German chamomile flowers grow in clusters, while Roman chamomile flowers grow singularly atop a hairy stem.

We also stock a wonderful Roman chamomile oil.

Origin: England
Variety: matricaria recutita
Part: Flower heads
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Ginger "Top Note" CO2, P. Jungle Essence
products.description:
The prestigious V. MANE Fils offers two ginger Pure Jungle Essences (CO2 extracts). They are this Ginger "Top Note" CO2 with dazzling bright top notes, and the rich, Dark Ginger CO2, a heart / base note variety.

This material opens with an explosive burst of fresh-cut ginger that hits you immediately with sharp, lemony brightness. The effervescent quality feels alive and electric, capturing the exact moment when you slice open a fresh rhizome. Nothing about this extract feels cooked or processed—it's pure, vibrant ginger in its most energetic form.

You'll find this CO2 extract transforms compositions by adding incredible lifting power and naturalistic warmth simultaneously. Unlike steam-distilled ginger oil, which carries heavier cooked notes, this fractionated extract isolates only the brightest volatile compounds. Use it to energise woody bases, cut through rich florals, or create sophisticated gourmand accords where authentic ginger character matters most.

The persistence surprises many perfumers—while it functions as a brilliant top note, it maintains presence throughout the heart. Combine with citrus for explosive freshness, pair with pink pepper for modern spice blends, or use alongside vanilla for authentic gingerbread effects. This extract bridges traditional spice work with contemporary perfumery's demand for hyper-realistic naturals.

We recommend a pairing of this top note ginger CO2 with Payan Bertrand's dazzlingly citrus-fresh Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire,

products.name: Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire
products.description:
This is, in our opinion, the finest fresh ginger essential oil you will ever experience. Once again the master distillers at Payan Bertrand have managed to capture the very soul of the plant in producing this masterpiece of perfumery art — and it's not a CO2 or molecular distillation!

When compared against the far more common Ginger Fresh (or fraiche) essential oils from Indonesia, Madagascar and China, this Ivorian oil is not just a step up… it is a total reinvention of what ginger oil should be. Smelling this oil is like smelling ginger for the first time. It will take your breath away.

Ivory Coast ginger has all the expected character of fresh ginger but with a whole extra layer of dazzle. There is no dustiness here (often characteristic of poor quality oil) just pure effulgent ginger.

2026 Update: due to weather events in the region, this oil has more than doubled in price. We hope to see a drop in the future but for now we have had to increase the cost accordingly.

products.name: Ginger Oil Fresh, Madagascar
products.description:
This exceptional essential oil opens with an explosive burst of sparkling, fizzy freshness that immediately energises your compositions. The initial citrusy-lemony effervescence, reminiscent of verbena or crushed lemongrass, provides tremendous lift and radiance. Unlike typical ginger oils, the finest Madagascar qualities reveal an unexpected floral heart with distinct rose and geranium facets.

What sets this material apart is its "Blue Ginger" chemotype containing geranyl acetate—a rare component that bridges spicy and floral families with remarkable elegance. Fresh distillation from rhizomes harvested within hours preserves delicate aldehydes while preventing the harsh, turpentine-like notes found in oils from dried material. This creates a clean, sophisticated warmth devoid of earthy off-notes.

Use it strategically as an olfactory binder to create seamless transitions between different fragrance families. It excels at cutting through excessive sweetness in gourmand compositions while adding sophisticated contrast to heavy ambery bases. The material's complete olfactory journey—from vibrant citrus opening through complex spicy-floral heart to warm woody-gourmand drydown—functions as a "perfume-in-itself" that enriches entire compositions from initial spray to final moments on skin.

Madagascar vs Ivory Coast and CO2

Madagascar ginger oil differs significantly from other origins and extraction methods. Ivory Coast ginger oil delivers a more direct, powerfully peppery char

products.name: Givescone®
products.description:
When is a damascone not a damascone? When it's Givescone! To the untrained nose it would be easy to presume that this sticky and fruity chemical is part of the rose ketone family, but it isn't. As a consequence it can be thrown in your scents with gay abandon. It has no IFRA restriction at all.

The author of Perfumery: Techniques in evolution describes it as “a well known chemical that is difficult to describe. It has many nuances of the damascones and damascenone, but is less sharp-metallic and has more of a sweet-apple note. It combines very well with undecavertol[.]”

Givescone is used at 0.2% in My Way (2020) by Armani where it enhances the fruitiness of a blend of damascones and raspberry ketone. A larger 0.8% is found in Kurkdjian's Gentle Fluidity Gold (2019) backed up by a massive 38% of sweet musks Helvetolide and Tonalide.

“The tall striped tulips stood straight up upon their stalks, like long rows of soldiers, and looked defiantly across the grass at the roses, and said: We are quite as splendid as you are now. The purple butterflies fluttered about with gold dust on their wings, visiting each flower in turn; the little lizards crept out of the crevices of the wall, and lay basking in the white glare; and the pomegranates split and cracked with the heat, and showed their bleeding red hearts.” — Oscar Wilde, The Birthday of the Infanta.

products.name: Globalide
products.description:
Globalide belongs to the macrocyclic musk family, with a clean, modern character. Its particular quality is warmth and creaminess: a waxy, powdery musk with sandalwood-like facets that sits close to the skin and wraps the wearer rather than projecting outward. There is a soapy, clean-linen quality without the intense metallic "hot iron" bite of its close relative Habanolide.

That creamy, soft-focus character makes it especially effective in skin-scent compositions and intimate fragrances where the musk should feel like an extension of the wearer rather than an announcement. It blends naturally with lactonic materials, soft woods like Iso E Super and cashmeran, and floral hearts where it provides a warm, seamless base. Even below one per cent of a formula, its influence on the drydown is substantial.

Globalide and Habanolide share the same base molecule but are manufactured differently, and the result is a genuine olfactory distinction. Habanolide is more radiant, metallic, and bright — the "hot iron" pressed-linen character that gives compositions lift and transparency. Globalide is creamier, waxier, more powdery, and more diffuse — it wraps and softens where Habanolide illuminates. The choice depends on whether you want your musk to radiate or to envelop.

The individual isomers of Globalide/Habanolide-type musks can be distinguished under suitable GCMS conditions. In our finished-perfume GCMS work, however, these peaks elute very close together and are not resolved clearl

products.name: Globanone®
products.description:
Globanone is an elegant and underrated macrocyclic musk that is solid at room temperature so we offer it here at 50% dilution in DPG or pure. Closely related to the well-known Velvione (the Givaudan copy of the vastly superior Ambretone from Takagasco), globanone is cost effective and an essential musk for perfumers.

Globanone offers a fresh, less animalic profile compared to Velvione, while still maintaining elegance. Both musks share a similar behaviour, though Globanone’s affordability makes it the practical choice. Exceptionally stable in detergent powders, it also burns beautifully, making it ideal for agarbati and bakhoor fragrances.

NOTE: pure globanone solidifies at low temperatures.

products.name: Gnidia Flower Absolute
products.description:
Once again V. MANE Fils hits a home run with this marvellous and unusual floral absolute. Gnidia has one of the highest amounts of natural maltol and it is very obvious. With an odour somewhat resembling stewed bananas, flowers and brown sugar this is a truly novel material for perfumer's who seek something extraordinary.

According to MANE, “The multifaceted scent of the flowers unveils notes of narcissus, violet, cucumber, tea, and tuberose. The extract contains natural maltol, which brings a note of delicious sweetness.” The Gnidia flowers are hand picked by two associations of women living in Madagascar.

We offer this incredible product from V. MANE Fils at 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. Undiluted the material has a thick paste-like consistency that requires warmth to liquify.

Origin: Madagascar
Part: Flowers
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Grape Butyrate
products.description:
Grape Butyrate opens with a delicate, airy fruitiness - think fresh grape skin with a tart green-apple edge and a whisper of wine. It sits between ethereal and fleshy, never loud, offering a quiet juiciness that reads as unmistakably natural. The overall impression is of freshly pressed white grape juice touched with tropical pineapple.

This is a workhorse nuance material rather than a headline note. Add it to fruity-floral accords to inject convincing freshness without synthetic sharpness, or blend it with methyl anthranilate to build a complete Concord grape effect. Its hydroxyl group gives it better tenacity than most fruit esters - expect around four hours on a blotter - bridging the gap between fleeting citrus top notes and the heavier floral heart.

Try it in wine or cognac reconstructions alongside ethyl lactate and damascenone for a rich fermentation effect. In tropical accords, pair it with ethyl butyrate to create a full pineapple-juice impact that neither material achieves alone. Use it at low levels in citrus compositions for a dewy, freshly peeled quality you won't get from terpenes.

products.name: Grapefruit Base 184062 D
products.description:
Grapefruit Base hits the nose with an immediate sharp citrus burst — zesty, bitter, and unmistakably grapefruit. It captures both the juicy freshness of the flesh and the aromatic bite of the peel. The effect is brighter and cleaner than natural grapefruit oil, without any of the sulphurous off-notes that plague the natural.

The real advantage here is performance. Natural grapefruit oil fades fast and develops unpleasant sulphurous undertones as it ages. This base avoids both problems entirely, giving you reliable grapefruit character that lasts. Use it as the core of any citrus accord, or add it to floral compositions where you want a sparkling, bitter-fresh lift.

Build a full grapefruit accord by combining this base with Methyl Pamplemousse for added juiciness, or pair it with nootkatone for extra depth and persistence. It layers well with bergamot and neroli for a complex hesperidic opening. Try it against pink pepper or cardamom for a modern spicy-citrus contrast.

184062 D vs 015794 R

This is Firmenich's 184062 D, not the older 015794 R. Both are synthetic grapefruit bases, but the 184062 D incorporates Firmenich captive molecules not found in the earlier version. The result is a smoother, more stable base with broader application versatility, while the 015794 R is sharper and more raw-peel in character. If you've used the 015794 R before, expect the 184062 D to be more polished and better behaved in formulation — particularly in applications where stability matters.

products.name: Grapefruit Heart
products.description:
Grapefruit is one of the most recognisable citrus notes in perfumery and one of the hardest to sustain. Standard grapefruit oil blazes brilliantly for twenty minutes and then vanishes. Grapefruit Heart solves that problem. This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction designed to boost the grapefruit profile of your formula, even at very low dosage.

LMR describes it as juicy and bitter-fruity with a hint of sulphurous undertone — that distinctive metallic, almost tropical edge that separates grapefruit from every other citrus. Here it is cleaner, more focused, and far more tenacious than the standard oil. A small amount provides grapefruit character that conventional oil cannot sustain past the first half hour.

Use it alongside our Grapefruit Oil Pink for a complete grapefruit statement — the pink oil gives natural breadth and juicy sweetness in the opening, the Heart extends it into the heart and beyond. Essential for any serious citrus composition, aquatic accord, or fresh fragrance that needs grapefruit to last.

products.name: Grapefruit Oil 5 Fold
products.description:
Standard grapefruit oil is almost entirely limonene — pleasant but generic. This 5-fold version is still mostly limonene, but vacuum distillation has concentrated everything else roughly fivefold. Those trace compounds are what make grapefruit smell like grapefruit, and now they come through with real authority.

With the character compounds amplified, you get the woody-bitter quality that links grapefruit to vetiver, the bright aldehydic sparkle, and the subtle sulphurous-tropical facet that gives grapefruit its identity. The oil is stronger and more persistent than standard cold-pressed grapefruit. Far more useful in fine fragrance.

Pair it with vetiver for a natural woody-citrus accord, with bergamot and neroli for a sophisticated citrus heart, or with black pepper and cedarwood for modern masculine compositions. It still functions as a topnote, so layer it over longer-lasting base materials. Worth every penny of the premium over standard oil.

We also stock 10-folded orange Oil, terpeneless orange, terpeneless Lemon oil, and terpeneless Bergamot oil.

products.name: Grapefruit Oil, Pink
products.description:
Pink grapefruit opens brighter and sweeter than its white counterpart. The bitter, almost quinine-like edge of white grapefruit is dialled back here, replaced by a rounder, juicier, almost berry-tinged citrus that feels more approachable from the first sniff. The colour difference in the fruit translates directly to the oil.

Where white grapefruit excels in sharp masculine colognes, pink grapefruit moves naturally toward fruity-floral and feminine territory. It bridges citrus and fruit accords in a way that few other naturals can — try it alongside peach, raspberry, or blackcurrant materials and the results feel effortless. The characteristic sulphurous bite underneath the sweetness keeps it honest and unmistakably grapefruit.

Use it generously as a sparkling top note. It pairs beautifully with rose, neroli, and white florals where you want citrus freshness without the austerity of lemon or the heaviness of orange. A natural companion to our Grapefruit Heart for extended citrus impact through the drydown.

Note: This oil is rectified to reduce furocoumarins and fortified with a trace of natural tocopherol to extend its life on the shelf. That gives it an IFRA category 4 usage of a whop[ing 40% rather than the typical 4% for grapefruit oils.

products.name: Grapefruit Oil, White
products.description:
Despite the enormous popularity of grapefruit notes in perfumes (usually through the use of Methyl Pamplemousse), the essential oil is less often seen in mainstream scents though masterpieces such as Bleu and Égoĩste by Chanel both incorporate the natural oil and Dolce & Gabanna Light Blue has 1%.

This grapefruit oil from the United States is robust and rich. Oftentimes grapefruit can be disappointingly thin but Payan Bertrand once again has perfected the extraction process and this oil is outstanding.

Because this is American oil, it has far less of the bitterness associated with European grapefruit oils. It blends beautifully with our Pomelo Grandis base, Methyl Pamplemousse and Thiocineole when an extra bitter note is wanted.

Note: This oil is rectified to reduce furocoumarins and fortified with a trace of natural tocopherol to extend its life on the shelf.

products.name: Greencatcher™
products.description:
Arguably the finest producer of naturals in the world today, V. MANE Fils also produces a few very special bases. Greencatcher™ is one such. Built around an overdose of the MANE captive Bigarane™ and containing absolutely no sensitising materials, this base is pure magic. 

Greencatcher™ is not just another green base loaded with the usual suspects of Cis 3 Hexenol and its esters, instead it is fruity, woody, tropical and incredibly addictive. This is one of those rare products that upon first sniff triggers an instant desire to create with it.

Blends with Celestafleur™, Cassis base, Rose Oxide Laevo, Robertet's natural Cucumber and pineapple are sublime. Also blends with most green materials and fresh or fruity chemicals. Use it to add a twist to Amazonia™ and Verdantol™ or just put a drop on a smelling strip and enjoy it all day long.

products.name: Grenoble Pyrazine
products.description:
Grenoble Pyrazine is intensely walnut-like. It has a distinct "green," oily, and slightly tannic bitterness that smells like the papery skin on a raw peanut or a fresh walnut. It also has a "burnt sugar" or dark caramel undertone that is less "clean" than the related materials Praslin and Torref Pyrazine.

Grenoble Pyrazine opens with powerful nut-skin character—that slightly bitter, papery quality of freshly roasted peanuts and walnuts. Unsweetened cocoa facets follow, dry and powdery rather than sweet. A warm peanut butter richness dominates the heart, while savoury corn chip and roasted grain notes add nostalgic edibility. The overall effect is snack-like and comforting.

This pyrazine forms naturally during the Maillard reaction when sugars and amino acids meet heat. You'll find it in roasted peanuts, cocoa, coffee, grilled meats, and toasted grains. The high odour strength demands respect—evaluate at 0.1% dilution or less. It anchors gourmand compositions with genuine roasted warmth, particularly where nut or peanut butter effects are needed. Coffee and chocolate accords benefit from its unsweetened cocoa depth.

Use Grenoble Pyrazine at 0.02–0.2% in your concentrate. Despite its short substantivity on blotter (under 3 hours), it performs well in finished compositions. It blends beautifully with vanillin, lactones, and coffee materials for realistic gourmand effects. Works in tobacco and leather contexts where savoury warmth adds sophistication.

Grenoble, Praslin, and T

products.name: Grisalva
products.description:
Grisalva captures the character of natural ambergris with striking fidelity — warm, animalic, and immediately recognisable. Dry leathery facets sit beneath the ambergris body, with a slight metallic edge adding complexity. The overall impression is of deep warmth radiating from the base of a composition.

The defining quality here is diffusion — Grisalva projects ambergris character through an entire composition even at trace levels. Over 48 hours on blotter tells you this is a material that defines the drydown. Use it in amber accords, orientals, and woody bases where you want warmth that carries.

Pair with ambroxan and labdanum for a complete ambergris accord, or use alone to give woody and floral compositions a warm animalic foundation. The leathery facet strengthens chypre and tobacco blends. Even the smallest additions generate enormous presence — dose in traces and let the diffusion do the work.

products.name: Grojsman Plus
products.description:
In 1990 IFF perfumer Sophia Grojsman changed the face of perfumery when she created Trésor for Lâncome with an accord which overdosed four materials (Hedione®, Galaxolide®, Gamma Methyl Ionone and Iso E Super™). In so doing she created a canvas style accord (nicknamed a "hug me" accord) which can be used as the basis for virtually any type of perfume.

What we present here is that great accord in a low-ionone form with Paradise Molecule® and discreet enhancements to add radiance and extend longevity. This is the ultimate Grojsman accord and it can be used at up to 55% of your finished fragrance. Just add your favourite blend or base to Grojsman Plus and you have a complete modern perfume.

See the formula below for our re-envisioning of Guerlain's Champs Élysées (1996) fragrance to understand how to work with this base.

products.name: Guaiac Wood Oil
products.description:
Pure classical guaiac wood (pronounced “gwy-ack”) essential oil is getting more difficult to obtain these days and recently Robertet has discontinued their rectified or so-called "heart" fraction which, while beautiful, lacked the entire spectrum of the wood that was loved by the great perfumers of days gone by.

We are offering here the finest single origin (Paraguay) true guaiac wood in all its glory, completely unchanged by post-processing. Upon smelling this wood for the first time you may be surprised just how rich and luxurious it is. If you only know guaiac essential oil in its fractionated form, you are in for a real treat.

Guaiac, in addition to its smoky and woody scent also has facets of spice and tea rose. It is a very versatile natural and is indispensable when making an Oud accord.

This product is solid in pure form and needs heating to liquify. For convenience we also sell it at 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate to render it easier to use.

Pure Guaiac Wood Oil (Bulnesia sarmientoi) is a CITES appendix II product. In most countries this can be lawfully traded without extra paperwork if purchased for personal use. We recommend checking in advance with your own regulatory bodies.

If you are purchasing pure Guaiac Wood Oil for commercial reasons you may need a CITES re-export or origin certificate to accompany your purchase. Again, you should check with your national authorities. We charge $60 USD for this certificate and it takes approximately ten days

products.name: Guaiacol
products.description:
Guaiacol is a wonderfully smoky, vanilla and phenolic chemical which can contribute enormously to a natural vanilla type base when blended with Vanillin or Ethyl Vanillin.

Use it for a smoke note when Birch Tar is a little too powerful for your needs or exploit its phenolic qualities in an otherworldly modernist scent.

Guaiacol is very powerful so you may wish to dilute it to 10% or even 1%.

products.name: Guaiyl Acetate
products.description:
Guaiyl Acetate is a lovely soft floral woody material resulting from the acetylation of Guaiacwood oil. It is a perfect material for extending and fixing rose bases (especially tea rose) owing to its complex nuance of rose, spice and wood.

Guaiyl Acetate also works as an alternative or supplement to Vetiveryl Acetate which is quite restricted in use under IFRA 51.

NOTE: Guaiyl Acetate (also associated with CAS 61789-17-1) is an acetylation of fractions of natural guaiacwood oil and so, like vetiveryl acetate, it derives from a number of alcohols (principally guaiol and bulnesol). Guaiol Acetate (CAS 134-28-1) is the acetylation of the pure guaiol molecule. Guaiyl acetate is more complex, with soft, sweet, spicy and slightly smoky notes in addition to the usual tea rose found in both.

Blends very well with Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Rose Crystals, and Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon as well as all Rose Bases.

products.name: Guava Base 270237
products.description:
Guava Base 270237 hits you with an unmistakable wave of ripe tropical guava. There's a dry-sweet tartness that reads as realistic rather than candied, balanced by juicy mango-like warmth. Sharp catty undertones give it the same pungent bite found in the real fruit.

Even at low levels this base punches through a blend, adding instant tropical recognisability. It works especially well in fruity-floral top notes where you need realistic guava without building the accord from scratch. Think of it as a shortcut to tropical authenticity.

Combine with Passion Fruit Base 109223 and peach for layered tropical complexity. Bergamot brightens the guava's tartness beautifully, while cassis base adds complementary catty depth when you blend both. A small addition transforms any fruity accord.

products.name: Guided Smelling Experience
products.description:
We offer a deluxe sit-down smelling experience at our workshop in Lower Hutt (15 minutes from Wellington City). Discover our entire range of raw materials and see how the business operates. 

Visit prices starts from $80 US for thirty minutes. During the experience you will be accompanied by a trained member of staff who will assist you. You will have access to all of our raw materials (including many that we don't list on the website).

This is a perfect opportunity to get advice, make notes on materials you may want to purchase or simply spend time with like minded lovers of the fragrance industry.

As a bonus we have an extensive collection of historic and luxury fragrances which you may sample at your leisure. We have perfumes from Creed, Clive Christian, Chanel, Dior, Coty, Guerlain and many more.

When you purchase we will contact you to arrange a time that is most suitable for you. This experience is available from Monday to Saturday inclusive.

Light refreshments are provided for bookings of 60 minutes or greater.

products.name: Gulab Attar
products.description:
A rich, jammy damask rose over soft, creamy sandalwood — Gulab Attar is the classical Indian co-distillate, produced in Kannauj by the traditional deg-bhapka method. The rose reads honeyed and lush, with faint spicy and green facets. Sandalwood sits underneath, giving body to the rose without muting it.

In blends it works as the anchor of classical Indian floral accords. Use it as the central note in rose soliflores, as the rose voice in mukhallats, or to give warmth and body to oriental rose-oud structures. It also enriches modern rose fragrances that feel thin at the base.

Pair with oud and saffron for a mukhallat base, or use alongside labdanum, benzoin and a trace of clove for an amber-rose oriental. In a soliflore it carries the rose without needing a separate fixative. Undiluted the sandalwood reads heaviest; in dilution the rose opens up properly.

products.name: Gurjun Balsam Oil
products.description:
Gurjun Balsam Oil is a mild oil distilled from the pathological resin of the Dipterocarpus turbinatus tree. Despite its light odour, it is a very useful wood oil for blending stronger wood notes and setting a delicate background when something more interesting than Iso E Super is called for.

With a gentle spice running through it and a very long drydown (over 400 hours!) it is an excellent fixative that blends with a great variety of other materials - including florals. Use it with Guaiyl Acetate and Cypriol for the beginnings of your very own luscious agarwood accord. 

Gjurjun Balsam Oil features in Tom Ford's Black Orchid fragrance, Duro and Baraonda by Nasomatto, Kilian's Apple Brandy and M7 by YSL. It also contributes to the wonderful Oud character of Dahn Oudh Al Shams by Ajmal.

products.name: Habanolide®
products.description:
Habanolide® is considered a metallic or hot iron musk. It is a macrocyclic musk of the highest quality by Firmenich, indispensable and certainly irreplaceable (though Globalide® by Symrise is frequently touted as such, but that does have its differences). Habanolide® is a radiant musk which adds freshness and vitality.

Habanolide® has featured in numerous modern scents. The writers of Scent and Chemistry give by way of example Silver Mist (2006) by Alessandro Gualtieri for Nasomatto, in which it makes up 25% of the fragrance:

250 Habanolide
250 Ethylene Brassylate
125 Scentolide
25 Cashmeran
10 Exaltone

products.name: Harsingar Attar
products.description:
Of all the attars, Harsingar is the one that most smells like a complete fragrance. This is a blended attar, combining rich Indian Mysore Sandalwood with natural floral extracts and aroma chemicals.

Harsingar attar opens with a sweet, intensely floral aroma somewhere between jasmine sambac and orange blossom. A clean, soapy brightness lifts the top before honeyed warmth and gentle animalic depth take over. You get creamy, woody softness from the sandalwood base throughout.

Use harsingar attar as an exotic floral heart in your oriental compositions where its jasmine-orange blossom character adds unexpected sophistication. It blends beautifully with oud, rose, and tuberose to create richly layered Indian-inspired accords. The built-in sandalwood base gives you fixative depth from the start.

Try it alongside champaca and frangipani for an opulent tropical floral bouquet. Add benzoin or frankincense to push it toward a meditative incense direction. This attar works as a finished perfume by itself, but give it space to interact with other materials and you unlock something extraordinary.

products.name: Hawthorn Extra
products.description:
Hawthorn Extra is the wonderful classic De Laire Aubepine Extra base. Under IFRA regulations the key synthetic material used to create this base (anisaldehyde) was heavily restricted. Under IFRA 51 that restriction has been considerably relaxed and consequently it is now possible, once again, to exploit this magnificent floral scent (up to 4.4% of your finished product).

Having use of Hawthorn Extra allows perfumers to add an interesting colour and nuance to perfumes that have been all but forced to rely on muguet and lilac florals due to regulations and prohibitions. We are thrilled to put this base back in the spotlight where it belongs.

The scent of hawthorn (also known as May flower) shares much in common with lilac but with a distinctly anisic / almond quality. In May, a profusion of hawthorn blossoms soak the air with their gourmand aroma. Hawthorn Extra allows you to recreate that magical moment of nature in your perfumes.

“Ne'er cast a cloot til Mey's oot!”

products.name: Hay “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Hay absolute, otherwise known as foin or foin coupé (literally meaning "cut hay") is one of the most beautiful of all the absolutes. Critic Chandler Burr said: "One of the most sublime of all perfume materials. Hay is, as literally as possible, the smell of liquid summer sunlight." Combined with our stunning classic Foin Coupé base and a fond of green oakmoss and lavender "Avice Hill", you have the tools for truly remarkable fragrances.

In addition to the expected coumarin notes, this absolute from the high French Alps is fruity, tobacco like, sweet and radiant. In traces it imparts a special je ne sais quoi, and in larger amounts it can become the star of the show.

Steffan Arctander had this to say: "Hay absolute is used in perfumery not only in “new mown hay” bases, or in combination with flouve, melilotus, tonka, woodruff, deertongue, etc., but also as an individual note to be introduced whenever a truly herbaceous-sweet undertone is required: in lavender, fougere, chypre, colognes, tea-notes, tabac-notes, forest notes and various bouquets."

Because hay absolute is so thick, we now optionally supply it at 10% dilution in Triethyl Citrate Natural making it ISO 9235 compliant. This product will replace our previous hay sold at 50% dilution. 

If you are seeking a similar product with a different profile, we also offer Flouve “Signature” Absolute (an IG Pays de Grasse product).

Origin: France, High Alps
Part: Dried leaves
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Hay “Super Premium” Absolute
products.description:
An extraordinary evolution of hay absolute, this Super Premium edition captures the very essence of golden fields at their peak ripeness. Where our V. MANE Fils Signature Hay Absolute evokes liquid summer sunlight, this LMR produced gold hay transcends into pure solar opulence - a more intensely coumarinic experience that borders on the divine.

This exceptional absolute from select parcels in the high French Alps presents an amplified gourmand character that sets it apart. The coumarin heart pulses with unprecedented richness, revealing layers of caramelised honey, vanilla-touched tobacco leaf, and sun-warmed tonka bean. The familiar fruity radiance of hay is here transformed into something more indulgent - think dried figs and golden raisins nestled in fresh-cut grass.

The gourmand facets make this absolute particularly suited for:

Oriental compositions seeking herbaceous depth

Modern fougères requiring extra warmth and sweetness

Tobacco accords demanding authentic hay-cured richness

Gourmand creations needing natural sweetness without sugar molecules

Luxury bases where only the most precious materials will suffice

You will appreciate how this Super Premium edition bridges the gap between green and amber families with remarkable finesse. Its enhanced coumarinic profile provides exceptional longevity and sillage, whilst maintaining the authentic hay character that makes this material irreplaceable.

Like our Signature edition, this absolute is available at 10% dilutio

products.name: Hazelnut CO2
products.description:
Open the bottle and you smell freshly roasted hazelnuts — warm, creamy, unmistakable. There is praline sweetness, a buttery depth, and the faintest coffee-like warmth underneath. The CO2 extraction captures the full roasted character with remarkable fidelity to the real thing.

This is the alcohol-soluble fraction — the fats and waxes stripped away, leaving behind only what carries the scent. It dissolves cleanly in perfumer's alcohol for direct use in fine fragrance. Build praline accords, chocolate-nut compositions, and gourmand bases around it.

Pair with tonka bean and vanilla for praline effects, with coffee CO2 for a hazelnut latte accord, or with cocoa absolute for something approaching Nutella in a bottle. We also stock Filbertone — the single molecule that defines hazelnut character — for when you need just a trace.

products.name: Hedione®
products.description:
There is only one type of Hedione® a perfumer should use: Firmenich manufactured hedione. The rest are inferior and nothing comes even close. 

First used in Eau Sauvage (1966, formula below) by Edmond Roudnitstka (1.8%) Hedione is now ubiquitous, being found in virtually all fragrances today. It boosts citrus (in particular lemon), and adds a radiance and beauty that nothing else can match. From mere traces to overdose, Hedione is indispensable. 

 Also known as methyl dihydrojasmonate.

products.name: Hedione® High Cis
products.description:
Hedione HC (High Cis) is a version of Hedione which is specially enriched with a higher amount of the favoured cis isomer which gives Hedione its characteristic power, bloom and radiance. Despite the higher cis isomer content, Hedione high cis is less radiant than the regular molecule due to the overall makeup of the product, nevertheless it has a beautiful enriching quality and is still an incredibly valuable product. 

Hedione High Cis is a common choice of Chanel perfumers in their modern fragrances where they often pair it with Muscenone Delta and Exaltone crystals.

Hedione and hedione HC are delicate chemicals with a beautiful nuance of magnolia blossoms and jasmine.

We also stock regular Hedione®, also from Firmenich. And for something truly glorious, check out our Paradise Molecule®, the closest thing you can get to Firmenich's captive Paradisone.

products.name: Helional®
products.description:
Helional® from IFF really needs no introduction. It is a classic chemical used to impart a sense of cool water, ocean air, and delicate white florals.

It is indispensable to the modern perfumer and is found in numerous fragrances that have been highly successful as our demo formulas below will attest.

Helional works beautifully in blends with Amazonia, Cyclamen Aldehyde, Floralozone, Florhydral, Calone Plus, Cis Jasmone all the muguet bases, Celestafleur and the green chemicals.

products.name: Heliotrope Flowers, Natural
products.description:
Heliotrope notes are difficult to obtain within natural perfumery as the high cost and potential misuse of the raw materials put them out of reach of most. That's where our 100% natural Heliotrope Flowers base comes in.

Built around a heart of the most wonderful natural isolates, including the much sought after natural heliotropin (piperonal), with resins, luxurious and costly floral oils and a sympathetic and truly perfumistic approach to natural bases, Heliotrope Flowers is the only heliotrope product you need.

In traces this base adds anisic sweetness, in overdose it is a complete floral bouquet.

products.name: Heliotropin 20% DPG
products.description:
Our synthetic heliotropin is a high purity food grade quality, surpassing virtually all synthetic forms on the market right now.

Heliotropin (piperonal) is the classic material used in perfume since the late 1800s to represent the odour of heliotrope flowers. It is also excellent when blended with coumarin and vanilla and adds a wonderfully different sweet nuance to fragrances. It has a quiet anisic quality to it and blends very well with anisic aldehyde as demonstrated by Jean Carles in his fragrance Canoe (1936) for Jean Patou.

Because heliotropin (piperonal) is restricted by the DEA in the USA and in most countries at varying levels, we sell this product diluted. While it was previously sold at 50% we are now selling it at 20% to match the requirements of US customs. If you have a license to import this to your country we can sell it pure.

If crystallisation occurs in colder climes, gentle heating may be required to bring this product back to solution.

We also stock a 100% natural form of this product.

Note: This product contains a diluted form of a regulated chemical and is sold in accordance with NZ regulations. Not for synthesis or diversion.

Thai regulations: heliotropin is, according to notification B.E. 2568 (No 3) of the Thai Ministry of Health, officially exempt from restrictions in perfume use to a finished product level of 1%. More information can be found here.

products.name: Heliotropin Natural 20% TEC
products.description:
This is a simple solution of 20% pure natural heliotropin crystals in natural triethyl citrate. We dilute it to this level to make it easier for US based customers to purchase legally due to DEA requirements in that place.

Heliotropin will contribute a wonderfully sweet and powdery effect to your fragrances and it blends beautifully with other crystallines such as natural Vanillin ex Clove and natural Coumarin ex Cassia.

For a full flower option we offer a synthetic Fleur D'Heliotrope base and additionally a rich 100% natural base called Heliotrope Flowers; both are loaded with natural absolutes and oils and exemplify the full beauty of the heliotrope flower in bloom.

Note: May require gentle heat as this material may crystallise in cold temperatures.

Note: This product contains a diluted form of a regulated chemical and is sold in accordance with NZ regulations. Not for synthesis or diversion.

Thai regulations: heliotropin is, according to notification B.E. 2568 (No 3) of the Thai Ministry of Health, officially exempt from restrictions in perfume use to a finished product level of 1%. More information can be found here.

products.name: Heliotropin Repl X24
products.description:
According to European regulators, Heliotropin (Piperonal) is going to receive a new classification of "toxic to reproduction (Repr. 1B; H360FD)." The result of this change is that  the European government may ban European perfumers and those selling in to Europe from using Heliotropin in their fragrances in any quantity. At this stage IFRA agrees with the reclassification but, as with Lyral, does not intend to prohibit or restrict heliotropin.

Because of this, we have created Heliotropin Repl X24, a marvellous base that stands in as a one for one replacer for heliotropin, offering all the same benefits of that material without the regulatory barriers. Start to use it now in your fragrances and you won't even blink an eye if the potential prohibition comes into action.

Heliotropin Repl X24 is beautiful in its own right and offers a lovely powdery note that can be used to supplement vanilla or tonka bean notes, or as a support for modern violet and iris scents.

Note: This product contains NO heliotropin (piperonal), Anisic Aldehyde or Benzaldehyde.

products.name: Helvetolide®
products.description:
Helvetolide® is one of the few musks that can be perceived not just in the dry down but also in the top notes of a fragrance. It is considered a radiant (like the rose ketones) and even traces can have enormous impact on a perfume.

Having a delicate nuance of pears, this musk is an excellent addition to gourmand type fragrances.

Combine Helvetolide with our highly popular Pear Belle base, or blend it with other musks to increase their power and diffusion.

products.name: Herbac®
products.description:
Herbac offers a powerful, fresh aroma characterised by distinct woody, herbal, and camphoraceous notes, enriched with hints of eucalyptus, mint, and cedar leaf. Its sharp, invigorating scent evokes coniferous freshness, making it ideal for capturing outdoor, nature-inspired impressions.

Herbac excels at imparting brightness and lift, particularly in woody and herbal accords, fougère compositions, and masculine fragrances. With good stability across various products, including personal care items and home fragrances, it provides a dynamic, impactful top-to-heart note in diverse scent applications.

products.name: Herbanate®
products.description:
In Givaudan's own words: “Herbanate has a fruity note with hints of banana, pineapple and blackcurrant. The background is fresh and herbal with a warm spicy element. Herbanate is a versatile material that provides or enhances the natural effect of fragrances, particularly in fruity notes where it gives a juicy tropical fruit effect. It can also be used as a 10% dilution to give a green herbal freshness and blends well with citrus, green and even spicy notes.”

Herbanate blends extremely well with agrestical materials such as Clary Sage, Lavender Absolute and Lavender Oil. It offers excellent diffusion in combination with the rose ketones and blends surprisingly well undecavertol and methyl heptine carbonate. Try it with our Daphne base for a very modern and unique mix.

products.name: Herbavert
products.description:
Herbavert arrives with startling diffusion—a blast of camphoraceous brightness shot through with mentholic coolness that reads as crushed rosemary and eucalyptus leaf. This opening is aggressive, modern, and intensely clean. Within minutes the rubbery edge softens, revealing a gentler herbal-vegetative character.

The material's real magic lies in its evolution. As the initial sparkle fades, Herbavert transforms into something unexpectedly delicate: soft apple-blossom, transparent rose nuances, and a clean sweetness that supports fruity-floral hearts beautifully. This two-stage personality makes it invaluable for smoothing the gap between punchy top notes and developing heart accords. Pair it with Verdox for juicy apple realism, or blend with Rose Oxide at equal parts for a sparkling, metallic rosebud effect.

products.name: Herboxane
products.description:
Herboxane opens with sweet basil and chamomile, fresh and cooling, with a gentle red-pepper spiciness underneath. The overall impression is aromatic and round — green without sharpness. It smells remarkably natural for a synthetic material.

Use it as a background ingredient to smooth and round assertive herbal oils like thyme, lavender, and rosemary. It calms their spikier edges and adds body and coherence to green accords. Combined with citrus oils, it brings crisp, natural-smelling greenness that lifts the whole composition.

Pair it with lavender and coumarin for classic fougère construction, with bergamot for a herbal-citrus opening, or with clary sage and geranium for rich aromatic heart notes. It also works well with blackcurrant bud materials, where its slight berry facet creates a seamless bridge.

products.name: Hercolyn® D
products.description:
Firmenich's Hercolyn® D is a high quality deodorised version of hydrogenated pine resin. It is extremely viscous and light amber in colour. This virtually odourless material is a wonderful fixative and blender and finds many uses in fragrances and bases. Its very thick nature makes it excellent for adding body and texture to dilutions.

This material has been used successfully in Guerlain's recent efforts to enrich and extend IFRA compliant oakmoss in combination with Mastic Absolute for use in their reformulations of their classic fragrance Mitsouko (1919).

Note: Formerly we were selling this under the name Hercolyn® DW.

products.name: Hexyl Acetate
products.description:
This versatile ester opens with an immediately recognisable burst of crisp, green apple and unripe pear. Its bright, watery character captures that mouth-watering moment of biting into fresh fruit. Unlike heavier fruity materials, it delivers a clean, sharp freshness that never becomes cloying or artificial.

Your compositions benefit from its exceptional blending properties—subtle floral facets allow seamless integration into white florals like lily of the valley or magnolia without creating olfactory clashes. The material's "fuzzy" quality creates soft transitions, functioning as an olfactory bridge between sharp citrus top notes and richer floral hearts. Its high diffusion provides immediate impact while low tenacity ensures it doesn't interfere with your composition's development.

Use it strategically as a naturalising agent in fruit accords where synthetic components need softening. Its role in Jean-Claude Ellena's apple accords demonstrates sophisticated deployment—paired with Fructone and Benzyl Acetate for yellow apple effects, or with Allyl Caproate for red apple nuances. The material excels in functional perfumery with excellent stability in most product bases.

products.name: Hexyl Benzoate
products.description:
Hexyl benzoate opens with a remarkably fresh take on balsamic—clean and sappy rather than heavy or cloying. The woody-green character evokes freshly stripped cypress branches ready for distillation. Sweet herbaceous undertones provide warmth without muddiness.

This ester excels as a fixative, particularly for labdanum where it extends longevity while contributing its own subtle character. You'll find it indispensable in amber compositions needing freshness alongside depth. Chypre and fougère structures benefit from its ability to bridge woody and balsamic elements seamlessly.

The exceptional 192-hour substantivity makes hexyl benzoate a true base note anchor. Use it to add clean, sappy freshness to coniferous accords or to lift heavier balsamic materials. It blends beautifully with woods and resins, never dominating but always supporting.

products.name: Hexyl Butyrate
products.description:
Hexyl butyrate delivers that unmistakable sweet apple character with a gentle pear softness underneath. The green-waxy facet keeps it naturalistic rather than candied. A subtle pineapple sweetness emerges as you work with it, adding tropical warmth to the fruit profile.

This ester proves remarkably versatile across fruit compositions. It anchors apple accords with authentic bite while lending pear its characteristic juiciness. Tropical fruits like guava, kiwi, and passionfruit benefit enormously from its presence—it bridges temperate and exotic fruit notes seamlessly. The natural occurrence in lavender oil means it also supports fresh floral-fruity effects.

Blend hexyl butyrate with other fruity esters to build complex fruit salad effects. Its medium odour strength allows generous dosing without overwhelming compositions. The waxy undertone helps fruits feel ripe and natural rather than artificial—essential when creating convincing orchard accords.

products.name: Hexyl Caprylate
products.description:
Hexyl caprylate smells of crisp green apple and ripe melon — fresh, light, airy, with a clean waxy texture. It is one of perfumery's invisible workhorses: a background material that makes everything around it smell fresher. You will not notice it, but you will notice when it is missing.

Use hexyl caprylate to add natural-smelling freshness to citrus openings, aquatic accords, and light florals. It lifts and brightens without adding any recognisable character of its own — the fruity-green quality blends in rather than standing out. Short-lived on skin, so pair it with longer-lasting materials.

Combine it with bergamot and linalool for a transparent citrus-floral opening, or with hedione and dihydromyrcenol for a clean, modern masculine effect. It gives fruit notes a natural, skin-like texture rather than synthetic candy sweetness. Inexpensive, stable, and endlessly useful.

products.name: Hexyl Cinnamic Aldehyde
products.description:
An unctuous floral, Hexyl Cinnamic Aldehyde is the key building block to some of the most famous muguet bases and is found in fragrances such as Eau Sauvage (1966), Gabrielle (2017, Chanel — demonstration formula below), Dolce & Gabbana Light Blue (2001), and Tom Ford's Tobacco Vanille (2007).

When constructing a jasmine base, this material is preferred over its close relative Amyl Cinnamic Aldehyde, owing to the fact that the hexyl version is sweeter and more floral. Hexyl Cinnamic Aldehyde tempers the harsh character of Benzyl Acetate and other strong jasmine chemicals while providing a light and discreet unisex floral heart note.

At room temperature, Hexyl Cinnamic Aldehyde is liquid but at lower temperatures it may solidify. A little heat will return it to a liquid state. Importantly, Hexyl Cinnamic Aldehyde can sour quite quickly so it is recommended that you buy small quantities often, rather than bulk amounts and refrigerate it.

products.name: Hexyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
Hexyl isobutyrate opens with bright apple-pear sweetness but quickly reveals a distinctive winey, grape-like richness that sets it apart from simpler fruity esters. A ripe tropical warmth sits underneath. The dry-down stays sweet and clean with gentle peach undertones.

That winey quality makes it invaluable for grape and concord accords — territory most fruity esters cannot reach. In apple and pear compositions, it adds a riper, more complex dimension than hexyl butyrate alone. Tropical fruit blends gain depth and a fermented, juice-like naturalness.

Layer it with phenoxyethyl isobutyrate and citronellyl acetate for a convincing pear accord. In floral compositions, a trace adds overripe, almost boozy warmth — the kind of winey depth that separates flat fruit notes from convincing ones. It occurs naturally in apples, apricots, and chamomile.

Hexyl Isobutyrate vs Hexyl Butyrate

Both deliver apple-pear fruitiness, but hexyl butyrate is sweeter and waxier with clean pineapple undertones — straightforward orchard fruit. Hexyl isobutyrate trades some of that sweetness for a winey, grape-like richness and a drier, more tart edge.

Use hexyl butyrate for bright, uncomplicated apple-pear; use hexyl isobutyrate when you want that same fruit foundation with darker, more fermented depth. Blending the two gives you the best of both.

products.name: Hexyl Isovalerate
products.description:
This material captures the exact character of unripe fruit with remarkable precision. The initial sweet-fruity impression immediately reveals sharp, pungent lift that prevents cloying—this is the key to its sophistication. The apple dominance isn't generic sweetness but specifically evokes apple skin with its characteristic waxy texture and slight tartness.

The strawberry facet adds complexity whilst the "unripe" character provides that crucial naturalistic edge. This prevents fruit accords from smelling like candy, instead creating the impression of biting into firm, crisp fruit. Its three-hour substantivity makes it perfect as a top-to-middle note bridge.

Use this when you need to move beyond simple fruity sweetness into photorealistic territory. Essential for apple and strawberry accords, but surprisingly effective in modern fougère compositions where its green character bridges aromatic herbs with contemporary freshness. Even works in sophisticated tobacco accords where its dried fruit aspect mimics fine cured leaf.

products.name: Hexyl Salicylate
products.description:
This material opens with a sweet herbaceous whisper that immediately brings to mind fresh witch-hazel and dewy clover fields. Its delicate floral-green character creates an invisible bridge between volatile citrus tops and heavier base notes. You'll find it indispensable for smoothing rough edges in complex accords.

Use Hexyl Salicylate when building sophisticated white florals—it elevates lily-of-the-valley and jasmine with subtle depth. The material excels at extending dry-down without dominating the composition. Pair it with fellow salicylates to create that coveted "salicylate heart" found in classic perfumes.

Deploy this versatile modifier across fragrance families—from marine accords needing floral softness to fougères requiring natural green sap. Its remarkable alkaline stability makes it perfect for functional fragrances in soaps and detergents. At higher doses, it becomes a characterful protagonist; in traces, an invisible hand guiding harmony.

products.name: Hexyl Tiglate
products.description:
Hexyl tiglate opens with a striking green freshness that immediately evokes garden settings after rain. The nasturtium character is unmistakable—peppery, leafy, and utterly natural. Beneath that bright top note sits a softer herbal quality that grounds the material beautifully.

This ester belongs to the tiglate family, which gives Roman chamomile its characteristic fruity-herbal sweetness. You can exploit this connection to build convincing chamomile accords or to add that particular warmth to green compositions. The material also excels in gardenia reconstructions where naturalistic green facets are essential.

Blend hexyl tiglate with white florals for lifted, outdoor freshness. It pairs exceptionally well with leafy notes and herbal aromatics. The high odour strength means careful dosing—smell at dilution first to understand its full character before committing to your formula.

products.name: Hindinol®
products.description:
Hindinol is one of the most beautiful and radiant of the sandalwood aroma chemicals and somewhat unique in being something of a top note material. 

Perfumery: Techniques In Evolution speaks highly of the product: “This is […] one of the best sandalwood chemicals, as captivating as as it is extraordinary[.] Most sandalwood chemicals lack a natural top note and we perfumers need to create it; however, when using Hindinol, the natural top note appears and this top note is a dream come true.”

While a number of suppliers make this product, the Takasago quality is the nicest and that is what we stock.

products.name: Hinoki Wood Oil
products.description:
