The scent of Shinto shrines, Buddhist temples and palaces in Japan, Hinoki Wood is a type of cypress with a distinctive top note character with a rounded camphoraceous quality. It is softer than pine and fir oil and has a very lovely smoky and leathery facet.

It would be ideal in a forest based scent or a fantasy fresh fragrance and would be very interesting with Dihydromyrcenol as the main part of a modern top note accord.

IFRA: Hinoki Wood has no limitations under IFRA however LMR undertakes internal testing and they use that testing when they produce their “IFRA” documents. Consequently while LMR says the limit is 0.02% in this product, that is not the IFRA limit. This is a quirk of LMR. We supply their IFRA document as a matter of reference only.

Hinoki wood oil blends with Bouleau Pyrogene 1840, Apo Patchone Coeur, Royal Leather, Pineapple Supreme, and Oud Intense.

products.name: Hivernal® Neo
products.description:
Named after the man who discovered it in 1994 (Béat Winter), Hivernal Neo has a similar structure to Lilial but replaces its fatty qualities with fresh and clean notes of white linen and muguet. It is very long lasting and powerful so care should be exercised in its use.

From Firmenich perfumer, Harry Frémont: “[T]he freshest and the longest lasting ingredient, although freshness and long-lastingness normally do not coexist. Very monolithic and linear, its modifying power is unequaled with brightness and a humid facet.”

Hivernal Neo blends beautifully with Galbex®, Florol®, Nympheal™, Mimosal™, Celestafleur™ and all our Muguet bases.

products.name: Ho Wood “Superior” Oil
products.description:
While many companies produce Ho Wood oil, it is often from a blend of branches and leaves and is rarely treated as a luxury oil owing to its low cost and abundance. But Payan Bertrand have produced what we would consider the finest of all the suppliers bar none.

This oil is so good it is practically on a par with Brazilian Rosewood which is now virtually impossible to obtain due to CITES regulations. This oil can be used in very much the same way as Linalool but it is, of course, 100% natural.

This oil forms part of Mandy Aftel's naturals starter kit.

Origin: China
Part: Wood
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Homage Attar Type Formula
products.description:
Homage (in homage to the rose and the 25th anniversary of Amouage) was released in 2008 as a limited edition 12ml luxury attar. This is our reconstruction of the original formula based on a GCMS of the red wooden box release which we are fortunate to have in our perfume vault.

While Amouage has a bit of a rocky reputation for quality (especially with some of its newer scents), the Attars are unimpeachable. Homage is a magnificent example of how great this house can be when it puts its mind (and dollars) where its mouth is. This is a complex formula with many luxurious naturals and it is a surprisingly light scent for an attar type. Wear it as is without diluting, or dilute it for more of a European fragrance experience.

Top Notes: Taïf Rose, Frankincense, Petitgrain, Lavender, Lemon, Orange
Heart Notes: Jasmine, Geranium, Helichrysum, Orange Blossom
Base Notes: Cedarwood, Oud, Sandalwood, Patchouli, Guaiacwood

Total Lines: 58
Bases: 1 — Rose Taïf

products.name: Honey Provence Firabs
products.description:
Honey Provence Firabs opens with the unmistakable aroma of honeycomb freshly broken from the hive—sweet, gooey, and irresistibly appetising. Smooth beeswax depth grounds the sweetness, while subtle chocolate nuances add sophisticated complexity. This is honey done in the modern gourmand style: indulgent and edible without the animalic weight of traditional honey materials.

This Firmenich base belongs to their Firabs range—specialties created through co-extraction of natural materials with carefully selected synthetic molecules, including proprietary captives. Firabs products contain the actual named natural ingredient (in this case, beeswax and honey extract), distinguishing them from Firbest bases which recreate scent profiles without the named natural. The co-extraction process captures authentic honeycomb character while synthetic additions enhance intensity and performance.

Work with Honey Provence Firabs sparingly—its power demands a light hand. The semi-solid consistency becomes pourable with gentle warming. Blend with florals like rose, orange blossom, and osmanthus, or use in amber, tobacco, and oud compositions where honeyed sweetness adds warmth. Excellent diffusiveness makes it project beautifully in fine fragrances.

products.name: Honey Supreme
products.description:
Fraterworks Honey Supreme is the ultimate honey base. It blends a heart of finest French beeswax absolute with radiant modern molecules.

Honey Supreme encapsulates the scent of a long-abandoned bee hive bursting with sweet honey that hints of the wild flowers and fields that nourished the golden bees that produced it.

Pure Honey Supreme is IFRA safe at doses up to 5% of a finished product, however we recommend working with a 10% dilution due to its incredible power. Honey supreme adds a truly modern note of luxury to fine fragrances and works as a one for one replacer of Firmenich's Honey Signature (Honey Provence Firabs).

Fraterworks also sells the classic non-discolouring De Laire Miel Blanc base restored in all its Belle Époque glory, and the vegan compatible Mielarome of Chiris featured in masterpieces like La Rose Jacqueminot by Coty.

products.name: Honeyflor 1% DPG
products.description:
We can say with almost total certainty that this is the one of the most potent honey chemicals you will smell and so we sell it at 1% in dilution with DPG.

As well as a classic miel note, Honeyflor also exhibits a lovely powderiness and a green hyacinth quality making it perfect for adding unusual nuances and character to floral blends.

Honeyflor blends well with Honey Supreme, Miel Blanc (a classic base), Mielarome (also classical) and hyacinth and rose products.

products.name: Honeysuckle
products.description:
Honeysuckle is one of those most beautiful spring floral scents that seems to float on the air and greet you before you even see it. Fraterworks® Honeysuckle 584569 is a thoroughly modern base built around a luscious core of natural oils and absolutes enhanced by scientifically accurate synthetics as found in the headspace of the living flowers in the wild.

This is a sweet, elegant and rich floral base that can be used at up to 19% of your finished product.

Despite the beauty of the flower's scent, honeysuckle bases are rare and the historic Honeysuckle No 6 and Chevrefeuille 70 of De Laire were long ago discontinued. For the sake of historical interest we will be re-introducing the classic Chevrefeuille 70 in the future.

products.name: Hyacinth Body
products.description:
Hyacinth Body smells of a spring morning — dewy, transparent, leafy-green with an unmistakable hyacinth character. There are clear impressions of nasturtium and sweet pea alongside the hyacinth, plus a subtle mushroom-metallic facet that adds depth. It is fresher and more watery than Hyacinth Body No. 3, which is more herbal and aggressive by comparison.

This material is one of the essential building blocks for green floral accords. It forms the structural core of hyacinth reconstructions and contributes convincingly to lilac, muguet, and sweet pea compositions. Used as a modifier in rose accords, it creates a "rose on the stem" effect — the green, living quality of a freshly cut flower rather than a dried petal.

Pair Hyacinth Body with phenylacetaldehyde for hyper-realistic hyacinth, or with galbanum for a sharper green edge. It works beautifully with Hedione for diffusive transparency, and with indole for narcotic white floral depth. Use it at modest levels as a modifier, or push it higher as a structural core in green floral soliflores.

products.name: Hyacinth Body No. 3
products.description:
Hyacinth Body No 3 opens with an assertive burst of crushed green leaves and sappy stems. This powerful green-floral fusion carries the unmistakable character of hyacinth but with enhanced vegetal depth. The material's exceptional impact allows minute quantities to transform entire compositions.

Deploy this acetal when you need aggressive green character without sacrificing floral elegance. Its herbal edge makes it perfect for masculine florals or compositions requiring botanical authenticity. Layer it beneath traditional rose accords to create the impression of roses growing wild among herbs and foliage.

Build unexpected contrasts by pairing its vegetal sharpness with creamy white florals like tuberose or gardenia. Use traces in citrus compositions to add mysterious green depth. Combine with galbanum and violet leaf for hyper-realistic stem effects that ground even the most ethereal florals.

The No 3 Designation

IFF developed multiple Hyacinth Body variants in their quest to capture different facets of the living flower. No 3 offers more pronounced herbal character than the original version (standard Hyacinth Body, CAS 2556-10-7). While No 1 and No 2 appear to have been developmental stages or discontinued variants not commercially available today, No 3 survived as the more assertive, herbaceous alternative perfumers reach for when the original's dewy transparency needs more green muscle.

products.name: Hyacinth Storm
products.description:
Hyacinth Storm is so named because it is an effusion of glittering green, floral and aldehydic notes. While we also sell the beautiful classical Jacinthia, Hyacinth Storm is modern, radiant and utterly beguiling. One sniff draws you in and you find yourself going back to the bottle over and over to inhale once again a marvel of perfumery.

This base is the only hyacinth you need. It fits readily into any modern perfume or can be used as a luxurious green starting point in overdose for a new masterpiece in the direction of such scents as Oscar (1977) by Oscar de la Renta, Ombré de Hyacinth by Tom Ford (private blend), Malle's Synthetic Jungle (2021), Accento by Xerjoff (2019), or Nasomatto's Narcotic Venus (2007).

Pair it with a modern jasmine base like Jasmin Fleurs, Pineapple Supreme and Neobutenone Alpha and you have the start of something wonderful.

If you are looking for a Hyacinth absolute replacer, we also have the incredible 100% natural Hyacinth TruAbs®.

products.name: Hyacinth TruAbs
products.description:
It may not exhibit the prettiest smell (though it comes from what could certainly be considered the prettiest bloom), but Hyacinth absolute does exist and has some practical use as a floraliser, complexor and nuancer. However, it is almost impossible to obtain in the 21st century and certainly not consistently enough for use in commercial fragrances.

Enter Fraterworks' Hyacinth TruAbs®. This 100% natural blend replicates with astonishing accuracy the genuine absolute and can be used one for one in the same manner. It is deep yellow, thick and incredibly realistic. It is best used at below 1% for adding a je ne sais quoi to fragrances. It's ability to impart naturalness and character to the mostly chemical classic Hyacinth (Jacinthe) bases is extraordinary.

Like our amazing Rose de Mai and Boronia TruAbs' this base is created scientifically for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from pure and natural (albeit practically non-existant) true hyacinth absolute.

Due to the high cost of this replica, we also sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Hyacinth Supreme TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing.

products.name: Hydratropic Aldehyde
products.description:
Hydratropic aldehyde captures the essence of fresh hyacinth leaves with remarkable stability that sets it apart from volatile alternatives. This material opens with sharp, crisp green notes evoking dewy morning gardens where hyacinth blooms release their intoxicating scent. Its additional methyl group provides crucial stabilisation, preventing the polymerisation issues that plague phenyl acetaldehyde while maintaining full floral impact.

Many perfumers prefer hydratropic aldehyde to phenyl acetaldehyde in hyacinth compositions, finding it outperforms in both stability and olfactory refinement. Use at 0.01-0.5% for optimal effect—its power requires restraint but rewards with exceptional longevity. The material excels in creating springtime freshness, working beautifully in lilac, rose, narcissus, and tulip accords where its green-floral duality adds natural depth.

What makes hydratropic aldehyde special compared to other hyacinth aldehydes is its structural advantage—the alpha-methyl substitution creates steric hindrance that dramatically improves stability without sacrificing potency. While phenyl acetaldehyde requires stabilisation with phenyl ethyl alcohol and tends toward harsh pungency, hydratropic aldehyde remains pleasantly smooth and controlled. This stability means cleaner formulations, better shelf life, and more predictable performance in finished products. Use it when you need reliable hyacinth character that won't deteriorate or overwhelm.

products.name: Hydrocarboresine
products.description:
“Ab illo benedicáris, in cujus honóre cremáberis.” or “May you be blessed by Him, in Whose honour you will be burnt.” This is the blessing said over the incense as it is set alight during Holy Mass. And anyone who has been present at that moment will recognise immediately that most wonderful smoky scent of incense when they first smell Biolande's Hydrocarboresine.

Despite the incense connection this is a labdanum product, but through the proprietary pyrogenation technique (the process of overheating or burning) it is transformed into one of the most popular cistus specialities on the market.

To create a full blast Three Kings Incense replica, blend Hydrocarboresine with Myrrh Absolute and Robertet's wonderful Olibanol.

products.name: Hydroxyambran
products.description:
Hydroxyambran seems demure at first sniff but it is a wonderful material in the super amber family (though somewhat more woody than ambergris) that is more versatile and longer lasting than most. 

In fact, Hydroxyambran is so long lasting it works as a fixative for Ambrocenide. It is absolutely synergistic with other amber type materials and is particularly good in combination with Permawood™, Operanide, Dextro Norlimbanol and Z11 (Ambraketal).

Hydroxyambran is a waxy solid at room temperature but it melts easily with a little warmth. Far too few perfumers utilise this very lovely amber wood chemical. It deserves some time in the spotlight.

Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) sings the praises of Hydroxyambran stating it is "one of the best chemicals I have known and smelled … One of the sublime odours, the best of the best."

products.name: Hydroxycitronellal
products.description:
Hydroxycitronellal (since 1905) in its most radiant form is Cyclosia® (which we also stock) but its cost puts it far out of budget for most perfumery projects. On the other hand, BASF produces a spectacular quality at a price that fits most budgets. Luxury fragrance houses frequently use the BASF version while Cyclosia® is relegated to speciality use as a showpiece in much the same way as we now use other treasures such as Rhodinol isolated from Bourbon Geranium and Geraniol ex Palmarosa.

Today, Hydroxycitronellal remains one of the few elegant lily of the valley aldehydes that can be used in fairly generous amounts (up to 2.1% of the finished perfume) whilst retaining IFRA 51 compliance.

Discovered around the same time as the orris / violet chemical Iralia, Hydroxycitronellal formed a substantial part of the midcentury masterpiece Muguet des Bois, the lily of the valley perfume and then base created by Henri Robert for Coty.

products.name: Hyraceum Tincture 10%
products.description:
Resembling a rodent but related to elephants, the rock hyrax is a wild animal from Africa that marks its territory with a thick pheremone-laden spray which petrifies over time. It is the rock-like nature of the aged material that leads to its nickname: “hyraceum stone”. The animals that produced the fossilised material we tincture at Fraterworks lived hundreds (and even potentially) thousands of years ago.

Hyraceum tincture exudes a wonderfully complex barnyard-like odour crossed with wild honey which immediately transports you to the unspoilt savannahs of Africa. A most interesting and unique animalic, hyraceum blends beautifully with the other classic perfumery animalics.

products.name: Hyraceum “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
In 2024 Firmenich announced the discontinuation of their acclaimed Hyraceum Absolute 60% DIPG. In 2025 Fraterworks began manufacturing its replacement in Grasse. We are now the only supplier of this wonderful natural musk absolute.

Hyraceum Absolute opens with fierce animalic intensity—phenolic, urinous notes mingle with tarry leather and scorched earth. This fossilised essence captures millennia of African sun and stone. Use it where you need uncompromising animalic depth without ethical compromise.

This material transforms on warm skin from challenging rawness to seductive warmth. Build leather accords with unprecedented realism or add subliminal sensuality to florals. Master perfumers reach for Hyraceum when synthetic musks lack soul and natural alternatives prove too tame.

Dose carefully—traces add mysterious depth whilst higher amounts create bold animalic statements. Combine with labdanum for rich leather effects or blend into oud reconstructions for authenticity. In chypres, it provides the dark foundation modern regulations have diminished in their restriction on oakmoss.

What is Hyraceum?

Hyraceum comes from the fossilised urine and faeces of the Rock Hyrax (Procavia capensis), a small mammal native to Africa and the Middle East. These rabbit-sized creatures live in colonies and use communal latrines in protected rock crevices over many generations.

The hyrax produces unusually viscous, jelly-like urine that's exceptionally rich in calcium carbonate and other m

products.name: Hyssop Oil
products.description:
Hyssop oil opens with a bracing camphoraceous freshness that feels cool and mineral, almost crystalline. As this initial diffusive blast settles, warm spicy-herbaceous notes emerge alongside a distinctive tea-like dryness. The effect recalls sun-baked Mediterranean hillsides studded with wild herbs.

This oil excels at bridging fresh top notes to warmer base materials in complex compositions. Pair it with lavender and coumarin in fougères, where it reinforces the herbal architecture while adding vertical lift. Blend with citrus oils for colognes that smell authentically botanical rather than synthetic, or use it with labdanum and patchouli in chypres where its bitterness cuts through sweetness beautifully.

Work at trace levels - a little goes a long way. Combine with clary sage to amplify the hay-like facets, or with frankincense where hyssop extends and freshens resinous top notes. Classic masculine fragrances like Hermès Equipage and Caron Yatagan showcase its structural power in aromatic-woody compositions.

products.name: Immortelle Absolute
products.description:
Immortelle absolute (also known as Everlasting and more technically as helichrysum) is a wonderful floral absolute that has no equal. It has complex notes of hay, tobacco, caramel, fruit, honey and tonka.

Our variety (replacing the previous by MANE) is by LMR and it is part of their "For Life" range. With this update we get a more beautiful and truer scent profile, as well as an easier to use pure absolute as its viscosity, whilst thick, is pourable with just a little warmth.

A key component of Sables (1985) by Annick Goutal and  L'Heure Bleue (1912) by Jacques Guerlain for Guerlain, this absolute combines beautifully with wood notes (especially Sandalwood), ionones, orris and violet and suits modern gourmand type fragrances where its sweetness is especially favoured. Blends with Sotolone are interesting.

Note: Immortelle absolute is prized for perfumery especially, while the essential oil is preferred by aromatherapists. 

Immortelle is quite viscous so in addition to pure, we offer it at 50% in natural triethyl citral, an odourless isolate from citrus.

products.name: Indocolore
products.description:
Indocolore gives you the sensual, animalic depth of indole without the two problems that make indole difficult: discolouration and that persistent mothball-naphthalenic edge. What remains is a beautifully floral animalic note — heady jasmine and hyacinth with a feral undertone. It stays colourless in your finished product, which the name makes clear.

This material excels wherever you want indolic richness in a transparent composition. White floral accords — jasmine, tuberose, gardenia, orange blossom — all benefit from its depth without the yellow-brown staining that indole causes over time. It lasts exceptionally well on blotter, making it a reliable base-note anchor in floral hearts.

Use Indocolore as a direct replacement for indole in any formula where colour matters. Combine it with Hedione and benzyl acetate for a clean jasmine accord, or pair with tuberose absolute for narcotic intensity. It is extremely powerful, so work in heavy dilution — traces are usually enough to bring a floral composition to life.

products.name: Indolarome
products.description:
This material solves indole's biggest problem—it gives you that narcotic white-floral depth without discolouring your formula or overwhelming compositions with harsh mothball notes. The "sparkle" perfumers describe is real: by removing indole's heavy, musty facets, Indolarome lets the radiant floral-animalic core shine through with brilliant diffusion.

Use it wherever you need authentic jasmine, tuberose, lily or orange blossom realism—trace amounts transform simple floral sketches into living, breathing flowers with sensual warmth. Blend with hedione for transparent radiance or combine with benzyl acetate to enrich basic fruity-floral notes into complex natural territory. Its civet-like facets build sophisticated animalic accords whilst subtle leather nuances add dry, smoky depth.

Handle with precision at trace to moderate levels depending on intensity desired. In tobacco and tea accords it contributes earthy, fermented realism; in oriental compositions it bridges spicy tops to balsamic bases with skin-like intimacy. Pair with ylang-ylang for tropical narcotic florals or use with musks and amber for primal, sensual warmth that lasts.

products.name: Ionone Alpha
products.description:
Ionone Alpha is the most floral and violet-like of the ionone family and it is absolutely essential to the creation of natural violet notes in a fragrance. Like its counterpart, Ionone Beta, there are also berry and woody nuances but if it is a floral ionone you are after, this is the one.

If you are looking for an especially refined version of Ionone Alpha, particularly for violet and iris fragrances, we also offer Irisone® Alpha.

According to Arctander, “[Ionone Alpha is] used widely in perfume compositions of almost all types. It is many decades since the single floral Violet note was appreciated as a fragrance for cosmetic purposes, but lonone has found numerous other applications. The use of lonone in Rose bases is very common and generally well liked, and smaller amounts of lonone are used in woody, herbaceous, floral, balsamic, piney or Citrus-like fragrances. It is almost not possibe to name a fragrance in which Ionone has not been tried for modifications, blending, floralizing mellowing etc. It is often part of the highly desirable complex that displays 'powdery' undertones in a fragrance.”

products.name: Ionone Alpha, Natural
products.description:
Natural alpha-ionone is the most floral and violet-like of all the ionones — sweet, powdery, with a juicy raspberry edge that makes people think immediately of Parma Violets. This version, produced by sugar fermentation, is a single natural enantiomer and smells purer and more defined than the standard synthetic blend.

For natural perfumers, this solves one of the hardest problems in the palette: how to create a convincing violet without synthetics. Use it as the heart of violet and iris accords, or add it to rose bases for powdery depth. It pairs beautifully with orris, mimosa, and boronia — materials that share its soft, cosmetic quality.

Combine it with beta-ionone (natural is coming later this year) for a complete violet effect (alpha gives the floral sweetness, beta gives the woody depth), or with methyl ionones for rich, powdery iris compositions. It also softens citrus and aldehydic openings beautifully. Tenacious for a violet material — well over four days on a blotter.

products.name: Ionone Beta
products.description:
Ionone beta is the sweetest of the ionones, having aspects of red berries, tropical fruit and beeswax. It is the chemical that plays the biggest role in giving Boronia its wonderful scent and is indispensable in recreations of the same. It serves a minor role in many other florals and is valuable as a nuancer for wood blends.

According to Arctander, “It finds its way more into fragrances rich in woody notes, including those employing newer derivatives of Cyclohexanol, etc. It is also more widely used in lipstick fragrances on account of its compatibility with fruity fragrance materials.”

products.name: Iraldeine® Beta
products.description:
Iraldeine Beta (Methyl Ionone Beta Coeur) opens with a powdery orris-violet character — clean, slightly woody, with a soft leathery and tobacco depth underneath. A faint creamy-tropical sweetness threads through the heart and base.

Use Iraldeine Beta in the heart of orris bouquets, violet-leather accords, classic chypres and modern woody florals. It bridges floral hearts to woody-leather bases without the candy-violet sweetness of other methyl ionones. A small dose deepens iris replicas; larger doses push compositions toward dry tobacco, violet suede and classical leather territory.

As used in both Kadine (1911) and L'Heure Bleue (1912) by Guerlain. In L'Heure Bleue it is masterfully blended with Iriseine (Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra), Iraldeine Delta (Isomethyl Ionone Beta), and a little Iralia for polish. The demo formula below demonstrates how truly considered every ingredient was in a classical perfume.

From the GCMS Library

Iraldeine Beta has been confirmed by GCMS analysis in many landmark fragrances. Quantified examples include Chanel No 5 (1.87%), Replique by Raphael (1.00%), Synarome Cuir HF base (2.09%), Synarome Cuir de Russie base (0.91%), Roja Chypre Extraordinaire (0.43%), Dior Cuir Cannage (0.41%), Detchema by Revillon (0.33%), Histoires de Parfums 1740 Marquis de Sade (0.28%) and Patou 1000 (0.02%). It is also identified in Aromatics Elixir, Twilly d'Hermès, Chanel Le Lion and Comète, Amouage Jubilation XXV and Interlude Black Iris, and several Henry Jacques

products.name: Iraldeine® Delta
products.description:
With subtle nuances of fruit, this is the woody member of the family and is very rare today, being very difficult to obtain. While Iralia is sweet powdery iris and Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha is diffusive floral violet, Isomethyl Ionone Beta is polished wood.

This is the famous ionone rediscovered by Edmond Roudnitska discarded in barrels in the stock yard of De Laire during the second world war. With raw materials hard to come by, he decided to turn the "waste" into something wonderful and his Prunol SP was born: a rich and complex floral base with nuances of fruit.

It had been previously featured in great perfumes like Styx by Coty (1911). We also sell Iraldeine Beta.

Iralia®: Finest and sweetest all round powdery iris / violet chemical. Historic.
Isoraldeine™ Cetone Alpha: Highly purified rare form of Isoraldeine 95. Most floral methyl ionone.
Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur: Cheapest. Floral, violet, soft, powdery.
Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra: Bolder, orris, leather, beeswax. Diffusive. Long lasting.

products.name: Iralia®
products.description:
Iralia® is the very pinnacle of Firmenich perfection in methyl ionone products. It was first synthesised at the turn of the 20th century alongside Cyclosia®, the finest quality of hydroxycitronellal which we also stock.

Iralia's first use, and perhaps still its finest, was as a 25% overdose in L'Origan (1908) by Coty where it couples with Dianthine, the famed De Laire carnation base. The complete original formula can be found below.

Similar products are Isoraldeine® 70 and 95, Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra.

products.name: Iralia® Total
products.description:
Iralia Total smells like opening a vintage face powder compact — rich violet and orris wrapped in a warm woody veil. A creamy floral heart sits underneath, with a subtle raspberry sweetness that surfaces on the dry-down. François Coty built L'Origan around this very note in 1908.

Use Iralia Total as your workhorse violet-orris heart — it gives you the powdery richness of orris butter at a fraction of the cost. It bridges heart and base seamlessly, preventing the abrupt drop-off that plagues lighter florals. Push it to high concentrations where it becomes a dominant structural pillar.

Pair Iralia Total with Hedione for a luminous, lifted violet or combine it with vetiver and salicylates for sophisticated leather effects. Try it alongside damascones for convincing rose accords. Its exceptional tenacity — over 200 hours on the strip — means a little carries a composition for days.

Iralia Total vs Iralia

We also sell Iralia, the classic version. Both share the same CAS number and belong to Firmenich's methyl ionone family, but they're tuned differently. Iralia is the refined, more purely floral version — the most elegant methyl ionone Firmenich makes, with a richer orris character, a softer powdery quality, and a subtle tea-like nuance that makes it the fine fragrance connoisseur's first choice.

Iralia Total trades some of that refinement for robustness: a more pronounced woody facet, superior stability in difficult bases, and better substantivity on fabric. Think of Iralia

products.name: Iris Nitrile
products.description:
Iris Nitrile delivers exceptional power and radiance that transforms ordinary iris compositions into memorable creations. This material works at incredibly low concentrations—typically 0.05-0.5%—where its diffusive character amplifies ionones and natural orris. This molecule is excellent for bridging floral hearts to woody bases while maintaining transparency and modern appeal.

Apply Iris Nitrile in trace amounts using pre-diluted solutions for accurate dosing. Layer this material with alpha and beta ionones for authentic iris reconstruction. Combine with cedarwood and vetiver to emphasise its woody-rooty facets. The material performs exceptionally in functional products, maintaining stability in soap and shampoo formulations where other iris materials fail.

products.name: Irisone® Alpha
products.description:
Irisone® Alpha is a highly refined 90% pure form of Ionone Alpha and, as a result, is more costly. This is the Ionone Alpha of choice for particularly high quality products and is almost certainly the version of this chemical that you would want to use in making a violet or iris note. If you are constructing a rose accord or need a more general purpose ionone, we recommend our standard Ionone Alpha offering instead.

According to Arctander, “[Ionone Alpha is] used widely in perfume compositions of almost all types. It is many decades since the single floral Violet note was appreciated as a fragrance for cosmetic purposes, but lonone has found numerous other applications. The use of lonone in Rose bases is very common and generally well liked, and smaller amounts of lonone are used in woody, herbaceous, floral, balsamic, piney or Citrus-like fragrances. It is almost not possibe to name a fragrance in which Ionone has not been tried for modifications, blending, floralizing mellowing etc. It is often part of the highly desirable complex that displays 'powdery' undertones in a fragrance.”

products.name: Irival Oliffac
products.description:
Irival Oliffac opens with distinctive fatty-floral richness reminiscent of precious orris butter. Its powdery violet character emerges alongside camphoraceous-woody facets. The initial sharpness softens into sophisticated iris root with subtle gourmand undertones.

You'll find this base invaluable when building iris accords without natural orris's prohibitive cost. It excels when combined with ionones where it amplifies violet powder effects whilst adding rooty depth. Use it at 0.5-2% to create the ethereal grey quality found in modern iris fragrances without overwhelming delicate florals.

Blend Irival with beta-ionone and methyl ionone for complete violet-iris reconstructions. Combine with woody molecules like Iso E Super to enhance the rooty facets. Pair with aldehydes (especially compatible is Aldehyde C-12 Lauric) where its fatty character adds creamy sophistication to powdery accords.

products.name: Irone Alpha
products.description:
When Orris Absolute (80% Irones) went past six figures in cost per kilogram, Irone Alpha stepped up to takes it place in most fragrances. While it doesn't have the complexity of Orris Absolute (which is a blend of Irone Alpha, Irone Gamma and Irone Beta), it is incredibly beautiful, powerfully diffusive and radiant.

Irone Alpha is sweet and fruity (towards a raspberry note) with woody and seedy nuances and a distinctly iris heart.

There is no question at all: no perfume lab is complete without this material. It is pricey but a little goes a long way. Effective from traces so we also offer it at 10% dilution in DPG.

products.name: Irotyl
products.description:
Irotyl opens dewy and almost misty before settling into dry, powdery orris root with a fruity undercurrent. A grape-like juiciness and faint herbal-carrot nuance set it apart. Light and diffusive, it reads as a modern, airy take on violet root.

Forty-four hours on a blotter means this is more than a fleeting top note — it carries the orris quality well into the heart. Pair it with ionones for a believable iris accord, or lean into the grape-like facet for fruity compositions where that juicy quality is unexpected and welcome.

Violet leaf absolute and carrot seed oil reinforce the natural orris impression. Heliotropin extends the powdery side. In rose compositions, a small amount of irotyl introduces an iris nuance that gives the heart a sophisticated, three-dimensional quality without requiring expensive orris concrete.

products.name: Irrozol
products.description:
The sophisticated Irrozol base was launched in the early 20th century by Chuit Naef & Cie and very quickly adopted by all of the great perfumer's of the time. It remained in constant demand until the ravages of the late 1990s led to its disappearance.

Today it returns in the form of Fraterworks Irrozol in all its complex glory, loaded with iris naturals and synthetics as well as muguet, rose, jasmine, orchid, woods and a particularly lovely ambrette seed note. Use it in overdose as the core of a multiflor fragrance or in smaller quantities to simply add floral interest to the heart of a scent.

products.name: Iso E Super™
products.description:
Iso E Super is probably the most popular wood chemical on the market today, with the high isomer Iso G Super being the single ingredient in the famed Molecule 01 of Escentric Molecules. Iso G Super is not available on the market as it is an IFF captive, but the next best thing (even if you are wishing to simply clone Molcule 01) is the IFF quality of Iso E Super.

This is the cleanest and most translucent version of this synthetic aroma chemical and it is fair to say that it improves almost every formula to which it added. It comprises a key part of the well known Grojsman accord which, in its original form is:

428 Galaxolide® 50 (IFF)
180 Iso E Super™ (IFF)
180 Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (Takasago)
60 Hedione® (Firmenich)

products.name: Isoamyl Acetate
products.description:
Isoamyl Acetate opens with overwhelming power—pure, sweet banana that can momentarily dominate everything in its path. This isn't subtle fruitiness; it's the concentrated essence of overripe banana peels mixed with British pear-drop sweets. At high concentrations, a sharp solventy character emerges, reminiscent of nail varnish remover, but proper dilution reveals its true nature: intensely sweet, heady fruitiness that captures the exact moment when tropical fruits reach peak ripeness. The material's remarkable potency means even traces can transform a composition.

Utilise Isoamyl Acetate with extreme restraint—typically at 0.1-2% in fragrance compositions to avoid artificial, candy-like effects. Its exceptional volatility makes it a pure top note with limited tenacity (around 4 hours), demanding careful support from longer-lasting materials. Use minute amounts to add authentic banana character to tropical accords or to create playful pear effects. In jasmine compositions, traces provide fruity lift without overwhelming the floral heart. Blend with other fruity esters like ethyl butyrate for complex fruit salads, or combine with vanillin for creamy banana dessert effects.

Iso or Not?

The critical difference between Isoamyl Acetate and Amyl Acetate lies in their molecular structure and resulting odour profiles. Isoamyl Acetate (3-methylbutyl acetate) features a branched carbon chain that creates its distinctive banana-pear character with remarkable intensity and sweetness. A

products.name: Isoamyl Benzoate
products.description:
This material demonstrates remarkable dual functionality based on concentration. At typical usage levels (up to 15%), it acts as a soft, sweet blender that harmonises and rounds out compositions—particularly valuable for smoothing harsh fruity esters and creating cohesive fruity-floral accords. Its waxy, balsamic character provides substantive foundation for volatile top notes.

At extreme dilution (0.1% or less), it transforms dramatically into a powerful vegetal modifier, creating realistic tomato plant effects. This concentration-dependent behaviour gives perfumers access to two distinct tools from one ingredient. The phenomenon occurs because pungent, green molecules have much lower odor thresholds than sweet, balsamic ones.

Use this when you need exceptional blending power without IFRA restrictions. Perfect for ylang-ylang, jasmine, and tropical fruit accords. Its 90+ hour substantivity makes it an excellent fixative, whilst its natural occurrence in benzoin provides clear synergistic pathways. The key is understanding dosage determines function—blender at high levels, special effect at traces.

products.name: Isoamyl Isovalerate
products.description:
Few materials capture the smell of a ripe apple as convincingly as this one. The fruitiness is rich, sweet, and thoroughly naturalistic — more orchard than candy shop — with apricot and mango notes rounding out the edges. A faintly jammy quality keeps it from feeling too clean or abstract.

The limitation is persistence. Under three hours on a blotter means this vanishes quickly without support. Pair it with longer-lasting fruity materials or fixatives to carry its apple character deeper into your composition. At its best, it provides a burst of realistic fruit in the opening that nothing else quite matches.

Champagne and cider accords benefit from its natural-smelling apple quality. Damascenone reinforces the fruity depth. In gourmand compositions a trace alongside chocolate or cognac materials adds an unexpected freshness that lifts the whole accord.

products.name: Isoamyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
At full strength isoamyl phenyl acetate smells primarily of fresh cocoa beans — dark, warm, and unmistakable. Dilute it and the honeyed-rose and beeswax facets open up, alongside a faintly animalic, castoreum-like depth that gives this material real complexity. The range is impressive: chocolate, honey, rose, and animalic warmth from a single material.

That cocoa character is its most celebrated quality. Combined with vanillin or ethyl vanillin, it produces convincing chocolate accords — one of the classic pairings in perfumery. But it works equally well in honey and beeswax compositions, where its floral-animalic side contributes naturalness. In warm floral bouquets, a trace brings a dark, sweet richness that stops the composition from feeling polished and sterile.

Heliotropin pushes the chocolate side further. Eugenol takes it toward carnation. Phenylethyl alcohol brings out the rose. Coumarin and benzyl benzoate add powdery warmth in the base. Its 172-hour blotter life means whatever direction you take it, the effect persists.

We also sell Amyl Phenyl Acetate which is more floral than chocolate.

products.name: Isoamyl Salicylate
products.description:
Isoamyl salicylate offers an orchid-like floralcy with balsamic warmth, while amyl salicylate presents a greener, more herbaceous character reminiscent of clover. This olfactory distinction stems from their different molecular structures.

Isoamyl salicylate excels in creating sophisticated floral accords, particularly orchid, lilac and hyacinth notes. Use at 1-5% concentration in fine fragrances, floral compositions, and fougères. It functions brilliantly as a middle-note modifier, enhancing complexity and diffusion.

See our demo formula “Kayak ”below of Jean Carles' Canoe (for Dana) which illustrates the use of this material in overdose.

While both the iso and standard forms of this material have uses, if you're only going to purchase one, we recommend Isoamyl Salicylate for its versatility across multiple fragrance families.

products.name: Isobornyl Acetate
products.description:
Isobornyl acetate opens with a bright, resinous pine-needle freshness that immediately evokes a walk through a fir forest. A gentle camphoraceous lift sharpens the opening. The dry-down settles into something warmer and more balsamic — clean, woody, and quietly persistent.

Combine it with coumarin and amyl salicylate and you have the skeleton of a fougère. It sits comfortably in the heart-to-base transition, lending piney structure without overwhelming lighter elements above it. In chypres and forest accords, it provides the coniferous backbone that holds everything together.

Use it alongside oakmoss, lavender, and rosemary to build classic masculine structures. It blends naturally with cedarwood and pine needle oils, adding stable forest depth where lighter top notes fade too quickly. One of the most affordable materials in the perfumer's palette — and among the most reliable.

products.name: Isobutavan
products.description:
Isobutavan (Vanillyl Isobutyrate) is a delightful gourmand chemical of white chocolate, cream soda and vanilla with nuances of apricot. It is indispensable for soap perfumers where it is a non-discolouring alternative to vanillin which causes soaps to blacken with time. 

Isobutavan is less powdery than vanillin and has a more thickening effect on a blend which can be particularly useful when combined with that crystalline to add a richer and more complete vanilla note.

Isobutavan blends extremely well with other sweet materials such as Vanillin Signature, Heliotropin, Veratraldehyde, Tonka Bean, Lactones and fruit materials like Pineapple Natpop, Wild Cherry and Pineapple Supreme.

products.name: Isobutyl Benzoate
products.description:
Isobutyl benzoate is an interesting material that should see see more frequent use. With soft fruit and powdery nuances, the vaguest hint of cinnamon and a definite musty green quality, this is a product that could find many uses as a blender and to provide character and naturalness to floral and fruity fragrances.

Isobutyl benzoate can be used to add leafy character to rose and geranium bases and it blends exceedingly well with cinnamyl cinnamate, amyl benzoate, rose and fruit materials, especially tropical fruits, many of which naturally contain this aroma chemical.

products.name: Isobutyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
This material opens with an intensely sweet honey-chocolate character that immediately captures attention with its warm, enveloping presence. You'll notice how the cocoa facet presents itself as dry and slightly bitter, more reminiscent of unsweetened cocoa powder than confectionery chocolate. The honey note brings a waxy, almost beeswax-like quality that adds natural depth and animalic warmth.

When you blend this material with vanillin or ethyl vanillin, it creates an instant chocolate illusion that reads as genuinely edible. This powerful synergy transforms both materials—the combination produces a chocolatey richness far exceeding what either brings alone. You can push this accord darker by adding patchouli for bitter dark chocolate effects or soften it with lactones for milk chocolate sweetness.

Use Isobutyl Phenyl Acetate at 0.1% to 10% in your compositions, but exercise restraint—its diffusive power easily dominates blends. In floral compositions, it brings honeyed warmth to rose and carnation while adding gourmand intrigue. For animalic accords, combine it with civet replacers to create warm, sensual honey-beeswax effects that feel both natural and sophisticated.

products.name: Isobutyl Quinoline
products.description:
Isobutyl Quinoline (Pyralone) is the classic leather chemical. Its discovery led the great De Laire company to invent the famed Mousse de Saxe base (our Saxon Moss) as it was considered too difficult to use alone. In the early years of the golden age of perfumery, this material was considered mossy, but nowadays it is more often seen as leathery. This illustrates how our perceptions of scent have changed over the decades.

Traces to 0.5% were key to many of the great 1970s – 1990s masterpiece gentlemen's perfumes and even today a textured and long lasting dry down is often created with small amounts of this marvelous material. 

Isobutyl Quinoline is extremely strong and seldom needed above 0.5% in a fragrance. It is also pricey so we offer it at 10% in Dipropylene Glycol. For those who have speciality needs for the material, we also offer it pure.

NOTE: This product should not be confused with 2-Isobutyl Quinoline (CAS 93-19-6) which we also sell. That product is much softer and far less common in perfume, though it makes an appearance in Creed's Aventus.

Blends well with the more rare Isopropyl Quinoline, Royal Leather, Saxon Moss, Sandexol, Artemal, and Castoreum Hyperessence (Robertet).

products.name: Isobutyl Salicylate
products.description:
Isobutyl salicylate has a sweet, herbaceous quality that recalls fresh clover fields on a warm afternoon. A gentle wintergreen coolness sits in the background without ever becoming medicinal, and the overall impression is soft, floral, and gently aromatic. It dries down to a pleasant, hay-like warmth with faint fruity undertones.

This is a fougère building block that works at unusually high doses without becoming harsh or overbearing. It provides the herbaceous-floral body that sits between lavender top notes and mossy-coumarinic bases. Use it in clover and orchid fantasy accords where it can form the structural backbone, or add it to carnation and hyacinth bases for sweet aromatic depth.

Pair isobutyl salicylate with coumarin and oakmoss for classic fougère architecture, or with lavender and clary sage for fresh aromatic blends.

products.name: Isocyclocitral
products.description:
Isocyclocitral opens with a piercing, almost suffocating green-aldehydic blast that transforms in dilution to reveal photorealistic wet earth and crushed stems. This powerful modifier captures the complete flower shop experience - sappy green foliage, damp soil, and that distinctive cool humidity. Its unique marine-grassy duality revolutionised fresh fragrances in the 1980s.

You'll find Isocyclocitral indispensable for cutting through oakmoss sweetness while lifting its top notes. Use sparingly at 0.1-3% where its impact is profound - Bedoukian noted "unusual effects obtained by small quantities cannot be achieved with other known synthetics." Its exceptional synergy with ionones adds dewy freshness to powdery violets.

The material excels in creating specific effects: tomato leaf accords, hyacinth compositions, and modernised pine notes for functional products. Combine with Triplal for intensely diffusive aquatic-green effects. React with methyl anthranilate to form woody-orange blossom Schiff bases for unique captive notes.

Difference from Citral

Though citral and isocyclocitral contain identical atoms, their structural arrangement creates entirely different olfactory profiles. Citral presents pure, linear lemon character - the dominant note in lemongrass oil and citrus compositions. Isocyclocitral delivers no citrus character whatsoever, instead creating complex atmospheric greenness reminiscent of a florist's workspace: crushed stems, humid air, wet earth, and that dis

products.name: Isoeugenol
products.description:
Isoeugenol is a very long lasting spice material with a distinctive clove, pimento and carnation character. It adds warmth to an otherwise cold or uninteresting drydown and it blends beautifully with regular eugenol and dihydroeugenol for a top to bottom carnation.

IFRA restricts the use of this lovely (and deceptively powerful) chemical to 0.11% of your finished product. However, if you need to beat the IFRA restriction, our popular Isoeugenol Replacer base may be just what you need.

products.name: Isoeugenol Replacer
products.description:
Isoeugenol was a key component of many historic perfumes (including Chanel's No 5) and is the best spice synthetic to take a rich clove and pimento note long in to the drydown of a scent. Unfortunately its use is now restricted to 0.11% of a finished product.

Other Isoeugenol "replacer" types such as Methyl Diantilis from Givaudan introduce unwanted nuances such as vanilla and while these materials are wonderful in their own right, they are not true replacers of Isoeugenol.

For that reason Fraterworks® offers Isoeugenol Replacer 296766, a complex blend of materials that mimics the top note elegance and the base note longevity of isoeugenol while providing all the volumizing power of the original material. Isoeugenol Replacer can be used at a whopping 7.35% of your finished product and doesn't introduce any unwanted notes.

products.name: Isoeugenyl Acetate
products.description:
Isoeugenyl Acetate is the acetylated version of Isoeugenol. It functions like a softer and sweeter version of Isoeugenol with less diffusion, however like its related alcohol it adds a lovely warmth to the dry down of a scent. It has a particularly good synergy with balsams and resins as evidenced by its use in Coco (1984) by Jacques Polge for Chanel at 1.2% (demo formula below).

Use Isoeugenyl acetate to add a soft carnation or clove note or use it in a gourmand Speculaas cookie accord. Oftentimes a little of this material is all that is needed to add an inviting rounding out of basenotes in a scent which may otherwise seem cold. It could be perceived perhaps as adding colour. It's value should definitely not be underestimated.

Previously unrestricted in use, this has now changed and the maximum use in a finished perfume under IFRA 51 is 0.9%. This is a powder and can be added to your fragrance compound directly as it will dissolve readily in the other materials.

products.name: Isojasmone B-11
products.description:
Isojasmone B-11 opens with a surprisingly herbal-vegetal facet reminiscent of fresh celery seed, immediately grounding its jasmine character in botanical reality. This distinctive green note prevents the material from reading as purely floral candy. The waxy, petal-like texture creates volume and substance that synthetic jasmine reconstructions desperately need.

Unlike cis-jasmone which can feel sharper and more penetrating, isojasmone offers a rounder, fruitier jasmine character that works beautifully as a heart note modifier. Use it at 0.1–1% to add natural jasmine presence to floral bouquets, or blend with quinolines for classic chypre constructions. The 32-hour substantivity on blotter extends to approximately 3 days at working concentrations.

Work with Isojasmone B-11 alongside methyl jasmonate and hedione for complex jasmine reconstructions. It blends excellently with undecanolide's fruity lactone character and the clean musk of ethylene brassylate. Ionones and methylionones provide excellent background support.

products.name: Isomuscone
products.description:
A complex floral and animalic musk (in the deer musk direction), Isomuscone is a very cost effective alternative to other members of the same family such as Muscone Laevo. Coming in crystal form, you simply add the powder to your formula and it will dissolve during resting.

Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) describe its synergies: “Although I love Isomuscone on its own, mixtures of it with other musks increase its perception. For in- stance, a mixture of Isomuscone with ethylene brassilate [sic] at a ratio of 80/20 is stronger than both chemicals smelled separately. This results from a strong synergy amongst ketones, lactones and dilactones. The same happens when mixing Globanone and Isomuscone. The mixtures of 20 percent Isomuscone + 80 percent Globanone, or the inverse, 20 percent Globanone + 80 percent Isomuscone, are stronger than the chemicals smelled separately. It is very common to see mixtures of Galaxolide, Helvetolide, Habanolide, Muscenone, Ambrettolide and ethylene brassilate. Mixtures of Isomuscone, Habanolide, Velvione [AKA Ambretone] and Globanone are very, very good — approaching perfection.”

Blends well with Aerolide®, Grojsman Plus, Miraclewood™ and Veticoeur™.

products.name: Isophytol
products.description:
Isophytol opens with remarkable subtlety—this is not a material that announces itself but rather one that whispers sophistication into every blend it touches. Its gentle floral-green character reads like crushed jasmine leaves rather than the indolic flowers themselves, providing the crucial naturalistic foundation that synthetic jasmine reconstructions desperately need. The distinctive tea-like quality adds an unexpected dimension of refinement, making this material indispensable for contemporary clean compositions that demand both complexity and restraint.

Use Isophytol at 1-5% when reconstructing jasmine absolute—it literally comprises 7% of the natural material, providing authentic depth without heaviness. Beyond jasmine, it excels in creating sophisticated tea accords where its dry-leaf character combines beautifully with bergamot and hedione for photorealistic Earl Grey effects. Use it to extend white florals like tuberose and gardenia, where its fixative properties anchor volatile top notes while contributing subtle green-herbal complexity that prevents these flowers from becoming cloying.

The practical applications of Isophytol extend far beyond its jasmine heritage into realms where delicate complexity meets functional performance. Its exceptional substantivity (up to 168 hours) makes it your secret weapon for creating lasting impressions without the heaviness of traditional fixatives. products.name: Isopropyl Myristate (IPM)
products.description:
Isopropyl myristate brings virtually no odour contribution to your compositions, functioning purely as a technical perfumery material. This clear, mobile liquid dissolves lipophilic fragrance materials effortlessly while maintaining complete transparency to the nose. Its exceptional spreading properties ensure rapid absorption without the sticky residue common to other solvents.

You'll find IPM excels in oil-based fine fragrances, beard oils, and solid perfumes where alcohol cannot be used. It enhances fragrance uptake into skin whilst paradoxically increasing perceived intensity through controlled dilution—a synergistic effect unique among perfumery solvents. Unlike DPG's tendency towards stickiness or TEC's hydrophilic nature, IPM maintains a dry, elegant feel throughout wear.

Use IPM at up to 85% in perfume oils for optimal fluidity and projection. Combine with crystals and resinoids only after pre-dissolving them in compatible materials. In reed diffusers, balance with alcohol to control evaporation rate and throw.

The abbreviation "MIP", derived from the French name "Myristate d'Isopropyle," is commonly used in French perfumery circles, particularly in Grasse. Both IPM (English) and MIP (French) refer to the identical compound—the ester of isopropyl alcohol and myristic acid.

products.name: Isoraldeine™ 70
products.description:
Isoraldeine 70 is the workhorse grade of Givaudan's alpha-isomethyl ionone line — 70% purity, which means roughly 30% of the mixture consists of other methyl ionone isomers. Those additional isomers are not waste; they contribute a woodier, drier, more leathery character that some perfumers actually prefer. This is not a lesser Isoraldeine 95 — it is a different tool.

We also sell Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra as the direct equivalent of Isoraldeine 70. Same molecule, same purity tier, same olfactive profile. The additional isomers in both give them more body and more woody backbone than the purer grades. Where Isoraldeine 95 is all violet finesse, Isoraldeine 70 brings violet muscle — it pushes through heavier compositions and holds its own against woods, leathers, and resins.

Use it in leather accords where its dry-powdery character enhances suede and hide notes. It is superb in fougères, where it bridges the lavender heart and the coumarin-moss base. And in large-volume productions where budget matters, it delivers serious violet impact for a fraction of what the 95 grade (and even more so the Cetone Alpha variant) costs. The two are not interchangeable — they are complementary.

products.name: Isoraldeine™ 95
products.description:
Isoraldeine 95 smells of soft, powdery violet with a velvety orris depth and a creamy, almost cosmetic quality. It is gentle and refined — the kind of material that makes everything around it smell more expensive. One of the most widely used materials in all of modern perfumery.

Use it to build violet, iris, and orris accords, or add it to virtually any composition for powdery radiance and diffusion. It was a key ingredient in the Grojsman Accord — the legendary combination that underpins Trésor and countless other modern classics. It bridges floral top notes to woody-amber bases like nothing else.

We also stock Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF), the equivalent of Isoraldeine 95, as well as Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha — the highest-purity variant, a costly treasure with an astonishingly beautiful floral radiance at low doses. For the woodier, more leathery side of this family, see Isoraldeine 70.

products.name: Isoraldeine™ Cetone Alpha
products.description:
More commonly known just as Cetone Alpha, this is the perfected methyl ionone surpassing even Iralia® in quality (and, notably, in price). It first emerged in the mid 1920s as a key material in the Cetonia and Amarante bases of Marius Reboul (1873-1952). This is, effectively, a highly refined version of Isoraldeine 95.

Cetone Alpha quickly became the go-to methyl ionone in Givaudan's internal product range, and, as it became easier to produce in larger volumes, it eventually hit the market as a non-captive material.

Compared to Givaudan's Isoraldeine 95 and Iralia (Firmenich's top product from this family with strong powdery nuances), Cetone Alpha is supremely floral. Used below 5% of a formula Cetone Alpha has an astonishingly beautiful and radiant floralising effect, while higher amounts add a rich iris and violet character.

Iralia typifies the early 20th century era of rich powdery fragrances (exemplified by Coty and Guerlain). Its first outing, and perhaps still its finest, was as a 25% overdose in L'Origan (1908) by Coty where it coupled with Dianthine, the famed De Laire carnation base.

On the other hand, Cetone Alpha launched the floral and radiant era beginning in the 1930s with Chanel's aldehydic Ivoire (1932) with its Florentine iris and Parma violet heart. Cetone Alpha is to the methyl ionones what Paradisone® is to the methyl jasmonates.

products.name: Ivy Dioxolane
products.description:
Ivy Dioxolane (Glycolierral) opens with an abstract impression that can be described as "intense smell of nothing" - this paradox reveals its true genius. The material creates a milky-green aura reminiscent of broken plant stems releasing their sap. This unique ivy-tomato vine character provides naturalistic humidity that transforms synthetic compositions into living gardens.

You'll find Ivy Dioxalane invaluable for taming aggressive herbal notes like lavandin, armoise, and tarragon without erasing their character. Use it at 0.5-2% to build authentic fig accords where its inherent milky-green duality eliminates the need for multiple modifiers. Its exceptional stability across pH 2-10.5 makes it perfect for functional fragrances.

The material's subtle "sweaty" undertone adds the realism that separates amateur from professional work. Combine with Stemone for photorealistic fig leaves or pair with lemon oils for unexpected roundness. At higher doses (2-8%), it becomes the textural foundation that allows sharp aromatics to coexist harmoniously.

products.name: Jabir Type Formula
products.description:
Introduced in 2014, Jabir by Kemi Blending Magic—a prestigious line under the Xerjoff umbrella—emerges as a captivating highlight in the brand’s alchemical-inspired portfolio. Crafted by perfumer Chris Maurice, this oriental floral fragrance unfolds with a vibrant opening of freesia, violet, and strawberry, setting a lively yet refined tone. The heart reveals a lush bouquet of rose, peony, and lily-of-the-valley, evoking an enchanting floral elegance, before settling into a rich base of agarwood (oud), musk, vetiver, patchouli, and vanilla—blending woody depth with a sensual, lingering warmth.

Kemi Blending Magic, founded by Xerjoff’s Sergio Momo, channels the mystique of alchemy into its creations, and Jabir pays homage to Jabir ibn Hayyan, the legendary ‘father of alchemy.’ Xerjoff’s reputation for opulence shines through here, with a composition that balances intricate floral notes against an oriental-woody foundation, delivering a fragrance that’s both sophisticated and evocative.

Top Notes: Freesia, Violet, Strawberry
Heart Notes: Rose, Peony, Lily-of-the-Valley
Base Notes: Agarwood (Oud), Musk, Vetiver, Patchouli, Vanilla

products.name: Jacintheme
products.description:
Jacintheme blooms with an intensely green, almost sappy floral character — true hyacinth rather than generic white flower. There is a waxy, balsamic quality underneath that gives it body and persistence. The overall impression is of freshly cut hyacinth stems on a cool morning.

This base works as a standalone hyacinth core or as a green-floral modifier in larger compositions. Add it to jasmine accords for a leafy green lift, or use it alongside lilac materials for a convincing springtime bouquet. It has real presence in the mid-notes, bridging the gap between fresh green topnotes and heavier floral hearts.

Jacintheme pairs beautifully with phenylacetaldehyde for added realism, or with galbanum for a sharper green edge. Try it against a muguet base for a classic lily-hyacinth duo. Keep doses modest — this base has serious throw and can overwhelm lighter neighbours.

products.name: Jacinthia Extra
products.description:
Jacinthia is a jewel of classical floral perfumery. It was used in the original No 19 for Chanel with traces of Z-11 10 MIP in another base illustrating the wonderful ability of these classical bases to blend with extremely modern synthetics.

Use in traces to enrich your scent or in a larger dose for an obvious hyacinth note. This luxurious base is enriched with many high class natural absolutes and oils, including the rare treasure: hyacinth absolute.

Jacinthia is wonderful in the classic French trilogy of Muguet, Hyacinth and Lilac. We recommend Lilac A07 and Coroliane for this purpose.

products.name: Jacée Extra
products.description:
Centaurée jacée (centaurea jacea) is a French meadow flower that has vanished from the perfumers palette in the 21st century. Once a beloved member of the esteemed violet / iris family it so inspired François Coty that in 1905 he released a fragrance named La Jacée based entirely on its delicate scent!

Blending beautifully with hawthorn, iris, violet, mimosa and cassie this really is a wonderful flower that should stage a comeback.

As with all our classical bases, Jacée Extra is enriched with large doses of the finest floral absolutes and oils. A mere trace adds complexity and luxury while an overdose can form the heart of an innovative perfume. What was old is new again.

products.name: Jasmal®
products.description:
Jasmal is a jasmine material that smells of the jasmine plant rather than the jasmine flower. It opens oily and herbaceous, with a clear note of tea and a lavender-like edge, and the mushroom is there but kept in check. The jasmine itself sits behind all of this — present, recognisable, but seen through leaves and stems rather than petals.

Use Jasmal to add green realism to a jasmine accord without adding sweetness. It is the green end of this family, so it brings leaf, stem and tea where Jessemal brings cream. It behaves like a green lactone: it smooths the rough edges of a floral and gives indolic, narcotic flowers a living, picked-this-morning quality.

Use it alone where Jasmonyl’s creaminess is unwanted. It works well with lavender and in tea accords, sits comfortably beside green materials such as galbanum and violet leaf, and lasts well over three hundred hours on a smelling strip. Against Jasmopyrane Forte it is the cleaner cut: the same material with less mushroom and a tidier edge.

Understanding the Jasmine Pyrans

Jasmal is one of a small family of jasmine materials that are all the same molecule in two forms. One form is green, herbaceous and mushroomy, with a tea note. The other is rich, creamy and petal-like, and lasts longer. Nobody sells either form on its own: every product in the family is a mix of the two, and the proportion is what you are buying.

Jasmal (IFF, CAS 18871-14-2) is mostly the green form: herbaceous, with pronounced tea and mushroom notes a

products.name: Jasmin 1109
products.description:
Copying in the perfume industry is no new thing. Just as every perfume company has their own variant of Aventus these days, the perfumers of the past also made products inspired by their competitors.

Jasmin Blanc (231) of Chuit Naef & Cie so inspired master perfumers of Roure Bertrand that they came up with Jasmin 1109, a wonderful jasmine base with nuances of narcissus that would go on to become wildly popular and feature in the some of the greatest fragrances. Bernard Chant took the base with him to IFF where he was the head perfumer and used it liberally and often. 

Jasmin 1109 was used in Aramis (9% along with 23 natural oils and absolutes!), Calandre, Oscar (1977) for Oscar de la Renta, Miss Dior (16%) and so many more. And now it can be used in your fragrances. Jasmin 1109 in its original form is IFRA compliant and so we present it to you completely unaltered.

products.name: Jasmin Blanc
products.description:
Perhaps the most famous jasmine base in history, this is the Fraterworks restoration of Jasmin blanc (Jasmin 231) of Chuit Naef & Cie. Used in such masterpieces as Joy by Jean Patou and First by Van Cleef and Arpels.

Luscious sweet jasmine blends with the seductive note of narcissus in this classic base updated for today. Overdose or under dose, it doesn't matter; Jasmin Blanc adds radiance and beauty.

This base was later copied by Roure as their Jasmin 1109 and it works perfectly well as a substitute.

products.name: Jasmin Fleurs
products.description:
The original Jasmin A490 by Chiris featured in such blockbuster fragrances as La Rose Jacqueminot and Jasmin de Corse by Coty — much loved by the Grand Duchess Olga Romanov. This base is the scent of wild jasmin blossoms floating on a warm breeze across the distance. It is an "absolute" type base but with a delicate softness that makes it far easier to work with at high doses than a true absolute replacer like Jasmin Imperial. Slightly updated from the classic formula to take advantage of the latest radiant jasmine molcules.

Usable at a massive 12% of your finished product, this is a perfect jasmin base for modern fragrances to add a touch of classic opulence and class.

products.name: Jasmin Imperial
products.description:
Jasmin Imperial is a French jasmine grandiflorum absolute replacer. In the words of M. De Laire, "Jasmin of Grasse is perfect" and if we may be so bold as to add, nothing but the flower itself can surpass the beauty of our Jasmin Imperial base.

Richly complex and constructed on the basis of the chemical composition of a particularly fine historic crop of genuine French jasmine absolute, Jasmin Imperial allows perfumers to return to the golden days of overdosing floral absolutes as it can be used at up to 2.5% of your finished product for IFRA 51.

This complex and true to life base is enriched with luscious and expensive natural absolutes and oils.

products.name: Jasmin Russe
products.description:
A warm spiced classic jasmine base in which Russian coriander takes pride of place to add natural freshness and a novel tone. Jasmin Russe is a beautiful companion to orange blossom and Dianthus notes, but holds its own as a jasmine soliflore.

Reminiscent of classical Jasmin Invar, a companion to the more well-known Muguet Invar, Fraterworks Jasmin Russe is a truly special jasmine that you will fall in love with. This is a base so beautiful that it makes you seek a reason to use it.

For a base that mimics the scent of jasmine blossoms floating on the air across fields of hay in the summer morning sun, you need look no further.

products.name: Jasmin Épicé
products.description:
Jasmin Épicé meaning "spicy jasmine" is one of the earliest Jasmin bases. It was used to great effect in L'Origan by Coty in synergy with the glorious Rose D'Orient base. It was created to utilise the most recently discovered jasmin molecules during perfume's age of discovery (the early 20th century) in conjunction with the finest spice oils.

Despite its vintage, Jasmin Épicé is still a truly capable workhorse jasmine base and it blends beautifully with citrus notes (especially bergamot and orange) and spices (including carnation bases such as Dianthus), making it ideal for oriental types.

products.name: Jasmine Absolute, Egypt
products.description:
While India is the largest general supplier of Jasmine Grandiflorum to the world, Egypt also has a roaring trade. Despite being the same species, the three main origins (India, Egypt and France) are very different.

Egypt: Light, diaphanous, delicate.
India: Rich, almost tuberose-like, intense
France: Creamy and unctuous, almost enfleurage-like

The Egyptian oil is the most "classic" and lends itself very well to modern fragrances when you need an obviously natural luxurious jasmine note to blend with a lighter minimalistic profile. It can also be used in richer floral blends where its sheer quality can add space and freshness without sacrificing volume.

Very small amounts are all that are needed to floralise a fragrance, but as history has shown us (see the demo formulas below), overdoses are also effective and incredibly beautiful. The only limit nowadays is the IFRA restriction of 0.6% of your finished product.

With supreme beauty comes high cost and cognisant of that we also offer this incredible absolute diluted to 10% with natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate, an odourless diluent derived from citrus.

If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the finest jasmine grandiflorum replacer on the market: Jasmin Imperial.

Origin: Egypt
Part: Flowers only

products.name: Jasmine Absolute, France
products.description:
Formerly the premiere source of Jasmine, Grasse in France (the epicentre of the perfume industry) has now but one supplier left. Most of the treasured oil from the small French harvest goes to houses like Chanel and Dior who still use it (albeit in traces) in some of their hallowed scents.

French Jasmine, despite being of the same type as Indian and Egyptian (Grandiflorum), is absolutely unique in its odour profile. It has a soft delicateness and full bodied naturalness that other jasmine oils, no matter how good, exhibit.

This extraction from V. MANE Fils is so unctuous it seems like it is the result of an enfleurage extraction. When smelling the original classic fragrances of Roudnitska and Jean Carles it becomes very obvious that their luscious and rich style was inspired by this oil and its sister: Rose de Mai from Grasse which exhibits a similarly complex and yet demure quality.

Pair this sublime Jasmine absolute with Orris Absolute Landes, French Violet Leaves and Rose De Mai from Grasse in our stunning restoration of the classical masterpiece 1000 by Jean Kerleo for Jean Patou (formula below).

Origin: Grasse, France
Part: Flowers only

products.name: Jasmine Absolute, Select
products.description:
Our Jasmine Select is an authentic Indian jasmine grandiflorum absolute - the quintessential white floral that has defined luxury perfumery for over a century - at a price that makes this precious material accessible for regular use. This product delivers the full character of jasmine grandiflorum: its intoxicating floral sweetness, warm honey-like facets, and the distinctive indolic richness that makes jasmine irreplaceable in perfumery.

While our signature Floral Concept jasmine offers the classic Indian-style profile found in masterpiece fragrances, and our opulent "gold" MANE jasmine provides an almost tuberose-like intensity, this Fraterworks® jasmine absolute captures the essential beauty of Indian grandiflorum in a form that's practical for daily work. It maintains jasmine's transformative power - its ability to add luminous floralcy in traces or create stunning soliflores when used more generously (within IFRA limits of 0.6%).

Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate.

Origin: India
Part: Flowers
Process: Solvent extraction

products.name: Jasmine Auriculatum Absolute
products.description:
Jasmine auriculatum does not smell like the jasmine you know. The first impression is green, grassy, and almost gardenia-like, with a surprising frankincense-like top note and rich balsamic warmth underneath. It is the most herbaceous and least conventionally floral of the three commercial jasmines.

Use it to bring green complexity to white floral compositions — it lifts jasmine accords out of the familiar and into the exotic. It pairs beautifully with tuberose, ylang ylang, and frankincense. A few drops add tropical depth and waxy richness to any floral heart.

Three jasmines, three entirely different flowers. Grandiflorum is the classic — clean, fruity, universally floral — while sambac is headier, more indolic, with orange blossom facets and narcotic richness. Auriculatum stands apart from both: greener, more gardenia-like, with a frankincense-balsamic dimension neither of the others possess.

products.name: Jasmine DEC Abs MD, India
products.description:
Jasmine DEC Abs MD opens with intensely sweet, narcotic white floral character—immediately recognisable as true jasmine. Rich fruity-banana facets emerge alongside the heady floral notes, while warm indolic undertones provide the carnal, sensual depth that defines this material. A herbaceous-tea quality and subtle clove-like spiciness add complexity that synthetic jasmine bases cannot replicate.

This decolourised absolute from LMR (Laboratoire Monique Rémy, now part of IFF) represents the pinnacle of jasmine extraction technology. The "DEC" indicates decolourisation via molecular distillation—a technique pioneered by Monique Rémy herself to remove colour while preserving the full olfactory profile. The "MD" confirms molecular distillation processing. This yields a pale, workable material rather than the typical dark reddish-brown of standard jasmine absolute, making it invaluable for light-coloured formulations without sacrificing any aromatic richness.

Indian jasmine (Jasminum grandiflorum) from Tamil Nadu delivers exceptional quality—richer and denser than Egyptian material with pronounced musky-coumarin undertones. Eight million hand-picked flowers yield just one kilogram of absolute, explaining both its cost and its irreplaceable value. The substantivity ensures your jasmine heart persists beautifully into the drydown. Blend with rose, ylang-ylang, tuberose, and sandalwood for classic floral orientals.

If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the

products.name: Jasmine Enfleurage Tincture 2%
products.description:
This product is now out of stock. It was a once-off product which will not be returning.

In the early days of the golden age of perfume (late 19th century to mid 20th century) jasmine oil was extracted by the only means known: enfleurage from animal fat pomade. This involves the repeated laying of thousands of single jasmine blossoms on a bed of highly purified and odourless fat. As the old flowers lost their scent, the fat (or pomade as it is known) was recharged with fresh flowers.

Most modern producers of enfleurage products now use palm or other vegetable oils, but in 2015 in collaboration with a producer of traditional enfleurage products, we commissioned a large quantity of classical jasmine enfleurage oil, known in French as “extrait (de pommade aux fleurs), № 36, de jasmin”, produced using the ancient method of extraction via animal fats. We are very excited to be the only company offering this truly remarkable piece of fragrance history for sale.

Our 2% tincture of that Jasmine extract is a work of perfume art. It is like no other jasmine product on the market, bearing many more of the natural facets of genuine jasmine flowers than any other extraction method. There is a magical quality to this product which is not apparent in plant oil based enfleurage.

The alcohol we use in all of our tinctures is purest food grade ethanol produced in New Zealand by a small batch distillery in the foothills of the glacier covered Southern Alps.

The flowers used to create this

products.name: Jasmine Grand “Enfleurage” CO2
products.description:
Jasmine Grandiflorum E-Pure Jungle Essence opens with the unmistakable scent of jasmine petals still dewy from morning mist. This revolutionary extract captures the living flower's ephemeral beauty through MANE's proprietary low-temperature extraction technology. The characteristic indolic richness remains present but softened, allowing delicate fruity nuances and green freshness to shine through. This is the most refined and true to life jasmine extract you'll find.

Jasmine E-Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils uses MANE's special CO2 extraction process (called Pure Jungle Essence) but with a twist: the starter material (jasmine flowers) is first extracted by modern enfleurage techniques using vegetable oils rather than animal fat as in times past. And so we have E-Pure Jungle Essence, rather than just regular Pure Jungle Essence.
