Until now a MANE captive, this treasure is sublime in the extreme and one of the surest ways to get a rare natural into your fragrant creations. Due to the high price and the hot demand, we offer this in its pure form (supplied by MANE as a 10% ethanol solution) but also in a 10% solution (so 1% pure jasmine extract) with naturally isolated triethyl citrate, our preferred odourless diluent which allows natural perfumers to have access to this precious material at reasonable rates whilst retaining their fragrances' "all natural" designation.

Use this extract when traditional jasmine absolute feels too heavy or animalic for modern compositions.

products.name: Jasmine Green “Enfleurage” CO2
products.description:
Jasmine Green E-Pure Jungle Essence from MANE has all the beauty of enfleurage extracted jasmine flowers but with a decidedly green and earthy quality. Additionally the special process by which it is made brings cinnamic and spicy notes to the fore that might otherwise be missed in a jasmine extract.

Combine this with Jasmine “Grand” E-Pure Jungle Essence for a truly complete jasmine note (a note you can't really obtain with regular solvent extraction of the flowers). Or use it with Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence to temper its sweetness and add natural depth.

Modern Enfleurage

Until recently a captive, E-Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils uses a non-destructive CO2 extraction process but with a twist: the starter material (usually floral matter) is first extracted by enfleurage using vegetable oils rather than animal fat as in times past. And so we have E-Pure Jungle Essence, rather than just regular Pure Jungle Essence.

This process is extremely time consuming and costly and so MANE offer it in a 10% ethanol solution only. Due to the high price and the hot demand, we offer this in its original 10% form but also in a further 10% solution with naturally isolated triethyl citrate, our preferred odourless diluent which allows natural perfumers to have access to this precious material at reasonable rates whilst retaining their fragrances' "all natural" designation.

This is Jasmine Green E-Pure Jungle Essence. We also stock Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence and Ja

products.name: Jasmine Petals
products.description:
Jasmin Petals is one of the nicest classic De Laire jasmine bases. Characteristic of its time, it is build around an overload of the known synthetics of the time, particularly benzyl acetate and is very powerful. Henri Robert used it in Chanel No 19 (1970) and it also features in the Guerlain men's chypre Derby (1985). Demo formulas of both are below.

Use it alone where you might normally use Benzyl Acetate for a more complex and beautiful jasmine note, or in combination with natural jasmine absolute or other jasmine bases for your own special accord.

products.name: Jasmine Sambac “Enfleurage” CO2
products.description:
Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence from MANE is one of the most extraordinary jasmine extracts I have experienced. On first sniff you do not smell Jasmine Sambac in the way you do with Floral Concept's incredible “Signature” Absolute (crafted in collaboration with Chanel); instead you smell jasmine, and orange blossom, grape soda and blueberries. This modern enfleurage CO2 extract has to be smelled to be believed.

Combine this with Jasmine Green E-Pure Jungle Essence which has temper the sweetness and add natural depth. This also has the potential to be part of some extremely interesting floral gourmands.

Modern Enfleurage

Until recently a captive, E-Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils uses a non-destructive CO2 extraction process but with a twist: the starter material (usually floral matter) is first extracted by enfleurage using vegetable oils rather than animal fat as in times past. And so we have E-Pure Jungle Essence, rather than just regular Pure Jungle Essence.

This process is extremely time consuming and costly and so MANE offer it in a 10% ethanol solution only. Due to the high price and the hot demand, we offer this in its original 10% form but also in a further 10% solution with naturally isolated triethyl citrate, our preferred odourless diluent which allows natural perfumers to have access to this precious material at reasonable rates whilst retaining their fragrances' "all natural" designation.

This is Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence. We also stock

products.name: Jasmine Sambac “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
From Floral Concept comes the most spectacular Jasmine Sambac you will ever experience. With the richest and most beautifully indolic dry down, this oil is the very same one used by Olivier Polge in Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) — see our "smells-like" formula for this perfume below. 

Jasmine Sambac has a much greener character than the Grandiflorum type (French, Indian and Egyptian) and immediately recalls the lovely scent of Chinese tea. Also, due to the chemical composition of extracts of Jasmine Sambac this product can be used at a much higher 4.1% of your finished fragrance, so really only price limits its high use.

products.name: Jasmine “Gold” Absolute, India
products.description:
Jasmine grandiflorum absolute is a luxurious oil that has been the trademark of fine fragrances (particularly the French type) for more than 100 years. This Indian absolute from MANE is rich, long lasting, and powerful. It is unquestionably the richest Indian jasmine on the market. It is, in fact, so opulent it presents with almost the same power as Tuberose absolute. That is the reason we call it our "Gold" type.

Very small amounts are all that are needed to floralise a fragrance, but as history has shown us (see the demo formulas below), overdoses are also effective and incredibly beautiful. The only limit nowadays is the IFRA restriction of 0.6% of your finished product.

With supreme beauty comes high cost and cognisant of that we also offer this incredible absolute diluted to 10% with natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate, an odourless diluent derived from citrus.

If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the finest jasmine grandiflorum replacer on the market: Jasmin Imperial.

We also now stock French Jasmine absolute from Grasse, Egyptian Jasmine Absolute and the Floral Concept classic version — our Jasmine “Signature” Absolute, India.

Origin: India
Part: Flowers only

products.name: Jasmine “Signature” Absolute, India
products.description:
We sell three types of Indian Jasmine Absolute. The first is our rich V. MANE Fils absolute, the second is this material from Floral Concept, and the third is decolourised Jasmine from LMR. The MANE material is an intense and deep version of Jasmine Absolute which almost verges on Tuberose. And then we have this product. This is what you will find in the masterpiece perfumes of companies like Dior, Chanel, Tom Ford and Amouage, while the MANE product suits luxury niche brands and artisanal products. We highly recommend having both in your arsenal.

Very small amounts are all that are needed to floralise a fragrance, but as history has shown us (see the demo formulas below), overdoses are also effective and incredibly beautiful. The only limit nowadays is the IFRA restriction of 0.6% of your finished product.

With supreme beauty comes high cost and cognisant of that we also offer this incredible absolute diluted to 10% with natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate, an odourless diluent derived from citrus.

If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the finest jasmine grandiflorum replacer on the market: Jasmin Imperial.

We also now stock French Jasmine absolute from Grasse, Jasmine Sambac Absolute, Egyptian Jasmine Absolute, and, as mentioned above, we also have Indian Jasmine Absolute from MANE, and LMR's Jasmine DEC Abs MD.

Origin: India
Part: Flowers only

products.name: Jasminlactone
products.description:
Not to be confused with the classic Jasmolactone (found in traces in nature in Osmanthus absolute), Jasminlactone (or Creamy Lactone) is essential for realistic replicas of the same.  It has prominent peach and apricot skin notes with a celery-like or vegetable undertone. It provides the heavy, waxy petal weight found in natural Tuberose and Jasmine absolutes. It feels thicker and more authentic to the natural oil.

Jasminlactone occurs naturally in high abundance in Jasmine grandiflorum and Jasmine sambac, as well as Tuberose, Gardenia, and Peach. It is the key to the waxy scent of real jasmine flowers.

It's a costly material, and ours (the highest quality on the market) is manufactured by Firmenich, but a little goes a long way.

products.name: Jasmolactone® Delta
products.description:
Jasmolactone® Delta by Firmenich (product 965414) is an incredibly powerful lactone with nuances of peach, coconut, cream and jasmine petals. Quantities between 0.1 – 1% make a profound contribution to white floral accords, naturalising and adding radiance.  

Jasmolactone® Delta blends beautifully with jasmin notes, Hedione®, the rose ketones, ethyl safranate, and other lactonic chemicals.

Also known as 5-hydroxy-7-decenoic acid delta-lactone.

products.name: Jasmoneige™
products.description:
The Hedione® family contains a number of products that are valued for different reasons. Classic Hedione (including high cis and Paradisone) represents the "dihydro" part of the family containing 35%, 70% and 90% Methyl Cis Dihydrojasmonate respectively.

More favoured, but significantly more expensive, is Methyl Jasmonate. Methyl Jasmonate occurs naturally in Jasmine flowers but exhibits more of a magnolia tonality. Zeon, a Japanese company, produces the finest form of Methyl Jasmonate on the market and they call it Jasmoneige™ — this product. Firmenich previously made it also under the trade name Splendione® but they have discontinued it to reduce public availability of products that can complete against its captive Paradisone®.

Jasmoneige has a light floral scent which is extremely beautiful. But despite its delicate odour, it has a great power and considerably less is needed to get a similar effect to Hedione. Jasmoneige blends perfectly with Hedione®, Hedione® High Cis and our own best selling base Paradise Molecule®.

products.name: Jasmonyl®
products.description:
Jasmonyl hits your nose as oily, waxy jasmine underscored by a pronounced mushroom earthiness. It’s not a clean, polished jasmine — there’s a green, slightly dirty realism here that reads as convincingly natural. That mushroom facet is the signature that makes it instantly recognisable.

Use Jasmonyl to add organic, earthy believability to your jasmine accords. Givaudan has balanced the two forms of this molecule so that the green mushroom and the creamy petal arrive together, and that is what makes it read as a flower rather than a note. Where Jasmal gives you the leaf and Jessemal gives you the petal, Jasmonyl gives you the whole bloom in one bottle.

Jasmonyl excels where you want jasmine that smells alive, not synthetic. Pair it with indole to push animalic depth further, or with Hedione to brighten its heavier facets. Its waxy texture grounds neroli and orange blossom accords beautifully, it sits naturally with lavender, and it carries unusually well in soap.

Understanding the Jasmine Pyrans

Jasmonyl is one of a small family of jasmine materials that are all the same molecule in two forms. One form is green, herbaceous and mushroomy, with a tea note. The other is rich, creamy and petal-like, and lasts longer. Nobody sells either form on its own: every product in the family is a mix of the two, and the proportion is what you are buying.

Jasmonyl (Givaudan, CAS 18871-14-2 and 63270-14-4) is Givaudan’s own balance of the two — green mushroom and creamy petal in one bottl

products.name: Jasmophore® 184195
products.description:
Jasmophore, famed for its use in the original Joy formula, opens with a wall of dense, heady jasmine that immediately conjures the richness of natural grandiflorum absolute. The character is profoundly indolic with a slightly rubbery, lactonic warmth that sits between salicylate freshness and animalic depth. It smells unashamedly vintage — full-bodied, opaque, and intensely diffusive.

This is a jasmine base engineered for classical composition styles: aldehydic florals, opulent chypres, and grand floral bouquets built with rose, civet, and amber. The thiophenes and furans within the formula provide a naturalistic complexity that single jasmine molecules cannot achieve alone. Pair it with aldehydes, galbanum, and musk to build a convincing 1930s floral structure, or blend with rose absolute and sandalwood for a lush white floral heart.

Use Jasmophore sparingly — its projection and opacity can dominate a composition quickly. Temper the indolic character by layering with lighter jasmine molecules like Hedione or methyl jasmonate. It rewards patience: the drydown softens into a creamy, animalic warmth that lingers for hours on skin and fabric.

products.name: Javanol®
products.description:
Javanol opens with rich, creamy sandalwood that immediately announces its exceptional quality. Rosy-floral facets emerge alongside subtle milky-lactonic undertones, creating complexity that rivals natural East Indian sandalwood. The clean, powdery character feels refined rather than heavy, while the radiant projection seems almost impossible given its base note weight.

This Givaudan molecule represents the pinnacle of sandalwood chemistry. Discovered in 1996, Javanol achieves what many consider the closest synthetic approximation to natural beta-santalol—the principal odour-active component in precious East Indian sandalwood oil. The 400-hour substantivity on blotter translates to extraordinary real-world performance, and its odour threshold makes it approximately 400 times more potent than comparable sandalwood synthetics.

Work with Javanol at 0.5–2% of your concentrate—its power means a little goes remarkably far. Even at trace levels of 0.02–0.1%, it functions as a radiance booster that lifts entire compositions. Blend with vetiver, patchouli, rose absolute, Iso E Super, and cashmeran for sophisticated woody accords.

products.name: Jessemal®
products.description:
Jessemal opens rich, creamy, and unmistakably jasmine. There’s a lactonic smoothness here that feels like actual petals — dense and voluptuous rather than green or airy. A subtle herbaceous note, almost celery-like, sits quietly underneath, adding just enough complexity to keep it interesting.

Use Jessemal where you want body. It is the creamy end of this family with only a trace of the green, so it fills out a jasmine, tuberose or white-floral heart without bringing mushroom or earth with it. If a white floral smells thin and sketched rather than fleshy, this is the material that gives it weight.

Layer it under indole for animalic depth, or beside Hedione and benzyl acetate for a fuller, more rounded jasmine heart. Its exceptional stability means the jasmine character holds true from application through to dry-down.

Understanding the Jasmine Pyrans

Jessemal is one of a small family of jasmine materials that are all the same molecule in two forms. One form is green, herbaceous and mushroomy, with a tea note. The other is rich, creamy and petal-like, and lasts longer. Nobody sells either form on its own: every product in the family is a mix of the two, and the proportion is what you are buying.

Jessemal (IFF, CAS 38285-49-3) is mostly the creamy form — the richest, most petal-like and longest-lasting of the group.

Jasmal (IFF, CAS 18871-14-2) is mostly the green form: herbaceous, with pronounced tea and mushroom notes and an oily, plant-like feel.

Jasmonyl (Givaudan, CA

products.name: Jonquil Extra
products.description:
Jonquils are members of the narcissus family. They have multiple blooms on each dark green stalk and they are a uniformly deep gold in colour. Their scent is sweetly cinnamic and rich with nuances of orange blossom.

Fraterworks Jonquil Extra (formerly just "Jonquil") is enriched with genuine jonquil absolute and its presence in a blend can be felt at very low quantities. This is the same jonquil type used at 2% in Je Reviens by Worth and also used by Coty in his great Jasmin de Corse (see demo formula below).

products.name: Jonquille Absolute, France
products.description:
Jonquil and Narcissus are variants of the same plant family (Narcissus). Visually the jonquil is all yellow (sometimes with a darker orange corona) while narcissus flowers have a golden corona surrounded by white petals.

Olfactorily, the Jonquil is warm, honeyed, fruity and floral while the narcissus is green, leathery and indolic with a vaguely animalic facet. These extracts are beautiful materials, and some perfumers blend them together for a layered floral complexity but there are also distinct uses for each so we highly recommend including both in your palette.

This Jonquil absolute is the finest on the market today. It is produced by LMR and comes from freshly gathered blossoms from the French countryside.

Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC with a touch of natural benzyl benzoate as a co-diluent to ensure complete solubility.

We also offer the very cost effective classical base Jonquil Extra (as seen in Coty's Jasmin de Corse, and Je Reviens by Worth).

Origin: France
Part: Flowers only
Process: Steam distillation

products.name: Juniper Berry Oil, Rectified
products.description:
This wonderfully fresh and fizzy rectified Juniper Berry oil is a signature speciality of LMR. With no off notes at all, this should be every perfumer's go-to Juniper oil.

Juniper features at 1.5% in The Dreamer byVersace, Aventus by Creed, Light Blue Pour Homme (2007) by Dolce & Gabbana, and Chanel's Sycomore (2016).

Juniper blends beautifully with Frankincense Oil, Armoise Oil, Ginger Oil and bases such as Pineapple Supreme and Permawood®.

Origin: Balkan Peninsula, Italy
Part: Berries
Process: Steam distillation and rectification

products.name: Karanal
products.description:
Karanal opens with radiant, powerful woody-amber character—dry, clean, and almost electric in its diffusiveness. Unlike heavier amber materials that sit close to the skin, Karanal projects outward with sharp clarity. Subtle fruity nuances reminiscent of watermelon add unexpected freshness, while the overall effect feels modern and energetic rather than warm and resinous.

This spiky woody character transforms florals into architectural statements and gives citrus compositions unprecedented longevity. You'll find Karanal provides the structural spine that connects volatile top notes directly to the base, creating verticality. When combined with macrocyclic musks, it forms the clean-sexy drydown that defined an entire generation of masculine fragrances.

Use Karanal at trace levels for invisible lift, or push it to 2% for aggressive woody projection. Mix it with ionones to create masculine florals, or pair with Ambroxan for that endless-freshness effect.

Karanal featured prominently in Gucci pour Homme (2003) and Frédéric Malle's Une Rose—both masterworks that showcased its ability to add radiance without heaviness. Sadly, European authorities designated Karanal a substance of very high concern, requiring products containing it to be reformulated by August 2023. Givaudan ceased supply during 2022. While alternatives exist, perfumers mourn the loss of this unique material that could energise compositions like nothing else.

products.name: Katafray “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Absolutely underrated and absolutely beautiful, Katafray Bark Oil is the next great men's fragrance just waiting to happen. With a light wood heart and a character that seems to float between a lighter gentler cascarilla bark and buddhawood, this is almost the perfect canvas for something novel and unique.

Blends wonderfully with Geosmin 1%, Cascarilla Oil, Mulacro Oil, Thujopsene ex Cedarwood, and Fleur de Cuir as well as Animalia™ CMP and Ambergris Intense.

Origin: Madagascar
Variety: Cedrelopsis grevei
Part: Tree bark
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Kephalis
products.description:
Kephalis is a rich woody and tobacco material that really holds its ground in a blend of lighter wood chemicals such as Iso E Super. Use it to add softness and velvety goodness to a wood accord, or simply use it alone for a more interesting take on amber wood than the classic patchouli ethanone family.

According to Givaudan, “Kephalis is a very versatile and rich product, used as a long lasting heart and base notes. It blends well with floral notes (jasmine, rose, violet, lavender, etc.) as well as sophisticated ambery, woody-aldehydic, tobacco and masculine creations.”

Though typically used between 2 – 5% of a total formula, Kephalis can be overdosed quite comfortably.

Extremely synergistic with Oud Intense, Patchouli, Iso E Super, Thujopsene, Sandalwood materials, Cetonal, Operanide and Ambrocenide.

products.name: Ketoisophorone
products.description:
Ketoisophorone delivers the exact aromatic signature of Buddleia flowers, that elusive butterfly bush scent that combines honeyed sweetness with dusty, woody undertones. This unusual material is deceptively strong—its musty-tea character can dominate at high concentrations. The tobacco leaf facet makes it indispensable for creating authentic cigarette and pipe tobacco accords where it bridges fresh green aspects with cured brown notes.

This material is essential for both tea and tobacco bases, owing to its unique ability to capture dried leaf aromatics. Use at 0.01-2% maximum in concentrate—its potency demands restraint. The material excels at adding depth to woody compositions where its musty sweetness prevents flatness, while in florals it contributes an intriguing dusty-honey backdrop reminiscent of late summer gardens.

Use ketoisophorone to achieve naturalistic effects impossible with conventional materials. It transforms simple tea accords into complex ceremonial blends, elevates tobacco compositions beyond simple vanilla sweetness, and gives woody bases an unexpected floral lift. Combine with ionones for violet-tobacco sophistication, blend with honey materials for Buddleia recreations, or layer with actual tobacco absolute for unprecedented depth. This is your secret weapon for compositions requiring that specific dried-flower dustiness found in nature but rarely captured in perfume.

products.name: Kewda Attar
products.description:
kewda — also spelled kewra — comes from the male flowers of the screwpine (Pandanus), a spiky coastal plant that grows along the Bay of Bengal. The flowers are picked at dawn and distilled into sandalwood oil over twelve to fifteen days, each day's batch of fresh flowers adding more depth. The Mughal emperor Babur described the scent as "moist musk" — an apt description of something humid, radiant, and honeyed.

The first impression is almost overwhelming: sharp, penetrating, intensely sweet. Let it settle and a luminous honeyed-hyacinth character emerges, greener and brighter than any European floral you have worked with. There is something of wind and salt in it — a solar, coastal quality that reflects where the plant grows. It opens like a top note but persists like a heart, and can cut through heavy bases with ease.

Use kewra attar as a floral heart in orientals, or to sweeten woody bases with green-honeyed radiance. It pairs beautifully with rose, cardamom, saffron, and sandalwood. Keep doses restrained — kewra has extraordinary projection and easily dominates a composition. Best appreciated well diluted, where its complexity unfolds.

The screwpine (Pandanus odoratissimus) is a dioecious plant — male and female flowers grow on separate plants. Only the male flower spikes are used for kewra attar; the female produces a segmented pineapple-like fruit with no fragrance value. You may already know the pandanus plant from Southeast Asian cooking, where the leaves are used t

products.name: Koavone®
products.description:
Koavone opens with bright balsamic-pine freshness that quickly reveals its complex woody-violet heart. This sophisticated former IFF captive delivers the powdery elegance of classic methyl ionones while adding warm amber depth impossible to achieve with older materials. The subtle toffee-caramel facet provides unexpected gourmand intrigue.

You'll find Koavone invaluable as a modern replacement for methyl ionones, offering superior diffusion and stability. Use it at 1-10% to enhance amber accords where it synergistically amplifies warmth and radiance. At higher levels (up to 30%), it creates powerful aldehydic-pine effects perfect for fresh woody compositions.

The material's isomeric complexity creates its unique character - commercial Koavone contains multiple isomers that work synergistically. Build sophisticated violet-orris accords by combining with alpha-ionone and natural orris. Create rich woody structures by pairing with Iso E Super and sandalwood molecules for multi-layered depth.

products.name: Kohinool®
products.description:
Kohinool opens with quiet, polished warmth — a woody-amber character that reads refined rather than heavy. A distinctly floral quality sets it apart from other amber materials, with dry vetiver-like depth beneath. Subtle raisin sweetness and quiet dryness complete an unusually elegant profile.

This is a material you can build entire bases around — few amber chemicals tolerate such generous dosing without distortion. Twenty-four hours on blotter gives you woody-amber warmth that anchors compositions through the full drydown. It works across fine fragrance, soaps, and functional products with equal conviction.

Combine with Iso E Super and cedarwood to build transparent woody-amber accords, or layer with labdanum and vetiver for richer oriental depth. The floral facet makes it unusually sympathetic to rose and iris. A backbone material that rewards bold use rather than cautious traces.

products.name: Kumquat Base 270258
products.description:
Kumquat Base from Firmenich opens with a sparkling, tangy burst — sweeter and more complex than orange, with a distinctive candied-peel quality and fizzy green brightness. The effect is mouth-watering: somewhere between mandarin zest and preserved citrus rind. Firmenich captive molecules add facets you cannot source elsewhere.

Kumquat is the only citrus fruit eaten whole — sweet rind over sour flesh — and that sweet-tart contrast defines the note. Use this base to add exotic citrus complexity beyond standard orange, bergamot, or lemon. It lifts fresh compositions and adds a sparkling, piquant twist to florals.

Pair kumquat with ginger and pink pepper for an energising opening, or with neroli and jasmine for a sparkling floral heart. It bridges beautifully into woody bases — try it over cedar or vetiver. The name comes from Cantonese: golden orange.

products.name: Kyphi Vert
products.description:
Kyphi Vert is a co-distillation — vetiver distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is vetiver taken somewhere it has never been: darker, more resinous, genuinely oud-like.

The vetiver is immediately recognisable — earthy, rooty, green — but the gurjun co-distillation introduces a remarkable labdanum-like warmth and a cinnamic nuance reminiscent of methyl cinnamate. This combination pushes the material into territory that recalls Guerlain's Djedi (1927), Jacques Guerlain's legendary vetiver pushed to its smoky, animalic extreme. There is genuine oud-like depth here. This is, effectively, a prêt-à-porter attar.

Use it wherever you want vetiver with ritualistic weight. It bridges Western vetiver compositions and Middle Eastern oud traditions without synthetics. Layer it with rose for an instant oriental, or let it stand alone as a base that needs nothing else.

products.name: Labdamate
products.description:
With gourmand perfumes being all the rage today one can never have too many aromachemicals that trigger thoughts of food. Labdamate (Ethyl hydrocinnamate) is ethereal and sweet, bringing to mind rum, fruit, wines and honey. It also has a floral side reflecting the cinnamic facets of pink rose and hyacinth. Comprising part of labdanum naturally, it is no surprise that this product blends exceedingly well with that material.

Labdamate contributes cinnamic sweetness to the masterpiece oriental fragrance Opium Pour Homme (1995) by Jacques Cavallier for Yves Saint Laurent.

products.name: Labdanum Absolute “Super Premium”
products.description:
We are very excited to be able to offer this intense and rich “super premium” labdanum (cistus) absolute, a speciality of Floral Concept in Grasse and certainly the finest we have seen. It is a near-black and extremely viscous extraction and consequently is offered here either pure or at a 50% dilution in odourless Triethyl Citrate (100% natural isolate from citrus). 

In comparison to labdanum resinoid, this absolute is lighter, more volatile, and has a cleaner floral-balsamic scent that outshines the thicker, earthier resinoid. This is the labdanum of the golden age of perfumery. You will never need another.

Part: Exudate of leaves and flowers
Method: Ethanol extraction of concrete.
tags: locale:heat needed for pure. Diluted is still thick.

products.name: Labdanum Light Absolute
products.description:
This honey-sweet light labdanum absolute (sometimes referred to as labdanum clear) is a truly sublime cistus material. This light product has a clear and bright tonality and can act to bridge the gap between the deep intense base notes. of standard dark labdanum absolute and resinoid and the dazzling vibrant top notes of cistus essential oil (AKA rock rose).

Our light labdanum is a specialty product of our supplier and is simply the most elegant light product on the market. This is a kinder gentler labdanum that is perfect when you want the rich balsamic effects without the intense animalic notes of some absolutes.

Origin: Spain (processed in Grasse, France)
Variety: Cistus ladaniferus
Part: Exudate of leaves and flowers
Method: Ethanol extraction of Cistus ladaniferus L.concrete.

products.name: Labdanum Resinoid
products.description:
Labdanum resinoid opens with a dark, honeyed sweetness layered over balsamic warmth. An unmistakable ambergris-like richness defines its heart. Beneath that, you find dry leather, aged tobacco, and a faintly animalic depth that makes this material utterly captivating.

This is the material that built the amber accord. Pair it with vanillin and benzoin for the classic combination, or lean into its leathery side alongside oakmoss and patchouli for sophisticated chypres. It excels as a fixative, anchoring volatile top notes and extending the life of your blend.

Use labdanum resinoid to add warmth and body to oriental bases. Try it with bergamot and vetiver for a refined masculine accord. Its dark colour limits use in pale formulations, but that rich resinous character is irreplaceable when you need genuine amber depth.

Labdanum resinoid and labdanum absolute both come from the same crude gum harvested from the rockrose shrub, but they differ in extraction and character. The resinoid is extracted with a hydrocarbon solvent, producing a thick, dark, waxy material with full-bodied earthy depth. The absolute is the alcohol-soluble fraction, cleaner and brighter with a more refined sweetness. Use the resinoid when you want raw depth and body in your base. Choose the absolute when your formula needs clarity and elegance.

products.name: Labienoxime 10%
products.description:
Labienoxime (Cassis Oxime 10%) is blackcurrant at its freshest and most natural. Juicy, fruity and green, it sparkles with grapefruit and carries a soft sage-flower nuance underneath. Best of all, it skips the sulphury, catty edge that so many cassis materials drag along, staying clean and bright.

Use it as a modifier to thread fresh blackcurrant realism through fruity florals, or to add a grapefruit sparkle to citrus tops. It brightens modern muguet, freshens lavender and fougère structures, and lends a green, fruity lift to rose.

This is extremely potent so you may find it easier to work with at 1% dilution rather than the Givaudan supplied 10%.

products.name: Lactojasmone
products.description:
This lactone transforms white florals from simple to sumptuous. Its creamy-milky texture adds tangible waxy petal quality that smooths harsh synthetic edges into cohesive luxury. Think of it as the material that gives jasmine and tuberose their velvety depth rather than just their scent.

Use it to anchor opulent florals with exceptional staying power—it lasts eight days on a blotter. Add milky accents to sandalwood reconstructions where synthetics alone feel hollow and incomplete. In stone fruit accords it mimics that fleshy, succulent texture you get biting into fresh peach, moving compositions beyond abstract fruitiness into photorealistic territory.

Blend with hedione for radiant jasmine diffusion or combine with other lactones for sophisticated peachy-coconut complexity. In gourmand work it provides creamy foundations that soften vanilla and caramel into decadent richness. Watch how it underlines fruity facets in osmanthus whilst adding tropical depth to frangipani—it's a masterful harmoniser across floral families.

products.name: Lactone Storm
products.description:
With decidedly peachy and apricot nuances, Lactone Storm is a balanced base of classic fruit aroma chemicals and deluxe lactones. Lactone Storm works as an alternative to the more common Undecalactone Gamma (Aldehyde C-14 so called) and imparts a far more modern and interesting character to a scent. This base takes the popular peach fruit note and makes it more diffusive, radiant and long lasting.

As well as being used for fruit notes, Lactone Storm blends beautifully with white florals, particularly Florol, Mayol and Cyclomethylene Citronellol. Blend it with Irotyl (Orris Capronate) and Iralia® for a radiant fruity orris. Lactone Storm is sublime with Gardenia J. Ellis and transforms the marvellous Visa (2007) by Aurélien Guichard for Piguet, the demonstration formula for which can be found below.

products.name: Laevo Citronellol
products.description:
Laevo Citronellol (or l-Citronellol) is the S-enantiomer of citronellol while Citronellol 98 is the racemic. For most of us that is not particularly important, but what it means in a real world application is that the more expensive nature-identical laevo type is far more beautiful and closer to the scent of rose than regular citronellol which has acessory notes of citrus.

This is a prestige aroma chemical and Takasago is the superior manufacturer. We highly recommend it. You can use it one-for-one in place of Citronellol 98 for a more lush result.

Laevo-Citronellol blends beautifully with Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Geraniol Extra, Rose Oxide Laevo, and Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon.

Laevo-Citronellol is suitable for fine fragrances, detergents and soaps.

products.name: Laevo Menthol
products.description:
Laevo Menthol hits immediately with crystalline peppermint coldness that penetrates and diffuses powerfully. Its camphoric sweetness adds medicinal depth whilst maintaining clean freshness. The cooling sensation lingers, creating perceived temperature drop on skin.

You'll find l-menthol essential for functional perfumery in shaving products, aftershaves and cooling gels where its TRPM8 receptor activation delivers genuine cooling. It excels at minute doses for lifting top notes and adding sparkle to citrus accords. Use it to create authentic peppermint and spearmint systems or emphasise floral notes through menthyl esters.

Combine l-menthol with eucalyptus and camphor for enhanced cooling effects or blend with peppermint oil to intensify mint character. Pair with rose absolutes where menthyl esters highlight floral sweetness. This crystalline powerhouse transforms compositions with mere traces.

Menthol vs Menthone

Menthol laevo smells medicinal, icy and camphoric whilst menthone offers sweeter, gentler mint with herbal-green character. Where menthol delivers aggressive cooling punch that dominates compositions, menthone provides subtle mint freshness that enhances florals. Choose menthol for functional cooling and powerful mint impact; choose menthone for delicate mint nuance in complex accords.

products.name: Laurel Noble Oil
products.description:
Laurel Noble oil delivers an uncompromisingly fresh, spicy-camphoraceous signature. Its robust, diffusive power is the very backbone of classic aromatic Fougères, lending an iconic, invigorating profile that defines quintessential masculine elegance.

Use this material to build the aromatic heart of Fougère and Chypre structures. Combine it with lavender, bergamot, and cedarwood to amplify its signature herbaceous character. Dose below 0.5% for a subtle lift or use at 1-5% for a dominant, bracing effect.

products.name: Lavandin Abrialis Oil
products.description:
Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander (Lavandula spica). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents.

The most popular forms are Lavandin Grosso, Lavandin Super and Lavandin Abrialis. The Abrialis cultivar was the first to be created in the 1920s and was, for a very long time, the most popular. Due to disease, Abrialis fell into disuse and the stronger (and newer) Lavandin Super became the favoured breed. However, in the 1970s Pierre Grosso created the eponymous Lavandin Grosso which was stronger and more prolific.

Nowadays the Grosso type sees more sales and wider use but the Abrialis has a charm all of its own and is more floral than the other two making it particularly well suited to that rare gem: the feminine lavender scent.

Lavandin is most often found in gentlemen's perfumes (such as Azzaro and Paco Rabanne) but can be a wonderful addition to unisex and female scents (as demonstrated by our formula Ravishing which is derived from a GCMS of Musk Ravageur by Frederic Malle). It also works well as a naturaliser in linalool rich bases (some muguet types for example).

We also have a lovely New Zealand grown Lavandin Grosso Oil and Lavandin Super (which, like this Abrialis oil, is also from France).

Origin: France
Variety: Lavandula hybrida Reverchon
Part: Flowers

products.name: Lavandin Absolute
products.description:
Lavandin (a cross between spike and regular Lavander) should not be passed over for its more dignified and popular ancestor Lavender. It may be the rought and tumble little brother but it has a majestic richness all of its own and for those looking for a decidedly present lavender note, this wonderful Lavandin Absolute from Payan Bertrand it just what you need.

It has 6% coumarin, doubling that of our decolourised Lavender Absolute (and matching that of our pure Lavender “Signature” Absolute) and it shows. Despite being a Lavandin product, this is sweeter and more hay-like in the drydown but having a more camphoraceous top note. But don't be put off, the camphor is so well balanced that this could easily pass as a lavender absolute or even oil (despite its intense green).

Origin: Provence, France
Part: Flowers only
Method: Solvent extracted

products.name: Lavandin Absolute Enfleurage
products.description:
This is not ordinary lavandin absolute. LMR's Enfleurage 2.0 process uses a fully organic, bio-sourced solvent at low temperature — no hexane, no petrochemicals — to capture lavandin's fragrance with extraordinary fidelity. The result opens with fruity pear notes and fresh herbs, develops into a rich coumarinic hay-like heart, and dries down warm and tea-like. This has become my personal favourite lavandin. The elegance of this luscious absolute cannot be overstated.

Standard lavandin oil is camphoraceous and short-lived. Conventional lavandin absolute is richer but carries faint solvent traces. This enfleurage version preserves delicate top notes that both methods lose, giving you the most complete, most luminous lavandin extract available. The coumarin content provides natural fixation and a rounded, long-lasting sweetness.

Pair it with bergamot and oakmoss for refined fougère construction, with clary sage and tonka for warm herbaceous depth, or with patchouli and labdanum for a dark aromatic base. It works beautifully in colognes, where its fresh-fruity opening and hay-sweet drydown create something that smells simultaneously classic and modern.

products.name: Lavandin Grosso Oil
products.description:
Lavandin Grosso opens with fresh herbaceous-floral character—clean, camphoraceous, and immediately evocative of lavender fields in Provence from which our oil hails. The sweet floral heart develops quickly, while woody undertones add depth without heaviness. The linear quality that some consider a limitation is actually a strength: predictable, consistent, and exceptionally versatile.

Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander (Lavandula spica). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents.

An excellent blender for labdanum (essential oil, resinoid and absolute), Oakmoss, Vetiver and its by-products, Patchouli, Douglas fir needle, Coumarin, Clary sage, chypres and fougeres.

products.name: Lavandin Heart
products.description:
Lavandin Heart smells like lavandin with its best face forward: clean, fresh and floral, with a soft herbaceous body. The harsh, camphor-like sharpness of ordinary lavandin is gone. In its place sits a warm, hay-like, almost gourmand sweetness that reads close to fine lavender.

Use it as a cleaner, rounder lavender at the top and heart of fougères and colognes, where it lifts without the medicinal bite. Its gentle sweetness sits beautifully with coumarin and tonka, and it bridges into gourmand territory. Bergamot, oakmoss and clary sage all sharpen and extend it.

products.name: Lavandin Super Oil
products.description:
When the original Lavandin (Abrialis) began to vanish due to disease, a new cultivar arose. That cultivar was a super hero in the commercial lavender and lavandin market as it saved the day. Appropriately named Lavandin Super Oil remained the most common oil until the 1970s when a stronger and larger variety called Lavandin Grosso began to replace it.

Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander (Lavandula spica). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents.

We also have a lovely New Zealand grown Lavandin Grosso Oil and an intense classical Lavandin Abrialis oil.

Origin: France
Variety: Lavandula hybrida Reverchon
Part: Flowers

products.name: Lavender Absolute, Decolourised
products.description:
From Payan Bertrand, one of the leading producers of luxury essential oils in Grasse, comes a truly beautiful lavender absolute which is, for all intents and purposes, colourless. While lavender absolutes are usually intensely green, this product maintains a classical lavender scent without the risk of staining your fragrance.

With 3% coumarin (around half the amount in our full-colour Lavender “Signature” Absolute) this French lavender extract has a lovely balanced hay note in the dry down and a tempered top note, this is a must-have for modern perfumers.

Origin: Provence, France
Part: Flowers only
Method: Solvent extracted and molecular distilled

products.name: Lavender Diva Oil
products.description:
Lavender Diva opens with remarkably clean, precise floralcy that immediately distinguishes it from standard lavender oils. This sophisticated cultivar delivers pure lavender sweetness without the mushroom-earth secondary notes that mark traditional varieties. The exceptional 50-55% linalyl acetate content creates green-citrus facets with subtle mint-caraway nuances, while lower linalool levels provide fresher, sweeter floral attributes without sharp herbaceous edges.

You'll find Lavender Diva invaluable for modern compositions requiring lavender's signature without rustic character. Use at 1-10% where its linear, soft profile won't overwhelm delicate florals. The material's 1.2% borneol content adds subtle camphoraceous-pine undertones that enhance rather than dominate. Its beautiful warm amber drydown distinguishes it from the dusty-earthy finish of standard lavenders, maintaining floral elegance throughout wear.

The cultivar excels in fine fragrance applications where traditional lavender reads too agricultural or medicinal. Combine with bergamot for sophisticated colognes, coumarin for modern fougères, or rose absolutes for refined floral bouquets. Its cleaner profile makes it perfect for contemporary interpretations of classic aromatic structures without vintage heaviness.

Difference from Other Lavenders

Traditional French lavender (25-45% linalyl acetate, 25-38% linalool) provides the classic aromatic profile but often carries earthy-mushroom undertones and dusty dry

products.name: Lavender Oil “Avice Hill”
products.description:
Lavender “Avice Hill” NZ ALPS P&N is an incredibly fine lavender angustifolia variety grown in New Zealand at the foothills of the rugged and wild Southern Alps (pictured), located in the South Island.  The lavender plants are raised on glacial water which takes thirteen years to travel down the alpine slopes in the form of purified ice.

Because every second counts when working with cut lavender, our partner farm distills the oil-rich flowers in under one hour of harvesting. No other producer boasts this speed and the resulting oil is one of the best in the world.

In comparative testing against the finest lavenders from the fragrance industry, this oil comes first every time. When other lavenders dry to a dusty or earthy note, our Lavender “Avice Hill” maintains is superb floral character with a sweetness and intensity not found in any other variety. The near-mythical lavender Barreme is the oils that would have been the closest match to the sublime scent, longevity and elegance of this pure New Zealand essential oil. Tragically true lavender Barreme is now extinct due to French growers adopting genetically modified varieties to replace the old wild lavender fields due to higher yields of oil - an oil inferior in quality.

Lavender “Avice Hill” is astonishingly high in linalyl acetate content giving it a more elegant and refined floralcy than most. This is the mark of true quality in lavender. Our partner farm neither spikes nor blends across harvests to meet commercialised

products.name: Lavender Oil, Balkans
products.description:
Balkan lavender oil opens with balanced floral sweetness where linalool's fresh character meets linalyl acetate's fruity depth. Grown in Vojvodina's semi-dry Mediterranean climate, it presents gentle herbaceous notes without excessive camphor. The higher sesquiterpene content adds subtle woody complexity distinguishing it from other origins.

You'll find this oil valuable for creating authentic lavender accords with distinctive character. It excels where balanced composition matters, with 24-40% linalool and 7-32% linalyl acetate providing versatility across applications. Use it in aromatic compositions where its moderate pricing and consistent quality offer excellent value without compromising sophistication.

Blend Balkan lavender with bergamot for fresh cologne structures or combine with rosemary for herbaceous depth. Pair with eucalyptus where its balanced character prevents medicinal dominance. This oil performs beautifully in both fine perfumery and functional fragrances.

Lavender Variety Comparison

Provence Lavender “Signature” Oil delivers supreme refinement with highest linalyl acetate (40-45%) and minimal camphor. Avice Hill excels with 40-50% esters creating refined fruity-floral sweetness with candy undertones. Diva presents sweeter, less herbaceous character ideal for softer applications. Lavandin oils offer intense herbaceous aromas with 6-12% camphor at lowest cost for functional perfumery.

products.name: Lavender Oil, English
products.description:
Grown on a single estate in the Hampshire chalk downs, this oil is a quintessential expression of the English landscape. Unlike the sweet, "jammy" profiles typical of Provencal harvests, this variety is defined by a crisp, silver character. It offers an austere, herbal profile that prioritises clarity over balsamic weight, making it the definitive choice for those seeking a traditional, dry lavender.

The olfactory profile is remarkably bright, leaning into a medicinal clarity that provides immediate impact in the top notes. It possesses a refined camphorous edge that lends a soapy, starched-linen freshness to formulations. This lack of heavy sweetness allows the oil to remain transparent and bracing, maintaining its integrity even when used in high concentrations.

For the perfumer, our English lavender provides a vertical, piercing light that is indispensable for recreating 19th-century-style colognes and British lavender waters. It is a functional and aesthetic staple, offering a hygienic purity that anchors a composition in the noble tradition of English horticulture. It is a rigorous, honest botanical.

In contrast, our Signature French Lavender (LMR Provence) represents the height of Provencal luxury, leaning away from herbal austerity and into a profound floral sweetness. While the English variety provides a bracing, vertical top note, this French oil offers a tenacious, "golden" warmth that acts as a link to the heart for fine fragrance.

products.name: Lavender “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
It is almost impossible to put into words how truly incredible this Lavender “Signature” Absolute is. This is so rich it is a solid mass, not a liquid. There is not a single bad note here, just 100% pure lavender. This is so universally loved by our staff that we keep a small container in the laboratory so we can have the pleasure of smelling it through the day.

We have tested many lavender absolutes from all the top French houses and this is not just better than everything we sampled - this is better than anything we ever imagined possible with a lavender product.

A single sniff transports you to the middle of Provence where the scent of lavender soaks the air. This absolute is rich with notes of dried fruits, tonka beans and herbs.

There does not exist under the sun a more profoundly beautiful expression of French lavender.

Pair this with Lavender “Avice Hill”  (nourished by the glacial waters of the Southern Alps), our exquisite small batch Lavandin, Grosso Oil, and the classic De Laire Foin Coupé base for a truly sublime fougère.

NOTE: this absolute is extremely thick (to a point of being nearly solid) but can be added directly to your fragrance compound as-is. To bring it to melt point a fairly significant amount of heat is required. For that reason we offer it at 50% dilution in a blend of 50% triethyl citrate. This creates a viscous but pourable solution making it far easier to work with than pure.

We also stock a beautiful practically colourless lavender absolut

products.name: Lavender “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Renowned through the centuries and found in so many masterpieces of fragrance history, Provence Lavender is truly the Crème de la Crème, and LMR is the finest producer and supplier today.

In the 1960s the Provençal wild high altitude lavender supply began to dry up and so farming became the norm. Lavandula angustifolia Mill. was the variety of choice and all major regional suppliers took stakes in various farms to maintain their own special quality of oil.

Over the course of many months we have gathered lavender samples from all of our suppliers (MANE, LMR, Payan Bertrand, Floral Concept, Biolandes and Robertet). We have tested them in every way possible, from the sniffing of mouillettes to including them in various demonstration formulas.

Each oil has its own character but ultimately one stood out as the true reference for French lavender oil; that oil was the COSMOS certified Lavender Oil Provence from LMR (Laboratoire Monique Remy, part of IFF). It is so good we call it our signature lavender.

Lavender “Signature” Oil opens with the most classical lavender scent - it is the epitome of fine French lavender and it's superior quality was demonstrated time and again through trials. This lavender has a diffusion that far surpasses all others and a stable drydown that never seems to reach an earthy conclusion; its sweetness and floralcy just go on forever.

Lavender “Signature” Oil is a masterpiece of meticulous farming and skilful distillation. For a lavender extravaganza p

products.name: Leather Oud
products.description:
Leather Oud is a synthetic base created around a captive molecule found in natural oud. This material is a beast - extremely strong and doesn't smell good at all until you dilute it considerably. The material delivers primarily a leather accord with a nice oud bed, ranging from saddle leather to biker jacket profiles.

You should deploy Leather Oud 293316 with pre-dilution to 10% or 1% solutions due to its overwhelming neat potency. This specialty base transforms dramatically upon dilution, revealing sophisticated leather-oud character impossible to achieve from individual components. Use at 0.1-2% in final compositions depending on desired intensity - even trace amounts provide profound impact.

Combine Leather Oud 293316 with Rose Imperiale for the signature leather-rose-oud triad explicitly recommended by the manufacturer. Veil harsh aspects with sweet woody notes like Mysore sandalwood oil or our acclaimed Vanilla Supreme, or amplify richness with patchouli and labdanum. Enhance with Saffron Attar FW for spicy-metallic brightness whilst maintaining leathery character.

products.name: Lemon Heart
products.description:
Standard lemon oil gives you thirty minutes of brilliance and then vanishes. Lemon Heart gives you the same brilliance anchored into the heart of your composition. This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction developed to boost the citrus profile of your formula, enhancing the sparkling zesty character even at very low dosage.

LMR describes this as fruity and zesty, very sparkling and mouthwatering. The citral-driven brightness that makes lemon so valuable in eau de colognes, fougères, and fresh florals is preserved and amplified. What is removed is the terpenic bulk that contributes volume without character.

Use it in small amounts alongside standard lemon oil for a citrus opening that sustains itself. It transforms hesperidic accords that normally collapse within an hour into structures that carry bright citrus well into the drydown. Pair with Lime Heart and Orange Heart for a complete LMR citrus heart foundation.

products.name: Lemon Oil FCF, Terpeneless
products.description:
Terpeneless citrus oils are useful for two reasons: concentrated odour and solubility in alcohol. If you have made fragrances using high amounts of citrus you will know that there can be problems with clouding in the final solution, and so chilling and filtering is absolutely essential to get a perfectly clear perfume.

Lemon Oil, Terpeneless solves that by considerably reducing the non-soluble materials (mostly limonene). The end result is a lovely and intense lemon scent that can be used with other citrus oils or blended with the classic top note products like linalool its esters.

This lemon oil contains no furocoumarins.

Origin: Sicily, Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source then molecular distilled

products.name: Lemon Oil Pelatrice, Messina
products.description:
Lemon oil Messina is the premiere fine Italian lemon oil with a high citral content (usually three to four percent) giving it a fresher and more powerful character than standard cold pressed lemon oil from other regions.

Lemon Oil Messina blends beautifully with other oils within the citrus family, including our incredible Bergamot “Superior” Oil FCF, Cedrat oil, Sweet Orange, Distilled Lime, and Litsea Cubeba, another high citral oil. Also try it with the wonderfully rich Lemon Heart from LMR.

Lemon Oil Messina has a synergistic relationship with Fraterworks' Magnificent Mandarin, Lemon Verbena, and Verdantol™.

NOTE: this oil is not furocoumarin free and so it should be counted towards the total furocoumarin content of your finished product.

products.name: Lemon Oil, Washed
products.description:
Washed lemon oil has much value in the flavours world but it also has practical uses in perfumery. To wash lemon, the furocoumarin free essential oil (from cold pressing) is washed with food grade solvents (usually alcohol) to remove certain terpene fractions. The result is softer, sweeter and less toppy.

Origin: Sicily, Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source and post-processed

products.name: Lemon Terpenes
products.description:
Lemon Terpenes captures the volatile essence of fresh lemon peel without any fruity sweetness. You'll notice its extremely diffusive, sharp character hits immediately upon application. The material consists of over 75% d-limonene, creating that unmistakable citrus-pine combination.

This terpenic fraction proves invaluable for adding explosive lift to citrus accords and sparkling brightness to floral compositions. Use it to amplify bergamot and neroli in cologne formulations or add traces to cut through heavy florals like jasmine. The material works brilliantly with woody notes, creating a fresh-cut timber effect when blended with cedarwood or vetiver.

Handle this volatile powerhouse with precision—overdosing quickly turns elegance into harshness. Layer it with folded citrus oils for complete lemon character. Combine with aldehydes and citrus oils to build authentic zesty accords that maintain their sparkle throughout the top note development.

products.name: Lemon Tetrarome®
products.description:
You will never find a more gourmand lemon oil as Lemon Tetrarome® from Firmenich. First developed in the 1950s, the Tetrarome range featured highly concentrated citrus oils with low terpenes (meaning low-volatility) that express their edible side in a far greater way than comparative terpeneless oils. They are particularly sweet and candy-like.

Owing to its very common use in flavours (especially sweets), a sniff of Lemon Tetrarome immediately conjures up images of hard candy, citrus-based power drinks, lemonade and lemonade ice blocks.

Lemon Tetrarome blends elegantly with fresh citrus essential oils, offering incredible long-lasting effects and pure performance. “All is in the citrus peel! Tetrarome® are like pure magic zesty concentrates. They give the impression we crunch the entire fruit and bring to composition an incredible long lastingness.” Loic Bisceglie, Firmenich Perfumer

Pair this with Bergamot and Cedrat oils from CAPUA 1880, Maltol Isobutyrate for caramellic sweetness and a splash of aldehydes for fizz and you have the beginnings of a superb gourmand scent.

products.name: Lemon Verbena
products.description:
Lemon verbena is an incredibly beautiful essential oil which is now completely prohibited from perfume use. It was a key to the olfactory style of numerous perfumes including Chanel's Pour Monsieur and the classic YSL Pour Homme.

Fraterworks® Verbena is an incredibly true-to-life replica of lemon verbena oil that is absolutely safe for use in fragrances at up to 4% of the finished product for IFRA compliance. It is loaded with natural essential oils and absolutes for a truly natural result.

Lemon verbena is sweet, herbal and bursting with lemon freshness.

products.name: Lemon “Superior” Oil, FCF
products.description:
First we brought you superior Bergamot Bergaptene Free, now we bring you Capua's beautiful Lemon Furocoumarin free. Regular cold pressed lemon can be used to an IFRA limit of 2% of your finished product, but Lemon “Superior” Oil FCF can be used up to 28%. That is because the dangerous furocoumarins are removed from the oil without harming its beautiful scent.

Origin: Calabria, Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source

products.name: Lemonile
products.description:
Lemonile greets you with intense, natural-smelling lemon — bright citrus peel character with a cologne-like lift and subtle green-herbaceous nuances. A faint metallic edge distinguishes it from citral, though the overall impression remains convincingly lemon. The first impact is of raw citrus power with surprising depth.

What sets Lemonile apart is persistence — three weeks on blotter is extraordinary for a citrus note. This Givaudan nitrile outlasts citral, limonene, and geranitrile by a wide margin, giving you lemon character that endures into the heart and base. It excels in colognes, verbena accords, and lime compositions.

Pair with Kephalis for a zesty-sparkling wood effect, or blend with other citrus oils to anchor their fleeting top notes. Alkali stability makes Lemonile invaluable in soap and detergent fragrances where most citrus materials fail. Dose from traces upward — its intensity easily dominates a blend.

products.name: Levistamel 25% TEC
products.description:
Levistamel greets you with rich caramelised sugar — not the simple sweetness of vanillin, but something layered and savoury. Green celery and fenugreek notes weave through the caramel, adding a salty, almost curry-like edge. Anise-liquorice warmth and balsamic depth emerge as it develops on skin.

This Givaudan lactone is your answer when you want caramel complexity without defaulting to vanillin or ethyl maltol. Herbal and pine compositions gain unexpected warmth from small additions. The celery-fenugreek facet connects it to lovage, immortelle, and maple accords where that savoury-sweet interplay defines the character.

Levistamel comes diluted in triethyl citrate for easy handling — the pure material is a solid. Tenacity on blotter reaches several weeks, and stability across soap, shampoo, and detergent is excellent. Blend with sotolon, ethyl maltol, and coumarin for deep gourmand warmth.

products.name: Levulinic Acid
products.description:
Levulinic acid brings a quiet caramel sweetness to compositions — not the bold hit of ethyl maltol or vanillin, but a softer, more refined burnt-sugar nuance that sits underneath other materials and warms them from below. Think of it as the difference between caramel sauce and the browned edges of a crème brûlée. It is understated but it changes the character of everything around it.

It is also the starting point for ethyl levulinate, a fruity rum-like material used in fine fragrance — so if you work with levulinate esters, this is where they begin. On its own, use levulinic acid in amber and gourmand bases where you want sweetness that doesn't announce itself. It rounds hard edges on resinous materials and adds a toffee-like depth beneath vanilla and benzoin.

Try it in orientals alongside tonka, benzoin, and labdanum. It fills the space between the obvious sweetness on top and the darker resinous notes underneath. A small addition goes a long way — this is a modifier, not a feature note.

products.name: Liatrix TruAbs
products.description:
Liatris flowers have a scent as unique as their appearance. Also known as deer tongue, liatris provides us with liatrix absolute, perhaps the finest of all the coumarin rich plant oils. Liatrix absolute takes the best of hay, vanilla, tobacco and genet and combines them into one: a floral herbaceous almost creamy scent that is the olfactory equivalent of a bright sunny day. Smelling liatrix you simply can't help but smile with sheer pleasure.

Use this base when building sophisticated tobacco accords that demand authenticity with fewer regulatory constraints. Its complex profile bridges the gap between gourmand sweetness and masculine hay-leather dryness. Layer it beneath rose and geranium for vintage barbershop fougères, or combine with vanilla and benzoin for opulent oriental bases.

Because liatrix absolute is now virtually impossible to obtain, we have produced this marvellous TruAbs, a 100% natural replica that is truly to die for.

products.name: Liffarome
products.description:
Liffarome is a kinder and gentler member of the Cis 3 Hexenol family with a lovely soft nuance of apples and pears in addition to the expected classic scent of cut lawns, violet leaves and foliage. It also has a hint of nasturtium and red radish. Despite being easier to use than many materials in the green family, it is still a very powerful molecule that shines when blended with others.

Liffarome is found at 0.1% in Light Blue of Dolce and Gabbana in synergy with 0.065% Triplal, 0.1% in Carolina Herrera's 212 VIP Pour Homme, Lipstick Rose by Frederick Malle and Dior's Sauvage Elixir, 0.12% in Armani's My Way, 0.4% in YSL's Libre and many many more.

Liffarome blends well with Triplal, Helional, Cyclamen Aldehyde, Amazonia™, Verdantol, Daphne Supreme, Veticoeur, Vetimoss and Artemal™.

products.name: Lilac A07
products.description:
Lilac A07 is the original unaltered formula of the same name by Chiris in Grasse. This is our finest Lilac base and if you wish to have only one, this is the one we recommend. It is painstakingly crafted over a period of days in a traditional multi-step process to carefully control all the chemical reactions that take place. The result is tranquility, softness and beauty encapsulated.

Chiris (founded in 1768) was a French fragrance house specialising in highest quality essential oils and absolutes and it is from their prestigious school that François Coty emerged after just one year in the early 1900s. But perhaps the most esteemed name connected to the company was Ernest Beaux. Upon fleeing Russia after the communist revolt, Rallet (Beaux's employer) set up shop at Chiris and it was there that he met Madame Chanel. The rest, of course, is history.

Chiris made heavy use of the naturals they produced and so their bases tend to be even richer and more expensive than many others. Lilac A07 is no exception to that rule being enriched with luscious French jasmine and rose absolutes.

Lilac A07 featured alongside natural jasmine extract and Jasmin Fleurs in Jasmin de Corse (formula below) by Coty where it sets the tone for the whole scent. It was a perfume fit for a princess as it was the favourite of Russian Grand Duchess Tatiana Nikolaevna.

Chiris's Lilac A07 was so popular that Givaudan made and sold its own replica which was also an acclaimed base in its own right. That Giva

products.name: Lilac Supreme
products.description:
With the recent news that Heliotropin may be heading for a total ban under the proverbial butcher's knife of the European Union bureaucracy very soon, it seemed timely for us to make available our Lilac Supreme base. 

Lilac Supreme is a beautiful and complex modern lilac base containing absolutely no heliotropin. That chemical has long been ubiquitous in Lilac bases but modern tastes (and now a potential ban on heliotropin in the EU) seek a less powdery and more transparent floral heart in fragrances. Lilac Supreme is perfect for that use.

This base is not just interesting for its lack of heliotropin, but also because it featured in a number of Guerlain perfumes in the late 20th century. It is also extremely well priced.

NOTE: We currently sell Heliotropin and Heliotropin Natural and will continue to do so despite any possible ban for EU cosmetics that may come to pass.

products.name: Lilas Blanc
products.description:
Lilas Blanc (white lilac) is a delicate classic lilac base suitable for filling out the heart of a floral fragrance or even as the star of a soliflore. With a few minor additions Lilas Blanc can be an entire scent at a time when lilac is coming back into vogue.

This base can be used up to 9.6% of the finished product, making it a great alternative to the abundance of muguet centred perfumes. This lilac is particularly soft and enticing and upon first sniff one has an overwhelming feeling of nostalgia. Lilas blanc is simply comforting.

products.name: Lilas Pourpre
products.description:
Richer and more intense than our delicate Lilas Blanc, Lilas Pourpre is full bodied and powerful enough to hold its own in a multi-floral fragrance. Natural absolutes and oils add volume.

This robust base is of an invar type - it performs consistently from start to finish without dramatic changes as it dries down. Wonderful for a general floraliser.

products.name: Lilial
products.description:
Lilial opens with crystalline lily-of-the-valley freshness, its aldehydic sparkle creating immediate lift and radiance. The watery-green transparency reads as morning dew on white petals. This legendary molecule (discovered in the 1960s by IFF) captures muguet's elusive character with extraordinary fidelity and power.

Lilial transforms heavy florals into airy bouquets through its unique Schiff base formations. Combine it with hydroxycitronellal for classic muguet or add traces to rose for aldehydic brilliance. Its metallic-clean edge cuts through oriental bases, adding transparency without sacrificing richness.

The material's 236-hour substantivity means your compositions maintain fresh character throughout wear. Use it at 0.5-3% in fine fragrance for optimal impact without overwhelming delicacy. Its affinity for phenylethyl alcohol, citronellol, and hedione creates synergies that amplify overall radiance.

The variant we sell is a particularly fine “Extra” quality in the Fraterworks® Signature range.

NOTE: Over time lilial may oxidise which appears in the form of white crystals or clumps (lysmerylic acid). Remaining liquid can still be used by the oxidised material should be discarded. Lilial may contain a touch of Tocopherol for protection, but storing this material at temperatures below 15°C (59°F) is still advisable.

Regulatory: this is banned by the EU but is still permitted by IFRA to 1.4% of your finished product.

products.name: Lilyflore®
products.description:
Lilyflore® delivers extraordinary volume and structure in muguet compositions. This powerful floral material bridges the gap between Hydroxycitronellal's soft petal character and Lilial's creamy fullness while offering superior tenacity. In addition to being an alternative to the virtually prohibited Lilial and Lyral, Lilyflore® excels due to maintaining integrity where traditional aldehydes can falter.

Add Lilyflore® at 0.05-0.3% in your blend to lift muddy florals and add clean radiance. Combine with 0.5% Hedione and a trace of Melonal for solar lily effects. Blend with 1% Iso E Super to create a convincing muguet-stem accord. Use with caution—this material dominates easily and turns plastic-sweet when overdosed. It's beautiful… until it's not.

products.name: Lime Heart
products.description:
Heart oils are not ordinary essential oils. They are LMR specialities — highly concentrated citrus fractions developed to boost the citrus profile of your formula, enhancing the zesty and fruity notes even at very low dosage. A trace of Lime Heart does what generous amounts of standard lime oil cannot — it persists.

LMR describes this as fruity and zesty with clean, fresh, mouthwatering undertones. The fleeting top notes that vanish from conventional lime within minutes are captured here in concentrated form. What remains is the most intensely lime impression you can put in a bottle — bright, sharp, unmistakable.

Use just a hint to extend lime presence from top note well into the heart. Layer it over our Persian Lime Oil FCF for a citrus accord that opens with natural breadth and refuses to fade. Essential in gin-and-tonic accords, mojito constructions, and any bright aquatic or citrus cologne that needs staying power.

products.name: Lime Oil, Distilled
products.description:
Lime oil is one of the most (if not THE most) intense citrus oils. It practically explodes out of the bottle and is perceptible in very small amounts. For me it is about the scent of cocktails and VIP parties. It is an oil that, in the youthful slang of today, goes hard.

Use it to brighten up a citrus accord, add a sparkle to a masculine or build a stunning key lime pie gourmand scent around its zesty magic.

products.name: Linalool
products.description:
Linalool really needs no introduction; it is one of the most commonly used aroma chemicals today. It is abundant in nature with the oils of Rosewood (Aniba roaeodora, not the type Pianos and stringed instruments are made from, Dalbergia nigra) and Shiu wood (also known as Ho wood) containing the highest amounts naturally (over 80%).

In combination with its ester Linalyl Acetate, Linalool can be used to create the effect of citrus freshness without its characteristic odour of oranges or lemons. This makes it incredibly useful for novel top notes.

Linalool blends extremely well with Dihydromyrcenol and the entire citrus family where it can modify and extend those notes. It has a light woody quality and also blends well with most materials in that category also.

Our Linalool comes from BASF in Germany which makes extremely fine aroma chemicals. BASF is our preferred supplier for many standard materials due to their meticulous care in manufacturing. No other supplier produces such a clean and true Linalool.

products.name: Linalool Dextro ex Coriander
products.description:
In perfumery there are many products that we don't have to have, but we absolutely must have. This is one such product. Here we present 100% natural linalool dextro extracted from Russian coriander, and while it has all the beauty you would expect from a natural linalool product, it layers it with the delicate warming spice of fine coriander seeds. This is a material we can't help but smell from the bottle… only to return five minutes later for more.

Linalool ex Coriander (also known as Coriander Oil Fractions) was a highly popular raw material in the French fragrance houses located in Imperial Russia and was much loved by Ernest Beaux, creator of Chanel No 5. Our own Jasmin Russe relies heavily on this linalool in fact. It is key to the inimitable quality of that very popular classical jasmine base.

We show off this natural isolate in our demonstration version of Arpège, the formula for which can be found further down this page.

Payan Bertrand, the creator of this marvellous product is a family owned French company specialising in natural products; it was founded in 1854.

products.name: Linalool ex Bois de Rose
products.description:
Linalool ex Bois de Rose is one of the most perfect forms of linalool available. It is the purest heart of luscious rosewood oil and was formerly used in the very finest fragrances. We use it in many of our classical bases as its full bodied character is so vital to restoring the complete odour spectrum of those historic masterpieces.

For the purposes of compliance with IFRA recommendations we add a trace of natural antioxidant to prevent degradation of the product.

products.name: Linalool Oxide
products.description:
With its almost minty camphoraceous freshness, Linalool Oxide is a perfect aroma chemical for naturalising reconstituted essential oils or adding a lovely fresh earth note to fragrances. If you want to mimic the scent of a forest floor dank with decaying leaves, look no further than Linalool Oxide — it's so close it seems like cheating!

In the classic French tradition of perfume making, florals need a little "ugly" and so we often rely on the likes of celery seed oil, civet absolute and aroma chemicals like cis jasmone, but linalool oxide is an often overlooked alternative.

It blends incredibly well with Fenchone Alpha, Ambrinol 95, Ambrofix and Orcanox, and bases such as Amazonia™, Suralette™ Extra, Artemal™ and Verdantol.

products.name: Linalyl Acetate
products.description:
Linalyl Acetate is, in most cases, found in nature paired with its parent alcohol Linalool. It is the fresher material of the two and can be used alone (in quite large amounts) to add a generic freshness to the top notes of a scent. It works well to boost Bergamot and other citrus oils and is essential for recreations of the same.

Linalyl Acetate is green, citrus, bergamot, floral and woody. It adapts incredibly well to virtually every type of fragrance and so we consider it one of the most important top note tools in the perfumer's arsenal.

Our Linalool and Linalyl Acetate come from BASF in Germany which makes extremely fine aroma chemicals. BASF is our preferred supplier for many standard materials due to their meticulous care in manufacturing.

products.name: Linalyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Linalyl cinnamate has a soft floral-lily scent with balsamic warmth and a subtle fruity-herbaceous edge. It blends smoothly into delicate florals, particularly muguet, lily, and freesia, where it lends body and quiet persistence without dominating the composition.

It pairs especially well with citronellol, enhancing green-fruity facets and creating a bridge between floral and oriental styles. Used as a fixative and modifier, it helps unify accords while adding a gentle, natural lift to the overall structure.

products.name: Linalyl Formate
products.description:
Linalyl formate is greener and sharper than its more familiar cousin linalyl acetate, with a bright bergamot-like citrus character and herbal depth. There is a soapy lavender quality and a subtle woody drydown. It adds real bite and lift to top notes without losing the natural, herbaceous feel.

Use linalyl formate to add green, citrusy brightness to your fougeres, colognes, and lavender accords. It bridges fresh top notes and floral hearts with a pungent herbal quality. Where linalyl acetate smooths and softens, this formate ester sharpens and lifts.

Blend with bergamot and lavender for enhanced citrus-herbal accords. Try it alongside dihydromyrcenol and citronellyl formate for a modern, sparkling freshness. Pair with oakmoss and coumarin for fougere constructions where you want a greener, more aggressive opening.

products.name: Linalyl Propionate
products.description:
Linalyl propionate opens with fresh bergamot and lavender, but sweeter and softer than its famous cousin linalyl acetate. There is a distinct pear-berry fruitiness that the acetate simply does not have — richer, rounder, more floral. It smells like bergamot with the sharpness dialled down and the sweetness turned up.

Use it as a modifier for linalyl acetate rather than a replacement. A small amount added to an acetate-based accord introduces fruity sweetness and depth without changing the overall bergamot-lavender direction. It is also more stable than linalyl acetate, which is notoriously prone to degradation — a practical advantage in finished products.

Pair it with bergamot and clary sage for enriched fougère openings, with geranium and citronellol for soft floral hearts, or with lavender and oakmoss for a rounded, classic cologne effect. Use restraint — overdosed, it can become cloying. At the right level, it adds a beautiful fruity glow.

products.name: Linden Blossom Absolute
products.description:
Linden Blossom Absolute opens with an almost edible honey sweetness, immediately transporting you to a grove of blooming Tilia trees humming with bees. This extraordinarily rare absolute captures the narcotic warmth of sun-warmed blossoms with their distinctive citrus-green freshness.
