The material's rich farnesol content provides exceptional radiance while maintaining the delicate tea-like transparency that makes linden so prized.

Utilise this precious absolute when creating compositions that demand authentic floral opulence without heaviness. Its honey-beeswax character transforms simple florals into luxurious nectarous bouquets. The material's natural complexity allows it to bridge bright citrus top notes with deeper woody bases, creating seamless transitions that synthetic recreations cannot achieve.

Perfumers treasure its ability to add golden warmth to white florals without masking their individual characters. Combine with jasmine and orange blossom for intoxicating summer night accords. Build unexpected depth by pairing its honeyed sweetness with green tea notes and soft musks for contemporary clean luxury.

products.name: Litsea Cubeba Oil
products.description:
Litsea Cubeba has a bit of a bad reputation owing to the fact that it has a fairly high amount of citronellal — a chemical people often attribute to pest repellant. But the complexity of this very lemony oil makes it a wonderful nuancer and it most definitely deserves a come back.

In 1946, Jean Carles created Ma Griffe (1946) for Carven using 1% Citronella oil and 2% Styrallyl Acetate. Replacing the Citronella with Litsea Cubeba makes for a more subtle effect.

With around 70% citral, this blends with all members of the citrus family and is a great booster for lemon especially. As it lasts around ten times longer than that oil, it is a perfect solution when you need to prolong lemon into the heart of your fragrance.

Origin: Indonesia
Variety: Litsea Cubeba
Part: Berries
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Little Miss
products.description:
Little Miss is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Coco Mademoiselle by Chanel. Launched in 2001 and created by Jacques Polge, Coco Mademoiselle was an oriental floral fragrance built around a bright citrus opening and the patchouli-rose accord that defined the modern fruitchouli.

Our compound features a substantial patchouli base softened with vanilla, tonka bean and opoponax. The top notes of orange, mandarin and bergamot give a sparkling citrus lift, while a rich heart of Turkish rose, jasmine, mimosa and ylang-ylang provides classic floral depth. White musk and vetiver round out the drydown. The result is a polished, instantly recognisable feminine fragrance with excellent longevity and strong sillage – confident without being heavy.

This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

Top Notes: Orange, Mandarin Orange, Bergamot, Orange Blossom
Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Jasmine, Mimosa, Ylang-Ylang
Base Notes: Patchouli, White Musk, Vanilla, Vetiver, Tonka Bean, Opoponax

products.name: Lotus Storm
products.description:
LOTUS STORM® is an exquisite base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the iconic Blue Lotus (Nymphaea caerulea)—the sacred flower treasured by ancient Egypt—this innovative composition captures the flower’s rich floral elegance, captivating fruity nuances, and alluring earthy warmth and layers it with a diaphanous jasmine note and galbanum. Traditionally associated with ritual, trance, and twilight, Blue Lotus takes on a new dimension in The Night Garden: a sacred bloom that seems to awaken only when the world is quiet.

Scent Profile

LOTUS STORM® opens with the aroma of a serene, shadowed pond. Dew-kissed foliage entwines with the earthy depth of galbanum and warm whispers of beeswax, brightened by delicate fruity nuances. At its heart unfolds an entrancing bouquet, as the mystical fragrance of blue lotus flowers rises gracefully amid an abundant cascade of night-scented jasmine. Soft, creamy white florals lend a velvety finish. With the first light of dawn, the fragrance gently recedes, leaving behind a subtly spiced, musky echo of the Night Garden.

Perfumery Usage

LOTUS STORM® is formulated to deliver exceptional authenticity, longevity, and complexity, making it ideal both as a complete base or as a distinctive note within fragrance formulations. It blends seamlessly with aquatic materials such as Amazonia®, Cascalone®, Melozone®, and luxurious florals like Tuberose Absolute and Egyptian Jasmine, opening endless crea

products.name: Lovage Root Oil
products.description:
Lovage root oil hits you with an intense wave of warm celery, angelica, and liquorice - spicy, sweet, earthy, and almost savoury. The power is remarkable; it ranks among the strongest-smelling natural materials in existence. A single drop perfumes an entire room.

Use lovage root oil in micro-doses — it produces extraordinary effects even at trace levels. It adds savoury warmth to rose and carnation compositions and lends unique earthy depth to orientals, fougères, and spice accords. Pair it with oakmoss, opopanax, costus, and coumarin.

Lovage belongs to the same botanical family as celery and angelica, and you can hear that kinship clearly. Try a trace in a rose or carnation composition — the warm, savoury effect is genuinely surprising. Always dilute heavily; this is one of perfumery's most concentrated naturals.

products.name: Lyfral®
products.description:
Lyral® is one of the most beautiful floralising chemicals we have; it is soft, radiant and incredibly long lasting. Unfortunately it is also now banned by the EU and restricted to a mere 0.2% of a finished fragrance by IFRA.

While patents have been filed for singular molecules that allegedly replace Lyral®, none are commercially available and neither are they likely to be so in the near future. Thus was born Lyfral®, the Fraterworks alternative.

In creating Lyfral® our first goal was to have a floralising base that was simply beautiful to smell — appealing at the most fundamental level. Next was the task of mimicking the essential aspects of Lyral® as best we could. The result is Lyfral®, a base which is lovely in its own right but also functions as a direct one for one stand-in for Lyral®.

This can also stand in as a one-for-one replacer for captive Mahonial.

products.name: Lyral®
products.description:
Banned in the EU and restricted to 0.2% by IFRA for the rest of the us, Lyral remains one of the most profoundly beautiful white floral chemicals. It gave life to Aventus illustrating its amazing ability to floralise masculines without adding a feminine touch, and without it the masterpiece Chanel fragrance Coco (1986) wouldn't be possible.

As Europe strips bare its greatest works of modern fragrance art in honour of health and safety regulators, we can at least be happy to know that thousands of bottles of now-vintage perfume are still floating around on eBay to allow us to enjoy the beauty of this material. And thankfully most non-European perfumers are still free to use this in commercial scents.

And of course, if you are perfuming for your own pleasure or gifts, you may continue to use this glorious aroma chemical.

products.name: Lys De La Reine
products.description:
A complex Lily base enriched with luxury floral absolutes, Lys de la Reine ("Queen's Lily" - formerly Lys de france) is an entire bouquet of flowers at its peak of blossoming. Lys de la Reine has a room filling diffusion and a wonderful naturalness.

Traces add floral richesse and shimmer to a fragrance while an overdose can be used to replace muguet or generic white florals in a scent. 

Lys de la Reine is, like the lily flower itself, indolic, cresylic and powerful. It is constructed using only the finest aroma chemicals and naturals. 

This is a perfect base to use as a starting point for fragrances like Nasomatto's Narcotic Venus, Lys Mediterranee by Frederic Malle, Passage d'Enfer by L'Artisan Parfumeur, and Un Jardin Sur La Lagune by Hermès.

products.name: Lysmerex™
products.description:
Lilial, one of the finest muguet chemicals of the late 20th century is now completely banned in fragrances in the EU and many other countries. It has a power and special character that is impossible to find in any one chemical. Consequently Fraterworks has produced Lysmerex™ a complex base which stands in as a one-for-one replacer. 

This base is sophisticated and true to the original. It is built around modern and classic molecules for a scent profile matching lilial and a chemical profile allowing for the formation of schiff bases.

Synonyms for Lilial: lilestralis, lysmeral, mefloral, butyl phenyl methyl propional.

products.name: Madranol
products.description:
MADRANOL® has a clean, sweet, powdery violet scent with nuances reminiscent of orris root, violet leaves, and faint raspberry or berry undertones. It is significantly less woody and less dry than the better-known methyl ionones. Compared to beta-ionone, it is more floral and less austere, which makes it especially useful for modernised violet accords where a lighter, fruitier tone is preferred over classical austerity. Its diffusiveness is moderate, with very good tenacity, making it well-suited for use in mid to base notes.

Usage

MADRANOL® elevates compositions with its refined powdery-floral character. Modern perfumers utilise it at 0.5-2% for sophisticated violet signatures. It delivers exceptional tenacity while maintaining transparency throughout development. Use MADRANOL® in conjunction with ionone derivatives for dimensional violet accords. Dose at higher concentrations (2-4%) in soaps for substantivity. Pair with green galbanum notes or heliotropin to create classical yet contemporary floral foundations.

Applications

Violet accords (paired with ionones, methyl heptine carbonate, or methyl ionone gamma)

Orris reconstructions (especially in combination with irone-type materials)

Floral-powdery blends, such as heliotrope, mimosa, or aldehydic florals

Soft berry or lipstick notes (when dosed subtly)

Retro-modern feminines, especially in the 1950s–70s French tradition Its low harshness and gentle, slightly waxy sweetness make it ideal for high-end cosmetic applicat

products.name: Magnificent Mandarin
products.description:
Green mandarin is the most elegant of all the mandarin oils (Red, yellow and green) but high prices and IFRA restrictions make it difficult to get a strong and clear mandarin top note from the pure and natural oil.

Magnificent Mandarin by Fraterworks is just that: magnificent. It explodes with a citrus aldehydic quality from every perfume. In traces it is a beautiful nuancer. In overdose it is a dazzling top note refreshingly different from the far more common bergamot.

products.name: Magnolan
products.description:
Magnolan is an often overlooked and certainly underused aroma chemical that works as an excellent canvas material when the muguet florals are just too perfumey. It is very long lasting (over 300 hours) and blends very well with citrus, woods and green chemicals making it an ideal core for modern fresh fragrances.

Owing to its long life and power it is also used frequently in functional fragrances; but it's time in fine fragrance has most certainly arrived.

products.name: Magnolia Flower Oil
products.description:
Magnolia flower oil is a hidden gem in perfumery. It opens with the sparkling luxury of a fine wine leading to a heart of creamy goodness with traces of delicate citrus, reminiscent of a bowl of thick medieval posset. Nuances of peach, apricots and freesias make this a really incredible oil that should have more use in perfumer's palettes.

Long lasting and wonderfully characterful, this is the very finest magnolia flower oil supplied by one of the finest naturals companies.

Small amounts are all that are needed in fine fragrance for an interesting twist, while larger quantities can provide unique and novel aspects to a multi-floral.

We also manufacture and supply the finest complete magnolia base: Magnolia Plumier.

Note: Due to weather conditions affecting harvets, LMR has increased the price of Magnolia flower oil considerably this year. We hope it will return to normal at the next harvest but have, accordingly, increased our prices to keep the product viable. We have added the option to purchase this oil in a 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless natural solvent) to help manage the cost.

Synonyms: White Champaca
Origin: China
Part: Flowers only
Method: Steam distilled at source

products.name: Magnolia Leaf Oil
products.description:
Magnolia Leaf Oil delivers the quintessential green character that defines modern transparent florals. Its exceptional ability to inject a "dose of green goodness" into compositions prevents white florals from becoming cloying. Perfumers utilise this powerful modifier primarily at low concentrations where it significantly shapes accords.

Use magnolia leaf oil to create photorealistic floral effects. Add to freesia bases where it becomes the crucial element transforming simple accords into living flower representations. Apply sparingly as its potency easily dominates compositions when overdosed. This material works effectively as a bridge note, connecting citrus openings to floral hearts.

The relationship between Magnolia Leaf Oil and Magnolia Flower Oil mirrors that of petitgrain and neroli. While the flower oil presents a voluptuous, heady, sweet floral character with creamy vanilla accents, the leaf oil isolates and amplifies the fresh, crisp green "aura" surrounding the living bloom. This allows perfumers to deconstruct magnolia, building "transparent" or "green magnolia" compositions that feel contemporary and luminous—capturing the scent of the entire living branch rather than just the isolated blossom.

We also stock a beautiful LMR Magnolia Flower Oil and a marvellous Magnolia Plumier base.

products.name: Magnolia Plumier
products.description:
The creamy scent of magnolia blossoms is an elusive one but decidedly memorable once smelled with a heart of Ylang Ylang gently warmed by spices and refreshed by a delicate touch of lemon.

Fraterworks® Magnolia Plumier (named for the French botanist who introduced the tree to France in the 1700s) is an elegant floral base enriched with precious magnolia flower oil. In low doses it adds volume and richness to a multi-floral bouquet, while in overdose it becomes the star of the show — and what a star it is!

Magnolia Plumier can be used at up to 12.4% of a finished product.

products.name: Mahua Pearl
products.description:
MAHUA PEARL® is a fragrance base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour for Fraterworks, inspired by the rare and sacred Mahua flower (Madhuca longifolia). Pale, round, and pearl-like, these fleshy blossoms fall silently to the forest floor during the night and are gathered by hand at dawn. Traditionally fermented into a sweet tribal spirit, the flowers carry a rich, nectarous scent touched by warmth, fruit, and fermentation. This base captures that transformation—soft, golden, and quietly intoxicating.

The scent of Mahua Pearl is boozy, fruity, floral and sweet. It rests on a luxurious base of creamy sandalwood, vanilla and musk.

Perfumery Usage

MAHUA PEARL® is ideal for adding richness, sweetness, and complexity to florals, gourmands, and amber compositions. It harmonises beautifully with Beeswax Glacé Absolute, Immortelle, Rum CO2, and tobacco. A perfect ingredient for perfumers looking to explore unconventional sweetness with story and soul.

Process

The base was developed through careful reconstruction of the Mahua blossom’s rare olfactory signature. Combining lactonic materials, honeyed accords, and subtle fruit notes, Duchaufour built a portrait of this wild bloom as it ferments in the shadows of the forest.

Background

Mahua is sacred in parts of India, yet almost completely unknown in the global fragrance world. MAHUA PEARL® introduces this hidden flower as a perfumery note for the first time—bridging ancient practice with modern scent design.

MAHUA PEA

products.name: Majantol®
products.description:
Majantol is a vibrant synthetic aroma chemical, providing a transparent and intensely floral Lily of the Valley note.  This material is valued for its ability to impart a fresh, clean, and uplifting floral character to fragrances and is particularly valuable these days as more and more muguet materials are put on the chopping block of EU compliance.

Use at 1-5% concentration for balanced floral heart notes. Combine with Hedione® for enhanced diffusion and radiance. This material exhibits excellent stability across most product bases and exceptional substantivity on fabrics, making you successful in both fine fragrance and functional applications like detergents and softeners.

products.name: Maltol
products.description:
Maltol is a sweet chemical that can be used for a decidedly gourmand note in a fragrance or as a delicate sweetener for recreations of essential oils and absolutes. Found naturally in some flowers and plants, this synthetic version is extremely versatile and very cost effective.

Maltol pair's beautifully with its stronger relative Ethyl Maltol, Signature Vanillin and Sotolone.

products.name: Maltol Isobutyrate
products.description:
Maltol Isobutyrate is a high-impact, stable aroma chemical that combines a sweet, fruity strawberry note with caramel and cotton candy facets. Its balanced profile makes it effective in gourmand compositions, where it adds depth and richness without overpowering other elements. The material is highly stable across a variety of formulations, making it useful in both fine fragrance and flavour applications.

Compared to maltol and ethyl maltol, which contribute a direct caramelic sweetness, Maltol Isobutyrate introduces a distinct fruity dimension, particularly with its pronounced strawberry character. Maltol provides a simple sugary effect, while ethyl maltol intensifies the caramel aspect. Maltol Isobutyrate, however, enhances compositions with its unique fusion of fruit and confectionary notes, allowing for more complex and layered accords in both fragrance and flavour development.

products.name: Mandarin Aldehyde Total 10 TEC
products.description:
Mandarin Aldehyde was first discovered in orange skins in the 1940s. It is a wonderful chemical to use when needing an aldehydic boost to citrus and green fragrances.

Mandarin Aldehyde is only available as a diluted product owing to its great strength. Even at 10% it conveys the most intense odour of Vietnamese mint, coriander and mandarin peels. The total version is a blend of isomers and makes for a very cost-effective citrus bomb.

products.name: Mandarin Oil, Green
products.description:
Our Green Mandarin Oil is, simply put, a work of extractive art. It is the finest mandarin oil we have had the pleasure of smelling — and we have smelled a lot of mandarin in our time.

This Green Mandarin Oil is every bit the scent that remains on your hands after peeling the fruit. Every nuance from every drop of juicy goodness is found in this oil.

Green Mandarin is the preferred variety (the others being red and yellow) and it has been used in numerous luxury fragrances, as evidenced by the demonstration formulas below.

Oil Comparison

Green Mandarin Essential Oil: Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends.

Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil: Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications.

Red Mandarin Essential Oil: Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it the sweetest, ideal for calming diffusion and cosmetics. It’s the most widely available of the trio.

products.name: Mandarin Oil, Red
products.description:
Red Mandarin Essential Oil is the richest and sweetest of all mandarin varieties, offering a deep, intensely fruity citrus aroma with a soft, almost velvety character. Unlike the crisp zestiness of Green Mandarin or the balanced brightness of Yellow Mandarin, Red Mandarin is fully ripened, resulting in a scent that is smooth, warm, and lusciously sweet with hints of candied orange peel.

Red Mandarin Oil stands out for its unique composition, containing a higher proportion of aldehydes and esters that contribute to its roundness and longevity. It pairs exceptionally well with vanilla, tonka bean, and creamy florals, enhancing their depth with a naturally sweet citrus glow.

Oil Comparison

Green Mandarin Essential Oil: Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends.

Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil: Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications.

Red Mandarin Essential Oil: Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it

products.name: Mandarin Oil, Yellow
products.description:
While red mandarin is fruit and green mandarin is herbaceous, yellow meets them in the middle with its fresh and delicate scent. It still maintains a distinctly mandarin character when smelling pure while being great for adding lift and zest to a scent.

Yellow mandarin is the lightest of the three in terms of impact which means you can dose it with more bravado than the others.

Oil Comparison

Green Mandarin Essential Oil: Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends.

Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil: Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications.

Red Mandarin Essential Oil: Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it the sweetest, ideal for calming diffusion and cosmetics. It’s the most widely available of the trio.

products.name: Mandarinal® SAEF
products.description:
Mandarinal opens with a diffusive blast of sparkling aldehydes carrying the essence of ripe mandarin fruit on a wave of exhilarating freshness. This isn't your typical citrus - it's mandarin reimagined with a waxy, pillowy texture that removes all harshness while maintaining powerful projection. You'll find it captures not just the fruit but the entire sensory experience of a mandarin grove after rain.

This material transforms traditional citrus structures by providing remarkable longevity and stability where natural citrus oils quickly fade. Reach for Mandarinal when you need a citrus note that carries from the opening through the heart of your composition. Its aldehydic engine provides exceptional lift and bloom, making surrounding notes feel brighter and more expansive while maintaining sophisticated elegance.

Use Mandarinal at 2-4% in your cologne concentrate to create a modern citrus accord with unprecedented staying power. Combine it with bergamot and grapefruit for a sparkling citrus cocktail, or pair with neroli and orange blossom for seamless floral integration. The material excels in contemporary structures where its aldehydic freshness cuts through heavier bases while its unique texture prevents the soapy effect common with other aldehydic materials when properly dosed.

Pairing this with Citroasis base, a long lasting lemon base from Firmenich, and a jot of Terpeneless Bergamot will give you a citrus melange that lasts long into the dry down of your scent. Tempe

products.name: Manuka Oil βTK25+
products.description:
Manuka is a shrub endemic to New Zealand and Australia and it is the source of the nectar from which honeybees produce the highly esteemed manuka honey, the finest honey in the world.

Manuka oil is similar in chemical makeup to tea tree oil but it is softer, more elegant and more herbaceous. New Zealand manuka oil is beloved by herbalists and while it has yet to be exploited fully in a fragrance, it is not entirely absent from the industry.

Being located in New Zealand, Fraterworks is in the position to find and supply the absolute crème de la crème of fine manuka oil, and indeed we have. The New Zealand East coast, in particular the East Cape is renowned for its high quality manuka oil and it is from that region that we source ours.

Manuka oil was historically used to treat wounds as it was believed to have antibacterial properties and early colonial settlers to New Zealand made tea from the foliage of the plant. The presumed efficacy of the oil is typically determined by the beta-triketone level (sometimes indicated by the βTK or MβTK™ term). Our oil has as minimum of 25%.

NOTE: This is sold for perfumery purposes only and should not be consumed or used neat on the skin. This is neither a food nor a health care product.

Origin: East Cape, New Zealand
Variety: Leptospermum scoparium
Part: Leaves and twigs
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Manzanate
products.description:
A wonderful bright top note material that brings a wonderful pineapple and apple quality to a scent especially when used in combination with the rose ketones. Manzanate is key to the opening of Aventus and is found in too numerous fragrances to number.

Mere traces are all that you need to take advantageous of this lovely Givaudan product.

products.name: Maple Lactone
products.description:
Maple Lactone is a powerhouse aroma chemical, prized for its rich, caramellic warmth with a distinctive licorice twist. It adds depth to gourmand compositions and enhances classic fragrance families like fougères and chypres, where it can partially replace coumarin to create a warmer, more rounded profile.

According to Arctander, Maple Lactone delivers a sweet, spicy caramel effect with nutty, walnut-like undertones, alongside subtle hints of celery and tobacco. It pairs beautifully with tonka, tobacco, new-mown hay, and celery seed oil, reinforcing their warmth and extending longevity.

For perfumers, we offer Maple Lactone in pure crystal form or diluted to 10% in DPG, ensuring ease of use while maintaining its bold, stable character.

Know Your Maple Lactone: Stability Matters

Not all “Maple Lactone” on the market is the same. Methyl Cyclopentanedione (CAS 765-70-8) is often confused with it, but that diketone tautomer is weaker and less stable. Over time, it reverts to the stronger, more potent 80-71-7 form—the one trusted by professionals for its superior performance in fine fragrance and flavour applications.

With Maple Lactone (80-71-7), you’re getting the real deal—bold, stable, and ready to elevate your compositions.

For an alternative with a toasty brown sugar warmth, keep an eye out for Methyl Corylone (CAS 13494-06-9), launching soon—an exceptional choice for smooth, buttery caramel notes in gourmand blends.

products.name: Maritima
products.description:
Maritima opens with an intense burst of cold sea spray and metallic ocean air. This powerful marine pyridine captures the minerality of oyster shells and wet rocks at low tide. You'll recognise its distinctive character—that peculiar freshness after a storm at sea.

This material transforms aquatic accords from abstract freshness into photorealistic seascapes. Use it at 0.1% to add wet texture to white florals or green notes. At higher levels, it creates powerful marine effects that dominate compositions. Pair with Calone and Floralozone for complex oceanic accords that capture both the sparkle and depth of the sea. And for naturalness of course you mustn't forget Dimethyl Sulfide.

Maritima works brilliantly with aldehydes to amplify its metallic freshness. Combine with rose oxide for striking metallic-marine effects. Add traces to citrus compositions for a mineralic edge that cuts through sweetness and adds textural wetness.

products.name: Mastic (Lentisque) Oil, Rectified
products.description:
This is a very fine quality of lentisque (mastic) oil from LMR. It is a top note herbaceous oil with a terpenic and almost cascarilla-like quality.  Wonderful in colognes for a unique top note, this material blends very well with Galbanum oil. The strikingly unique scent of mastic oil conjures up images of antiquity — its rituals, traditions, and the warm sun-soaked breeze of the Aegean sea.

Mastic oil is a star in niche and artisanal fragrances. Its inclusion in perfumes such as Diptyque’s Eau de Lierre highlights its fresh, green characteristics, while Serge Lutens' La Myrrhe showcases its resinous, balsamic richness. Other masterpieces like Amouage Jubilation XXV use touches to evoke a sense of ancient luxury.

Origin: Morocco
Part: Leaves
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Mate “Signature” Abs 40% TEC
products.description:
Mate (pronounced MAH-tay) absolute opens with the unmistakable warmth of steeped green tea — not bright or grassy but deep, dried, and slightly roasted. Hay and herbaceous facets emerge quickly, lending a sun-baked quality. Beneath it all sits a tobacco-leaf dryness that anchors everything to the base.

This is the material when you need a convincing tea accord built on a natural foundation. It slots into fougères alongside lavender and oakmoss, adding an intellectual herbal dimension that synthetics struggle to replicate. In tobacco compositions it provides the leafy dryness of cured leaves without resorting to isolated pyrazines or coumarin alone. The phenolic undertow gives it backbone in chypres and mossy structures.

Use mate to ground bright bergamot openings or to add bookish complexity to vetiver bases. It pairs exceptionally well with osmanthus, guaiacwood, chamomile, and hay absolute. At 40% in TEC this LMR material is ready to use — add it directly to your formula without further dilution. A touch of warmth may be needed to slacken the liquid in cooler climes.

Mate has been used to great effect in modern scents such as Tempo (2018) by Olivier Pescheux for Diptyque, Louis Vuitton's Cactus Garden (2019) byJacques Cavallier Belletrud, Xerjoff's Torino22 (2022) and the luxurious Matsukita (2021) by Clive Christian.

products.name: Mayciane
products.description:
One of the two great classical muguet bases from De Laire that gave the lily character to Chanel's No 19 (the other great base was Coroliane). This soft and elegant base was also the key lily of the valley in 1,000 of Patou in concert with Aldehone.

Use this base together with Coroliane, or on its own for a sweet and surprisingly modern muguet at up to 6.1% of the finished product for IFRA compliance.

Mayciane was created by Henri Robert in 1953.

products.name: Mayol®
products.description:
Mayol is a clean and bright floral ingredient with a fresh scent that closely resembles lily of the valley. It adds a natural, smooth quality to fragrances and blends beautifully with jasmine, lilac, and tuberose. Its light and airy character also lifts citrus notes like bergamot while softening woody bases for a balanced effect.

Mayol is versatile, working well in both fine perfumes and functional products like soaps and detergents. Its floral freshness is long-lasting, making it a valuable tool for creating soft, elegant compositions.

Mayol's versatility can be seen where 2% modifies 9.5% lyral in Tom Ford's Tuscan Leather. It is also found in his Ombre Leather and Amouage's Opus XIV where a modest 0.05% contributes a light floral undertone.

products.name: Mefranal
products.description:
Mefranal opens with refreshing lemon-geranium brightness—clean, aldehydic, and immediately uplifting. The floral heart reveals lily-of-the-valley character that feels vibrant rather than heavy, while aldehydic facets add sophistication. Unlike typical citrus materials that fade quickly, Mefranal maintains its fresh, bright character well into the late heart.

Mefranal bridges citrus top notes and floral hearts beautifully. Its unique structure allows it to extend further into compositions than typical citrus materials, maintaining freshness where others would have evaporated. Use it to add aldehydic lift to muguet accords, or to bring geranium-citrus brightness to peony and fresh floral compositions. The material excels in functional perfumery where its outstanding stability in fabric conditioners, shampoos, and detergents is invaluable.

Work with Mefranal at up to 2–3% of your concentrate. The exceptional substantivity makes it remarkable value for lasting freshness. It shows excellent stability in most applications except acidic products and liquid bleach. Blend with other muguet materials for bright lily accords, or pair with geranium and citrus notes for sophisticated fresh florals.

products.name: Melafleur
products.description:
Melafleur (Cyclemone A) is the scent of an unkempt garden with green melon and fresh air nuances. It is neither heavy nor indolic as some muguet materials can be. It is an excellent material to add lily of the valley without soapiness. It is a great naturaliser for for green accords and it blends very well with herbal notes.

Comparing it to its close relative Precyclemone B (Aldemone), Melafleur is is fresher and more complex-marine. However, it is softer and rounder and lacks the grapefruit pop that precylemone exhibits.

Combine Melafleur with Precyclemone B for a powerful synergy. Pair with Hedione to amplify luminosity, or layer with hydroxycitronellal and cyclamen aldehyde for naturalistic muguet reconstructions. At typical levels of 0.2–0.6% it provides remarkable diffusion without overwhelming your composition.

products.name: Mellitis
products.description:
Mellitis is the classical Givaudan mellis base launched in 1921. It features a perfectly balanced heart of carnation accented by rose, jasmin and wild flowers. It was a favourite of Jean Patou's perfumer Henri Almeras who used it in overdose to great effect in Moment Supreme (1929) where he blended it with lavender and aldehydes.

Mellitis can also be used as fixative base and small quantities add complexity and warmth to any fragrance dry down. Use up to 14.9% in your finished product for compliance with IFRA 50.

products.name: Melon Oliffac
products.description:
Melon Oliffac opens with bright, sparkling freshness - think ripe honeydew just sliced open on a warm morning. The juicy, fleshy sweetness sits over a clean green-rind character that keeps the note from ever becoming cloying. A subtle waxy-floral undertone adds body and realism that isolated melon chemicals simply cannot match.

This IFF specialty base works as both a featured theme and a background modifier depending on dosage. At trace levels, it adds a dewy, fresh-cut quality to floral bouquets without being identifiable as melon. Overdose it and it becomes a full-blown fruity statement - ideal for summer scents and aqua-floral constructions. It excels at bridging volatile citrus top notes with heavier floral absolutes, adding moisture and transparency that dry aromachemicals struggle to provide.

products.name: Melonal
products.description:
Melonal is used to contribute notes of watermelon skin, fresh air with a marine undertone. Usually used at well below 1%, this material is due for an outing as an overdose feature in a novel modernist scent.

As well as pure, we sell a version of this diluted to 10% because most scent makers will rarely need to use it in pure form. Arctander, in his lesser-known tome on aroma chemicals, suggests it has a practical use in cucumber type products (particularly hand lotions) and as a modifier for the fatty aldehydes where it helps to contribute a clean quality.

Melonal is found in Frederic Malle's Carnal Flower at 0.02%, at 0.09% in Amouage's Opus XIV Royal Tobacco, 0.02% in Paco Rabanne Phantom, 0.03% in J'Adore by Dior, and a rather huge 0.25% pure in DKNY's Be Delicious Fresh Blossom and 0.15% in Coach Blue.

products.name: Melozone®
products.description:
This material is unbelievably underated. It is perhaps the most naturalising and radiant of all the green aroma chemicals yet it is so often overlooked. It has a dense earthiness absent from other similar products and a complexity that would make you believe you were smelling a blend rather than a single molecule.

Traces can completely transform a mixture contributing fresh air and mildly aldehydic qualities. This material blends well with Melonal, Cis 3 Hexenol and its Acetate, Verdantol™, Amazonia™, Triplal, Floralozone, Calone Plus, Liffarome and Helional.

products.name: Menthone
products.description:
Menthone opens with immediate cool peppermint freshness that's sweeter and less harsh than pure menthol. Its diffusive character carries subtle floral undertones reminiscent of geranium and rose. The woody-dry base emerges gradually, providing unexpected depth.

You'll find menthone invaluable when building authentic peppermint accords or adding freshness to floral compositions without overwhelming them. It excels at trace levels in geranium and lavender where it provides lift whilst maintaining the delicate balance. Use it below 1% in non-mint fragrances to avoid dominating the composition with peppermint character.

Combine menthone with geranium oil to enhance freshness or blend with lavender for aromatic complexity. Pair with rose absolute where its cooling effect modernises traditional florals. This ketone bridges mint top notes with floral hearts beautifully in eau de cologne structures.

Menthone vs Menthol

Menthone smells brighter and sweeter than menthol, with herbal-green facets rather than menthol's medicinal coldness. Where menthol hits hard with icy blast and camphoric sharpness, menthone offers gentle mint sweetness with floral compatibility. Choose menthone when you want mint freshness without the aggressive cooling punch, particularly in delicate florals where menthol would overpower.

products.name: Mesifuran
products.description:
Mesifuran opens with sweet burnt sugar and a distinctive musty earthiness — mushroom, raw potato, and a savoury warmth that initially reads more umami than gourmand. Coffee and nutty undertones add complexity. It occurs naturally in strawberry, raspberry, mango, and pineapple.

Use Mesifuran to add that elusive cooked-fruit quality — the warmth of strawberry jam rather than fresh strawberry. It deepens and rounds fruit accords, particularly berry, tropical, and dried fruit compositions. A trace amount transforms a flat fruity note into something utterly convincing.

Blend with the closely related strawberry furanone and gamma-decalactone for rich strawberry constructions. Try it in coffee and chocolate accords where the musty-caramellic facet adds authenticity. Over sixteen days' tenacity on blotter makes this one of the most persistent materials in your palette.

products.name: Metal Oxazole
products.description:
METAL OXAZOLE (AKA Sclarene) opens with an immediate dry woody impact that's distinctly different from typical wood notes—there's something almost mineral-like in its presentation. This sclareol derivative doesn't smell of clary sage but rather presents a fascinating herbal-metallic character reminiscent of heated metal or steam rising from hot iron. The camphor facet adds coolness without menthol's sharpness, while earthy-green undertones ground the composition. What makes this material unique is its ability to suggest temperature—it smells warm yet cool, dry yet moist, creating an almost synesthetic experience. At 80% in DPG, this Givaudan specialty delivers consistent, powerful effects. We also offer a further dilution of 10% but note that when purchasing the 100% pure you are receiving the Givaudan standard 80% as it is the only form in which they manufacture it.

Use Metal Oxazole at 0.1-1% for standard applications, though it can be overdosed for unique signature effects. Its primary value lies in enhancement rather than standalone character—use it to add metallic warmth to Ambrofix and other ambergris materials, creating more complex amber accords. As a "musk booster," it amplifies musky notes without contributing its own musk character, adding substantivity and fixation through different mechanisms.

In modern masculine fragrances like Hermès H24, it provides the distinctive herbal-metallic signature that defines contemporary perfumery. The material excels at creating

products.name: Methyl 2-Methyl Butyrate
products.description:
This remarkable ester opens with an immediately recognisable burst of fresh green apple that captures that crisp, first-bite sensation. Its ethereal quality provides tremendous volatility and lift, creating a sparkling opening that radiates from the skin. Unlike heavier fruit materials, it delivers clean brightness without weight or density.

Your formulations benefit from its exceptional potency—detectable at just 0.92 parts per billion. This extreme sensitivity means tiny additions create massive impact, making it invaluable for boosting the perceived freshness of fruit accords. The material's unique ability to bridge fruity and floral territories stems from its subtle lily-of-the-valley undertones, allowing seamless integration into white floral compositions.

Use it strategically as a brightness catalyst rather than a dominant note. Its fleeting nature makes it perfect for creating dynamic fragrance openings that quickly recede to reveal heart materials. Combine with Ethyl 2-Methylbutyrate for fuller apple effects, or blend with cis-3-Hexenol for authentic Granny Smith apple accords. Its natural occurrence across numerous fruits validates its role in creating realistic, mouth-watering effects.

Methyl 2-Methyl vs Ethyl 2-Methyl

The fundamental difference lies in the alcohol portion of these esters. Methyl 2-Methylbutyrate uses methanol as its alcohol component (C6H12O2, MW 116.16), while Ethyl 2-Methylbutyrate uses ethanol (C7H14O2, MW 130.18). This seemingly small struc

products.name: Methyl Anthranilate
products.description:
Methyl Anthranilate is an essential aroma chemical for orange flower notes, as well as jasmine and tuberose. It has a distinctly grape-like odour which makes it great for fruit bases also. 

Methyl anthranilate has impact from very low amounts and is very beautiful when used in a Mellis accord with Hydroxycitronellal, Eugenol, Patchouli and Benzyl Salicylate.

Methyl Anthranilate reacts with certain materials to form schiff bases. More information on that is below.

We offer this material at 100% pure only.

products.name: Methyl Benzoate
products.description:
When it comes to versatility it doesn't get much better than this! Methyl benzoate is essential to recreate tuberose, ylang-ylang (both Cananga and Artabotrys hexapetalus types), wintergreen, root beer and fruit like the intensely flavoured fejioa (of which methyl benzoate can be up to 90% of its odour volatiles!) found all over New Zealand gardens. It has a subtle almond-like or honeyed nuance. Its scent is warm and rich, making it a versatile note that blends well with other ingredients.

The powerful phenolic character of this chemical is tempered by the judicious use of lactones. Despite its power, it is rather well behaved when handled right. A must have material — dare I say as essential as benzyl acetate!

products.name: Methyl Butyrate
products.description:
Methyl butyrate bursts off the blotter with a rush of crisp apple and ripe pineapple—bright, juicy, and immediately cheerful. A soft banana sweetness hovers behind the fruit, with a faint creamy-fermented quality that stops the material reading as purely synthetic. The overall impression is fresh fruit juice rather than boiled sweets.

Use this material when you need instant fruit impact in the opening of a composition. It adds a juicy apple bite to summer colognes, a tropical pineapple flash to aquatic and floral blends, and a bright fruity lift over heavier woody or musky bases. It is also useful as a masking agent in functional products, where its volatile fruitiness effectively covers sulphurous off-notes.

Methyl butyrate is one of the most volatile esters you will handle so support it with longer-lasting fruit materials like gamma-undecalactone or ethyl maltol to carry the fruity impression into the heart. At a trace to five percent it delivers all the fruit you need without tipping into heaviness.

products.name: Methyl Chavicol
products.description:
One sniff and you know tarragon — a bright, sweet anise that carries a distinctly green, leafy quality underneath. The spiciness registers immediately, warm and herbal rather than peppery. As it dries, a subtle balsamic-woody depth emerges that connects it naturally to base notes.

Methyl chavicol belongs in the aromatic-fougere toolkit. It furnishes that characteristic anise-herbal warmth that sits between lavender and coumarin in classic masculine structures. Combine it with clary sage and oakmoss for vintage aromatic accords, or introduce it into citrus blends where its spicy sweetness adds unexpected complexity.

The anise facet amplifies liquorice quality when you use it alongside star anise materials and anethole. In trace, it steers rose and jasmine accords towards warm spicy territory. You can also exploit its green herbaceous side by combining it with basil ct. linalool and galbanum.

GCMS analysis detects methyl chavicol in Tabu Vintage (1.08%), Aramis (0.96%), Patou Pour Homme (0.57%), Chanel Pour Monsieur (0.54%), Guerlain Mouchoir de Monsieur (0.28%), YSL Opium Men (0.21%), Derby Vintage (0.20%), Hermes Jardin sur le Nil (0.11%), Schiaparelli Shocking (0.07%), Chanel Bel Respiro (0.05%), Old Spice (0.03%), Dior Diorella Vintage (0.02%), Nuit de Noel Vintage (0.02%), Tom Ford F* Fabulous (0.01%), and Brut (0.01%).

products.name: Methyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Methyl cinnamate opens with a bold, sweet rush—strawberry and cherry laced with warm cinnamic spice. It is surprisingly powerful for a crystalline solid; even a trace fills a room with fruity-balsamic radiance. Diluted, the strawberry character becomes unmistakable, clean and ripe with a warm, almost jam-like sweetness beneath.

This material is a workhorse in oriental and amber compositions, where it adds fruity-balsamic power at very low doses. It brings convincing freshness to carnation accords, sweet depth to narcissus bases, and a fruity sparkle to citrus colognes—particularly when blended with labdanum. Try it in lavender and fougère compositions for an unexpected sweet-spicy twist that reads as both modern and rich.

Methyl vs Benzyl Cinnamate

These two cinnamate esters occupy opposite ends of the volatility spectrum. Methyl cinnamate is brighter, more intense, and distinctly fruity—strong strawberry and cherry notes with a sweet balsamic punch that projects immediately.

Benzyl cinnamate is heavier, quieter, and far more tenacious—a powdery balsamic base note where methyl cinnamate is a radiant top-to-heart modifier.

Use methyl cinnamate when you want a vivid fruity-balsamic opening; reach for benzyl cinnamate when you need warm, lasting balsamic depth in the drydown. Together, they create a complete cinnamic arc from bright fruity flash to slow resinous fade.

products.name: Methyl Corylone
products.description:
Methyl Corylone (Donut DIketone) is a go-to chemical if you need to make a bready edible accord or gourmand scent. It creates immediate warmth at 0.1-0.3% in sweet accords. Pair with vanillin for bakery effects or lactones for milky caramel. Structure compositions with this material as a middle note bridge between fruity tops and woody bases.

We also sell this at 10% in DPG for better workability across formulations. Use Methyl Corylone to elevate simple vanilla accords into sophisticated gourmand compositions that maintain character throughout dry-down.

NOTE: The naming of this product can be confusing due to trade terminology, but the Ventos Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is accurate for what we’re selling. It lists the material as 3,4-Dimethyl-1,2-Cyclopentanedione (CAS 13494-06-9), correctly identifying its chemistry—a cyclopentane ring with two ketone groups at positions 1 and 2 and methyl groups at 3 and 4 (C₇H₁₀O₂). While we and Ventos use "Methyl Corylone" as a trade name for this compound, some in the fragrance industry might expect "Methyl Corylone" to refer to a different chemical, 2-hydroxy-3-methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one (CAS 80-71-7), which has a distinct structure and profile.

products.name: Methyl Cyclogeranate
products.description:
Methyl cyclogeranate belongs to the same family as damascone alpha and delivers a similar luminous, fruity-rosy radiance — but without the sensitisation issues that increasingly restrict the damascones. This is the unrestricted alternative that gives you the same palette of effects.

The character is lighter and more transparent than damascone itself. Where damascone alpha punches hard with a jammy plum-rose impact, methyl cyclogeranate suggests it. The apple facet is clean and ripe, the rose dewy rather than heavy, and a faint camphoraceous undertone keeps it from tipping into sweetness. It functions as a top-heart material rather than a heart-base, lifting compositions upward.

Think of methyl cyclogeranate as your regulatory pressure valve. Wherever IFRA limits force you to ration damascones, this material fills the gap with its own fruity-floral signature. Try it alongside linalool and linalyl acetate to brighten citrus-herbal accords, or blend it with Ambrox for a contemporary fruity-amber contrast.

products.name: Methyl Diantilis®
products.description:
Isoeugenol, the classic clove-like basenote, is highly restricted and so other avenues are needed to give a long lasting carnation dry down to a scent. Enter Methyl Diantilis®. This chemical mirrors much of the effects of its older cousin but with the added advantages of greater stability and less susceptibility to discolouration.

Methyl Diantilis works brilliantly in both the heart and base of a fragrance, enhancing florals, vanilla and spicy blends. It complements rose, ylang-ylang, and jasmine for soft and balanced compositions, it enriches blends featuring vanilla, amber, and tonka bean, and it adds warmth and complexity to masculine tobacco and leather accords.

Methyl Diantilis should not be seen just as an isoeugenol replacer. It has a beauty and soft warming elegance all of its own.

products.name: Methyl Heptenone
products.description:
Methyl Heptenone opens with bright green-citrus freshness—lemongrass-like, fruity, and immediately uplifting. The apple-pear facets add juicy naturalism, while musty undertones provide unexpected depth. Herbaceous nuances recall verbena and citronella, creating a versatile top note material that bridges citrus and green families effortlessly.

Use Methyl Heptenone to add natural green freshness to hesperidic top notes and agrestic accords. It excels in lemongrass reconstructions, apple compositions, and citrus colognes seeking herbaceous lift. Blend with citral, linalool, and geraniol for lemongrass effects, or with fruity esters for apple-pear naturalism.

products.name: Methyl Heptine Carbonate
products.description:
Methyl Heptine Carbonate is one of the nicest of the violet leaf meets melon chemicals but highly restricted by IFRA to 0.047% of a finished product. Nevertheless it has a powerful presence in a blend and even at that low amount is is a wonderful aroma chemical well worth using. We often use it dosed to the maximum and then blended with other less restricted chemicals like Undecavertol and Violettyne MIP which come with lovely tonalities and nuances of their own.

Made famous by its overdose in Dior's Fahrenheit (1988, demo formula below) by Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Michel Almairac and Maurice Roger, this chemical can surprise in a multitude of ways. It is key to the top note of our wonderful Bois de Violette base and we suggest that the unfounded fear of its use could well be preventing a truly magical new fragrance from exploiting it properly within the regulations.

products.name: Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra
products.description:
Where Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur is the most floral and sweet of the methyl ionone family, Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra is the bolder, more leathery and orris member of the family. Use this slightly more expensive product when you seek a strong note of iris with more complexity and richness.

The power behind this product is that it contains the highest quantity of the Alpha Methyl Ionone isomer (CAS 7779-30-8) while Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur contains the highest amount of the weaker Alpha Isomethyl Ionone (CAS 127-51-5).

Iralia®: Finest and sweetest all round iris / violet chemical. Historic.
Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur: Cheapest. Floral, violet, soft, powdery.
Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra: Bolder, orris, leather, beeswax. Diffusive. Long lasting.

products.name: Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur
products.description:
Woody, floral, violet, orris. Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur is the most floral and sweet of the methyl ionone family (outside of the Firmenich Iralia® and Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha). 

This product has a premium odour despite its surprisingly low price. If you can't afford the supreme Iralia or Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha, this is the product you need.

Due to manufacturing shortages with Takasago we have switched our supplier to IFF.

Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur contains the highest amount of the weaker Alpha Isomethyl Ionone (CAS 127-51-5) while the power behind Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra is that it contains the highest quantity of the stronger Alpha Methyl Ionone isomer (CAS 7779-30-8)

Iralia®: Finest and sweetest all round iris / violet chemical. Historic.
Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur: Cheapest. Floral, violet, soft, powdery.
Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra: Bolder, orris, leather, beeswax. Diffusive. Long lasting.

products.name: Methyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
This material strikes you with immediate, penetrating brightness that commands attention through pure ethereal intensity. Its extraordinarily low odour threshold means even traces create significant impact, transforming compositions with sparkling vivacity. The sharp apple-pineapple character feels incredibly natural and juice-like rather than synthetic or cloying.

You harness this powerhouse exclusively as a top note modifier, never exceeding 1% in your concentrate due to its overwhelming potency. Work it into apple accords with manzanate and hexyl acetate, or build pineapple effects alongside allyl caproate and tropical thiols. Its champagne-like effervescence, stemming from natural occurrence in sparkling wines, creates sophisticated sparkling effects when paired with aldehydes and crisp florals.

Remember its ephemeral nature—this brilliant opening vanishes within an hour, making way for your heart notes. Use this material to create that crucial first impression of vibrant, realistic fruitiness that hooks the wearer's attention before gracefully disappearing.

products.name: Methyl Isoeugenol
products.description:
Methyl isoeugenol opens with a refined spicy sweetness that captures carnation's distinctive peppery floralcy. This material delivers the warm, diffusive character you need without the phenolic harshness of its relatives. Its woody undertones ground the composition whilst maintaining elegant floralcy.

You'll find this invaluable for building classic carnation bases at 5% or higher, where it forms the structural heart. In rose and ylang accords, use it at 0.5-1% to add sophisticated spice without overwhelming the floral core. The material's exceptional 240-hour tenacity means it anchors volatile top notes whilst contributing its own character through the drydown.

This material is key to Chanel No 5's warm spicy dry down.

products.name: Methyl Laitone 10% DPG
products.description:
Methyl Laitone is a versatile chemical with a distinctive creamy, coconut-milk profile. Its scent is enriched with soft, fruity undertones reminiscent of ripe plum or apricot, making it a key material when creating tropical, gourmand, or lactonic accords.

Highly potent, Methyl Laitone is effective in low concentrations, typically used up to 2% in formulations. It excels at adding depth and texture to white florals such as jasmine, gardenia, and tuberose, while also enhancing fruity notes like peach or osmanthus. Its lactonic quality pairs beautifully with sandalwood, creating a smooth, milky base that enriches the overall composition.

products.name: Methyl Linoleate
products.description:
Methyl Linoleate opens with an almost imperceptible oily-fatty note reminiscent of fresh vegetable oil or cosmetic base. This specialist material functions as an olfactory texturiser rather than a primary scent. Its value lies in what it does to other materials - smoothing harsh edges, adding creamy substance, and creating the waxy richness found in natural absolutes.

You'll find Methyl Linoleate invaluable for building realistic white floral reconstructions where it replicates the fatty components of jasmine and tuberose absolutes. Use it at 0.5-3% to soften aggressive leather notes, transforming harsh phenolic character into supple suede. Its extremely low volatility makes it an effective co-fixative, anchoring more fleeting notes while adding substantive body.

The material excels in creating specific cosmetic effects: the waxy scent of luxury lipstick, the creamy richness of face cream, or the fatty cleanliness of fine soap. Keep cool as it is prone to oxidation. Add tocopherol to formulations for stability. Despite handling challenges, its unique ability to impart natural fatty texture makes it irreplaceable for sophisticated compositions.

products.name: Methyl Myristate
products.description:
Methyl myristate is barely there on the blotter—a whisper of waxy petals, faint honey, and the unmistakable fatty-smooth character of orris butter. This is not a material you smell and immediately identify; it is a material you notice when it is missing. That quiet, lipid-rich smoothness is the backbone of what makes natural iris smell so luxurious.

Use methyl myristate to bring waxy realism to orris and iris accords built on ionones and methylionones. It rounds out mimosa, cassie, and tuberose bases with a fatty-floral body that reads as natural and expensive. In powder compositions alongside musks, it provides that soft, skin-like smoothness that separates flat from three-dimensional.

Methyl myristate is the same fatty ester that constitutes much of orris butter's waxy body, so you are effectively adding the structural backbone of real iris without the price tag.

products.name: Methyl Nicotinate
products.description:
Methyl Nicotinate is a curious herbal aroma chemical which can be used to add naturalising and complex nuances to blends. It works particularly well in jasmine, tobacco and herbal accords.

This material is found naturally in champaca absolute and many fruits so there is potential value in its use in the recreation of those materials.

While unrestricted by IFRA, it should be noted that Methyl Nicotinate is a rubefacient which means that in sufficiently high doses it can cause a reddening of the skin due to vasodilation and for that reason it is sometimes used in topical medicaments to soothe inflammation.

We recommend starting at quantities under 0.5% of your compound as a starting point.

products.name: Methyl Nonyl Ketone
products.description:
Methyl nonyl ketone delivers a powdery, waxy, orris-like character that reads as remarkably close to genuine iris root. The opening has a subtle fruity-orange brightness that quickly settles into the creamy, rooty elegance perfumers associate with expensive orris concrete. It refines beautifully on dilution.

Use this molecule as an affordable orris replacement or extender in your iris and violet compositions. It brings powdery depth to rose accords and adds quiet elegance to any floral heart. Blend at low levels — it works best as a subtle modifier rather than a dominant note.

Pair with methyl ionones and violet leaf for classic iris accords. Try it alongside rose absolute and oakmoss for a powdery chypre foundation. Combine with lavender and clary sage for sophisticated aromatic-floral compositions where the orris facet adds unexpected refinement.

products.name: Methyl Octine Carbonate
products.description:
More complex and, sadly, more restricted than Methyl Heptine Carbonate (MHC), the octine variant of this family is a lovely green and slightly fruity aroma chemical (in the direction of strawberry but not so pronounced as ethyl decine carbonate, another marvel) that lends its magic (which is effective in traces fortunately) to numerous fragrances such as Chanel's Coco Noir at 0.08%, and there is even a trace (0.001%) in Kurkdjian's Oud Satin Mood where it modifies a large dose of Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur.

Danute Pajaujis Anonis recomended its use in Fougère scents to bolster the green facets and, indeed, we see it prominently in the superstar of that genre, the original 1985 edition of Green Irish Tweed by Creed (our Compound Tweed). Methyl Octine Carbonate (MOC) works marvellously to temper the 10% dihydromyrcenol overdose of that same scent and in internal trials we have found the same to be very effective in smaller amounts in replicas of Abercrombie and Fitch's all-too-frequently (and wrongly) maligned Fierce (2002) by master perfumers Christophe Laudamiel and Bruno Jovanovic. Its ability to naturalise that chemical means it should be far more widely used today though (alas) fear of breaching IFRA or EU standards may make some perfumers reticent to approach it.

Combined, your total finished fragrance load of Methyl Octine Carbonate and Methyl Heptine Carbonate is 0.047%, and because MOC is restricted to 0.01%, you can use the remaining 0.037% in MHC to fill the gap. Be

products.name: Methyl Palmitate
products.description:
Methyl palmitate is almost silent on the blotter—a ghost of candle wax, faint oily fatness, and a whisper of orris. You will not smell it and think "perfume ingredient"; you will smell it and think "the waxy residue left when an expensive iris dries down." That is precisely its value. It provides texture rather than scent.

This fatty acid methyl ester is one of the building blocks of natural orris butter, where it sits alongside methyl myristate as part of the waxy matrix that gives iris its luxurious, buttery mouthfeel. Use it in iris and violet accords to add that characteristic fatty-waxy body beneath the ionones and irones. In powdery compositions, it contributes a smooth, skin-like warmth that makes synthetics read as more natural and three-dimensional.

Methyl palmitate melts around body temperature, which means it arrives as a low-melting waxy solid that liquefies easily in the hand. Dose it generously—it has almost no odour impact of its own, so it functions as a textural modifier rather than a scent contributor. Pair it with methyl myristate for a more complete orris-butter effect, or use it alongside alpha-isomethyl ionone and heliotropin to build affordable iris accords with genuine waxy realism.

products.name: Methyl Pamplemousse
products.description:
Methyl Pamplemousse is the classic grapefruit chemical, widely used and widely adored. It suits both feminine and masculine scents and can be used in small amounts as a nuancer for citrus or in overdose for an interesting top note character.

Blends with Dihydromyrcenol and Cassis Base 345B are outstanding. 

Methyl Pamplemousse is found in so many superstar fragrances they are too numerous to name, but a few that stand out are 0.45% in Gabrielle (Chanel, 2017), 1% in Bleu (Chanel, 2010), 1.4% in Terre d'Hermès (2006), 0.8% Grand Soir (2016, Maison Francis Kurkdjian), 2% in Vetiver (Frater, 2022), 2.2% in Spicebomb (2012, Viktor&Rolf), 0.65% in Opus XIV Royal Tobacco by Amouage (2022), and Creed's Royal Oud (2011) dosed at 0.17%.

products.name: Methyl Phenyl Acetate 40% DPG
products.description:
Methyl Phenyl Acetate is the methyl ester of Phenyl Acetic Acid and is sweeter and more honey-like but also more penetrating. It works exceptionally well in combination with its parent acid and other honey notes and associated florals such as Ethyl Benzoate, Methyl Anthranilate, and Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol.

Due to DEA requirements in the USA we sell this at 40% dilution only.

products.name: Methyl Propionate
products.description:
Methyl propionate opens with a sharp, fresh burst of rum-like fruitiness that immediately evokes dark sticky strawberry preserves and crisp apple. This ester's ethereal quality creates an airy, juicy sensation. Its medium strength provides four hours of substantivity at full concentration.

You'll find this material invaluable for building realistic fruit complexes, particularly when you need authentic strawberry or apple notes with alcoholic depth. It excels at adding tropical fruitiness to top notes whilst contributing the aged quality found in rum accords. Blend it with other fruity esters to create mouth-watering gourmand effects.

Combine methyl propionate with ethyl butyrate for enhanced pineapple-rum character or pair with isoamyl acetate for banana-fruit punch effects. Use alongside William's ester to amplify pear notes. This ester bridges fresh citrus openings with sweet fruity hearts beautifully.

products.name: Methyl Salicylate
products.description:
Beyond its dominant wintergreen character, methyl salicylate reveals subtle floral undertones reminiscent of tea rose with a hint of sweet ylang-ylang when used in high dilution.

At microscopic concentrations, methyl salicylate unveils surprising floral facets that remain imperceptible at conventional usage levels. Its delicate tea-rose quality emerges only when masterfully diluted, contributing ethereal warmth to sophisticated floral compositions.

Under IFRA 52, starting in 2027, Methyl Salicylate will be dramatically restricted to 0.035% of your finished product. This will have knock-on effects relating to tuberose, ylang-ylang, jasmine and many other florals.

products.name: Methyl Tuberate
products.description:
Methyl tuberate captures the waxy, lactonic heart of tuberose with remarkable precision. This powerful modifier brings an authentic white floral signature that lifts tuberose and gardenia accords beyond what absolutes achieve alone. You'll notice its metallic edge cuts through heavy florals whilst the creamy lactone body adds dimensional depth.

Use this material to build the fleshy, fruity core of tuberose compositions alongside gamma decalactone and benzyl alcohol. It works brilliantly with fruity lactones to provide lift and airiness to otherwise dense white floral structures. Keep dosages around 0.5-1% in your concentrate—its strength means a little delivers substantial impact without overwhelming more delicate floral notes.

Pair methyl tuberate with methyl anthranilate to amplify exotic white floral character. Benzyl salicylate softens its metallic facets whilst hydroxycitronellal extends its muguet-like freshness. This lactone excels when you need authentic tuberose tonality without the indolic heaviness that can dominate a composition.

products.name: Microcare PEHG
products.description:
Microcare PEHG is a ready-to-use liquid preservative blend of phenoxyethanol and ethylhexylglycerin in a 90:10 ratio. It barely smells of anything — just the faintest rose-like hint from the phenoxyethanol, which vanishes entirely at working concentrations. Add it to any formula that contains water.

If your product contains water — body sprays, room mists, toners, anything with an aqueous phase — it needs a preservative. Microcare PEHG gives you broad-spectrum protection against bacteria, yeasts, and moulds in a single, easy-to-use liquid. It is paraben-free, formaldehyde-free, and approved for use globally.

Add it during the cool-down phase at half to one percent of your finished product. Phenoxyethanol also acts as a mild fragrance fixative, so it does double duty.

products.name: Miel Blanc
products.description:
Miel Blanc was a classical honey base from De Laire that found its way into many great perfumes indirectly by way of the great Mousse de Saxe base and directly as a honey note.

This non-discoloring almost clear formula is perfect for perfumes needing a sweet honey note without the intense colour of our other honey base Mielarome. While less floral than Mielarome, this base contributes a more powerful note and works very well in minute amounts up to overdose as it is completely IFRA compliant to a whopping 40% of your finished fragrance!

products.name: Miel de Ciste
products.description:
Miel de Ciste is a co-distillation — labdanum distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is labdanum taken back to its origins — raw, green, herbal, recalling the ancient Cretan tradition of dragging leather straps through wild cistus bushes to collect resin.

What distinguishes Miel de Ciste from standard labdanum absolute is an unexpected honeyed facet. Not bright floral honey but something closer to honeydew — the dark, malty, almost mineral honey produced when bees feed on aphid secretions rather than flower nectar. This note exists only because of the co-distillation; the interaction between gurjun balsam and labdanum under steam creates byproducts neither material produces alone. The cinnamic warmth typical of labdanum is present but softened, less dominant.

Use it in chypres and ambers where you want labdanum that feels wild-harvested rather than industrially extracted. It gives raw garrigue authenticity to Mediterranean compositions. The honeyed quality lets it double as a natural honey note in orientals without adding a dedicated honey material.

products.name: Mielarome
products.description:
An intense and highly floral honey base in the clasical style enhanced with natural absolutes and essential oils. This base can be used at trace amounts to add sweetness and richness. Originally sold as Melarome by Chiris, this base was found in such fragrances as La Rose Jacqueminot, by Coty.

Try it in larger doses with lavender and related notes for a unique and appealing modern fougere type fragrance. 

For a non-discolouring honey try our Miel Blanc.

products.name: Milk Lactone
products.description:
Milk Lactone (so-called as it is really an acid), is an intriguing material which, while clearly milky, exhibits an unusual but rather natural green quality. A hint of cheese and floralcy completes it. Use this to add a peach-skin effect to a fruity base or to enhance a lovely Gardenia base such as our Gardenia J. Ellis.

This fine aroma chemical should not be confused with the product sold by some vendors as Milk Lactone Super or Milk Lactone (Mixture) which is really just a base built around Delta Dodecalactone.

Milk Lactone blends with all the other lactones as well as green chemicals Stemone, Triplal, and Liffarome. This also finds use as an extender for rose absolute when combined with Phenoxanol.

products.name: Mimosa Absolute, France
products.description:
Because the annual quantities of Mimosa absolute are dependent on weather, it is a material that can be difficult to keep in steady supply. Consequently we offer stock from the two finest suppliers, V MANE Fils and this beautiful product from LMR. In both cases the absolute comes from the same village in France but methods of extraction are unique to the two companies. Both are wonderful and interchangeable. We tend to fluctuate between liking one over the other.

Mimosa has a delicate sweet odour somewhere between cassie and violet. It is perceptible in trace amounts and does an astonishing job of naturalising a fragrance. The lightest touch will elevate virtually all perfume types. Needless to say it blends exceptionally well with Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute, Fleur de Cassie, Violette Bleue and the classic violet synthetics Iralia® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF).

Unlike lesser qualities, our two mimosa offerings are not brittle but have rather a stiff honey-like consistency. However, it is still extremely difficult to work with so we also offer it at dilution in natural triethyl citrate. That means this is a 100% pure and natural ISO 9235 standard product.

We also offer a wonderfully complex floral base in the form of our Mimosa De Provence.

products.name: Mimosa De Provence
products.description:
Fraterworks® Mimosa de Provence (formerly just Mimosa) is a beautiful recreation of wild harvested French mimosa smelling intensely of honeyed woods with fatty and violet nuances and an anisic drydown. Mimosa de Provence is an updated reconstruction of the classic base of the same name from Th. Mühlethaler S.A., the great Swiss early 20th century manufacturer of bases and fragrances.

Mimosa de Provence is a sweet and refined note which can be used in large doses for an eccentric twist or in touches as a fixative and nuancer. This base  is enriched with precious essential oils and rare absolutes.

Classification: Mimosa (Acacia dealbata also sometimes called Acacia deccurens) should not be confused with Cassie (Acacia farnesiana) or the entirely unrelated Pink Acacia (Robinia pseudoacacia), all of which are items of interest to perfumers and, consquently, for sale here.

products.name: Mimosa “Supreme” Absolute
products.description:
Mimosa has a delicate sweet odour somewhere between cassie and violet. It is perceptible in trace amounts and does an astonishing job of naturalising a fragrance. The lightest touch will elevate virtually all perfume types. Needless to say it blends exceptionally well with Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute, Fleur de Cassie, Violette Bleue and the classic violet synthetics Iralia® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF).

Unlike lesser qualities, our mimosa is not brittle but has rather a stiff honey-like consistency. However, it is still extremely difficult to work with so we also offer it at dilution in natural triethyl citrate. That means this is a 100% pure and natural ISO 9235 standard product.

You will never use another mimosa product after you have experienced this jewel in the crown of France's finest naturals.

We also offer a wonderfully complex floral base in the form of our Mimosa De Provence.

products.name: Mimosal™
products.description:
The latest muguet floral to hit the markets, Mimosal™ is designed to fill, at least partially, the gap left in the market with the banning of Lilial and Lyral. Mimosal is powerfully aldehydic bearing soft powdery floral notes with a watery aspect. It is novel in having something of a dual personality — crossing between muguet and Mimosa. Mimosal brings a clean, fresh long lasting muguet note for floral fragrances and is so elegant it could be considered a perfume in its own right.

From Firmenich: “Intense green muguet note with a soft anisic facet and fresh cyclamen undertone. Mimosal is really performing and offers an impressive clean and long-lasting effect. It brings a fresh and soft muguet signature to floral accords. Mimosal is part of Firmenich's Beyond Muguet 2018.”

Mimosal blends beautifully with Gardenia J. Ellis, Cyclamen des Alpes, Sandexol, all our Muguet bases, Dreamwood™, Florol, and Hivernal® Neo.

products.name: Mintonat
products.description:
Mintonat is not a straightforward mint material. It opens minty and fresh, yes, but immediately reveals floral-lavender depth, a warm spicy-clove facet, and a green herbal quality that makes it far more interesting and versatile than menthol or carvone. It smells like a herb garden rather than a peppermint sweet.

Use it to boost freshness and vivacity across a wide range of compositions. It has a particular affinity for lavender, where it amplifies and rounds the herbal character beautifully. In fougères, it unites the aromatic top with the coumarin-oakmoss base in a way that feels seamless and natural. A little goes a long way.

Pair it with lavender and coumarin for classic fougère construction, with bergamot and dihydromyrcenol for modern aromatic freshness, or with geranium for a herbal-floral heart. It fades quickly on paper but clings well to skin and fabric — judge it in wear, not on a blotter.

products.name: Mirabelle Base 002000 F
products.description:
Mirabelle de Nancy is a type of yellow mirabelle plum tree that has scented blossoms — a rarity for fruit trees. Firmenich's Mirabelle base takes that delicate scent and builds a fantasy chord around it, of lactones, fruit, spices and florals.

Mirabelle Base is unusual on first sniff, with its powerful lactones dominating the opening, shortly followed by the classic plum aroma chemicals and finally a balsamic cinnamon dry down which is very beautiful. In its own, the odour is quite reminiscent of the fruity character of Visa by Piguet.

Blend it with Lactone Storm to add character, and with Prunella (Firmenich's classic plum base) to add radiance and top note power. You may not reach for this as frequently as Prunella, but it is definitely worth keeping in the arsenal.

products.name: Miraclewood™
products.description:
If you are looking for a megadose wood material like Iso E Super®, Miraclewood™ is for you. Built around the finest and most radiant wood materials enriched by luxurious and rare natural oils such as “mulacro” oil, Miraclewood is the cedar of our time. Velvety smooth with subtle greenness and all the volume you desire but can never get from Iso E Super, Miraclewood is absolutely essential for all perfumers.

Use Miraclewood as a one for one replacer for Iso E Super in your formulas and be amazed. Add a ribbon of warm animalics with our incredible Ambrexol™ and a touch of Laevo Muscone and you have a complete perfume.

products.name: Mitti Attar
products.description:
Mitti attar is the distillation of earth itself — that is not a metaphor. In Kannauj, India's perfume capital, clay from dried lakebeds is shaped into crude vessels, half-baked in small kilns, then distilled into sandalwood oil. The result captures something you already know: petrichor, the intoxicating smell of rain on dry ground. Indian perfumers have been bottling this scent for centuries. For all intents and purposes, this as close as you'll get to a natural geosmin.

The opening is cool and mineral — baked clay, wet stone, a faint electric charge. There is nothing floral about it. A quiet, bread-like sweetness emerges as the sandalwood base rises, and the mineral edge softens over several hours into something serene and meditative. Mitti attar does not project aggressively.
