It radiates from the skin, intimate and contemplative.

Use mitti attar to ground florals or add realism to green compositions. With vetiver it creates deep forest dampness; with rose, a garden-after-rain effect. It layers well with patchouli and oakmoss for a complete forest-floor accord. Dose carefully — too much flattens a composition into mud rather than enriching it with earth.

products.name: MMB
products.description:
MMB (Methoxymethyl Butanol) is a new product from Kuraray designed as a general purpose diluent to be used with air fresheners (reed diffusers, plugins, pump sprays etc).

MMB has excellent solubility properties, exceeding those of most classic diluents, and a low odour.

This is a must have material because solvents like DPG, TEC and IPM are not suitable for use in reed diffusers.

MMB can be combined with alcohol to increase its evaporation rate, or with water to decrease it. It can also safely be combined with Isopar-M, Dowanol DPM and Dowanol TPM which are the more traditional types of diluent used for reeds. 

With a flash point over 70 Celsius degrees, it can be safely uses in products that need international air shipping without the fear of triggering dangerous goods costs.

Check out our demonstration formula below to see MMB in use. This is our excellent and highly accurate replica of Ernesto by Cire Trudon.

products.name: Motia Attar
products.description:
Motia Attar opens with a sharp, bright jasmine character — narcotic and indolic in the way only Jasminum sambac can be — laid over soft, creamy sandalwood. The honey side of jasmine sits in the heart, lifting into faint green and tea-like nuances. Sandalwood underneath gives the whole composition body.

Use Motia Attar where you want a true Indian jasmine anchored to sandalwood — oriental floral bouquets, mukhallats, soliflores and Mughal-style attar reconstructions. It bridges naturally to oud, saffron, rose and ylang-ylang. A small amount lifts simple white-floral bases into dense, Indian-style depth.

Pair with rose otto and saffron attar for a Mughal mukhallat heart, or use alongside oud and ambergris for a luxurious oriental. A trace under champaca or magnolia adds Indian warmth without obscuring the lighter florals. Undiluted, the sandalwood reads heavier than the jasmine until a few minutes in.

Motia Attar is the traditional Indian jasmine perfume — fresh Jasminum sambac flowers (locally called Bela), hand-picked at dawn in the monsoon and co-distilled by deg-bhapka into sandalwood oil. The night-blooming north-Indian jasmine was a Mughal-era court favourite and the signature scent of the Nizams of Hyderabad. This Motia is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, a Kannauj distillery run by five generations of the Kapoor family using copper degs and the traditional water-distillation method.

products.name: Muguet 16
products.description:
Muguet 16 was one of the greatest lily of the valley bases. Created by Marius Reboul in 1929 for Givaudan (founded by Léon Givaudan in 1895 at the young age of 20 with his brother Xavier, eight years his senior), Muguet 16 went on to feature in numerous fragrances over the decades, including Mais Oui by Bourjois. So popular was Muguet 16 that it was copied by every fragrance house (right up to Drogco as late as the 1960s in their Muguet Nouveau base).

Muguet 16 is a real delight and despite the limited number of materials available to perfumers in the early 20th century is perhaps a more perfect fit for modern fragrances than most classical Muguet bases. 

Reboul constructed this base with a very light hand, using transparent materials over heavier ones, and so, for example, we find Cinnamyl Acetate taking the place of the far heavier Cinnamic Alcohol favoured at the time. Every material is balanced to perfection and the resulting base stands as a testament to the brilliance of this gentleman who is perhaps more famous for his bases than his perfumes.

Long gone from the modern perfumer's palette (and tragically long forgotten by most), we are thrilled to be able to offer our restoration of this timeless masterpiece to our discerning clients.

If you are interested in Marius Reboul's work, we also offer his Amarante base, Sophira (the key to Rigaud's Un Air Embaume from 1914).

products.name: Muguet Aldehyde
products.description:
Muguet Aldehyde opens with a burst of aldehydic freshness that captures the elusive scent of lily-of-the-valley petals covered in morning dew. Its distinctive ozone character provides a cold, metallic sharpness reminiscent of fresh air after rain. The material combines a rosy-citrus heart with an almost aquatic transparency.

You'll find this aldehyde transforms heavy floral accords by introducing ventilation and lift where traditional muguet materials feel flat. It bridges the gap between aggressive marine molecules and soft florals seamlessly, making unisex fragrances sing with its gender-neutral freshness. At 0.1-1% in your concentrate, it provides the diffusive power that projects off skin during the first four hours.

Combine it with Florol to recreate the volume once provided by restricted materials. Layer it over patchouli for the legendary Mellis accord that vibrates with sweet-woody harmony. Trace amounts will modernise rose compositions by highlighting their lemony morning aspects rather than their heavier afternoon sweetness.

products.name: Muguet Chiris
products.description:
Chiris was the oldest of the French perfumery houses, also being the first to set up large scale manufacture of essential oils in Grasse and establishing a perfumery school there. The two most famous graduates of the school were François Coty and Ernest Beaux who, as fate would have it, ultimately ended up back there when he fled with Rallet to France from the murderous rampage spreading across revolutionary Russia.

Chiris produced some wonderful bases and Beaux and Coty made much use of them in their early years. This one (originally called Muguet A204) was a vital floraliser in Chanel No 5 while Lilac A07 was the main ingredient in Coty's early Jasmin de Corse fragrance.

Muguet Chiris is the most luxurious of the muguet bases and incorporates many extremely costly naturals and the very best aroma chemicals. It is a classic muguet base built around Hydroxycitronellal and despite its age is very useable in modern fragrances where it can replace the less interesting singular chemical floral hearts so often seen in department store brands today.

For a simpler option, consider Muguet de Grasse, Ernest Beaux's own muguet creation (though not the one he used in the early versions of No 5).

products.name: Muguet de Grasse
products.description:
From the great Muguet des Bois by Henri Robert to the masterpiece of Coroliane crafted by Edmond Roudnitska, we have your muguet needs covered... with one exception. That exception is Muguet de Grasse, this is the muguet beloved by Ernest Beaux who trained and worked at Chiris both before and after the revolution forced the company to relocate from Russia to France. Chiris had purchased the great Russian fragrance company Rallet the year Beaux started work there and it was during this employment that he created Bouquet de Catherine (Rallet le No 1) which later became Chanel No 5.

As simple as simplicity itself, Muguet de Grasse is a diaphanous effusion of floralcy created with only the essential early muguet aroma chemicals and a delicate touch of natural absolutes. The very high concentration of hydroxycitronellal (then a revolutionary molecule) makes this a perfect muguet to use in place of that chemical for more character or as an accent in a lily of the valley fond.

Muguet de Grasse is perhaps the most versatile of all our muguet bases, and most definitely one that suits a modern fragrance as much as it did the great classics of the early 20th century.

For a dazzling and novel modern accord, try a blend of Muguet de Grasse with Mimosal™ and the merest trace of cumin seed oil and Cassis Base 345B.

products.name: Muguet Des Bois
products.description:
Important: This is not a perfume. It should not be applied to the skin directly. It is a blend of chemicals used in the manufacture of fragrances.

This is the famed Muguet des Bois base made by Henri Robert when he was working at Coty. It was released as a fragrance in 1941 under the same name but repurposed later as a base. It is a sweet and very natural green muguet base replicating the scent of wild lily of the valley flowers.

Edmond Roudnitska considering it the finest muguet ever made (despite making his own incredible Coroliane base) used it as the foundation of his Diorissimo fragrance for Dior in 1956.

In a coincidental turn of events, Henri Robert admired Roudnitska's Coroliane base so much that he used it as the foundation of No 19 for Chanel in 1970. We also sell the wonderful Coroliane base.

Muguet Des Bois was the key lily in Poison by Dior.

Reminder: This is not a perfume.

products.name: Muguet Fleurs
products.description:
Safe for use up to 15% of the finished product for IFRA 51, this is a radiant and modern lily of the valley taking as its starting point a scientific headspace reconstruction. Use it as a complete muguet fragrance or as a luscious floral canvas.

Fraterworks Muguet Fleurs' fresh green character is boosted with incredible radiant molecules and luscious absolutes and essential oils.

products.name: Muguet Invar
products.description:
From 1914 to the 1930s, Roure made a series of bases they called referred to as invariable, or invar, meaning that they maintained the same odour profile from start to finish. They were effectively linear bases. These bases were enormously popular with Muguet Invar and Jasmine Invar being two of the most used.

Muguet Invar presents a fresh and soft muguet with no rough edges. It is a perfect all-round floralising base. This is simply muguet. Useable at up to 8.4% of your finished product.

products.name: Muguet Royale
products.description:
If you only have one muguet, Muguet Royale is it. Wtih an astonishing pedigree, Muguet Royale made famous many great scents, among them Arpège and Miss Dior. Beloved of Jean Carles, this base is floral to the max and accented with many delightful naturals.

With an IFRA 51 max-use of 7.29% of the finished product, you can use Muguet Royale almost indiscriminately. In small amounts it adds richness and interest, while in overdose it adds a glorious lily of the valley note immediately recognisable to all.

products.name: Muguet Weriguine
products.description:
Constanin Wereguine (1899–1982) was a master perfumer who was assistant and second perfumer to Ernest Beaux at both Chanel and Bourjois and Henri Robert at the Former. A Russian aristocrat educated in Yalta, Wereguin eventually went on to work at Rhône-Poulenc. 

Muguet Weriguine is the personal creation of this great perfumer and was used in place of other classic muguet bases that were fading from use in the 1970s and 1980s, notably Muguet 16 and Ernest Beaux's own Muguet de Grasse.

Weriguine cleverly enriched his muguet with natural citrus (including a rather large dose of neroli oil) which gives it a lovely unique character that blends exceedingly well with the likes of Bouvardia De Laire, Floranol, Fleur D'Oranger and Jasmine 1109 which has its own orange blossom nuance.

products.name: Muguissimo™
products.description:
Muguissimo opens with a fresh, clean burst of lily-of-the-valley—bright and aldehydic but never harsh, with an immediate watery transparency. Beneath the muguet sits a soft cyclamen facet and subtle anisic sweetness. The overall effect is elegant, modern, and unmistakably floral.

This is Firmenich's newest addition to their Beyond Muguet collection, released publicly in 2022 after years as a captive ingredient. What makes Muguissimo special is its linearity—it brings that fresh, clean muguet character from top note all the way through to the drydown, maintaining consistency throughout the life of a fragrance. Use it in white floral compositions, fresh feminine accords, and anywhere you need transparent lily-of-the-valley without the regulatory concerns of older muguet aldehydes.

Despite being classified as a base note by volatility, it reads as fresh and transparent throughout. Dose it where you would use hydroxycitronellal or other muguet aldehydes. Pair it with Hedione, linalool, and other white floral materials for luminous bouquets, or use it in aquatic compositions where its watery facet enhances freshness.

products.name: Musc Doré
products.description:
Musc Doré (Golden Musk) is the first in a new Bertrand Duchaufour x Fraterworks trilogy, Les Trois Voiles. In French, voile holds three meanings at once — veil, sheer fabric, and sail — and each musk takes one:

Musc Doré — the veil: a sheer golden veil of warmth drawn over the skin.
Musc de Lin — the fabric: voile is the gauze-fine cloth woven from flax, clean air made textile.
Musc d'Embruns — the sail: canvas wet with sea spray, carrying the skin into open air.

Musc Doré is a warm golden skin musk with powdered facets. It bears an almost fougère-like structure which hints at Duchaufour's masterpiece Sartorial (2010) for Penhaligons. This is the scent of the golden hours at the close of day, the scent of warm skin, the scent of nostalgia.

While Musk Doré, and indeed the other two members of the trilogy, can be used as the foundation upon which to construct a fragrance, it is, in itself, so elegant and complete that it can be simply overdosed and worn as-is.

products.name: Muscarome
products.description:
A warm, powdery musk with buckskin softness — Muscarome J5 is a classical reconstruction of Tonkin deer musk 5% tincture. The smell is sensual and animalic, with creamy ambery-balsamic warmth and a subtle leathery edge. It is built around musk ketone and a supporting cast of musky-animalic materials.

Use Muscarome J5 to give orientals, fougères, chypres and leather bases a classical animalic warmth without the cost of natural musk tincture. A small amount rounds the base and adds powdery skin depth; larger doses push into full deer-musk territory. It fixes light materials around it and extends the dry-down.

Pair with sublimolide and Civettone Base for a rounded, refined musk accord, or push it alongside castoreum and costus Oliffac for a more openly animalic base. A trace under cedar or oud pulls them into skin territory. In chypres it revives a dusty oakmoss-labdanum backbone.

Among the three classical deer musk reconstructions on the market, Muscarome J5 is the softest and most powdery, with a buckskin-smooth character and balsamic-ambery sweetness. Tonquitone (IFF) reads sharper and more openly animalic, with a pronounced civet-urinous edge and sweet caramel-vanilla facets. Shangralide Oliffac (IFF) sits between them — dirtier and more leathery than Muscarome J5, but less fierce than Tonquitone's direct deer-musk character.

products.name: Muscenone®
products.description:
Muscenone is perhaps the nicest of the musk chemicals and certainly one of the most profound in its ability to add radiance, blending and fixation to a fragrance. This musk has the ability to put people at ease and to induce comfort, so much so that casinos famously spray it through their air conditioning ducts to keep clients gambling longer. Muscenone can be used in trace to overdose.

According to Arctander: “Delicate, but extremely tenacious musky odor, upon dilution developing more woody notes, not quite as soft and velvety as those of the Muscone, perhaps equal in power, but inferior in beauty.”

And Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) says: “If habanolide is radiant, floral and musky with metallic notes, muscenone is animal, strongly musk tonkin, and plays a role in [replicating] the natural product’s odor, perhaps, more important[ly] than muscone. […] Muscenone smells of the most animal-like part of deer musk powder or musk absolute, if made. All of these unsaturated macro cyclic musks are incredibly strong and accords we made in the past mixed cresols with exaltolide or muscone and are now much finer and more elegant when using muscenone or chemically related products. It is being widely used in fragrances such as Bulgari for Men.”

Muscenone even finds its uses in the world of ouds and attars; the wonderful tonkin musk note of Ajmal's Areej Al Shouk is owed largely to this chemical in combination wit

products.name: Muscone
products.description:
Muscone by Firmenich represents the perfumer's essential interpretation of this legendary musk molecule—a masterwork of versatility and refinement. While its sibling Muscone Laevo captures the raw magnificence of natural Tonkin musk, regular Muscone offers the perfumer a more nuanced canvas, revealing different facets of the musk family's extraordinary character.

Where Laevo muscone delivers intensity and primal warmth, Muscone provides a softer, more diffusive quality that makes it remarkably adaptable across a broader palette of compositions. Its gentler animalic signature allows it to enhance rather than dominate, making it the preferred choice for modern interpretations where musk must dance rather than command. Think of it as cashmere to Laevo's fur—equally luxurious, but with a whisper-soft touch that invites rather than announces.

This exceptional material exhibits remarkable radiance and projection, creating an invisible aura that extends the life and sillage of any composition. Its fixative properties remain extraordinary, binding volatile top notes while allowing heart notes to bloom with unprecedented clarity. Professional perfumers often describe it as having a "clean" animalic quality—sensual without being overtly carnal, warm without overwhelming delicate florals or fresh accords.

In this era of global Muscone Laevo shortage, Firmenich's regular Muscone emerges not merely as an alternative, but as an opportunity to explore new dimensions of musk in perfumery.

products.name: Muscone Laevo
products.description:
While we do have some stock coming, this product is going to be scarce until 2026 as both main manufacturers are having serious supply chain issues. We will update as more information comes to hand and will also start offering racemic Muscone shortly.

There can be no doubt that Firmenich is unsurpassed in the production of the finest musks. From Helvetolide® to Muscenone®, their products reign supreme. We are currently the only retail supplier of their incredible Muscone Laevo, the highest quality form of muscone produced by any company and the chemical which is at the very heart of genuine natural Tonkin deer musk.

When compared to the more common (and inferior) muscone (usually referred to simply as "muscone"), laevo muscone is stronger, more animalic, more natural and more erogenous. Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) once opined: “It is perceptible in very small amounts and its fixation is so extreme that it seems incredible. Although it doesn’t substitute completely for the natural product, it is equal to it on the lasting properties. We can consider it outstanding and it imparts great elegance.” It should be noted that some people are completely anosmic to muscone and laevo muscone. 

This noble product adds astounding fixation and a ribbon of refined and luxurious animalic warmth. Sniffing Firmenich's Laevo Muscone is like burying your face in a rich fur coat. Undeniably this musk is essential for ev

products.name: Mushroom Abs, Deco
products.description:
Decolourised mushroom absolute opens with the unmistakable scent of autumn forests after rain. Damp earth mingles with fungal sweetness, creating an immediate sense of place. This pale version retains all the olfactory power of traditional mushroom absolute while offering formulation flexibility for delicate compositions. Bear in mind, however, that while paler than standard absolute, this is still brown in colour.

This material works magic at trace levels, transforming simple accords into complex experiences. In chypres, it grounds mossy notes with authentic forest floor depth. Modern perfumers exploit its savory-sweet duality to create unexpected gourmand effects—think dark chocolate with mysterious umami undertones that intrigue rather than overwhelm.

Deploy this treasure sparingly—its potency demands respect. At 0.01-0.1%, it adds subliminal earthiness that makes compositions feel grounded and natural. Combine with oakmoss for ultimate chypre depth, or pair with cocoa and coffee for avant-garde gourmands that challenge conventional sweetness.

Owing to the high cost we are also offering this at 10% in natural odourless Triethyl Citrate.

products.name: Musk Ambrette
products.description:
Musk Ambrette is the fruitiest of the nitro musks and the classical musk that blends best with floral notes. It has an astonishing power to tame and beautify large quantities of coumarin and tonka bean and so became something of a work horse (often in concert with Musk Xylene) in the fougère fragrances of the past. Edmond Roudnitska loved it so much that when he created Eau Sauvage for Dior (which contains no musks at all), he had a special version made with 10% Musk Ambrette. It was his private signature fragrance for the remainder of his life.

Its most famous overdose was in the original Brut where it was used at 13% by Karl Mann for Fabergé in 1964. It is, however, effective at very small amounts. It blends beautifully with the other classic nitro musks which we also stock: Musk Xylene and Musk Ketone.

IMPORTANT: Musk Xylene and Musk Ambrette are prohibited from fragrance use in most countries. At Fraterworks we do not use either of these musks in any of our products. We sell the musks solely so that fragrance aficionados can have access to all the materials of classical perfumery. This should not be used in production cosmetics or fragrances unless you are certain your target market allows it. 

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Musk Ketone
products.description:
Musk ketone is the true workhorse of the nitro musk family and, fortunately, is not prohibited from use, though some jurisdictions limit the total amount in a finished perfume to 1.4%. Our musk ketone is tested to ensure it complies with the regulatory requirement that it contain < 0.1% musk xylene which can occur as a manufacturing byproduct.

Musk ketone is the softest of the nitro musk trilogy and next to musk xylene the one most closely resembling the scent of deer musk. It works beautifully when combined with Muscone Laevo, the chemical found in natural musk.

Musk ketone is a crystalline powder which you can add directly to your juice by weight as it will dissolve in the blend.

This musk has a powdery quality and is one of the longest lasting synthetic musks on the market. For that reason it is highly valued even in trace amounts. Musk ketone featured heavily (often at very high doses) in most of the great fragrances of the past, from Fougère Royale (the first fragrance to contain synthetic ingredients in 1882 — formula below) to modern masterpieces such as Frederic Malle's Musk Ravageur (2000) and Ambre Sultan (1993) by Serge Lutens.

products.name: Musk R1
products.description:
Musk R1 opens with creamy, powdery softness that immediately evokes warm, clean skin. This macrocyclic lactone delivers the quintessential white musk character modern perfumery demands. Its lactonic sweetness brings an intimate, sensual dimension that transforms compositions.

This material excels at creating that coveted "your skin but better" effect in fragrances. You'll find it indispensable for contemporary clean compositions where it adds depth without heaviness. Its exceptional substantivity ensures your creations maintain their intimate warmth for days on fabric.

Combine Musk R1 with florals to enhance their creamy facets, or use it in amber bases for added sensuality. Layer it with other musks like Habanolide for complex skin effects. Small additions transform aldehydic compositions, rounding harsh edges while maintaining transparency.

products.name: Musk Xylene
products.description:
Musk Xylene (or Musk Xylol) is the gentlemen's "shaving musk". Because of its soapy and fatty qualities, it was frequently found as part of classic fougère type fragrances and men's colognes in general.

Perhaps its most famous overdose was in Canoe created by Jean Carles for Dana (see our demo named "Kayak" below for the formula of this classic fougère fragrance). It is, however, effective at very small amounts. It blends beautifully with the other classic nitro musks which we also stock: Musk Ambrette and Musk Ketone.

Musk Xylene is a crystalline powder which you can add directly to your juice by weight as it will dissolve in the blend.

IMPORTANT: Musk Xylene and Musk Ambrette are prohibited from fragrance use in most countries. At Fraterworks we do not use either of these musks in any of our products. We sell the musks solely so that fragrance aficionados can have access to all the materials of classical perfumery. This should not be used in production cosmetics or fragrances unless you are certain your target market allows it.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Myrac Aldehyde
products.description:
At full strength myrac aldehyde is waxy and overwhelming, but at working dilution it opens into something fresh, clean, and faintly floral — like standing outdoors on a bright morning. The citrus character is more orange than lemon, with an ozonic, marine quality underneath. It smells very different at 10% than it does neat.

It extends citrus top notes well into the heart of a composition, maintaining orange-like brightness alongside materials that would otherwise be left without citrus support. In muguet accords it contributes a clean, green brightness. In marine compositions the ozonic facet adds outdoor realism.

Bergamot, lemon oil, and hydroxycitronellal are natural companions on the citrus-floral side. For marine accords, hedione and dihydromyrcenol amplify the clean-air quality. Cedarwood and Iso E Super in the base give its brightness a woody foundation to rest upon.

products.name: Myrcene
products.description:
Myrcene opens with an immediate burst of fresh, almost citrus-like sweetness reminiscent of ripe mango. This monoterpene's character sits between resinous warmth and ethereal freshness. Its volatility delivers instant impact that dissipates quickly.

You'll find myrcene invaluable as a lightening agent in heavy spice compositions where it adds buoyancy without diluting character. It excels at smoothing fatty citrus notes whilst contributing its own sweet-balsamic warmth. Use it sparingly in masculine fragrances to brighten bay leaf and clove accords without sacrificing depth.

Combine myrcene with linalool for calming lavender-like effects or pair with limonene to amplify citrus vibrancy. In trace amounts it bridges green top notes with woody bases. At higher concentrations it creates the characteristic freshness found in premium masculine colognes.

products.name: Myristic Acid
products.description:
Myristic acid is nearly odourless — a very faint waxy, fatty quality with a whisper of coconut, nothing more. Its value has nothing to do with smell and everything to do with texture and fixation. This is the molecule that makes orris butter feel like orris butter.

Orris concrete is largely myristic acid — it provides the buttery, lipstick-like smoothness that defines premium iris and violet accords. Add it to powdery, creamy compositions for that same waxy body. It lasts up to 400 hours and anchors volatile materials like nothing else.

Pair myristic acid with ionones and methyl ionones for iris and violet bases, with vanillin and coumarin for powdery warmth, or with lactones for creamy, skin-like effects. It is a white waxy solid — warm before use. Inexpensive and indispensable.

products.name: Myroxide
products.description:
Myroxide is an astonishingly powerful chemical. It opens with sweet, metallic freshness — herbal and immediately aromatic, like the best facets of lavender and clary sage distilled into a single material. Warm opoponax resinousness emerges underneath, adding unexpected depth. Fruity pear and tarragon accents round out a remarkably complex profile.

Think of this as ocimene refined for fine perfumery — all the aromatic freshness and diffusion, none of the terpenic harshness. Even small additions give tremendous lift and volume to fougères, lavender compositions, and spicy accords. It brings unexpected brightness to citrus and oakmoss work too.

Apply sparingly in citrus colognes where 0.3% increases brightness dramatically without smelling chemical. Combine with hedione for clean, diffusive floral-citrus topnotes or pair with oakmoss and coumarin for contemporary fougère structures. Works exceptionally well with coranol, vetiver, and aldehydes to accentuate woody-green facets. Avoid overdosing - this material's high power means even small amounts transform a composition's topnote character completely.

products.name: Myrrh Absolute 50% TEC
products.description:
One of the oldest resins used in perfumery, Myrrh is the bitter sweet gum which was offered as a gift by St. Balthasar to Christ at His birth. It was used by the Ancient Egyptians as a beautifying skin treatment and by the Ancient Greeks as a food additive.

In the fragrance industry, Myrrh often forms part of a classic Opoponax base which should not to be confused with Opoponax resinoid sometimes called “sweet myrrh” adding further confusion.

It should be noted that this product is technically a “resin-absolute” because it is cold extracted directly from the raw gum with ethanol. This is the preferred method for better odour properties as no damage is done to the product in manufacturing.

Origin: Somalia
Part: Raw Exudate
Method: Solvent (ethanol) extraction

products.name: Myrrh Oil
products.description:
Myrrh Oil is an ancient wonder of perfumery that still captivates the senses today. Sourced from the resin of the Commiphora myrrha tree, this rich oil has been celebrated for its warmth and mystery since the days of pharaohs and emperors. Its aroma is a beguiling blend of balsamic sweetness and earthy richness, with a smoky edge that evokes flickering incense in far distant sacred temples.

In perfumery, Myrrh is nothing short of a cornerstone. Its resinous profile gives fragrances a grounding quality, pairing effortlessly with Frankincense, Patchouli, and Sandalwood. Whether you’re wanting a brooding oriental or a bright citrus-floral with character in the dry down, Myrrh is a powerhouse amongst base notes.

This wonderful material features in Amouage’s Opus VI (2012), Tom Ford’s Sahara Noir (2013), and the iconic Shalimar (1925) by Jacques Guerlain. It is also a discreet but key material in Dior's original Homme (2005).

products.name: Myrrh Wildii Oil, Namibia
products.description:
In the boiling heat of the Namibian desert comes a special type of myrrh oil: wildii (Commiphora wildii). The chief olfactory difference between this and traditional resinous myrrh (Commiphora myrrha) is that wildii is fresh, invigorating and diffusive. In other words, classic myrrh is rich, deep and dark while Namibian myrrh is an explosion of top notes. Use the two together to create a top to bottom myrrh accord. Further anchor it with myrrh resinoid.

Myrrh Wildii oil blends extremely well with all amber bases, but particularly those of the opoponax variety: Opoponax Doux and Black Opoponax especially.

products.name: Myrtle Oil, Rectified
products.description:
Myrtle Oil, Rectified opens cool and green, a fresh herbal top note carrying clean camphor and eucalyptus brightness. Underneath sits a soft, almost floral sweetness and a whisper of spice. Rectifying strips out the harsh, bitter edges, leaving a clearer, rounder oil.

Myrtle is not a note often discussed amongst perfume aficionados but it appears in surprisingly many popular scents such as Neroli Portofino by Tom Ford, Invictus from Paco Rabanne, Ambre Sultan of Serge Lutens, the much-lauded Tam Dao from Diptique and Amouage Epic Man.

Our Tunisian oil is from LMR so you can be certain you are getting the very best on the market.

products.name: Mysoralex™
products.description:
Mysoral means two things in perfumery today. The first is the classic base by Synarome (Mysoral Base 601651) built around an overdose of sandela, amyris wood oil and spices. The second is a Firmenich captive molecule 2-methyl-4-(2,2,3-trimethylcyclopent-3-en-1-yl)pent-4-enal (CAS 166432-53-7). Mysoral is the aldehyde counterpart of Firsantol but unlike the alcohol, Mysoral has a brighter and shaprer quality, pushing higher into the top notes. Mysoral also has pine, cedar and frankincense nuances lacking in Firsantol.

Mysoral has gained attention of late due to its inclusion (in relatively high doses) in a number of Louis Vuitton fragrances, however it should be noted that it forms part of the popular Firmenich Dreamwood base (at around 0.5%) so traces may appear in GCMS analyses of fragrances incorporating that (alongside considerably larger quantities of santalols).

Our Mysoralex base is intended as a direct 1 for 1 replacement for captive Mysoral in modern formulas, however it is a beautiful and radiant sandalwood base in its own right also. Mysoralex is particularly great at bridging sandalwood notes with cedar, pine, fir, frankincence, and pink pepper. It has a synergy with Firsantol and blends of the two are a real delight. Add a touch to your existing blends and watch the sandalwood dance!

products.name: Mysore Acetate
products.description:
Mysore Acetate has a clean, soft sandalwood character with an unusual violet-floral accent that sets it apart from every other sandalwood material. There is subtle amber warmth and a light tropical-fruit nuance in the background. It reads as transparent and woody rather than creamy or milky.

The violet facet is what makes Mysore Acetate special — it bridges woody and floral notes in a way other sandalwood synthetics cannot. Use it to add woody depth to iris and violet accords, or floral dimension to sandalwood bases. It lasts well over a week on a blotter.

Pair Mysore Acetate with ionones to amplify the violet-wood effect, or blend it alongside Javanol and Sandalore for a full sandalwood accord. The name references Mysore sandalwood — the Indian benchmark — and that is the quality it aims to evoke. Also sold under Symrise's trade name Sandelione.

products.name: Narcisse Base 184092D
products.description:
Narcisse Base 184092D opens with sharp green freshness carrying mentholic and herbaceous facets that evoke snapped flower stems. This legendary Firmenich base transforms into a narcotic white floral heart where narcissus mingles with jasmine and tuberose. The sophisticated blend captures the living flower's intoxicating presence more faithfully than natural absolute, though we highly recommend naturalising the base with the natural material.

You'll find this base superior to natural narcissus absolute for most applications - it's brighter, more consistent, and vastly more affordable. Use it as the floral heart of your composition where it provides both character and exceptional tenacity. Its subtle animalic-honey drydown with chypre-like mossy undertones adds vintage elegance without overwhelming.

The base contains approximately phenylethyl alcohol providing rosy sweetness, Veloutone for fruity-lactonic creaminess, ionones for powdery violet depth, and Evernyl for mossy sophistication. Build classic narcissus soliflores or use it to add narcotic floralcy to orientals. Combine with coumarin in fougères where its hay-like facets create perfect synergy. But be wary: you'll be surprised just how powerful this base can be so start off slowly.

products.name: Nearly Deer™ CMP
products.description:
Fraterworks' Nearly Deer™ is a masterful recreation of Tonkin deer musk tincture. This can be used as a one-for-one replacement in vintage formulas for musk tincture or in modern perfumes to enrich and extend.

Use in traces to boost performance and longevity or overdose it for a wonderfully natural animalic musk indistinguishable from the real thing.

Tonkin deer musk is banned from international trade leaving a gap in the perfume industry in the range of animalics. Nearly Deer™ fills that gap.

products.name: Nebulux
products.description:
This blend exists to solve a specific problem: Nebulone is an IFF captive that independent perfumers cannot buy. Nebulux reconstructs its soft, powdery volume and woody-amber depth using commercially available materials and another IFF captive available no where else. Use it as a direct substitute wherever formulas call for Nebulone — typically at the same concentration.

Nebulux opens with a soft woody radiance and a subtle pear-like fruitiness. As it develops, a warm amber backbone emerges — clean, textured, skin-like. The drydown is extraordinarily tenacious: a deep, velvety musk that clings to blotters for days.

Combine Nebulux with Ambroxan and Hedione for the modern, diffusive skin-scent aesthetic found in fragrances like Le Labo Another 13. It also anchors woody and oriental accords superbly. Pair with Iso E Super and sandalwood for a warm, abstract, second-skin effect.

products.name: Nectarate
products.description:
Nectarate opens with pleasant, immediately recognisable peach and nectarine character—ripe, juicy, and naturalistic. The woody-balsamic undertone adds sophistication that prevents the fruit from becoming confectionery, while subtle green facets provide freshness. It delivers stone fruit realism that simpler peach materials cannot match.

Use Nectarate to modernise rose and jasmine accords where it softens metallic edges while adding dewy freshness, to build realistic stone fruit accords in fruity-florals, or to add juicy lift to tropical and gourmand compositions. It amplifies the fruitiness of other molecules beautifully when blended with materials like Fructalate or ethyl 2-methyl butyrate.

This material excels where others fail. Layer it with ethyl butyrate for seamless top-heart transition. Partner with ionones for sophisticated violet-peach lipstick accords.

products.name: Nectarol 184139 D
products.description:
Nectarol smells convincingly of real honey — thick, waxy, and sweet with a slightly phenolic edge that keeps it from becoming saccharine. There is a piercing, almost wine-like depth beneath the sweetness. This is not a simple sugar-sweet honey; it has genuine complexity and bite.

What sets Nectarol apart is how clean it reads in compositions. Firmenich designed it to push floral strength without dirtying the blend, and it does exactly that. Add it to rose or jasmine accords to bring warmth and richness, or use it as the heart of an oriental where you need honey without animalic heaviness.

Build an amber accord around Nectarol by pairing it with benzoin and labdanum for a golden, nectarous warmth. It also works beautifully with tobacco absolute and tonka for a sophisticated gourmand facet. Dose carefully — the phenolic edge can become sharp if overdone, but at the right level it adds irresistible depth.

products.name: Nectaryl
products.description:
Nectaryl opens with luscious nectarine character—ripe, juicy, and effortlessly natural. The peach-apricot facets add stone fruit depth, while creamy lactonic undertones evoke custard and coconut warmth. This is summer fruit rendered with sophistication: not candy-sweet but elegantly ripe, with the complexity of fruit fresh from the tree.

This Givaudan chemical delivers what gamma-undecalactone promises but with far greater naturalism and tenacity. The material has 380-hour substantivity making it valuable across fine fragrance and functional applications alike; Nectaryl persists through the entire fragrance journey, anchoring fruity accords that would otherwise evaporate.

Blend with Javanol for an unexpected peach-sandalwood accord, or layer with other lactones for tropical creaminess.

products.name: Neo Patchouli
products.description:
It's like a mix of Apo Patchone, cloves, camphor, patchouli and Iso E Super. What a marvel and a wonderful material that almost no one knows about! Use it in traces as an alternative to all of the above, or in overdose for a truly novel approach to leather, earthy and even gourmand fragrances.

A hidden jewel of perfumery, Neo Patchouli brings a polished, modern twist to classic woody and spicy themes. Its ultra-slow evaporation and deep, sweet-amber warmth create remarkable fixation, sophistication, and enduring presence in any composition.

products.name: Neobergamate Forte
products.description:
Neobergamate Forte is a little known fresh top note chemical with a clear bergamot character but a floral and vaguely buchu and green stick heart. It has great potential as a non-allergenic material to use in place of Bergamot oil when a more novel effect is wanted.

Citrus-like accords with Linalool, Dihydromyrcenol, Coranol and Linalyl Acetate are excellent, but this material is also valuable for tea blends and other areas where a bolder bergamot note is needed.

products.name: Neobutenone® Alpha
products.description:
Firmenich's Neobutenone® Alpha is the supreme expression of greenness in modern fragrances. At mere traces Neobutenone Alpha adds a modernity impossible to achieve with other materials. This is the Paradisone of green materials. Closely related — but vastly superior — to dynascone® (also known as galbascone).

Neobutenone Alpha features in Aventus and many other fragrances were traces add an inimitable green fruity top note. This really is an essential material. Due to the high cost and strength we offer it here pure and in dilution at 10% in DPG.

products.name: Neofolione
products.description:
Neofolione hits you with vivid green — crushed violet leaves, sliced green apple, a flash of cucumber. There is a metallic, almost aldehydic brightness to it that cuts through any composition. It is powerful, so measure carefully.

This is the modern replacement for the now-restricted methyl heptine carbonate, and it has become a standard building block for violet accords. Use it alongside ionones and methyl ionones to construct realistic violet, or add it to green florals for that sharp, leafy opening that makes a fragrance feel alive and immediate.

Pair it with alpha-ionone and methyl ionones for classic violet, with violet leaf absolute for depth, or with cassis and nonadienol for a contemporary green-fruity effect. It fades within about sixteen hours, so layer it over longer-lasting heart and base materials.

products.name: Neomagnolan
products.description:
Neomagnolan opens with a sheer, luminous flash of white flowers—magnolia and peony wrapped in a tart pomelo-citrus brightness that feels immediately modern. Beneath the sparkle, green tea-leaf and water-lily facets add a cool, transparent airiness. The effect is floral without weight, like light passing through petals.

What a curious character this material is! Neomagnolan is like the big brother of classic Magnolan. Every time you smell it you discover a new nuance: indole, pomelo, orange blossom, moth balls, magnolia, rhubarb, vetiver, and on and on. Despite that, it remains a great floraliser for masculines that won't take your perfume in a feminine direction. But, dress it up right, and it will glow in the heart of a well-blended ladies' bouquet type scent.

Use it to add a touch of freshness to an otherwise dense or cloying floral. Build a cologne to exploit its hot iron and citrus nuances. The possibilities are endless. 

Neogmagnolan is a solid at room temperature and requires quite a lot of heat to melt. For that reason we offer it at 50% dilution in DPG. At slightlyh lower temperatures, even in dilution, Neomagnolan may separate and require warming.

Neomagnolan vs Magnolan

Both share the same parent molecule but Neomagnolan is an enriched fraction containing the isomer with superior olfactory qualities. Original Magnolan is a mixture of diastereoisomers that delivers a broader, denser floral-green character with pronounced grapefruit-lychee facets and an indolic d

products.name: Nerol
products.description:
Nerol (high purity) is the little brother of the rose alcohols, being used in smaller quantities and fewer formulas than the big boys: Citronellol, Geraniol and Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol.

In addition to being vital for recreations of Neroli and Orange Blossom oils, Nerol really does add important nuances to rose materials, particularly an inimitable freshness. It can also be used to add seashore and ozonic hints to a scent.

BASF, founded in 1865 as a dye maker, has come to produce some of the best aroma chemicals. Boasting high purities and a quality much appreciated by perfumers, they are the top of the class in many instances. 

Nerol blends beautifully with Citronellol 98, Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Geraniol Extra, Rose Oxide Laevo, and Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon.

products.name: Neroli Oil, Morocco
products.description:
From Fez and its surrounding areas, this opulent essential oil extracted from the blossoms of the bitter orange tree is a marvel. Compared to Tunisian neroli oil, the product from Morocco is more rounded, indolic and rich. It is a wonderful oil to add top note fresh floralcy to perfumes that link into a beautifully blended heart. Pair it with Orange Blossom absolute for a complete orange flower note. As usual, LMR one again tops the quality charts with this incredible oil.

Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC.

For a breathtaking alternative, try our Neroli Supreme which is practically indistinguishable from natural neroli oil and significantly less expensive.

Tunisia vs Morocco

While both oils are from the same plant species, the terroir has much to play in the difference between the two for perfumery purposes.

Tunisian oil is brighter, greener, fresher and more eau de cologne like. It is slightly zesty with petitgrain nuances.

Moroccan oil is softer, rounder and more orange blossom like. It tends to be more linalool-rich and to have a creamy and honeyed side.

products.name: Neroli Oil, Tunisia
products.description:
A wonderful pure neroli oil from Tunisia by master distillers LMR. Touches will add freshness and floralcy to a fragrance. Much admired by both ladies and gentlemen, neroli oil enhances almost all perfumes. 

For a breathtaking alternative, try our Neroli Supreme which is practically indistinguishable from natural neroli oil and significantly less expensive.

Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC.

We also stock Neroli Oil from Morocco, also from LMR.

Tunisia vs Morocco

While both oils are from the same plant species, the terroir has much to play in the difference between the two for perfumery purposes.

Tunisian oil is brighter, greener, fresher and more eau de cologne like. It is slightly zesty with petitgrain nuances.

Moroccan oil is softer, rounder and more orange blossom like. It tends to be more linalool-rich and to have a creamy and honeyed side.

products.name: Neroli Supreme
products.description:
With the rising cost of natural oils and absolutes, floral materials such as a rose and neroli are now priced far beyond the range of most perfumers. That is where Neroli Supreme comes in. 

Neroli Supreme is a complex blend of the same aroma chemicals found in neroli oil crowned by beautiful naturals from LMR. Dare we say it: Neroli Supreme is better than most commercial neroli oils on the market today.

Once you try Neroli Supreme, you will be a convert for life.

products.name: Nerolidol
products.description:
Nerolidol opens with an understated elegance—a whisper rather than a shout. This sesquiterpene alcohol presents faint woody-floral notes that seem to hover just at the edge of perception, like "an aura of light or a cool breeze." The initial impression is deceptively mild: soft rose petals, fresh apple skin, and delicate muguet float above a woody base. Yet this subtle character masks exceptional staying power—what starts as barely perceptible evolves into a persistent presence that can last over 280 hours on a blotter, quietly supporting and enhancing everything around it.

Deploy Nerolidol at 0.5-3% when you need sophisticated structural support without obvious character modification. Its true genius lies in functional excellence: as a blender, it seamlessly links disparate notes, smoothing harsh transitions between top and base; as a fixative, it anchors volatile materials while adding its own substantive trace. Use it to build delicate florals like muguet, honeysuckle, and peony where heavy fixatives would overwhelm. In woody-vanillic accords, it provides an "airy side" that prevents density. Its ability to enhance skin penetration makes it valuable in functional fragrances.

Despite the similar names, Nerolidol and Nerol are fundamentally different materials with distinct roles in perfumery. The key difference lies in their molecular structure: Nerol is a C10 monoterpene alcohol (rose-fresh, citrusy, lighter), while Nerolidol is a C15 sesquiterpene alcohol (woody-floral,

products.name: Nerolin Bromelia
products.description:
Nerolin Bromelia opens with a soft acacia, wattle and neroli character that's distinctly more refined than its methyl ether cousin. You'll discover a mild yet tenacious orange blossom fragrance with grape and strawberry nuances emerging at lighter concentrations. This crystalline material melts easily at body temperature, releasing its characteristic powdery-floral sweetness that persists for hours.

Use Nerolin Bromelia frequently with oranger crystals, methyl anthranilate and petitgrain to build convincing orange blossom accords. Its exceptional alkali stability makes it irreplaceable in fine soaps where other florals decompose. The drydown remains fresher compared to oranger crystals' honeyed warmth, providing the dry petal-like quality that grounds volatile citrus notes.

Bromelia vs Yara Yara vs Fragarol

The nerolin family comprises three beta-naphthyl ethers that share orange blossom character but differ meaningfully in personality.

Yara Yara (methyl ether) is the most intense and industrial—powerfully diffusive with a harsh, pronounced naphthyl (mothball) edge that dominates functional fragrances where sheer impact matters. Its 400-hour substantivity and rock-bottom cost make it a workhorse for soaps and detergents. 

Bromelia (ethyl ether) is softer and rounder, retaining the orange blossom character but with less harshness and better alcohol solubility—easier to blend into refined compositions while still offering 400-hour tenacity. 

Fragarol (isobutyl ether) is t

products.name: Nerolin Fragarol
products.description:
The strawberry note hits first — sweet, ripe, unmistakable. Underneath sits a warm orange blossom character, musky and slightly powdery, that gives this material far more depth than a simple fruit note. The crystals melt close to room temperature, making them easy to work with as a liquid.

That 116-hour persistence on a blotter is remarkable for something that smells this fresh and fruity. It works as both a heart note and a genuine fixative, holding your composition together long after brighter top notes have faded. In berry and orange blossom accords the dual character is especially valuable.

Methyl anthranilate and neroli oil both complement its orange blossom side. For the strawberry facet, fruity lactones and ethyl maltol help build a convincing berry accord around it. White musks in the base extend the musky drydown into something genuinely long-lasting and skin-like.

Yara Yara, Bromelia, Fragarol

Three materials share the nerolin name but smell quite different. Nerolin Yara Yara is the most intense — a strong, somewhat harsh orange blossom note with a pronounced naphthyl character, historically popular in soaps.

Nerolin Bromelia is softer and rounder, with a cleaner orange blossom quality better suited to fine fragrance.

Nerolin Fragarol is the fruitiest of the three — the strawberry and berry facets set it apart, and it is the most versatile for modern perfumery work.

products.name: Nerolin Yara Yara
products.description:
Intensely orange blossom with strong naphthalenic (mothball) nuances. Very useful for industrial or functional fragrances but also a wonderfully powerful neroli note to boost oranger crystals which are heavily restricted by IFRA.

Blends extremely well with methyl anthranilate, oranger crystals, citrus products (orange blossom, neroli, petitgrain, citrus oil) and rose alcohols. 

We also stock Nerolin Bromelia and Nerolin Fragarol.

products.name: Neryl Acetate
products.description:
Neryl acetate is a luminous, fruity-floral material essential for neroli, jasmine, and citrus-floral accords. With a rosy-raspberry sweetness, it elevates compositions with clarity and diffusion, far superior to the duller geranyl acetate often used as a cheap substitute. Moderate in tenacity, it serves as a refined bridge between notes, adding natural brilliance and depth to any well-crafted fragrance.

This material is essential for building a true-to-life neroli or orange blossom effect in fine fragrance. It delivers a crisp, citrus-floral glow with natural depth, while offering better stability than fragile essential oils.

products.name: Night Queen
products.description:
NIGHT QUEEN is a rare fragrance base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the elusive Queen of the Night flower (Selenicereus grandiflorus)—a cactus that blooms for a single night each year—this composition captures the fleeting purity and nocturnal magic of this ghostly blossom. Its delicate floralcy is brightened by cool green facets and softened by creamy undertones, echoing the brief, beautiful life of a bloom that lives only in moonlight.

Perfumery Usage

NIGHT QUEEN brings a haunting elegance to compositions, with excellent lift and translucency. It pairs effortlessly with white florals such as Jasmine Sambac and Orange Blossom Absolute, as well as night-themed molecules like Helional, Melonal, and Methyl Dihydrojasmonate. It can be used as a central floral motif or layered for shimmer and mystery.

Process

Created through a blend of specialty aroma materials and carefully selected natural isolates, NIGHT QUEEN reflects Fraterworks’ commitment to olfactory innovation. Every element was guided by Duchaufour’s vision to reimagine a scent that lives in shadow—a floral portrait composed entirely in the dark.

Background

Despite its mystique and reputation among plant lovers, Queen of the Night has been largely absent from perfumery due to its unextractable nature. NIGHT QUEEN fills this gap, offering perfumers access to a completely original accord, conceptualised and brought to life through imagination, chemistry, and

products.name: Nootkatone Crystals
products.description:
Nootkatone represents the quintessential grapefruit character in modern perfumery. Its exceptional tenacity outperforms most citrus materials, providing remarkable longevity in compositions. At 98% purity, it delivers a powerful, bright aroma, essential for authentic citrus fragrances. Its fresh, slightly woody profile adds unique character and sophistication.

It is also an exceptional product to combine with vetiver notes for a magical and modern style. For fine fragrance, 98% purity and higher is the only choice.

products.name: Nopyl Acetate
products.description:
Nopyl Acetate opens with sweet woody-herbal character—fresh, bergamot-like, and immediately evocative of quality eaux de cologne. Pine-coniferous facets add naturalistic freshness, while soft lavender undertones connect it to the fougère family. The amber warmth in the drydown provides unexpected depth for a top note material. This materials functions similarly to linalyl acetate but with a distinctly woodier, less sweet profile. 

Nopyl Acetate's medium odour strength and forgiving nature make it easy to blend. Use it wherever linalyl acetate appears but where you want less sweetness and more woody character. It excels in citrus colognes, orange blossom accords, and fougère compositions alongside lavender and coumarin. The herbal-coniferous aspect works beautifully with pine, juniper berry, and rosemary.

Nopyl Acetate vs Linalyl Acetate

These two esters occupy similar perfumery space but with meaningful differences. Linalyl acetate is sweeter, more floral-fruity, with pronounced lavender and bergamot character—the classic fougère heart.

Nopyl acetate is woodier, less sweet, with more herbal-coniferous depth and subtle amber warmth. Use linalyl acetate when you want bright lavender-bergamot sweetness; reach for nopyl acetate when you need that freshness grounded in woody naturalism. They blend beautifully together, with nopyl acetate adding body and tenacity to linalyl acetate's sparkling lift.

products.name: Norlimbanol®
products.description:
Norlimbanol® is the classic Firmenich version of Timberol. It is a racemic blend and so is softer and easier to work with than the highly purified Norlimbanol® Dextro which we also stock; this racemic version is also much more affordable. 

Like the dextro form, Norlimbanol — in traces — boosts the woody and ambery notes of a fragrance, with an impact from top to bottom. This is the hedione of wood materials. It is indispensible and every perfumer should have it even if they already have Norlimbanol® Dextro.

Nolimbanol® blends beautifully with Sandexol®, Ambre Royal, Ambrexol™ and Royal Leather.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Norlimbanol® Dextro
products.description:
Firmenich's Norlimbanol® Dextro is the purest form of the desirable dextro isomer of norlimbanol (timberol) on the market. It has a radiance and power that is unequalled. In traces this boosts the woody and ambery notes of a fragrance, with an impact from top to bottom. This dextro product is to norlimbanol, what paradisone is to hedione. This is the supreme quality.

Nolimbanol® Dextro blends beautifully with Sandexol®, Ambre Royal, Ambrexol™ and Royal Leather.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Nutmeg Oil, Aceh
products.description:
Nutmeg is a very versatile spice which blends extremely well with modern woody aroma chemicals imparting complexity and naturalness. It is a rather key material in Fahrenheit (1988) by Dior and Vetiver (1959) by Guerlain. Demo formulas for both can be found below.

This Nutmeg oil is a speciality product of Payan Bertrand which is prized for having a particularly low methyl eugenol and safrole content, making it suitable for use at higher doses under IFRA 51 (up to 25% of your finished product). This is ethically sourced and is not molecular distilled, the low allergens are entirely a naturally occurring quality resulting from the selection of particularly fine nutmeg fruit.

products.name: Nutty Furan
products.description:
Nutty Furan opens with an intense, musty nuttiness — roasted hazelnuts and toasted almonds layered with sweet hay-coumarin warmth. A coconut-milky softness emerges underneath, giving the material a genuinely edible quality. The overall impression is warm, roasted, and deeply comforting.

This is a concentrated material — a trace transforms vanilla and tonka compositions into praline-gourmand territory. It adds toasted depth to tobacco and coffee accords, and that hay-coumarin facet gives it versatility beyond pure gourmand. Pair it with vanillin, coumarin, and cocoa absolute for dark confectionery effects.

Use Nutty Furan at microdose levels — its strength is remarkable. It occurs naturally in coffee, black tea, roasted filberts, and raisins, all foods defined by that same toasted character. Blend with ethyl maltol, benzoin, and tonka for a warm praline accord that smells genuinely baked.

products.name: Nutty Pyrazine
products.description:
It may be called Nutty Pyrazine but on first whiff it is decidedly hot buttered popcorn. What a delightful chemical when used correctly. It features in our own Frater fragrance Menagerie and is often used to create a nutty scent or as part of a broader gourmand blend. Essential for recreations of coffee and, of course, nuts and popcorn, this chemical is powerful so we sell it at 1% in DPG. If you want pure, we can accommodate you, just drop us a line. Even at 1% so we recommend further dilution.

Nutty Pyrazine blends beautifully with Filbertone, Orbitone, Nutmeg Absolute, Birch Tar, gourmand and wood chemicals.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Nympheal™
products.description:
Nympheal is the most recent captive muguet molecule to come to the market (the other being Mimosal™ from Firmenich) and the first for Givaudan. With the banning of Lyral and Lilial in Europe, Nympheal is a much needed material for the modern perfumer. First appearing in Woman In Gold (2017) by Killian, this is Givaudan's "Lilial-replacer" holy grail.

Nympheal can be dosed higher than some muguet materials (such as Dupical and Hivernal Neo), however, it should be noted that in contrast to Lilial, Nympheal is much more powerful (around 20 times) and so it does not function as a one for one replacer. To replace Lilial, start at 5 – 10 times less Nympheal and work up until you are satisfied.

Nympheal creates an astonishing synergy when blended with LMR Patchouli Heart No 3, though blends with any patchouli oil are beautiful. Nympheal also combines well with the classic Muguet 16 and all our Muguet bases, Florol, Amazonia™, Suralette® Extra, Acetal CD, Cyclamen Aldehyde and Rose Oxide Laevo.

See our demo formula below which exploits the patchouli / Nympheal synergy. It is a modern floral fresh Mellis type fragrance in the tradition of Dior's Poison (1985) and Moon Dance (2014) by Juliette Has A Gun.

Nympheal is biodegradable.

products.name: Oak Barrel CO2
products.description:
This is the same material as Vigon's Oakwood CO2. It differs from our LMR Oakwood CO2, Extra which has a strongly smoked wood quality.

When constructing a boozy spirit note, this Oak Barrel CO2 is our first choice. For a peaty whisky accord I'd recommend the LMR product, and for a decidedly sweet and sticky woody blend, Ventos' Oakwood Base is second to none.

If you are looking for a powerfully intense smoked wood, I recommend our Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 which is modelled on a genuine 180 year old bottle of classic French perfumery birch tar.

products.name: Oakmoss DEC Abs MD 55% TEC
products.description:
Note: This is IFRA compliant and our recommended go to oakmoss.

One of the downsides to the restriction on oakmoss being coupled with the need to remove certain chemicals from it is that you can be left with a somewhat flaccid absolute. The great Laboratoire Monique Remy (LMR) has solved this problem with this molecular distilled IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute. The material is as colourless as oakmoss can get (being a very pale orange) but it punches well above its pay grade. It is pre-diluted by LMR at the laboratory in non-natural triethyl citrate so it is not suitable for natural perfumers.

While we love pure unadulterated green Oakmoss for non-commercial use, this special molecular distilled product is our general oakmoss of choice. It is rich, intense, longer lastinging than all others (so much so it is almost hard to believe) and truest to the scent of the classic green Yugoslavian oakmoss used in the original Chypre by Coty. 

If you only buy one oakmoss, this is the one.

We also stock original pure and natural non-IFRA compliant green oakmoss absolute from the former Yugoslovia, diluted to 50% in natural triethyl citrate for your convenience, making it suitable for natural fragrances.

products.name: Oakmoss Green Absolute
products.description:
When Francois Coty created the great feminine masterpiece Chypre, there was only one oakmoss he would accept: pure and natural green Yugoslavian oakmoss. He adored it so much that he used a whopping 8% in that famous fragrance. Over the forthcoming decades all other perfumers used the same product - from Ernest Beaux with No 5 for Chanel, all the way up to the 21st century when tragically pure and natural oakmoss was restricted by IFRA and only permitted if it were chemically altered to remove atranol.

Most suppliers today only stock the chemically altered brown IFRA compliant oakmoss which lacks a lot of the beauty of this product. But not all... we are absolutely thrilled to be able to offer pure and natural Yugoslavian green oakmoss absolute. This is not IFRA compliant. Despite that, it still finds many uses and is still permitted in numerous regions of the world. Needless to say, this incredibly rich and beautiful material is essential for recreating the classic scents of yesteryear.

This is classic green oakmoss absolute sold pure (as a solid material) or in liquid form diluted to 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate.

We also offer an IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute (pure or at 50% dilution) from Laboratoire Monique Remy (LMR).

Origin: Nations of the former Yugoslavia
Part: Moss
Method of production: Solvent extraction in Grasse
