products.name: Oakmoss “IFRA 43” Absolute
products.description:
One of the tragedies of modern perfume legislation is the ban on pure and natural oakmoss and the severe restriction on low-atranol versions of the same. Thankfully we have wonderful synthetics available to us such as evernyl, but those alone can not convey the true beauty of oakmoss. That's where this rich and intense IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute from LMR comes in. This is the ultimate IFRA-safe oakmoss absolute, tweaked to remove the banned material atranol.

This oakmoss is earthy, green, sweet and the closest IFRA compliant material to the original product so beloved by Coty when he created Chypre. The original formula of that wonderful fragrance is below — simply replace the pure and natural green oakmoss with this product for a less allergenic version, but do bear in mind that this material is still restricted to a low 0.1% of your finished fine fragrance if you intend to commercialise it.

Oakmoss absolute is extremely viscous so in addition to this 100% pure version, we are also offering it at a 10% and 50% dilution in natural triethyl citrate.

We also stock original pure and natural non-IFRA compliant green oakmoss absolute from the former Yugoslavia and the most wonderful decolourised IFRA compliant oakmoss also from LMR.

Origin: Macedonia
Part: Moss
Method of production: Extraction in Grasse

products.name: Oakmossarome
products.description:
Oakmossarome, a Synarome base, opens with a clean, mossy-woody impression that feels polished and refined. There's a gentle sweetness here—not gourmand, but balsamic and resinous, like warm amber. Soft leathery undertones emerge in the dry-down, lending the kind of furry, animalic depth that once defined classic cuir fragrances.

This Synarome specialty base acts as a powerful harmoniser, smoothing transitions between heart and base notes. You can use it as the structural backbone of a chypre or fougère, or at trace levels to add green depth and fixation to white florals. Pair it with bergamot, labdanum and patchouli for a modern chypre skeleton, or combine it with lavender and coumarin for a classic masculine dry-down.

Think of Oakmossarome as the refined sibling of traditional oakmoss - all the structural power, none of the heavy seaweed-mushroom baggage. Try it alongside Isobutyl Quinoline or Ambrarome for dark leather accords, or blend with Helional or Algenone to build contemporary marine chypres. Its great tenacity makes it a serious fixative weapon.

products.name: Oakwood Base, Ventos
products.description:
Oakwood Base, Ventos smells like the inside of a spirits cellar. Dark, rich oak wood meets cognac and whisky-barrel booze, threaded with woodsmoke, sweet vanilla and a nutty chestnut warmth. A balsamic sweetness rounds the whole thing off. Because of the sweetness, it is an excellent base to add a touch of smoke without dominating as easily as you can with Birch and Cade.

A touch will ground woody, leather and oriental accords in aged-barrel warmth, and it turns sweet gourmand ideas boozy, lending cognac, rum and whisky effects an authentic woody backbone.

products.name: Oakwood CO2 Extra
products.description:
This is the most perfect encapsulation of the scent of smoky and newly sawn oak. Oakwood CO2 from LMR is so good you'll want to build an entire fragrance around it! Blend it with a smoky base like Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 and an overdose of Orbitone® T for a modern scent.

This is quite a dark viscous material at 60% (the default dilution from LMR) so we also offer it further diluted to 10%.

Oakwood CO2 is an upcycled product because it is made from offcuts of oak used in the manufacture of superior aging barrels for the fine wine industry.

In the words of LMR: “Creating unique, sustainably sourced natural extracts starts with the precise selection of the best trees. In the interests of protecting the environment and sustaining a quality resource, this sourcing of the best oakwoods by our partner has been awarded PEFC certification, as it meets very demanding specifications in compliance with the French National Forests Office.

Together with IFF perfumers, LMR scientists have established a precise burning process for the discarded oakwood chips, to bring out the exact aromas desired by perfumers. The result: sustainable, unique, and memorable extracts that make waste beautiful.”

products.name: Oceanol
products.description:
An IFF captive until 2024, this is an amazing material very closely related to Veramoss, but where that is dank and dusty, Oceanol is marine. It is a powder and very powerful so we are also offering it at 10% dilution.

Oceanol opens with a striking briny saltiness that recalls sea spray drying on coastal rocks. The iodine-rich seaweed character sits atop a fluffy, almost powdery texture. This isn't the melon-fresh aquatic of the nineties—it's darker, more mineral, authentically oceanic. It also has a beautiful, but seldom discussed, orange flower nuance leaning in the direction of oranger crystals and coumarone. A real opportunity to exploit this facet exists.

Build modern chypres around this material to replace heavy oakmoss with airy freshness. It functions simultaneously as a diffusive top note modifier and a tenacious base fixative—a rare combination. Pair it with Veramoss for neo-chypre structures or layer beneath citrus for sparkling saline lift.

Use Oceanol to add cotton-fresh minerality to laundry accords or deep-clean signals to personal care. Combine with ambers for abyssal depth or white florals for sun-kissed skin effects. Its exceptional longevity anchors marine compositions that would otherwise evaporate.

IFF suggests specific pairings to maximize Oceanol’s potential:

The "Solar-Saline" Accord:

Ingredients: Oceanol + Ylanganate + Tropicalia.

Effect: Ylanganate provides the creamy, solar white floral heart; Tropicalia adds the diffusive exotic fruit top; O

products.name: Ocimene
products.description:
Ocimene opens with an immediate burst of warm, herbaceous sweetness that reads as both floral and vegetal. This chemical captures the essence of sun-warmed basil leaves crushed between fingers. Its distinctive wet cloth facet brings a modern, clean dimension that perfumers exploit for contemporary freshness.

You'll find ocimene indispensable when building gardenia reconstructions where it provides the crucial mushroom-like dewy quality of the living flower. Layer it into tropical fruit accords to achieve that resinous mango peel effect that transforms synthetic esters into believable fruit. In masculine fragrances, use it to modernise traditional lavender fougères by suppressing medicinal camphor notes whilst amplifying floral freshness.

Deploy ocimene as your vertical lift agent in transparent compositions built on hedione and Iso E Super bases. Its exceptional diffusivity creates immediate spatial expansion upon application. Combine with aldehydes and white musks to achieve that coveted steam-pressed linen effect in functional fragrances.

products.name: Octinoxate
products.description:
Octinoxate is sunscreen for your perfume, not a scent material. This colourless, low-viscosity liquid absorbs UVB radiation (280–320 nm) before it can break down fragrance molecules. At typical use levels, it contributes no detectable odour to a composition.

Use Octinoxate wherever UV-sensitive ingredients need shielding — citrus oils, aldehydes, and terpenes are the first casualties of light exposure. It's miscible with most fragrance oils and doubles as a co-solvent, dissolving other oil-soluble additives with ease. Simply stir it into your oil phase.

One critical caveat: Octinoxate and Avobenzone destabilise each other under UV light unless a photostabiliser is also present. Add Oxynex ST at just 0.5% to quench this reaction and protect both filters. For UVB-only protection, pair Octinoxate with 2-Ethylhexyl Salicylate instead.

Octinoxate vs Avobenzone

Octinoxate and Avobenzone protect against different portions of the UV spectrum. Octinoxate absorbs UVB (280–320 nm) — the shorter-wavelength radiation that degrades terpenes, aldehydes, and other volatile components. Avobenzone absorbs UVA (320–400 nm) — the longer-wavelength light responsible for yellowing liquids and breaking down vanillin.

Octinoxate is a pourable liquid that incorporates instantly; Avobenzone is a crystalline powder requiring heat (80–85°C) and a co-solvent to dissolve. Octinoxate itself can dissolve up to 26% Avobenzone by weight, making it a useful carrier for the powder. However, the two destabi

products.name: Oeillet 208
products.description:
The great Oeillet 208 used in Chypre by Coty and the great L'Air du Temps. This is a wonderfully sweet carnation base which perfectly complements and extends the life of Dianthus. Thanks to a revolutionary Fraterworks® Isoeugenol replacer, we are able to offer this base for the first time in decades at an astonishing high safe usable level of 8.9% of the finished product.

And just like the original, this base is richly floralised with natural absolutes and essential oils. A truly beautiful and realistic carnation.

Used in Emir by Jean Carles for Dana, Fête (Molyneux), Fleurs de Roacaille (Caron), L'Air du Temps (Nina Ricci) and Cartier's Panthère.

products.name: Okoumal
products.description:
Okoumal smells of warm, dry wood wrapped in soft amber and snuff. It is not loud — in fact, some people cannot smell it at all in isolation. But add it to a composition and the effect is unmistakable: warmth, volume, and richness appear from nowhere.

This is one of those rare materials that works by stealth. Use it at low doses to fill out woody and amber bases, adding body and expensive-smelling roundness. It lasts over 420 hours on a blotter — well over a month — making it one of the most tenacious fixatives available. Evaluate it in blends rather than on its own.

Pair it with cedarwood for rich woody depth, with patchouli and vetiver for dark, earthy warmth, or with sandalwood materials for a smooth, enveloping base. A little goes a long way — start at trace levels and build up until you feel its effect on the composition's body.

products.name: Olibanol
products.description:
The very purest heart of olibanum, Olibanol from Robertet is a perfect natural isolate that can be used anywhere a clean incense note is needed. It is a co-distillation on natural triethyl citrate making it very easy to use.

When comparing it to our other beautiful Olibanum Coeur MD, the Olibanol is fresher and more vibrant but less complex. They are both very compatible with one another and you should certainly have both.

This is a pure and natural material and complies with ISO 9235.

products.name: Olibanum Absolute
products.description:
Biolandes has a number of products in which they truly shine. When it comes to resins we have a range from a number of suppliers, but when it comes to a reference olibanum resinoid (via alcohol extraction) no one can beat this incredibly beautiful extract.

Olibanum Absolute is a solid (fragrant dry pebbles in various sizes) so we offer it pure and in a 50% solution in TEC.

If you are looking for other options we also have the highly popular Olibanol, Biolandes' Olibanum Coeur MD, Payan Bertrand's Frankincense Essential Oil and the historic Olibanum CNC base formerly of Chuit Naef and Cie.

products.name: Olibanum CNC
products.description:
Olibanum CNC is one of the finest Chuit Naef bases from the early 20th century. It incorporates the noblest aspects of the frankincense tree (Omani Boswellia sacra) — from the pure heart of the resin to the sacred essential oil.

Olibanum CNC is richly floralised with pure and natural oils and absolutes and further enriched with the highest quality aroma chemicals. This base was so beloved that it extended past company boundaries and great perfumers with no connection to Chuit Naef & Cie (perfumers such as Jean Carles,) used it liberally in some of their greatest creations, for example Miss Dior.

Olibanum CNC can be used in traces to impart a fine frankincense note through the entire life of a fragrance, or in overdose for a special cachet. Olibanum CNC is practically a perfume unto itself and it transports you to the wonderous ancient orient from whence came the Three Magi, golden pharaonic dynasties, and incense clouded sultanates.

products.name: Olibanum CO2
products.description:
Olibanum CO₂ is the ultimate embodiment of frankincense resin, capturing its sacred essence in exquisite fullness. Unlike traditional distillations, this superior extraction retains both delicate, ethereal notes and deeper, resinous facets often lost in the process. Its profound, aroma evokes ancient rituals and spiritual serenity, unfolding with remarkable presence and longevity to lend depth and character to sophisticated fragrance compositions.

Olibanum CO₂ shines at concentrations between 0.5–2%, anchoring fragrances with a compelling intensity. It blends beautifully with the dark sweetness of myrrh, the amber warmth of labdanum, and the structured elegance of cedar wood and vetiver extracts. Introduced into heart and base accords, it imparts a timeless, grounding dimension.

products.name: Olibanum Coeur MD
products.description:
Under the beating desert sun the frankincense tree exudes its sweet gum so revered it was offered as one of the Magi's gifts to Christ. For millennia this precious resin has been used in religious sacraments and ceremonies and blended with sweet oils to make fragrances for royal courts. If heaven were scented, this would be that scent.

Olibanum Coeur begins as pure olibanum resin and through the mastery of modern molecular science is distilled to its purest heart. This is the most sublime extraction of the Frankincense tree on the market today. It can be used one for one anywhere olibanum gum, resinoid and absolute are used.

This is a pure and natural material and complies with ISO 9235. It is a viscous liquid but pourable at room temperature.

products.name: Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain
products.description:
“Introibo ad altare Dei,” intones the priest as he ascends the steps to the altar amidst billowing clouds of frankincense and myrrh.

Anyone who has attended a high mass knows well that fragrant scent of sacred smoke; but in fact its connection to religious places transcends faiths. Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain from Firmenich is that odour. Singularly, it encapsulates the fullness of the most common incense blends used in Church and it is most certainly the most important extract to use when replicating it.

Vulcain is Firmenich's term for pyrogenation, the act of heating a raw material to create novel olfactory profiles. This process works well on all types of resins but its effect is particularly well observed with olibanum.

The raw material is very viscous (albeit pourable at slightly higher than room temperature) so we also offer it diluted to 50% in odourless natural triethyl citrate for the benefit of natural perfumers and those who prefer working with mobile liquids.

products.name: Olive Fruit Absolute
products.description:
What a rare treasure this one is! Olive fruit absolute has a rich, fruity-green aroma with distinctive fatty, oily notes and subtle nuances of freshly cut grass, green leaves, and ripe olives. It is an amazing and unusual material with the very distinctly unctuous lactonic character rarely seen in a natural.

It has an amazing ability buff away all the sharpness of green chemicals which makes it suitable for all manner of natural replacers that rely heavily on synthetics. We highly recommend it.

products.name: Ombre d’Iris
products.description:
Ombre d'Iris is a co-distillation — iris distilled directly onto cedarwood, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is cedarwood transformed into something older, lonelier, and infinitely more complex — aged wood panels glowing with a century of shellac, and somewhere behind them, the powdery violet-root signature of iris drifting like a memory.

The cedar announces itself first. But as the material develops on a blotter, the iris emerges — not as a dominant note but as a spectral presence woven through the wood. It does not compete with the cedar; it haunts it. There is a quality of dusty enclosed space, of books in rooms with closed doors, of fireplaces that haven't been lit in decades but whose stone still carries the memory. This is beautiful enough to wear undiluted as a skin scent.

Combine it with Osmanthe sur Gurjun for a complete perfume — the sweet, physical osmanthus against this shadowy iris-cedar creates something extraordinary with nothing else needed. Alternatively, use it beneath any floral to add woody-powdery depth that reads as effortlessly expensive.

products.name: Onestolide®
products.description:
Onestolide (high purity Dihydroambrettolide) opens with a sophisticated sweet muskiness that immediately distinguishes itself through its balsamic richness and distinctive animalic undertones. This macrocyclic lactone presents a fascinating duality—simultaneously clean and animalic—creating depth without heaviness. The crystalline, vibrant quality particularly characteristic of Synarome's 98% grade adds luminosity to its inherent warmth.

Use Onestolide when you need exceptional fixation combined with character. Its remarkable diffusion enhances delicate florals without overpowering them, while its animalic facets create sensual depth in amber accords. This material excels at bridging modern clean aesthetics with classical warmth, making it indispensable for contemporary oriental compositions.

Combine with Aerolide®, Exaltolide or ethylene brassylate for complex musk accords. It harmonises beautifully with methylionones, vetiver derivatives, and aldehydes, while lending crucial support to labdanum and vanilla in amber bases.

Dihydroambrettolide vs Ambrettolide

The key distinction between Dihydroambrettolide and its unsaturated cousin Ambrettolide lies in their fundamental olfactive characters. While Ambrettolide presents pronounced floral and fruity facets with red fruit sweetness reminiscent of ambrette seeds, Dihydroambrettolide shifts the balance toward animalic warmth and balsamic depth.

Where Ambrettolide might lift a composition with botanical muskiness, Dihydroambr

products.name: Operanide
products.description:
First discovered in 2001 by the same IFF chemist that discovered AmberXtreme, Operanide is one of the most perfect modern amber molecules with a creamy quality nuanced by moss, soft woods and gourmand facets. It is an incredibly diffusive and radiant material which joins the likes of Amber Xtreme, Ambrocenide, Amberketal and others in the radiant amber family, though usable in far greater amounts as it is considerably easier to control. Until recently a captive of IFF.

A simple blend of Operanide and Amber Xtreme results in an accord more elegant, more radiant and more beautiful than either chemical singularly. To that you can add profound fixative qualities with a touch of Z11® MIP (preferable to the HD version). Even a small amount of Operanide adds a lovely creaminess and naturalises blends astonishingly well. It adds varnish to wood materials.

In addition, Operanide blends beautifully with Ambrocenide, Musks Zenolide and Edenolide, tonka materials (for example Florex and Coumarone), everything patchouli (especially Clearwood®), Vetiverol and Vetiveryl Acetate, the Rose Ketones (with olfactorily similar chemicals such as Ethyl Safranate) and the ozonic / marine family (Cascalone, Calone, Maritima, Floralzone, etc).

products.name: Opoponax 216
products.description:
Created by a master perfumer at Chuit Naef & Cie in its earliest days, Opoponax 216 differs from Opoponax Doux in that it has a more intense vanilla note and subdued woods. It was favoured by the early Guerlain perfumers and featured in the original Jicky of 1889 with a wonderful overdose of Mysore sandalwood. It was also the key amber of Arpège by Lanvin.

Usable at up to 16.6% for IFRA compliance, this is a very versatile and luscious base, rich with all the usual resins and luxurious naturals such as aged patchouli and Mysore sandalwood.

products.name: Opoponax Doux
products.description:
This is the famous opoponax base beloved by Coty and used in L'Origan and Chypre. Additionally it was used in numerous perfumes by Guerlain, including an early formula of Jicky. Opoponax Doux is a wonderfully balanced and rich amber base loaded with all the finest resins balanced with the perfect dose of fresh citrus oils and sweet vanilla.

The historic opoponax type base is a little confusing because "opoponax" is also the name of a resin used in perfume. However, opoponax bases are a type of ambreine base - artful blends of vanilla, citrus, resins and other luxurious naturals. The main difference is that opoponax bases are narcotic while ambreine bases are erogenous. This means they are synergistic.

Combinations of Opoponax Doux and Ambreine are found through many historic perfumes and were particular favourites of Coty and Guerlain. This opoponax base is very similar to the other historic base Balsamol.

products.name: Opoponax Doux, Natural
products.description:
This is a 100% natural edition of the famous opoponax base beloved by Coty and used in L'Origan and Chypre. It was also used in numerous perfumes by Guerlain, including an early formula of Jicky. Opoponax Doux is a wonderfully balanced and rich amber base loaded with all the finest resins balanced with the perfect dose of fresh citrus oils and sweet vanilla.

The historic opoponax type base is a little confusing because "opoponax" is also the name of a resin used in perfume. However, opoponax bases are a type of ambreine base - artful blends of vanilla, citrus, resins and other luxurious naturals. The main difference is that opoponax bases are narcotic while ambreine bases are erogenous. This means they are synergistic.

Combinations of Opoponax Doux and Ambreine Samuelson are found through many historic perfumes and were particular favourites of Coty and Guerlain. This opoponax base is very similar to the other historic base Balsamol.

For a great blend, try 2% Opoponax Doux Natural with 0.8% Ambreine Natural.

products.name: Opoponax Oil
products.description:
Opoponax Oil is resinous, spicy, and immediately evocative of ancient incense rituals. The distinctive mushroom-earthy undertones emerge quickly, adding savoury complexity that sets this material apart from simpler balsams. Subtle animalic facets provide depth, while a curious broth-like richness (somewhat like vegetable soup or lovage) makes this one of the more characterful naturals in our arsenals.

Often called "sweet myrrh," opoponax belongs to the same Burseraceae family as myrrh and frankincense but offers a distinctly sweeter, less medicinal profile. Where myrrh is sharp and slightly bitter, opoponax is warm and effervescent. 

Use it in oriental compositions where its sweet-spicy balsamic character anchors heavier notes, or in chypres where it adds unexpected sweet lift. The mushroom-earthy facet works beautifully in leather accords and dark florals. Blend with labdanum, benzoin, myrrh, frankincense, sandalwood, and patchouli for classic resinous effects. The animalic depth makes it valuable in natural perfumery seeking complexity without synthetic musks.

Opoponax Oil vs Myrrh Oil

These two Commiphora oils share family character but differ meaningfully. Myrrh (Commiphora myrrha) is sharper, more medicinal, with bitter-aromatic facets and a drier, more austere profile. Opoponax is sweeter, warmer, more balsamic, with that distinctive mushroom-broth richness and subtle animalic depth.

Use myrrh when you want incense severity and bitter complexity; reach for opoponax

products.name: Opoponax Resinoid 50% TEC
products.description:
Opoponax resinoid is not as common today as it should be, perhaps due to its hardness (hence being offered here at 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate). It is also known as sweet myrrh which is understandable as it has a delightfully sweet caramel note making it especially valuable nowadays due to the popularity of gourmand scents.

Unsurprisingly it blends well with other gourmand notes and with the other perfumery resins. Opoponax resinoid is not to be confused with the unrelated amber bases sold under the same name.

In the words of the great Steffen Arctander, "Opoponax is a natural oleo-gum-resin, formed as a physiological product in natural cavities or tubular vessels in the parenchym (where most of the tree’s activity takes place,) between the bark and the wood. Harvesters make incisions in the trunks, but some opoponax flows out by itself. The crude botanical product is dark reddish, rarely dark yellow or brownish, and it occurs in comparatively regular lumps, tear shaped or bean shaped, of nut size to walnut size. Its odor is sweet-aromatic, reminiscent of spicy soups (a faint resemblance to celery or lovage,) a sweet-woody undertone, and a peculiar, animal-like, also sweet and root-like note. Although to a certain degree reminiscent of myrrh, the typical difference is that opoponax has a spicy, and an animal, root-like note, neither of which is hardly, if at all, distinguishable in myrrh. The difference in odor is wide."

Origin: Ethiopia
Variety: Commiphora e

products.name: Orange Blossom Supreme
products.description:
Orange Blossom Supreme is so realistic you can't tell it apart from natural orange blossom absolute from Morocco. Rich with natural oils and true to the spirit of the genuine material, you can entirely eliminate the need to purchase orange blossom absolute once you switch to this product.

Luxury companies like Creed and Amouage use identical products in their fragrances to keep costs low despite their reputation as haute perfume houses. Try our proof of concept demonstration formula for Green Irish Tweed below to see why.

We also stock the famous Fleur D'Oranger historic fantasy base that was used in L'Origan by Coty and Tabu by Jean Carles for Dana.

products.name: Orange Flower Absolute, Egypt
products.description:
The molten sun surrenders to the horizon as jackals bay into the vast indifferent night. Linen-clad priests murmur prayers to long-forgotten gods and golden braziers cast tendrils of acrid smoke amongst baskets of ripe figs burst open in the dying heat. The thick air is filled with the scent of orange blossoms and lotus flowers. This is ancient Egypt; mysterious, opulent and eternal.

This is the imagery evoked when smelling this stunning and rare orange blossom absolute from LMR. Whilst most suppliers offer Moroccan and Tunisian varieties of orange blossom absolute, LMR products this little-known radiant treasure of the old orient. While this has less of the rich honeyed notes of other varieties, it has a complex profile that embodies more of the entire tree and environment. This is dirtier, but in the direction of earthy rather than indolic.

If we were to sum up the key differences between the three origins, we would say the following:

Egypt: Fresh, luminous, airy, radiant, aldehydic, exotic, refined, transparent, elegant, complex.

Tunisia: Rich, warm, floral, opulent, honeyed, deep, creamy, smooth, full-bodied, inviting.

Morocco: Intense, balsamic, deep, narcotic, animalic, sultry, luxurious, smoky, heady, seductive.

As with all high-cost naturals, we offer this diluted in natural TEC or pure.

products.name: Orange Flower Absolute, Tunisia
products.description:
This is the orange blossom the world means when it says orange blossom. The bitter orange has been grown around Nabeul for centuries, and its flowers, gathered by hand in a few short weeks of spring and extracted at the peak of their freshness, yield the absolute against which every other origin is measured.

This absolute is rich, honeyed and warm, a creamy white-floral heart that opens into a sweet, faintly waxy depth without ever tipping into the animalic. Where the Egyptian material is luminous and airy and the Moroccan dark and narcotic, the Tunisian sits in the golden middle: full-bodied, smooth and inviting, the very picture of the flower on the branch. It is the most familiar of the three and the most dependable, which is why it is so often the first one reached for. If there is to be only one orange flower absolute on your bench, this is the one it ought to be.

If we were to sum up the key differences between the three origins, we would say the following:

Egypt: Fresh, luminous, airy, radiant, aldehydic, exotic, refined, transparent, elegant, complex.
Tunisia: Rich, warm, floral, opulent, honeyed, deep, creamy, smooth, full-bodied, inviting.
Morocco: Intense, balsamic, deep, narcotic, animalic, sultry, luxurious, smoky, heady, seductive.

As with all high-cost naturals, we offer this diluted in natural TEC or pure.

products.name: Orange Flower Ether
products.description:
Orange Flower Ether opens with an immediate burst of bitter citrus reminiscent of fresh grapefruit peel, yet softened by subtle floral whispers that prevent it from being aggressively sharp. This sophisticated duality makes it indispensable for contemporary perfumery where clean, bright openings are paramount. Its unique position between pure citrus materials and true orange blossom extracts provides perfumers with precise control over their top note architecture.

Deploy this material at 2-5% when you need to inject life into tired citrus accords or create seamless transitions from citrus tops to floral hearts. Its particular genius lies in enhancing natural neroli without the heaviness of orange blossom absolute—think of it as neroli's sparkling cousin who arrives early to every party. Combine it with natural bergamot to amplify its Earl Grey facets, or layer it with pink grapefruit for a photorealistic pomelo effect that maintains stability where natural oils fail.

The practical applications for Orange Flower Ether extend far beyond traditional cologne structures into modern clean beauty and functional fragrances. Its exceptional stability in soaps and acidic products makes it your go-to for maintaining citrus-floral character in challenging bases. Use it to build contemporary "white shirt" accords by combining with hedione and white musks, or create addictive fresh-fruity openings by pairing with rhubarb and cassis bases.

products.name: Orange Flower Water
products.description:
Vallebona, a town in the Province of Imperia in the Italian region of Liguria has been home for seven generations to the family of Pietro Guglielmi. La Vecchia Distilleria, the family distillery, has been lovingly restored by Guglielmi under the watchful eye of his 97 year old grandmother who helps pick and sort the blossoms from their many bitter orange trees.

La Vecchia Distilleria makes neroli oil, but the item of especial interest for us is the left over water from that process. We wanted only the very best orange flower water (hydrosol) for our colognes and our search ended here. The Guglielmi family puts as much love and care into the production of their flower water as they do their neroli oil. And for that reason we had to have it.

Below is a demonstration formula for Eau de Coty which demonstrates the use of floral waters in fragrance making.

NOTE: Adding water to a fragrance is always a risky undertaking that can lead to clouding. Always chill and filter fragrances before bottling.

products.name: Orange Flower Water Absolute
products.description:
Orange Flower Water Absolute is a byproduct of the manufacture of neroli oil. It is made by solvent washing the water and materials remaining after the distillation of orange flowers for other purposes.

The material is wonderfully rich despite being secondary product and has an intensely earthy quality absent from the oil and absolute of orange blossoms making it ideal as a nuancer and enricher of those products. Orange Flower Water Absolute is harsher but less indolic than Orange Blossom Absolute or Neroli Oil.

products.name: Orange Heart
products.description:
Orange Heart is the warmest of the LMR citrus hearts. Where Lime and Lemon Hearts push zesty brightness, this one pushes richness — a deep, juicy, almost candied orange-peel sweetness that sits in the heart of a composition like sunlight through amber glass. It is unmistakably orange but with a depth that standard sweet orange oil never achieves.

This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction developed to boost the citrus profile at very low dosage. Standard sweet orange oil is beautiful but notoriously fleeting — it can vanish from a composition within the first hour. Orange Heart anchors that warmth. Use it when you need the golden sweetness of orange to carry through into the drydown alongside woods, vanillas, and ambers.

A natural partner for oriental and gourmand compositions. Try a touch in tonka-vanilla bases for a luminous citrus lift, or blend with our Bergamot Oil FCF (Côte d'Ivoire) and Cinnamon Absolute for a sun-drenched hesperidic accord with unusual warmth and gentle spice.

products.name: Oranger Crystals
products.description:
Oranger Crystals (Methyl Beta Napthyl Ketone) are a fine powder with a delicate and extremely long lasting scent of orange blossoms. They are easier to dose than the much stronger (and impactful) Methyl Anthranilate and Nerolin (Yara Yara) and the two are often found together in Neroli type bases.

Oranger Crystals are also wonderful nuancers for Jasmine and Sweet Pea notes. They blend extremely well with the classic nitro musks, particularly Musk Ketone.

Despite the high IFRA restriction, they are still a very useful addition to the perfumer's toolkit.

products.name: Orbitone® T Neo
products.description:
Orbitone® T Neo is the Takasago version of Iso E Super® and it is the closest single product in chemical makeup to IFF's captive Iso G Super®. The key chemical in Iso G Super is called “Iso Gamma” and in the captive Iso G Super there is 15%. Iso E Super® has 11.7% and Timbersilk® (also from IFF) has 13.5% (with a touch of AmberXTreme as a booster). Orbitone™ T on the other hand has a whopping 14.2%. At the other end of the scale, Sylvamber by DRT has the lowest amount at 9.5% but it is often wrongly lauded due to the higher quantity of the other key isomer called Arborone.

Fraterworks is offering this amazing Takasago product for the first time at small retail quantities. We love it and highly recommend it to anyone wanting a variant on the classic Iso E Super profile. In comparison to regular Iso E Super, Orbitone T is more balsamic and creamy. It has an elegance and a sense of space lacking in classic Iso E. It has a more profound transparency and sheerness.

Note: In 2026 Takasago have refined their manufacturing process further resulting in this higher purity Orbitone T which they are calling "Orbitone T Neo". It has slightly increased diffusion and sheer beauty but is otherwise the same. This replaces Orbitone T which is no longer being manufactured.

products.name: Orcanox™
products.description:
Orcanox™ from V. MANE Fils is a new form of Ambroxan taking the perfume world by storm. It is chemically the same as Ambrofix™ of Givaudan (a higher quality version of Firmenich's Ambrox Super). But Orcanox is special…

Orcanox is a rare treasure that has been hitherto impossible to obtain in small quantities. It has an olfactory profile that is richer and more complex than regular ambroxan and it is more diffusive than our go-to quality.

Orcanox has a modernising undercurrent of sweetness and a unique character that makes it a clear standout when compared to the common types from the last decade. 

Featured in The Ghost in the Shell (2021) and Sous Le Pont Mirabeau (2023) by Etat Libre d'Orange, Bella (2021) by Baldessarini and Smoking Hot (2023) by Kilian.

NOTE: Ambrofix, ambroxan, Ambrox®, Ambrox Super, and ambroxide are synonyms. They are simply different trade names for the same chemical though produced through different processes.

products.name: Orchidée № 2
products.description:
De Laire produced two orchid bases, Orchidée №s 1 & 2. Fraterworks Orchidée № 2 is a restoration of the latter — the more floral and historically more popular and widely used base. Orchids are generally odourless and in perfumery circles the term is commonly used to refer to clover (treflé) or salicylate based fantasy aromas. Orchidée is no exception. Rich with natural floral absolutes, aldehydes and luxurious musks, this is a top to bottom base that can be used alone as a wonderful fragrance, or as part of a new fragrance.

Usable in large quantities (up to 29% of your finished product), Orchidée is a perfect alternative to the far more common heart note synthetics (hedione and the like) around which most modern fragrances tend to be built. For a touch of je ne sais quoi, look no further than Fraterworks Orchidée.

products.name: Orcinyl 3
products.description:
This crystalline captures the essential phenolic and leathery facets of traditional oakmoss absolute. It has impressive tenacity and provides reliable structure and longevity to sophisticated compositions.

Use orcinyl at 0.05-1% concentration in formulations with Evernyl for complete oakmoss effects. This material creates excellent synergy with patchouli, vetiver, and labdanum notes. Apply in chypre and fougère bases requiring compliant mossy character.

Owing to the high cost and strength, we are offering this diluted to 10% or pure.

products.name: Orivone®
products.description:
Orivone imparts a distinctive floral-woody aroma characterised by prominent iris-like and powdery notes, enriched with subtle camphoraceous and earthy undertones. Its sophisticated scent effectively mimics the prized orris root, making it invaluable for crafting elegant iris accords economically.

Orivone is highly valued for enhancing floral compositions, notably violet and iris-centric fragrances, and lending depth to powdery, woody blends. Its powerful diffusivity and cost-effectiveness also make it ideal for use in functional products like soaps, lotions, and detergents.

products.name: Orris Absolute, France
products.description:
Iris is perhaps the most esteemed natural in perfumery. It comes in multiple forms depending on use and Fraterworks stocks all of them! Orris is a complex material so here is a little primer on the types.

Orris Tincture (variable Irones): Clear liquid. Alcohol extract from powdered iris roots.
Orris Resinoid (1 – 10% Irones): Dark brown thick paste. Alcohol extracted.
Orris Butter (10 – 20% Irones): Solid white wax. Also sometimes called orris concrete or orris essential oil. Steam distillation.
Orris Absolute (80% Irones): Clear liquid. Almost never available for retail sale.

Orris absolute is rarely seen in modern fragrances; the most notable recent exception was the masterpiece Dior Homme (2005 edition) with 0.25% and 0.3% in Iris Ganache (Guerlain, 2007). 

Of all the orris materials, the absolute has the most profoundly strong scent of orris root and a little goes a long way which is fortunate because the price is eye watering.

This orris absolute is from orris Pallida.

products.name: Orris Germanica Butter
products.description:
Orris Butter is renowned in perfumery for its luxurious aroma and this Germanica concrete is the finest example of the material. While Orris Pallida is the most common source of iris butter, the Germanica product has nuances it lacks. Germanica iris is creamier, more balanced and a little less powdery.

Obtaining orris butter is a years-long process that involves digging up and curing the rhizomes, followed by a highly specialised distillation. The final product is a solid material with a butterscotch colour that melts to the touch.

Sourced from the top supplier in Grasse, our Orris Germanica Butter is the most perfect quality, surpassing all other online offerings. Additionally, because our supplier is the world leader, a constant supply is assured. This is the gold standard with Chinese origin rhizomes far surpassing the cheaper Moroccan variety in beauty.

products.name: Orris Germanica Resinoid
products.description:
With the highest fixative power of all the iris products, orris resinoid is a hidden gem that far too few perfumers take advantage of. This should not be confused with orris butter which is actually a true essential oil; orris resinoid is deep brown in colour while orris butter (also known as orris concrete) is a white waxy solid.

In addition to being a great fixative, Orris Resinoid imparts a lovely sweet Iris root note quite similar to that of orris powder but more intense and certainly more compatible with perfumery. This is perhaps the truest scent of the rhizome as the concrete (essential oil) has a far lighter and less earthy scent.

We are selling this resinoid pure and in a 50% dilution in natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate as it is difficult to work with pure as it is highly viscous. Please ensure you select the right dilution from the options. 

In addition to this well priced Germanica resinoid, we also stock the more expensive Orris Pallida Resinoid which is more floral and deep and less powdery.

Origin: Morocco
Part: Roots
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Orris Givco® 204/20
products.description:
Orris Givco is a modern Givaudan base for contributing orris notes to a fragrance. It was designed to mimic orris absolute and orris butter but in reality it is brighter and more radiant than both. The steady reduction in natural orris materials in the base over time (due to cost) means that it can benefit from the addition of small amounts of natural iris butter or resinoid (Germanica or Pallida) also.

If you are looking for a richer and more luxurious alternative we recommend the great Orrisodore which featured in Jacques Fath's famous Iris Gris (1946, Vincent Roubert — download formula) and Paco Rabanne's Calandre (1969, Michael Hy).

products.name: Orris Imperial
products.description:
The price of orris butter has risen exponentially in recent years, placing it beyond the reach of most perfumers. Yet its role remains indispensable—it anchors floral hearts with sophisticated depth, bridges woody and powdery elements seamlessly, and acts as a fixative that amplifies surrounding notes while slowing their evaporation. The complex interplay of over 200 aromatic compounds, particularly the precious irones that develop during aging, creates effects no single synthetic can replicate.

Orris Imperial answers this challenge with a replacer rich in irones that matches natural orris butter's character and radiating power. Use it one-for-one wherever orris butter appears in formulae, bringing the same violet-suede elegance and fixative strength without compromise. When replacing orris absolute, increase the quantity fourfold to achieve equivalent impact. This allows you to work with one of perfumery's most refined materials without the prohibitive cost that has made true orris butter practically vanish from perfumers' shelves.

products.name: Orris Pallida Butter
products.description:
Orris Pallida Butter 15% Irones (sometimes called concrete) is a solid essential oil that strikes with its signature powdery violet character—soft yet penetrating, creamy yet dry. This waxy white material captures the essence of aged iris rhizomes from Italian Tuscany, rich in gamma-irone that develops only through years of patient maturation. Its scent hovers between floral delicacy and woody earthiness, with unexpected fruity facets that peek through like raspberry sherbet dusted with cocoa.

Use this precious material primarily as a fixative where its tenacity amplifies and anchors surrounding notes without dominating them. Pair it with rose absolute and sandalwood to build elegant floral-woody structures, or combine it with vetiver and labdanum for sophisticated chypre bases. Its powdery character transforms aldehydic compositions, whilst its fatty richness smooths sharp citrus and adds creamy depth to berry accords. Apply it sparingly—even at high dilution, its strength emerges dramatically in the dry-down.

We also stock Orris Germanica butter.
