products.name: Orris Pallida “Signature” Resinoid
products.description:
With the highest fixative power of all the orris products, this is a hidden gem that far too few perfumers take advantage of. This should not be confused with orris butter which is actually a true essential oil; orris resinoid is deep brown in colour while orris butter (also known as orris concrete) is a creamy white waxy solid.

We are selling this resinoid at 50% dilution in natural odourless triethyl citrate as it is almost impossible to work with pure as it is so viscous that it borders on solid. We are, however, also supplying it pure so please check your selected dilution. 

This resinoid contains a maximum irone load of 1.7%.

We also stock the lower cost more powdery Orris Germanica resinoid.

Origin: Italy
Part: Roots
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Orris Root CO2
products.description:
Orris Root CO2 (3% Irones) opens with a cool, powdery breath of violet that softens immediately into buttery cream and warm suede. Beneath that elegance sits a damp, earthy rootiness - almost carrot-like - that gives the material its grounding character. The overall impression is of vintage face powder resting on warm skin. The odour impression of the 10% variant (diluted in IPM which keeps it crystal clear and liquid even at very low temperatures) is that of orris absolute, making this an excellent way to naturalise irone alpha when cost is a consideration.

This material functions as a powerful structural bridge between floral hearts and woody bases, smoothing harsh transitions and rounding sharp edges. Add it to rose accords for a couture finish or pair it with ionones and methylionones to build a convincing lipstick accord.

Try it in trace amounts alongside sandalwood to amplify creaminess, or with vetiver to accentuate its suede-woody facets. Combine with aldehydes C-11 Undecylenic and C-12 Lauric (the classic French iris aldehyde) to soften their metallic bite into something polished. Keep your dosage restrained - too much orris will flatten a composition into dry, cosmetic monotony.

products.name: Orris Root Tincture 10%
products.description:
Orris root tincture is a powdery soft iris product with a marvellous fixative property. It blends very well with fruit notes giving them grounding and naturalisation. It has a long history in perfumery where it joins the other plant based fixatives such as the popular tincture of benzoin and extracts of ambrette seed.

Fraterworks produces this tincture in the classical French manner using nothing but rich and buttery dried and powdered iris roots and pure and natural ethanol produced using water from southern alpine glaciers.

Orris root tincture is a dependable and trusted material that fits in to virtually any context. It can be used alongside or in place of Poudre à la Maréchale tincture.

Also known as: orris rhizome tincture or iris root tincture.

products.name: Orrisodore™
products.description:
Orrisodore™ is the supreme iris base. Rich with orris butter, iris resin, iris absolute, mysore sandalwood and so many other regal naturals, this base is the glory of the golden age encapsulated.

One drop adds an indescribable iris beauty to your scent, while an overdose gives you a fragrance fit for a sultan. Just add peach and you have a perfume that makes Fath's Iris Gris seem mediocre.

products.name: Osmanthe sur Gurjun
products.description:
Osmanthe sur Gurjun is a co-distillation — osmanthus flowers distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is osmanthus at its most extravagant: sweet, sticky, overwhelmingly present, with the gurjun providing body and balsamic warmth without ever competing.

The osmanthus dominates from the first moment — ripe apricot, suede, the full multifaceted complexity of the flower in unapologetic expression. Where Payan Bertrand's Fleur de Cuir co-distils osmanthus onto cedarwood for a drier, more restrained effect, our version on gurjun is sweeter, thicker, more lush. The balsamic base acts as a warm platform that amplifies the osmanthus rather than constraining it. The fruit and the leather and the floral facets all come through at once.

Add Ombre d'Iris and you have a complete perfume — practically nothing else needed. The sweet, physical osmanthus against that spectral iris-cedar creates a dialogue between substance and shadow, fruit and ghost. Alternatively, use Osmanthe sur Gurjun beneath tuberose or jasmine to add sticky, apricot-skin warmth that no synthetic can replicate.

products.name: Osmanthus Flowers
products.description:
Fraterworks Osmanthus Flowers (formerly just called Osmanthus) is an elegant and rich base featuring large amounts of the finest osmanthus oil. With its notes of leather and apricots, this base is a perfect unifier for modern gourmand types. Or simply overdose it for a luxurious and unusual floral fragrance.

Osmanthus was a key note in 1,000 by Jean Patou and it is often used as a sweetener or complexing agent. This Fraterworks base is an excellent way to incorporate genuine osmanthus absolute at an unbeatable price.

products.name: Osmanthus Heart
products.description:
Apricot, suede, warm milk, and flowers — all from a single natural material. Osmanthus Heart concentrates the most compelling fractions of this famously expensive absolute. The ripe fruit quality is immediate and unmistakable, unlike any synthetic peach or apricot note. Beneath the fruit sits a soft leather character that gives the material its extraordinary complexity.

This is one of the rare naturals that provides a genuinely fruity note — most apricot and peach effects in perfumery rely on gamma-decalactone and similar synthetics. Osmanthus Heart delivers that fruit with a floral-animalic depth that no single molecule can match. Use it as the centrepiece of luxury floral compositions where the apricot-suede character becomes the signature.

The leather facet makes it a natural bridge between floral hearts and animalic bases without needing a separate leather accord. It enriches rose and jasmine compositions with a fruity warmth. In oud-based compositions, the milky softness tempers harshness. Try it alongside iris butter and sandalwood for the quietest, most refined luxury accord imaginable.

products.name: Osmanthus “Gold” Absolute
products.description:
Given it's rarity and price, Osmanthus Absolute is only produced by a few companies at present. There are, of course, the "supreme five": LMR (IFF), Floral Concept, V. MANE Fils, Payan Bertrand and Robertet, and then the mid-range Givaudan (Albert Vielle), and Firmenich. As with all our naturals, we don't seek the lowest prices, we seek the finest products and so we tested all the offerings of the aforementioned (even those at the lower end of the scale). The choice was an easy one: LMR.

Rcently LMR has been producing an Osmanthus that simply astonishes. From the succulent scent of ripe apricots to the aristocratic leather scent of a royal stable, this Osmanthus absolute is the reference for this remarkable and exotic oriental flower extract. Smelling this absolute is like smelling Osmanthus all over again for the first time. It is, simply put, breathtaking.

Note: this replaces the absolute we were previously selling by V. MANE Fils as it took the crown in our 2025 internal product competition in which we test naturals from a variety of sources. 

We are selling this at 10% in natural triethyl citrate and pure.

If you are looking for something a little lower cost, try our Osmanthus Flowers speciality base or the wonderful Fleur de Cuir, a co-distillation of Osmanthus with Cedarwood by Payan Bertrand.

products.name: Osyrol
products.description:
Osyrol is a very light sandalwood chemical (one of a myriad). It is extremely versatile as it can be used in very high doses as a canvas chemical. It is sweet and clean and has floral nuances and it blends extremely well with most of the sandalwood family.

It is used to good effect in Coco (Chanel, 1984) with Sandalore and Mysore Sandalwood, and the original M7 (2002) by YLS at 1%. It also features in Allure Homme by Chanel (0.3%), Burberry Women at a huge 9%, 1.25% of J'Adore by Dior, and Pardon by Nasomatto.

products.name: Oud Assafi®
products.description:
East truly does meet West in this most famous of all wild harvested oud oils. Oud Assafi is the result of a collaboration of Bangladeshi master distillers Jalali Agarwood and Swiss fragrance giant Firmenich.

Oud Assafi is intensely animalic and woody with a sweet undertone. It is perceptible in traces (which is fortunate given its high price).

For a surprising good (and very cost-effective) extender to this treasured essential oil, blend it with a generous amount of Laine de Mouton absolute. The two are extremely synergistic and the combination allows a perfumer to mimic the effect of an Oud Assafi overdose.

Owing to the intensity of this pure oil and the extremely high price, we are also offering it diluted to 1%, 5% and 10% in natural triethyl citrate, a marvellous odourless diluent produced from citrus.

If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings.

products.name: Oud Firbest®
products.description:
Oud Firbest is Firmenich's general Oud base, balancing woods, florals and animalic notes in such a way as to not focus on a specific terroir or variety of Oud. It was designed to give a consistent and cost-effective realistic oud note in perfumes as natural ouds can vary wildly in odour from batch to batch. It is a versatile base but is particularly well suited to oriental and woody fragrances.

Firmenich's Firbest® range contains bases made of both synthetic and natural elements which replicate the scent of a natural extract without containing that extract itself. These bases solve problems often associated with naturals such as extremely high cost or, as mentioned, variability in batch quality.

If you are looking for a 5-star alternative to the Firbest range, we also produce our own Oud Intense™ base which is, in the words of one reviewer: “one of the best oud bases I've tried.”

We also offer Oud Laos Firbest—a lighter and more fruity-floral oud base, Pretty Oud, a rich animalic but extremely easy to use Oud base, Oud Synth 184007 a lower cost Firmenich base and Black Agar Givco from Givaudan which is really more fantasy than reality.

And for those with the budget for it, we offer Oud Assafi® a glorious (but eye-wateringly expensive) natural Oud Assam wild harvested in Bangladesh. Alternatively you may like the much more frugal Aetoxylon or White Oud oil from V MANE Fils.

products.name: Oud Intense™
products.description:
Wild, radiant and complex Fraterworks® Oud Intense™ is a powerful base offering the full spectrum of notes found in natural oud oil. Oud Intense is built around a fond of rich wood extracts — including, at its heart, 1.2% pure wild Oud Assafi from Bangladesh. The finest synthetic and natural musks add longevity while powerful contemporary molecules add an almost-impossible diffusion and radiance to the whole.

Perceptible in traces, dazzling in overdose, Oud Intense is the holy grail of oud bases.

products.name: Oud Laos Firbest®
products.description:
Oud Laos Firbest® is the second of Firmenich's Firbest bases to focus on the wonderful world of Ouds. Compared to the more general purpose Oud Firbest, this Laos version aims to replicate the oils from the territory of Laos—oils known to have a lighter, fruitier and more floral character. Both Firbest bases are very similar to one another but if you are seeking a more modern or broadly appealing type, the Oud Laos Firbest option is for you. It is less animalic, greener and certainly more approachable. It also serves as a good starting point for an accord in the direction of Yellow Kynam.

Natural Laotian Oud is unique among agarwood varieties. The top notes often present an initial smoky, fruity and balsamic intensity, followed by a heart of leathery spice, musky citrus, and warm florals. The dry-down is notable for its smooth, slightly creamy woodiness, which enhances the overall balance and longevity of the fragrance.

Firmenich's Firbest® range contains bases made of both synthetic and natural elements which replicate the scent of a natural extract without containing that extract itself. These bases solve problems often associated with naturals such as extremely high cost or, as mentioned, variability in batch quality.

If you are looking for a 5-star alternative to the Firbest range, we also produce our own Oud Intense™ base which is, in the words of one reviewer: “one of the best oud bases I've tried.”

We also offer Oud Firbest—a more general purpose base, Pretty Oud, a

products.name: Oud Malacca
products.description:
Fraterworks Oud Malacca opens with a dank, almost murky hit that immediately signals authentic Malaysian oud character. Rich woody complexity unfolds quickly — resinous depth shot through with a hint of cinnamon warmth and a surprising suggestion of ocean air. A green, almost minty quality rounds out the profile with camphoraceous freshness.

Use Oud Malacca base as the foundation of a luxurious oriental — usable at 0.92% of your finished product, it carries the weight. It works equally well as a subtle nuancer where you want oud presence without animalic dominance. Its versatility mirrors the natural oil: equally at home in fresh compositions and deep, resinous accords.

Pair with Moroccan rose absolute and Saffron Attar for a classic Middle Eastern accord, or with marine and citrus notes to exploit that oceanic facet. Malaysian oud is the most versatile origin in perfumery — this base belongs in every perfumer's organ.

Note: this base contains no natural oud oil and thus is not subject to any CITES restrictions.

products.name: Oud Oil, Vietnam
products.description:
LMR's Oud Oil from Vietnam is sweeter and less intensely animal than the better known Oud Assafi from Firmenich. This will sit more politely in your blend, though make no mistakes about it, this is unmistakably oud: dark, foreboding and rich. It also has a price point that is less jaw-dropping.

This particular oud comes from a single family-owned Vietnamese distillery that manages four forests of Aquilaria crassna. The trees produce two grades of resinous wood: white wood is distilled into Agarwood Boya Oil, while the higher-resin grey wood becomes this oil — the darker, more animalic of the two.

The benefit of buying Oud from LMR or Firmenich is that the sheer size of these companies means the supply is consistent and ongoing. These are oud oils you can trust from batch to batch.

If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings.

products.name: Oud Oliffac
products.description:
This IFF oud base opens with fruity sweetness, a touch of dank earth, and the whisper of a medicinal note. This is followed by balsams, spices (particularly cinnamon) and a quiet animalic growl.

This is almost like a refined version of the classic Firmenich Oud Synth. Unlike Oud Synth, this IFF speciality is less vetiver forward. The blending is impeccable. This is one of the most polite (but not tame) oud bases and one I heartily recommend. If you are new to oud, this is a good start.

Blend it with red berry aromachemicals like dulcinyl, rasberry ketone, and raspberry glycidate, or with our highly popular Raspberry Ripple base. To bring out the spiced notes I recommend Firmenich's Pretty Oud.

products.name: Oud Synth 184007
products.description:
Firmenich's classic Oud Synth 10760 base has undergone a facelift in order to remove phthalates and furfural for better compliance with customer demands and updated IFRA standards. The odour profile of this new Oud Synth 184007 is very little changed from its predecessor and this is now the only version available from Firmenich.

In Firmenich's own words: “A reconstitution of agarwood oil. Intensely woody, animalic and reminiscent of vetiver, with sweet balsamic undertones.”

This is one of those oud bases built around a common blend of natural woods with Ambrinol supplying the animalic element. It is a lovely material that blends well with other Oud products. It can be used to add depth and richness to Givaudan's Black Agar Givco.

products.name: Oudhbois
products.description:
Oudhbois is a speciality product (sold by some retailers as Oudamide). It is a woody aroma chemical with nuances of grapefruit (nootkatone type) and oud and a whisper of animal. It blends beautifully with other woody materials such as Cedrol crystals, Aetoxylon Oil, Orbitone® and Iso E Super™. Use it to make a dark fantasy base of gnarled wood or as an alternative to the common woods that are overdosed in most modern fragrances.

This product is found in a few significant fragrances such as Marc-Antoine Barrois's 2019 Ganymede (formula below) and Tom Ford's Santal Blush and Plum Japonais, however widespread adoption is still yet to occur. Be the first!

products.name: Oxane 50 TEC
products.description:
Oxane (the high cis version of Tropathiane) opens with extraordinary tropical intensity—green, tart, and immediately evocative of fresh passion fruit and grapefruit. The sulphurous character provides the exotic depth that makes tropical fruit accords convincing, while galbanum-like freshness adds crisp green naturalism. This is one of perfumery's most powerful materials, revealing its true beauty only at significant dilution.

This iconic Firmenich molecule (discovered 1974) forms a cornerstone of the legendary Thioxane base, and Cassis Base that has defined blackcurrant accords for decades. It delivers the sulphurous tropical character found naturally in passion fruit. The 60-hour substantivity on blotter belies its top note character; despite being highly volatile, Oxane's impact persists through sheer potency. 

Work with Oxane at 50% dilution (as supplied) and dose with extreme caution. Evaluate at 0.1% dilution or less; at higher concentrations the sulphurous notes dominate and the tropical beauty remains hidden. Use it in passion fruit, grapefruit, mango, and exotic fruit accords. Combine with Isospirene for classic blackcurrant effects. It adds surprising warmth and naturalism to florals—jasmine, rose, and muguet all benefit from trace amounts. Excellent in green aldehydic compositions seeking tropical lift.

products.name: Oxynex® ST
products.description:
Oxynex® ST is an essential stabiliser, safeguarding fragrance integrity against light and oxidation. It ensures your perfumes and cosmetics remain true and vibrant. Use it alone in your finished product or with Solgard® for added protection.

Oxynex® is the commercial name for Diethylhexyl Syringylidenemalonate in Fractionated Coconut Oil (FCO). This oil base ensures DESM’s solubility and modifies its texture and consistency. Due to the FCO, Oxynex® ST also acts as an emollient, offering a light conditioning skin-feel upon perfume application. Oxynex® ST is a synthetic molecule derived from Syringa Aldehyde and no natural form exists.

If you already use our Solgard® technology, you may still want to add a touch of Oxynex® ST because it has a powerful synergy with Avobenzone which is a key material in that best seller. Use it at just 0.2 – 0.5% of your finished perfume. 

Use Case: Eau de Parfum

200 Fragrance Compound
788 Perfumer's Alcohol
8 Solgard® E
4 Oxynex® ST

In the formula above you can omit the Solgard® but keep the Oxynex® quantity the same. If you are using our Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol, omit the Solgard® from the formula above.

products.name: Oxyoctaline Formate
products.description:
Oxyoctaline Formate opens with a distinctive moist woodiness — not the dry, static cedar of most woody molecules, but something that feels alive, like freshly sawn timber still wet with sap. An incense-like dryness settles in quickly, powdery and dusty, with a refined amber warmth that recalls good frankincense without the sharp resinous bite.

Givaudan developed this as a blender, and that is where it truly excels. It fills the space between transparent woody notes and heavy amber bases, creating seamless transitions that make compositions feel more expensive and more coherent. Use it in sandalwood accords where its moist character adds realism, or drop it into oud compositions where its resinous quality supports the raw-wood facets without adding sweetness.

Think of it as the mortar between bricks. It does not call attention to itself, but remove it and the structure feels hollow. Pair it with Iso E Super for a modern woody foundation, or combine with labdanum and olibanum for an amber accord that smells like it grew rather than being assembled.

products.name: PADMA
products.description:
Also known as Viridine, PADMA is an acronym for Phenyl Acetaldehyde Dimethyl Acetal. It is a very classic green chemical that has long been exploited in fragrances to contribute a hyacinth note.

Despite its years it has managed to avoid the relentless march of legislative banning and remains completely unrestricted for perfumery use. But be careful: it is deceptively strong.

products.name: Palisandrol 17979F
products.description:
Built around a wonderfully high dose of Norlimbanol, Palisandrol is a radiant wood base from Firmenich featured in such fragrances as YSL's M7 (0.5%) and Dolce and Gabanna Light Blue (2007) at 1.5%.

With trace captives and a delicate fruity nuance, this is an excellent product to add high impact materials in easier to manage doses. Palisandrol is radiant and extremely diffusive.

Palisandrol blends extremely well with Fauxmoss®, Kephalis, Benzyl Acetone, and wood materials in general.

products.name: Palmarosa Oil
products.description:
Palmarosa Oil opens sweet, rosy, and unmistakably floral. A fresh grassy-citrus quality lifts the opening, while gentle metallic and herbaceous undertones add dry complexity. The overall effect is warm, soft, and remarkably close to geranium oil.

Use Palmarosa as your workhorse rosy-floral heart. It builds convincing rose, geranium, and carnation accords at a fraction of what rose absolute costs, blending beautifully with bergamot, jasmine, and cedarwood. In lily of the valley and apple blossom compositions, it provides the soft floral body that ties everything together.

Don't overlook Palmarosa where you'd never expect a rose note — a trace softens and rounds woody accords beautifully. It adds an almost tea-like freshness to citrus blends. Pair it with oakmoss for an unexpectedly gorgeous chypre foundation.

products.name: Palmitic Acid
products.description:
Palmitic acid greets you not with a shout but a whisper - a barely-there fatty warmth that feels more like clean skin than perfume. It reads waxy and bland in isolation, with a faintly oily, candle-like smoothness. This is a textural material, not a decorative one.

Think of palmitic acid as invisible scaffolding. It slows the evaporation of volatile top notes, anchors fleeting musks to the skin, and adds creamy body to lactonic and floral accords. Pair it with ambrettolide or isoambrettolide for substantive, realistic skin-musk effects. Blend into jasmin or tuberose bases to recreate the thick, waxy feel of living petals.

Try it at low levels to soften harsh aliphatic aldehydes like dodecanal, or fold it into orris reconstructions alongside myristic acid to mimic the fatty matrix of genuine orris butter. You can also use it to build convincing dairy and gourmand textures with gamma-undecalactone and butter esters.

products.name: Pamplefleur®
products.description:
Pamplefleur opens with a tart, zesty burst of grapefruit peel tempered by a sharp rhubarb bite. Unlike fleeting citrus terpenes, this material carries dry, earthy vetiver undertones. The effect sits somewhere between fresh-cut peel and sun-warmed root vegetables.

This phenyl-substituted alcohol solves the age-old citrus problem: longevity. Where Methyl Pamplemousse flashes brightly and fades, Pamplefleur persists through the heart and into the base. Layer both materials together for a linear grapefruit effect that carries from opening spray to final drydown. Its animalic warmth also makes it unexpectedly effective for lifting jasmine accords.

Think of Pamplefleur as your citrus anchor rather than your citrus sparkle. Blend it with Iso E Super for clean, modern woody-citrus effects found in sport and blue fragrances. Pair with Paradisamide for tropical guava-grapefruit combinations. Use restraint—overdose pushes it toward rubbery synthetic territory, but at trace levels it adds convincing rind realism to any fruit accord.

products.name: Pamplocoeur
products.description:
Pamplocoeur opens with a bright, fizzy grapefruit burst that feels almost effervescent on the blotter. There is a distinct sweetness here - think pink pomelo flesh rather than bitter rind. A soft floral shimmer sits underneath, giving the whole impression an airy, sparkling quality that natural grapefruit oil simply cannot sustain.

This is Firmenich's answer to the instability problem that plagues natural grapefruit oil. Where the natural decays into sulphurous off-notes, Pamplocoeur holds its juicy, tart character throughout the life of your product. Pair it with Hedione to boost its radiance and sillage, or add Oxane to push the profile toward tropical passionfruit and blackcurrant. It works brilliantly as a freshener in floral hearts - a few percent into jasmine or rose prevents heaviness without adding obvious citrus.

Think beyond straightforward grapefruit accords. Combine Pamplocoeur with Methyl Pamplemousse to build convincing yuzu reconstructions. Blend it into woody compositions alongside Iso E Super and vetiver for a bitter-fresh contrast that reads as sophisticated and modern.

products.name: Pandanol
products.description:
If you have ever buried your nose in chrysanthemums, you already know this molecule. Sharp, green, and penetrating, with a metallic floral brightness and rosy-jasmine facets underneath. It is the main component of kewda oil and essentially is the chrysanthemum note in perfumery.

What surprises is the tenacity. Pandanol smells like a fleeting top note but persists for nearly ninety hours on a blotter — a genuinely unusual combination of ethereal character and lasting power. On dilution the sharpness softens into something grassy and warm, almost pungent, with more rose showing through.

A trace in heavy floral accords cuts through the opacity and weight. Indispensable for kewda (it comprises up to 80% of the natural material from Pandanus fascicularis) and chrysanthemum recreations, it also lifts jasmine and hyacinth compositions with its penetrating green radiance. Phenylethyl alcohol, hedione, and galbanum are its most natural companions.

products.name: Para Cresyl Acetate
products.description:
Para cresyl acetate demands respect—this is one of perfumery's most powerful and potentially treacherous materials. At full strength, it reveals horse-like, almost urinous undertones that can ruin compositions. But dilute below 1% and something magical happens: a gorgeous narcissus-lily character emerges, fresh yet unmistakably animalic in the way real spring bulbs smell on a warm day.

This material provides the distinctive animal note that makes bulbous flower accords convincing. You simply cannot create a natural-smelling narcissus, hyacinth, or jonquil without it—the flowers themselves contain related compounds that give them their characteristic edge. Use between 0.1% and 1% in your creation to capture that authentic quality. Even lower doses add tension and spice to jasmine and oriental florals.

Work with para cresyl acetate at 10% dilution minimum, or prepare a 1% dilution for finer control. It pulls wood, amber, and certain spices to the top note, so balance carefully. The material can totally destroy a composition when combined with certain notes—experience teaches you which. But master its use and you'll have access to some of the most beautiful and realistic floral effects in perfumery.

products.name: Para Cresyl Caprylate
products.description:
Para Cresyl Caprylate is the gentle member of the cresyl family. But don't be fooled! While it has a much smaller impact on top notes, it has a wonderfully long dry down and modifying effect.

A delicately fecal animalic with traces of hay, ylang-ylang, narcissus and jasmine, this has a surprisingly broad range of applications, from florals to oud recreations.

Para Cresyl Caprylate was sometimes used in overdose in honeysuckle and animalic accords, but in smaller amounts (typically under 0.1%) it adds texture and naturalness to florals.

This is a material that all perfumers should stock. It may have fewer applications than classic Para Cresol but it is invaluable nonetheless.

products.name: Para Cresyl Methyl Ether
products.description:
Para cresyl methyl ether hits you with an immediate phenolic punch that rapidly unfurls into something unmistakably ylang-ylang. Beneath that sweet floral attack, you catch powdery, nutty facets and a faint camphoraceous edge. On a strip, it softens into a greener, almost marigold-like drydown.

This is one of those materials whose true magic only reveals itself inside a blend. A trace amount lifts narcissus, jasmine, and ylang accords from pleasant to convincing, lending the phenolic-animalic undertow that makes real flowers smell alive. It bridges the gap between clean florals and the darker, cresylic facets found in narcissus absolute, tuberose, and champaca, without the heaviness of para cresol itself. Work with it at low levels in a 10% dilution to keep control.

Pair it with indole and para cresyl phenyl acetate for a narcissus heart, or stir it into ylang reconstructions alongside benzyl acetate and isoeugenol. In leather accords, it reinforces the phenolic backbone beautifully. Always evaluate in dilution first—neat, the camphoraceous top note can mislead your nose about what this material truly contributes.

products.name: Para Cresyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
Passing this chemical around the laboratory amongst the staff who had never smelled it resulted in uniform cries of "pee!". For one it is rabbit pee, for another it is the scent of sheep in the field (we are in New Zealand after all) and for a third "horse pee on flowers!"

Para Cresyl Phenyl Acetate is the most floral of the para cresol esters and it is virtually indispensable when constructing a narcissus accord. It forms the fundamental animalic note in the famed Animalis base (our Animalia™ CMP) and is in countless elegant scents from history where a careful balance with other materials accentuates the florals and links the bestial facet to the natural animalics.

Para Cresyl Phenyl Acetate is a powder but it dissolves easily when blended pure into the remaining ingredients of your formula. However, should you wish to dissolve it for ease of use (both due to the physical form and the power of the odour) we have saved you the trouble and are offering it also at 10% in DPG.

products.name: Para Methyl Acetophenone
products.description:
This material is an accord in a bottle—hawthorn blossoms never yield natural oil, so this molecule gives you access to that dense spring-flower sweetness you can't extract. Its powdery almond-floral character defines hawthorn in perfumery. Use it to recreate what nature won't give up commercially.

Build realistic mimosa with its honeyed, powdery sweetness or add vintage warmth to compositions through its coumarin-hay facets. It bridges floral and fougère families beautifully, lending classic elegance that softens sharp edges. Pair with anisaldehyde for powerful hawthorn impact or blend with heliotropin to amplify powdery almond facets into full heliotrope territory.

Handle at dilution—evaluate at ten percent or lower as its strength overwhelms at full concentration. Combine with oakmoss and patchouli for classic chypre structures or use with benzyl formate for fresh green-clover lift. It performs exceptionally in soap where many delicate materials fail, delivering lasting floral character in challenging bases.

With acetophenone likely to be banned in the EU from 2027, this similar material is going to be in much higher demand. Para Methyl Acetophenone offers a superior alternative to Acetophenone—it delivers the same almond-cherry impact you need but wraps it in powdery floral warmth instead of harsh chemical sharpness. Where Acetophenone feels raw and solvent-like, Para Methy Acetophenone gives you that bite plus hawthorn sweetness and coumarin richness, so you're not jus

products.name: Para Tolyl Aldehyde
products.description:
Para Tolyl Aldehyde opens with an unmistakable burst of maraschino cherry, deeper and warmer than simple fruit esters. This potent cherry-almond fusion carries surprising phenolic depth that prevents sweetness from becoming cloying. The material's exceptional 120-hour substantivity transforms it from mere modifier to structural foundation.

Deploy this aldehyde to bridge volatile top notes with tenacious base materials in cherry compositions. Partner it with benzaldehyde for complete cherry evolution from bright opening to warm drydown. The material excels at lending fruity warmth to heliotrope accords when combined with heliotropin, creating richness impossible with single molecules.

Consider exploiting its dual nature in unexpected contexts beyond obvious fruit themes. Add traces to lilac bases for the elusive almond-hyacinth facet of natural blooms. Build gourmand marzipan effects by amplifying its inherent spicy-sweet character with vanillin and cinnamates.

We sell this pure and diluted to 50% in DPG with a touch of Oxynex® ST to help prevent oxidation and UV damage which can be a problem with Para Tolyl Aldehyde long term.

products.name: Paradise Molecule®
products.description:
The most desired material in perfumery today is the captive Paradisone® of Firmenich. Paradisone is the very heart of Hedione®. It offers room filling diffusion and a radiance unequalled… until now.

Fraterworks' Paradise Molecule is a blend that mimics the power and beauty of the Firmenich masterpiece and offers an alternative to Hedione and the members of its family.

Hedione® can be imagined as putting space between each molecule in a blend, thus causing diffusion (and the corollary of diminishing richness). On the other hand Paradise Molecule has the apparent effect of charging particles, thereby adding an almost impossible cloud of diffusion with no correlated loss of intensity.

Use the Paradise Molecule as a one for one replacer for Hedione® and Hedione® High Cis, or in blends with both. Effective from traces to overdose.

Keep in a cool dark place place when not in use to maintain its full two year shelf life.

products.name: Parmantheme
products.description:
Parmantheme opens with an unmistakable blast of Parma violet — green, leafy, almost cucumber-fresh on top, then quickly powdery and sweet. The ionone backbone gives it terrific projection. In dilution, it becomes beautifully soft and cosmetic.

This is a complete violet accord in a bottle. The green-waxy topnotes come from nonadienol and nonadienal components, while a generous ionone core provides the classic powdery body that defines violet in perfumery. Use it as a starting point for any violet-forward composition, or add traces to floral bouquets for an elegant powdery lift.

Parmantheme rewards restraint — try it at low levels in a chypre for subtle violet warmth, or push it harder in a standalone soliflore. Pair it with orris butter for added realism, or with musks and sandalwood for a vintage powdery effect. It dominates easily, so build around it rather than layering it in.

products.name: Parmentier Pyrazine
products.description:
Parmentier Pyrazine opens with unmistakable roasted character—nutty, coffee-like, and immediately evocative of foods transformed by heat. The burnt woody facets add complexity, while earthy potato notes provide the distinctive quality that earned this material its name (after Antoine-Augustin Parmentier, the French agronomist who championed the potato). Toasted cocoa and savoury broth undertones complete a profile that smells genuinely edible.

Work with Parmentier Pyrazine at high dilution—evaluate at 0.1% or less to appreciate its nuances without overwhelming your nose. Use it alongside other pyrazines like Grenoble, Praslin, and Torref to build complex roasted accords. The earthy-potato facet distinguishes it from purely nutty pyrazines, making it valuable in compositions where root vegetable warmth or cooked-food authenticity is desired. Excellent in gourmand, tobacco, and leather contexts.

This pyrazine is named after Antoine-Augustin Parmentier (1737–1813) who convinced the French to add potatoes to their diet by various clever marketing tricks such as having King Louis XVI wear potato flowers in his buttonhole.

Some Clever Uses

The Synthetic Oudh Base

Real Oudh oil has a "rot" and "fermented" quality that is very hard to fake. A trace of Parmentier Pyrazine combined with Castoreum and Cypriol creates an incredibly realistic "barnyard" Oudh effect. The earthy/potato note mimics the rotting wood of the Agar tree perfectly.

The "Dark" Chocolate

Most chocolate accord

products.name: Passifloran 1% DPG
products.description:
Unbelievably potent, we sell this at a usable 1% in DPG (previously at 0.1% so check your dose carefully). Passifloran is catty, buchu-like, tropical, fruity, sulphurous and vegetative. It is a profoundly good material for adding naturalness to fruit accords or even in traces as a passionfruit note in a fragrance. Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) calls this “one of the best tropical fruit ingredients every synthesized.”

Passifloran blends beautifully with Oxane, Magnificent Mandarin, Pomelo Grandis, Citrus oils and fruit notes.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Passion Fruit Base 109223
products.description:
Passion Fruit Base 109223 GEB opens like a spoonful of fresh tropical fruit puree. You get soft, rounded smoothness leaning toward kiwifruit, mango, and creamy peach rather than sharp passion fruit. Everything sits in a gentle milky haze that makes the impression plush and almost edible.

This base builds tropical accords instantly without sourcing a dozen individual components. It excels in modern fruity feminines where you want creamy, rounded fruit rather than sharp acidity. Dose carefully though; the full impact develops over a week and will sneak up on you.

Layer it with peach and apricot for stone fruit richness, or brighten with bergamot and lychee for a sparkling tropical opening. Add Oxane or Passifloran in traces to push the character toward authentic passion fruit tartness. At higher levels the kiwifruit facet becomes more pronounced.

products.name: Pastry Carbaldehyde
products.description:
Pastry Carbaldehyde (5-Methyl Furfural) opens with soft caramellic warmth that's gentler and more refined than furfural's harsh character. This extraordinarily powerful material captures the essence of heated sugars transforming into rich caramel, with prominent bready-brown notes of fresh pastry crust. The spicy roasted grain character carries subtle almond-cherry facets nuttier than benzaldehyde, adding unexpected depth.

You'll find Pastry Carbaldehyde invaluable for creating authentic caramelised effects in gourmand compositions. Use at 0.01-0.2% maximum where it provides the crucial "heated sugar" foundation beneath coffee, chocolate, and brown sugar accords. The material excels in tobacco themes where its roasted sweetness enhances leaf character, and in autumn concepts evoking harvest warmth.

The compound bridges sweet and savoury territories brilliantly - think maple bacon, roasted nuts, or rum-soaked fruitcake. Combine with coffee Arabica CO2 for enhanced roasted depth, maltol for sweeter caramel effects, or almond pyrazine for nuttier facets. Its natural occurrence in coffee, roast beef, and baked goods explains its authentic culinary warmth that synthetic sweeteners cannot replicate.

Difference from Furfural

While both are furan aldehydes born from sugar caramelisation, Pastry Carbaldehyde offers crucial advantages. Furfural brings harsh, bitter secondary notes and faces severe IFRA restrictions (0.001% skin contact). Pastry Carbaldehyde's methyl group creates a

products.name: Patchone
products.description:
Patchone has a dry, woody, distinctly patchouli-like character with a camphoraceous bite and subtle leathery warmth. It reads as the stripped-back, structural side of patchouli — the woody earthiness without the sweet, fruity top notes. A balsamic, pine-like quality rounds out the profile and keeps it from feeling too austere.

Use patchone as a patchouli modifier or replacement in your woody, oriental, and chypre compositions. It dries down floral notes effectively, adding structure and earthy depth. Combine it with richer patchouli materials to extend and sharpen the woody base of your accords.

Blend with patchouli oil and vetiver for a deep, earthy woody foundation. Try it alongside cedarwood and Iso E Super for a modern transparent woody base. Pair with rose and violet materials where its drying effect creates elegant contrast between floral sweetness and woody depth.

products.name: Patchouli Dark PA30
products.description:
This dark patchouli is a full-bodied oil with all the good and none of the bad that can be associated with patchouli oils. It has the most refined and sheer dry down we have ever experienced in an iron distilled patchouli. It is consistently good from top to bottom and for that reason it is our own go-to patchouli oil.

Despite patchouli being an earthy material, the less dirty the dry down the higher the prestige. This dark oil has a wonderfully smooth quality that lasts. We tested dark patchouli oils from all the major suppliers in France and Indonesia and even many artisanal manufacturers to offer you the very best dark patchouli. And every year we re-test to ensure we are keeping up with the latest qualities coming from those suppliers.

Patchouli is steam distilled using stainless steel or iron distilling units. Oil produced in a stainless steel vat is called “light” and it is the colour of pale straw. The classic iron distilled oil is dark (deep gold through orange to dark brown). The odour profile between the products is similar but the dark oil has a more complex and rich dry down.

Origin: Aceh, Indonesia
Part: Leaves

products.name: Patchouli Heart MD PA50
products.description:
The most sublime part of patchouli oil is the patchouli alcohol (patchoulol). A typical high quality patchouli will have at least 30% with some natural oils going considerably higher, such as our Patchouli Light Aceh with a whopping 38%.

Our Patchouli Heart from Floral Concept, one of the finest suppliers of luxury niche naturals in France, is the result of molecular distillation in which some of the unappealing side-notes are removed from the oil giving a significant boost to the patchoulol — fully half in fact.

Patchouli Heart MD PA50 is the scent of spring rains falling on freshly furrowed earth. It is the scent of winding rivers through dank woodlands. This patchouli is nature at its best.

NOTE: patchouli prices are currently on the rise due to political changes in Indonesia. We are doing our best to absorb some of that impact and there appear to be signs of stabilisation in the industry so we hope there will be no further increases.

Origin: Indonesia, processing France
Variety: Pogostemon cablin Benth.
Part: Leaves

products.name: Patchouli Heart N.3 PA60
products.description:
Patchouli Heart N.3 from LMR (Laboratoires Monique Remy) is a molecular distilled COSMOS certified patchouli oil and considered by many to the be the finest example of the type.

The patchoulol content of Patchouli Heart N.3 is guaranteed by the LMR lab to be between 52% and 59%, the highest amount found in any of our patchouli collection. This is one of two molecular distilled patchouli oils we offer, the other being Patchouli Heart MD PA50 from Floral Concept.

The Floral Concept product has a very soft and subtle opening with an earthy dry down, while this Patchouli Heart N.3 has a more characterful opening and a sweeter and creamier dry down. Both oils are wonderful and bring different nuances to a scent. We use and recommend both.

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

products.name: Patchouli Heart SFE
products.description:
Patchouli Heart SFE is a CO2 extract of dried patchouli leaves. Notably, it lacks sesquiterpenes— heavier, less fragrant molecules like caryophyllene or germacrene—which are typically present in steam-distilled oils. This removal enhances purity and creates a cleaner, more focused scent.

Patchouli Heart SFE evolves into a softer, more harmonious note, sometimes with minty undertones. The absence of sesquiterpenes reduces the raw, heavy earthiness, making it more versatile and elegant for modern perfumery.

products.name: Patchouli Light Aceh PA38
products.description:
This light patchouli oil from Aceh in Indonesia is so balanced that it's hard to believe it is not molecular distilled. Yet it is 100% pure and natural and still boasts a whopping 38% patchouli alcohol content (standard patchouli is usually 30% or lower).

Since the ancient days of the sultanate of Aceh, patchouli from this region has been revered and it was an item of trade with the English East India Company (along with black pepper) in its heyday. Aceh is to patchouli as Île de Bourbon is to geranium and Comoros to ylang-ylang.

Patchouli is steam distilled either using stainless steel or iron distilling units. Oil produced in a stainless steel vat is called “light” and it is the colour of pale straw. The classic iron distilled oil is dark (deep gold through orange to dark brown). The odour profile between the products is similar but in the long dry down the light oil is cleaner.

Despite being an earthy oil, the less dirty the dry down the higher the prestige. This light oil is naturally high in patchouli alcohol, the heart of the oil with virtually no dirty qualities, and so the oil has one of the sweetest and softest dry downs possible in a pure and natural patchouli oil.

For modern fragrances requiring a refined and regal patchouli note, this is the oil you need.

Origin: Aceh, Indonesia
Variety: Pogostemon cablin Benth.
Part: Leaves

products.name: Patchoulol Crystals PA99
products.description:
Patchoulol (patchouli alcohol) is the "coeur" element of patchouli oil. After trials and tests of products from all the major suppliers, the Ventos patchoulol comes out miles ahead. It has absolutely no off notes.

Small amounts can sweeten patchouli oil, while large overdoses can add a wonderfully novel new woody earthy character to a fragrance. 

This product is 100% natural according to ISO 9235 standards and can be used in all natural perfumes.

products.name: Patchoulyl Acetate
products.description:
A speciality of Ventos, Patchouli Oil Acetylated is a real treasure for those who love patchouli. It has a more intense and definitely sweeter profile than regular patchouli oil.

Its blends with the rose ketones are astonishingly good and it can be used with no limits under IFRA.

It can't be stressed enough that this is perhaps the most elegant of all the patchouli extracts and one we highly recommend.

products.name: Pear Belle
products.description:
Pear Belle is, as its name suggests, beautiful. It is the entire pear: flesh, skin and foliage. No pear base better represents the most beloved childhood fruit as this one from Fraterworks.

Pear Belle blends beautifully with gourmand notes and citrus, as well as patchouli and vanilla. It is used to great effect in Infanta by Frater Perfumes and it adds an touch of elegance in all uses.

“The pear tree was in full bloom, and its faint, sweet scent drifted through the open window, making her feel as if she were floating.” — Bliss (1918), Katherine Mansfield

products.name: Pear Ester
products.description:
Pear Ester, or ethyl decadienoate, smells like a ripe, juicy pear, with crisp green and fresh fruity notes. Its aroma is bright, diffusive, and perfect for adding energy to fragrances. Used mostly as a top-note booster, it works in fruity, floral, and even gourmand blends.

This ester doesn’t just smell like pear—it can also mimic other fruits, like tart quince or sweet apple, depending on the formula. Its versatility and natural feel make it a favourite for creating bold, modern fruit accords.

Pair it with bergamot or mandarin for a sharp, bright start. Add it to green galbanum materials for a fresher edge, or combine it with vanillin and caramel for a creamy, sweet finish. It shines in juicy-fruit mixes, working seamlessly with materials like cis-3-hexenyl acetate or benzyl acetate. Pear Ester is a powerful tool for any perfumer.

We recommend you keep Pear Ester at a cool, stable temperature, ideally below 25°C (77°F). Under those conditions it has a typical 2 year shelf life.

products.name: PEG 60 HCO
products.description:
PEG-60 hydrogenated castor oil is a non-ionic solubiliser that dissolves fragrance oils cleanly into water. The result is a crystal-clear solution — no cloudiness, no separation, no residue. It is essentially odourless, so your fragrance reads exactly as you intended.

The critical technique is premixing: blend PEG-60 HCO with your fragrance oil first at a 3:1 to 5:1 ratio, then add this premix slowly to water. Skipping this step produces cloudy, unstable solutions. Use it in room sprays, body mists, linen sprays, water-based perfumes, and micellar waters.

It arrives as a white wax that melts around 35°C — warm it gently to liquefy before measuring. Unlike polysorbate 20, it produces virtually no foam and has no detectable odour of its own. Always use distilled water and always add a preservative to water-based formulations.

This can also be used in regular alcohol fragrances as a texture enhancer.

Fraterworks makes no guarantees as to the suitability of this material for any purposes beyond its minor use in alcoholic fine fragrances.

products.name: Peomosa
products.description:
Peomosa opens with an impressively natural wet-petal aroma that captures flowers still glistening with morning dew. This distinctive green-cortex character immediately distinguishes it from traditional rose alcohols. You'll notice how it creates spatial dimension in florals, adding the waxy texture of real petals.

This material excels at bridging harsh top notes to creamy bases while maintaining transparency. Use it at 1-3% to add peony's characteristic dusty-powdery sweetness to any floral bouquet. A green freshness and subtle wet-earthy quality give this material its distinctive transparent, watery character that feels like petals just after rain.

Combine Peomosa with rose oxide for wet-petal realism, or blend with ionones for cosmetic powder effects. It has excellent compatibility with syringa aldehyde. Its medium strength allows generous dosing without overwhelming compositions. Apply it strategically when you need florals to feel alive rather than dried.

products.name: Peonile
products.description:
Peonile opens with an unmistakable burst of fresh geranium-rose lifted by zesty grapefruit nuances. This powerful nitrile delivers the rare combination of heart note character with base note tenacity. The distinctive metallic clarity that defines nitriles adds modern brightness, preventing the floralcy from feeling dated or heavy.

You'll find Peonile invaluable for creating harmony in complex floral accords where other materials clash. Use it at 1-10% to smooth aggressive florals into seamless bouquets while adding exceptional volume and fixation. Its legendary stability across pH 2-11 and five-star substantivity on both wet and dry fabric makes it irreplaceable in functional fragrances.

The material's linear performance means its rosy-citrus character persists unchanged through a month-long drydown. Combine with Javanol at 80:20 for the famous "rich sandalwood" synergy. Build modern fougères around its stable geranium core, or use its grapefruit facet to extend volatile citrus compositions.

Despite its name, Peonile is not particularly peony like.

products.name: Peony Storm
products.description:
Peony (known as pivoine in French) is one of the most beautiful flowers to behold, from bud to blossom. The delicate odour is reminiscent of roses (indeed most classic peony bases rely on many of the same aroma chemicals) with the key difference being a lightly waxed quality and a faintly almond-like persistence to the peony blossom.

As with all our luxurious classical perfumery bases, Peony Storm is loaded with opulent and expensive essential oils and absolutes giving it a truly marvellous natural quality.

Peony flowers don't give up a natural essential oil, but with a base as rich and appealing as Peony Storm, it simply doesn't matter.

products.name: Peppermint Oil “Black Mitcham”
products.description:
Peppermint oil is one of the most abused and adulterated oils in the fragrance industry, with large quantities of the most common oils (Indian and American) really being cornmint that has been stripped of menthol for the pharmaceutical industry. True French oil is the standard bearer of quality. But there is one other peppermint on the market that blows even the French out of the water: fine aged Peppermint Oil “Black Mitcham” indigenous to England and, after a period of extinction from those green isles, restored to its glory in recent years.

Pining for the superior peppermint oil of his youth, Sir Michael Colman (of the Colman's Mustard family) sought out, discovered in far distant America, and restored this glorious plant to its native land where it has now thrived across generations.

The black mitchan oil that we stock at Fraterworks is the very oil from Sir Michael's family estate in England. The Colman family produce the oil and age it for two years ensuring utter perfection.

Dating back to the 1750s, Peppermint oil "Black Mitcham" is the supreme peppermint. It is the peppermint of candy canes, peppermint creams, and all things wonderfully Wonka. In a side by side comparison with finest French peppermint oil, Black Mitcham is distinctly gourmand. It has a sweetness and even a subtle floralcy that is lacking in the French. Additionally, due to the aging the oil undergoes, the penetrating top notes common to oils of the mentha piperita family are tempered, allowing the

products.name: Peranat
products.description:
Peranat delivers one of the most convincingly natural pear notes available. The aroma is clean, sweet, and unmistakably pear-like, with subtle floral undertones that hint at jasmine and a faint woody-orris quality in the drydown. It reads as genuinely fruity rather than synthetic or candy-like.

Use peranat to add realistic pear character to your fresh and fruity-floral compositions. It pairs naturally with white florals — freesia, lily of the valley, peony — where its clean fruitiness brightens the heart. Combined with bergamot it creates sparkling citrus-fruit openings that feel contemporary and sophisticated.

Blend with other pear materials for a layered, multidimensional fruit effect. Try it alongside sandalwood and cedarwood where its fruity sweetness creates an elegant contrast against warm wood. Pair with hedione and muguet bases for the kind of fresh fruity-floral accords that typify modern feminine perfumery.

products.name: Perfumer Consultancy
products.description:
Harness the mastery of Fraterworks’ founder and chief perfumer in a format that suits your goal—whether you require a swift course-correction or a deeper strategic partnership. Upon purchase you will receive an instant, secure online Non-Disclosure Agreement; once signed, we proceed without delay.

products.name: Periploca Root Oil 10% TEC
products.description:
Periploca opens with an unexpected flash of green cucumber before settling into warm, vanillic-almond territory. Think rice milk, toasted marzipan, and cream soda — not straight vanilla but something more complex and interesting. Soft floral facets of heliotrope and mimosa hover in the background.

This oil is solid at room temperature, so it comes diluted to ten percent in triethyl citrate. Even diluted, it quietly takes over blends during maceration — dose with real restraint and revisit after several weeks. Use it to add natural vanillic depth to gourmand and oriental accords.

Blend with tonka bean and benzoin to amplify the gourmand warmth, or layer beneath white florals for an almond-blossom effect. It also pairs unexpectedly well with vetiver and tobacco. This is not a vanilla substitute — it is something richer and stranger.

products.name: Permawood™
products.description:
Permawood™ is a high-performance wood base which is effective from traces but is perfectly suitable for uses up to five percent. It is a top to bottom blend which adds body and strength to the heart of a scent, a luxurious ambery dry down, and a softening and rounding polish to top notes.

Permawood™ is composed of extremely modern aroma molcules with a very delicate odour which belies its astonishing power. Permawood™ is all about radiance, rounding and fixing. This is a base which will improve any fragrance to which it is added.

Permawood™ can be used as a one-for-one replacer for Fixobois® which has undergone reformulation in recent times.

Ambrox DL (EC 942-754-1) and Cetalox (EC 701-326-2) Update: This product contains Ambrox DL or Cetalox. As a result of recent testing, Firmenich has updated the hazards of those two materials to a new hazard category − Reproductive Toxicant Category 2 - H361d: Suspected of damaging the unborn child.

Permawood™ is the perfect fixative for Lorysia®, and Iso E Super™, and has a synergy with Miraclewood™, Thujopsene, Ambrexol™, Ambergris, Saxon Moss, Suralette™ Extra, Verdantol™ and woody, herbal or green notes in general.

products.name: Persian Lime Oil, FCF
products.description:
While the most common lime oil in perfumery is distilled Mexican lime, this Persian Lime (ex Mexico) is expressed (cold pressed), giving a truer and more complex lime impression. Additionally, this LMR speciality is rectified to reduce the harmful furoucoumarins making it a really great alternative to the safe distilled oil without losing parts of the lime profile.

Cold pressed lime retains the most natural, zesty, and vibrant aroma of the lime peel. Due to the risk of oxidation over the long term, a touch of BHT or Tocopherol (less than 0.1%) is recommended if you plan to store this oil. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight.

This is a lovely and rare lime oil and one that all perfumers should try, even if you already have the distilled oil.

Note: this contains 0.1% tocopherol as a preservative, added by LMR at the source.

products.name: Persicol
products.description:
Persicol is one of the most famous classical bases, being first used in Nuit de Chine (1913—formula below) by Maurice Schaller for Paul Poiret's Les Parfums de Rosine, but most famously ten years later as the key peach note at 0.4% pure in Mitsouko (1919) by Jacques Guerlain. It also featured in Bois des Îles by Ernest Beaux for Chanel with 4% Ambre Solide.

Contrary to popular belief, Persicol (created by Chuit Naef & Cie) is not a synonym for the chemical undecalactone gamma (so-called Aldehyde C-14) which was patented in 1908 but an achingly sweet peach base featuring that chemical to exploit and demonstrate its commercial uses to perfumers of the day, just as De Laire created Mousse de Saxe to market the then recently discovered chemical isobutyl quinoline.

Persicol is used in the same way as undecalactone gamma and can be used as a one for one replacer.

products.name: Peru Balsam Essential Oil
products.description:
Peru Balsam Essential Oil opens with a remarkably different character than its resinoid sibling—where the resinoid overwhelms with dense vanilla sweetness, the steam-distilled oil whispers amber sophistication. This clear, pale gold liquid captures the ethereal aspects of the crude balsam while leaving behind the heavier, potentially problematic components. The result is a more transparent balsamic note that allows perfumers to build nuanced amber accords without the overwhelming darkness and viscosity of traditional extracts.

Use this essential oil at 0.4-2% when you need the characteristic Peru Balsam warmth but require regulatory compliance and formulation flexibility. Unlike the banned crude balsam or rich resinoid, the essential oil offers greater freedom while maintaining exceptional fixative properties. Its lighter character makes it invaluable for modern transparent formulations where the resinoid's dark colour would be problematic—think clear serums, light-coloured creams, or minimalist alcoholic fragrances demanding visual clarity.

The practical advantages of Peru Balsam Essential Oil extend beyond compliance into creative territory previously inaccessible with traditional forms. Its reduced vanillin content allows you to control sweetness precisely by adding vanillin or ethyl vanillin to taste, while its cleaner profile integrates seamlessly with delicate florals that might be overwhelmed by the resinoid's intensity. Combine it with benzoin and labdanum for class
tags: Locale:Thin oil not resin or absolute

products.name: Peru Balsam “Signature” Resinoid
products.description:
Peru balsam resinoid is a wonderfully sweet and complex exudate from myroxylon balsamum trees which have been intentionally scarred with cuts and burns to promote the outpouring of the healing raw gum. This exudate, or drug, is collected via cotton cloths which are pressed to the weeping trunk of the tree. Once removed from the clothes, the balsam is washed and made into a resinoid via ethanol or other solvent extractions to produce the IFRA safe product we stock.

Peru balsam has a strongly vanilla quality and could be said to have the odiferous properties of a blend of vanilla absolute, benzoin resinoid and styrax resinoid. It is sweet, resinous, leathery, cinnamyl and powdery.

Peru balsam resinoid is of a viscous but pourable consistency so we sell it pure. Note that this is the rare deep brown resinoid and not the clear essential oil, an entirely different product.

Origin: El Salvador
Variety: Myroxylon Balsamum L. var pereirae Klotzsch
Part: Exudate from tree bark
Method of production: Solvent extraction

products.name: Petalux
products.description:
Petalux, a replacer for Givaudan's captive Petalia, opens with an airy burst of rose petals dusted with lychee sweetness. The peony character emerges soft and dewy, rounded by delicate muguet transparency. This is modern florality at its most radiant—fresh, clean, and effortlessly pretty.

Build your floral hearts around this material for immediate lift and diffusion. It brings a contemporary, juicy quality to classic rose accords without heaviness. Pair it with citrus top notes to amplify freshness, or layer with musks to extend its soft glow into the drydown.

Use Petalux at twice the dosage of Givaudan's Petalia when reformulating. Combine with hedione for enhanced radiance or phenylethyl alcohol for richer rose depth. Try it alongside fruity notes like cassis or raspberry to exploit its lychee facet.

products.name: Petitgrain Bergamotier Oil
products.description:
Petitgrain bergamotier is produced by steam distilling the foliage from bergamot trees. This is a wonderful material to add interest and lift to a fragrance. It blends exceedingly well with other members of the citrus family which it modifies and extends, most especially bergamot, lemon and sweet orange. Try it with our Lemon Verbena and Suralette Extra.

Petitgrain bergamotier was a part of the petitgrain fond in the original Green Irish Tweed by Creed (see our demo formula Tartan Dream below) where it was blended with petitgrain paraguay and petitgrain citronnier (from the lemon tree).

Origin: Italy
Variety: Citrus bergamia risso
Part: Leaves and branches
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Petitgrain Bigarade Oil
products.description:
Petitgrain Bigarade is the extraction of the foliage from bitter orange trees (the fruit of which is used for classic Seville orange marmalade). Of all the petitgrain oils, this is probably the most widely used for fine fragrance.

This oil is extracted exclusively from the bitter orange tree making it the finest type, different from the lower quality so-called “Bigarade (Paraguay)” variants that flood the market. Petitgrain Paraguay is extracted from hybrid trees which cross the bitter orange with sweet (or other) varieties. Pure Petitgrain Bigarade is much more rare and considerably more beautiful.

Origin: Italy
Part: Foliage
Method: Steam distilled at source

products.name: Petitgrain Citronnier Oil
products.description:
Petitgrain oil citronnier is produced by steam distilling the foliage from lemon trees. Less common than bigarade petitigrain (from bitter orange), this is a wonderful material to add interest and lift to a fragrance. It blends exceedingly well with other members of the citrus family which it modifies and extends, most especially lemon, lime and cedrat. Try it with our Lemon Verbena and Verdantol.

Petitgrain citronnier was a vital part of the petitgrain fond in the original Green Irish Tweed by Creed (see our demo formula Tartan Dream below) where it was blended with petitgrain paraguay and petitgrain bergamotier (from the bergamot tree).

Origin: Italy
Part: Leaves and branches
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Petitgrain Mandarinier Oil
products.description:
The most unusual and intense of the petitgrain oils, Mandarin petitgrain is green, dusty and incredibly complex. It can be a great asset when wanting to add natural earthiness to a melange of citrus notes or to help soften the chemical nature of loved top notes like Dihydromyrcenol.

Of interest is the fact the Petitgrain Mandarinier can contain up to 50% natural dimethyl anthranilate which is restricted by the DEA in the US so this oil is one way to incorporate that material without having to worry about problems with customs.

Origin: Italy
Part: Foliage
Method: Steam Distilled at source

products.name: Petitgrain Oil Terpeneless
products.description:
This LMR produced petitgrain oil terpeneless (Petitgrain Oil Tpls.) is hands-down the finest example of the material we have ever experienced. It isn't just slightly better — it is leaps and bounds ahead of the competition. This is so good it could pass for neroli oil with just a few small tweaks.

W. A. Poucher uses this formula to convert Petitgrain Oil Tpls. into a neroli substitute with just four materials:

800g Petitgrain Oil Tpls.
100 Nerol Extra
90 Neroli Oil Tunisia
10 Aldehyde C-10, 10% in Petitgrain Oil Tpls.

This deterpinated oil consists mainly of linalool, alpha-terpineol, linalyl acetate, geraniol, nerol and their esters.

Petitgrain oil terpeneless finds use in all manner of fragrances but it is especially useful in heavy oriental types where it can convey a wonderful freshness in the midst of rich resins and sweet materials.

Origin: Paraguay
Variety: Citrus aurantium L.
Part: Leaves and branches
Method: Hydro distillation followed by rectification

products.name: Petitgrain Paraguay
products.description:
Petitgrain Paraguay is the most common and, in the words of Steffen Arctander, the "most important by far of all the petitgrain oils." It is distilled exclusively from the bitter-sour variety of the orange tree (Citrus Aurantium), while Petitgrain Bigarade is made from the true Bitter orange tree (Citus Aurantium, Amara).

In terms of the difference in odour and use, Petitgrain Paraguay is more fleeting and fresh while Petitgrain Bigarade has a slightly waxier and more woody quality. For slightly superior solubility and a longer lasting dry down we also have LMR's marvellous Petitgrain Paraguay Terpeneless.

Petitgrain Paraguay blends well with orange bases such as Orange Blossom Supreme, Neroli Supreme, Floranol, Fleur d'Oranger and aroma chemicals such as Theaspirane, Nerolin (Yara Yara and Bromelia), Oranger Crystals and Coumarone.

Origin: Paraguay
Part: Foliage
Method: Steam distilled at source

products.name: Pharaone 10% DPG
products.description:
Pharaone (only commercially available at 10%) opens with a searing burst of green pineapple rind - not the sweet pulp, but the tart, aromatic skin. Underneath, you'll catch tomato-leaf herbal warmth and a galbanum-like metallic edge. In dilution, gentler facets of tropical orchid and hyacinth emerge alongside a faint ozonic shimmer.

This is a structural powerhouse that punches far above its weight. Use it at trace levels to inject transparent, living greenness into citrus and floral accords without the heaviness of older resinous green materials. Pair it with Spirogalbanone for a linear green effect that lasts from top note right through to the drydown, or blend with Stemone to recreate a convincing crushed tomato-leaf accord.

Try Pharaone in masculine fougères where you want energetic freshness instead of traditional herbal notes. It extends the life of volatile citrus oils like bergamot and lemon, and at very low doses it adds a crisp, photorealistic edge to fruit accords. Overdose it and you'll land in vegetable-metallic territory - so keep your hand light.

products.name: Phenoxanol®
products.description:
Phenoxanol stands in for rose absolute when rose absolute is too costly to use in large doses. It is a rich and long lasting heart note with similarities to Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol. 

Cécile Zarokian uses it in a megadose in her Rose Aqor (2021) attar for Amouage (formula below) to contribute the main rose note in addition to a selection of high powered synthetics and it is also a key rose note in Gris by Dior.

Phenoxanol has a strong yet refined character which allows for the creation of fragrances with remarkable radiance and persistence. It is one of those chemicals that contributes a highly appealing quality to perfumes and certainly should be exploited far more often because of it.

products.name: Phenoxy Ethyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
Phenoxy Ethyl Isobutyrate is a sheer fruity material with nuances of honey, green leaves and rose. It is very long lasting, remaining more than seven days on a smelling strip so it is an extremely good product for extending the life of fruit accords, particularly plum (it makes up nearly forty percent of the great Prunella® plum base of Firmenich in fact).

Not surprisingly its blends with Persicol and Wild Cherry are supreme, but as a floral nuancer it works wonders with the classic rose materials, particularly Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol. Try it with Zanzibar Clovebud, Ceylon Cinnamon and the rose ketones for a delightful apple pie filling, or combine it with a touch of Theaspirane to mimic the scent of tea soaked prunes.

products.name: Phenyl Acetaldehyde 50% PEA
products.description:
Phenyl Acetaldehyde opens with overwhelming power—an almost aggressive blast of pure hyacinth that can momentarily stun the nose with its intensity. This isn't a gentle floral; it's the sharp, watery greenness of spring flowers with their stems freshly cut, leaves crushed, and petals still dewy. The aldehyde delivers not just flower but the entire plant experience: green calyx, watercress-like leafiness, and that distinctive "flower shop" humidity that makes florals feel alive rather than merely pretty.

Use Phenyl Acetaldehyde with extreme caution—typically at 0.01-0.3% in finished products. Its power demands respect: overdose creates harsh chemical notes that destroy compositions. Use it in traces to add authentic spring flower character to hyacinth, lilac, and lily of the valley accords. In rose compositions, minute amounts provide crucial dewy freshness that prevents jammy sweetness. For creating "living flower" effects, combine with other green materials like cis-3-hexenol for complete vegetative authenticity. The teensiest trace of skatole can completely naturalise this material and take your scent into a whole new level of naturalness.

The unique practice of selling Phenyl Acetaldehyde at 50% in Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol rather than standard diluents reveals sophisticated chemistry at work. Unlike stable materials diluted in DPG or TEC for convenience, this aldehyde requires PEA's protective embrace to prevent rapid polymerisation that would destroy its character. PEA acts

products.name: Phenyl Acetic Acid 40% DPG
products.description:
Phenyl Acetic Acid is one of the finest materials for introducing a sweet honey note to fragrances. It is a perfect material for adding the characteristic miel note desired in Rose D'Orient type bases.

Phenyl Acetic Acid has shades of civet, powder, honeysuckle (chèvrefeuille), chocolate and tobacco.

Due to DEA requirements in the USA we sell this at 40% dilution only. 

Note: This product contains a diluted form of a regulated chemical and is sold in accordance with NZ regulations. Not for synthesis or diversion.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Acetate
products.description:
This material opens with an immediate sweetness that rounds sharp floral edges while adding body to rose accords. You'll find its honeyed character transforms simple compositions into complex bouquets. The fruity-peach facets emerge as it develops, creating natural depth without synthetic harshness.

Use phenyl ethyl acetate to soften phenylethyl alcohol's sharper notes in rose reconstructions, where it provides the jammy sweetness of petals at full bloom. Combine it with citronellol and geraniol for authentic rose accords, or pair with coumarin and heliotropine for powdery florientals. The material accepts remarkably high dosages—up to 50% in functional applications—making it invaluable when you need quality fragrance at commercial scale.

Apply this versatile ester from trace amounts for subtle dewy freshness to dominant themes in cost-effective formulations. Its exceptional stability and pleasant character work equally well in fine fragrance heart notes at 1-10% or as a structural foundation in soaps and detergents. You'll discover its true power when blending with modern materials like rosetone, where it tempers intensity while maintaining radiance.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol
products.description:
Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol is the main material used for reconstructions of rose. On its own it paints a picture of dried red roses, but in combination with the other rose alcohols (geraniol, nerol, and citronellol) an entire bloom emerges. Add cinnamic nuances, greenness and honey notes and you begin to paint the full picture of a wild rose, foliage and all. 

Our Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol is direct from Firmenich and unlike generic PEA, this is full of life with more intense and interesting nuances of honey, cinnamon and green floralcy. A true gem.

According to Arctander, “This material enters perfume compositions at the rate of 5-10-20% or sometimes much more. Its low cost, versatility and general acceptability on odor, its excellent stability are factors speaking strongly in favour of this otherwise relatively weak odourant. However, its odor is clearly demonstrated in an experiment with an apparently weak crystalline fixative/odourant, such as [rose crystals]. With 5% of the crystalline material, Phenyl ethyl alcohol will smell not only much more rosy, it will last much longer, and its 'rough' topnotes are pleasantly subdued, it has 'three dimensions' instead of two.

“But it is in the 'everyday' perfumery that the subject alcohol is most appreciated. It is almost never 'out of place' in a composition, be it floral, balsamic, Oriental, mossy, herbaceous or 'modern-aldehydic'. It is an inevitable companion to the 'rose alcohols', Citronellol, Geraniol, Nerol, Dimethyl octanol [tetr

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol ex Rose
products.description:
This is the most beautiful phenyl ethyl alcohol (PEA) you will experience as a perfumer. And, unsurprisingly, the most expensive. Extracted solely from roses, this natural isolate is the building block you need to create the most profound of perfumes. It needs to be paired with similarly luxurious materials—Rhodinol ex Geranium, Cinnamic Alcohol ex Styrax, Cyclosia, and so on. Just imagine the rose accord you can blend with this incredibly material as its heart.

The complexity of this product is such that it can pass as a replacement for rose oil!

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Natural
products.description:
Highly sought after, this is 100% natural Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol produced by Biotech (AKA Novorate Biotech) in China. It is EU and US natural and is the gold standard of this natural rose alcohol.

In their own words: “Natural Phenethyl Alcohol (EU Standard, 99.9%) is [Biotech′s] first industrialized natural product. Our product, obtained by biotransformation of natural amino acid using yeast, has been confirmed natural by Eurofins Scientific. Cross-contamination is avoided through a unique production process consisting of a computer-controlled fermentation system, centrifugation, concentration, and rectification. Each unit in the line is fabricated from stainless steel in compliance with the hygiene requirements for food-grade products.”

Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol is the main material used for reconstructions of rose. On its own it hints of red roses, but in combination with the other rose alcohols (geraniol, nerol, and citronellol) an entire bloom emerges. Add cinnamic nuances, greenness and honey notes and you begin to see the full picture of a wild rose, foliage and all.
