products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Butyrate
products.description:
Phenyl ethyl butyrate takes the familiar rose character of phenylethyl alcohol and pushes it somewhere heavier, sweeter, and more fruit-forward. You get warm, honeyed rose with a rich, slightly fermented quality — dried plum, stone fruit, and a buttery depth. This is rose with real body and weight.

Use phenyl ethyl butyrate to add warmth and fruity richness to your rose accords. It fills the gap between clean synthetic rose and the heavy sweetness of natural rose absolute. In honey and beeswax accords it contributes a floral-fruity dimension that reinforces the naturalistic effect.

Blend with rose absolute and damascone for a multidimensional rose heart. Try it alongside gamma-undecalactone and vanilla for a rosy gourmand effect. Pair with champaca and ylang ylang where its heavy floral-fruit character adds depth and exoticism.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Phenethyl Cinnamate presents a distinctive olfactory profile, characterised by rich, balsamic warmth, complemented by sweet, rosy nuances, subtle spicy undertones, and gentle hints of honey, vanilla, and green foliage. This complex, multifaceted aroma provides depth and enduring warmth, making it a prized ingredient within the perfumer's palette.

Phenethyl Cinnamate serves prominently as a base note and effective fixative, enhancing the longevity and richness of floral and oriental fragrances. It excels in harmonising compositions, imparting volume and body, while specifically boosting the persistence and presence of delicate floral notes such as rose, lilac, and gardenia.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Formate
products.description:
Phenyl ethyl formate opens with a bright green flash—watercress and chrysanthemum leaves—before settling into a warm, rosy-floral heart with unmistakable hyacinth character. There is a dry, slightly spicy-cinnamic edge that gives the material real personality. The effect is clean, fresh, and immediately recognisable as something botanical and alive.

This is a classic modifier that deserves far more attention than it currently gets. It excels in hyacinth accords at higher doses, but try it at lower levels in muguet, orchid, lilac, and narcissus bases where its green-rosy freshness lifts the entire composition. The warm cinnamic undertone makes it surprisingly useful in spicy florals too.

Pair phenyl ethyl formate with phenyl ethyl alcohol for a rounded rose effect, or with galbanum and violet leaf for sharp green-floral contrasts. Keep your stock dry and cool—if moisture or free formic acid creeps in, the material deteriorates fast and turns pungent. A well-stored bottle, however, keeps beautifully and rewards you with crisp, natural freshness every time.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Isobutyrate
products.description:
Phenyl ethyl isobutyrate opens with a beautiful rosy-floral character enriched by honey sweetness. The fruity pear facet adds freshness without becoming juvenile, while a subtle winey quality provides sophistication. This ester delivers warmth and roundness that feels natural and approachable—never synthetic or harsh.

Blend phenyl ethyl isobutyrate with phenethyl alcohol and geraniol to build complex rose effects. It pairs excellently with ionones, adding warmth to violet-rose hybrids. Try it alongside honey materials like ethyl phenyl acetate for gourmand florals, or with balsams where its fruity sweetness creates unexpected depth.

Phenyl Ethyl vs Phenoxy Ethyl Isobutyrate

These two esters share superficial similarities but differ meaningfully in character. Phenyl ethyl isobutyrate (CAS 103-48-0) emphasises the rosy-floral aspect with honey warmth and a winey sophistication—it's the more classically floral choice.

Phenoxy ethyl isobutyrate (CAS 103-60-6) leans greener and more tropical, with apple and exotic fruit facets that feel fresher and more contemporary. The phenoxy variant offers slightly longer substantivity at 184 hours and projects with a brighter, more diffusive quality. Choose phenyl ethyl for traditional rose and oriental work; reach for phenoxy ethyl when you want green-tropical lift in modern fruity florals.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Phenyl Acetate
products.description:
Phenyl Ethyl Phenyl Acetate (PEPA) is a rich honeyed aroma chemical with a light sprinkling of tea rose, apricots, hyacinth and cinnamon. It has great potential as a core blender in a modern carnation base but historically finds use in Lilac, Rose and miel accords.

Phenyl Ethyl Phenyl Acetate is usually found in small amounts as a nuancer but it is not unheard of for it to be used in a semi-overdosed state for special cases (particularly honey bases).

Phenyl Ethyl Phenyl Acetate blends with Rose materials, Vanillin, Eugenol, and Dianthine Extra.

We are also offering this as a 40% solution with DPG.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Pivalate
products.description:
Phenyl Ethyl Pivalate opens with immediate distinction from typical rose esters—this isn't grandmother's rose. Tea-rose delicacy mingles with unexpected berry fruitiness. The bulky pivalate group creates unique dewy freshness, as if rose petals were sprinkled with morning moisture and crushed berries.

This ester's structural complexity delivers multifaceted performance where simpler esters provide single notes. Deploy it for contemporary rose interpretations that demand more than honeyed sweetness. The material bridges floral and fruity families effortlessly, creating accords that feel both sophisticated and accessible—perfect for modern consumers seeking familiar-yet-distinctive signatures.

Work with this treasure at 0.5-3% to exploit its exceptional stability in alkaline conditions. Where phenyl ethyl acetate degrades in soap, pivalate persists brilliantly. Combine with Peonile for ultra-modern rosewater effects, or pair with aquatic molecules for innovative marine-floral fusions. The 40-hour substantivity ensures your rose blooms from top through heart.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Propionate
products.description:
Phenyl Ethyl Propionate opens with immediate sweet floralcy—not just any rose, but the rich, velvety character of red rose petals warmed by sunlight. This primary floral impression quickly reveals sophisticated complexity: deep fruity notes suggesting berries and stone fruits merge with distinct honeyed sweetness. The material's warmth comes not from spice but from its inherent balsamic-herbaceous undertones, creating a naturalistic depth that prevents it from reading as simple or one-dimensional.

Phenyl Ethyl Propionate is excellent at 0.5-20% when you need to add warmth and sweetness to floral compositions without sacrificing sophistication. Its remarkable blending properties make it invaluable for smoothing transitions between notes—use it to bridge sharp florals with rich base notes seamlessly. In rose accords, it amplifies and enriches rather than dominates, adding the fruity-honeyed facets that transform a basic rose into something luxurious. For Oriental compositions, its balsamic warmth and moderate tenacity provide essential support through the heart notes.

Making Sense of Esters

Understanding the differences between phenyl ethyl esters transforms your formulation approach entirely. The propionate (C3) delivers warm, fruity-honeyed rose with excellent balance and moderate tenacity. The acetate (C2) presents brighter, more volatile rose with green-fresh facets ideal for top notes. The formate (C1) offers sharp, fresh rose with aldehydic brightness but fleeting pres

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Salicylate
products.description:
Phenyl Ethyl Salicylate opens with gentle balsamic-floral character—sweet, soft, and quietly elegant. Rose facets emerge alongside fresh hyacinth brightness, while a subtle carnation spiciness adds complexity. The mild medicinal undertone characteristic of salicylates remains refined rather than intrusive, creating a smooth, polished effect.

This material transforms rose accords from simple prettiness into sophisticated depth. Combine it with phenethyl alcohol to extend rose's life on skin, creating that precious moment when fresh petals transition to potpourri richness. In hyacinth reconstructions, it provides the essential balsamic body that grounds the sharp green aspects of phenylacetaldehyde. The magic happens when you pair it with gamma-nonalactone—suddenly your coconut shifts from tropical drink to sophisticated sunscreen accord, that coveted "warm skin by the pool" effect modern perfumery craves.

Work it at 2-5% in floral hearts for seamless blending, or push it to 10% in oriental bases where you need serious fixation. Remember this material builds texture rather than providing standalone character—overdosing creates a flat, soapy wall that kills sparkle.

products.name: Phenyl Ethyl Tiglate
products.description:
Dark, green, herbal and floral, Phenyl Ethyl Tiglate is like smelling a preserved and polished dark red rose. It is a wonderful nuancer for rose bases and also works extremely well in hyacinth compositions owing to its green and balsamic qualities.

Phenyl Ethyl Tiglate blends very well with Amazonia™ and chemicals Cascalone and Calone Plus. Use it to add nuance to our lovely rose bases or blend it with Pineapple Supreme or Pear Belle.

products.name: Phenyl Propyl Alcohol
products.description:
Phenyl propyl alcohol opens with a warm, honeyed sweetness that immediately recalls old-fashioned garden peonies in full bloom. A soft cinnamic-balsamic quality sits beneath the floral heart, giving it a richness that sets it apart from sharper floral alcohols. The drydown is clean, gently powdery, and lingers quietly for days.

This is one of those rare materials that improves almost everything it touches. Add it to rose bases for balsamic warmth, to hyacinth and lilac accords for body and naturalness, or to oriental compositions for smooth floral sweetness. It rounds off rough synthetic edges without drawing attention to itself—think of it as the warm undertone you always felt was missing.

Blend phenyl propyl alcohol with cinnamyl alcohol and phenyl ethyl alcohol for layered floral depth. It pairs beautifully with geraniol in rose work and with styrax or Peru balsam in oriental bases. Unrestricted and stable across most applications, it performs well in everything from fine fragrance to soap and candles.

products.name: Phenyl Propyl Cinnamate
products.description:
Phenyl propyl cinnamate smells of soft roses wrapped in warm balsam, with a delicate apricot sweetness underneath. It is mild at first impression but builds in richness over time. This is one of those materials that defines the character of classic oriental perfumery.

It occurs naturally in Peru balsam, storax, and benzoin — the great balsamic resins — and carries their warm, enveloping quality in a pure, controllable form. Use it as a fixative in oriental and rose bases, where it adds tenacity and a sweet, rosy depth that lasts over 400 hours on a blotter.

Pair it with ionones and methyl ionones for rich floral compositions, with benzoin and labdanum for full oriental warmth, or with mimosa absolute for a sweet, powdery, golden effect. Work from dilution — a small amount transforms a formula's base without announcing its presence.

products.name: Piconia
products.description:
Piconia is a diffusive and lively chemical that is not at all as widespread as it should be! Think of it as a patchouli and pipe tobacco radiant with dank vetiver elements. It is earthy, forest-like, fresh and has an interesting power in both top and base notes. A touch of Piconia can really give lift to a scent. 

Piconia is usually used pure and while you can use a fairly hefty dose, it is more commonly seen in the 0.1-2% range. Piconia may contain a trace of butylated hydroxytoluene as a preservative. That is added by IFF directly and not Fraterworks. Fortifying chemicals in this way is common in the industry and should pose no problems.

Piconia is synthesised from the same starting material (isolongiopolene) as some other great chemicals, notably Symroxane, Ysamber, Ambermax and Folenox.

Piconia blends marvellously with Ethyl Linalool, Linalool, Coranol, Dihyhdromyrcenol, Dimetol, Citrus and green bases like Amazonia and Verdantol. And of course it is a masterful modifier of patchouli naturals and members of the Clearwood family.

products.name: Pine Needle Oil, Sylvestris
products.description:
This is the reference standard for dry, airy coniferous freshness—distinct from the jammy sweetness of firs or the camphoraceous weight of spruces. The opening hits with a sharp terpenic bite that quickly softens into something sparkling and almost citrus-like. You'll find none of the cloying balsamic density that makes cheaper pine materials smell like floor cleaner.

What makes Pinus sylvestris so valuable is its remarkably low bornyl acetate content compared to other conifers. This gives you a transparent, austere character that lifts rather than smothers your compositions. Pair it with bergamot or grapefruit to extend citrus longevity; the shared bitter-fresh quality creates a seamless bridge. In fougères, it acts as a vertical pillar connecting lavender's herbal top with oakmoss's earthy base.

Use this oil sparingly in your heart notes—its medium diffusion power punches above its weight. Blend with frankincense to create modern incense accords stripped of musty church associations. Combine with labdanum for a "sun-baked forest" effect, or with juniper berry for ultra-dry gin-like freshness in masculine colognes.

products.name: Pine Oil, Cembra
products.description:
Pine oil cembra is unlike any other pine oil you have encountered. Where Scots pine is sharp and turpentine-like, this Alpine species opens soft, sweet, and balsamic with a gentle coniferous freshness. A velvety warmth sets it apart — refined where other pines are rough.

Use it to build forest accords, Alpine compositions, and coniferous elements in fougères and colognes. Its sweetness makes it more versatile in fine fragrance than harsher pine oils — it sits comfortably alongside bergamot, lavender, and cedarwood. The balsamic undertone blends naturally with labdanum, frankincense, and oakmoss.

Longevity is the trade-off — like most pine oils, the coniferous top fades within hours. Extend it with isobornyl acetate, Iso E Super, or ambroxan to anchor the pine character into the drydown. Pinus cembra is the Zirbe of Austrian tradition, distilled from trees that grow above the Alpine timberline.

products.name: Pineapple Natpop™
products.description:
V. MANE Fils is one of our favourite suppliers of naturals, but they are also (like Fraterworks) makers of some truly wonderful bases. Pineapple Natpop™ is one. In MANE's own words, Natpops are 100% "olfactory reconstitutions of fresh fruit notes." 

Pineapple Natpop™ is a marvel. Unlike our highly popular top note Pineapple Supreme base, Pineapple Natpop™ is a top to bottom blend which is not just pineapple, but tropical fruit, sweetness and wonderful richness. This base is absolutely essential for all perfumers. When you smell it you won't know how you lived without it. We have never been more passionate about a natural fruit base and honesty this surpasses many times over the more well-known Robertet natural fruit accords.

Use Pineapple Natpop™ in a large amount for a rich pineapple note that lasts the life of your scent, or use traces to sweeten and add a fruity je ne sais quoi.

products.name: Pineapple Supreme
products.description:
Have you wondered how Creed gets that incredible pineapple top note into Aventus? Wonder no more! This is it: the Aventus Pineapple. Incredibly powerful and intensely sweet, this base is impactful at mere traces.

From DK Donna Karan, one of the most incredible men's scents of the '90s to Aventus — the modern blockbuster, pineapple is a note beloved by everyone. This powerful base is the only pineapple top note you will want. Nothing else comes close.

products.name: Pink Acacia
products.description:
Pink Acacia (black locust or faux acacia) differs from the unrelated cassie and mimosa (members of the true acacia family) in that it has an intense note of orange blossom mixed with hawthorne. It is a very elegant floral note seldom seen in modern perfumes which is a shame as it has such a universally appreciated scent. Pink Acacia conveys the scent of warm summer breeze; it creates a sense of happy nostalgia. It is perfectly suited as the main floral heart of a contemporary fragrance.

Fraterworks Pink Acacia is loaded with natural floral oils and it can be safely used in small amounts (for adding nuance and richness) or in overdose as is evidenced in the demo formula below.

products.name: Pink Carnation, Natural
products.description:
With an overload of French iris extracts, spices, floral oils and absolutes and the ultimate natural isolates, Pink Carnation is a 100% natural base that brings not just a wonderfully natural carnation note to your fragrances but contributes a number of high class materials seldom affordable for hobbyist and artisanal perfumers.

Combine Pink Carnation with natural Ionones and orange blossom for the beginnings of a luxurious natural take on Coty's great masterpiece L'Origan.

This base is also able to be used as a one for one replacer for our classic non-natural Dianthus and Dianthine Extra bases, the use of which are demonstrated in our formulas below.

products.name: Pink Lotus Absolute
products.description:
Pink lotus absolute bears no resemblance to the sheer aquatic lotus of mainstream perfumery. The living flower is light and sweet, but extraction concentrates it into something dense, dark, and honeyed. Expect spicy green top notes, a waxy floral heart, then leather, tonka-like warmth, and unmistakable animalic depth.

Use pink lotus absolute as an exotic heart in your oriental and oud-based compositions, where its honeyed animalic character creates instant opulence. It transforms white floral blends, adding a dark richness that jasmine and tuberose alone cannot achieve. A little goes a very long way.

Pair it with sandalwood and oud for a meditative, incense-like accord. Try it alongside mimosa or beeswax absolute to amplify its honey facets. Dose carefully from a dilution — the raw absolute is intensely concentrated, and even a trace rewrites your entire composition.

Pink and white lotus are both colour forms of Nelumbo nucifera, the sacred lotus. They are the same species but produce noticeably different absolutes. The pink form is sweeter, more honeyed, and more complex. The white is bolder, less fruity, and more aquatic. Always check which you are buying.

Blue lotus — Nymphaea caerulea — the sacred flower of ancient Egypt, is not a lotus at all. It is a water lily from an entirely different plant family. Its absolute is sheer, waxy, and fruity-sweet where pink lotus is dense and animalic. They share almost nothing in common despite the confusingly similar name.

products.name: Pink Pepper CO2
products.description:
Pink Pepper (unrelated to Piper Nigrum or black pepper) comes in two varieties: Schinus Molle (Peru) and Schinus Terebinthifolius (Brazil). They are closely related and quite similar in scent but the Brazilian extracts are brighter and fresher and, generally speaking, preferred. 

This CO2 extraction from LMR is the finest version of Schinus Terebinthifolius on the market today. It is supremely beautiful and a must-have for all perfumers. It is extracted from the berries of the tree.

We also stock the essential oil of Peruvian pink pepper (Schinus Molle) also from LMR.

products.name: Pink Pepper Oil, Molle
products.description:
Pink peppercorn is not really from the pepper family (Piper nigrum). Schinus molle (false pepper tree, Peruvian pepper) is an evergreen tree native to Peru with a wonderfully piquant and fresh top note and resinous balsamic dry down that is universally loved.

This prestige essential oil from LMR is extracted from the berries of the tree and is extremely versatile. Not to be confused with the close relative Schinus terebinthifolius (Brazilian Pepper and a native of that place) which, although also very beautiful, has a more astringent top note quality. We also stock Pink Peppercorn “Terebinthifolius” CO2 extract from LMR.

products.name: Pink Pepper Oil, Terebinthifolius
products.description:
Pink pepper oil opens with a bright, sparkling burst of spice — peppery but lighter and more radiant than black pepper. There is a distinctive rosy-floral quality underneath, with green, citrusy freshness and a warm woody drydown. It reads as luminous and uplifting rather than heavy.

Pink pepper is not a true pepper — it belongs to the cashew and mango family, which explains its fruity, rosy warmth. It became a modern perfumery staple after Estée Lauder Pleasures in 1995. Use it to add sparkling lift to florals, fresh masculines, and unisex compositions.

Pair pink pepper with rose for an effect that is almost magical — the rosy facets in both materials amplify each other. It also works beautifully with bergamot, neroli, geranium, vetiver, and cedarwood. A little goes a long way; overdose and it turns harsh.

Different species, different characters

This oil — from Schinus terebinthifolius, the Brazilian pepper tree — is the brighter, fresher, more modern of the two varieties, with distinctive rosy-green nuances.

Pink Pepper Oil, Molle (Schinus molle, the Peruvian pepper tree) is more balsamic, smoky, and woody — closer to juniper berry or angelica in character.

We also stock LMR's Pink Pepper CO2, a supercritical extract of terebinthifolius that captures even more of the fresh berry — brighter top notes and a fuller, more rounded body than this steam-distilled oil.

products.name: Piperitone
products.description:
Piperitone occurs naturally in eucalyptus, peppermint, and various Cymbopogon grasses. It sits in the camphor-mint-eucalyptus triangle but occupies its own corner — warmer and more herbaceous than camphor, less sharp than menthol, deeper than eucalyptol. It smells like dried herbs hanging in a warm room with the window open to a eucalyptus grove.

In fougères, piperitone adds an old-fashioned herbaceous warmth that modern aromatic chemicals often lack. Use it alongside lavender, rosemary, and coumarin where you want the composition to feel grounded and natural rather than scrubbed clean. It sits comfortably in the heart, bridging the aromatic top notes and the mossy base.

For perfumers, its value is in adding herbal complexity — the kind of slightly rough, unpolished character that makes a fragrance feel handcrafted rather than industrially assembled. It belongs to the same aromatic world as thymol and menthol but brings warmth where they bring cold.

products.name: Piperonyl Acetate
products.description:
Piperonyl acetate smells of sweet cherry and strawberry wrapped in powdery heliotrope warmth — floral, honeyed, with a hawthorn softness. It shares the methylenedioxy backbone of heliotropin but delivers it in a fruitier, more rounded form. It lasts over 400 hours on a blotter.

Use it in heliotrope and muguet accords for sweet, fruity depth, or add it to berry compositions where it contributes a natural-smelling cherry-strawberry character without synthetic sharpness. It also works beautifully in lilac and jasmine bases, where its powdery sweetness fills out the floral heart.

Note: this product should not be confused with piperonyl acetone (Dulcinyl / Cassione), which is a crystalline solid with a darker, jammier raspberry-blackberry character and a woody dryness. Piperonyl acetate is lighter, more floral, and more cherry-forward — think cherry blossom versus blackberry jam.

products.name: Pistachio Thiazole
products.description:
This material opens with the unmistakable scent of fresh pistachios – green, vibrant, almost creamy. At 0.1% dilution, you get pure nut clarity. Its power rivals the strongest pyrazines but offers unique savoury depth.

Use pistachio thiazole when you need authentic nut character in gourmand fragrances. Combine it with cocoa absolute for realistic praline effects or blend with coffee CO2 for espresso depth. This thiazole bridges sweet and savoury worlds, turning flat chocolate accords three-dimensional, hence its sometimes name of Chocolate Thiazole.

Start with 0.01% in your trials – this material dominates quickly. The green facet persists through drydown, unusual for such volatile notes. Mix pre-diluted stock to maintain control over its exceptional diffusion.

This material is available pure on request.

products.name: Plicatone
products.description:
Plicatone is a lovely synthetic from Firmenich which has a light herbal top note reminiscent of artemisia and myrtle with side notes of cedarwood. It also has a hint of fruity rose ketone. It's dual nature makes it ideal to link wood base notes with herbal top notes.

A trace is used in Calvin Klein's Defy (2021), while 0.2% is found in Valentino Uomo (2014) though it is perhaps more famously known for its inclusion in the great Fixobois base of Firmenich.

products.name: Poirenate
products.description:
It's not overripe or underripe: poirenate is a pear at its most perfect stage of ripeness. Even better, it is more of a classical pear note, so it is not saccharine sweet like the genetically manipulated varieties sold in supermarkets today. This makes it far more useful for building a pear note as you don't have to fight stickiness.

The balanced quality of this aroma chemical makes it useful in non-fruit contexts also. It can add freshness and an aquatic sense to fruit notes, and it can temper the harshness of green notes in florals like hyacinth and lilac.

For pear texture and fruity realism, pair Poirenate with a touch of safraleine and Pear Ester. Ethyl-2-methyl butyrate will take it in the direction of overripe, and a higher dose of safraleine and a touch of cis-3-hexenol will unripen it.

products.name: Poivre Fort
products.description:
Poivre Fort is a classic spice base which, characteristically of products of this type, includes sympathetic woody and floral notes. The base has a wonderfully warming black pepper top note on a creamy and soft heart of Bulgarian rose, ylang-ylang and its related salicylates giving it a solar quality. This base works as a wonderful blender while imparting an elegant spice note.

Poivre Fort is an ideal base to add freshness and lightness to heavy compositions. It can be used in high doses without dominating at up to 2.19% for IFRA 51 compliance.

products.name: Polysantol®
products.description:
Strong and profoundly beautiful, Polysantol is perhaps the most useful sandalwood chemical we have today. It works in traces to add a true to life radiant sandalwood note that is beloved by all and in overdose it can add interesting effects. But do bear in mind that it is restricted by IFRA 51 to a maximum of 1.1% of your finished product.

Polysantol is, like Javanol® from Givaudan, incredible in its power. At 0.85% it makes up the entire Sandalwood note of Creed's Original Santal and first appeared in Samsara by Guerlain in a 9.5% overdose.

products.name: Pomelo Grandis
products.description:
Natural grapefruit and pomelo oils are the most easily degraded in perfumery and as a result synthetics like Methyl Pamplemousse are used liberally. However sometimes we need a genuinely realistic note of Pomelo or grapefruit that can be used in the same way as any other regular citrus oil with little to no risk of degradation. That's where Fraterworks Pomelo Grandis comes in.

Pomelo Grandis has the power and longevity of true Pomelo oil as well as the wonderfully sulphurous and bitter top note quality. This base is almost entirely natural and blends with all the members of our Citrus Suite.

This can be used as a one-for-one replacement for Grapefruit oil or Pomelo oil in a formula.

products.name: Popcorn Pyrazine 1% DPG
products.description:
Holy guacamole! This is one of the most powerful gourmand materials you'll ever try. At high doses it is intensely corn-chip-like, while in lower dilutions it is the scent of hot buttered popcorn at the movies. We can supply this pure but please email to request pricing as it requires special handling.

Popcorn Pyrazine blends beautifully with Nutty Pyrazine, Filbertone, Orbitone, Nutmeg Absolute, Birch Tar, Cade Oil, gourmand and wood chemicals.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Poplar Bud Absolute 50% TEC
products.description:
This product has seen a steep price increase from our suppliers and alas we must pass that on. We are monitoring the trends in pricing and will make reductions when possible.

With no restriction in use, Poplar Buds absolute can be used in a similar way to styrax but in far greater amounts. It is a wonderful fixative and has the most alluring and unusual scent of honey, fruit and resin making it perfect for adding body and longevity to fruit bases and accords; indeed Edmond Roudnitska used this in his most famous Prunol SP﻿ base.

Poplar Bud Absolute is diluted to 50% in natural triethyl citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) at the source by Biolandes.

Origin: Eastern Europe
Manufactured: France
Part: Buds
Method: Solvent Extraction

products.name: Potato Pyrazine
products.description:
Warm potatoes, roasted hazelnuts and a faint cocoa sweetness is what Potato Pyrazine brings to your blends. It is one of the most powerful roasted materials so traces are all you need and we offer it at 10% to get you part way there: we recommend going further to 1% or even 0.1% to get all of its nuances.

Pair with cocoa and coffee extracts and use it with Praslin Pyrazine and Parmentier Pyrazine for a more complex layered base than either will give alone. A nice little trick is to put the faintest whisper with tobacco leaf absolute to add a deeper cured quality to it; outstanding for a pipe tobacco accord.

products.name: Poudre à la Maréchale Tincture 20%
products.description:
The scent of powdered wigs. This is an 18th century tincture of dried flowers, spices, roots and seeds. Use it as a fixative or the foundation of an entire scent.

A very precious and little-known ingredient of many French fragrances from the golden age of perfumery was Infusion Poudre à la Maréchale (tincture of marechale powder). Poudre à la Maréchale was a scented powder that had risen to popularity during the era of powdered wigs (perukes) in which horse-hair wigs (which were seldom if ever washed) would be dusted to mask malodours. The original marechale powder was created in the late 1600s for the wife of the Maréchal d'Aumont. The materials used varied from perfumer to perfumer though there were some fundamentals that were common to most: ambrette seeds, sandalwood, orris root, cloves and a variety of other spices, herbs and usually one or both of rose petals and orange blossoms.

So popular was Poudre à la Maréchale that even as perukes fell into disuse, the great perfume houses that were beginning to emerge across Europe continued to supply the scent as cosmetic powders but also as an infusion (or tincture). Initially it was sold as an article for wear on its own like a cologne, but it also came to be added to other fragrances as a fixative base. Most of the early Guerlain fragrances incorporate this infusion, and Coty's L'Origan (formula below) owes much of its powderiness and complex dry down to it.

Fraterworks is the only company in the world that is currently ma

products.name: Pralinol™
products.description:
Praline: roasted hazelnuts, toffee and chocolate. This is an outstanding and powerful base that lets you add a praline note to your perfumes with the minimum off fuss. It contains extremely powerful and rare materials for a truly unique blend.

Pralinol can be used in overdose when mixed with the right accessories, but a trace is all you need (0.1% or lower) to add a decidedly edible note. It is particularly nice with vanillin and veratraldehyde.

products.name: Praslin Pyrazine
products.description:
Praslin Pyrazine (named after the 17th century Marshal du Plessis-Praslin who invented the toffee-nut candy) opens with that unmistakable roasted nut character—think freshly made praline or warm peanuts. The cocoa facet follows immediately, rich and slightly powdery. An earthy, musty undertone grounds the material, adding depth.

This pyrazine forms naturally during the Maillard reaction when sugars and proteins meet heat—the same chemistry that creates the irresistible aromas of roasted coffee, fresh bread, and chocolate. It is naturally present in cocoa products, roasted peanuts, potato crisps, and roasted barley. In perfumery, it anchors gourmand compositions with genuine roasted warmth that synthetics so often find difficult to replicate.

Use Praslin Pyrazine sparingly—up to 0.1% in fragrance concentrate. It works beautifully with vanilla, lactones, and other chocolate materials to build convincing praline and hazelnut effects. The powdery quality pairs well with iris and violet notes for sophisticated gourmand-floral hybrids. Combine it with unctuous Coconut Pure Jungle Essence (CO2) for a toasted coconut note.

Praslin Pyrazine vs Torref Pyrazine

Both share the chocolate-nutty pyrazine family character, but their differences matter for formulation. Praslin Pyrazine (2,5-dimethyl Pyrazine) leans more musty, earthy, and powdery—closer to raw cocoa powder and roasted peanuts with a grassy undertone. Torref Pyrazine (2,6-dimethyl Pyrazine) is more intensely roasted, with

products.name: Precyclemone B
products.description:
Precyclemone B (Aldemone) opens with a radiant ozone-aldehydic character that evokes crisp outdoor air and sea spray. Its clean, almost ethereal quality combines sharp citrus brightness with a smooth marine freshness. You'll notice the muguet undertones emerge as the material develops, lending an unexpected floral softness to the otherwise bracing profile.

This material transforms masculine fragrances with its exceptional diffusion and tenacity. Use it at low concentrations in floral or woody bases—typically around 0.1%—though citrus compositions can accommodate higher levels approaching 2%. It blends beautifully with dihydromyrcenol, calone, and ambroxan to build classic aquatic accords, whilst patchouli, rose, pepper, and gardenia benefit from its uplifting brightness. Pair it with florhydral and citrus oils to accentuate its aldehydic grapefruit facets.

Consider Precyclemone B when you need a booster that lifts compositions without dominating them. It defined the fresh wave of 1990s masculines and remains essential for creating that distinctive Cool Water-style freshness. Work carefully with dilution—its power reveals itself best when you resist the temptation to overdose, letting its radiant character enhance rather than overwhelm your accord.

products.name: Prenyl Acetate
products.description:
Prenyl Acetate opens fresh, sweet, and immediately fruity — green apple and pear dominate, with a softer banana note sitting just behind. Unlike the candied banana punch of isoamyl acetate, this ester is etheric and light. Subtle floral undertones of jasmine and heliotrope emerge as it develops.

Use Prenyl Acetate to add fruity sparkle to your top notes without the cloying sweetness heavier fruit esters bring. It lifts ylang, jasmine, and champaca while adding a bergamot-like freshness to citrus blends. A convincing swap wherever isoamyl acetate feels too brash.

Blend Prenyl Acetate with benzyl acetate for a fruity-jasmine top, or layer it over green notes to build realistic apple and pear accords. It also quietly enhances lavender compositions, adding a sweet lift that mimics natural complexity. Found in trace amounts in ylang ylang.

products.name: Pretty Oud
products.description:
This is an extremely attractive and easy to dose oud base by Firmenich which could almost be a fragrance in its own right. Pretty Oud offers a sensual woody profile with smoky and leathery facets, providing a direct and elegant interpretation of ambery fragrances.

I would be surprised if this doesn't form an important unlisted component in Gucci's rather interesting 2017 Gucci Guilty Absolute for men (and perhaps the feminine version also with blackcurrant and rose materials added).

products.name: Prunella®
products.description:
For most, Prunella needs no introduction. It is the industry standard dried plum base from Firmemich which has most certainly withstood the test of time, being featured in such classics as the original Dior Poison and Chanel's Égoïste.

Built around an overdose of phenoxyethyl isobutyrate, this is a very easy base to dose and while small amounts contribute a gentle sweetness, overdoses also work very well in a modern gourmand context.

Prunella® blends very well with the Rose Ketones and other fruit bases and it makes beautiful accords with patchouli.

products.name: Prunol SP
products.description:
After Mousse de Saxe perhaps no other classical base is as well known as Prunol SP by De Laire. Prunol is a wonderful floral and fantasy fruit base with a stronger emphasis on the floral than fruit. Nevertheless it imparts a luscious sweet plummy note to fragrances. Edmond Roudnitska created the base after his wartime discovery of casks of a rare type of methyl ionone discarded in the De Laire yard.

To this he added many other products including luxurious naturals of Poplar bud, Helichrysum absolute, precious Boronia absolute and more. Blended with spices, lactones and a fond of De Laire bases, Prunol SP was born. Our base is 100% faithful to that formula by Roudnitska and so, in consquence, it contains Poplar bud absolute - a natural plant extract rich in salicin which may need to be avoided by people with allergies to aspirin or salicylic acid.

Prunol is fruity, spicy, aldehydic, and floral. It is a powerful base and has a usability level up to 7.8% for IFRA 49 compliance, it can be used in an overdose for a novel effect. It featured heavily in the 1943 perfume Femme for Rochas. In the 21st century in which we find gourmand fragrances all the rage, Prunol SP deserves a renaissance.

products.name: Pyroprunat
products.description:
This Symrise aroma chemical is primarily plummy with a dried fruit, peach skin and floral quality. It is naturally fruity and not sugar-sweet making it a nice material to put alongside more saccharine fruit bases or products.

The classic blend of rose and violet is great enhanced by Pyroprunat as it pairs extremely well with the damascones and ionones. Much fun could be had playing around with the original YSL Paris form to create something new and more appealing to a younger generation that craves more edible scents.

products.name: Raspberry Glycidate
products.description:
First let's deal with the naming conventions. Like strawberry glycidate, this chemical is often known under a false name.

Strawberry Glycidate: Aldehyde C-16 (so-called); Ethyl 3-methyl-3-phenylglycidate
Raspberry Glycidate: Aldehyde C-20 (so-called); Ethyl 3-(4-methylphenyl)glycidate

Despite the molecular similarities, the scents (and power) are quite different.

Raspberry Glycidate delivers an intense sweet, ripe berry impression with a distinct iris and rose-like florality that sets it apart from its weaker strawberry cousin. Broader fruity facets emerge — bold grape, tutti-frutti, banana, and a soft warmth that reads almost amber-like. The overall effect is sweeter and more complex than C-16, with a considerably bolder presence. In fact, this could well be a contender for unexplored power-notes. In addition to its fruit note, a clear affinity with ionones and methyl ionones is clear.

Use Raspberry Glycidate in berry accords, red fruit compositions, and anywhere you need fruity sweetness that endures. It nuances rose, orris, and violet notes with convincing berry realism. At over three hundred hours on blotter, this is one of the most persistent fruity materials available.

products.name: Raspberry Ketone
products.description:
Raspberry ketone (also known as raspberry crystals) is a very versatile sweet crystalline chemical that can be used in traces to add a fruity sweetness to materials like Vanillin or Heliotrope.

It is used to great effect in Coco by Chanel to unify the resins and add novelty to the oriental type of scent.

It is definitely a must have material and we recommend diluting it to 10% as it is significantly more impactful than you would expect.

Steffen Arctander describes it thus: "This ketone is used in perfume compositions, particularly in Jasmin, Gardenia, Tuberose, etc. where floral notes need fruity undertones, or where fruity notes need fixation and supporting delicate sweetness. One known Jasmin speciality contains a considerable proportion of this material in its fruit-preserve-like undertones and terminal notes."

products.name: Raspberry Leaf Absolute
products.description:
Raspberry Leaf Absolute opens with complex green-leafy character—with a jammy nuance, and layered with unexpected depth. Delicate fruit facets mingle with musky tea notes, while balsamic-resinous undertones evoke mulled wine and dried fruits. The leathery warmth adds sophistication, creating a profile that transcends simple berry sweetness. This is a forest floor, not candy.

This French absolute comes from the leaves of Rubus idaeus, extracted via solvent to capture the full aromatic complexity of the plant material. The resulting substance is extremely thick and sticky—practically solid at room temperature—requiring patience and warmth to work with. For that reason we offer it pre-diluted in natural triethyl citrate for practical use. Despite coming from raspberry, the leaf absolute smells nothing like the bright fruit; instead it offers deep green character with davana-like jamminess and amber-tobacco warmth.

Work with Raspberry Leaf Absolute as a base note modifier where its green-jammy character adds sophisticated depth. Use it in berry accords seeking complexity beyond simple raspberry ketone sweetness, or in chypre compositions where fruity-green notes complement oakmoss and bergamot. It blends beautifully with rose, agarwood, patchouli, and vanilla. Try it in tea, tobacco, and cognac accords where its musky-resinous facets add naturalistic warmth. The balsamic depth makes it valuable in precious wood and amber compositions.

products.name: Raspberry Ripple
products.description:
This is an intensely sweet raspberry base which can be used in traces for subtle fruity sweetness or in overdose for a fun modern gourmand. It blends incredibly well with other gourmand notes such as coconut and amaretto and it can be used in place of materials like ethyl maltol or maltol when a more interesting sugar note is wanted.

Make Raspberry Ripple the centrepiece of a wild fruity chypre or simply add it to a monolithic base like the Grojsman Plus and leave it at that!

For a luxury touch, add a little Ambrette Seed oil from LMR and sticky sweet Rose Ultimate Extract (boosted with some Rose Essence).

products.name: Reaumur
products.description:
Reaumur is our internal formula for Angels' Share by Kilian. Launched in 2020 as part of The Liquors collection and created by Benoist Lapouza, this is a sweet gourmand fragrance built around cognac and oak barrel, with praline, vanilla and warm spice.

This compound features a rich cognac accord laid over oak, giving the unmistakable impression of spirit ageing in a barrel. The opening is boozy and immediate, with cinnamon and tonka bean absolute warming the heart and hedione lending lift to what would otherwise be a very dense composition. The base delivers praline, vanilla, candied almond and creamy sandalwood for a finish that reads as stewed apples and Christmas baking. The result is a thick, enveloping gourmand with above-average projection and excellent longevity – indulgent and unmistakably festive. It is easy to see why this is one of the most popular gourmand perfumes.

This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. We recommend a 22% concentration (Parfum).

Top Notes: Cognac
Heart Notes: Cinnamon, Tonka Bean, Oak Barrel, Hedione
Base Notes: Vanilla, Praline, Sandalwood, Candied Almond

products.name: Red Champaca Absolute
products.description:
Red champaca absolute is the deeper, more intense cousin of golden champaca. Where the yellow form is delicate and tea-like, this is heavy and sultry — rich dried apricot and raisin sweetness layered over warm clove-spice. Hay, tobacco, and vanilla emerge in a lingering drydown.

Use red champaca as an opulent floral heart in your oriental compositions. It adds a spiced, fruity richness that jasmine and ylang alone cannot deliver. Blend it with sandalwood to highlight its tea-like warmth, or pair with patchouli for a darker, more brooding accord.

Try red champaca alongside rose and tuberose for a layered floral of extraordinary complexity. A trace in amber accords contributes a fruity-spicy dimension you won't get from any other material. This is one of perfumery's rarest and most rewarding naturals to work with.

This is a very expensive material and so we also sell our five start 100% natural replacer base, Red Champaca TruAbs.

products.name: Red Champaca TruAbs
products.description:
Red Champaca TruAbs® is a scientifically crafted base designed to provide the full olfactory impact of precious Red Champaca Absolute. This 100% natural TruAbs® blend replicates the absolute's narcotic sweetness and complex dry down with astonishing accuracy. Perfumers can use this cost-effective material to achieve opulent, oriental accords and add unique depth to floral compositions.

Incorporate Red Champaca TruAbs® at 0.1-5% to recreate a luxurious and exotic floral heart note. Blend with sandalwood and amber to enhance its warm, resinous qualities. TruAbs® bases, created in Grasse exclusively for Fraterworks, offer a consistent and readily available alternative to often unobtainable absolutes.

products.name: Red Ginger Oil
products.description:
Red ginger (halia bara) is related to regular ginger but is smaller and red with a pink to yellow interior. This red ginger essential oil (steam extracted from the roots) is spicier and more pungent than ginger. This is a wonderful and unique oil that can add a really interesting and unusual character to your fragrances.

Blends well with: other spice oils, sandalwood, resins and balsams.

This product is certified halal and kosher.

Synonyms: Halia Bara
Origin: Indonesia
Variety: ZIngiber officinale Linn Var. rubrum (Zingiberaceae)
Part: Fresh Roots
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Red Seaweed CO2
products.description:
Trembling beneath the saliferous waters of the Breton coast can be glimpsed long reddish fingers of Palmaria palmata, a precious red seaweed. In Ireland, Palmaria palmata (also known as dulse) has been a staple food for centuries and now, thanks to MANE (the premium supplier of oils and absolutes from Grasse) it finds a new home in the world of fragrance.

Red Seaweed Pure Jungle Essence™ is a jewel in the crown of MANE. While most seaweed materials come with unpleasant top notes, Red Seaweed has an almost gourmand quality, with nuances of fresh barnyard blended with the wild scent of the ancient Celtic Sea.

Jungle essences are MANE's special CO2 products (watch the video clip below for a fascinating look at how these materials are made). This Red Seaweed is a pure jungle essence™ meaning it has nothing added in the making and is the pure essence extracted from the raw material. 

Due to its intensity and very high cost, Fraterworks offers this pure jungle essence pure and in a more affordable and usable 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate, making it a product that can be used by natural (EU and US) perfumers.

Origin: Brittany, France

products.name: Red Thyme Oil
products.description:
Red Thyme Oil Extra has a powerful and complex aromatic profile, characterised by intense warmth and a potent, spicy-herbal quality. This primary impression is often described as medicinal or phenolic, a direct result of its high concentration of constituents like thymol and carvacrol. Supporting these dominant notes are earthy, loamy undertones, a dry woody character, and subtle sweet, balsamic overtones that add richness. The "red" designation indicates this is the unadulterated, initial distillate, which provides a more tenacious, potent, and raw aromatic experience compared to its rectified counterpart, White Thyme Oil.

As a perfumery ingredient, Red Thyme Oil Extra is a versatile and impactful tool used to add distinctive character to many fragrance types. It is a classic component in fougère compositions, where its herbaceous strength complements notes of lavender and oakmoss. Its aromatic quality also adds a "sunny touch" to woody and chypre fragrances, and its inherent spiciness makes it valuable in oriental blends. The dry, phenolic facets of the oil can even contribute to the creation of sophisticated leather accords. Beyond its primary scent, the oil's less volatile phenolic compounds allow it to act as a natural fixative, helping to anchor lighter notes and prolong a fragrance's longevity.

We can prepare documents for formulas that include materials we do not stock — including third-party bases — provided you supply the material's own Safety Data Sheet, IFRA certificate and allergen declaration. Because each such material must be built into our regulatory system from your supplied documents before your formula can be processed, a Third-Party Material fee applies to each one.

Modifications

Once we have delivered your paperwork, we can make changes for a fee that reflects the work involved. A change to the quantities of materials already in your formula is a Min

products.name: Rhodinol Ex Geranium Bourbon
products.description:
Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon comes closest to the scent of rose otto than any other single raw perfumery material making it extremely valuable in reconstructions of rose absolute and oils and an excellent additive in the highest class muguet bases.

This product is naturally isolated from geranium Bourbon. Other materials are sometimes sold under the name of rhodinol (products such as alpha-citronellol or blends of geraniol with laevo-citronellol) but those are incorrectly labelled. Our rhodinol is the true classical rhodinol ex geranium bourbon.

Rhodinol ex Geranium Bourbon has long been a highly prized fragrance material and it was a key component of the rose note in Chypre by Coty along with Rose D'Orient and French Rose de Mai absolute.

products.name: Rhodinyl Acetate
products.description:
Rhodinyl Acetate has some similarities to other rose Acetates (it even shares an IFRA standard with Citronellyl Acetate) but with a darker and more leafy quality and significantly longer drydown period. Rhodinyl acetate is a lovely rose bouquet note with nuances of citrus and rose leaves.

Use this material to add lasting vitality to rose, muguet, geranium and citrus bases. Use it as a basenote counterpart to continue the citronellyl acetate theme through a scent. Novel effects may be had mixing this with cyclomethylene citronellal.

Blends beautifully with Mimosal®, Cyclosia®, Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Phenyl Acetic Acid, Rhodinol, Geraniol, muguet, rose and honey bases.

products.name: Rhodinyl Formate
products.description:
Rhodinyl formate opens with a soft, rosy character—less assertive than many rose materials, with a distinctive dried-leaf quality that evokes pressed geranium petals. There is a faint fruity sweetness beneath the floral notes. The overall effect is gentle, diffusive, and naturally elegant.

Use it in rose and geranium accords where you want to enhance naturalism without adding brightness or sweetness. It excels in muguet bases, where its green-leaf facet supports the floral heart, and in citrus-floral blends where it provides a smooth transition from fresh top notes to the floral body. Pair it with rhodinol, geraniol, or citronellol to build authentic rose accords. It also works beautifully with citrus oils and ionones to create fresh, natural-feeling floral compositions.

Rhodinyl Formate vs Rhodinyl Acetate

Both are esters of rhodinol, but they occupy different spaces in a composition. Rhodinyl acetate is the richer, more complex material—a red-rose character with powdery, spicy, and citrus-leafy facets that reads as darker and more tenacious. 

Rhodinyl formate is lighter, greener, and more transparent—a softer rosy-floral with dried-leaf and fruity notes that supports rather than dominates. Choose the formate when you want subtle rosy depth and green naturalism in the background; choose the acetate when you need a bold, complex rose heart with exceptional longevity.

products.name: Rhubofix
products.description:
Rhubofix opens with crisp green rhubarb and bright grapefruit, then develops into a dry, woody core with vetiver-like facets and spicy warmth. It has real verticality — presence from top through heart to base. This is the structural, long-lasting member of Firmenich's rhubarb family.

Where Rhuboflor is floral, fruity, and powdery, Rhubofix is woody, spicy, and dry. Rhuboflor gives rhubarb an orris-like softness; Rhubofix gives it a vetiver-like backbone with grapefruit sparkle. Rhubofix also lasts twice as long — four days on a blotter versus Rhuboflor's two. Use both together for a complete rhubarb picture, or choose one depending on the direction you want.

Pair it with vetiver and cedarwood to amplify its woody side, with bergamot and grapefruit for citrus-green freshness, or with pink pepper and cardamom for spicy warmth. It also creates interesting effects with salicylates, especially when sweetened with heliotropin. Always evaluate well diluted.

products.name: Rhuboflor
products.description:
Rhuboflor opens with a vivid burst of tart rhubarb — green, fruity, sharp. Underneath sits unexpected depth: berry sweetness, a powdery floral quality recalling orris and hyacinth, and a rooty herbal undertone. It is far more refined than actual rhubarb and extraordinarily potent.

Use Rhuboflor in traces — it is extremely powerful and easily dominates a composition. A tiny amount adds green-fruity sparkle to rose accords, berry compositions, and fresh florals. It lasts 48 hours at full strength, giving rhubarb effects real persistence.

Pair it with Bergundian blackcurrant bud and fig signature for an edible rhubarb-fruit effect, or with bergamot and galbanum for tart green freshness. Rhuboflor is the most floral of the rhubarb materials — Rhubofix is woodier, Rhubafuran sharper. Always evaluate well diluted.

products.name: Rhumacetal
products.description:
Rhumacetal delivers that unmistakable boozy rum character—refined alcohol warmth without harsh solvent notes. The tobacco facet emerges alongside, adding a dry, slightly smoky complexity. Woody undertones ground the composition, evoking aged oak barrels and fine spirits.

This acetal serves as a cornerstone material for building convincing rum accords in perfumery. Some perfumers describe it as the best pure alcohol aromachemical available, providing a concentrated hit of refined spirits character. The tobacco fixative effect makes it valuable beyond simple gourmand applications—try it in oriental compositions where that aged, sophisticated warmth enhances the overall blend.

Combine Rhumacetal with MANE's incredible Rum Jungle Essence, rum ether, vanillin, oakwood materials, and Peru balsam for dark rum effects. It pairs beautifully with woods like cedar and sandalwood, and enriches gourmand notes of vanilla, chocolate, and caramel. The material can seem underwhelming against very powerful notes, so balance carefully.

products.name: Riotous Red™
products.description:
The Fraterworks® Perfumer's Palette™ is a range of dyes that can be used alone or in combination with each other to add vibrance and colour to your perfumes or cosmetic products. Our proprietary blend of FD&C and D&C colours are sold in liquid form.

Perfumer's Palette colours contain preservatives and distilled water which is perfectly safe for alcoholic perfumes in the quantities needed for colouration. Typical use is from 0.01–0.5% of finished product. This product complies with the current BP / Ph Eur Preservative Efficacy Test Criteria A for Topical products. The PET Certificate can be downloaded below.

At these low levels, staining of clothing or skin is minimal to none but you should always test your finished product against white cloth or paper.

Riotous Red contains FD&C Red 4 (Ci 14700).

According to the New Zealand cosmetics group standard, this product should not be used in hair dye products but is permitted otherwise.

products.name: Roasted Barley Extract 40% ETH
products.description:
Roasted Barley Extract opens with the intoxicating richness of freshly brewed espresso, immediately complemented by the warm sweetness of toffee and toasted hazelnuts. This is no simple cereal note—it's an "accord in a bottle" that captures the entire sensory experience of a cosy bakery or whisky distillery. The Maillard reaction during roasting creates hundreds of aromatic compounds, particularly potent pyrazines that deliver those deeply satisfying nutty, coffee, and cocoa nuances.

This material has a remarkable ability to add instant sophistication to gourmand compositions. Its complex evolution from sweet caramel top notes through bready, malty hearts to smoky, tobacco-laden bases provides extraordinary depth that synthetic materials struggle to match. The boozy facets make it essential for whisky and cognac accords, whilst its dark chocolate and coffee characters elevate simple vanilla compositions into compelling, textured experiences.

products.name: Roman Chamomile Oil
products.description:
Roman chamomile (also known as English Chamomile) possesses a distinct aroma that is sweet, fruity, and herbaceous. It is characterised by its warm, floral aroma with subtle hints of apple and honey. The fragrance is often considered soft and comforting, with gentle notes that evoke a sense of relaxation and tranquility.

Use this wonderful oil as a middle note or a supporting ingredient in floral, herbal, or aromatic fragrances where it adds a touch of warmth and complexity.

The difference between German and Roman chamomile plants is that German chamomile flowers grow in clusters, while Roman chamomile flowers grow singularly atop a hairy stem.

We also stock the finest rare single estate German (or blue) chamomile from England.

Origin: Italy
Part: Flower heads
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Romandolide®
products.description:
Romandolide opens with a remarkably clean, delicate musk character that immediately distinguishes itself from heavier polycyclic musks. This alicyclic musk delivers subtle fruity-berry top notes that dance above its core musky heart, creating an effect both fresh and substantial. Soft ambrette-like nuances add sophistication without the animalic edge of natural ambrette, while gentle balsamic facets emerge as it develops. What sets Romandolide apart is its ability to maintain delicacy while building exceptional volume on the drydown—it whispers initially but grows to fill space with its clean, modern presence.

Use Romandolide at 5-20% when you need a modern musk with universal perception—unlike some musks, everyone can smell it. As an alicyclic musk, it bridges the gap between light top-note musks and heavy base musks, offering the clean character of the former with the tenacity approaching the latter. Use it as a direct replacement for polycyclic musks like Galaxolide where you need similar performance with a cleaner, less fruity profile. In floral compositions, it provides invisible support without the sweetness that can overwhelm delicate petals. For oriental fragrances, its balsamic facets and sandalwood-like drydown create sophisticated depth without heaviness.

The structural innovation of Romandolide places it perfectly between traditional musk families. Unlike macrocyclic musks (like Muscenone) with their animalic depth, or polycyclic musks (like Galaxolide) with the

products.name: Romascone
products.description:
Romascone delivers a unique aromatic signature defined by distinct rosemary and thujonic qualities. Its true value lies in its potent, damascone-like radiance, providing exceptional lift and diffusion. Perfumers leverage this molecule to build modern accords that require vibrant, red fruity-rose effects with a novel herbal twist.

Combine Romascone with aldehydes C-11 Undecylenic and C-12 MNA to amplify radiance and diffusion. This material excels in fine fragrances where its dual character fully develops. Add armoise oil to enhance the thujonic aspect. Blends beautifully with Artemal.

Use Romascone strategically to augment restricted rose ketones in your formulas. Since IFRA limits rose ketones to 0.043% combined, add Romascone at 0.05-0.3% to restore the missing radiance. This material acts as a force multiplier—its fruity-damascone character harmonises with trace damascones while contributing its own distinctive freshness.

products.name: Rooibos “Red Tea” Resinoid
products.description:
Rooibos resinoid smells of warm honey, sun-dried hay, and soft caramel, with a fruity-apricot sweetness and a gentle woody depth. It is softer and sweeter than black tea, warmer and rounder than green tea. There is a faint bitterness in the drydown that keeps it from ever becoming cloying.

Rooibos is not actually tea — it comes from Aspalathus linearis, a legume found only in the Cederberg Mountains of South Africa's Cape fynbos. That unique origin gives it a character no true tea can replicate: honeyed warmth with a red, almost wine-like quality. Use it in gourmand and oriental compositions where you want natural sweetness and depth.

Pair it with vanilla and tonka for rich gourmand warmth, with immortelle and honey absolute for a golden, honeyed heart, or with cedarwood and vetiver for a darker, woodier direction. It also works beautifully with bergamot, black pepper, and orris for a sophisticated tea-inspired composition.

The Payan Bertrand quality we stock is from their precious Signature range.

products.name: Rose Absolute “Signature” Bulgaria
products.description:
If you possess only one rose for perfumery purposes, this absolute is it. Its versatility is unparalleled and even mere traces can have a wonderful enriching and exalting impact on a fragrance.

We obtain this signature product from one of the finest suppliers of oils and absolutes in the world and the quality shows. With a full body and a long rich dry down, this is rose absolute perfection.

Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate, making it suitable for natural perfumers.

We also stock Rose Bulgarian oil (otto).

products.name: Rose Absolute, Isparta
products.description:
Isparta in Turkey has a long history of rose production; in fact it is called The City of Roses. The most common variety is Rosa Damascena, the same type that is used for the classic Bulgarian Rose Oil (otto) and Absolute. The other most used type of rose in perfumery is Rose Centifolia, a French variant. We stock the famous Rose de Mai from Grasse and the luscious Rose Centifolia Absolute, Tunisia.

In the words of LMR: “This unique petal rose note has a pronounced fruity top, green and spicy facets, and a touch of honey.” Rose extracts from Isparta are slightly more costly than standard Turkish products as the climate and soil produces richer and more balanced results. 

In Isparta, roses are still often farmed and harvested in the traditional way on multi-generational farms. LMR certifies this product as part of their “For Life” range which seeks to support these family-owned suppliers which tend to be highly sustainable due to their adherence to heritage methods.

We also stock numerous other natural roses which can found in our rose collection.

Fun fact: the waste produced in the extraction of this beautiful Turkish rose absolute is the starting material for the modern marvel of upcycled perfumery: LMR's Rose Ultimate Extract which we also stock.

Origin: Isparta, Turkey
Part: Flower petals only
Process: Solvent extraction

products.name: Rose Absolute, Morocco
products.description:
The main rose used in perfumes today is from Rosa Damascena. It typically goes by the name of just Rose Absolute (or oil) and the Bulgarian variety is the most common. However, it's lesser-used cousin, Rosa Damascena from Morocco is a somewhat different beast, with a lovely tea rose quality that is lacking in the slightly lower-cost Bulgarian absolute.

The best Bulgarian roses tend to be used for the essential oil which is the most costly of the rose extracts, whereas in Morocco the best roses go to making the absolute. The soil of Morocco produces roses that give a lighter, more nuanced absolute with hints of herbal green and an almost peppery undertone.

Moroccan Rose Absolute is definitely something to have even if you already use the Bulgarian absolute. The differences make both extremely useful for different ends.

Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate from citrus, making it suitable for natural perfumers.

We also stock Rose Bulgarian oil (otto) and Rose “Signature” Absolute from Bulgaria.

Origin: Morocco
Part: Flowers only
Process: Solvent extraction

products.name: Rose Absolute, Select
products.description:
Fraterworks' Bulgarian rose absolute select is the cornerstone material for any perfumer's palette at an accessible price point. This product captures the rich, deep character that makes Bulgarian rose absolute indispensable in perfumery: its velvety texture, complex floral heart, and remarkable ability to enhance and elevate compositions even in trace amounts.

While our signature Payan Bertrand rose absolute represents the pinnacle of luxury with its exceptional depth and longevity, this Fraterworks® Select rose absolute delivers the true essence of Bulgarian rose in a format that makes it practical for regular use, experimentation, and learning. It maintains the characteristic full-bodied profile and the transformative quality that rose absolute brings to fragrances - from simple soliflores to complex oriental compositions.

This is an ideal choice for perfumery students developing their skills, enthusiasts building their organ, and professional perfumers who need a reliable, quality rose absolute for trials and formulation work where cost efficiency matters. Like all Fraterworks® Select products, it's been chosen to ensure authentic quality at an exceptional price.

Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate.

We also stock value Rose Bulgarian oil (otto).

products.name: Rose Blanche
products.description:
Rose Blanche is the white rose base featured prominently in the stunning Detchéma fragrance by Révillon (1953). It is a luxurious and rich blend of the finest rose synthetics available and loaded with natural absolutes.

Rose Blanche, in traces, imparts sweetness and sophistication but in larger amounts modifies a modern rose and adds a precious and noticeably expensive quality. This base is a top to bottom accord, so it can also stand alone as an entire fragrance unto itself. Rose Blanche has a synergy with Rose D'Orient and the two blend seamlessly together.

products.name: Rose Centifolia Absolute, Tunisia
products.description:
The two main roses in perfumery are Rose Damascena and Rose Centifolia. Rose Damascena is rich, warm, and slightly spicy while Rose Centifolia is soft, fresh, and powdery. The latter is great for adding a soft rosy floralcy while the Damascena gives a bolder and more intense rose heart note.

The finest extracts of Rose Centifolia are from Grasse (Rose de Mai) but due to the extremely high cost, most harvests now come from Tunisia.

Rose de Mai comes from roses harvested during the month of May only, while Tunisian Rose centifolia is harvested at different times through the year; due to the hotter climate, the Tunisian absolute has a lighter, fresher, and slightly more citrusy profile with a delicate floral character.

products.name: Rose Crystals
products.description:
Rose acetate has a lovely soft scent akin to that of the scent of a deep red rose floating across a great distance. It has facets that are powdery, sweet (almost gourmand) and floral.

While it is a nice material in its own right, its true power comes to light when blended with phenyl ethyl alcohol (PEA) as part of a rose accord. Rose crystals have an astonishing ability to add an almost three dimensional effect to PEA, imparting a naturalness and an inimitable quality that is extremely appealing.

For any perfumer serious about making good rose bases or sophisticated rose notes, this is an essential material. 

Rose crystals are a fine white powder which can be simply added to your blends into which it will quite happily dissolve.

products.name: Rose D'Orient
products.description:
Rose D'Orient is one of the two great classic rose bases from the golden age of perfumery. It is a rose otto type base with a honeyed nuance. A large number of naturals (including orris materials) mean that this base, even in small amounts, exalts and enhances every perfume in which it is used.

Famous uses: L'Origan, Chypre, Nuit de Chine, Miss Dior, Mitsouko, and many more. Between the absolute type of Rose Imperiale and the otto type of Rose D'Orient, we have all your bases covered.

products.name: Rose de Mai Absolute, France
products.description:
Rose de Mai is the name given to the absolute produced from the rosa centifolia flowers picked only during the month of May. Traditionally this was produced in Grasse but limited supply and cost meant that most of the world's supply was moved to Morocco and Egypt.

Fraterworks is, as far as we know, the only supplier to the artisan market of the true Grasse grown and produced May rose absolute. This is 100% pure and natural Rose de Mai absolute made in France. Almost all of the annual production of this absolute is taken by Dior and Chanel so we are very fortunate to be able to offer it.

This masterpiece has an indulgence that defies belief. From the naturally sweet opening notes to the astonishingly balanced spice of the dry-down accented with hints of farmyard smoke and spring rains, it evokes every aspect of the Provence countryside.

Use this oil for very special personal projects or simply as a historic treasure of indescribable beauty.

Because of the high cost of this rose de mai absolute we are also offering it in one and ten percent dilutions in natural triethyl citrate (an all-natural odourless isolate from citrus which works particularly well with rose).

We also stock LMR's Rose Centifolia Absolute from Tunisia which is a much lower cost alternative to French grown Rose de Mai.

Certified: IG Absolue Pays de Grasse.

Origin: Grasse, France
Variety: Rosa Centifolia
Part: Flowers only, May harvest only

products.name: Rose de Mai Supreme TruAbs
products.description:
Exhibiting a rich yellow colour and a viscosity matching pure and natural French Rose de Mai absolute, this is the finest replica on the market and because it is all natural it is compliant with ISO 9235.

This exclusive Fraterworks product is made in France to our very exacting specifications in order to replicate a particularly fine historic rose absolute extracted in Grasse from May blooming Centifolia roses only. Even more marvellous is the fact that it is priced at a fraction of the cost of Rose de Mai absolute.

French Rose de Mai absolute is virtually impossible to obtain outside of France as the entire annual production is locked away for the exclusive use of one or two multinational fragrance houses. 

If you are looking for other options, we offer Rose Imperiale, the once captive version of the acclaimed Rose Wardia® from the early 20th century (a masterpiece in classical perfumery,) and we also stock pure and natural Bulgarian Rose Otto and Bulgarian Rose Absolute. Check out our entire Rose Collection.

products.name: Rose Essence
products.description:
Rose Essence is a replacer base for Bulgarian rose oil. Built upon a foundation of a scientific reconstruction of the natural oil, this Fraterworks® base is unbeatable in quality, elegance and price.

Loaded with natural extracts from Bulgarian rose, this is a must-have base as rose oil gets more expensive year after year.

Rose Essence is so good you can't tell it isn't pure and natural.

This formula has been slightly updated (reference 655235A) to increase the total content of natural rose extracts.

products.name: Rose Imperiale
products.description:
Rose Imperiale is our reconstruction (developed from our own analysis and research) of a very well-known classical rose base representing the whole French rose de mai. The original was a key base in many historic fragrances but fits perfectly well in a modern context.

Fraterworks brings you the scent of glorious rose de mai in a product we consider as elegant as the pure absolute itself. This base is rich with natural materials and high class oils and absolutes found only in the finest fragrances. This is what Wardia was meant to be.

Even traces of Rose Imperiale can enhance a fragrance with its complex yet beautifully balanced formula.

products.name: Rose Maréchal Niel
products.description:
Soft and woody with a soft purr of floralcy, Rose Maréchal Niel was a much appreciated early 20th century base mimicking the scent of the beloved rose of the same name that appeared a century earlier. 

Forming part of the complex and sweet floral heart of Arpège, this rose base has all but dissapeared in the 21st century. If you are looking for a rose with that special je ne sais quoi, look no further.

Rose Maréchal Niel is loaded with rich and costly floral and wood oils and absolutes making it an expensive base to produce, however it is effective in traces and makes for a wonderful addition to a general floral bouquet.

products.name: Rose Oil “Superior” Bulgaria
products.description:
Rose oil (also known as rose otto) from Bulgaria is the premiere rose product. It is effective in traces but can be overdosed in the most luxurious floral fragrances. Rose otto is the classic pairing with jasmine absolute and blends beautifully with our signature Rose Bulgarian Absolute.

We are offering this wonderful oil pure and in a 5% and 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus which is a particularly good diluent for rose materials.

Our rose is produced by LMR and is COSMOS certified. LMR produces the highest quality Bulgarian Oil on the market bar none.

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

products.name: Rose Oil, Isparta
products.description:
We've made no secret of the fact that we love LMR when it comes to rose essential oil and so it should come as no surprise that they are also our go-to for Turkish oil.

In perfumery rose oil usually comes in two varieties: Bulgarian and Turkish. But what a lot of people don't know is that Turkish oil also comes in two varieties: regular (mostly from Afyon, Denizli, and Burdur) and deluxe (Isparta region). The Isparta oil is the finest of the Turkish rose oils and even has a special designation much in the same way that Champagne has in France.

When selecting between Bulgarian oil and Turkish oil, the differences to consider are: Bulgarian oil is sweeter and more intense, while Turkish oils are fruitier, fresher and spicier.

We are offering this wonderful oil pure and in a 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus which is a particularly good diluent for rose materials.

products.name: Rose Oil, Select
products.description:
Introducing Fraterworks® Select products, our new range designed to make exceptional perfumery materials accessible without compromising on quality. Our Bulgarian rose oil maintains the characteristic beauty of this precious material - the same origin, the same steam distillation process, the same captivating floral essence that has made Bulgarian rose the gold standard in perfumery.

This product provides an excellent entry point for perfumers, students, and enthusiasts who want to work with authentic Bulgarian rose oil at a more accessible price point. While our signature LMR rose otto remains the ultimate luxury choice, this Fraterworks® rose oil delivers the true character of Bulgarian rose - its honeyed, fresh petal notes and subtle spicy undertones - making it perfect for study, experimentation, and formulation where budget considerations matter.

Like all Fraterworks® products, this rose oil is carefully selected to ensure it meets our quality standards while offering exceptional value. It blends beautifully with jasmine, other florals, and can be used effectively in both simple and complex compositions.

Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate.

products.name: Rose Orientale
products.description:
Oriental rose bases represent or replace natural rose oil (usually of Rosa x damascena) in a fragrance. The term "oriental" or "d'Orient" referred to such places as Persia from whence the Damascus rose originated.

Two oriental rose bases dominated the 20th century; the first was Rose D'Orient (enriched with Orris concrete and used in L'Origan, Chypre, Miss Dior, and many more) and the second was this Rose Orientale (originally from Roure where its internal name was simply "No 6").

Rose Orientale found its way into some great fragrances, such as Tabu by Jean Carles, but its most famous outing was in the Ernest Beaux masterpiece Chanel No 5.

products.name: Rose Oxide
products.description:
Rose Oxide (Racemic) opens with an almost aggressive metallic freshness that cuts through compositions like a blade. This sharp, gassy-green character delivers the unmistakable scent of rose stems being snapped in half. You'll recognise its penetrating quality immediately—that bright, almost electrical sensation that makes roses feel alive rather than preserved.

This material transforms predictable rose reconstructions into dynamic, three-dimensional experiences. Use it when you need compositions to project powerfully from the bottle, creating that crucial first impression. Combine Rose Oxide with traditional rose alcohols like citronellol and geraniol to build complexity, or pair it with black pepper for unexpected vibrancy that modern perfumery demands.

Deploy Rose Oxide with extreme restraint—overdosing creates harsh, unpleasant effects that dominate rather than enhance. Working concentrations rarely exceed 1% in your concentrate, with trace amounts often sufficient for remarkable transformation. Its poor tenacity makes it purely a top-note material, disappearing within hours but leaving behind space for your heart notes to bloom.

We also stock Rose Oxide High Cis and Rose Oxide Laevo.

Rose Oxide Variations

Rose Oxide comes in three commercially significant forms, each offering distinct olfactory profiles and potency levels.

Racemic Rose Oxide (this product) contains approximately seventy-five percent cis isomers mixed with trans forms, delivering strong rose-geraniu

products.name: Rose Oxide HC
products.description:
