Rose Oxide has the most value in three forms: Racemic (cis isomer ~ 75%), [Racemic] High Cis (cis isomer ~ 90+%) and Laevo. The latter is the finest, containing only the purest odour quality and is incredibly powerful with an odour threshold of 0.5 ppb (racemic is 50 ppb). 

Of the lower cost racemic types, Rose Oxide High Cis has a beautiful scent of red roses and geranium and lacks the metallic sting of the 75% cis version. It is far easier to dose than the laevo material owing to its considerably lower strength, and is extremely diffusive. Rose Oxide High Cis is used far more often in commercial fragrances due to the affordability.

This product blends extremely well with the regular rose materials (Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol, Geraniol, Citronellol and Nerol) and with the less common Peomosa. It is lovely when combined with Black Pepper.

products.name: Rose Oxide Laevo
products.description:
Rose Oxide has the most value in three forms: Racemic (cis isomer ~ 75%), [Racemic] High Cis (cis isomer ~ 98%) and Laevo. The latter is the finest, being of the purest odour quality and incredibly powerful with an odour threshhold of 0.5 ppb (racemic is 50 ppb).

Racemic rose oxide (regular and high cis) has a beautiful scent of red roses and geranium, while Laevo Rose Oxide has that same scent but with added greenness and a radiance that has to be experienced to be truly appreciated. The merest whisper of Rose Oxide Laevo can convert a lovely rose or geranium accord into something sublime. This product is many times more expensive than the others for very good reason.

Due to the high cost and strength we sell this product pure and diluted to 10% in DPG.

products.name: Rose Queen Marie
products.description:
Rose Queen Marie (formerly Rose Parisienne) represents the scent of roseraies (rose gardens) blooming in the French royal gardens as Spring arrives. It is a modern rose base of the essential oil type (Rose D'Orient) and has been used in a number of Guerlain fragrances since the 1980s. The base is named after Queen Marie Antoinette.

This base has all the typical components of a rose oil base but in true French royal style it has a more refined and genteel character. Used in traces it imparts a subtle Rose Otto, or in overdose to create a delicate rosy canvas upon which to built an elegant multi-floral fragrance.

Rose Queen Marie suits both masculine and feminine fragrances due to its subtle freshness and it is enriched with oils and absolutes from our premium selection of finest naturals.

products.name: Rose Rouge
products.description:
Rose Rouge is a sweet classical rose base that layers French geranium with rose absolute and rose otto with other rich naturals to create an incredibly luscious and impactful rose note. Use it in traces to add natural rose to your fragrance, or in overdose for a spectacular and luxurious fragrance.

This is a classical base from the early 20th century but there is nothing old fashioned about this wonderful deep red rose.

products.name: Rose St. Columba
products.description:
Rose St. Columba is an incredibly natural sweet rose exhibiting all of the qualities of the living flower. This is our most modern rose base and it can be used alone or in combination with our other rose bases or natural rose materials.

Inspired by an analysis of the flowers from an old rose bush planted in Ponsonby, Auckland in colonial times, Rose St. Columba is a dream rose.

products.name: Rose Taïf Base
products.description:
Rose of Taïf (also known as Taïfi Rose or Wardh Taif) is the most precious rose on earth (even surpassing French grown Rose de Mai in cost). It grows only in the cool mountain air of the Taïf region of Saudi Arabia and is the variety Rosa damascena trigintipetala. Because of the difficulty in obtaining the rose oil we have crafted this ultra-luxurious replica base which is modelled on the real oil.

Our Rose Taïf base is enriched with more than 30% pure rose damascena extracts and is the closest thing you will find to the scent of true Taif rose. Use it just like you would any rose essential oil.

Due to the high cost of this base, we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural triethyl citrate which is the ideal diluent for rose products.

products.name: Rose Ultimate Extract
products.description:
This rose extract is supremely rich and sticky sweet. It is almost impossible to believe it is taken from the materials that were formerly discarded in the process of making rose oil. And the price is simply outstanding. Now any perfumer can have genuine intense natural rose in their fragrances at prices nearly matching those of quality bases.

Every perfumer needs this material. Even if you can afford lashings of Bulgarian Rose Absolute and finest Bulgarian Rose Essential Oil, there is room in your perfumer's organ for this astonishing product. LMR has outdone itself in the making of what we agree is the ultimate extract.

We also stock Rose Absolute Isparta, the elegant Turkish Rose Absolute, the production of which is the source of the waste materials upcycled in this ultimate extract.

Owing to the density of Rose Ultimate (0.96 g/mL) you get more mL than grams in each size. For example 5g gives you 5.2mL. This means that when you buy in mL you are buying less than when you buy in grams. See our FAQ below for more handy conversions and an explanation for this.

Origin: Turkey (Isparta)
Part: Upcycled Distillate
Process: Molecular Distillation

products.name: Rosemary Oil, Tunisia
products.description:
A luxurious and complex aromatic oil that has diverse uses in perfumery. This variety from Tunisia is rich in cineole (eucalyptol) which gives it a particularly vibrant top note. This type is often preferred in nature by bees for the production of a particularly delicate and fragrant honey. 

Rosemary blends incredibly well with lavenders, cedarwood, petitgrain, coumarin and the fresher resins such as labdanum, olibanum and elemi.

Origin: Tunisia
Part: Flowering tops
Method: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Rosethyl
products.description:
Rosethyl delivers a beautifully natural Rose de Mai character — green, earthy, and spicy with honeyed warmth. You get tea rose and peony facets that read as convincingly natural rather than synthetic. The tenacity is excellent, lasting well over two days on a blotter, making it unusually persistent for a rose-type material.

Use rosethyl as a core building block in your rose and peony accords. It adds the green, earthy authenticity that phenylethyl alcohol and citronellol alone cannot deliver. In ylang ylang compositions it contributes a natural rosy quality that enhances and refines the floral heart.

Pair with rose absolute, geraniol, and damascone for the most complete rose accord possible. Try it alongside hedione for a fresh, radiant rose-peony effect. Blend with citrus and green notes where a natural rose character needs to emerge gradually from a sparkling opening.

products.name: Rosewood Cayenne
products.description:
Fraterworks Rosewood Cayenne is a high quality replica of natural bois de rose (rosewood) oil from Cayenne (French Guiana). At more than 90% natural oils it fits beautifully into any composition needing fresh top notes with a touch of elegance. Use as a one for one replacer for linalool or rosewood oil. 

Historically Brazilian rosewood oil was the most common, being both elegant and plentiful. More rare and supremely beautiful was Cayenne rosewood used by only the very best fragrances houses. 

Fraterworks Rosewood Cayenne is a scentific reconstruction of this supreme oil. This is the pinnacle of elegance in rosewood replacers.

products.name: Rosewood Oil
products.description:
This is one of the great historic wood oils of perfumery. The warm rosy heart running through the golden age of French fragrance — through Guerlain, Caron, and Chanel — came from this tree. Every synthetic alternative, every reconstruction on the market exists because this material became almost impossible to source. You are looking at the original.

Open the bottle and you understand why nothing replaced it. A sweet, rosy, woody warmth that seems to glow from within — no harshness, no rough edges, just serene floral-wood radiance. The peppery-spicy opening lasts only moments before the oil settles into its true character: luminous, sweet, deeply tenacious. It sits at the exact intersection of wood and flower, belonging fully to neither, and that is precisely what made it irreplaceable.

Use it where nothing else will do. It brings a sweetness to woody compositions that cedarwood and sandalwood cannot, and a woody depth to florals that no flower oil can provide. Pair it with ylang-ylang, bergamot, oakmoss, vetiver, or sandalwood — it makes everything around it more refined. Most perfumers alive today have never worked with the real oil. This is your chance.

CITES

This oil is derived from Aniba rosaeodora, listed under CITES. If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings.

For those who prefer not to use a CITES-l

products.name: Rosyrane Super
products.description:
Rosyrane Super hits you with immediate, expansive rose — bright, green-edged, and remarkably diffusive from the first moment. A geranium-like freshness and distinctive metallic sharpness give it realism that simple rose alcohols cannot match. This is rose with presence, not delicacy. But be warned, it will absolutely take over everything you add it to so the lightest touch is needed.

Seventy-two hours on blotter gives you rose persistence that outlasts most floral materials. Use it as the core of rose and geranium accords where diffusion needs to carry through functional bases. In fine fragrance, lower doses let the metallic-green edge add complexity without overwhelming.

Blend with citronellol and geraniol for naturalistic rose, or pair with linalool and methylionones for green-floral bouquets. The metallic facet makes it particularly effective alongside hedione in modern transparent florals. Start at traces and build — the diffusion here is considerable.

products.name: Royal Leather
products.description:
While Cuir de Russie is wild, smoky and floral, Royal Leather is sophisticated, prim and proper. Royal Leather is the scent of gracefully aged bridle leather, nubuck shoes and peccary gloves. It is the scent of heritage, wealth and class.

In traces Royal Leather adds a soft purr to your scent, while an overdose makes a bold statement. Enriched with the finest animalics, resins and sandalwood, this is a must-have modern base that is extraoardinarily easy to use at up to 49% of your perfume formula! So good you can just dilute and go.

Royal Leather blends beautifully with Ambre Royale and Sandexol®.

Fraterworks® Royal Leather is a modern leather base. If you are looking for a more intense classical styled leather, see Cuir De Russie 394013.

products.name: Ruh Khus
products.description:
Ruh khus means "soul of khus" — and khus is what India calls vetiver. This is not the tidy, linear vetiver most Western perfumers know from Haiti or Madagascar. This is the wild oil, distilled from roots dug out of the alluvial soils of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, then processed in traditional copper degs in Kannauj using methods that have barely changed in centuries. Our supplier is the premiere traditional maker of this oil in India.

The oil is thick, dark brown, almost syrupy. It will keep improving with age — growing rounder, more velvety, more complex over months and years of storage. Its chemical complexity is staggering: over 150 identified sesquiterpene constituents, many still not fully characterised, with an olfactory signature that distinguishes it sharply from all cultivated vetivers.

Wild North Indian khus is consumed almost entirely within India, where it commands prices several times higher than the cultivated oil. There is a tonal quality in it — a sweetness woven through the earthiness — that cultivated vetivers simply do not possess.

Use it with restraint. Unlike sandalwood, which recedes politely into support, ruh khus insists on being noticed. Build chypre and oriental accords around it with patchouli, cinnamon bark absolute, and oakmoss. Layer it beneath sandalwood for a devastating wood foundation. In fougère structures, it provides a dark, rooted gravity that nothing synthetic can replicate.

products.name: Rum CO2
products.description:
This speciality Pure Jungle Essence (CO2 extraction) from V. MANE Fils is a true revelation. It encapsulates the purest aspects of an entire cask of rum from the most volatile alcoholic top notes to the nuanced drydown of scorched sugar. This is a must have natural ingredient for a Piña Colada type base (see our free demonstration formula below) or any scent needing a novel liquor character.

“Rum is an alcoholic beverage obtained from sugarcanes and developed in the 17th century on the Caribbean plantations. The distillate is usually aged in barrels and coloured with burnt sugar. Rum became so popular that it was an accepted currency in Europe in the 18th century and George Washington ordered 700 litres of the finest Barbados rum for his pre-election celebration.” — V. MANE Fils.

As evidenced by our Golden Seraglio formula (also below), this blends extremely well with MANE's other incredible product: Coffee Arabica Pure Jungle Essence and the magnificent Davana Essential oil from LMR.

This material is extremely strong so we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate.

Origin: Martinique
Method: CO2 Extraction

products.name: Rum Ether
products.description:
Rum Ether (Ethyl Oxyhydrate) has been discontinued but fortunately Firmenich makes this base which is excellent in its own right and can be used as a one for one replacer.

On first sniff you can have no doubt that this is a boozy material, with caramellic and buttery notes. It also has a distinct fruity quality: primarily pineapple but also some shades of banana — fresh, not overly ripened. It is also aldehydic.

While this is an obvious pick for alcoholic top notes, it works extremely well with labdanum (particularly the light variety or as a sweetener for the more volatile Cistus Oil). It would be a wonderful addition to our demo formula for Bertrand Duchaufour's Or du Serail (for Naomi Goodsir) which we've added below for completeness sake. It's aldehydic facets make it a great partner to Aldalia (Chuit Naef & Cie) or Jean Carles' classic Aldehone.

If you are looking for a rum note which is easy to use and won't overwhelm, while lasting a little longer than the very ethereal Rum CO2 extract we sell, this is it.

products.name: Sabinene, Natural
products.description:
Sabinene has an unmistakable peppery warmth—dry, woody, and immediately spicy. An oily, herbaceous quality sits behind the pepper, with faint citrus and pine-like facets adding complexity. This is the molecule responsible for much of the spicy bite we recognise in black pepper, nutmeg, and carrot seed oils.

Use sabinene to build convincing black pepper accords or to inject authentic spicy warmth into woody and herbal compositions. At two to three percent it delivers a peppery kick that reads as genuinely natural. It lifts citrus blends with spicy depth, strengthens nutmeg and cardamom reconstructions, and gives fougères and aromatic bases a dry, masculine edge.

This quality is a 100% natural isolate.

products.name: Saffron Attar Base
products.description:
Attars are beautiful extractions of precious materials, particularly rose and sandalwood. Given the high cost of the raw materials it is not surprising that these can be some of the most expensive products in the naturals trade.

Fraterworks' Saffron Attar Base (formerly known as Saffron Attar FW) is a blend which replicates the most sought after and precious extract of crocus stamens. Built around a heart of more than 30% natural Mysore Sandalwood, this base is further enriched with the most delicate trace of fine Omani Frankincense. It's worth every penny.

If you are looking for genuine distilled Saffron Attar, we also stock Zafran Attar from the esteemed M. L. Ramnarain.

Saffron Attar Base blends well with Osmanthus Flowers, Osmanthus Gold Absolute, Fleur de Cuir, Royal Leather, Olibanum CNC and LMR's Rose Ultimate Extract.

products.name: Saffron Hamra Attar Type Formula
products.description:
By far this 2021 Attar from Amouage is the richest and most luxurious of the entire range. Crafted by Cécile Zarokian, it is a beautifully concise 25-line formula, with virtually every ingredient available right here at Fraterworks. Because the naturals in this attar—Bulgarian rose oil, genuine saffron, and a whisper of cade smoke—are so precious, the supporting aroma chemicals must be impeccably pure. Fortunately, Fraterworks offers only the highest-quality aroma chemicals, ensuring a result that rivals the original.

Although some enthusiasts feel Amouage scents have lost a bit of their brilliance since Christopher Chong’s departure, the Attars remain a standout series—compact, sophisticated, and reliably elegant.

Notes: Saffron, Rose, Cade

Difficulty Level: Easy
Total Lines: 25
Naturals: 11

products.name: Saffron Oleoresin 5% PG
products.description:
Saffron oleoresin performs great in modern compositions. It combines spicy warmth with hay-like and leathery facets while maintaining blend compatibility. It shows versatility across fragrance families and maintains its signature from opening to dry down.

Saffron works well with animalic accords, woody bases, and sweet orientals as both key ingredient and modifier. The material transforms compositions into multidimensional creations that project character without overwhelming neighboring notes in complex accords.

Blends with Rose Taïf are masterful and, as you would expect, it is wonderful with classic Oud and Attar materials and spices.

While we tend to use DPG and TEC as our main solvents for perfumery raw materials, Saffron Oleoresin benefits from dilution with PG (propylene glycol) as it blends well with Saffron's polar and aromatic mix. For that reason Biolandes uses PG (referred to as MPG in their literature) and we purchase this material pre-diluted. PG blends just as well in ethanol based scents as DPG.

products.name: Safraleine®
products.description:
While Safranal is the closest material to Saffron in terms of odour, it is highly restricted and so we rely on the very elegant and luxurious Safraleine from Givaudan which has no limits at all. Safraleine is usually used in small doses (below 0.5%) as it is very potent, but in some contexts it can work in overdose.

Safraleine smells of saffron, herbs and leather with phenolic nuances and hints of tobacco and wood. It is a hugely versatile material that works wonders in leather bases or can simply provide a necessary saffron note much loved in Middle Eastern perfumery.

This is a wonderful blender and booster of our highly popular Saffron Attar FW Base.

products.name: Safranal
products.description:
Safranal is an incredibly high impact material that is felt in traces in a scent (as you can see by our Attar of Three Roses demonstration formula below.

The IFRA restriction on this material is rather tragically strict (0.012% in your finished product) but because of its high impact it is still our first choice for a saffron note. If you need to boost it you can use Safraleine which has no restriction in use and is, in its own way, a beautiful product.

Safranal smells every bit like saffron (crocus stamens). It is medicinal, herbal, phenolic and leathery.

products.name: Sage Officinalis Oil
products.description:
Sage Essential Oil opens with an immediately recognisable blast of camphoraceous intensity that announces its presence with unwavering authority. This is not a gentle herb but a forceful aromatic statement—the characteristic thujone content (think absinthe) creates a sharp, almost medicinal edge that cuts through any composition with surgical precision. Behind this assertive opening lies warming spice from camphor and subtle pine-like freshness from cineole, creating a complex aromatic architecture that defines classic masculine perfumery.

Sage Essential Oil's power lies not in volume but in impact—tiny amounts provide the authentic herbal lift that transforms pedestrian fougères into classics. Use it to sharpen lavender accords, add bite to citrus colognes, or create that distinctive masculine edge in traditional compositions. Its natural complexity provides what no synthetic can—the full-bodied herbal character that reads as authentically aromatic rather than merely fresh.

Understanding the crucial differences between Sage and Clary Sage prevents formulation disasters. Where Sage shouts with sharp camphoraceous-thujone intensity, Clary Sage whispers sweet herbaceous-tea sophistication. Sage functions as a restricted top note modifier (thujone limits: 0.11% in lip products, 1.4% in fine fragrance), while Clary Sage serves as unrestricted middle-base fixative rich in linalyl acetate. Sage's medicinal sharpness suits masculine fougères and colognes, whereas Clary Sage's hay-

products.name: Sakura Salicylate
products.description:
Sakura Salicylate smells of soft, pink petals — sweet, powdery, gently fruity, with a faint berry nuance and a warm, solar glow underneath. Takasago named it after the Japanese cherry blossom, and the connection is genuine: it captures the delicate, ephemeral quality of sakura without being literal about it.

Use it as a direct substitute for benzyl salicylate where allergen labelling is a concern — it shares the same fixative and blending properties but brings a more distinct, more beautiful floral character. It gives compositions cohesion and bloom, softening sharp edges and adding a powdery radiance to rose, muguet, and peony accords.

Pair it with linalool and rose materials for a classic cherry blossom accord, with hedione for airy, transparent florals, or with berry notes and aquatic materials for contemporary compositions. It projects well without shouting, and works best in lighter, fresher fragrances where its delicate character can breathe.

products.name: Salicynile®
products.description:
Salicynile has a luminous, sun-drenched quality — warm white flowers, orchid petals, with a fruity breath of banana and pear floating underneath. There is a subtle metallic freshness and a hint of something marine. The overall impression is solar, radiant, and extraordinarily persistent.

Salicynile gives you the warm, solar quality of materials like hexyl salicylate — but roughly five times stronger and vastly more stable. It lasts close to 200 hours on a blotter. Use it in white floral accords, orchid reconstructions, and anywhere you want fruity-floral radiance that refuses to fade.

A little goes a very long way — evaluate Salicynile well diluted, where its floral complexity unfolds. At higher doses the fruity facets dominate. Pair it with Hedione for maximum solar radiance, or with ylang ylang to amplify its natural orchid-banana character.

products.name: Sampafleur™
products.description:
Sampafleur™ is a beautiful modern base which can be used as a replacer for Jasmine Sambac absolute but in much higher doses.

Sampafleur™ is enriched with natural Jasmine Sambac absolute and other luxurious florals. This means that the base alone is sufficient to add richness and classical refinement without the addition of other expensive oils and absolutes.

Sampafleur™ blends with all our muguet and rose bases and can extend or replace Jasmine Sambac “Signature” Absolute.

products.name: Sandalore®
products.description:
Sandalore® is a creamy and warm sandalwood aroma chemical with a stronger top note than natural sandalwood and a shorter life on the blotter. It does an excellent job of adding santalaceous volume to a scent and is particularly good in blends with other sandalwood materials. Excellent as a booster and extender for natural Sandalwood oil.

Sandalore is the key sandalwood in Chanel's Égoïste (1990) by Jacques Polge (see formula below named Egotist), Guerlain's Samsara (1989) and many other truly great fragrances from the 1980s and beyond. Whilst being quite highly restricted (1.2% of the finished product) it has a wonderful ability to add a true sandalwood volume and so fairly small amounts are impactful. And at 1.2% it can be combined with other restricted materials for synergy and expanding their impact. For example Christophe Laudamiel's wonderful Amber Absolute for Tom Ford (2007) which blends 12% of Sandalore with 8% of Polysantol against a massive 28% dose of vanillin.

products.name: Sandalwood 77125 B
products.description:
Sandalwood 77125 B opens with a surprisingly bold sandalwood hit, faster and more immediate than natural Mysore oil. The heart is rich and creamy with deep milky warmth and subtle ambery-leathery complexity. It captures the precious-wood quality of true sandalwood with great fidelity.

This base gives you instant sandalwood impact wherever you need woody warmth. In oriental hearts its creaminess wraps beautifully around spice and amber, while its bold opening projects more than natural oil ever could. The trade-off is slightly less tenacity, so layer with fixatives for lasting power.

Pair with Dartanol and Hindinol to reinforce the creamy sandalwood core, or combine with vetiver and cedar for woody-masculine structures. It supports white florals surprisingly well, adding milky warmth beneath jasmine and tuberose. Rose absolute makes a particularly beautiful partner here.

products.name: Sandalwood By-Absolute
products.description:
When Biolandes first sent me a sample of this material I was completely unfamiliar with it. By-Absolutes (absolutes produced from the by-products or waste materials of essential oil or absolute manufacturing) are relatively new and it was one I had never sampled. On the first sniff I was in love. This was the truest encapsulation of the soul of historic long-aged sandalwood

This is pure nostalgia; secret rooms, vintage perfumes discovered in the back of a medicine cupboard, polished floors in now-vacant European palaces. No Sandalwood material has so excited me in many years. Once a regular part of the Biolandes offering but discontinued, it is now back and we are thrilled to be offering it.

Blend this with our marvellous Sandalwood Mysore Oil to give it an instantly aged quality—the perfect blend of luxurious modern sandalwood with the rich complex heart of 100 year old vintage oil. Or simply use it in a scent with such modern wonders as Javanol and Polysantol to naturalise and add complexity to your sandalwood notes.

Because it is highly viscous, we sell this at 50% in TEC natural.

products.name: Sandalwood Imperial
products.description:
With the skyrocketing costs of genuine Sandalwood Mysore there is a real need for a well priced alternative. Fortunately there are a plethora of incredible sandalwood aroma chemicals out there. Anyone having spent time with those aroma chemicals knows that no single material can really stand in for the natural oil. That's where Sandalwood Imperial comes in.

Sandalwood Imperial is a beautifully balanced blend of the best sandalwood chemicals enhanced with large quantities of natural wood materials to replicate that perfect balance of wood and creaminess. 

Sandalwood Imperiale is a one for one Sandalwood oil replacer. It bears the same strength, longevity and richness of the natural material and blends just as easily.

This product blends with virtually all wood chemicals and has a synergy with our highly popular Sandexol®, a powerful sandalwood base built around the most radiant and powerful aroma chemicals in the santal family. Sandalwood Imperial also works exceedingly well with Firmenich's Dreamwood® which, while very beautiful, lacks a core of natural wood materials.

products.name: Sandalwood Mysore “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Distilled from wild and plantation sandalwood trees (including the esteemed heartwood) in Mysore (Mysuru), Karnataka with a minimum age of 25 years, this is the finest quality sandalwood essential oil (मैसूर चंदन तेल). This is the authentic sandalwood of bygone days, sourced from the region formerly known as the Kingdom of Mysore (encompassing a greater area than the present day Mysore city).

This essential oil is so vibrant and alive that it dances. Packed with creamy goodness that typifies the highest quality sandalwood, this product also has a classic almost musky animal intensity in the dry down. This is not a linear B-grade sandalwood extraction, this is a rich and complex classic sandalwood oil. Wear it straight on the skin, add it to a perfume, or put it down to age for a decade. This is the gold standard of sandalwood which is why it carries our “signature” mark.

Authenticity

Our oil has a verified (Z)-α-santalol content of 47.5% and a (Z)-β-santalol content of 20.4% confirming its authenticity via ISO 3518:2022 (the international standard for verifying Sandalwood oil).

Kingdom of Mysore

Mysore sandalwood oil is extracted from trees that come from the southern parts of the Western Ghats, basically encompassing present day Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and the Konkan region of Maharashtra. The finest quality is from the forest regions of Marayoor in Kerala and present day Mysore city in Karnataka (formerly the capital of the greater Mysore kingdom). Much confusion

products.name: Sandalwood Oil “Indian”, Australia
products.description:
Unfortunately the demand for sustainable Indian sandalwood has been so low that the grower and supplier (Quintis) has fallen into receivership - the Australian equivalent of Chapter 7 Bankruptcy. Consequently once our supply of this oil runs out, we will be unable to replenish stocks.

If the notion of terroir is less important to you than the sustainability and ethics of your raw materials, this is the sandalwood for you. Not only is our Australian Santalum Album environmentally friendly, it also has the beauty and regal quality of classical Mysore sandalwood - the sandalwood of epic poems and history. Australia is now a source of both Santalum Album (“Indian” Sandalwood) and Santalum Spicatum (an Australian native). This product is the Indian variety.

Environmental Data

We can trace each batch of our Australian sandalwood oil down to the hectare of trees from which it was extracted. Using continuous distillation, our supplier is able to lower their energy needs by 75% compared to regular distillation, and of the remaining energy used over 80% is from renewable sources. The entire plantation absorbs 195,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere each year.

Carbon Zero Transport

Because we are right next door to Australia we don't need to ship our sandalwood oil half way across the planet before we offer it to you; the trip from “farm” to Fraterworks is a short carbon zero flight.

Origin: Australian
Variety: Santalum Album (Indian sandalwood)
Part: Heartwood
Method

products.name: Sandalwood Oil, Australia
products.description:
Australian Sandalwood Oil opens with surprisingly fresh, green-terpenic character—drier and sharper than you might expect from sandalwood. The signature creamy-milky notes emerge quickly but remain lighter, more yoghurt-like than the thick buttery richness of Indian sandalwood. Warm peppery spice adds complexity, while cedary-woody undertones provide the familiar sandalwood base.

This essential oil comes from Santalum spicatum, a small evergreen tree native to arid southwestern Australia. The lower santalol content (20–40% versus Indian's 70–90%) creates a distinctly different olfactory profile: fresher, woodier, and more terpenic. Crucially, S. spicatum presents earlier in a formula than other sandalwood species, projecting its character during the dry-down rather than lurking purely at the base. This makes it effective at surprisingly low concentrations (0.1–2%).

Australian Sandalwood vs Indian Sandalwood

These two sandalwood oils offer fundamentally different characters despite sharing the Santalum genus. Indian Sandalwood (Santalum album) is the richer, creamier option—soft, buttery, sensual, with thick lactonic sweetness and clove-like spice. It's intimate and enveloping, the classic sandalwood of fine perfumery.

Australian Sandalwood (Santalum spicatum) is drier, greener, and more terpenic—fresh woodshop sawdust rather than warm butter, with sharper spicy facets and cedary depth. It projects more readily and presents earlier in the dry-down.

Use Indian when you wan

products.name: Sandalwood Oil, New Caledonia
products.description:
You will find it hard to beat our price on this sublime New Caledonian essential oil from LMR, the top supplier in the world with decades of experiencing in the sandalwood field.

Despite being a different species to the Indian oil, New Caledonian sandalwood is not an inferior product but must be taken on its own merits. The oil is highly sustainable and has an odour profile very similar to the Indian oil. In fact it is so good that Chanel used it to replace the 10% Mysore Sandalwood in their famous Égoïste when cost and scarcity became problems.

LMR has partnered with a 100% kanak company located on Lifou Island in New Caledonia, in the Xepenehe village, for responsibly sourced sandalwood. LMR pre-financed all the equipment needed by our partner to build a new facility. Their Sandalwood Oil New Caledonia is "For Life" certified, showing their commitment to transparency and sustainability.

For a tiny boost and to tweak the oil in the direction of Mysore Sandalwood try this little accord:

900 Sandalwood Oil, New Caledonia
60 Amyris Oil
25 Cedarwood Virginia Oil
8.5 Firsantol
5 Guaiac Wood Oil
1.5 Polysantol

products.name: Sandela® 85 IPM
products.description:
Sandela is perhaps the most important of all the sandalwood aroma chemicals. It is very light in odour strength but it is extremely long lasting, sweet and pleasing to pretty much everyone. Sandela's odour profile is creamy, nutty and sweet. It is a beautiful material to work with and every perfumer should be using it. 

Sandela can be used in an overdose as the main Sandalwood chemical in a blend (and it is not IFRA restricted so you really can go crazy with it) or in very small amounts for its fixative properties.

Note that it may be difficult to smell initially if you haven't used it before, but in time you will develop the ability to smell it (much like Galaxolide and other very heavy molecules).

Because Sandela is very viscous, Givaudan sells it with a 15% addition of IPM.

products.name: Sandexol®
products.description:
Fraterworks Sandexol® is a powerful and radiant sandalwood base which can be used standalone as a one for one replacement for natural sandalwood oil. Sandexol is also perfect for extending sandalwood notes in a fragrance or adding a nuance to a multi-wood fond. 

Sandexol® is constructed around natural absolutes and oils in addition to the very latest radiant sandalwood molecules. This is an essential tool for all perfumers, adding beauty and exaltation to your creations. Sandexol® is perfect for creating a luxurious woody foundation for modern gourmand fragrances.

products.name: Sarriette Base 199618
products.description:
Sarriette Base 199618 is a Firmenich aromatic herbal specialty of extraordinary potency. The opening is dry and thyme-like with a sharp, piercing green edge, settling into vegetal pepper notes and cool spearmint. It smells like wild savory growing on a sun-baked Mediterranean hillside, intensified tenfold.

This base transforms fougeres and aromatic compositions with a raw, wild herbal character that polished lavender and rosemary alone cannot achieve. Use it to add untamed Mediterranean intensity to your accords. It reinforces and lifts other herbal notes, making them feel more vivid and natural.

Dilute well before blending — this is extraordinarily powerful and a single drop changes a composition. Pair with lavender, oakmoss, and coumarin for classic fougere construction. Try it alongside pine, juniper, and cedarwood for wild forest accords that smell genuinely alive.

products.name: Saxon Moss (Mousse de Saxe)
products.description:
The famed Mousse de Saxe base has been, until now, long gone — although modernised bases have appeared in recent years as historic perfumery becomes popular once again. Fraterworks recreation of the original, which we call Saxon Moss, is true to the original Mousse de Saxe as we can make it.

Rich with naturals, including a megadose of Mysore sandalwood, this wonderful mossy leathery base can be felt at less than 1% of a fragrance yet it can still be used in large amounts (as the original was) in such fragrances as Nuit de Noel by Caron (formula below) and Chanel No 19.

The original Mousse de Saxe contained musk xylene which we have judiciously replaced in our Saxon Moss base for IFRA compliance.

products.name: Scent Strips, 100 Pack
products.description:
Scent strips are an essential tool for perfumers. Our high quality strips (also known as mouillettes) are made from luxurious acid free card stock 400 microns thick. This stock is environmentally friendly and contains no glues or resins — just pure and natural paper.

Each white strip (sold in sets of 100) measures 20mm by 160mm and has a crease down the centre to allow you to fold the strip when dipping into bottles with small mouths. The crease runs end to end.

These strips are designed with the perfumer in mind and can be used for soaking (via dipping) or spraying (hold the wide end and spray the pointed end).

Our scent strips are made in New Zealand.

NOTE: The stand pictured here does not come with the scent strips.

products.name: Scentenal®
products.description:
Scentenal opens with crisp, watery freshness that immediately reads as sea breeze and coastal air. A green floral quality follows, clean and translucent, with hints of fresh cucumber skin and wet moss. The overall impression is bracing, crystalline, and remarkably long-lasting.

This is one of the most powerful marine-fresh materials in perfumery, effective at remarkably low doses. Use it to enhance and modify other ozonic materials or to add watery green sparkle to chypres and colognes. It performs exceptionally well in masculine freshness and sheer floral compositions.

Start at trace levels and build up, as Scentenal's tenacity on blotter exceeds two weeks. Combine with Calone for deeper aquatic structures, or add to violet-leaf and orris notes for a dewy, naturalistic effect. A tiny addition lifts any composition with transparent, ozonic brightness.

It's strong, so we're offering it diluted and pure.

products.name: Schisandra Fruit CO2
products.description:
Schisandra does not smell like a bright berry. The first impression is warm, woody, and softly balsamic — dried plums and goji berries layered over a peppery, lightly smoky base. It reads as comforting and rooty, more forest floor than fruit bowl.

Use it as a blender to add quiet complexity to orientals, spiced compositions, and woody-fruity accords. It fills gaps between notes rather than standing alone. Pair with ylang ylang, patchouli, and frankincense for a dark, contemplative base with an unusual fruity undertow.

This is Schisandra chinensis — the legendary "five-flavour berry" of Chinese medicine, named for possessing all five basic tastes simultaneously. It grows wild in the forests of Manchuria and the Russian Far East. The CO2 extract is still uncommon in perfumery — an explorer's material.

products.name: Sclareolate®
products.description:
Sclareolate opens with crystalline freshness that sits between linalool and linalyl acetate, capturing the aromatic brightness of clary sage within a white floral framework. This transparency makes it invaluable when you need clean radiance without heaviness. Its diffusive nature lifts entire compositions while maintaining remarkable stability across all media.

This material excels at bridging citrus tops with floral hearts, particularly in lavender-cologne structures where its aromatic facets enhance naturalness. Use it to modernise classic fougères or add sparkle to white floral bouquets. In functional fragrances, Sclareolate maintains its character through aggressive bases where traditional florals might distort or disappear entirely.

Deploy Sclareolate from trace amounts for subtle refinement up to 10% for pronounced fresh-floral impact. It partners brilliantly with bergamot and lavender in masculine structures, while in feminine accords it amplifies lily-of-the-valley and freesia notes. Consider it your go-to for adding contemporary freshness to any composition requiring both immediate appeal and lasting radiance.

products.name: Seaweed Fucus Absolute
products.description:
Fucus absolute hits you with raw, salty iodine and an immediate phenolic dryness — seaweed drying on rocks after a storm, with smoke and leather underneath. It is far rougher and more confrontational than Laminaria absolute. Where Laminaria is refined, Fucus is feral. It is extraordinarily powerful.

Use it when you want marine character with real bite — in dark chypres, leather accords, and compositions that need an animalic, oceanic edge. It reads more like wet harbour rope and weathered wood than clean seaside air. On dilution it becomes greener and more aquatic, with mineral-oyster facets emerging in the drydown. Always work from heavy dilution.

Three seaweeds, three tools.

We carry three seaweed materials — they are not interchangeable. 

Seaweed Fucus Absolute (bladderwrack) is the roughest and most animalic — salty, phenolic, with harbour-side leather. That's this product.

Laminaria absolute is the most refined: iodine into mushroom and cocoa, with mossy depth.

Red Seaweed CO₂ (Palmaria palmata) from V. MANE Fils is almost gourmand: umami richness and savoury briny depth with none of the harshness. Layer all three for the most complete natural marine accord you can build.

products.name: Seaweed Laminaria Absolute
products.description:
Briny iodine, wet rocks, seaweed drying in the sun — laminaria absolute is the genuine smell of the Atlantic coast. It has nothing in common with synthetic aquatic notes. The drydown shifts into dark mushroom, walnut, and cocoa, finishing mossy and woody.

Use laminaria wherever you want marine character that smells like a real coastline. In chypres, it fills the dark, grounding role of oakmoss but with an oceanic identity. A trace in green or woody compositions adds mystery and a convincing sense of place.

Pair it with oakmoss and vetiver for a full coastal chypre, or with labdanum and cypriol for dark marine depth. The cocoa-mushroom drydown works surprisingly well alongside tobacco and leather notes. Work from a dilution — it is extremely powerful.

This is a Payan Bertrand Signature material.

Three seaweeds, three tools.

We carry three seaweed materials — they are not interchangeable. Laminaria absolute (this one) is the most refined: iodine into mushroom and cocoa, with mossy depth.

Seaweed Fucus Absolute (bladderwrack) is rawer — saltier, greener, overtly phenolic, with harbour-side roughness that reads more animalic than marine.

Red Seaweed CO₂ (Palmaria palmata) from V. MANE Fils is almost gourmand: umami richness and savoury briny depth with none of the harshness. Layer all three for the most complete natural marine accord you can build.

products.name: Sesame SFE Absolute
products.description:
Sesame SFE Absolute opens with unmistakable roasted warmth — toasted bread, caramelised hazelnuts, and a coffee-like richness that signals gourmand territory immediately. A balsamic woody undertone sits beneath the nuttiness. The effect is deeply comforting and remarkably true to freshly toasted sesame seeds.

Use Sesame SFE to boost and enrich gourmand accords — it adds volume and naturalistic warmth that synthetic alternatives struggle to match. This Firmenich CO2 extract pairs brilliantly with vanilla, tonka, and amber bases. Even small additions transform a composition's gourmand credibility.

Blend with coffee absolute and vanillin for a rich café accord, or layer beneath sandalwood and benzoin for an oriental with toasted depth. Supercritical CO2 extraction captures the complete aromatic profile of the seed without heat damage. Sesame remains rare in perfumery — your compositions will stand apart.

A costly material, we dilute this to 10% in natural triethyl citrate. Note that the 10% solution also includes 10% food grade ethanol. There are no denaturants or non-natural additions to this product.

products.name: Shamama
products.description:
Shamama is one of the great traditional Indian attars: warm, spicy, herbal, woody, resinous, and long-lasting. It may be worn directly as a perfume oil, but it is also widely used as a compounding base in mukhallat, bakhoor, incense, tobacco, and oriental-style perfume blends.

Shamama opens with a warm spice-smoke accord — clove, cinnamon, cardamom and nutmeg over roasted cypriol, spikenard and valerian roots. The sandalwood base sits underneath, threaded with charila lichen and choya smoke. A faint floral lift from rose, jasmine and saffron lights up the heart.

Use Shamama as the anchor of orientals, mukhallats and bakhoor compositions where you want dense Indian complexity in one material. A few drops bind disparate notes into a unified whole, scaffolding rose, oud, ambergris and saffron. In tobacco and incense bases it adds heating animalic depth lighter florals cannot reach.

This Shamama is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, one of the oldest continuously operating distilleries in Kannauj. The Kapoor family has been distilling for five generations using the traditional deg-bhapka method. Their Shamama is widely considered among the finest examples of the form.

For more information on how Shamama are made, read our article Oils and Attars of Indian and Oriental Perfumery.

products.name: Shangralide Oliffac
products.description:
Shangralide Oliffac hits you first with a feral, leathery punch - almost aggressive neat, with a phenolic bite that recalls wet animal hide. Give it time and that rawness melts into a honeyed, skin-warm sweetness. The dry-down is creamy, powdery, and astonishingly long-lived on paper and skin alike.

This IFF specialty base is built on a Galaxolide skeleton but bears almost no resemblance to standard white musks. Trace amounts of phenylacetic acid and other animalic modifiers give it a convincingly "biological" character that rounds sharp indoles in jasmine and tuberose, softens synthetic edges in woody accords, and anchors leather compositions with raw-skin realism. Layer it with macrocyclic musks like Ambrettolide for a musk cocktail that has both volume and radiance.

Try Shangralide at low doses to add a living, breathing quality to florals and ambers. Push it higher in leather and oud accords where you want unmistakable animalic grit. Remember that this material transforms radically on dilution — what smells aggressive in the bottle becomes seductive and intimate below one percent.

For a truer-to-nature deer musk base, we recommend Tonkin Intense or Nearly Deer which are built around laevo muscone, the key musk molecule in deer musk, rather than the cheaper Galaxolide and white musks in other third party bases.

products.name: Siberian Castoreum Tincture 3%
products.description:
Siberian castoreum has historically been considered inferior to the Canadian variety, but upon smelling this beautiful tincture one can't help but wonder if cold-war politics may have had a part to play in that judgement. 

This tincture is, in our opinion, finer than Canadian and more nuanced. While both varieties have a soft smokiness the main difference is that the Siberian product has a more profoundly natural leather note with fewer fruity aspects making it drier.

This is our favourite castoreum tincture, a tincture which transports you to the wintery woodlands of ancient Russia so beloved by Chanel perfumer Ernest Beaux.

Our Siberian castoreum tincture is made in exactly the same way as all of our tinctures, using finest pure and natural alcohol.

‘Castoreum [tincture's] warm, animal, leather-like sweet odour makes it an interesting item in “men's perfumes”, fougeres, chypres, Oriental bases, leather notes, Tabac bases, etc. [It blends] particularly well with ambra notes, calamus, cananga, cedarwood Atlas, chamomile moroccan, creosol, labdanum products, isoeugenol, oakmoss products, sandalwood oil, […] etc.’ — S. Arctander. Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin, Carol Stream: Allured Publishing Corporation, 2008, pp. 136–137.

French Name: Infusion de Castoréum

products.name: Silvanone® Supra
products.description:
Silvanone Supra opens with a soft, sweet powderiness - warm skin dusted with talc, underscored by a gentle animalic presence that recalls vintage nitromusks without their harshness. There is a milky, almost lactonic quality beneath the powder. The effect is intimate, enveloping, and unmistakably musky.

This Givaudan macrocyclic musk is a blend of cyclohexadecanolide and cyclopentadecanone (Exaltone), combining the powdery sweetness of a macrocyclic lactone with the animalic warmth of a macrocyclic ketone. Use it in orientals and ambers where you need musk that radiates rather than merely sits. It brings a living, skin-like warmth to white florals and adds powdery depth to spicy carnation accords.

Silvanone Supra is extraordinarily tenacious—it will last months on a blotter. You can dose it generously, up to twenty percent in your concentrate, without distortion. Pair it with woody-amber bases for rich oriental foundations, with Hedione and jasmine for radiant white florals, or layer it with other musks to build complex, multifaceted skin accords.

products.name: Silvial®
products.description:
Silvial opens with a bright floral burst that feels clean and watery, followed by a subtle sparkle that hints at citrus zest. This powerful muguet material delivers crystalline lily of the valley freshness without the heavy sweetness of older alternatives. You'll find its marine quality and aldehydic touch particularly valuable when modernising classic floral structures.

At low levels Silvial refreshes top notes and adds a watery floral sheen, perfect for modern colognes. Push it into the mid-range and it becomes the star of a muguet accord, often paired with traces of hydroxycitronellal or rose oxide for added petal realism. The material blends beautifully with lilac materials, rose alcohols, styrax and methylionones . Its aldehydic character provides exceptional lift to dense orientals whilst the marine facet brings contemporary freshness to woody bases.

Use Silvial between 1-15% in fine fragrance, capping around 5% to prevent sharpness. Reserve higher dosages up to 20% for functional products where bloom after dilution is vital. The material shows excellent tenacity at one week on blotter with good substantivity both damp and dry. Combine with other modern muguet materials like Nympheal or Hivernal® Neo to build complex lily accords that replace restricted aldehydes.

products.name: Sinensal Natural ex Orange
products.description:
Sinensal is what gives orange oil its deep, juicy richness — isolated here from the peel in its natural form. The aroma is sweet, full-bodied orange with a powdery, mandarin-like quality. This smells like the heart of a ripe orange, concentrated and intensified far beyond standard orange oil.

Use sinensal to extend your orange top notes deep into the heart of a composition. Where standard orange oil fades in minutes, this natural isolate persists for hours — remarkable staying power for a citrus material. It adds depth and juiciness to citrus accords that synthetic alternatives cannot match.

Pair with bergamot and neroli for a rich, natural hesperidic accord. Try it alongside blood orange and nootkatone for the most complete citrus spectrum possible. Blend with petitgrain and orange flower absolute to build orange blossom compositions rooted in authentic orange character.

products.name: Skatole 1% DPG
products.description:
Skatole is undoubtedly one of the strongest and most repellent chemicals the perfumer has to work with, nevertheless it remains an indispensable item for many reasons. Traces of skatole can impart a sense of true naturalness to a floral bouquet (impossible to achieve with any other material), while a touch in excess can create the illusion of dying flowers wilting as they gracefully expire.

In high doses skatole contributes a distinctly animal quality which can, as if by magic, be tamed by high doses of natural sandalwood oil with which it has an inimitable synergy. Skatole is frequently found as the chief component in civet compounds.

Skatole can be a useful booster for indole where an excess of that related aromachemical can introduce an unwanted naphtholenic character. Skatole, like indole, can be highly discolouring which should be borne in mind when using it in fragrances demanding little to no colour.

We supply skatole in a 1% solution with DPG but we recommend diluting it further to 0.1% or even 0.01% for most practical needs.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Solafleur™
products.description:
Solafleur is a modern multifloral base of great softness and finesse. It blends together delicate materials with natural oils to make a high-use base that sits perfectly at the heart of a modern fragrance. 

Solafleur smells like a tranquil summer day at the beachside: suntan lotion, warm sand and the scent of light florals floating on a gentle breeze. In the scent of Solafleur you can almost hear the distant laughter of children at play and seabirds crooning from above frothy waves.

Solafleur's blends with Gardenia J. Ellis, Neroli Supreme, Tuberose Supreme and Rose Blanche (white rose) are sublime, but it also creates beautiful accords with Pink Acacia, Bouvardia DL, Amarante, Muguet 16, Mellitis, Lilac A07, Lyfral®, Dianthine Extra, Prunol SP, and Saxon Moss.

products.name: Solgard®
products.description:
Solgard® is a proprietary blend of virtually odourless industry standard UV blockers, conditioners and preservatives for fine fragrances. Now your products can benefit from the very same protection used by all the major fragrance producers. 

Solgard offers protection from UVA and UVB rays, potentially reducing discolouration and changes to the odour profile due to exposure to light.

To support long-term stability, Solgard contains Tocopherol (Vitamin E) as its antioxidant preservative system. This natural antioxidant helps extend shelf life without the labelling and perception issues sometimes associated with synthetic stabilisers. The previous Solgard® B variant, which contained BHT, has been discontinued and is no longer supplied.

Solgard also contains octyl salicylate, parsol (Neo Heliopan®) and avobenzone.

Typical use is to pre-fix your perfumers alcohol with 1% Solgard (10 grams of Solgard per kg of ethanol). Alternatively, Solgard can be safely added directly to your fragrance juice, with typical use from 0.5% – 4%. British, New Zealand and European destined fragrances should not contain more than 15% Solgard.

You can boost the effects of Solgard® with Oxynex® ST.

Solgard® is a registered trademark [1229641] of Frater Perfumes Ltd. Because this product is designed to be added to blends in quantities over which Frater Perfumes has no control we make no warranty or guarantees as to its suitability for your fragrances.

Solgard® is for commercial use only and is not

products.name: Sophira
products.description:
Sophira is the restoration of the classical base Sophora, an artistic copy (created by Marius Reboul of Roure) of the competing Cedarome base by Chuit Naef & Cie. In Sophira, Reboul focussed on the intense vetiver quality of the original base which was a balance of vetiver and cedarwood.

Sophira formed the core of Un Air Embaumé by Rigaud in 1912 combined with a healthy dose of Jasmin Blanc and it was key to Tabac Blond by Caron in 1919. It was also used in the magnificent Nuit de Chine (1911, Rosine) in harmony with Rose D'Orient and sandalwood. Like most bases of the era, Sophira is built around a delicate balance of other bases, resulting in a very complex and rich foundation for your fragrances.

NOTE: This product may crystallise slightly in cold environments. Apply gentle heat to dissolve.

products.name: Sotolone
products.description:
Sotolone is an incredibly powerful sweet material commonly used in flavours but absolutely wonderful for modern gourmand fragrances. Depending on the dose sotolone fluctuates between the penetrating scent of sugar and the exotic and spiced warmth of fenugreek. A truly remarkable sweetener that blends beautifully with members of the maltol family and other sweet "edibles" such as strawberry and maple furanone.

This material is so powerful and long-lasting that we are offering it at 10% and 1% dilution in DPG and we highly recommend diluting it further to 0.1% or even 0.01%, both levels at which it still performs well.

products.name: Southernwood Oil
products.description:
Opening with a light tangerine note mixed with camphor, pine and wormwood, this rare oil was called both Lad's Love and maiden's ruin in the 18th and 19th centuries because of its alleged aphrodisiacal properties and the promise to cure baldness and grow beards in men. It was frequently used as part of a church nosegay (a small bouquet of flowers) sniffed during long church sermons to keep the holder awake and to mask the malodours of large gatherings of people. The French called it "garderobe" for its reputation protecting clothes from moths.

The pine-woody undertones add structure, while bitter wormwood character (for it is a member of the artemesia genus along with Armoise) provides the distinctive signature of that genus. Green herbaceous depth emerges as the oil develops, creating a profile that feels simultaneously medicinal and refreshing.

Work with Southernwood Oil sparingly—its intensity requires respect. Use it in fougère and chypre compositions where bitter herbal notes provide complexity, or in masculine aromatics seeking green freshness with character. The camphoraceous lift works beautifully alongside lavender, rosemary, and other aromatic herbs. Blend with oakmoss, coumarin, and citrus oils for novel aromatic effects. Its wormwood-like bitterness adds sophisticated depth to otherwise sweet compositions.

All in all, this is an unusual and interesting oil that deserves a wider use in modern perfumery.

products.name: Spearmint “Signature” Oil
products.description:
This is the most refined spearmint oil we have ever experienced! From a single estate in England, this oil has perfectly balanced top notes which bear the signature spearmint scent from the very first sniff. Use small amounts to add vibrance and freshness to top notes, both masculine and feminine, or overdose it for a characterful minty scent.

You will never want another spearmint oil after trying our Signature product.

Origin: England
Variety: Mentha spicata L.
Part: Leaves
Method: Steam distillation at source and aged 2 years

products.name: Special Order Items
products.description:
Sometimes you need a material that isn't listed for sale but we have stock in our warehouse. Contact us to confirm availability and pricing and use this product to add the necessary value to your cart.

For a $40 special order, add two $20 items to your cart. For a $100 add a $100 item. If you need to pay $120 add a $100 item and a $20 item.

When checking out be sure to tell us in the order notes what the special order is to pay for.

products.name: Spicyrup™
products.description:
There is no denying it: we love the naturals from V. MANE Fils, but we also love their bases, an area in which we ourselves are specialists. Spicyrup™ is one such base. Built around an overdose of the MANE captive Presantone H™, this base opens with dank earthiness and dries down into a rich gourmand accord reminiscent of carrot cake, caramel, liquorice, and spices.

An incredibly unique and unusual base, the possibilities are endless. The loamy opening is crying out for a rich patchouli pairing, while the exceptionally balanced, vanilla-leaning dry down would work beautifully with a classic Tabu-like blend, albeit in a highly modernised context.

products.name: Spiked Ginger Lily Oil
products.description:
Do not expect ginger — this is something else entirely. The oil opens fresh and camphoraceous, almost eucalyptus-like, then unfolds into a rich, warm cinnamon-spice body of extraordinary depth. The drydown is woody and balsamic, less sweet but still warmly spiced.

Use it in balsamic, woody, and heavy-floral bases where you want warm cinnamon-spice without using actual cinnamon oil. It works beautifully in lavender and lavandin compositions, adding spicy richness and remarkable tenacity. Blends well with styrax, benzoin, sandalwood, and ionones.

This is Hedychium spicatum — a Himalayan ginger lily distilled from its rhizomes, known in India as kapur kachri and in Japanese perfumery as sanna. Arctander considered it exceptionally versatile but noted it was never regularly available outside Asia. That scarcity persists today (unless you are a Fraterworks customer!)

products.name: Spikenard Oil
products.description:
Spikenard (Jatamansi) hits the nose with deep, sweet earth — damp forest floor, rooty warmth, and a musky-animalic depth that is entirely its own. There are facets of chocolate, ginger, cardamom, and Atlas cedarwood, but the overall impression is darker and more primordial than any of those. It smells ancient.

Use it as a base note in orientals, heavy florals, and woody-animalic compositions. It blends naturally with patchouli, vetiver, labdanum, and oakmoss — anywhere you want earthy depth and fixation. A single drop anchors a formula and extends the life of everything above it.

This is one of the oldest perfume materials on earth — the nard of the Bible, burned by Nero and used by St Mary Magdalene to anoint the feet of Christ. It grows wild above 3,000 metres in the Himalayas and is still harvested by hand from remote slopes. Scarce, irreplaceable, and profoundly beautiful.

Spikenard essential oil is derived from a species listed in CITES Appendix II. However, the essential oil itself is generally excluded from CITES controls under the annotation that applies to this species. For that reason, a CITES export, re-export, or certificate of origin is not usually required for normal trade in the oil.

Import requirements can still vary by country, and some jurisdictions may have their own customs or wildlife rules. We recommend checking with your local authorities before ordering if you are unsure.

products.name: Spirambrene
products.description:
Spirambrene is a woody and elegant amber material with extremely good diffusion. It ranks amongst the very best of the woody chemicals (with Dextro Norlimbanol, Cedroxyde, Orbitone and others). It is rare to find in small traces but really should be part of every perfumer's palette.

Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) discusses the chemical: “Spirambrene is a nice, strong chemical with a closeness to boisambrene forte, norlimbanol, cedroxyde and cedramber. It is somewhat more seaweed-like than the above and imparts important velvety nuances to woody notes. Again, I believe it is a chemical that has a bright future in our industry. It is being widely used in fragrances such as Kenzo for Men (0.8%), Eden, Gio (0.85%) and Agua Fresca (0.3%) by Adolfo Dominguez, among many others.”

Givaudan describes it thus: “Spirambrene blends well with sparkling, green, spicy and aldehydic top notes. It is an interesting complement in woody accords for providing a diffusive ambery effect. Due to its high impact, it produces unique and original effects when combined with other woody elements.”

Featured in such fragrances as Duro by Nasomato (0.3%), Enigma by Roja Dove (0.4%), Black Agar Givco (1%), Himalaya by Creed (0.55%), 

Blends beautifully with Dextro Norlimbanol, Muscenone, Muscone Laevo, Exaltolide and all the amber chemicals.

products.name: Spirogalbanone
products.description:
Spirogalbanone is pure green, and plenty of it. It smells like a freshly snapped flower stem: sharp, cool and sappy, with the clean bite of galbanum. A juicy green-pineapple facet keeps it bright and fresh rather than bitter or resinous.

Use it to build a green galbanum signature that holds. Where galbanum oil and other green materials flash and fade, this one keeps its sharp, sappy freshness deep into the drydown, anchoring the green of a composition. It lends green florals and chypres a crisp, natural stem realism.

Because it lingers, it doubles as a quiet fixative for greenery: add a trace under violet leaf, cis-3-hexenol or other fast green notes to stop them vanishing. Blend it with Florhydral for a fresh cut-flower, flower-shop accord. A little goes a long way, so dose with restraint.

products.name: Squalane
products.description:
Squalane is a completely odourless, colourless carrier oil that adds nothing to the scent of your composition. It absorbs into skin quickly, leaving a silky, non-greasy finish rather than the oily residue of heavier carriers. This makes it ideal for perfume oils and roll-on fragrances.

Your skin produces squalene naturally as part of its own sebum — squalane is the stabilised version, hydrogenated to prevent oxidation. This means it absorbs readily and feels familiar on skin rather than sitting on the surface. It will not go rancid, turn yellow, or develop off-notes over time.

Use squalane anywhere you would use jojoba or fractionated coconut oil, but with a lighter feel and longer shelf life. It is non-comedogenic and suitable for face-safe formulations. This olive-derived version is identical in every functional way to sugarcane squalane.

products.name: Star Anise Oil
products.description:
Leverage Star Anise for its remarkable ability to impart immediate character and warmth, bridging top and middle phases effectively. Its complex undertones offer versatility beyond the expected liquorice facet, adding depth to aromatic Fougères and even floral compositions. This is a cornerstone spice material.

While both Star Anise oil (Illicium verum) and Anise oil (Pimpinella anisum) share a dominant sweet, liquorice-like aroma from trans-anethole, Star Anise is botanically distinct, often stronger, woodier, and contains IFRA regulated estragole (also found in tarragon oil), unlike Anise.

At low temperatures this oil may crystallise. In that case, simply warm to melt.

products.name: Starfleur™ 40
products.description:
Starfleur smells like a handful of fresh spring flowers: lily of the valley and freesia, clean and see-through, with a cool green edge. A soft citrus brightness lifts the top. It reads natural and dewy, the floralcy transparent rather than heavy or soapy.

Use it to build fresh muguet, freesia and lily accords with real body and lift. It gives white florals a modern, watery transparency and a natural, just-picked feel. Pair it with hydroxycitronellal, citronellol and a trace of indole to round out a full lily-of-the-valley.

products.name: Stemone®
products.description:
With Fig Leaf prohibited by IFRA a quality fig note must be made synthetically. Enter Stemone — intensely green, leafy and ivy-like. It is really the most perfect way to recreate the note of figs and, in the words of one perfume critic in reviewing Fig My Love (2016) by Christophe Laudamiel for The Zoo: “It is often based on stemone, a molecule bearing the unusual oxime -NOH functional group, which always confers a green-camphoraceous feel to molecules. Many perfumers have chosen to bend this aromachemical towards a more natural accord. I think the fig tree smells so chemical in the first place that there’s no point in pretending. Laudamiel agrees[.]”

A masterpiece of subtle perfumery, Balade Sauvage (2018) by François Demachy for Dior, also builds its central accord around the classic fig fruit duo of Stemone (0.02%) and Gamma Octalactone (0.07%) with fig tree nuances from Triplal (0.02%) and Liffarome (0.09%).

This material has no restrictions so you can approach it with gay abandon, but beware: this is no delicate snowflake; traces can come screaming to the fore if not balanced right.

Other uses that may help as a guide are the must-have Oscar de la Renta Pour Lui (1980) 1.8% overdose, 0.15% in Azzaro Pour Homme (1978, Gerard Anthony & Richard Wirtz), Ombre Nomade's (2018) 0.004% trace from Louis Vuitton, and 0.07% in Philosykos by Diptyque.

products.name: Strawberiff
products.description:
In high dilution, Strawberiff reads as jammy ripe strawberry with a sour, slightly sweaty edge and a faint woody undertone. Concentrated, the sweaty-acidic side dominates and the fruity note retreats so care is needed.

Use it in trace amounts to add realism to strawberry, raspberry, blackcurrant and tropical fruit accords. It supplies the fermented-jam character that pure fruity materials cannot achieve alone. It also bridges fruity tops to gourmand bases by adding a sweaty, lactic-fruit nuance.

Pair with strawberry glycidate, gamma undecalactone and beta damascenone for a complete strawberry accord. A trace under blackcurrant or passionfruit lifts the natural ripeness without adding sugar. Dose extremely low — one drop too many and the whole composition turns rancid.

products.name: Strawberry Furanone
products.description:
This material opens with an intensely sweet, almost burnt caramel character that transforms dramatically upon dilution. At proper concentrations below 1%, you'll discover the celebrated cotton candy sweetness alongside jammy strawberry and cooked pineapple notes. The pyrogenic facets that dominate the neat material recede, allowing the true fruity-gourmand heart to blossom magnificently.

Use Strawberry Furanone as the cornerstone of realistic strawberry and pineapple accords where it provides the essential cooked, jammy character. Combine it with Ethyl Maltol to create an exponentially enhanced cotton candy effect—these two materials exhibit remarkable synergy that multiplies their individual sweetness. In fruity-florals, traces transform fresh notes into succulent, edible compositions with remarkable tenacity.

Apply this material sparingly—its extraordinary potency means even 0.1% additions create noticeable effects. For strawberry accords, pair with ethyl butyrate for juiciness and gamma-decalactone for creamy ripeness. This versatile sweetener enhances virtually any composition when used in trace amounts, adding warmth and rounded sweetness.

products.name: Strawberry Furanone Ethyl Ether
products.description:
Do not confuse this with Strawberry Furanone. Where the parent molecule is all jammy-sweet strawberry and cooked pineapple, the Ethyl Ether is a different beast entirely — darker, browner, less fruity. Think burnt sugar scraped from a crème brûlée, maple syrup reduced to a thick glaze, the deep caramel note in aged tobacco. It occurs naturally in coffee and contributes to that rich, roasted sweetness.

Use it wherever you need brown-sweet warmth without obvious fruitiness. It thickens amber accords, gives body to vanilla bases, and adds a burnt-sugar facet to tobacco compositions that pure vanillin cannot provide. Try it alongside tonka bean, benzoin, and labdanum for a dark gourmand base. It also works in trace amounts to warm otherwise clean compositions — a touch in a white floral gives an unexpected caramelised depth.

Like all furanones it is powerful and must be dosed carefully. Start low. At high concentrations it can become cloying and one-dimensional, but at trace levels it adds a warmth and sweetness that feels completely natural — as though the composition were lit from within.

products.name: Strawberry Glycidate
products.description:
Ethyl Methyl Phenyl Glycidate or EMPG (often called Strawberry Aldehyde or Aldehyde C-16,) is not an aldehyde but rather a glycidic ester which smells of strawberry. It is one of the three most common fruit materials (the others being Undecalactone Gamma AKA Aldehyde C-14, Peach and Nonalactone Gamma AKA Aldehyde C-18, Coconut — also misnomers).

While large amounts can be used, this material is very high impact and tiny amounts can be felt through the entire life of a fragrance.

EMPG blends extremely well with the aliphatic aldehydes and is particularly nice as a nuancer to rose notes. Blends with ionones are classic. Use it with other fruity products such as Prunol SP or Persicol to create a highly modern gourmand scent.

products.name: Styrallyl Acetate
products.description:
Styrallyl Acetate (or Gardenol) is a green top note with a very distinctive odour that separates it from the rest of the family. Vaguely smelling like facets of Gardenia, but mostly like a very strong fruity green chemical of low tenacity, Styrallyl Acetate is surprisingly easy to blend and works well with Galbanum (and related chemicals like Neobutenone Alpha) and other fruity top notes like Allyl Amyl Glycolate.

In our opinion, no blend yet surpasses the wonderfully creative accord of 2:1 Styrallyl Acetate and Citronella Oil featured as the top note of Ma Griffe by Jean Carles for Carven in 1946.

Styrallyl Acetate is an essential material for perfumers.

products.name: Styrax Oil, Honduras
products.description:
Styrax (or more correctly storax) is a sweet and delicate material which blends well with the other classic perfumery resins; it works well as a fixative (especially for iris notes).

Styrax is most commonly found as a resinoid or absolute, but this more rare hexane free essential oil is a beautiful material for florals, particularly delicates ones such as muguet.

Felt more in the top notes but still a classic resinous dry down, this is really quite a valuable material at a very good price.

The proper naming conventions for all balsams is:

Crude Balsam → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil [this product]
Crude Balsam → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resinoid
Crude Balsam → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [and sometimes resinoid]

While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent).

Resinoid → Alcohol Extraction → Absolute

NOTE: This is IFRA compliant styrax oil

Country of Origin: Honduras
Part: Tree exudate
Method of production: Steam distillation at source

products.name: Styrax Resinoid EAL, Wild
products.description:
Styrax (or more correctly storax) resinoid is a sweet and delicate material which blends wonderfully with the other classic perfumery resins; it works well as a fixative (especially for iris notes).

These days most extracts on the market suffer from a pronounced styrene note (the plastic smell of polystyrene) which, being far from the genuine odour of styrax, more closely resembles the smell of an old mechanic's shop. As pleasant an odour as that may be for some, it has no place in the scent profile of styrax.

This styrax resinoid is sweet, cinnamic, vanilla, subtly spicy and enticing. It is extracted from the raw balsam of wild Liquidambar styraciflua trees (commonly known as American sweetgum or hazel pine) using just-warm alcohol (hence the EAL designation in the name). This produces a “resin absolute” as opposed to a true resinoid or absolute. However, the market has generally taken to referring to these styrax materials as resinoids and so we are using the name of the manufacturer. The proper naming conventions for all balsams is:

Crude Balsam → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil
Crude Balsam → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resinoid
Crude Balsam → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [and sometimes resinoid]

While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent).

R

products.name: Sublimolide™
products.description:
Sublimolide™ is the V. MANE Fils produced version of Scentolide, the high cis version of Ambrettolide which is considered to be the supreme form of that musk.

In comparison to the more fruity Ambrettolide by IFF which we sell, Sublimolide has a scent closer to true ambrette seeds and a stronger power. Sublimolide is the superior option but they are sufficiently different to justify owning both and using Sublimolide as a special treat. 

Sublimolide's super power in a perfume is a marvellous ability to elevate the senses of the wearer. To draw us closer to the achingly distant call of the sublime.

In MANE's own words: “SUBLIMOLIDE is a captivating macrocyclic musk whose structure and scent mirror the natural Ambrettolide found in ambrette seed, a plant from the hibiscus family. Rather subtle at the top, its musky note begins with a soft, understated introduction, only to bloom into a lavish and warm embrace, adorned with fruity nuances and powdery floral undertones. SUBLIMOLIDE is very long-lasting and has an impressive volume and sillage, exalting the top notes along the way. This musk can be used in vegan formulas.”

products.name: Suederal® LT 0710
products.description:
Suederal® is one of the most well-known leather bases and while we love and use Royal Leather far more, this IFF product is a wonderful addition to the perfumer's toolkit and one we highly recommend.

Small amounts can be used as a fixative while large amounts give a very distinctive suede character. Compared to Royal Leather, Suederal is drier and more chemical smelling, so it works particularly well when combined with other materials.

Suederal® blends marvellously with Royal Leather, Cuir de Russie, Fleur de Cuir, Verdantol™, Neobutenone® Alpha, Permawood™, and Saxon Moss.

products.name: Sugandh Kokila Oil
products.description:
Sugandh Kokila Oil smells warmly spicy and camphoraceous, with a fresh herbal-minty top and a resinous, slightly fruity base. It is steam-distilled from the dried berries of Cinnamomum glaucescens, a wild tree in the cinnamon family native to the mid-hills of Nepal. The oil runs pale yellow.

In fine fragrance it brings natural spice and warmth to masculine colognes, fougères and modern orientals. The camphor edge sharpens cedar, patchouli and vetiver, while the fresh top lifts heavier spicy materials like clove and cinnamon. It also ties citrus and green notes to a warm woody base.

Pair with bergamot, lavender and coumarin for a modern fougère, or use against benzoin, labdanum and amber for a spicy oriental. A touch alongside tobacco absolute adds smoky warmth. Use sparingly — the camphor side can push through and dominate if overdosed.

products.name: Sugandh Mantri Oil
products.description:
Sugandh mantri opens with a sweet, floral-woody freshness that immediately recalls rosewood — but give it a minute. Underneath sits a deep, damp, earthy rootiness like nothing else in the palette. The combination of floral top and earthy base makes it genuinely unusual.

Use it as an earthy base note in orientals, woody compositions, and Indian-inspired attars.
