It adds a damp, rooty depth that rosewood and ho wood cannot — they give you the floral sweetness but not the earth. Blend with sandalwood, patchouli, vetiver, and frankincense for warm, contemplative bases.

The name means "Minister of Fragrance" in Sanskrit — this root has been a cornerstone of Indian attar-making for centuries. Arctander judged it as just another linalool source, redundant alongside rosewood and ho wood — but he was evaluating supply, not character. Today's interest is in provenance and personality, and this root has both.

products.name: Sulfurol (Milky)
products.description:
Sulfurol delivers extraordinary dairy effects with remarkable authenticity. This specialised lactonic material creates realistic milk, cream, and condensed milk impressions at concentrations of 0.2-0.8%. Perfumers integrate this powerhouse when constructing high-impact gourmand accords requiring genuine dairy dimensions.

This material pairs exceptionally with vanillin, coumarin, and benzyl salicylate. The impact of sulfurol may not be immediately obvious so be cautious and wait at least 24 hours between additions.

Owing to its strength we are offering it at 10% in DPG or pure.

products.name: Suralette™ Extra
products.description:
Suralette™ Extra is a complex herbal base containing over 40 natural oils and absolutes. It is a key base in the original Aventus (formula below). Suralette Extra is green, herbal, anisic and woody and is a wonderful addition to the perfumer's library.

In small amounts it adds complexity and radiance, while in large amounts it provides a unique alternative to anise naturals such as star anise, mugwort and tarragon.

Suralette Extra blends beautifully with green notes and particularly with narcissus, jonquil, muguet and tropical fruit. Also synergistic with Verdantol™, Jonquil, and Pineapple Supreme.

products.name: Sweet Clover Absolute
products.description:
Opening with a profoundly coumarinic and edible tonka note with a curious seminal nuance, the herbaceous nature of this absolute becomes more obvious as it dries down. Known as Melilot in classical perfumery, this is a new offering from Biolandes and at a massive 15% allowance under IFRA 51 it clearly positions itself as a great alternative to tonka bean absolute.

Sweet Clover Absolute is extremely refined, offering not just the gourmand and agrestic qualities you'd expect for a coumarin rich grass, but it evokes warm days lying in green fields as clouds float lazily above. This is a dream in a bottle, a hint at summers to come and a distant memory of summers past. A true delight that belongs on every perfumer's shelf.

Sweet Clover holds a distinguished place in perfumery history as nature's coumarin source before synthetic alternatives emerged. Classic fougères relied on melilot's hay-like sweetness to create their characteristic aromatic warmth. Today's perfumers value this absolute for its complex natural profile that synthetic coumarin cannot replicate—those subtle tobacco, almond, and caramel undertones that develop during proper extraction make all the difference in sophisticated compositions.

Owing to the thickness and difficulty of working with this material, it is sold exclusively at 40% dilution in DPG so it is pourable.

products.name: Sweet Marjoram Oil
products.description:
Sweet marjoram opens with warm spice — nutmeg and cardamom, not the green herbs you expect. A gentle woody undertone and faint medicinal sweetness sit underneath, but the dominant impression is soft, inviting warmth. It is one of the most underused naturals in fine fragrance.

Use it in fougères to add warm depth between lavender top notes and oakmoss-coumarin bases. It gives colognes an unexpected richness — just enough exotic warmth to lift a simple citrus structure into something considered. A natural companion for nutmeg, bergamot, and clary sage.

Fraterworks also stocks Wild Marjoram Oil (Thymus mastichina), which despite the name is a thyme — eucalyptus-forward, camphoraceous, and bracing. Sweet marjoram shares no common ground with it. They are named the same but smell nothing alike, and are never interchangeable.

products.name: Sweet Orange Oil 10 Fold
products.description:
Folded citrus oils are highly concentrated, having been fractionated to remove many of the terpenes and leaving behind the heart of the oil (in this case limonene — up to 85% — and a considerable amount of aldehyde C-10). 

Our orange oil (taken from the peels of sweet and blood oranges) is ten times folded, making it very similar to terpeneless orange oil but retaining the natural colour of the oil. Folded orange is a little softer and easier to work with, and has the same benefit of terpeneless oil in being longer lasting than regular citrus. Additionally this has a better blended aldehydic character.

Mere touches contribute a wonderful character to colognes or use it to blend with linalool and linalyl acetate to create your own unique citrus oil.

Origin: Calabria, Italy
Variety: Citrus sinensis
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source and fractionated

products.name: Sweet Orange Oil, Decolourised
products.description:
Sometimes you need a hit of citrus without the extreme colour. This sweet orange oil is a wonderfully natural and fine Tarocco blood orange oil (a type of sweet orange with a particularly good character) that has the benefit of being completely devoid of all colour. It is as clear as water without sacrificing any odour.

Also known as Sweet Orange Oil Decolorized.

products.name: Sweet Orange Oil, Terpeneless
products.description:
Terpeneless oils can help to reduce the risks of clouding in fragrances and also pack a greater punch than the standard oils. In fact, this sweet orange terpeneless is about the most powerful orange note you can find in a non-single chemical form.

In a Chypre a trace of this will leave a lasting orange note right through the dry down and can certainly hold its own against overdoses of Oakmoss, Labdanum and other rich base materials. Or use a touch to boost and support a lovely blended citrus top note.

If you want something that is also very strong but retaining more of the terpenes and nuance of fresh orange, we also stock Sweet Orange Oil 10 Fold.

Origin: Calabria, Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source and deterpinated

products.name: Sweet Orange “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Our sweet orange signature oil is extracted from blood oranges, resulting in a slightly sweeter, richer and more elegant oil.

Being more than 99% Limonene, this beautiful natural can be used with no limitations at all though we recommend the addition of Solgard® or Butylated Hydroxytoluene to any fragrances in which you use this in order to prevent oxidation products from forming.

Origin: Italy
Part: Peel
Method: Cold pressed at source

products.name: Sweet Pea
products.description:
Sweet Pea has a bluish scent and it is the key note in Jour d'Hermes, the highly popular sweet floral from 2013. In recent years sweet pea has enjoyed a rebirth in fragrance circles and when you smell Fraterworks Sweet Pea you will understand why.

This base is not an abstraction of the flower, it is a full bodied rich and luxurious base loaded with rare and precious absolutes and oils. All you need is a trace, but overdoses are welcome too.

products.name: Sylvamber
products.description:
Sylvamber belongs to the Iso E Super family — all variations of the same base molecule produced by different manufacturers through different processes. The differences between them come down to the ratio of two key isomers: arborone and Iso Gamma. Understanding this is essential to choosing the right one.

Arborone is the main odour vector. The primary isomer in Iso E Super is almost odourless — it was discovered in 1990 that a minor impurity, arborone, is roughly 100,000 times more potent and accounts for most of what you actually smell. Arborone delivers an intense, woody, slightly animalic character.

Iso Gamma contributes the warm, amber, velvety facet that gives these materials their radiance and skin-like glow. This is the material people want, that presents in the largest quantity in IFF's captive Iso Gamma Super product.

Comparison of Products

Sylvamber (DRT)

14.9% arborone, 9.5% Iso Gamma. The highest arborone of any product on the open market, but the lowest Iso Gamma. This means Sylvamber has the most intense woody-animalic character but the least amber warmth. It smells oilier, more old-wood, more tactile.

Orbitone T Neo (Takasago)

2.5% arborone, 14.2% Iso Gamma. Nearly the opposite balance: low arborone but very high Iso Gamma, second only to IFF's captive Iso Gamma Super. This makes Orbitone the most radiant, amber, and velvety of the commercially available variants. It glows.

Timbersilk (IFF)

8.5% arborone, 13.5% Iso Gamma, plus a touch of Amber Xtreme a

products.name: Symroxane
products.description:
Symroxane opens bright, almost conifer-green and faintly earthy, then settles into velvety dry wood: vetiver root, old timber and a peppery spice, with dried apricot and a thread of tobacco leaf running through it. A soft amber warmth sits underneath. It is complex without ever being loud.

It has a family resemblance to Cashmeran, with a more pronounced woody side and less of that wet-concrete opening. Blend it with Ambrocenide and Timbersilk for a powerful modern wood, or with damascones, patchouli and vanilla for a warm, fruity-woody oriental. Piconia, Ysamber K and Ambermax share its starting material.

Our 212 VIP demo formula uses Symroxane at 5.5%, alongside Iso E Super, Habanolide and Cashmeran in its woody-amber base.

You can read an interesting article about it here.

products.name: Syringa Aldehyde 50% PEA
products.description:
Syringa aldehyde opens with a strong, sweet floral-green burst—immediately recognisable as the honeyed, powdery heart of lilac blossom. It shares the phenylacetaldehyde family's floral-green intensity but arrives with less pungency and more warmth. Beneath the floral top, a soft animalic facet and mimosa-like sweetness give it a living, breathing quality.

This is one of the essential building blocks for lilac accords, where it provides the warm, honeyed-floral depth that hydroxycitronellal and terpineol alone cannot achieve. Use it in hyacinth bases for green-floral impact, in rose accords for added freshness, and in mimosa compositions where its powdery sweetness enhances the honeyed character. It also brings a gentle animalic warmth to white florals—think indolic without the indole.

Syringa Aldehyde vs Phenyl Acetaldehyde

These two aldehydes are easy to confuse, but they occupy very different olfactory spaces.

Phenyl acetaldehyde is the powerhouse of the two—an overwhelmingly intense green-floral hyacinth note with harsh, almost aggressive pungency at full strength that softens into honeyed, chocolatey sweetness on extreme dilution. It is the sharpest and greenest of the three, and demands careful dosing at fractions of a percent.

Syringa aldehyde sits in the middle: it is structurally a phenylacetaldehyde with a methyl group added to the para position of the ring, which softens the harshness dramatically. The result is warmer, more honeyed, and more powdery—recognisab

products.name: Syringol
products.description:
Syringol is what makes wood smoke smell like wood smoke. Its character is intensely smoky and phenolic — charred hardwood, bacon, bonfire — but with a sweet, powdery, almost vanillic warmth underneath that keeps it from turning medicinal. Where guaiacol (its single-methoxy relative) can feel harsh and cough-syrup-like, syringol stays rounded and balsamic.

That sweetness makes it far more versatile than raw phenolic smoke materials. In leather accords it provides authentic smokiness without the medicinal edge that can spoil the effect. Tobacco compositions gain a genuine charred-leaf quality. Incense and frankincense accords become more convincingly burnt. Even whisky-inspired gourmand fragrances benefit from a trace.

At 356 hours on a blotter it outlasts almost anything you pair it with. Birch tar oil, cade oil, and labdanum reinforce the leather-smoke direction. Patchouli and vetiver add earthy depth. Vanillin and coffee absolute take it toward smoky-gourmand territory.

products.name: Syvertal
products.description:
Syvertal hits your nose with remarkable intensity—a wet, dewy greenness that captures freshly cut stems and vegetative sap. The radish-like character brings crisp bite while subtle gardenia and chrysanthemum tones soften the edges. A faint metallic shimmer runs through the profile, adding dimension without harshness.

This material excels at creating moisture effects in floral compositions where you need that fresh-cut flower impression. Use it in gardenia accords to capture stem and leaf alongside bloom, or work it into chrysanthemum reconstructions where its natural affinity shines. It strengthens citrus compositions with green depth that mimics peel oils without using them.

Apply Syvertal at low levels—its strength is considerable and a light hand rewards you with dewy freshness. Pair it with aldehydes to amplify its metallic sparkle, or combine with ionones in violet-gardenia blends. Work it into fougère bases for crisp green impact or layer with vetiver for earthy wetness.

products.name: Tabanon
products.description:
Tabanon captures the essence of warm, aged tobacco leaf — sweet, nutty, and unmistakable. Dry acorn and nut-skin facets give it a distinctive warmth unlike any other tobacco material. Fruity-plum undertones and a soft leathery quality add quiet complexity beneath the surface.

Diffusion is the defining quality here — even at traces, Tabanon radiates tobacco warmth through an entire composition. Use it as a heart-to-base connector in orientals, leathers, and woody-amber blends. It defines the drydown of some of the most celebrated niche tobacco fragrances.

Pair with labdanum and benzoin for rich oriental tobacco, or blend with oud and leather materials for smoky depth. The fruity-plum facet makes it surprisingly sympathetic to damascones and osmanthus. Start with the smallest additions — this is one of perfumery's most potent materials, and overdosing flattens a composition.

products.name: Tagetes Oil
products.description:
Tagetes (Marigold) oil hits your nose with an almost aggressive burst of green — crushed leaves, bitter herbs, and a sharp vegetal pungency. Give it a few moments and a sweet, fruity character emerges underneath. Dilute it further and you find a beautiful apple-like softness that explains everything.

This oil earns its place through transformation — in trace amounts it becomes an extraordinary green-fruity modifier. Add it to florals for an airy, naturalistic lift that nothing synthetic can replicate. Pair it with clary sage, bergamot, or jasmine for complex herbaceous-fruity accords.

Handle tagetes oil with respect — it resinifies on exposure to air and light, so keep it sealed and dark. No substitute exists for its unique character; once you build it into a formula, you will always need it. It helped define Calyx by Prescriptives and remains irreplaceable in modern perfumery.

products.name: Tamisone
products.description:
Tamison is an intense and powerful herbal green chemical with an obvious thujonic character and nuances of tropical fruit. It also exhibits a lovely green note not dissimilar to the highly restricted Methyl Octine Carbonate and Methyl Heptine Carbonate.

Tamisone blends incredibly well with super ambers such as Z11™, Boisiris® and Hydroxyambran, aroma chemicals like Iso E Super, Orbitone® T, Plicatone and Coranol, and with numerous naturals such as Davana, Clary Sage, and Frankincense. 

Firmenich was the last major manufacturer in the industry to make and sell Tamisone but they discontinued manufacturing in 2023 citing manufacturing difficulties. As a result, Fraterworks is working with a third party chemical manufacturer to return the product to market. Once you try it you'll definitely understand why this could not be allowed to vanish from perfumery organs around the world.

Tamisone is a rare chemical and there is very little information available. It is not restricted at all by IFRA or the EU. The RIFM Fragrance Safety Assessment (version 031618, 17 April 2018) “concludes that this material is safe under the limits described in this safety assessment.” [Download]

products.name: Tangerine Heart
products.description:
Tangerine Heart is the most generous member of the LMR citrus heart range. Where Lemon Heart is sharp and sparkling, Lime Heart is zesty and green, and Orange Heart is warm and marmalade-rich, Tangerine Heart brings something none of them offer: sweetness with genuine floral depth. It opens juicy and bright — ripe tangerine peel, immediately mouthwatering — but underneath there is a soft floralcy, almost neroli-like, that gives it a complexity the other citrus hearts lack.

This is an LMR speciality developed in partnership with IFF Citrasource in Florida. Like all the citrus hearts, it is a concentrated fraction produced by molecular distillation — the terpenic bulk removed, the character amplified, the tenacity extended far beyond what standard tangerine oil can achieve. A few drops in your formula will push that juicy, sparkling citrus character well into the heart of a composition.

Standard tangerine oil shares a species with mandarin — both are Citrus reticulata — but the tangerine cultivar runs sweeter, stronger, and more overtly fruity. The Heart version concentrates those differences further. Use it in fruity florals, gourmand compositions, and summer colognes where you want citrus sweetness rather than citrus sharpness. Pair it with Orange Heart for a rich, layered citrus accord, or combine with neroli and petitgrain for a tangerine blossom effect.

products.name: Tarragon “Signature” Oil
products.description:
Tarragon oil is a wonderful herb with a distinctive anise note. It is indispensible in Chypre fragrances and was found in the original (formula below). Our signature Hungarian tarragon is lively and fresh; a must have oil.

According to Steffen Arctander: “Tarragon (estragon) is a colorless, or very pale yellow to greenish-yellow liquid, with a sweet-anisic, green-spicy, slightly celery-like odor, very similar to that of the fresh herb.

Tarragon (Estragon) is used in perfumery, usually in trace amounts, in Chypre, l’Origan types, Fougères, lilac bases, green floral bases, etc.

Blends well with galbanum, lavender, vanilla, cardamom, clovebud, oakmoss.”

Origin: Hungary
Part: Leaves
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: TCD Alcohol DM
products.description:
TCD Alcohol DM is used for its woody, ambery, and slightly musky profile. Its molecular structure provides excellent diffusion and fixation, making it a suitable addition to chypres, modern ambers, and high-end woody accords.

This material is particularly valued for its ability to enhance depth and structure, seamlessly integrating with Iso E Super, Ambroxan, Vertofix, and musks. Due to its stability, TCD Alcohol performs well across different formulations, from alcoholic perfumes to personal care applications. Its low volatility and high substantivity make it an effective fixative, ensuring long-lasting impact in fragrance compositions.

NOTE: Our supplier, Ventos, has used incorrect data in its paperwork (supplied on by us). They wrongly refer to this material by the CAS 26896-48-0 (HHCB, Muscomer) when it is 26160-83-8 (Tricyclodecanedimethanol).

products.name: Tea Black SFE
products.description:
Open the tin, not the teapot. Tea Black SFE smells of the dry leaf itself: leafy and hay-like, with tobacco and a gentle smokiness, an astringent, tannic edge and a fresh, spicy lift running through it. Extracted with carbon dioxide rather than hot solvent, it stays true to the leaf.

Use it to bring a smoky, woody dimension to compositions. It anchors tea accords with the realism of the leaf, deepens leather and tobacco themes, and gives chypres and orientals a dry, tannic backbone. A little in a rose or osmanthus heart lends the thorny, bitter darkness of tea rose.

Bergamot on top gives you Earl Grey; cardamom, cinnamon and a touch of vanilla turn it toward chai. For a smokier direction add a trace of birch tar or guaiacwood. With osmanthus and violet leaf it slips into a floral-leather, and beside oud or labdanum it turns dark and contemplative.

Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol.

We stock the full tea SFE range: Jasmine Tea SFE, Tea White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

products.name: Tea Green SFE
products.description:
This is green tea as dried leaf rather than brewed cup: fresh, aromatic and green, with a hay-like herbal character, an oily, woody body and a faint seaweed nuance at the edges. The leaves come from China, oven-warmed straight after picking, and the extract smells more matcha tin than teahouse.

Use it to bring a fresh, aromatic green effect to aromatic and gourmand compositions, to lend leafy realism to a green tea accord, or to sharpen a citrus cologne with a herbal, slightly bitter greenness. Start small: a little gives a herbal accent, more gives a distinct tea signature.

Hedione opens it into the airy, transparent tea heart of modern fresh florals. With bergamot, petitgrain and a trace of mint it becomes a green tea cologne; with violet leaf and cucumber notes it turns watery and cool; over rice and milky notes it suggests a bowl of matcha.

Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol.

We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Tea White SFE, Jasmine Tea SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

products.name: Tea Keemun SFE
products.description:
Keemun is the black tea of Qimen county in Anhui, grown between the Yellow Mountains and the Yangtze, and this extract captures what sets it apart: a dark, plummy fruitiness, an unsweetened cocoa undertone and a soft tobacco smokiness, with a delicate floral facet and toasted grain beneath.

It reads darker and fruitier than a straightforward black tea note, so use it where a plain tea accord feels thin. It deepens tobacco and dried-fruit themes, lends cocoa-tinged warmth to gourmands without sweetening them, and gives woody autumnal compositions a brewed, leafy heart.

It suits noir directions. Pair it with tobacco absolute, davana and a dry amber for a fruity-tobacco accord, or with cocoa absolute and a whisper of birch tar for a smoky, bittersweet gourmand. Bergamot lifts it toward a Chinese-leaf Earl Grey, and osmanthus draws out its fruit.

This one is, in my opinion, the most beautiful and interesting of the tea extracts.

Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol.

We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Tea White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Jasmine SFE.

products.name: Tea White SFE
products.description:
White tea is the least handled of all teas, just young leaves and buds withered and dried, and the extract is correspondingly gentle: delicately aromatic, green and fruity, with fresh floral facets and sweet hay. Underneath sits a soft, mossy, tobacco-like dryness, with hints of osmanthus and peach leaf.

Its lightness is the point. Use it to give white florals a fresh, leafy tea nuance, to add volume and realism to a tea accord without darkening it, or to lend a green, faintly fruity softness to fresh florals and light gourmands. Jasmine, freesia and gardenia all take to it.

Osmanthus absolute draws out its fruit; violet leaf and a trace of melon note make it cooler and greener. In a tea-rose theme, set it against a dewy petal material such as Rosaphen for a soft, powdery effect, or build a Chinese white-tea accord with hay absolute and clary sage.

Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol.

We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Jasmine White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

products.name: Terpinene Gamma
products.description:
Gamma-terpinene smells of warm, oily lemon-lime with a herbal, almost thyme-like undertone. It is greener and more herbaceous than limonene, with a terpenic freshness that reads as natural and unpolished. This is what gives tea tree and thyme their bright, citrusy top.

Use it to reconstruct and extend citrus oils — it adds the warm, herbal dimension that pure limonene lacks, making lemon and lime accords feel more complete and realistic. It also brings fresh, zesty lift to aromatic compositions built on lavender, rosemary, and thyme.

Pair it with limonene and linalool for a full citrus effect, with thyme and marjoram for herbal depth, or with bergamot for a rich, complex citrus opening. It is volatile and fades within a few hours, so layer it over longer-lasting base materials. Store carefully — it oxidises over time.

products.name: Terpinene-4-Ol
products.description:
Terpinene-4-ol natural has a warm, earthy, peppery character with woody-herbal depth and a subtle nutmeg-like spiciness. This is the molecule that defines the smell of marjoram oil. At dilution it reveals sweeter, more herbaceous facets alongside a gentle green undertone.

Use this natural isolate to build realistic spice and herb accords in your compositions. It brings earthy-peppery authenticity to nutmeg, marjoram, and herbal fougere constructions. A trace in lavender accords adds naturalistic complexity that linalool and linalyl acetate alone miss.

Blend with geranium and lavender for aromatic-herbal compositions. Try it alongside black pepper and frankincense for warm, spicy depth. The natural version carries a subtle richness that the synthetic grade cannot replicate.

products.name: Terpineol Alpha
products.description:
Terpineol Alpha is an indispensable material for creating lilac notes in fragrances and as a delicate floraliser in general. Unfortunately most qualities of alpha terpineol suffer from an overly intrusive chemical note in the place of lime and lilac. 

Combine it with a high quality muguet or lilac base to modify it to your needs, or use it singularly to add a sheer lilac note. Accords with Cyclosia are delightful and this very versatile product blends with the rose alcohols exceptionally well.

We were formerly selling Lindenol from IFF, but due to the drop in quality of late we have switched to a 100% natural product with far greater purity and clarity. This natural version boosts the floral aspects while diminishing the pine notes that often cause terpineol to smell like floor cleaner. If you are seeking perfection in Alpha Terpineol, the search ends here.

products.name: Terpinolene, Rectified
products.description:
Terpinolene opens with a burst of fresh pine needles and sweet citrus—lime zest wrapped in a woody, turpentine-like haze. The sweetness is surprising for a terpene; it reads almost candy-like against the resinous backdrop. The overall impression is bright, clean (thanks to rectification), and immediately uplifting.

This material is a workhorse for pine and lime accords in functional products—detergents, cleaners, and air fresheners all benefit from its affordable citrus-coniferous punch. Use it to freshen lavender and rosemary blends, or to give herbal compositions a convincing top-note burst. It blends seamlessly into fougère and aromatic bases where you need that initial green-pine flash.

Terpinolene is fleeting so treat it strictly as a top-note modifier. Pair it with longer-lasting pine materials like pinenes and fir needle oil for sustained effect. In fine fragrance, use it in traces to add naturalistic sparkle to citrus and herbal openings without expecting it to carry beyond the first few minutes.

products.name: Terpinyl Acetate
products.description:
Terpinyl acetate opens with sweet herbaceous freshness reminiscent of lavender fields and bergamot groves. Its pine-like facets add coniferous depth whilst citrus notes provide sparkling lift. This versatile ester maintains refreshing sweetness throughout its development.

You'll find this material invaluable for building lavender and bergamot accords at reduced cost without sacrificing quality. It excels where linalyl acetate faces hydrolysis issues, particularly in alkaline formulations. Use it to extend fresh acetate top notes whilst adding spicy complexity to citrus-cologne structures and fougères.

Blend terpinyl acetate with linalyl acetate for authentic bergamot reconstruction or combine with citronellol and geraniol esters to enhance freshness. Pair with pine needle oil to amplify coniferous aspects. This ester bridges citrus openings with floral hearts beautifully in soap perfumes.

products.name: Terrasol
products.description:
Terrasol (2-Ethyl Fenchol) is perhaps the most true to life damp earth chemical next to geosmin which is literally the chemical that causes the scent of rain. On first sniff pure, Terrasol has a slightly camphoraceous scent - almost a blend of camphor, menthol, eucalyptus and ethyl salicylate. However, in dilution and in use, that gives way to pure petrichor and decaying leaves.

Use this to naturalise fragrances that are high in synthetics. With floral blends, Terrasol will root the flower in the earth. Touches of green materials give you the complete garden — soil, flower, foliage.

Another very clever use is to blend this with synthetic woods, or even dry woods like cedar, to dampen them down. Blended right this can contributed a cool effect by association (think autumn forests and winter wood piles). The material is long lasting so it will sit alongside your naturals quite comfortably matching longevity.

products.name: Tetrahydrogeraniol
products.description:
Tetrahydrogeraniol opens with an immediate waxy quality that sets it apart from every other rose material in your palette. Where geraniol sparkles with citrus-bright sweetness and fresh green vitality, this fully hydrogenated cousin brings gravitas—a rose viewed through frosted glass, softened and abstracted into something more textural than literal. The "tetrahydro" modification strips away geraniol's reactive double bonds, and with them goes much of the bright citronella edge and sweet floral lift, leaving behind a fascinating skeleton of waxy rose with unexpected soapy-clean nuances. In fact you can see this facet clearly exploited in our Amrita demonstration formula below.

This material excels where geraniol fails catastrophically—in the harsh alkaline environments of bar soaps, liquid detergents, and industrial cleaners where pH levels would normally decompose traditional rose alcohols into unrecognisable fragments. Deploy tetrahydrogeraniol at 0.5-5% in functional products to maintain authentic floral character through aggressive bases. Its remarkable stability extends beyond mere survival; it actively contributes to the perception of cleanliness through its inherent soapy-waxy character. This synaesthetic quality makes it invaluable for creating "clean laundry" accords and fresh textile impressions that feel authentic rather than imposed.

The chemical transformation from geraniol to tetrahydrogeraniol reveals perfumery's hidden architecture. By saturating all double

products.name: Tetrahydrolinalool
products.description:
Tetrahydrolinalool opens with sweet, soft floral character—gentler and less green than linalool, more powdery and delicate. The lily and lilac facets provide naturalistic freshness, while bois de rose undertones add subtle woody warmth. A distinctive tea-like nuance and clean oily quality complete a profile that feels refined and transparent. It works beautifully in muguet, lily, lilac, mimosa, rose, and jasmine compositions at levels from 1–8%.

Work with tetrahydrolinalool at up to 30% of your concentrate where stability is paramount. The 12-hour substantivity on blotter means it functions as a fresh top-to-heart modifier. While slightly weaker than linalool, its superior durability more than compensates in functional applications. Blend with other stable florals for tea accords, aromatic fougères, and transparent citrus compositions.

Linalool, Dihydrolinalool, and Tetrahydrolinalool Compared

These three materials represent a spectrum of stability versus olfactory intensity. Linalool is the most potent and complex—fresh, floral-citrus with distinctive rosewood character—but it's vulnerable to oxidation and it must be declared as an allergen in the EU.

Dihydrolinalool sits in the middle: having better stability than linalool while retaining a bois de rose-woody character with subtle blueberry and citrus facets.

Tetrahydrolinalool is the most stable of the three—it survives harsh detergent and soap bases where the others would degrade, and it requires no allergen declarat

products.name: Tetramethyl Pyrazine
products.description:
Tetramethyl pyrazine smells of roasted cocoa, fresh coffee, and black tea. It is milder than most pyrazines but still intensely concentrated — a crystalline solid you should pre-dilute before working with. The chocolate-cocoa facet dominates, with a warm, nutty, tea-like quality that adds naturalistic depth.

Use this molecule to build convincing chocolate and coffee accords in your gourmand compositions. It adds the authentic roasted dimension that synthetic sweeteners alone cannot deliver. In tobacco fragrances it provides the warm, cured-leaf facet that reads as genuine rather than artificial.

Blend with cocoa absolute and vanillin for rich chocolate effects. Try it alongside coffee CO2 and tonka for a sophisticated cafe-gourmand accord. Pair with black tea absolute to exploit its distinctive tea-like character in unexpected ways.

products.name: Theaspirane
products.description:
Theaspirane is a radiant blackcurrant, rose and tea-like note with a camphoraceous opening. It blends incredibly well with Velberry™ and Givescone™ and the rose ketones which it happily boosts. This really is an indispensable chemical for the modern perfumer and certainly one we would never be without in the Fraterworks labs.

Perfumery: Techniques in Evolution (a series of articles published in Perfumer and Flavorist magazine) has this to say about it: “Theaspirane is one of those singular chemicals that seldom emerge from research. It might even be considered one of the 10 best chemicals on the market. It is present in natural tea, and its fragrance is extraordinarily complex: herbal, greeen tea, moist and recently cut tobacco leaves, with metalic, woody, floral and spicy backnotes. Its blends with vanilla notes, [tabanon], formyl tricide decane, the macrocyclic musks, Oxo-Edulane, 4-oxo ionyl acetate, Oxo-Damascone or beta-Damascone are unique.

Its radiant and unequalled beauty places this chemical among the exalted ranks of products such as the Damascones and Damascenone, Hedione and Exaltolide, without implying of course, that all these aromatic chemicals can be grouped in the same family. Theaspirane is a jewel that will be used more and more in the future.”

products.name: Theobromal
products.description:
Also known as Syringaldehyde, this should not be confused with Syringa Aldehyde, which is a completely unrelated material. Theobromal smells of dark chocolate, soft smoke, and warm leather, with a grape-wine quality underneath and a whisper of vanilla. It is mild — you will not notice it immediately — but it lasts over 400 hours on a blotter.

Think of it as vanillin stripped of its obvious sweetness and given depth. Where vanillin is straightforwardly creamy and sweet, theobromal adds smoky, leathery, chocolatey dimensions that feel more grown-up and more interesting. Use it to build sophisticated amber and oriental bases, or add trace amounts to chocolate and tobacco accords for realism.

Pair it with vanillin for a smoky-vanilla effect, with labdanum and castoreum for full leather, or with benzoin and styrax for incense depth. It is a crystalline powder — dissolve in warm ethanol before use. One of perfumery's best-kept secrets for balsamic fixation.

products.name: Thesaron®
products.description:
Thesaron (Ethyl Tetrahydrosafranate) opens with crisp fruity-floral character—rosy, fresh, and immediately appealing. Peach and berry facets provide juicy richness, while subtle amber warmth adds depth without heaviness. Woody-herbaceous undertones keep the profile grounded, preventing it from becoming overly sweet. The overall effect is modern, diffusive, and remarkably versatile.

This Takasago product is classified as 100% bio-based, appealing to formulators seeking renewable ingredients. The 24-hour substantivity on blotter ensures your fruity-floral effect persists well into the heart and base of compositions. Excellent stability in everything from fine fragrances to functional products including bleach applications.

Work with Thesaron at up to 15% of your concentrate—the medium odour strength and forgiving nature make it easy to blend. Use it in peach, apple, and berry compositions where crisp fruitiness needs rosy support, or in floral accords seeking fruity freshness. The amber undertone works beautifully in oriental and woody contexts where fruit notes add modern appeal. Good substantivity on wet fabric and hair makes it valuable for personal care applications.

Thesaron vs Ethyl Safranate

These two esters share similar names because Thesaron is ethyl tetrahydrosafranate—but their olfactory profiles differ significantly. Ethyl Safranate (CAS 35044-59-8) is intensely spicy and saffron-like, with powerful damascone-rose character, apple cider facets, and woody depth;

products.name: Thiocineole 0.1% DPG
products.description:
Utterly intense, this grapefruit chemical will blow you away. Pure it has the most distinct odour of burnt rubber but when diluted its mimicry of bitter grapefruit skins is astonishing.

Traces are all you need to impart a very realistic and powerful grapefruit note to your blends. further dilution to 0.01% is recommended but in the right context this material can even be overdosed.

Thiocineole, in addition to grapefruit, has nuances of apricot, papaya, passionfruit and other tropical fruits, as well as a seedy and vegetative nuance. A hint of mint is also apparent.

This is truely a remarkable and interesting material.

NOTE: We package all high odour or high risk materials individually in separate heat sealed aluminium bags to mitigate any risk of cross-contamination.

products.name: Thioxane Base 38375 D
products.description:
Thioxane Base opens with a vivid blast of fresh green citrus — grapefruit peel, lemon zest — that quickly reveals a juicy tropical dimension underneath: ripe mango, passion fruit, a hint of something bitter and almost savoury. The overall impression is strikingly natural, far more realistic than most synthetic citrus or tropical reconstructions. It smells like actual fruit rather than a fragrance interpretation of fruit.

That realism comes from the same family of naturally occurring sulphur compounds found in yellow passion fruit and grapefruit peel. Firmenich has balanced these potent materials with supporting green and citrus ingredients to make the base usable without careful micro-dosing. Even so, it is powerful and best used from a dilution — it projects with unusual reach.

Use Thioxane Base to add a natural, peely freshness to citrus accords, or to introduce tropical fruit facets into floral compositions. It gives a lovely petal-like freshness to floral-citrus blends and adds convincing lemon-peel character to clean accords. Pair it with Hedione for a bright, diffusive citrus-floral effect, or with green materials for a naturalistic leafy opening.

products.name: Thujopsene Ex Cedar Wood
products.description:
Far too infrequently used by perfumers, thujopsene is a wonderful cedarwood note extracted from the heart of real cedar oil (typically it makes up 25% of the natural oil). It blends well with Iso E Super and other wood materials to provide a unique and distinctly modern wood quality. Thujopsene exhibits the clean scent of freshly sharpened pencils.

If you're sick of fragrances overloaded with the same cedar chemicals (such as Iso E Super), try blending those materials with this special natural or simply use this pure instead. Priced incredibly well and in plentiful supply, this is a must-have.

Best of all it is not under any form of restriction by IFRA or the EU and is not scheduled to be restricted in any way under IFRA 51.

products.name: Thyme Oil ct Linalool
products.description:
Sweeter than its red counterpart (despite being the same plant, Thymus zygis), Thyme ct Linalool has a soft quality which works very well in small doses to impart a non-specific herbal note to fragrances. Overdoses can give an interesting character, a trick exploited by François Coty in his original and rare Cologne Eau de Coty (1909) which later inspired Edmond Roudnitska to create Eau Sauvage (1966) for Dior.

The difference between White Thyme (this one) and Red Thyme (ct Thymol) is the growing conditions. Thyme ct Borneol, on the other hand, is from Thymus satureoides.

products.name: Thymol Crystals
products.description:
Thymol greets you with sharp, phenolic intensity that settles quickly into robust thyme warmth. The camphoraceous lift provides freshness while the medicinal character—surprisingly clean and almost sweet—adds authenticity. Unlike harsh phenols that evoke burnt or chemical notes, thymol remains herbaceous and agrestic, bridging clinical and aromatic territory beautifully.

Use thymol to cut through heavy gourmands or add savory depth to the emerging vegetable trend. It anchors olive oil reconstructions with peppery-herbal authenticity. When building modern masculine structures, its medicinal edge provides the hygienic signal consumers expect while maintaining sophistication.

products.name: Tilleul (Linden Blossom)
products.description:
The scent of tilleul blossoms (also known as tilia, linden blossom and lime tree) floating on the air in summertime is one of the most beautiful. Fraterworks® Tilleul captures the very essence of this wonderful tree.

With doses possible at up to 49% of your finished product, this can be used as the central core of a modern multiflor fragrance by simply adding accents of other flowers and woods. Forget muguet, try Tilleul for a head-turning difference.

products.name: Timberide®
products.description:
This radiant base opens with an immediate sensation of penetrating woody dryness — think sun-bleached driftwood. The effect is both brutal and refined—sharp enough to cut through any composition yet smooth enough for sophisticated wear. You'll recognise its signature "icy dagger" quality piercing through from top to base.

Composed around large doses of such materials as Ysamber® K, Ambrocenide and Timberol, this is a treasure trove of well-blended power molecules.

Reach for Timberide when building modern masculines that demand both power and polish. Its unique architecture amplifies citrus freshness while anchoring volatile notes with tenacious woody structure. This base transforms simple accords into radiating auras that project metres from the skin—essential for contemporary "beast mode" creations.

Deploy Timberide at 0.5-5% to create that coveted halo effect in your fragrances. It excels when paired with bergamot and grapefruit for vibrant woody-citrus structures. Combine with modern musks and sandalwood molecules like Javanol for compositions that seem to glow from within—the hallmark of today's luxury powerhouses.

products.name: Timbersilk
products.description:
Timbersilk is the close relative of Iso E Super (Patchouli Ethanone), in fact it is effectively the same material except that the two products have a different balance of isomers which effects their odour strength.

Iso E Super itself is relatively weak - most of its odour comes from small amounts of two of its related isomers: the gamma isomer and Arborone (Iso E Super Plus - the main odour vector of the material). Iso E Super has 4.8% Arborone and 11.7% Iso Gamma, while Timbersilk has 8.5% Arborone and 13.5% Iso Gamma making it stronger in scent and power. Timbersilk is also boosted with 0.07% of AmberXtreme. The near mythical captive "Iso G Super" of Molecule 1 fame has 8.5% Arborone and 13.5% Iso Gamma.

Timbersilk holds its own against stronger materials and is less inclined to be lost in the mix. It can replace Iso E Super in all areas and can work very well in a modified type of Grojsman accord.

products.name: Timut Pepper Oil
products.description:
Made in collaboration with Jean Claude Ellena when he was head of perfumes at Hermes, this wonderfully rare pepper oil is quite a surprise. With hints of styrax (and other balsamic notes on account of the material containing cinnamates), a coriander seed quality and a touch of grapefruit, this is a versatile and useful product and extremely beautiful.

Recently discovered by perfumers and gastronomes alike, the French eat the Nepalese spice with Foie Gras where its pomelo and candied lemon nuances complement the unctuous texture of the goose liver. And being a close relative of the Sichuan pepper makes it a suitable alternative to that popular spice also.

Blends with Styrax Oil, Styrax Resinoid, Coriander Seed, and Citrus Oils.

products.name: Tobacarol
products.description:
Tobacarol is a standout material for introducing the warm, velvety richness of a tobacco to a scent. Its inviting profile carries a complex interplay of smoky, woody, and ambery tones, subtly sweetened with faint leathery facets. With exceptional tenacity and diffusion, this material is a natural choice for masculine blends, oriental creations, or sophisticated chypres. It also provides a unique warmth to gourmand compositions and floral bouquets, acting as a harmonious base note anchor.

Tobacarol combines beautifully with smoky materials like Birch Tar and Oakwood CO2, sweet and resinous notes such as Benzoin and Tonka Bean, and warm woods like Sandalwood and Cedarwood.

Enhancing Versatility: Layer with lighter top notes such as Bergamot or Green Mandarin for contrast or blend with creamy elements like our wonderful Vanillin “Signature” for softer, gourmand effects.

A little goes a long way due to its strength; recommended usage levels are best kept below 1%.

Tobacarol appears in Creed's Tabarome Millesime (2000), Parfums de Marly's Herod (2012), and Aramis's Havana (1994).

products.name: Tobacco Absolute MD
products.description:
Tobacco absolute (nicotine content < 0.03%) opens with sweet hay-like warmth reminiscent of cured tobacco leaves. Caramel and honey facets emerge alongside dried fruit richness. The molecular distillation process removes colour whilst preserving the complex aromatic profile with its subtle leather undertones.

You'll find this absolute invaluable for creating authentic tabac accords where colour removal prevents staining in finished products. It excels at adding masculine sophistication to oriental bases and unexpected depth to aldehydic compositions. Use it sparingly at 0.1-1% where its concentrated power adds warmth without overwhelming delicate florals.

Combine tobacco absolute with vanilla and tonka for gourmand tobacco sweetness or blend with castoreum and leather for animalic depth. Pair with amber accords where honey facets enhance balsamic warmth. This material bridges woody bases with sweet top notes beautifully, particularly with bergamot and clary sage.

Molecular Distillation

This molecular distilled variety from Payan Bertrand undergoes vacuum distillation to remove colour whilst preserving aromatic integrity. The process eliminates a lot of the typical red-brown pigmentation that causes staining, creating a clearer (albeit not water-white) product ideal for light-coloured formulations. Where standard tobacco absolute limits usage due to colour concerns, Payan Bertrand's molecular distillation allows broader application whilst maintaining the full aromatic comp

products.name: Tobacco “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Over the years we have sampled many Tobacco absolutes, being ever on the lookout for that singular one which encapsulates every wonderful aspect of the plant in its most distinguished forms: snuff, pipes and cigars. This is it.

Upon first sniff of this marvellous absolute one smells antique wood and hay notes. Payan Bertrand's recent harvests have achieved an exceptional level of refinement, surpassing even our former offering. Their latest production attains such quality that one would be forgiven for believing oneself to be smelling a hand of aged tobacco leaves. Following the typical masculine opening is a distinctly honey and dried fruit nuance. Rounding it all out is a sweet vanilla-tonka complex that confirms the versatile role that tobacco extracts play in our art form.

We have made the decision to switch from our previous MANE tobacco absolute to this superior Payan Bertrand product for two compelling reasons: the recent harvests demonstrate notably finer aromatic qualities, and crucially, this absolute carries no IFRA restrictions whatsoever. Unfortunately, changes in MANE's processing methods resulted in their product becoming IFRA prohibited, making it unsuitable for our purposes.

We call this our "Signature" absolute because it is the first tobacco product we turn to in virtually every instance. It is used in a number of our products and we have yet to sample finer.

This product blends exceedingly well with the sticky dried plum note of Firmenich's Prunella, C

products.name: Tocopherol (Vitamin E)
products.description:
Tocopherol is an anti-oxidant which can be useful in materials such as linalool to prevent dangerous oxidation from occurring. While it doesn't entirely replace BHT (a synthetic preservative and antioxidant) it is a viable replacer for it and for natural perfumers this is a must.

Tocopherol is Vitamin E and it does have a slight odour (somewhat unpleasant) however it is usually used under 0.5% of your finished product so it is seldom and issue.

products.name: Tolu Absolute Replacer 50%
products.description:
One of the annoyances of Tolu Balsam is the intensely dark brown colour. Payan Bertrand has solved that problem by producing this marvel of blending, a synthetic Tolu Balsam Absolute Replacer which is both pale in colour and utterly sublime in scent (nicer, perhaps, than natural tolu!) Our love of this material is so great that we employ it in a number of products for its odour value alone. And best of all it is extremely cost effective and there are no supply chain risks around obtaining the raw material.

Tolu Balsam Resinoid and Absolutes are both permitted at fairly high amounts under IFRA, and this replacer is likewise allowed at 16% (in its diluted state), but even if you routinely use the natural products or don't need to worry about the dark colour of them, we still strongly recommend you purchase this replacer.

For the sake of ease of use, we sell this at 50% diluted in triethyl citrate which makes it pourable and allows the beautiful scent of the base to open up its beautiful cinnamic heart.
tags: locale:BASE not the usual resinoid or absolute

products.name: Tolu Balsam Absolute 50% TEC
products.description:
Tolu Balsam Absolute delivers exceptional fixation while imparting refined sweetness without Peru's medicinal edge or benzoin's cloying tendency. This material excels in hyacinth and tuberose compositions where its complex profile enhances white florals. Use 0.5-3% in alcoholic formulations for optimal impact.

Apply this material sparingly—overdosing dampens other materials more aggressively than benzoin. Create powdery effects by combining with hydroxycitronellal and linalool. Build sophisticated oriental bases by blending with labdanum and patchouli. This pre-diluted format ensures immediate workability without heating requirements.

Difference Between Tolu Balsam Resinoid and Absolute: Tolu Balsam Resinoid results from benzene or similar non-polar solvent extraction of crude balsam, yielding 60-70% of viscous, dark material containing waxes and heavier compounds. The absolute undergoes further alcohol washing to remove these components, producing a more refined, concentrated aromatic extract. Commercial "absolutes" sometimes bypass the resinoid stage through direct ethanol extraction, technically creating "resin absolutes." True absolutes exhibit cleaner profiles with enhanced solubility in perfume compounds, though both forms require heating for handling. The absolute's superior refinement justifies its use in fine fragrance, while resinoids suit soap perfumery where their retained acids pose no alkalinity concerns.

We also stock Tolu Balsam Resinoid at 50% in natural T
tags: locale:Tolu ABSOLUTE not resinoid. Always double check.

products.name: Tomato Thiazole
products.description:
Tomato thiazole hits the nose with an unmistakable burst of crushed tomato vine - green, earthy, and startlingly lifelike. In concentration it reads sharp and sulphurous, but proper dilution unlocks a warm, herbaceous vegetal character. Work exclusively from a 1% or 0.1% dilution; the neat material is far too powerful to dose accurately.

This is one of perfumery's true high-impact molecules, with a detection threshold around 3.5 parts per billion in water. Pair it with cis-3-hexenol to soften the metallic edges and bridge it into naturalistic leaf accords. Blend with galbanum and basil oil for full greenhouse realism, or add traces to citrus compositions to enhance the zesty peel effect and banish any candy-like sweetness.

products.name: Tonalide
products.description:
Tonalide is a classic polycyclic musk (like Galaxolide) which was discovered in 1954. It is very popular in functional fragrances (such as soaps, shampoos, and laundry detergents) as it is non-water soluble so it remains after rinsing. Tonalide is sweet, musky and slightly fruity.

In fine fragrance it has a long history of use in men's perfumes, having a somewhat synergistic effect on coumarin, but it also features in feminine perfumes such as Paris (1983) from YSL. It is also found in Apple Brandy by Kilian at 5.5%, in DKNY Be 100% Delicious at 3% and a huge 8% in Fleur de Male by Jean Paul Gaultier.

A more restrained 2% decorates both Lipstick Rose and The Night by Frederic Malle, Silver Mountain Water by Creed, and Fantomas by Nasomatto.

products.name: Tonka Bean CO2 Abs
products.description:
Tonka Bean CO2 opens with the familiar coumarinic warmth of tonka — but this version leans unmistakably cherry. A roasted almond-marzipan richness sits alongside that cherry note, creating something genuinely edible. The drydown is creamy vanilla-praline with the hay-sweet depth you expect from the bean. Beyond a doubt this is now our favourite Tonka Bean extract.

The CO2 process captures lighter aromatic facets that traditional solvent extraction misses — those cherry and almond nuances that make this version special. Use it anywhere you want tonka's warmth with a gourmand edge: amber bases, tobacco accords, oriental hearts. It anchors blends with exceptional tenacity.

Pair it with cocoa absolute for a dark chocolate-cherry accord, or blend with vanilla and benzoin for gourmand decadence. It lifts rose and jasmine with confectionery sweetness that smells effortlessly luxurious. Compare it with Fraterworks' Tonka Bean "Luxe" Absolute — each captures a different facet of the same bean.

Note that this is a superior CO2 Absolute in which an initial CO2 extraction is followed by an additional purifying alcohol extraction.
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.

products.name: Tonka Bean Tincture 20%
products.description:
Coumarin is the usual method of adding tonka bean nuances to a perfume today, but nothing beats the full complexity of the natural bean. Cold tincturing is the best way to extract this beautiful scent. By combining coumarin, tonka bean absolute and tonka bean tincture you can create fragrances that are out of this world.

Our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of tonka bean tinctures and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop.

NOTE: this tincture is not made in a food safe environment. This product is for perfume and cosmetic use only. This is not a food product.

Origin: Peru
Variety: Dipteryx Odorata
Part: Beans
Method: Cold ethanol tincture

products.name: Tonka Bean “Luxe” Absolute
products.description:
Up until recently, we offered a single tonka bean absolute—the wonderfully gourmand creation from V MANE Fils, known as our Tonka Bean “Signature” Absolute. However, as we embarked on our 2025 evaluations to ensure we continue providing only the finest materials, we made an extraordinary find: this Tonka Bean Absolute from LMR. This deluxe, meticulously crafted extract was too exceptional to overlook, compelling us to add it to our collection. While the MANE Signature absolute captivates with its sticky-sweet, gourmand charm, the LMR Luxe absolute offers a refined, drier profile, perfectly balancing elegant agrestic notes with gourmand delight. Its distinct sophistication justifies offering both side by side and the title Tonka Bean “Luxe” Absolute.

We offer both our tonka absolutes at 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. In pure form tonka bean is a solid paste.

In describing tonka absolute, Arctander says: ‘Tonka absolute is a semi solid or crystalline mass of pale amber or pale brownish-yellow color Its odor is very rich, sweet and warm, distinctly coumarinic / herbaceous, with a prune-like, or caramelic-sweet undertone. The odor description “tobacco-like” is somewhat confusing since Tonka tincture has been used quite extensively in the flavoring of cured tobacco leaves. The absolute consists of 20-45% coumarin, but the effect of a true Tonka absolute goes far beyond that of the coumarin contained in the absolute.
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.

products.name: Tonka Bean “Signature" Absolute
products.description:
If you have been searching for the holy grail of tonka, you have found it. Intensely edible, warm, spicy and sweet, this absolute is the profound expression of the full aroma of the beans. In this incredibly complex scent is the gourmand odour of delicious French patisserie, the vanilla sweetness of puddings, and a warm fond of subtle spices centred around a delicate cinnamon note.

We offer this incredible product 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. In pure form tonka bean is a solid paste.

In describing tonka absolute, Arctander says: ‘Tonka absolute is a semi solid or crystalline mass of pale amber or pale brownish-yellow color Its odor is very rich, sweet and warm, distinctly coumarinic / herbaceous, with a prune-like, or caramelic-sweet undertone. The odor description “tobacco-like” is somewhat confusing since Tonka tincture has been used quite extensively in the flavoring of cured tobacco leaves. The absolute consists of 20-45% coumarin, but the effect of a true Tonka absolute goes far beyond that of the coumarin contained in the absolute.

Tonka is a fixative and non-floral sweetener which introduces warm notes in chypres, fougères, new mown hay bases, lavender bouquets, Oriental bases, etc. It blends well with: Lavender, lavandin, clary sage, bergamot, oakmoss.’

Note: due to scarcity of supply, the price of tonka bean absolute has increased significantly in 2026.
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.

products.name: Tonka Torréfiée, Esprit d'Odeur
products.description:
Tonka Torréfiée Esprit d'Odeur is a luxurious combination of roasted tonka beans with fifteen year aged small batch rum, distilled with perfumer's alcohol into a light and ethereal perfumery spirit.

With subtle nuances of cherry, bitter almonds and caramel, this is a truly unique and precious material and one almost never seen on the stock books of modern perfumery raw materials suppliers.

First we roast fresh tonka beans which intensifies the ripe cherry and marzipan notes. These are then crushed and tinctured for a period of months in dark rum, triple aged for 15 years in oak casks. The final stage is to then distil the rich tincture resulting in a delicately scented colourless nearly pure perfumer's alcohol. This can be used as a tincture or the foundation of additional tinctures.

Tonka Torréfiée presents with a bouquet of sandalwood, freshly baked pastries, marzipan, black cherries, and the merest suggestion of musk. 

To smell this infusion is to smell happiness.

IMPORTANT: this product must not be consumed. It is for perfume manufacture only. It is not safe for human consumption. This should be treated as any other denatured alcohol product.

products.name: Tonkin Intense
products.description:
For those seeking an animalic note equalling the strength and ferocity of pure wild animal extracts, our Tonkin Intense and Ambergris Intense fit the bill. Forget Tonquitone, Shangralide and Muscarome… Tonkin Intense is the most profoundly luxurious deer musk you will ever experience.

Tonkin Intense is built using the most radiant and powerful synthetic musks with accents matching the full spectrum of molecules in natural deer musk. This is pure animal. We recommend diluting to 1% or less for modern fragrances and up to 10% for floral rich or classical styled perfumes.

products.name: Tonquitone
products.description:
IFF's Tonquitone opens with unmistakable animalic warmth — the rich, slightly urinous musk character of natural Tonkin deer musk, faithfully reconstructed. Ambergris-like depth sits beneath the animalic surface. Sweet caramel-vanilla facets and dry-woody undertones emerge as the base develops on skin.

This IFF base built entirely on macrocyclic musks gives you a true animalic backbone without the cost and variability of natural musk tincture. It fixes and enriches leather, chypre, oriental, and fougère accords at trace levels. Even small additions lend convincing skin-like presence to any composition.

Blend with castoreum and indole to amplify the animalic facets, or combine with ambroxan and sandalwood for softer skin-musk warmth. Push the dose and pronounced civet character emerges.

products.name: Torref Pyrazine
products.description:
Torref Pyrazine hits with unmistakable dark-roast intensity—think freshly ground espresso beans or chocolate pushed to the edge of caramelisation. The meaty, almost beefy undertone adds savoury complexity that distinguishes this from sweeter gourmand materials. An ethereal cocoa quality weaves through, rich and deeply satisfying.

This pyrazine forms naturally during the Maillard reaction at higher temperatures, which explains its more intensely torréfié (roasted) character. You'll find it in dark-roasted coffee, toasted bread, grilled meat, roasted nuts, and fermented foods like malt and beer. The French torréfié—meaning roasted or kiln-dried—perfectly captures its essential quality: deep, smoky, and almost burnt without becoming acrid.

Use Torref Pyrazine at medium strength—evaluate at 10% dilution before committing to your formula. It excels in coffee accords, dark chocolate compositions, and tobacco bases needing authentic roasted depth. The meaty facet also makes it valuable in unexpected contexts: leather compositions and certain animalic accords benefit from its savoury warmth.

Torref Pyrazine vs Praslin Pyrazine

Both share the chocolate-nutty pyrazine family character, but their differences matter for formulation. Torref Pyrazine (2,6-dimethyl Pyrazine) is more intensely roasted, with pronounced coffee and meaty-beefy notes alongside its chocolate character—think dark-roasted coffee beans or caramelised meat. Praslin Pyrazine (2,5-dimethyl Pyrazine) leans more must

products.name: Toscanol
products.description:
Toscanol is anise turned up loud. It carries the sweet, green warmth of tarragon and basil, wrapped around a soft black-liquorice heart and a nostalgic root-beer, sassafras note. Clean and linear, it stays true and never drifts soapy. With the extremely low permitted amounts of tarragon oil since IFRA 51, Toscanol is now an essential to replace it.

Use it to bring a natural anise-tarragon lift to aromatic and herbal work, or a warm liquorice sweetness to gourmands. It slots straight into fougères beside lavender, rosemary and coumarin, and reinforces basil and tarragon oils without the harshness they can bring.

Its warm, sweet-spicy side makes it a natural in liquorice and root-beer accords, and a saffron-and-caraway edge lets it lift spicy, balsamic bases. Try a trace in a lavender fougère to add a green, aromatic twist, or in an anise cologne for body. It holds up even when dosed hard.

products.name: Trans-2,Cis-6-Nonadienal
products.description:
This incredibly powerful aldehyde is an indispensable key to violet leaves (and their substitutes), especially in combination with its related alcohol Trans-2-Cis-6-Nonadienol (note the last two letters, -al and -ol, which indicate aldehyde and alcohol).

Smelling intensely like cucumber, melon and violet leaves (in which it occurs naturally) this aroma material is an outstanding blender and nuancer for green materials. Combine it with Neobutenone Alpha and Corps Racine or our powerful Verdantol™ base for a modern and radiant green note.

Also known as cucumber aldehyde and violet leaf aldehyde, this product is sold in dilution with DPG due to its extreme power.

products.name: Trans-2,Cis-6-Nonadienol
products.description:
This material delivers the authentic watery-green signature of natural violet leaf and cucumber at remarkably low concentrations. Work with pre-diluted solutions (we recommend 1%) due to extreme potency that overwhelms neat evaluation. The alcohol form provides softer, more floral character compared to its aggressive aldehyde counterpart, making it ideal for sophisticated green accords.

You achieve remarkable effects using trace amounts below 0.1% to add dewy naturalness to white florals like muguet and lily. Combine with cis-3-hexenol for initial green snap, then let this material provide sustained watery depth. 

Aldehyde-Alcohol Synergies

Trans-2,Cis-6-Nonadienol (alcohol) offers a softer, more floral profile compared to iTrans-2,Cis-6-Nonadienal's (aldehyde) sharp, aggressive character. The alcohol is fractionally more floral than the aldehyde. Perfumers often combine both: the aldehyde provides initial punch while the alcohol lends sustained, rounded body to violet leaf accords. Together with nonadienal, nonadienol creates the complete nostalgic odour of violet gardens. The alcohol's moderate tenacity bridges top notes into the heart, while the aldehyde's extreme diffusivity creates immediate impact. Balance these complementary materials to achieve dimensional green effects impossible with either alone.

We also stock Trans-2,Cis-6-Nonadienal which we sell at 1% dilution.

products.name: Trans-2-Decenal
products.description:
Trans-2-Decenal opens with an unmistakable fatty-waxy aldehydic punch that evokes rendered chicken fat at full strength. When diluted to perfumery levels, brilliant orange zest emerges alongside fresh coriander leaf. This powerful material transforms from heavy to luminous through careful dosing.

Use this versatile aldehyde to offset the harshness of decanal in classic aldehydic florals while adding photorealistic citrus peel texture. It excels at bridging fatty and fresh-green families, creating depth in orange accords at 20 ppm or authentic cilantro effects at higher levels. The material's exceptional diffusivity provides tremendous top note lift that persists for over eight hours on blotter.

Apply sparingly—its potency easily dominates when overdosed, particularly in delicate lemon compositions. In aldehydic florals it modernises classic structures; in green accords it delivers authentic cilantro character alongside other herbal materials. Store chilled.

products.name: Trans-2-Hexenol
products.description:
Trans-2-Hexenol hits the nose with a burst of green freshness — unripe banana, crisp apple skin, and freshly cut stems. It reads fruitier and sweeter than its cousin cis-3-hexenol. A sharp grassy bite gives way to softer herbaceous undertones.

Use Trans-2-Hexenol where you need green freshness with a fruity edge — it lifts jasmine, honeysuckle, and freesia accords with vegetal realism. Even tiny amounts add convincing leafy naturalism. Its power demands restraint; keep it at trace levels or it overwhelms the blend.

Blend with cis-3-hexenol for a complete green leaf effect — the trans isomer adds fruit where the cis isomer adds pure green. Try it in apple and pear reconstructions or to freshen violet leaf accords. Eight hours on a smelling strip gives adequate top-note presence.

products.name: Trans-2-Nonenal
products.description:
This aldehyde delivers pure, uncompromising fatty-green character. At full strength it's intensely waxy and substantial; upon dilution it transforms to brilliant cucumber freshness with melon brightness. Think of it as the purest expression of green-aldehydic power in perfumery.

Add traces to ionones and methyl ionones and watch their impact multiply—this material amplifies power and diffusion like nothing else. In cucumber and melon accords it provides photorealistic texture that grounds sweetness in naturalism. Use it in violet-leaf reconstructions for authentic fresh-green snap, or blend with florals to add crisp, naturalistic edges that keep compositions from becoming too rounded.

Handle this material with respect—it's exceptionally potent and performs best at trace levels. In green apple compositions it adds brilliant aldehydic lift; in orris and rose work it contributes fresh facets that prevent powdery sweetness from dominating. Store it carefully away from light and verify freshness regularly, as its intensity depends on quality.

products.name: Trans-2-Octenal
products.description:
Trans-2-octenal opens with a blast of fatty green freshness — cucumber, crushed leaves, a hint of green apple. It belongs to the family of unsaturated aliphatic aldehydes that includes trans-2-hexenal and trans-2-nonenal, sitting between them in character: greener and more herbal than the melon-cucumber nonenal, less sharply apple-like than the hexenal. The waxy, leafy quality gives it real body.

This aldehyde is extremely potent and must be used in heavy dilution. At trace levels it adds convincing green freshness and natural-smelling leafy character to floral compositions. It is particularly useful as a floral modifier — a touch of it makes rose, lily, and violet accords smell more like living flowers on the stem rather than clean synthetic reconstructions.

Use trans-2-octenal in cucumber and watermelon accords, or to add green realism to citrus compositions — it brings authenticity to orange and mandarin blends. Pair it with cis-3-hexenol for a lush green effect, or with trans-2-nonenal for a broader cucumber-melon spectrum. Always work from a dilution; undiluted, it overwhelms everything around it.

products.name: Trans-4-Decenal
products.description:
Trans-4-decenal opens with a blast of fresh, bright orange-mandarin peel — intensely green and aldehydic. The citrus reads naturalistic rather than synthetic, closer to a freshly peeled tangerine than a classic soapy aldehyde. On dilution, unexpected muguet nuances emerge underneath.

This is decanal's greener, more powerful relative — it occurs naturally in orange peel oil and cardamom, which explains why it reads so convincingly natural. It builds authentic mandarin and tangerine accords where decanal alone reads too waxy. A trace tones down excessive sweetness in citrus compositions.

Evaluate from a 0.1% dilution or lower — this is one of the most powerful aldehydes available. Blend it with cis-4-decenal (Cardamom Aldehyde) to cover the full citrus-spice spectrum. It pairs naturally with orange oil, bergamot, and linalool for naturalistic citrus accords.

products.name: Traseolide
products.description:
Traseolide opens with an enveloping musk quality reminiscent of expensive fabric against skin – soft, warm, and immediately comforting. Unlike sharper polycyclic musks, this material carries a distinctive sandalwood-like creaminess throughout its development. The combination creates an effect that's neither purely musky nor woody, but occupies a unique space between these categories.

This material excels at smoothing compositional rough edges. Sharp aldehydes become rounded, aggressive woods gain sophistication, and disparate notes merge seamlessly. The optimal usage at 10% provides this harmonizing effect while maintaining transparency – the composition improves without the musk becoming dominant. Consider this the perfumer's equivalent of a soft-focus lens.

Traseolide's interaction with sandalwood molecules creates particularly successful accords. The material enhances creamy, milky aspects while contributing its own textural richness. Exceptional stability in alkaline conditions makes this indispensable for functional applications. When extreme longevity matters – think fine fragrance base notes or premium laundry products – Traseolide delivers consistent performance across challenging conditions.

See our demonstration formula for Amrita, our smells-like version of the official Mysore Sandalwood Soap from Karnataka, to see Traseolide in action in a Sandalwood context.

products.name: Treemoss “Non-IFRA” Absolute
products.description:
What made fragrances like First (1976) by Van Cleef and Arpels, Coco (1984) by Chanel, Polo Green (1978) by Ralph Lauren the masterpieces they were? Perhaps not exclusively but most certainly significantly: pure treemoss absolute. 

Often looked down upon as the dull younger brother of Oakmoss, this Robertet extraction absolutely proves the contrary; this is every bit as wonderful as the nicest green Oakmoss (which we also stock).

This is so thick and deeply green that we offer it in a more mobile 50% solution with natural TEC so it remains viable for natural perfumers also. But, because of the rarity of supply of this product we are offering it pure despite the challenges that go along with melting such a tar-like material. 

This is NOT IFRA compliant and, as such, should not be used in any perfumes or cosmetics requiring adherence to those standards.

Origin: France
Part: Moss
Method of production: Solvent extraction

products.name: Triethyl Citrate, Natural (TEC)
products.description:
Triethyl citrate is a wonderful natural (US & EU) diluent for perfumery. It is naturally extracted with pure food grade alcohol from citric acid from citrus fruit. Triethyl Citrate (TEC) has no odour and allows for dilutions of natural materials that maintain an ISO 9235 standard.

TEC is particularly good as a diluent for rose materials and bases and it is widely used in the fragrance industry in both synthetic and natural versions.

TEC has excellent solubility in alcohol as well as fractionated coconut oil. It also solubilises in jojoba oil but may cause slight cloudiness. Always perform a small test to ensure compatibility as solubility can vary from medium to medium and depends upon the overall blend of materials in play.

products.name: Trifernal
products.description:
Trifernal hits the nose with striking green intensity — bitter foliage, crushed stems, and the raw vegetal bite of freshly torn leaves. It smells unmistakably natural despite being synthetic. This is among the most powerful green materials available, effective at vanishingly small concentrations.

This material excels in floral compositions built around lilac, hyacinth, violet, and muguet — adding the green backbone that makes those accords smell alive. It works equally well in aromatic and cologne creations. Combine with other green notes for layered botanical freshness.

Use Trifernal at trace levels — its power demands careful dosing. Pair with galbanum and violet leaf for intensely realistic green accords. Blend into citrus compositions where a bitter herbal edge adds welcome complexity and natural character.

products.name: Trimofix®
products.description:
With radiant nuances of earthy vetiver, subtle smoky tobacco, and a touch of musky softness, Trimofix adds depth and sophistication to fragrance. It can be used in traces as a fixative or in overdose (but keep in mind its 2.4% IFRA restriction). It can be seen as somewhat similar in profile to Ambraketal (Z11) but with a shorter lifespan and intensity. However, its complexity and ability to lift woody compositions make it a highly useful ingredient.

Trimofix blends well with Vetiver oils, Iso E Super™, Vertofix, and other woody synthetics and has a synergy with galbanum related materials like Dynascone, Neobutenone Alpha and Allyl Amyl Glycyolate.

Trimofix's popularity can be attested to by the large number of perfumes in which it is to be found: Green Irish Tweed, 1.8% in The One (Dolce & Gabbana, 2008), Nasomatto Duro (2007), Baccarat Rouge 540, Amouage Memoir Men, Bleu de Chanel (2010), Balade Sauvage (Dior), Opium for Men, By the Fireplace (Maison Martin Margiela) and many many more.

products.name: Triplal
products.description:
Along with the classic chemicals Cis 3 Hexenol and Cis 3 Hexenyl Acetate, Triplal is an indispensable material for bringing a true and natural green note to a fragrance. It is frequently used in combination with those other green materials but also has value when used alone.

Triplal was used to great effect in Le Male by Jean Paul Gaultier (0.5%), 0.65% in Light Blue of Dolce and Gabbana in synergy with 0.1% Liffarome, 0.25% in Drakkar Noir, Oscar de la Renta's Pour Lui (0.4%), 0.1% in Safari by Ralph Lauren, 0.2% in Chanel's Allure Pour Homme, 0.07 in Ani by Nishane, 0.2% in Grand Soir by Maison Francis Kurkdjian and many many more. 

Triplal has nuances of cucumber and ivy leaves and blends beautifully with Helional, Cyclamen Aldehyde, Amazonia™, Verdantol, Daphne Supreme, Veticoeur, Vetimoss and Artemal™.

products.name: Trisamber
products.description:
Trisamber is a powerful, dry, dusty woody-amber with an unusually velvety texture. Where most synthetic ambers at this strength feel harsh or chemical, trisamber stays smooth and elegant. Subtle animalic and musky facets give it a primitive, naturalistic quality. It persists for days on a blotter.

Use trisamber to build deep amber and dry wood accords in your orientals, chypres, and masculine compositions. It sits between the explosive power of AmberXtreme and the softer creaminess of Operanide — powerful enough to anchor any base, smooth enough to blend without fighting. It adds warmth and sensuality at remarkably low doses.

Blend with sandalwood and labdanum for classic amber accords. Try it alongside Iso E Super and cashmeran for a modern, transparent woody-amber heart. Pair with vetiver and patchouli where its dry, dusty character reinforces the earthy base without adding sweetness.

products.name: Troenan
products.description:
Troenan captures that unmistakable privet hedge in bloom—warm, honeyed yet distinctly green. The scent opens with broken twig freshness before blooming into a gorgeous floral heart. Subtle mushroom and metallic facets add complexity that keeps this material fascinating on the blotter.
