This material shines in white floral compositions where you need naturalistic green depth. It works beautifully in jasmine accords, lending that spring-garden authenticity. It also proves invaluable in lavender reconstructions for functional products, where its herbal-spicy character provides support and lift but it is equally at home in fine fragrance.

Pair Troenan with lily of the valley materials to build convincing privet effects. Its excellent stability in bases makes it reliable across applications. The 24-hour substantivity at full strength means it anchors green-floral hearts without fading too quickly—a genuine workhorse for fresh compositions.

products.name: Tropathiane 1% DPG
products.description:
Tropathiane is an incredibly powerful chemical which is virtually identical to the more common Oxane though there are minor differences due to the balance of isomers. Anyone who has smelled the famous Cassis Base 345B of Firmenich will recognise this family of odours as they are key to that base.

Traces of Tropathiane are extremely useful not just for the obvious tropical notes but also for other fruits such as grapefruit. Some consider this a cleaner and easier to use chemical than Oxane which can be quite repellent until you are used to it.

Sold here at 1%, this is so strong that it can be very useful diluted to a further 0.1%.

products.name: Tropicalia™
products.description:
Tropicalia bursts forth with the intensity of a tropical storm, capturing juicy mango, jackfruit, melon, and guava in a single molecule of extraordinary power. This newly liberated captive from IFF delivers what others merely suggest—true tropical environment memory. The unexpected mint facet cuts through sweetness like fresh leaves crushed underfoot, while white floral undertones add sophisticated opulence that elevates simple fruit into complex paradise.

Use Tropicalia when you need tropical fruit that transcends cliché beach cocktails. Its exceptional strength means trace amounts transform compositions—use in dilution for signature effects or pure for singular fruit explosions. The material's animalic castoreum effect in chypre accords reveals its versatility beyond fruit, supporting leather and oud with unexpected warmth while bringing naturality to vanilla bases. This high-impact ingredient maintains intensity from top through heart with medium base persistence.

Combine Tropicalia with Aprifloren for amplified fruit juiciness, layer with Isobutyl Quinoline for leather-tropical hybrids, or blend with Floralozone and Methyl Ionone Gamma for contemporary white florals with tropical twist. Released from captivity in 2024, this molecule represents IFF's answer to competitive tropical materials—more complex than typical passion fruit chemicals, more natural than synthetic mango bases, and powerful enough to define entire compositions at minimal dosage.

Tropicalia is very po

products.name: Tubereuse 184108
products.description:
Tubereuse demonstrates how popular bases are in both classical and modern perfumery and illustrates their ongoing use as key components of masterful fragrances.

Tubereuse is used in Anais-Anais, Fidji, Cartier's Must, Hermes Amazone, and a multitude more. It is one of the most popular tuberose bases.

Tubereuse is effective from 0.1% and is usually used to a maximum amount of around 2%. We highly recommend using it to add captive warmth to our Tuberose Supreme base which is loaded with natural tuberose absolute from LMR.

products.name: Tuberose Supreme
products.description:
An incredibly rich and oppulent tuberose base loaded with natural tuberose absolute and other complementary naturals. Orinally a Chuit Naef and Cie base replicating the popular Roure Tuberose (as found in Poison, Tendre Poison, Oscar de la Renta, Fracas and many more). Gently and sympathetically updated with modern molecules which provide radiance to this perfectly blended luxury floral.

Traces add richesse and depth, while larger amounts contribute a powerful and distinct tuberose note.

products.name: Tuberose TruAbs
products.description:
Tuberose TruAbs captures every facet of genuine tuberose absolute with astonishing accuracy. You get the full narcotic white floral intensity — creamy, honeyed, almost dangerously sweet — with the signature green, slightly medicinal opening and the buttery, animalic depth that makes tuberose unforgettable.

This 100% natural base is crafted in Grasse exclusively for Fraterworks. Use it anywhere you would use genuine tuberose absolute — narcotic white florals, heavy orientals, gardenia and frangipani accords. Incorporate at 0.1–5% for a luxurious floral heart that reads as completely authentic.

Blend with jasmine and ylang-ylang for a classic white floral bouquet, or pair with sandalwood and benzoin to bring out the warm balsamic drydown. TruAbs bases offer a consistent, readily available alternative to one of perfumery's rarest and most expensive absolutes.

products.name: Tuberose “Signature” Absolute
products.description:
Tuberose — a flower so intensely erogenous that in Victorian times an English lady would avoid the scent for fear of an sudden lapse of self-control. Meanwhile, in France, the extrait from pomade was liberally doused upon the décolletages of upper crust women who, with gay abandon, revelled in its scent.

No flower in the history of fragrance has so titillated, so intoxicated and so enthralled perfume wearers. Its high cost and powerful scent make it a very rare treasure today compared to what it once was but fortunately even trace amounts can have a profound effect on a scent. The merest soupçon can naturalise and enrich a simple classic floral accord of Jasmine and Rose or add a sultry je ne sais quoi appreciated by all.

Our signature Tuberose Absolute from LMR was selected from the offerings of all the top suppliers in Grasse. It stood out for its clarity of scent and the diaphanous quality of its dry down — rather unique for such a rich floral material. We are certain you will find this as sublime as we do.

products.name: Ultramber® Xtreme
products.description:
Super ambers are wildly popular today and they are now found in almost every new fragrance. 

For a novice perfumer they can be the hardest materials to dose right, and often for experienced perfumers there can be a tendency to simply add a touch of their favourite one or two to each blend keeping within safe margins.

That is where Ultramber® Xtreme comes to the fore. This product is a sophisticated blend of the very best of super ambers, adding harmony, diffusion and radiance to any fragrance while being easier to dose. If super ambers are the stars in the glistering firmament, Ultramber® Xtreme is a supernova.

This is where super ambers begin and end. You don't need anything else. Just add this from trace to overdose.

Ultramber® Xtreme contains the perfect dose of Ambrocenide, Amberketal, Dextro Norlimbanol (35%), and many other enhancing and boosting materials. Love Ultramber®.

products.name: Ultravanil
products.description:
Ultravanil is a big comfy bowl of warm custard. In addition to its bold vanilla qualities, this material has a discreet caramel edge and a clear phenolic depth with woody and spicy undertones.

Four hundred hours on blotter makes this one of the most tenacious vanilla materials available. Use it to boost vanillin and ethyl vanillin in any composition — even traces add remarkable depth and longevity to vanilla accords. The phenolic backbone gives it staying power that lighter vanilla notes simply lack.

Pair with vanillin and ethyl vanillin as a booster, or use alongside benzoin and labdanum for dark oriental richness. The smoky-spiced warmth strengthens gourmand and tobacco compositions beautifully. Sold pure and diluted in DPG — dose in traces and build upward, as the potency is exceptional.

It is worth noting that Givaudan sells this "pure" as an 80% concentrate, with the other 20% being DPG. We offer it further diluted to 10% (a total of 8% actual ultravanil) for price and strength reasons.

products.name: Undecavertol
products.description:
With the tight restriction on the much loved violet leaf materials Methyl Octine Carbonate (0.01% of the finished product) and Methyl Heptine Carbonate (0.047% of the finished product), Undecavertol has become vital for the modern perfumer.

Undecavertol is a wonderful material for green florals, whether it be violet or lindenblossom. Additionally it has nuances of kiwifruit and muguet. Undecavertol has less power than violet leaves and if using it as a replacer for the aforementioned carbonates, you will need to increase the quantity used.

In the words of its manufacturer, Givaudan: “Undecavertol was developed in connection with structural elucidation work on unknown trace components of lily-of-the-valley. It has a powerful green-floral character, somewhat related to lily-of-the-valley, with natural, fresh, fruity violet leaf and linden-blossom aspects. It can be used successfully in rose and fruity pear accords. Although easy to use in most perfumery types, Undecavertol requires careful dosage and blending due to its exceptional strength.”

Despite Givaudan's warning on dosing, this material can be wildly overdosed to great effect as evidenced by DKNY's Be Delicious (2004) by Maurice Roucel in which he used 10% pure!

products.name: Valencene
products.description:
Valencene takes its name from Valencia oranges, where it occurs naturally. The aroma is sweet, juicy citrus — unmistakably orange — with a subtle grapefruit edge and gentle woody warmth underneath. Unlike most citrus materials that vanish in minutes, valencene persists for hours, carrying its fresh orange character deep into a composition.

Use valencene to extend and deepen citrus accords that would otherwise fade too quickly. It bridges your bright top notes into the heart, maintaining fresh orange character where standard citrus oils have long gone. Pair it with nootkatone for a complete orange-to-grapefruit citrus spectrum.

Blend with bergamot and mandarin for rich, layered citrus openings. Try it alongside cedarwood and amyris where its woody undertones create a natural bridge to your base. Add to fresh masculine compositions where long-lasting citrus impact matters.

products.name: Vanellia™
products.description:
A wonderful Tahitian vanilla fantasy base at a fraction of the cost of natural absolute, Vanellia™ contains luxurious vanilla extracts in combination with revolutionary modern synthetics. Achieve all the radiance and gourmand elegance available to perfumes of yesteryear.

Usable at up to 5.2% of the finished product for full IFRA 50 compliance (and 35% for IFRA 51) this is an essential toolkit material for all perfumers.

products.name: Vanilla Barka Attar Type Formula
products.description:
By far this 2021 Attar from Amouage is the most popular of the range. Crafted by Dominique Ropion it is a simple 24 line formula with virtually all ingredients available here at Fraterworks. Because the naturals in this attar are scarce, the quality of the aroma chemicals must be absolutely supreme. Fortunately Fraterworks sells only the best aroma chemicals so you get a wonderful result from this formula.

The quality of Amouage scents has been a little in decline since Christopher Chong left the company but the Attars remain a relatively quality little side-line for the brand. 

Notes: Vanilla, Olibanum, Tonka Bean

Difficulty Level: Easy
Total Lines: 24
Naturals: 6

products.name: Vanilla Bean CO2
products.description:
Vanilla (planifolia) CO2 is the most recent addition to the natural extracts derived from this most important perfumery material. Vanilla is considered the salt of perfumery and it is found in almost every perfume to some extent.

This CO2 is an LMR speciality and the quality and luxury is immediately obvious. While the natural absolute is dark brown, this CO2 is pale straw in colour. It is organic at source, and uses no petrochemicals. All the CO2 in the process is recycled by LMR.

Starting with the creamy balsamic facets we all love in high quality natural vanilla, this extract contains the lovely phenolic and powdery drydown of the absolute at a much lower price point.
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.

products.name: Vanilla Bourbon Absolute
products.description:
Vanilla Absolute is pure indulgence, and Vanilla Bourbon Absolute from V MANE Fils is the height of said indulgence. This deep brown absolute is pourable with a little gentle heat and soluble at 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate (albeit with a touch of cloudiness which is to be expected with vanilla).

At a whopping 30% vanillin, this Vanilla Absolute has to be smelled to be truly believed and appreciated. It is so rich it verges on being chocolatey. We can say with absolutely no hesitation, that you will never want to use vanilla absolute from another supplier once you experience the beauty of this product.

A very interesting and unique powdery combination can be had blending Vanilla Absolute with Olibanum Coeur. Use a trace to naturalise our beautiful signature Vanillin ex Guaiacol, or simply indulge in an overdose. 

We sell this at 10% in completely natural odourless Triethyl Citrate (an isolate from citrus) or pure.

Our demonstration "smells-like" formula below for Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) demonstrates how beautifully well Vanilla Absolute blends into floral fragrances to add subtle and rich sweetness without the sometimes cloying solidity that can come from synthetic sweeteners. 

Origin: Madagascar
Part: Pods

products.name: Vanilla Intense, Esprit d'Odeur
products.description:
Vanilla Intense Esprit d'Odeur 20% is a vanilla lover's dream and rarely available in the perfume raw materials market these days. We start by tincturing finest Madagascan vanilla pods in French Cognac in perfumer's ethanol and after a long maceration period we perform a co-distillation over fresh vanilla pods. The result is a double-vanilla "spirit of odour" that is simply a revelation. This product is colourless and ethereal in scent. It is traditionally used in the same manner as a tincture of vanilla.

IMPORTANT: this product must not be consumed. It is for perfume manufacture only and is not safe for human consumption. This should be treated as any other denatured alcohol product.

products.name: Vanilla Pod Tincture 20%
products.description:
This is the finest vanilla tincture on the market today. Every care and the characteristic Fraterworks attention to detail has been engaged at every step of the way. Our intensely rich, dark and luxurious tincture of vanilla is a unique way to add the full complexity of vanilla to your scent.

We use specially harvested whole vanilla pods which are given extra drying time in the Madagascan sun to intensify their aroma for an especially dark and surprisingly powerful vanilla tincture. We use only the purest food grade alcohol made with remote New Zealand glacial water so nothing stands in the way of a perfect cold process vanilla extraction.

Because our tincture is made at such a high concentration, the alcohol can absorb quite a lot of water naturally from the pods. As Steffen Arctander says: “Certain perfume houses still use the old fashioned “infusion” method of extraction. […] The resulting infusion may be filtered immediately or after cooling. […] It will become cloudy and show additional precipitate on standing.” 

All fragrances created with naturals or tinctures must be chilled overnight after maceration (typically a period of one month) and fine filtered to remove any cloudiness that may remain.

Use the tincture directly in your perfume formulas or pre-blend it with perfumer's alcohol for a natural vanilla touch impossible to obtain any other way.

NOTE: this tincture is not made in a food safe environment. This product is for perfume and cosmetic use only. This is

products.name: Vanilla Supreme
products.description:
Madagascan vanilla absolute is one of the most luxurious materials available to perfumers but its price is far out of budget for most uses. Vanilla Supreme by Fraterworks is the cost-effective solution: a one-for-one replacer.

Despite its amazing price, Vanilla Supreme is enriched with luscious — and dare we say superior — naturals (including a judicious amount of finest Vanilla Bourbon absolute). 

Vanilla Supreme has a wonderfully creamy scent and unctuous texture and is safe for use at a whopping 10% of your finished product. Use it in traces to impart a naturalistic vanilla nuance to your scent or in overdose for pure decadence (as in our "Ravishing" demonstration formula below which replicates Musc Ravageur from Frederic Malle).

Try a marvellous accord by combining Black Opoponax To Vanilla Supreme in a 1:5 ratio. Vanilla Supreme also synergises with Coconut Delight, and all the lactones.

We also offer Vanellia™, our popular Tahitian vanilla fantasy base if you are looking for something different.

products.name: Vanillin Acetate
products.description:
Vanillin Acetate presents a refined vanilla warmth — sweet and creamy with a distinctive powdery heliotrope quality that sets it apart from standard vanillin. The balsamic character is smooth and rounded. Think of it as vanillin with the sharp edges gently filed away.

Use Vanillin Acetate wherever you want vanilla sweetness without the assertive punch of vanillin itself. It excels in oriental and amber bases where its heliotrope facet adds floral complexity. The powdery warmth blends naturally into tonka, coumarin, and benzoin accords.

Pair Vanillin Acetate with ethyl vanillin and benzoin for layered vanilla depth. Add it to white floral compositions — the heliotrope quality bridges jasmine and tuberose with gourmand warmth. Its occurrence in nature means it reads as convincingly authentic in naturalistic accords.

products.name: Vanillin ex Clove, Natural
products.description:
Vanillin has been on the market since 1874. In recent years with the rise of natural perfumery, there is also now demand for a naturally derived form. Our natural vanillin, extracted from cloves, is wonderfully creamy and realistic and is an enormously valuable tool in the natural perfumer's toolbox.

We also stock a very special synthetic vanillin, our Vanillin “Signature” which we consider superior in scent to this product. Vanillin “Signature” is GMO free but it is not a natural product.

Arctander says this of vanillin in general: “Among the more common perfume materials, Vanillin is one of the most tenacious odors known.”; “Its intense sweetness is utilized in industrial masking odors and in high-cost luxury perfumes, and it can be used in almost any type of fragrance, from woody or herbaceous to Oriental or floral.”

Perfumer Jean Claude Ellena makes the following suggestions for some fun chocolate accords using vanillin:

Plain Chocolate: Vanillin + patchouli
Chocolate Ganache: Vanillin + a touch of civet absolute
After Eights: Vanillin + spearmint (or Black Mitchan Peppermint for a British twist)
Cocoa Powder: Vanillin + Orris Germanica

products.name: Vanillin ex Vanilla Bean
products.description:
Vanillin ex Vanilla Bean smells profoundly, unmistakably vanilla — richer and more complete than any other grade, synthetic or natural. The tan-coloured crystals carry trace companions from the pod that give this isolate a creamy, caramelised warmth with subtle dark chocolate depth. It smells like freshly split cured vanilla beans.

This Firmenich isolate is the foundation of serious vanilla accords. Use it in your orientals, ambers, and gourmand compositions where authentic vanilla character matters. It rounds and sweetens everything it touches, adding a warm, enveloping base that persists beautifully through a fragrance's full life.

Pair with coumarin ex tonka for rich, powdery gourmand depth, or blend with benzoin and Peru balsam to build luxurious amber accords. Layer alongside vanilla absolute or CO2 for the most complete, multidimensional vanilla note you can achieve in a natural composition. And you absolutely must try it with Rum CO2.

Due to the very high cost of this material we offer it at 10% solution in 100% natural Triethyl Citrate, keeping it suitable for natural perfumers.

For a lower priced natural vanillin we offer Vanillin ex Clove. We also stock a very special synthetic vanillin, our Vanillin “Signature” ex Guaiacol, considered by many to be superior to natural vanillin and we concur. Vanillin “Signature” is GMO free.

products.name: Vanillin “Signature”
products.description:
Vanillin has been on the market since 1874 and in the years since its discovery little has changed… until now. In recent years a new vanillin has appeared, a food grade (FCCX) vanillin ex guaiacol which blows the classic "greats" such as vanillin ex lignin and natural vanillin ex clove out of the water. This new vanilla masterpiece is our wonderful “signature” vanillin.

This is the creamiest, sweetest and most full vanillin. Imagine crushing a handful of plump vanilla pods in your hands and inhaling the wonderful smell: this is that scent. Fraterworks is currently the only supplier of this incredible vanillin to the artisanal fine fragrance market. We are sure you'll be a convert for life once you try this.

Arctander says this of vanillin in general: “Among the more common perfume materials, Vanillin is one of the most tenacious odors known[;] Its intense sweetness is utilized in industrial masking odors and in high-cost luxury perfumes, and it can be used in almost any type of fragrance, from woody or herbaceous to Oriental or floral.”

Vanillin "Signature" is GMO free.

Perfumer Jean Claude Ellena makes the following recommendations for some fun chocolate accords using vanillin:

Plain Chocolate: Vanillin + patchouli
Chocolate Ganache: Vanillin + a touch of civet absolute
After Eights: Vanillin + spearmint (or Black Mitchan Peppermint for a British twist)
Cocoa Powder: Vanillin + Orris Germanica

products.name: Vanitrope
products.description:
Most perfumers default to vanillin or ethyl vanillin without a second thought. Vanitrope asks you to reconsider. Roughly twenty times vanillin's strength, it carries a heliotrope-violet dimension neither of those workhorses possess — plus tobacco warmth, a woody-spicy edge, and a powdery finish that belongs in a different league.

That potency changes how you work. Derive no more than half your vanilla character from vanitrope, filling the rest with ethyl vanillin or vanillin for balance. The heliotrope dimension gives you a vanilla accord of genuine complexity. And unlike vanillin, it won't yellow your formulations.

Ethyl vanillin is its best partner — the two boost each other in ways neither achieves alone. Heliotropin reinforces that violet-powder facet in the background. In tobacco accords, vanitrope's smoky warmth fits better than vanillin, which can flatten the complexity you're trying to build.

products.name: Velberry™
products.description:
Velberry™ is a soft sweet chemical with a red fruit character. It has some similarities to raspberry ketone but with interesting whisky and green facets. This can be a particularly useful material when an alternative is needed to the classic (but discolouring) vanillin and heliotropin.

Velberry adds volume and body to a scent and can be used in very large doses (particularly in functional fragrances). The price is incredibly good and has virtually no regulatory barriers to widespread use.

In BASF's own words: “The gourmand character combines soft, powdery notes with freshness and red fruits. Showing good stability in all applications, the top note material has an excellent blooming effect.”

In this interesting interview from Perfumer and Flavorist (sponsored by BASF,) Ralf Pelzer, director of new business development, BASF Aroma Ingredients, and Tony Dallimore, perfumery director of Phoenix Fragrances LTD., discuss the ingredient’s development, applications, profile and more.

products.name: Veloutone
products.description:
Veloutone opens with luscious peach-apricot sweetness wrapped in clean jasmine petals. This creamy fruitiness feels almost edible yet sophisticated. A subtle lavender whisper prevents any cloying sweetness, adding unexpected freshness.

This material transforms compositions by bridging disparate elements seamlessly. Reach for Veloutone when jasmine needs body or fruits lack sophistication. It smooths transitions between top and heart notes whilst adding that coveted skin-like sensuality.

Deploy Veloutone to achieve the modern "your skin but better" effect. Combine with Paradise Molecule® for radiant white florals that bloom. Partner with woody molecules like Iso E Super and Miraclewood™ to create intimate, cashmere-soft drydowns.

products.name: Veramoss
products.description:
Oakmoss is the most important ingredient in Chypre and Fougere fragrances and when used in small amounts it adds softness and beauty to virtually all types of perfume. But sadly the material is now highly limited in use by IFRA standards (0.1% of the finished product). Making up nearly 16% of the natural absolute is Atraric Acid, aka Veramoss® or Evernyl

Use this powdered material to boost natural oakmoss, or on its own for the wonderful scent it has in its own right. As with most aroma chemicals, there are varying qualities. Veramoss is the finest quality.

Veramoss was a key material in masterpieces such as Polo (1978) by Carlos Benaim for Ralph Lauren, and forms a whopping 10% of Baccarat Rouge 540 (2015). It is found in varying amounts in thousands of fragrances.

Veramoss blends incredibly well with natural oakmoss, whether it be the IFRA prohibited pure Green Oakmoss from the former Yugoslavia, the elegant IFRA compliant Oakmoss Absolute IFRA 43 of LMR or the sublime decolorised Oakmoss Absolute MD 55 PCT TEC from the same.

As with most crystalline materials, we recommend adding this pure to your fragrance juice as it will dissolve in solution.

products.name: Veratraldehyde
products.description:
Veratraldehyde is a crystalline aroma chemical with a soft powdery vanilla custard quality. It is a really good alternative to vanillin (though it suffers from the same discolouration problems in soaps) or can be used to add nuance and interest to the same.

In the age of the gourmand, this material absolutely cannot go unnoticed and we highly recommend it for all perfumers. If you are unfamiliar with the use of crystallines in perfume, take a look at our little primer: How To Weigh A Powder.

products.name: Verbena Absolute
products.description:
Verbena essential oil is banned by the EU and IFRA but fortunately that is not true of the absolute. Verbena Absolute opens with an effervescent lemon-sherbet luminosity that feels candied yet distinctly green. Crush a fresh leaf between your fingers and you'll recognise that unmistakable snap—bright aldehydic citrus married to an herbaceous coolness. The heart reveals a soft, neroli-adjacent floralcy and dried chamomile tea character that sets this absolute apart from crude citral reconstructions.

This material transforms standard citrus openings into something sophisticated and alive. Use it to naturalise synthetic lemon accords built on Litsea cubeba or geranyl nitrile (Citralva)—even trace amounts will contribute the waxy, tea-like nuances that reconstructions lack. Verbena bridges the Hesperidic top and aromatic heart beautifully, making it essential for authentic Eau de Cologne compositions and green-floral hearts.

Build verbena accords with petitgrain to extend its leafy woody facets, or pair with neroli for a seamless orange blossom continuum. The hay-like dry-down bonds naturally with oakmoss in chypre structures. Fix this volatile material with frankincense or elemi rather than heavy musks—these resins share its lemony-peppery character and extend longevity without suffocating its brightness.

products.name: Verdantol™
products.description:
Fraterworks® Verdantol™ is a penetrating and diffusive green herbal base built around powerful aromatic molcules and rounded out with luxurious extracts of natural foliage, galbanum and grapefruit.

Verdantol™ provides a sophisticated note perfect for modern fine fragrances, imparting complex layered tones of fresh herbs, cut grass and greenery. Its superior power makes it an ideal choice for novel and long-lasting effects.

Recommended use at a 10% dilution is from traces to a few percent of your finished formula. However novel effects may be achieved at higher amounts. Blends beautifully with fruity, citrus, agrestic and floral compositions.

products.name: Verdol
products.description:
Verdol hits with bracing camphoraceous freshness — clean, minty, and immediately arresting. A woody-pine body emerges beneath the minty impact, grounding the material in forest depth. Earthy patchouli undertones complete a profile that moves from bright aromatic top to dark, rooted base.

Use it in patchouli accords where it amplifies earthy-woody depth while adding bracing lift. It excels equally in pine-forest compositions and dark, brooding woody-amber blends. Pair with ambery and oud materials to add unexpected radiant lift to dark compositions. Blend into weathered, elemental accords for brooding atmospheric depth.

products.name: Verdone
products.description:
Verdone opens with an immediate cooling rush - think white camphor with bright mint leaves and clean medicinal clarity. This alicyclic ketone combines dry woody structure with herbal sharpness, creating a backbone that elevates top notes without weighing them down. The initial impact is intense and crystalline, delivering a sensation of freshness that cuts through heavier accords.

In laundry and home care formulations, Verdone performs exceptionally where heat and steam are present. Its unique ability to sublime when heated makes it invaluable in detergents and functional products - the material literally lifts into the air during hot water use, carrying your entire composition with it.

Use Verdone to anchor aromatic fougères, add structure to citrus-heavy blends, or introduce sophisticated powdery transitions in masculine fragrances. It pairs brilliantly with aldehydes to amplify sparkle, with vetiver to emphasise woody-earthy facets, or with ionones to strengthen powdery heart notes.

products.name: Verdox HC
products.description:
Verdox is a lovely green apple top note. It is a demure chemical that doesn't dominate and can be used in quite high doses to sweeten a blend and soften the harshness of chemicals like Dihydromyrcenol. It has been used to great effect in Safari (Ralph Lauren), Ambre Narguile (Hermes), Neroli Portofino (Tom Ford), and Light Blue Pour Homme by Dolce and Gabbana.

Verdox HC makes outstanding blends with Cashmeran which is almost a basenote mirror image, and is dynamic when combined with Dihydromyrcenol and Orcanox™. 

Note that the CAS number 20298-69-5 is specific to this very high purity verdox. Mixed isomer (the weaker form) is often listed as 88-41-5.

products.name: Vernaldehyde
products.description:
Vernaldehyde is a fresh, green aldehyde with a bright outdoor-air character. Underneath the aldehydic top sits a cool, dewy green freshness and a light waxy-citrus edge. The overall effect is airy and clean, closer to spring air than to the fatty aldehydes of the C-10 to C-12 range.

Use it in muguet, lilac and freesia for a sense of open-air freshness. In citrus colognes it reinforces the top and keeps bergamot from collapsing. It also pairs well with cedar, vetiver and Iso E Super, adding a cool lift to woody bases.

Overdose it in a chypre to update the aldehydic top, where the green reads cleaner and more modern than classic C-10 or C-11. A trace lightens a heavy amber without weakening its warmth. It also refreshes a muguet base that has lost its lift.

products.name: Vertenex
products.description:
We stock Firmenich's Lorysia® — the finest quality of Vertenex, having the highest amount of the preferred cis isomer. Comparisons of Lorysia® against generic and even other big name produced versions of Vertenex illustrate how truly marvellous this Firmenich product is.

While Vertenex (PTBCHA or p-tert-butyl cyclohexyl acetate) is a lovely volumising wood material, Lorysia builds on that with its soft fruitiness and almost edible quality. Arctander speaks thus: “Widely used in perfumery along with the Ionone, Cedarwood products, floral and non-floral perfume chemicals, a very versatile perfume material for soap and other low-cost fragrances, where volume is required. Generally as a blender / modifier in countless types of fragrances, from Pine to Rose, from woody to floral, it is one of the most successful perfume chemicals of the last few decades.”

A far more radiant material than regular Vertenex, we recommend this as a wonderful alternative or blender to the now more common Iso E Super.

See our demonstration formula below for Dior Dior to see how Edmond Roudnitska used Lorysia® to great effect in what he considered to be his greatest fragrance.

products.name: Vertofix® Coeur
products.description:
Before Iso E Super™ there was Vertofix® Coeur, a light woody material capable of use at very high doses and loved equally by women and men. As perfumes became simpler and novel scents were demanded, naturals like cedarwood oil were increasingly displaced. 

Vertofix Coeur from IFF is the most refined and elegant form of Methyl Cedryl Ketone. In extremely large doses it provides a wonderful canvas for other wood materials, green notes and florals. Vertofix Coeur is a dry cedar material with nuances of musk and leather.

Blend it with Iso E Super when you want a little more character than the latter alone can provide, or use it in combination with Veticoeur™, the great classical base which forms the key of the two greatest vetiver fragrances (demonstration formulas below) and makes up a considerable part of that most unique of Chanel fragrances: No 19.

Vertofix Coeur can be used without any restriction.

products.name: Vertoliff
products.description:
Vertoliff (closely related to Triplal) smells tart, green, and aldehydic with a citrus-herbal brightness and a distinctive bark-like quality underneath. There is nothing subtle about the opening — it announces itself immediately. On dilution the tartness settles and a more rounded herbal character emerges.

The strength is high, so work from a dilution. What makes vertoliff particularly useful is its breadth — it sits comfortably in citrus, herbal, floral, and green accords, lending crisp freshness to top notes without overwhelming the composition. That versatility across fragrance families is its chief virtue.

Bergamot, galbanum, and clary sage complement its green-citrus character well. A trace in floral compositions contributes a green transparency that can lighten heavier hearts. In fresh masculine accords the citrus-herbal bite makes an immediate impression.

Vertoliff appears in Chanel Bel Respiro (0.19%), Davidoff Cool Water (0.15%), Dior Rouge Trafalgar (0.09%), and Hermes Un Jardin sur le Nil (0.07%).

products.name: Vertosine
products.description:
Broom, orange blossom, and leafy green — all at once. The green aldehydic character hits immediately, sharp and bright, but a warm floral quality saves it from harshness. You catch a gentle anthranilate-like warmth reminiscent of night-blooming flowers. The effect is intensely natural for a synthetic material.

This Schiff base (Triplal and Methyl Anthranilate) excels at bridging green and floral notes in ways that simpler materials cannot. It naturalises mimosa and honeysuckle accords, giving them a green botanical depth that reads as freshly cut stems rather than perfumery abstraction. In gardenia compositions, it supplies the green-leafy top that expensive naturals provide at a fraction of the cost.

Vertosine gives green top notes a depth and complexity they rarely have on their own. Use it to enrich galbanum and violet leaf accords. It also lifts citrus-peel notes — try it alongside bergamot and petitgrain where its floral warmth softens sharp hesperidic openings into something rounder and more complex.
tags: locale:heat needed for pure. Diluted is still thick.

products.name: Very Violet™
products.description:
Very Violet™ can be used in combination with other colours in the Perfumer's Palette™ range or alone to reduce yellow tones caused by the use of naturals, or to add a purple touch.

The Fraterworks® Perfumer's Palette™ is a range of dyes that can be used alone or in combination with each other to add vibrance and colour to your perfumes or cosmetic products. Our proprietary blend of FD&C and D&C colours are sold in liquid form.

Perfumer's Palette colours contain distilled water which is perfectly safe for alcoholic perfumes in the quantities needed for colouration. Typical use is from 0.01–0.5% of finished product.

At these low levels, staining of clothing or skin is minimal to none but you should always test your finished product against white cloth or paper.

products.name: Veticoeur™
products.description:
A classical cedar base with delicate nuances of violet and leather, Veticoeur™ is a wonderful canvas type material that can be used up to a whopping 5% of your finished product. Veticoeur™ was used in No 19 by Chanel and numerous other great fragrances of the 20th century (see our demonstration formulas below).

Veticoeur™ (classic Vetyrisia) is a perfect starting point for a modern woody fragrance that can be twisted in many different directions, from dry and green with Galbanum oil, to gourmand with Ethyl Maltol.

It suits feminine and masculine scents and blends extraordinarily well with Miraclewood™, Vetiveryl Acetate, Aetoxylon Oil, Orrisodore and Cedarome.

products.name: Vetikolacetat®
products.description:
There is no denying it: this smells like cannabis… and vetiver and rhubarb. Vetikolacetat (also called veticol or vetikol acetate) is a truly interesting material. In small amounts it adds a wonderful vetiver note in the complete absence of any natural vetiver, but it is also a magnificent nuancer and booster for the essential oil.

We use it in our best selling Vetiver fragrance, Serge Lutens uses 0.4% as the sole vetiver note in his Ambre Sultan (1993) for ladies and gentleman, and 0.25% is found in the plush Amouage masculine Interlude Black Iris where it modifies 2% natural vetiver.

It's relatively long lasting, novel and versatile, being able to be coaxed in a myriad directions depending on the skill of the perfumer; in one direction it is the memory of a hazy drug fuelled party, in another it is a dank barnyard beneath a lowering sky, and in yet another it is a fresh rhubarb note adding interest to a delicious gourmand; add Veratraldehyde and lactones for a custard note (with a trace of Sulfurol and Butyric Acid for enhanced egginess).

products.name: Vetikone®
products.description:
Vetikone is vetiver made fresh and radiant. It keeps the cool, rooty, green-woody heart of the natural, but lifts it with a bright squeeze of grapefruit and a sweet gardenia floralcy. The effect is clean and tea-like, brighter and less earthy-heavy than raw vetiver.

Use it to build modern vetiver accords or to pull vetiver up into the top of a fragrance, where it adds air and light. It brightens woody and chypre bases, freshens masculine colognes, and gives fern and floral structures a green, rooty spine.

As with most vetiver synthetics, it pairs very well with grapefruit notes.

products.name: Vetimoss
products.description:
Vetimoss is a fascinating long-lasting material with weedy, leathery, mossy and almost salty nuances. It is usually used in fairly small amounts (less than 2%) to add green herbaceous notes to a fragrance and can be a very interesting alternative to the usual Isobutyl Quinoline for a more refined leather note.

Vetimoss blends well with Suralette™ Extra, Artemal™, Fixomusk™, 2-Isobutyl Quinoline, Fauxmoss®, Corps Racine, the Cis-3 Hexenol family, Cedarome, Sophira and Saxon Moss.

In terms of naturals, Vetimoss blends with Birch Tar, Castoreum, Vetiver (Bourbon and Haiti), Vetiveryl Acetate and Vetiverol, as well as all the patchoulis and Oakmoss (Green and Decolourised).

products.name: Vetiver Acetate 53281
products.description:
Vetiver Acetate is one of the most popular zizanoides products which is frequently blended with fine vetiver oil for a softening effect or used on its own as a fresh, long lasting and modern vetiver note.

There are two types of the acetate: Vetiver Acetate and Vetiveryl Acetate. The first (this product) is produced from Vetiverol (a mix of vetiver alcohols) which is extracted from the Vetiver roots prior to the acetylation process. The second, Vetiveryl acetate is produced by direct acetylation of the whole Vetiver essential oil and contains more accessory alcohols so it has a slightly higher IFRA limit and a more complex drydown. It is also slightly lower in price.

Our vetiver acetate from MANE (reference 53281) is more sheer and diffusive than most and is the star of Frater Perfumes' best selling Vetiver fragrance and Molecule 03 by Escentric Molecules. When other Vetiver Acetates fade away, this astonishingly good version keeps going and going. It has a presence and a royal quality that absolutely justifies its higher price point.

This Vetiver Acetate has a woody character with spicy and citrus nuances. This makes for a more interesting inclusion in fragrances and far more lively blends with aroma chemicals like Iso E Super, Lorysia and Vertofix Coeur. This is the closest you can get to the famed Acetivenol of times gone by.

NOTE: under IFRA 52 (in draft), vetiveryl acetate and vetiver acetate must be fortified with 1% Tocopherol. Our vetiver acetate is not (yet) so yo

products.name: Vetiver Bourbon Absolute
products.description:
Vetiver Bourbon Absolute is a rather rare gem in the vetiver world, particularly an elegant extraction from the “Bourbon” starting material. It has a bright (but rounded) top note similar to a fine lavender absolute but its heart and dry down are pure unadulterated vetiver; loamy, dank and rich.

Very small amounts are all you need but interesting effects could certainly be had in overdose. We offer this pure and diluted to 50% in TEC for ease of use.

Origin: Madagascar
Part: Roots
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Vetiver Bourbon “Signature” Oil
products.description:
A good perfumer needs one great vetiver oil. This is it; this is the vetiver of renown.

From the very first sniff you will recognise this oil from such masterpieces as Guerlain's Vetiver (2000) and Jean Claude Ellena's Terre D'Hermes (2007) for Hermes.

We refer to this oil as “Bourbon” oil as it is the closest product to the near-mythical vetiver of the golden age, now no longer produced in La Reunion (formerly Île Bourbon) but sourced on the neighbouring island of Madagascar. This is not a blend or derivative product — it is 100% pure and natural vetiver goodness from Biolandes.

Wonderful effects can be achieved with this oil by blending it with our incredible Vetiverol ex Vetiver Haiti.

Origin: Madagascar and Mauritius
Part: Roots
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Vetiver Haiti SFE
products.description:
This SFE extract captures Haitian vetiver at its most natural. The low-temperature CO2 process preserves delicate green top notes that steam distillation destroys, delivering a woody-earthy character that is cleaner, rounder, and truer to the freshly unearthed root. No burnt artefacts, no harshness.

Where standard Haitian vetiver oil can have unwanted asparagus-like or potato-peel top notes from thermal degradation, the SFE avoids these entirely. You get the full woody-smoky-earthy vetiver signature — the refined smokiness, the dry mineral bite, the sweet precious-wood drydown — but in a smoother, more user-friendly form.

Use this in fougère and chypre accords where you want vetiver depth without roughness. It blends seamlessly with bergamot, oakmoss, and sandalwood. Layer it with your steam-distilled Haitian vetiver for a complex, multi-dimensional vetiver accord.

products.name: Vetiver Oil, Fractionated
products.description:
This molecular distilled speciality product of Floral Concept is outstanding. It is a 100% pure and natural vetiveryl acetate alternative. Vetiveryl Acetate is never a natural product even when it starts from pure vetiver oil, whereas this speciality uses a fractionation technique to get to a similar odour profile without the use of synthetic additives.

This is not just a product for natural perfumery, this is a product for all perfumers with a passion for fine fragrance. It is a product we love so much that we use it ourselves extensively and know no equal. It is, perhaps, the nicest Vetiver oil you will ever smell.

Floral Concept continues to prove itself a leader in the industry when it comes to total refinement and elegance. Blends of this MD Vetiver oil with Floral Concept's Patchouli Heart are out of this world.

The source of this material is Haiti and owing to difficult circumstances in that nation global stock is low. We will always endeavour to keep this (and all) products in stock but we recommend buying more than you think you need until the situation in the area is resolved.

products.name: Vetiver Oil, Haiti
products.description:
Historically Haitian origin vetiver played second fiddle to the Bourbon type (now from Madagascar) but in more recent times tastes have shifted and the Haiti type is now preferred. LMR produced the finest qualities and so it is their stock we have.

The price on this material is as good as we can get it but due to unrest in Haiti (as of writing in 2024) supplies are becoming scarce and costs will increase so get it while you can! We will continue to supply it as long as we can get it and LMR will be resuming production once peace returns to Haiti.

This Vetiver oil is COSMOS certified and holds the LMR “For Life” Certification which “recognizes an organization’s compliance with specific sustainability criteria, including transparency, environmental responsibility, fair working conditions and positive relations with producers and local communities.”

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

Origin: Haiti
Part: Roots
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Vetiver Oil, Java
products.description:
Due to the scarcity of Vetiver oil from Haiti, LMR has just launched a high quality Vetiver Oil from Java. This is an astonishingly unique type of vetiver, being considerably more fluid, and decidedly more flinty and smoky. Owing to the great care exercised by LMR in its manufacture, this vetiver oil is vastly better than most Java types, revealing sweet, vanilla, and butterscotch undertones while cheaper oils are often little more than smoke and peanuts. It has a distinctive odour of spent matches and would work incredibly well alongside such oils as Cypriol and Guiacwood Oil.

Use it as you would any vetiver oil as a long lasting and woody, earthy and vaguely gourmand base note. This is definitely different enough to the Vetiver sourced in other parts of the world to justify every perfumer having some.

products.name: Vetiver Oil, South India
products.description:
When people talk of vetiver they usually think of Madagascar (the source of the near mythical Bourbon type), Indonesia (Java usually), and Haiti. But perhaps the best kept secret for speciality vetiver oils is South India (pictured). 

On the sandy coast of South India, Vetiver has long been grown not just for its treasured scent but also for religious and medicinal uses. One of the leading suppliers from the region is TMV Aromas, established in 1958 and holding many prestigious awards for the quality of their natural Indian origin extracts. TMV is our supplier of choice for this material.

Vetiver Oil, South India smells as all vetiver oils should, but with the added richness of baked earth and saltiness from the myriad sandy beaches facing distant Ceylon.

You may also like our Vetiveryl Acetate (V. MANE Fils), Vetiver Oil Bourbon (Biolandes) and, coming soon, Vetiver Haiti Oil CMS (LMR).

Origin: South India
Part: Roots
Method: Steam distillation

products.name: Vetiverol ex Vetiver Haiti
products.description:
Vetiverol is the molecular distilled heart of vetiver oil and the raw material precursor for acetylated vetiver (vetiver acetate). Vetiverol is sweeter and softer than the acetate and, better still, it's completely unrestricted in use. Despite its name it is not a singular vetiver alcohol but rather the name given to the mix of naturally occurring alcohols inside vetiver oil.

Our vetiverol is extracted from the most beautiful vetiver oil and is the same type as that used by Ernest Beaux in No 5 for Chanel and Jean Paul Guerlain in Guerlain's Vetiver (demo formula below).

This is a perfect material for adding vetiver goodness without dominating a fragrance. It makes a wonderfully rich alternative to the various wood chemicals so overused in today's perfumes.

Note: the price of vetiverol has increased significantly due to the tumultuous events in Haiti.

products.name: Vetiveryl Acetate 20326
products.description:
Vetiveryl Acetate (and related Vetiver Acetate) is one of the most popular zizanoides products which is frequently blended with fine vetiver oils for a softening effect or used on its own as a fresh, long lasting and clean vetiver note.

There are two types of the acetate: Vetiver Acetate and Vetiveryl Acetate. The first is produced from Vetiverol (a mix of vetiver alcohols) which is extracted from the Vetiver roots prior to the acetylation process. The second, Vetiveryl acetate (this product) is produced by direct acetylation of the whole Vetiver essential oil and contains accessory molecules so it has a slightly less restrictive IFRA limit and a more complex and slightly more metallic dry down. It is also lower in price.

While Vetiver Acetate (acetylated Vetiverol) is more popular due to being cleaner in the dry down, this wonderful Vetiveryl Acetate 20326 should not be overlooked. It blends particularly well with Orris materials and can be used anywhere Vetiver Acetate is used.

We also stock Vetiver Acetate from V Mane Fils.

Used in: Chanel No 19, Poison, Ma Griffe and Dior Homme.

NOTE: under IFRA 52 (in draft), vetiveryl acetate and vetiver acetate must be fortified with 1% Tocopherol. Our vetiver acetate is not (yet) so you should do this yourself when planning for IFRA 52 compliance.

products.name: Violet Leaf Absolute, France
products.description:
Violet leaf absolute is one of the most useful in perfumery, lending naturalness and freshness to virtually all types of fragrances. As a modifier to the ionone family they are unsurpassed by synthetics. From traces (in fragrances such as L'Origan by Coty) to overdoses of nearly 1% pure in 1000 by Jean Patou (formula below), violet leaves contribute a magical quality that simply can't be replicated.

When comparing French violet leaves with the more common Egyptian type (which we also stock), the main thing you will immediately notice is that the French material is cleaner, smoother and greener (in the direction of grass alcohol). The Egyptian leaves are a little more intense and have a distinct leather nuance.

Intensely green, oily, earthy and floral, violet leaf absolute is best appreciated in dilution where its myriad complex layers reveal themselves fully. We offer it in 10% and 1% solutions in natural triethyl citrate also.

Certified: IG Absolue Pays de Grasse.

products.name: Violet Leaf ”Signature“ Absolute
products.description:
Violet leaf absolute is one of the most useful in perfumery, lending naturalness and freshness to virtually all types of fragrances. As a modifier to the ionone family they are unsurpassed by synthetics. From traces (in fragrances such as L'Origan by Coty) to overdoses of nearly 1% pure in 1000 by Jean Patou, violet leaves contribute a magical quality that simply can't be replicated.

Our violet leaf “signature” absolute comes from Floral Concept, a renowned specialist supplier in Grasse. It is a signature product because it is the finest extraction of Egyptian violet leaves we have come across, with the perfect balance of floralcy and earthiness.

Intensely green, oily, earthy and floral, violet leaf “signature” absolute is best appreciated in dilution where its myriad complex layers reveal themselves fully.

Violet Leaf 10% Superessence (Natural)

In dilution, violet leaf absolute contains a lot of non-soluble low (or no) odour matter. Our violet leaf 10% Superessence is a deep green crystal clear 10% dilution. To achieve this, we dilute the pure violet leaf absolute in a blend of natural Benzyl Benzoate (approximately 20%) and natural Triethyl Citrate (approximately 70%). We then perform a special filtration which removes any remaining insoluble product. This results in a purer and more concentrated product that can be used one for one in place of regular 10% dilution of violet leaf. This is a 100% natural product.

Origin: Egypt
Part: Leaves
Method: Solvent extraction
