products.name: Violette Bleue
products.description:
A wonderfully complex modern base replicating the whole scent of parma violets. Using classical building blocks combined with modern discoveries from headspace analyses of actual violets, we are able to produce an inimitable product. 

Overdose it for a true violet note, or use small amounts to add a natural and luxurious green note to your fragrances. Safe at up to 30% under the new IFRA 51 guidelines.

This base is loaded with many rich floral oils and absolutes.

products.name: Violettyne MIP
products.description:
Sharp violet leaf cuts through with real presence the moment Violettyne MIP hits a blend. A fruity-tropical undercurrent and galbanum-like depth give the note dimension beyond simple greenness. Distinctive cucumber and bell pepper facets set it apart from every other violet-leaf material.

This Firmenich material offers what MOC and MHC cannot — a green-violet note with genuine stability across formulations. Twenty-four hours on blotter gives you green-violet persistence that those older materials rarely match. Use in florals, chypres, and fresh green accords where you need lasting impact.

Blend with ionones for a complete violet accord, or combine with hexenyl acetate and galbanum for lush green-floral depth. The cucumber-pepper facet adds unexpected dimension to aquatic and aromatic compositions. Start at traces and work upward — the strength here is considerable.

Note: MIP is simply the shortened form of IPM in French.

products.name: Violiff
products.description:
Violiff opens with striking violet leaf intensity—green, fresh, and immediately commanding. The fruity banana facet adds unexpected sweetness, while tagette-marigold brightness contributes an almost medicinal edge that keeps the material interesting. The overall effect is heady and aromatic, bridging green and floral territories with remarkable confidence.

This IFF material spent years as a captive molecule before its release to the wider market. The cyclooctenyl structure provides the violet leaf character, while the carbonate group adds stability and diffusion. Despite its 12-hour substantivity on blotter, the immense strength and projection mean Violiff punches far above its volatility—a little travels a very long way. The material works as both top note sparkle and heart note support.

Work with Violiff at up to 2% of your concentrate, but approach with caution—the intensity demands serious dilution before evaluation. Use at 10% or less to appreciate its nuances without overwhelming your nose. It blends beautifully with woody-floral materials, galbanum products like Dynascone, and metallic-pineapple notes. The banana facet makes it valuable in fruity-floral compositions where green freshness needs tropical warmth. Note: may form acidic compounds under heat, so store cool.

products.name: Whiskey Lactone
products.description:
Whiskey Lactone is a rich lactone with a more intense scent than many of the classics and bearing a slight maple quality. Despite its name, the connection to whiskey is a tenuous one and it is best thought of as adding interest and nuance within a lactone blend.

Whiskey Lactone features heavily at a whopping 5.3% overdose in Baraonda by Nasomatto and it blends extremely well with fruit notes such as Benzaldehyde and Wild Cherry.

products.name: Whisky CO2
products.description:
This speciality CO2 extraction from V. MANE Fils is a marvel. The company has positioned itself as one of the finest producers of modern SFE extracts and this whisky essence is no exception. It is very costly but very powerful so there is considerable value for money. We recommend using it as an ethereal top note natural.

It opens with a strong scent of fermented beer which gives way to the classic whisky notes that separate the two alcohols in their final form (whisky and beer are made from similar starting materials).

Whisky P. Jungle Essence blends very well (as you might expect) with Whiskey Lactone to which it contributes a naturalising and radiant power. Try it with a touch of LMR's incredible smoky and woody Oakwood CO2 Extra, an extract of pyrogenated aged fine wine barrels. Or overdose it in a luxe gourmand with our hugely popular Coconut Delight and Raspberry Ripple bases.

This material is extremely strong so we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate.

We also offer Rum Pure Jungle Essence.

Origin: Scotland
Method: CO2 Extraction

products.name: White Amber
products.description:
One of the areas of expertise at Fraterworks is animalics — natural and synthetic; we even have a whole category dedicated to them.

White Amber joins that collection as a magnificent and regal ambergris base rich with natural animal musk. This is not for the faint of heart and certainly not for the vegan perfumers out there. If you need a vegan option, our Ambergris Intense and Absolute Ambergris are the products for you. 

White Amber is loaded with incredibly rare naturals that are almost never seen in modern perfumery due to their high cost. With White Amber you can incorporate genuine Boronia absolute into your products, noble labdanum fractions, and more.

From traces to overdose, White Amber is a powerful natural fixative and naturaliser that brings together the very best elements of nature and aroma science.

products.name: White Paris Mushroom Extract
products.description:
White Paris Mushroom Extract offers something rare in perfumery—the genuine scent of mushrooms as they release their aroma in the pan. This extract from Agaricus bisporus presents soft, rounded earthiness without the aggressive savoury punch that plagues many fungal materials. Its delicate nature makes it approachable where other mushroom products feel too culinary or confrontational.

You'll find this material invaluable for building forest floor compositions where authenticity matters more than amplification. Layer it with oakmoss, patchouli and vetiver to construct complex woodland bases that feel genuinely wild rather than synthetic. Its gentle character allows higher dosing than typical mushroom absolutes—the 10% MCT dilution gives you control whilst maintaining olfactory precision. Combine it with damp earth accords, mossy notes and cool green materials to evoke morning walks through deciduous forests.

Use this extract when reconstructing truffle effects alongside leather and tobacco, or pair it with wet stone accords and metallic florals for modern compositions that reference natural decay without repulsion. Its softness works beautifully beneath violet leaf and iris where it adds humus-like depth. Consider it for chypre structures where you need earthy authenticity without the regulatory concerns of traditional oakmoss.

products.name: White Rose Absolute, Moldova
products.description:
This is one of the rarest rose absolutes available. It is produced in Moldova from the white Rose Alba type. This is a rose of extraordinary beauty; while Bulgarian ottos pounce at you with brightness and vigour, Rose Alba imparts a warm ribbon of rich cooked plums with a clove bud spiciness. A drop on the hand is so addictive that it is impossible to stop sniffing.

Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate from citrus, making it suitable for natural perfumers.

Origin: Moldova
Part: Flowers only
Process: Solvent extraction

products.name: Wild Cherry
products.description:
Wild Cherry represents the natural fruity sweetness of cherries in their fresh state. This is not an intensely almond glace cherry but rather a natural and extremely complex scent of freshly picked fruit.

Fraterworks Wild Cherry can be used in small amounts to add a sparkling fruit top note, or in larger doses for a decisively cherry note. Modify with benzaldehyde and ethyl maltol to create a classic glacé cherry.

products.name: Wild Civet Tincture 2% (13 Yrs Aged)
products.description:
This is a one-off chance to purchase the rarest and most wonderful of all civet products: 13 year aged 2% tincture of wild Abyssinian civet. Most civet today is farmed as it is now under CITES protection, but this Fraterworks tincture was created prior to that. As a consequence this is one of the finest forms of Civet tincture you will ever experience. Compounded with the fact that it was made with food-grade alcohol batch made in New Zealand and you have a treasure of perfumery past. 

Our wild civet tincture has the typical characteristics of civet but due to age it is mellow and rich.  Additionally, because this is a wild harvest, it is imbued with the incredibly profound scent of the wild glory of Africa herself.

NOTE: there are some ambiguities around the US customs position on the import of civet to the US. We are happy to take the advice of our clients so if you add this to your cart we presume you are aware and are giving us the green light. We ship civet and other high-odour products in sealed unmarked silver foil bags to prevent cross-contamination in the event of leaks or parcel damage.

French Name: Infusion de civette

products.name: Wild Marjoram Oil
products.description:
First sniff is pure eucalyptus — sharp, clearing, bracing. Underneath sits a quiet sweet-spicy warmth and herbaceous softness that eucalyptus itself never delivers. This is Thymus mastichina, a Spanish thyme carrying the name "marjoram" for centuries despite sharing nothing with it.

Use it sparingly where you need bracing herbal freshness without eucalyptus oil's one-dimensional quality. A few drops lift a fougère or cologne, adding sun-baked Mediterranean garrigue character. Pair with lavender, rosemary, and cypress for scrubland accords — but measure in drops, not millilitres.

Fraterworks also stocks Sweet Marjoram Oil (Origanum majorana), which is a completely different plant — warm, nutmeg-scented, and gently spicy where this oil is clearing and camphoraceous. Despite the shared name, they are never interchangeable. Treat them as entirely unrelated materials.

products.name: Wild Strawberry
products.description:
While most strawberry bases are achingly gourmand, Wild Strawberry represents sun-ripened berries, complete with seeds and greenery. It is still ideal for gourmand fragrances but it won't introduce overwhelming amounts of ethyl maltol or other highly-sticky aromatics.

Use it as a decisive strawberry note in a high dose, or as a novel alternative to the more common peach notes found in perfumes through the use of gamma undecalactone.

Use it with Raspberry Ripple, Passionfruit Base 109223, Pineapple Supreme, and IFF's Tropicalia for a full bodied tropical fruit salad accord. A strange, yet delightful, synergy occurs when pairing Wild Strawberry with Black Musk.

products.name: Woodol®
products.description:
Woodol® is a multifaceted heart note that delivers a warm, rich foundation to fragrance compositions. Its complex profile blends dry woody notes with sweet amber facets and a distinct patchouli-like earthiness. This material is particularly suited to functional perfumery due to its exceptional stability in alkaline products, however, it still has great potential in fine fragrances; it is just waiting for the right perfumer to exploit it.

Incorporate Woodol® in formulations to impart a substantive woody-amber base with unique patchouli nuances.  It pairs well with other woody, amber, and earthy notes, enhancing depth and longevity. Exercise caution with dosing, as its character can become dominant.

Woodol® has synergies with Patchouli, Cedarwood (and related materials), and Ambroxan.

products.name: Wool Absolute
products.description:
An incredibly low-cost animalic that comes from a highly sustainable industry, Wool Absolute is upcycled by Biolandes in France from wool shorn from 100% pasture reared New Zealand sheep.

In an age where classic animalics such as civet and deer musk are becoming difficult to obtain, novel products are needed to get the same blending and luxuriating fixative effects. Wool Absolute is a perfect addition to the perfumer's palette as it is the byproduct of an enormous existing industry and is extracted from the animal's wool after shearing. No sheep or lambs are harmed in the process however this would still be considered non-vegan as it is produced by an animal.

The scent of this musk is pure rich lanolin with nuances of booze and fruit. For those who have worked on farms or seek a farmyard scent without fecal notes, this is ideal. In terms of animalics it is softer and more genteel than most (in fact it is rather nice to apply a little neat to the skin for its soothing and natural moisturising properties). Excellent for Oud fragrances.

Wool Absolute has excellent 10% solubility in ETH, DPG, IPM, DEP, BB and TEC.

Starting in 2024, all Fraterworks orders ship using green eco-fuel.

Origin: France (from New Zealand grass fed sheep)
Part: Wool

products.name: Yellow Dawn™
products.description:
The Fraterworks® Perfumer's Palette™ is a range of dyes that can be used alone or in combination with each other to add vibrance and colour to your perfumes or cosmetic products. Our proprietary blend of FD&C and D&C colours are sold in liquid form.

Perfumer's Palette colours contain distilled water which is perfectly safe for alcoholic perfumes in the quantities needed for colouration. Typical use is from 0.01–0.5% of finished product.

At these low levels, staining of clothing or skin is minimal to none but you should always test your finished product against white cloth or paper.

products.name: Ylang Heart
products.description:
Ylang Heart captures the creamy, exotic centre of the ylang flower: radiant and floral, warmed by soft spice and a whisper of fruit. A bright, almost wintergreen freshness lifts the top. It smells lush and rounded, without the sharp or fatty edges of the whole oil.

This is the ylang to use when you want richness without harshness. It slots into the heart of white florals, deepening jasmine, tuberose and gardenia, and lends a creamy, solar glow to rose. Its rounded spice also warms orientals and softens chypres, blending seamlessly with sandalwood and soft musks.

products.name: Ylang Impériale
products.description:
Ylang Impériale is a rich and powerful replacer for ylang ylang extra oil. This base can replace the finest ylang ylang at a 1:1 ratio and can be used at a huge 7.3% of the finished product for IFRA compliance — many times the amount permissable with natural ylang ylang products.

This scientific reconstruction is enriched with natural cananga odorata extracts. It can be used in small amounts for floralcy or in overdose for a Chanel No 5 or Patou Sublime type fragrance.

products.name: Ylang-Ylang Absolute
products.description:
Ylang-ylang absolute is luxury to the max. Intensely sweet and so balanced it is almost hard to believe. Take the very best aspects of all the ylang-ylang essential oils and then add volume, richness and a smouldering radiance and you have this product.

Origin: Madagascar Grown, France processed
Variety: Cananga odorata
Part: Flowers only
Method: Solvent extraction

products.name: Ylang-Ylang Complete Oil
products.description:
Our Ylang-ylang complete is a magnificent oil 100% processed in Comoros, the home of the finest ylang oils. Ylang-ylang complete is a cost effective way to get the ethereal beauty of the more expensive extra oil with the full bodied creaminess of the lower-cost fractions. This is a superior alternative to ylang-ylang III and can be used as a one for one replacer.

This oil, being sourced directly from Comoros, is the most luxurious of all complete products. In side by side tests with products from other high-end suppliers, our ylang-ylang complete has the longest lasting and creamiest dry down, lacking the sharp unpleasant cresylic notes apparent in most other extractions.

We also stock the sublime ylang-ylang extra "superior" oil as used in Chanel No 5 and the very finest French fragrances. Additionally, if you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities under IFRA guidelines, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base.

Origin: The Union Of Comoros
Variety: Cananga odorata var. genuina
Part: Flowers only

products.name: Ylang-Ylang Extra Oil, Comoros
products.description:
While most Ylang-ylang extra is from flowers grown in Madagascar, this beautiful Robertet extraction is from Ylang-ylang trees grown on Comoros just as it was when Ernest Beaux created Chanel No 5. It was formerly considered the premiere origin until low harvests and economics nearly shut down the Comoros trade. Thankfully it is now back and running full steam so you can have access to this nearly lost treasure.

In addition to this Robertet product we also offer a beautiful organic version from Biolandes. The chief difference between them is that the Robertet Comoros oil is sweeter and richer with a creamier and more balanced top note and a fruitier and spicer cinnamic dry down. This Robertet Comoros oil is the Fraterworks default Ylang-ylang and we use it in all of our products.

In ylang-ylang production terms, the “superior” oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the fruitiest and most ethereal top notes. Following that is this more balanced (and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature) “extra” grade which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The functional remnants are sold as grade I, grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil. Of those remnants, only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and “complete oil” being useful as a general mid-range ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals.

If you are loo

products.name: Ylang-Ylang Extra Oil, Org
products.description:
While some fragrances such as Chanel's original No 5 required a special penetrating variety of ylang-ylang (our “Extra Superior” product), the finest and most balanced all round ylang-ylang is the “Extra” quality distilled in Comoros on the same day as harvesting. This oil has the perfect balance of sweet top notes with a rich creamy floral heart and luscious dry down. If you only have one ylang-ylang, this is the one to have.

In ylang-ylang production terms, the “superior” oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the fruitiest and most ethereal top notes. Following that is this more balanced (and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature) “extra” grade which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The functional remnants are sold as grade I, grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil. Of those remnants, only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and “complete oil” being useful as a general mid-range ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals.

If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base.

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered organic company so while this product is organic when it reaches us from Biolandes, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

Extracted: The Union Of Comoros (s

products.name: Ylang-Ylang Extra Superior Oil, Org
products.description:
This is the famed ylang-ylang extra "superior" oil from Comoros (organic edition), the brightest ylang-ylang quality there is. This is the oil that Ernest Beaux demanded for Chanel No 5 because nothing else had top notes penetrating enough to handle the aldehyde overload. Most vendors settle for Madagascan processed extracts as they are less costly, but the Comoros oils remain to this day the peak of cananga perfection.

From the ethereal fruity top notes to the intensely sweet and lasting dry down, you will be absolutely converted to this quality of ylang ylang. This is the stuff of legends.

In ylang-ylang production terms, the "superior" oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the truest and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature. Following that is the more heart balanced “extra” grade (organic) which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The more functional remnants are sold as grade I ,grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil. Only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and "complete" oil being useful as a general low-cost all-purpose ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals.

If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base.

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered organic company so

products.name: Ylang-Ylang III Oil, Org
products.description:
Sometimes you need natural floralisation that sits calmly in a blend without dominating. Ylang-ylang III is perfect for that. It has the lowest amount of top note volatiles so instead of a penetrating fruity oil you get a softer almost heart-note-only product. This is also a cost effective ylang-ylang oil that works especially well in modern fragrances that rely on very subtle nuances. It works quietly but surely in the background.

In ylang-ylang production terms, the “superior” oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the fruitiest and most ethereal top notes. Following that is this more balanced (and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature) “extra” grade which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The functional remnants are sold as grade I, grade II and grade III (this product) or taken on the whole as “complete” oil. Of those remnants, only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheaper and more discreet oil and “complete oil” being useful as a general mid-range ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals.

If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base.

Note: Fraterworks is not a registered organic company so while this product is organic when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

Origin: Comoros
Var

products.name: Ylanganate
products.description:
Ylanganate glows with solar white flowers. Ylang, orange blossom and tuberose all shine through, bright and creamy, over a fresh green edge and a soft grape-like fruitiness. It smells radiant and natural.

A small amount rounds and brightens ylang, orange blossom, neroli and tuberose, pushing them toward a fresher, more natural radiance. It also lends a dewy, creamy roundness to gardenia and softens synthetic-smelling florals.

Pair it with vanillin and coumarin to add a solar top to a gourmand, or with ylang and neroli to amplify a classic white bouquet. Keep the dose small; its lift is generous.

products.name: Ysamber® K
products.description:
Ysamber K opens with an exceptionally pure, luminous woody character that immediately distinguishes itself from heavier amber materials. It delivers remarkable diffusion without the aggressive metallic edge often found in super-ambers. Its exceptional substantivity anchors volatile notes whilst maintaining a luminous, unobtrusive quality. Ysamber K radiates with extraordinary diffusion yet never flattens a composition.

You'll find this material indispensable when building contemporary woody structures that demand both power and refinement. Use it at 1-2% to add radiant lift and tenacity to citrus top notes, or dose it generously at 5-10% as your primary woody pillar. The material excels at harmonising aggressive molecules like Ambrocenide or Norlimbanol, smoothing their sharp edges whilst maintaining their incredible performance.

Transform your woody accords by pairing Ysamber K with sandalwood molecules like Ebanol or Javanol for enhanced depth and creaminess. When combined with soft musks and transparent florals, it provides an elegant foundation that never overwhelms delicate nuances. Exercise caution with citral-containing materials—this combination can veer towards functional freshness if not carefully balanced.

products.name: Yuzu Oil
products.description:
This cold-pressed Yuzu Oil bursts open with a sparkling, bitter-sweet citrus tang, somewhere between tart grapefruit and juicy mandarin. Behind the zesty brightness sits a dry, green, almost tea-like nuance. Yuzu has a luminous quality that feels fresher and more three-dimensional than lemon or bergamot.

Pair Yuzu oil with ginger (it is especially good with our Ginger Oil, Cote d'Ivoire), Timut pepper and cedarwood virginia for a vivid modern signature, or with our Lemon Verbena base and Provençal clary sage oil to play up its herbal, tea-like side. A touch with jasmine or neroli add a dewy, translucent lift. It works equally in unisex, sporty and quiet-luxury styles.

products.name: Z11™ 10 MIP
products.description:
Z11 (Ambraketal) was initially sold only as part of Firmenich's Fixobois base and so it found early use in fragrances like Chanel No 19. In time the material itself became available as a 10% dilution in IPM owing to its high strength. That is Z11 10 MIP (sometimes simply called Z11 MIP). 

In recent years a new product emerged which is the so called HD or "high definition" version which is sold as both an 8.5% dilution (Z11 8.5 HD) and pure. It is in that pure crystalline form that it found its way in to the popular fragrance One Million by Paco Rabanne. 

The two products are very similar but the classic Z11 retains its supremacy in terms of sheer beauty and Firmenich keep the pure form captive. To compare the two in furniture making terms, Z11 8.5 HD is like a steel nail holding a door together — intense and penetrating, while Z11 10 MIP is like a wooden peg or a dovetail joint in an antique armoire. They both do the same job (holding two pieces of timber together) but the second has heritage, prestige and elegance.

Z11 10 MIP is the Fraterworks choice for this material as it is simply the most beautiful and far better suited to quality fragrances that rely on purest radiant elegance over intensity and short-lived dazzle.

Z11 10 MIP is ambery, woody and dry and has an astonishing trigeminal effect which causes intense psychological pleasure in those who smell it.

products.name: Z11™ HD 8.5 MIP
products.description:
First, it is worth noting that MIP is simply the French version of IPM so this is an 8.5% dilution of high purity Amberketal in IPM.

Z11™ HD delivers extraordinary woody-amber power with remarkable iris elegance. This sophisticated synthetic creates a multifaceted foundation with exceptional tenacity and projection. Perfumers value its dual nature as the cornerstone in prestigious compositions where powerful woody character and refined powdery nuances define modern luxury.

While our personal preference is for the softer form of this chemical (Z11™ 10 MIP) this more recently released HD (high definition) version is extremely popular and if you are looking for a more pronounced amber, this is the material to get. 

While it is already diluted to 8.5% by Firmenich, it is version powerful and you should still use Z11™ HD 8.5 MIP at 0.1-1.5% concentration in woody-amber accords. This material pairs beautifully with ionones, orris materials, and woody notes while adding sophisticated depth to floral and oriental compositions. Apply judiciously in fine fragrances where its distinctive radiant character provides exceptional longevity and seamlessly bridges base and heart notes.

products.name: Zafran Attar
products.description:
Zafran Attar is the classical Indian saffron perfume — Kashmiri saffron stigmas (Crocus sativus) hand-collected from the Pampore valley in autumn, then co-distilled by deg-bhapka into Mysore sandalwood oil over multiple rounds until the wood is fully saturated. Saffron remains the most costly spice on earth, which puts this attar among the more rarefied Indian co-distillates.

Zafran Attar opens with the warm, honeyed character of dried saffron over soft, creamy sandalwood. Classic saffron notes of earthy hay and a faint leathery edge threads through the heart. 

Use Zafran Attar in classical oriental-rose accords, mukhallats, leather chypres and Mughal-style attar reconstructions. It pairs naturally with rose otto and oud — the three-way saffron-rose-oud accord is a backbone of Middle Eastern perfumery. A small dose adds golden warmth to amber bases without competing with the resinous notes.

This Zafran is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, a Kannauj distillery run by five generations of the Kapoor family using copper degs and the traditional water-distillation method.

products.name: Zambezi
products.description:
Zambezi is our internal formula for the original Safari for men by Annie Buzantian (Firmenich) for Ralph Lauren. Launched in 1992. The scent built upon some of the earlier foundations of masterpieces like Polo Green (also for Lauren) in its artful use of the quite potent artemesia oil in concert with fir balsam. As Buzantian was with Firmenich, she did not have access to the great base at the heart of Polo, Artemal, and instead built a cut down fond that mimicked and modernised that base.

When comparing this compound (and please note that this is not compliant for IFRA or the EU as it contains atranol-rich green Yugoslavian oakmoss) to the formula in bottles today, the main thing you will notice is the richness from all the trace naturals. The scent was rather cutting edge for its time, having not just large doses of rich Firmenich bases, but layers of herbs and layers of spices. Its overdose of neroli oil is rather out of place today, but certainly still acceptable in a mass market scent of the 1990s. A smidgen of aldehydes adds a vaguely soapy note which reads "clean" rather than "bath time". 

If you need an IFRA or EU compliant version, we can, for a 5 kilogram MOQ, produce it to order. IFRA compliance is possible to around 16% with minimal changes.

Top Notes: Lavender, Bergamot, Aldehydes, Coriander, Artemisia, Green Notes, Neroli, Lemon
Heart Notes: Tarragon, Carnation, Cinnamon, Rose, Jasmine, Cyclamen
Base Notes: Leather, Oakmoss, Sandalwood, Cedar, Patchouli, Musk,

products.name: Zenolide
products.description:
Zenolide opens with a clean, airy muskiness threaded with a distinctive red berry sweetness you won't find in most other musks. The waxy, skin-like quality is immediate and inviting. As it develops, a gentle animalic warmth emerges beneath the softness, giving it real depth without any harshness.

This macrocyclic musk excels at adding volume and lasting power to compositions that need a polished base. It sits beautifully behind floral and fruity accords, lifting them with transparent warmth rather than weighing them down. Pair it with ethylene brassylate for a layered musk foundation, or use it to soften woody notes in modern masculine and unisex builds.

Zenolide works across fine fragrance, soaps, shampoos, and home care with excellent stability. Note that it can solidify below 18°C—warm it gently until fully liquid before weighing to avoid crystallisation issues. At typical usage levels of under one percent, it provides a quiet musky glow; push it higher for unmistakable soft-musk presence.

products.name: Zingerone
products.description:
Zingerone opens with the comforting sweetness of baked ginger, distinctly different from fresh ginger's sharp bite—this is the molecule that forms when ginger is heated, capturing that mellow, warm spiciness. You'll immediately recognise its vanillic sweetness balanced by a subtle phenolic edge that prevents it from becoming purely gourmand. The woody-balsamic foundation provides exceptional tenacity, with documented performance exceeding 300 hours on testing strips.

This material bridges fragrance families brilliantly—use it to warm white florals like ylang-ylang and jasmine, or to add spicy-sweet depth to leather and tobacco accords. Its synergy with raspberry ketone creates powerfully realistic berry notes, while combinations with castoreum and labdanum yield sophisticated animalic-oriental effects. Apply judiciously at up to 2% of your concentrate; its potency means a little transforms entire compositions.

Beyond its primary ginger character, zingerone functions as a sophisticated sweetener and fixative, anchoring volatile top notes while adding dimensional warmth. Reach for it when vanillin feels too linear or when you need to create edible warmth without resorting to obvious gourmand materials. It excels at making florals feel sun-warmed and giving woody bases a subtle sweetness that reads as refined rather than confectionery.
